items.title: Encode South Carolina TANF unearned income and benefit group (Policy Manual Vol. 67 §§3.6, 7.1, 7.7, 8.15)

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Encoding gap

South Carolina TANF (Family Independence) has no RuleSpec module. `us-sc/` holds the SNAP policy manual pages, the CHIP/Medicaid levels, the income tax pipeline and six deferred SNAP regulations; nothing encodes the TANF Policy Manual. So Axiom cannot say which income South Carolina TANF counts, or at what amount.

PolicyEngine fixed its own South Carolina TANF unearned income list and benefit group size in PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10184. Its list had been copied from the IRS gross income sources, so it counted only the federally taxable part of Social Security, unemployment compensation (2020: up to $10,200 excluded under IRC 85(c)), pensions and interest. It also counted discharged debt and SSI recipients' needs, and it left out child support, alimony, VA benefits, workers' compensation and cash contributions. This issue asks for the same provisions in Axiom, so the two can be checked against each other.

## Blocker

The source is in the corpus, but not in the release rulespec-us pins.

- axiom-corpus scope `us-sc/manual/2026-09-10-tanf-state-policy-manual` (manifest `manifests/us-sc-tanf-state-policy-manual.yaml`; lock `.axiom/corpus-locks/us-sc/manual/2026-09-10-tanf-state-policy-manual.json`) holds SC DSS TANF Policy Manual **Volume 67** (dated 2026-07-31), PDF sha256 `cac6566b74f52d7a880a79407c302a6d18e2b6a23c0e9eab0dc711b0cbecaae6`, one row per PDF page: `us-sc/manual/dss/tanf-policy-manual/page-N`.
- rulespec-us `.axiom/toolchain.toml` pins `axiom_corpus_release = "us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap"`, which predates that scope. Releases from `us-rulespec-2026-09-11-program-ingestion-union` onward carry it.
- Encoding needs a re-pin to such a release (or a release union that adds the scope), then a signed encoder run. Signed runs are OpenAI-billed and need Max's approval, so this issue does not dispatch one.

## Modules and corpus citations

One module per manual page, following `us-sc/policies/dss/snap-policy-manual/page-N.yaml`:

| Module | Corpus citation | Provision |
|---|---|---|
| `us-sc/policies/dss/tanf-policy-manual/page-102.yaml` | `us-sc/manual/dss/tanf-policy-manual/page-102` | Section 7.1 definitions of income |
| `us-sc/policies/dss/tanf-policy-manual/page-108.yaml` | `.../page-108` | 7.7 chart: alimony, capital gains (other), cash contributions, child support/direct |
| `us-sc/policies/dss/tanf-policy-manual/page-112.yaml` | `.../page-112` | 7.7 chart: farm income is earned |
| `us-sc/policies/dss/tanf-policy-manual/page-113.yaml` | `.../page-113` | 7.7 chart: income maintenance insurance; interest, dividends and royalties with the $400 exclusion |
| `us-sc/policies/dss/tanf-policy-manual/page-115.yaml` | `.../page-115` | 7.7 chart: pension |
| `us-sc/policies/dss/tanf-policy-manual/page-116.yaml` | `.../page-116` | 7.7 chart: rent payments, retirement pay, SSA benefits (gross) |
| `us-sc/policies/dss/tanf-policy-manual/page-117.yaml` | `.../page-117` | 7.7 chart: SSI recipient excluded |
| `us-sc/policies/dss/tanf-policy-manual/page-118.yaml` | `.../page-118` | 7.7 chart: trade readjustment allowance, unemployment compensation |
| `us-sc/policies/dss/tanf-policy-manual/page-119.yaml` | `.../page-119` | 7.7 chart: VA benefits |
| `us-sc/policies/dss/tanf-policy-manual/page-120.yaml` | `.../page-120` | 7.7 chart: workers' compensation |
| `us-sc/policies/dss/tanf-policy-manual/page-56.yaml` | `.../page-56` | 3.6 living arrangements: SSI recipient excluded from the benefit group |
| `us-sc/policies/dss/tanf-policy-manual/page-133.yaml` | `.../page-133` | 8.15 need standard (50% of poverty) for the number in the benefit group |
| `us-sc/policies/dss/tanf-policy-manual/page-91.yaml` | `.../page-91` | 6.4 resource limit of $2,500 per benefit group |

## Text (verbatim, corpus rows, `source_as_of` 2026-09-10)

**page-102 (Section 7.1):**
> Income is money received by a BG member (s) from any source. Money received is classified as either earned, unearned income or in-kind income/benefits. In-kind income/benefits received by the BG is excluded.
>
> Unearned Income Any income not defined as earned income

**page-108 (Section 7.7 chart; columns are Income, Type, Count, Remarks):**
> Alimony (spousal support) Unearned Y
>
> Capital gains (other) Unearned Y
>
> Cash contributions Unearned Y
>
> Child support/direct Unearned See Remarks A BG may receive either voluntary or court ordered support directly from an absent parent (AP) or through the court. The amount of the support, excluding any court cost, is counted as unearned income.

**page-112:**
> Farm income Earned Y Considered self-employment income if the farmer/fisherman is not an employee

**page-113:**
> Income maintenance insurance (including disability insurance) Unearned Y
>
> Interest, dividends and royalties Unearned Y Up to $400 per BG annually is excluded. Income above $400 must be averaged over the period of the remaining 12 months.

**page-115:**
> Pension Unearned Y See also Retirement Pay

**page-116:**
> Rent payments (directly engaged in management of property less than 20 hours per week) Unearned Y Deduct cost of doing business (if appropriate).
>
> Retirement Pay (Railroad Retirement, Civil Service, etc.) Unearned Y
>
> SSA benefits Unearned See Remarks Count gross amount. This includes Medicare premium

**page-117:**
> but does not include recoupments. [...]
>
> SSI benefit Unearned See Remarks Exclude the SSI recipient, his/her income, resources and SSI payments in determining benefits for other BG members.

**page-118:**
> Trade readjustment allowance Unearned Y Count the same as unemployment compensation benefits (UCB).
>
> Unemployment compensation benefits (UCB) Unearned Y This includes Pandemic Emergency Unemployment Compensation and/or Pandemic Unemployment Assistance.

**page-119:**
> Veterans Administration (VA) benefit Unearned Y CAUTION: Exclude VA benefits when used for educational purposes to cover the cost of tuition and mandatory fees.

**page-120:**
> Workers’ Compensation Unearned Y

**page-56 (Section 3.6, living arrangements chart):**
> SSI recipient lives with BG. Exclude the SSI recipient, his/her income, resources and SSI payments in determining benefits for other BG members. The individual has the option to receive benefits under either program. NOTE: If an SSI child is the only child in the home, include the parent(s) as the only BG member.

**page-91 (Section 6.4):**
> The resource limit for TANF is $2,500 per BG.

**page-133 (Section 8.15):** "The gross income limit, need standard and payment standard for TANF are revised each October 1st to reflect the annual adjustment to the Federal Poverty Guidelines." The table (2025 guidelines) lists, by number in the benefit group, annual guidelines $15,650 (1), $21,150 (2), $26,650 (3) and need standards "(50% of poverty)" $652, $881, $1110; "To determine the Gross Income Limit, multiply the Need Standard by 1.85 and drop the cents."

## Required outputs

- `sc_tanf_counted_unearned_income` (Person, Month, Money): the gross monthly amount of each counted source. Social Security at the gross amount including the Medicare premium and excluding recoupments; unemployment compensation (and trade readjustment allowance) in full; pension and retirement pay including railroad retirement; VA benefits not used for tuition and mandatory fees; workers' compensation; income maintenance and disability insurance; child support received directly, excluding court costs; alimony; cash contributions; capital gains other than from self-employment property; rent where the person manages the property under 20 hours a week, net of the cost of doing business; interest, dividends and royalties after the exclusion below. Zero for an SSI recipient.
- `sc_tanf_interest_dividend_royalty_exclusion` (benefit group, Year, Money): 400.
- `sc_tanf_countable_interest_dividends_royalties` (benefit group, Month, Money): max(annual interest + dividends + royalties of non-SSI members − 400, 0) / 12.
- `sc_tanf_farm_income_is_earned` (Person, Month, Judgment): holds for farm income of a farmer or fisherman who is not an employee.
- `sc_tanf_ssi_recipient_income_excluded` (Person, Month, Judgment): holds for an SSI recipient.
- `sc_tanf_benefit_group_size` (benefit group, Month, Count): members who do not receive SSI (page 56).
- `sc_tanf_need_standard` (benefit group, Month, Money): 50% of the monthly poverty guideline for that size; zero for an empty group (page 133).
- `sc_tanf_countable_resources` (benefit group, Month, Money): countable resources less the SSI recipient's own resources (pages 56, 117), compared with the $2,500 limit (§6.4, page 91).
- Discharged debt is not unearned income (Section 7.1, money received). The manual does not say whether periodic IRA/401(k) withdrawals are income (IRA and Keogh balances are resources, pages 92-93); PolicyEngine counts them at the gross amount, and the encoder should flag the open point rather than decide it.

## review_finding (pasteable)

```
review_finding: South Carolina TANF counts unearned income at the gross amount received (Policy Manual Vol. 67 §7.1, p.102: "Income is money received by a BG member (s) from any source"; §7.7, p.116: SSA benefits "Count gross amount"), not the federally taxable amount. Counted: Social Security, unemployment compensation (p.118), pension and retirement pay incl. railroad retirement (pp.115-116), VA benefits (p.119), workers' compensation (p.120), income maintenance/disability insurance (p.113), child support received directly, alimony, cash contributions, capital gains (other) (p.108), rent (p.116), and interest/dividends/royalties above $400 per benefit group per year, averaged over 12 months (p.113). Excluded: the SSI recipient, his/her income and resources (§3.6 p.56, §7.7 p.117); the need standard is 50% of the poverty guideline for the benefit group without SSI recipients (§8.15 p.133). Farm income is earned self-employment income (p.112). Discharged debt is not money received (§7.1).
```

## Companion tests

Expectations come from the manual text above, the same ground truth as the PolicyEngine YAML tests in PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10184 (`policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/sc/tanf/sc_tanf_gross_unearned_income.yaml` and `integration.yaml` Case 9). Monthly amounts are annual / 12.

1. Social Security retirement $6,000 a year, taxable part $0: counted unearned income $500 a month (p.116).
2. 2020 unemployment compensation $12,000 (federally taxable $1,800 after the $10,200 exclusion): counted $1,000 a month (p.118).
3. Taxable pension $2,400 and tax-exempt pension $1,200 a year: counted $300 a month (p.115).
4. $1,200 a year each of child support, alimony, VA benefits, workers' compensation, disability insurance, survivor pension, railroad retirement and cash contributions: counted $800 a month (pp.108, 113, 116, 119, 120).
5. Discharged debt $6,000: counted $0 (p.102). (PolicyEngine also counts IRA $9,600 + 401(k) $2,400 withdrawals as $1,000 a month; the manual is silent on periodic withdrawals, so this case is informational.)
6. Farm income $6,000 a year: unearned $0, earned $500 a month (p.112).
7. Interest $300 a year: counted $0 (p.113).
8. Taxable interest $600 and tax-exempt interest $1,000 a year: counted (1,600 − 400) / 12 = $100 a month (p.113).
9. Two members with $600 interest and $600 dividends: group counted (1,200 − 400) / 12 = $66.67 a month (p.113).
10. SSI recipient with Social Security $4,800 and interest $1,200: counted $0 (p.117).
11. Parent and two children, one child receiving SSI, a month from October 2025: benefit group size 2, need standard $881 from the table (pp.56, 133). PolicyEngine's YAML uses January 2025 and Volume 65's table: (15,060 + 5,380) / 12 x 0.5 = $851.67; it does not yet drop cents.
12. Parent and an only child who receives SSI, from October 2025: benefit group size 1, need standard $652 (pp.56, 133).
14. Parent with $800 and an SSI child with $1,800 in bank accounts: countable resources $800, within the $2,500 limit (pp.56, 91, 117).
15. Trust income: a $1,200 net loss passed through from a trust does not offset a $2,400 pension; counted $200 a month (p.102, money received).
13. Single parent, two children: parent receives child support $3,600 and interest $1,000 a year; one child receives Social Security survivors benefits $4,800 a year. Benefit group unearned income 300 + 400 + (1,000 − 400) / 12 = $750 a month (pp.108, 113, 116). The need standard and benefit calculation (§§8.15-8.16) are outside these modules.

items.title: Minnesota CCAP and MFIP: count RSDI only above the individual SSI federal benefit rate (Minn. Stat. 256P.06, subd. 3(2)(xvi)) (PE-US #10333)

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## PolicyEngine parity request

Mirror [PolicyEngine-US #10333](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/pull/10333), head `c3886690eba7ccb3d22d823fb7e7eb14c81ff7a4`. The PR adds a person-level `mn_ccap_countable_rsdi` for the Minnesota Child Care Assistance Program (CCAP, Minn. Stat. chapter 142E). For each recipient, it takes annual Retirement, Survivors, and Disability Insurance (RSDI) payments, including dependents' benefits, and subtracts 12 times the monthly individual SSI federal benefit rate (FBR), floored at zero. CCAP unearned income then counts that amount instead of gross RSDI. All YAML cases concern 2025 and 2026.

The same statutory item also covers MFIP (chapter 142G). PE-US does not apply it to MFIP yet; that is tracked in PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10387. Encode the item for both chapters.

### Existing-module search

Searched on October 22, 2026:

- **rulespec-us `main` at `fa533144540a7297ecda1e43c90a9e4344746c5d`** (recursive tree, not truncated). It has no module, test or encoding manifest for Minn. Stat. 256P.06, chapter 142E or 142G income, or RSDI counting.
  - `us-mn/statutes/` holds only `290/0121`, `290/0123`, `290/06`, `290/067` and `290/0671`.
  - `us-mn/policies/` holds the CMS eligibility levels, the income-tax pilot and two Combined Manual policies: `0020-21/msa-assistance-standards-2026` and `0022-12/mfip-total-grant`. Neither counts RSDI.
- **rulespec-us issues.** `gh search issues` for "256P.06", "Minnesota RSDI" and "us-mn" finds no covering issue. The nearest are #1735 (MSA, 256D.435 SSI exclusions) and #1859 (MSA guardian fees).
- **Federal FBR modules.** `us/statutes/42/1382/b.yaml` (annual benefit rate without an eligible spouse), `us/statutes/42/1382f/a.yaml` (cost-of-living increases) and `us/policies/ssa/cola/2026.yaml` (2.8 percent) exist. No module publishes the 2025 or 2026 monthly FBR amount as a value.
- **axiom-corpus `main` at `e26ec7b4e0715a8f80f75186199aa83d77707116`.**
  - **Statute: ingested.** Scope `us-mn/statute/2026-09-14-income-tax-chapter-us-mn-title-256p` holds row `us-mn/statute/256P.06` (provisions JSONL line 9, row UUID `694da3cb-3cd2-59bd-b30e-fa3421700da8`, expression date `2026-09-14`, file git blob `6f65ea39aa9a2d750a7a398dd5e1f8ac77fb3a7e`). The row is section level; there are no subdivision rows. Its text matches the 2025 revisor text below.
  - **Combined Manual: stale for this section.** The selected scope `2026-05-27-mn-combined-manual-r2026-07-15-self-contained` (from `dhs-327301.pdf`) has 0017.15.45 at `us-mn/manual/dhs/combined-manual/current/page-818` and `page-819`, with issue date **11/2019**. That version predates the rule and says "If a client receives RSDI, count the gross RSDI amount as unearned income." Do not use it as proof for this module. The 11/2024 version quoted below is not ingested.
  - **CCAP Policy Manual:** no manifest covers sections 6.6 or 6.15.24.
- **Pinned release.** rulespec-us pins `us-rulespec-2026-10-20-fs-pilot-reg-e-f` (content SHA256 `788608e7c7181d77f3c2313b3694b6c1f01b324e415e2dcadd8607edd0deee61`). Its only Minnesota statute scope is `2026-07-13-recovery`, which holds chapter 290 only. The 256P scope is selected by the union releases, for example `us-rulespec-2026-10-13-w7-bundle-gaps-union` and `us-rulespec-2026-10-12-w5-benefits-union`.

This is a new-module request, never an `encoded-correct` claim.

### Target module and corpus

| Target module | Corpus citation | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `us-mn/statutes/256P/06.yaml` (proposed, after `us-mn/statutes/290/0671.yaml`; confirm the path and case with the encoder's citation mapper) | `us-mn/statute/256P.06` | subd. 3(2)(xvi) only: countable RSDI per recipient for chapters 142E and 142G. Item (viii) and subd. 2(a) are context for controls. |

## Law, verbatim

**Minn. Stat. 256P.06, subd. 3 (2025 edition)** ([revisor](https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256P.06); corpus row `us-mn/statute/256P.06`), the opening words and the two RSDI items:

> Subd. 3. Income inclusions. The following must be included in determining the income of an assistance unit: (1) earned income; and (2) unearned income, which includes: [...] (viii) for the purposes of programs under chapters 256D and 256I, retirement, survivors, and disability insurance payments; [...] (xvi) for the purposes of programs under chapters 142E and 142G, the amount of retirement, survivors, and disability insurance payments that exceeds the applicable monthly federal maximum Supplemental Security Income payments.

**Minn. Stat. 256P.06, subd. 2(a) (2025 edition)**, which exempts only earned income, so a child's own RSDI still counts:

> (a) The following members of an assistance unit under chapters 142E and 142G are exempt from having their earned income count toward the income of an assistance unit: (1) children under six years old; (2) caregivers under 20 years of age enrolled at least half-time in school; and (3) minors enrolled in school full time.

**History.** Laws 2023, chapter 70, article 10, section 79 added item (xvi), naming chapters 119B and 256J, effective September 1, 2024. Those chapters were later renumbered 142E and 142G. Use `effective_from: '2024-09-01'`.

**Agency guidance (supporting the individual rate, applied per recipient; not in the corpus at these issue dates):**

- **CCAP Policy Manual 6.15.24**, issue date 01/2025 ([DHS](https://www.dhs.state.mn.us/main/idcplg?IdcService=GET_DYNAMIC_CONVERSION&RevisionSelectionMethod=LatestReleased&dDocName=CCAP_061524); read from the Wayback copy of 2025-04-11, because the live page shows a bot check): "RSDI is reduced by the amount of the Social Security Insurance (SSI) Federal Benefit Rate, currently $967 per month. [...] This reduction applies to RSDI received monthly and to RSDI retro payments." $967 is the 2025 individual FBR; the couple rate was $1,450.
- **CCAP Policy Manual 6.6** ([DHS](https://www.dhs.state.mn.us/main/idcplg?IdcService=GET_DYNAMIC_CONVERSION&RevisionSelectionMethod=LatestReleased&dDocName=CCAP_0606)): "The SSI Federal Benefit Rate is a required RSDI income deduction."
- **Combined Manual 0017.15.45**, issue date 11/2024 ([DHS](https://www.dhs.state.mn.us/main/idcplg?IdcService=GET_DYNAMIC_CONVERSION&RevisionSelectionMethod=LatestReleased&dDocName=cm_00171545); read from the Wayback copy of 2025-12-03), MFIP and DWP: "For each client who receives RSDI, count only the gross RSDI amount that exceeds the SSI standard amount for a household of 1 as unearned income." Its 09/2024 revision note: "RSDI income that is at or below the federal SSI level is not counted when determining or redetermining eligibility or benefits. This change applies to MFIP, DWP, and CCAP."
- **Combined Manual 0029.06.06**, issue date 11/2019 ([DHS](https://www.dhs.state.mn.us/main/idcplg?IdcService=GET_DYNAMIC_CONVERSION&RevisionSelectionMethod=LatestReleased&dDocName=cm_00290606)): "RSDI provides a monthly income to retired people, survivors or dependents of insured people, and people with disabilities."

**FBR amounts.** SSA's [SSI Federal Payment Amounts](https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/SSIamts.html) give the monthly individual FBR as $967 for 2025 and $994 for 2026 (couple: $1,450 and $1,491). The 2026 amount also follows from the existing modules: 967 × 1.028 = 994.08, rounded down to $994.

## Required outputs

Amounts are USD per person per month.

For each person who receives RSDI, under a program in chapter 142E or 142G, in a month on or after September 1, 2024:

- **Countable RSDI** = max(gross monthly RSDI − the monthly individual SSI FBR, 0).
  - Gross RSDI is the sum of the person's own retirement, survivors, disability and dependents' benefits.
  - The FBR is the individual rate (no eligible spouse), not the couple rate.
  - The offset applies to each recipient separately. One person's unused offset does not reduce another person's RSDI.
- **Control:** under chapters 256D and 256I, item (viii) counts the full RSDI payment.

Leaf inputs: the month; the program chapter; the person's gross monthly RSDI; the monthly individual FBR. Import the FBR from `us/statutes/42/1382/b` and `1382f` if the encoder can; otherwise take it as a leaf with SSA's published amount.

Out of scope: CCAP's Medicare premium deduction (manual 6.6), CCAP annualization (PE-US offsets annual RSDI by 12 × the monthly FBR, which agrees for level monthly payments), and the MFIP budget that uses this amount.

## Companion tests

Expected values come from the statute and SSA's published FBRs; case 6 also matches CCAP manual 6.15.24's $967. The cases mirror [the PE-US YAML at the PR head](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/blob/c3886690eba7ccb3d22d823fb7e7eb14c81ff7a4/policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/mn/dcyf/ccap/mn_ccap_countable_rsdi.yaml), whose annual values are 12 times these monthly values. Program: chapter 142E unless stated.

| Case | Month | Recipients and gross monthly RSDI | Hand computation | Expected countable RSDI |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| 1 | 2026-01 | one adult, retirement $800 | max(800 − 994, 0) | $0 |
| 2 | 2026-01 | one adult, disability $1,500 | 1,500 − 994 | $506 |
| 3 | 2026-01 | one adult, retirement $994 | 994 − 994 | $0 |
| 4 | 2026-01 | one adult, retirement $500 and survivors $750 | (500 + 750) − 994 | $256 |
| 5 | 2026-01 | two adults, disability $1,500 and $500 | [1,500 − 994, max(500 − 994, 0)] | [$506, $0] |
| 6 | 2025-01 | one adult, retirement $1,250 | 1,250 − 967 | $283 |
| 7 | 2026-01 | one adult, retirement $995 | 995 − 994 | $1 |
| 8 | 2026-01 | adult, disability $1,500; child aged 8, dependents' benefit $1,100; child aged 5, dependents' benefit $500 | [506, 1,100 − 994, max(500 − 994, 0)] | [$506, $106, $0] |
| 9 (control) | 2026-01 | one adult, retirement $800, chapter 256D program | item (viii): full amount | $800 |
| 10 (control) | 2026-01 | case 2 under chapter 142G | same rule as 142E | $506 |

Case 5 rejects the two other readings: one household-level offset gives 2,000 − 994 = $1,006 in total, and the couple rate gives 2,000 − 1,491 = $509 in total.

## Pasteable `review_finding`

> Encode Minn. Stat. 256P.06, subd. 3(2)(xvi), from corpus citation us-mn/statute/256P.06, using the encoder's canonical module path. For each person who receives RSDI under a chapter 142E or 142G program, from September 1, 2024, output countable monthly RSDI = max(gross monthly RSDI − monthly individual SSI federal benefit rate, 0). Gross RSDI includes the person's retirement, survivors, disability and dependents' benefits. Apply the offset per recipient, with the individual rate, never the couple rate or a household-level offset. Under chapters 256D and 256I, item (viii) counts full RSDI. Attach verbatim proof to each output. Reproduce the ten companion rows above. Do not use the corpus's 11/2019 Combined Manual 0017.15.45 page as proof; it predates the rule.

## Status

**Queued, blocked on a compatible corpus re-pin and signed encoder dispatch.**

- The statute is already ingested, so no new ingestion issue is needed for item (xvi). rulespec-us's pinned release does not select the 256P scope; advance to a compatible release that does.
- The current Combined Manual 0017.15.45 (11/2024) and CCAP manual 6.6 and 6.15.24 are not ingested. They support the reading but are not needed as proof, because the statute and SSA's FBRs fix the values.
- Each billed signed-encoder run needs separate approval. No RuleSpec was hand-written and no encoder was run for this request.

items.body:
## Objective

Ship New York HEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1b, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9744 (branch `ny-heap`), open and under review, not yet merged. It is a reference candidate, not an already-merged or independently validated oracle. Scope, policy periods, module paths, source text, required outputs and companion tests are in the sections below. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges; pin that revision, not the draft, for release validation.

## PolicyEngine implementation (historical snapshot)

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9744, open and under review, not merged. Head `f3971348a5` (2026-10-06): commit `0478fcd90a` applies DTrim99's round 1 review (Code A as living alone, Social Security and railroad benefits net of the Medicare Part B premium, per-source flooring, the FY2024 and FY2025 matrices with the $41 Tier I add-on, new branch cases, templated descriptions and reference fixes) and is merged with `upstream/main`. History: first head `ca443e2704` (2026-10-02); the 2026-10-02 review fixes (TANF not counted; `survivor_benefits`, `farm_rent_income` and `miscellaneous_income` counted; plan anchors; test rewrite) pushed as `2ee8a99173` (2026-10-03); a tidy pass pushed as `194a3b97bc` (2026-10-06). Everything below describes head `f3971348a5`. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges; pin that revision for release validation.
- **Scope:** the Regular benefit of the New York Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP) for the 2023-2024, 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 program years (FY2024 to FY2026): income and categorical eligibility, qualified household size, countable income, the direct-heating payment by fuel, the heat-included payments, and the Tier I and vulnerable-member supplements. ## Interpretations and gaps

1. **"Code C" (source conflict, owner decision pending, evidence unresolved).** Manual D.4(a)(5) excludes "Federal living arrangement code C SSI recipients". Its excluded-income rule D.13(a)(11) describes Code C as "Code C SSI payments made to the household for care of SSI adults", 14-ADM-07 Attachment 2 defines state Code C as family care in "a family type home for adults", and the SSA 2010 page describes state C as "Congregate care facility, Level 1". The draft maps the exclusion to the federal child-in-parental-household arrangement with SSI receipt, so every SSI child living with a parent leaves the household size, countable income, vulnerability and SSI categorical eligibility. `eligibility/ny_heap_household_size.yaml` Case 1 (adult with wages $24,000, a foster child aged 3 with $6,000 Social Security, an SSI child aged 10 with $6,000 SSI) expects size 1, income $24,000, not vulnerable, $400; under the family-care reading it would be size 2, income $30,000, vulnerable, $435. 393.4(b) names only foster members and roomers or boarders. No OTDA text resolving D.4(a)(5) was found. The owner kept the manual-literal reading on 2026-10-06; `ny_heap_is_excluded_person` now records D.4(a)(5), 393.4(b) and D.3(a)(2) and points to this issue, and test 16 covers reported SSI receipt in the Code C arrangement.
2. **Code A (settled 2026-10-06; one condition not determinable).** The glossary requires "Code A for both State and Federal SSI" and 14-ADM-07 defines state Code A as living alone: one eligible individual or one eligible couple, not living with an ineligible spouse, a child they are responsible for, or anyone they prepare food with. The model now requires every non-foster SPM member to be an SSI recipient (`ssi` > 0 or `receives_ssi`) who is the tax-unit head or spouse, plus a counted recipient in the federal own-household arrangement (test 15). Preparing food in common (condition 4) is not determinable from inputs. OTDA's page also says Tier I by receipt needs "at least one adult household member"; not modeled separately.
3. **Sizes 14 and above (source conflict; the draft follows the rule).** D.9(c) and plan 2.1 row 14 give 150% of the poverty guideline: floor(1.5 x (15,650 + 13 x 5,500) / 12) = 10,893 a month ($130,716, `eligibility/ny_heap_income_limit.yaml` Case 2). The matrix row "14+ | 595+ | 687+" and OTDA's "Add $687" give 10,221 + 687 = 10,908; Tier I by increment is 8,845 + 595 = 9,440 against floor(1.3 x 87,150 / 12) = 9,441. Sizes 1 to 13 reproduce exactly either way.
4. **TANF and the added sources (post-fix).** TANF is not counted because the plan's 1.9 TANF box is unchecked and the manual counts a TA grant only in the roomer-budgeted minor case of D.11(c)(1); it still confers categorical eligibility, so the benefit cannot change (`income/ny_heap_countable_income.yaml` Case 2). `survivor_benefits`, `farm_rent_income` and `miscellaneous_income` are counted under D.12(a)(13), (14), (27) and (38) (Case 3); Since 2026-10-06 every unearned source is floored at zero per member (test 18), so a rental or estate loss does not offset other income.
5. **Solar (interpretation without source support).** `base.yaml` pays SOLAR the $635 "other fuels" amount (`ny_heap.yaml` Case 1, ninth household, $696 in Tier I). No source names solar; the model reads a solar household's bill from the electricity bill, which matches the $400 row's description of direct payments "based on their household's actual usage to the vendor".
6. **Not modeled.** Safety Net Assistance as a categorical program (manual D.10(c) and 393.4(c)(1)(ii) include it; the plan and OTDA's page say "federally funded" PA); roomers and roomer-boarders, household employees, non-contributing adults and fleeing felons (D.4(a)(1), (2), (4), (6)); the Medicare Part D premium (no variable; the Part B premium is deducted since 2026-10-06, test 19, using the computed out-of-pocket premium, which is zero when a Medicare Savings Program pays it); application-month timing, recurring receipt "on or before the date of the HEAP application", expedited SNAP and emergency TA (D.11(a)); previously advanced nominal awards and once-per-program-year limits; the Section 8 market-rent exception (F.2(c)(1)); the Low Income Worksheet; SSN documentation; plan 1.9 items without inputs (contract income, mortgage or sales-contract payments, commissions, legal settlements, jury duty, royalties); D.13 exclusions that cannot be isolated (irregular income up to $30 a quarter, bonuses, non-recurring lump sums, regular cash support from outside the household); FECA, railroad and Medicaid-based disability pathways in B.3(b)(3).
7. **Unspecified fuel (coverage limit, not a rule).** `heating_type` is a required input. With direct heating, an unspecified fuel pays $0 because the matrix has no row to place it in (`ny_heap.yaml` Case 12); with heat included in rent, group residences or subsidized housing the $50, $45 and $21 amounts do not depend on fuel and are paid for any `heating_type` (Cases 3, 9, 14; `integration.yaml` Case 8).
8. **Poverty guideline vintage (inference).** The matrix states no guideline year. floor(1.3 x 2025 guideline / 12) reproduces all 13 Tier I cells and the 2026 guideline reproduces none, so `fpg_year_lag` is 1. `income/ny_heap_fpg.yaml` Case 1 (period 2022, size 2, $17,420 from the 2021 guideline) checks the lag mechanics only and is not verified New York policy.
9. **SMI arithmetic (inference).** The limit floors the four-person 60% amount ($80,165), applies the size factor, then floors to the month; this reproduces all 13 Tier II cells and equals the IM annual figures divided by 12 and floored. No source states the rounding order. The 0.6 rate is restated in `smi_rate` as the state's election.
10. **Household and period mapping (simplification).** The SPM unit stands in for the 393.4(b) economic unit, with no rebuttal of the relationship presumption. Annual income divided by 12 stands in for "gross income for the month of application" (weekly and biweekly conversion, year-to-date averaging of interest and IRA draws, and known changes in D.14 are not modeled). Ages are read in the model year rather than "on the application date". Foster care and the SSI living arrangement are read in January. Calendar 2026 stands in for the 2025-2026 season.
11. **Self-employment and rents (simplification).** D.12(a)(5) counts "Net profit from self-employment, (after allowable deductions)" by the manual's 12-month or 3-month methods with its own non-allowable list; the draft uses the model's net inputs floored at zero per source. Rents are counted as the `rental_income` input without the manual's deduction list.
12. **Disability (simplification).** B.3(b)(3) is applied through `is_usda_disabled`; a permanent-disability flag alone does not qualify (`payment/ny_heap_vulnerable.yaml` Case 1, seventh household). The plan's "permanently disabled" wording is broader than the manual's receipt-based list.
13. **Heat-included and subsidized households (interpretation).** The matrix shows no vulnerable add-on for heat-included households, so none is paid. A subsidized tenant who pays the vendor directly receives the fuel payment, because F.2(c) and F.3(a) limit the $21 to "heat included in the rent"; `receives_housing_assistance` and `is_in_public_housing` stand in for "Government subsidized housing". Group settings are an input because no existing input identifies them.
14. **FY2024 and FY2025 (encoded 2026-10-06).** The base amounts, the $35 vulnerable add-on and the $21, $45 and $50 heat-included levels are unchanged across the FY2024 to FY2026 matrices; only the Tier I add-on moved, $41 in FY2023 and FY2024 and $61 from FY2025 (tests 21 and 22). The FY2024 and FY2025 limits and Tier I lines reproduce from the lagged guidelines and the model's FFY2024 and FFY2025 state median income values (tests 17 and 22); those SMI tables were not re-read for this issue.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-ny-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ny-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)

Manifest presence is not proof that all attachments are captured, the source is complete, or it is admitted in the corpus release pinned by rulespec-us. Verify the signed release and fill the actual gaps rather than duplicating existing ingestion. The HEAP Manual, the 2023-2024 to 2025-2026 benefit matrices (and the 2022-2023 matrix for the $41 Tier I add-on), 18 NYCRR Part 393, the 2023 poverty guideline and the FFY2024 to FFY2026 SMI tables require source/admission reconciliation; reuse the 2024/2025 notices from axiom-corpus#778. Remaining missing sources need ingest with URL, date and hash provenance (the manual from the archived capture named above).

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-ny/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover published income limits and large-household boundaries for FY2024 to FY2026, all fuel/payment mappings, heat-in-rent, the Tier I ($41, then $61) and vulnerability supplements, foster/SSI exclusions, the living-alone Code A test, the Medicare Part B deduction, mixed-status households, categorical receipt/take-up, and disability pathways. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: Encode Texas's SSI supplement for Medicaid facility residents (HR Code 32.024(w); MEPD H-1500, H-6000): $45 to each SSI recipient on the $30 reduced benefit, including each spouse (PE #10145)

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Encoding debt

Texas's state supplement for SSI recipients in Medicaid long-term care facilities has no RuleSpec module. `rulespec-us` `origin/main` (`d0d45efe5`) has no `us-tx/statutes/` modules at all; `us-tx/policies/` covers only the Texas Works handbook (A-1340, C-110) and a CMS page.

PolicyEngine-US models the program as `tx_ssi_state_supplement` = personal needs allowance − the $30 reduced federal SSI benefit, gated by `tx_ssi_state_supplement_eligible`. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10145 fixes a bug there: eligibility read the SSI "eligible individual" label, which is false for the tax-unit-spouse member of an SSI couple, so only one spouse of a married SSI couple in a facility was paid. The handbook pays each SSI recipient on the reduced benefit, and a couple in a facility gets the $60 reduced couple standard, $30 each. Axiom cannot adjudicate this today.

## Rule (verbatim)

**Texas Human Resources Code 32.024(w).** Corpus path `us-tx/statute/hr/32.024`, axiom-corpus ingest `us-tx/statute/2026-10-06-w6-benefits-ssi-statute-us-tx-title-hr-r2026-10-07-consolidated` (the path follows `axiom_corpus/corpus/states.py`, `f"us-tx/statute/{code}/{section}"`; confirm whether the ingest also has a `/w` subsection row before dispatch). Source: https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/HR/htm/HR.32.htm#32.024, read 2026-10-12.

> (w) The executive commissioner shall set a personal needs allowance of not less than $75 a month for a resident of a convalescent or nursing facility or related institution licensed under Chapter 242, Health and Safety Code, assisted living facility, ICF-IID facility, or other similar long-term care facility who receives medical assistance. The commission may send the personal needs allowance directly to a resident who receives Supplemental Security Income (SSI) (42 U.S.C. Section 1381 et seq.). This subsection does not apply to a resident who is participating in a medical assistance waiver program administered by the commission.

**1 Texas Administrative Code §358.381(c)** (adopted effective September 1, 2009, 34 TexReg 5497). Not in axiom-corpus yet (there is no `us-tx/regulation` ingest); proposed path `us-tx/regulation/1-tac/358.381`, following `us-co/regulation/8-ccr-1403-1/3.111` (confirm before dispatch). Source: https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/1-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-358-381, read 2026-10-12. This is the binding rule for the supplement; H-1500 and H-6000 implement it.

> (c) A person in an institutional setting may retain a personal needs allowance (PNA) in an amount set by the HHSC executive commissioner in accordance with Chapter 32 of the Texas Human Resources Code.
> (1) The PNA is not applied toward the cost of medical assistance furnished in an institutional setting.
> (2) For a person receiving the reduced SSI federal benefit rate, HHSC issues a supplement to give the person a PNA at the minimum level set by the HHSC executive commissioner.

**HHSC Medicaid for the Elderly and People with Disabilities (MEPD) Handbook.** Not in axiom-corpus yet (the only `us-tx/manual` ingest is the Texas Works handbook). Read 2026-10-12.

H-1500, Personal Needs Allowance (Revision 24-1, effective March 1, 2024), https://www.hhs.texas.gov/handbooks/medicaid-elderly-people-disabilities-handbook/h-1500-personal-needs-allowance:

> SSI recipients who live in an institutional setting and receive the $30 reduced federal benefit receive a state supplement. This ensures they receive a PNA equal to the minimum level established by the state.
> Beginning Jan.1, 2024, the PNA is $75.
> From Jan. 1, 2006, through Dec. 31, 2023, the PNA was $60.

H-6000, Co-Payment for SSI Cases (Revision 26-1, effective March 1, 2026), https://www.hhs.texas.gov/handbooks/medicaid-elderly-people-disabilities-handbook/h-6000-co-payment-ssi-cases:

> Note: The reduced SSI payment standard is $30.
> Note: HHSC supplements the reduced SSI payment standard by $45 per month to ensure SSI recipients also have a $75 personal needs allowance.
> If both spouses enter the Medicaid medical facility and Medicaid makes substantial payments for each spouse, SSA lowers the SSI payment standard to the reduced standard for a couple ($60) for the months after the month of entry.

External confirmation for couples: SSA, *State Assistance Programs for SSI Recipients, January 2011 — Texas*, Table 1, Medicaid facility, note a: "Couples residing in this living arrangement for more than 30 days are treated as two individuals." (https://www.ssa.gov/policy/docs/progdesc/ssi_st_asst/2011/tx.html)

## Plan

**Step 1. Ingest** 1 TAC §358.381 (path above), and MEPD H-1500 and H-6000 into axiom-corpus as `us-tx/manual/hhs/medicaid-elderly-people-disabilities-handbook/h-1500-personal-needs-allowance` and `.../h-6000-co-payment-ssi-cases`, following the Texas Works handbook ingest.

**Step 2. Encode** `us-tx/statutes/hr/32.024/w.yaml` (or `us-tx/statutes/hr/32.024.yaml` if the ingest has no subsection row) through the signed encoder. Paste this as `review_finding`:

> Encode Texas Human Resources Code 32.024(w) (corpus us-tx/statute/hr/32.024, subsection (w)) as a Person-level module. Required outputs, each with verbatim proof excerpts:
> 1. A Money parameter: the statutory minimum personal needs allowance, $75 a month.
> 2. A Judgment: the resident is covered by (w), i.e. a resident of a facility licensed under Chapter 242 Health and Safety Code, an assisted living facility, an ICF-IID facility or a similar long-term care facility, who receives medical assistance, and who is not participating in a medical assistance waiver program administered by the commission. Use leaf inputs that state exactly those facts.
> 3. A Judgment: the commission may send the allowance directly to the resident, which holds when (2) holds and the resident receives SSI.
>
> Companion tests: A. SSI recipient on medical assistance in a nursing facility, no waiver: (2) and (3) hold. B. Same resident in a waiver program: (2) not_holds. C. Married couple, both SSI recipients on medical assistance in a nursing facility: (2) and (3) hold for each spouse; the allowance is per resident.

**Step 3. Encode** the handbook supplement as `us-tx/policies/hhs/medicaid-elderly-people-disabilities-handbook/h-1500-personal-needs-allowance.yaml`, importing the $75 minimum from step 2. Paste this as `review_finding`:

> Encode MEPD Handbook H-1500 with H-6000 (corpus us-tx/manual/hhs/medicaid-elderly-people-disabilities-handbook/h-1500-personal-needs-allowance and h-6000-co-payment-ssi-cases) as a Person-level module. Required outputs:
> 1. A Money parameter, the PNA, with versions $45 from 1999-09-01, $60 from 2001-09-01, $45 from 2003-09-01, $60 from 2006-01-01 and $75 from 2024-01-01 (H-1500). H-1500 also says "Before that, PNA was $30", so there is no supplement before 1999-09-01. PolicyEngine starts that $30 at 1988-07-01 as a modeling choice: it is the federal $30 minimum's effective date (42 USC 1396a(q)(2); Pub. L. 100-203 §9119(d)(2)), not a Texas date, and the sources give no Texas start. The dates are benefit months; the dated sources are in the table at the end of this issue.
> 2. A Money parameter, the reduced SSI payment standard, $30 (H-6000).
> 3. A Judgment, state supplement eligible: the person is an SSI recipient who lives in an institutional setting and receives the $30 reduced federal benefit (H-1500; 1 TAC 358.381(c)(2): "a person receiving the reduced SSI federal benefit rate"). Couples are not aggregated: when both spouses are in the facility each receives $30 of the $60 couple standard (H-6000), so each is evaluated alone.
> 4. A Money output, the monthly state supplement: PNA − reduced SSI payment standard if (3) holds, else 0 ($45 from 2024, H-6000). H-6000 states it as a fixed amount on the reduced standard, and no Texas source subtracts the recipient's own income from it. H-6000 separately has workers check SSI recipients for other income and calculate a co-payment.
>
> Companion tests: A. Single SSI recipient in a Medicaid facility on the $30 reduced benefit, 2024: holds, $45. B. Married couple, both in the facility on the $60 couple standard, 2024: each holds, $45 each ($90 for the couple). C. Facility resident who receives no SSI (for example above the resource limit): not_holds, 0. D. 2023: $60 − $30 = $30. E. 2011: $30, not the $60 in SSA's 2007-2011 tables (H-6000 Rev. 09-4 and 11-2). F. August 2001: $15; September 2001: $30. G. August 2003: $30; September 2003: $15. H. 1998: $0. I. 2024 resident with a $40/month pension (countable income $20, federal SSI $10): holds, $45.

**Step 4. Oracle coverage.** Map step 3's outputs to PolicyEngine-US `tx_ssi_state_supplement_eligible` and `tx_ssi_state_supplement` (monthly).

PolicyEngine-side tests with the same ground truth: `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/tx/hhsc/ssi_state_supplement/integration.yaml` Scenarios 6, 9 and 10 in PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10145. Dated amounts and the income cases: `tx_ssi_state_supplement.yaml` in PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10148. Cases 4-13 cover each period; Cases 17-27 are monthly cases at each change and are the natural companions to output 1's versions; Cases 14-16 and 28 compute SSI from real inputs, including a resident with both a pension and earnings.

## Dated history (resolved 2026-10-12 in PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10148)

Earlier versions of this issue noted that SSA's 2011 Texas table ($60 state, $90 combined) conflicts with H-1500's $60 PNA. HHSC's own records settle it: the supplement was $30 in 2007-2011, and the PE parameter is right for every period.

| Benefit months | PNA | Supplement | Texas source (quoted) |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| before Sept. 1999 | $30 | $0 | H-1500: "Before that, PNA was $30." |
| Sept. 1999 - Aug. 2001 | $45 | $15 | 25 TexReg 558 (Jan. 28, 2000), 40 TAC §15.450: "the state will supplement their incomes by $15 per month so they also have $45 for personal use", "retroactive to September 1, 1999" |
| Sept. 2001 - Aug. 2003 | $60 | $30 | DHS MEH Revision Notice 02-1 (Dec. 21, 2001), "Personal Needs Allowance - Effective September 1, 2001": "the state will supplement their incomes by $30 per month" ([archive](https://web.archive.org/web/20020504200936/http://www.dhs.state.tx.us:80/handbooks/archives/meh/02-1/memo.htm)) |
| Sept. 2003 - Dec. 2005 | $45 | $15 | H.B. 2292 (2003) §2.207: "not less than $45 [$60]"; MEH item 3250: "supplements the reduced SSI payment standard by $15 per month" ([archive](https://web.archive.org/web/20030910100110/http://www.dhs.state.tx.us:80/handbooks/meh/3000/3250.htm)) |
| Jan. 2006 - Dec. 2023 | $60 | $30 | MEPD H-6000, Rev. 09-4 (Dec. 2009) and Rev. 11-2 (June 2011): "HHSC supplements the reduced SSI payment standard by $30 per month so that SSI persons also have a $60 personal needs allowance" ([archive](https://web.archive.org/web/20100126020411/http://www.dads.state.tx.us/handbooks/mepd/H/H-6000.htm)) |
| from Jan. 2024 | $75 | $45 | H.B. 54 (2023); HHSC Information Letter 2023-45: "Starting in January 2024, the state PNA supplemental payment will increase from $30 to $45 per person." |

SSA's *State Assistance Programs* tables agree for January 2002 ($15), 2004 and 2005 ($15) and 2006 ($30). They are wrong in two places. Their January 2007-2011 state amount is $60, which equals the PNA, not the $30 supplement. Their January 2002 report dates the $15-to-$30 increase September 2002; HHSC's notice makes it September 2001.

**Income.** No Texas source reduces the supplement by countable income. For an individual on the reduced standard with countable income c ≤ $30, PNA − federal SSI − c = PNA − (30 − c) − c = PNA − 30, so that reading gives the same amount. SSA's "whose countable income is less than $60" has no Texas counterpart. Texas pays only SSI recipients: "State supplementation will not be allowed for a Medicaid recipient who is not an SSI recipient" (MEPD item 3233.1, 2008).

**Open conflict for the encoder.** HHSC IL 2023-45 says: "Individuals who receive a Retirement, Survivors, and Disability Insurance (RSDI) benefit, are not eligible to receive a PNA supplemental payment from HHSC." For residents who receive both RSDI and SSI (RSDI under $50 a month), this conflicts with 1 TAC 358.381(c)(2). PolicyEngine follows the rule. An encoding of output (3) should cite the rule and record the letter as a conflicting source, not silently add an RSDI exclusion.

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Alabama LIHEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 2a, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9967 (branch `al-liheap`), open and ready for review, not merged. DTrim99 requested changes on 2026-10-14 at `25dd283aa1`; head `af334f5714` (2026-10-15) answered that review, and PavelMakarchuk approved it with comments on 2026-10-19 (S5 and suggestions G7-G14). Head `af935eca5d` (2026-10-19) addresses Pavel's review; DTrim99's re-review is pending. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **Sources missing from the corpus.** No axiom-corpus manifest on `main` holds the branch's main source, the ADECA LIHEAP Policy Manual effective October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026 (household, income, housing and benefit rules); `us-al-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml` holds the edition effective October 1, 2024 to February 16, 2025 (PY2025 chart). Also missing: the 2025 HHS poverty guidelines behind every FY2026 limit and level (`us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml` holds the 2026 ones), the 2024 guidelines, the FY2025 and draft FY2027 state plans, Pub. L. 117-58 (the IIJA appropriation) and the HHS award record. These need ingest before the modules below can be proved.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-06, 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-19; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.
- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9967 is not merged: head `af935eca5d` addresses PavelMakarchuk's review and DTrim99's re-review is pending, so there is no revision to pin.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9967, branch `al-liheap` (status under Objective). Head `af935eca5d` (2026-10-19) addresses Pavel's review of `af334f5714`: `payment/al_liheap_base_payment` raises the level with `max_(band, 1)` (results unchanged); new cases pin a $0 chart amount for FUEL_OIL, UNSPECIFIED, SOLAR, OTHER and NONE and the size 5 and 15 level tops; countable Cases 16 and 17 now also change the award under the bug each targets; a new `integration.yaml` runs five households end to end; comments, two descriptions and four reference titles were reworded, and the household-size reference now cites pages 6-7, 13 and 22. Everything below describes `af935eca5d`; oracle fixtures will pin the merged commit.
- **Scope:** Alabama LIHEAP Regular Heating Assistance for the FY2026 heating season: residence, qualified household size, gross countable income, the 150% limit, three income levels, the Appendix D chart (over four paid as four), heating responsibility (heat in rent, subsidized housing), the HUD utility allowance deduction and the $100 Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) supplement through FY2026. Out of scope: Regular Cooling, Crisis Heating and Crisis Cooling, weatherization, equipment purchase or repair, the optional $50 for high energy need (a local agency decision), pre-pay crisis amounts, and tribal LIHEAP households.
- **Policy periods:** one verified season, FY2026 (PY2026) heating, October 1, 2025 to April 30, 2026 (plan item 1.1, page 4; manual section 3, page 9). Alabama variables are annual and read 1 January values, so period `2026` is FY2026 on the 2025 HHS guidelines (`fpg_year_lag` 1), as plan item 2.5 states. Nine parameter files hold one `2025-10-01` entry; `payment/iija_supplement.yaml` holds $100 from `2025-10-01` and $0 from `2026-10-01`. `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2026"`. Periods `2025` (2024 guidelines) and `2027` (2026 guidelines, no supplement) are unverified estimates reproducing the PY2025 chart (corpus-edition manual) and the May 15, 2026 chart (draft FY2027 plan; interpretation 13).
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/al/adeca/liheap/`: `al_liheap`, `al_liheap_household_size`; `eligibility/al_liheap_eligible`, `al_liheap_income_limit`; `income/al_liheap_countable_income`; `payment/al_liheap_base_payment`, `al_liheap_income_band`. No new input variable.
- **Parameters:** 10 files under `gov.states.al.adeca.liheap`: `eligibility/` `fpg_rate` (1.5) and `fpg_year_lag` (1); `income/` `earned_income_min_age` (18), `sources/earned` (5 sources) and `sources/unearned` (20); `payment/` `base_amount`, `income_band_reduction`, `additional_person_amount`, `maximum_payment_household_size` and `iija_supplement` (values under Required outputs). Plus a `programs.yaml` entry and a changelog fragment.
- **Tests:** 55 YAML cases in 8 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/al/adeca/liheap/` at head `af935eca5d` (`al_liheap.yaml` 10, `al_liheap_household_size.yaml` 2, `eligibility/al_liheap_eligible.yaml` 11, `eligibility/al_liheap_income_limit.yaml` 2, `income/al_liheap_countable_income.yaml` 18, `integration.yaml` 5, `payment/al_liheap_base_payment.yaml` 4, `payment/al_liheap_income_band.yaml` 3). Every case sends `heating_type`. The tests were not run locally; CI validates them.

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence on axiom-corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-06 (`e16ccb799f`; GitHub API and per-URL search), 2026-10-15 (`2137e79bec`) and 2026-10-19 (`e019e44563`; full manifest list, with the Alabama LIHEAP, poverty-guideline, SSP, SSI and UI manifests unchanged); the signed release was not checked. rulespec-us `main` (`874bce4fea`, 2026-10-19) has `us-al/policies/` (cms, dhr, income_tax), `us-al/regulations/` and `us-al/statutes/`, but no ADECA, LIHEAP or UI module and no `us/` poverty-guideline module; the paths below follow that layout. Pages are physical PDF pages (FY2026 manual: printed footer + 4); the manual manifest's `page-N` suffix counts text-bearing pages only.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-al/policies/adeca/liheap-policy-manual/fy2026/section-2/definitions` | Household and size at application (page 6); mixed-status households, qualified and non-qualified non-residents, the exception for a non-qualified parent of qualified children (page 7); resident (page 8) | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. ## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Income-level rounding and cents (inferred).** The plan states the method (“$1,956 by 3 = $652”; “$653 + $652 = $1,305”) but no rounding rule. Nearest-dollar rounding with halves up reproduces the 15 limits and 8 level tops of the PY2025, PY2026 and May 15, 2026 charts. Rounding down fails (2,643.75 prints $2,644; 4,019 / 3 = 1,339.67 prints $1,340), and the FY2025 plan's “$22,590 by 12 = $1,883” (1,882.50) rounds the half up. The unprinted size 5 and 15 tops of test 4 rest on this rounding (1,568.67 rounds up, 3,860.33 down). The whole-dollar ranges leave a gap between $652 and $653; the branch puts amounts above a top in the next level, so $652.01 a month is level 2 (`payment/al_liheap_income_band.yaml` Cases 1 to 3).
2. **Monthly test from annual inputs (simplification).** The rule tests gross income “for the month prior to the month of application” (pages 13, 17, 21). The branch compares annual income with 12 times the monthly limit and divides by 12 for the level.
3. **Household (simplification).** The SPM unit stands in for the economic unit on page 6. Size counts `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`, which adds conditional entrants (not named in the manual) and has no status for the battered or trafficking-victim categories on page 7. The page 7 and 4(b) applicant exception reduces to `size > 0`: any unit with one qualified member is eligible. Non-custodial children (5.4, 6.1.5) count in size (no custody input). Temporary absence for work or school (page 6) is not modeled.
4. **Subsidized and public housing with a bill (interpretation).** A positive `heating_expense` stands in for “proof of out-of-pocket utility expenses” and for a public housing “excess charge” (page 21): `eligibility/al_liheap_eligible.yaml` Case 7 (public housing, heat in rent, a $120 electric bill) is eligible; with a $0 bill the unit is not (Case 11, test 6(e)).
5. **HUD utility allowance (interpretation, owner's call).** The branch subtracts `hud_utility_allowance` / 12 from the chart amount, floored at $0, and pays the $100 only if something remains. The plan pays the supplement “Each time a household receives a Heating benefit” without saying whether a regular payment reduced to $0 is one: `al_liheap.yaml` Case 3, units 4 to 6 (allowances of $440, $450 and $600 a month against $440), pays $0. The deduction is not limited to subsidized tenants, although page 21 places it under 6.1.1. The input is $0 unless supplied and household-level, so two SPM units in one household would each lose the full allowance.
6. **Supplement funding, size and end (interpretation).** “if funding is available” is taken as met for FY2026 because award 2601ALLIEI exists. Its $1,359,705 covers about 13,600 supplements across heating and cooling; the model assumes the funds last, overstating funded awards in population totals. Plan 2.6's “$580” maximum is the largest chart cell ($530) plus the optional $50; the model's largest FY2026 award is $630. The supplement is $0 from 2026-10-01: the draft FY2027 plan (section 2.5) omits the IIJA sentence and IIJA's last tranche was FY2026 (135 Stat. 1412), although the award runs to 09/30/2027. By 2026-10-19 no final FY2027 plan was published (no Clearinghouse copy; ADECA still posts the Saved draft); if the accepted plan restores the sentence, the `2026-10-01` entry should revert. Period 2025 keeps $100 (same FY2025 plan sentence; FY2025 funding not checked).
7. **Optional $50 (not modeled).** Pages 23 and 57 and plan page 10 leave it to the local agency; no input carries that decision.
8. **Fuels without a column (coverage limit).** `heating_type` is a required input. Manual 3.1 names six fuels; FUEL_OIL, SOLAR, OTHER and UNSPECIFIED have no chart column and pay $0, though the unit can test eligible. A heat-in-rent household must also send its fuel. KEROSENE bills are read from `fuel_oil_expense`, as `heating_expense` pairs them; 3.1 names kerosene, not fuel oil. Issue 9754 (policyengine-us) tracks the unspecified default. `al_liheap.yaml` Case 9 ($6,000 of wages with FUEL_OIL and a $1,200 bill, or with UNSPECIFIED heat in unsubsidized rent) is eligible with chart $0 and award $0 (the supplement needs a positive regular payment); `payment/al_liheap_base_payment.yaml` Case 4 pins chart $0 for FUEL_OIL, UNSPECIFIED, SOLAR, OTHER and NONE across sizes 1 to 4 and all three levels.
9. **Stale manual example.** The page 22 example pays “$410” to an electric household of four with income of $1,000; the chart (page 57) gives $470 for that row in both PY2025 and PY2026. The branch follows the chart; do not use the example's $410 or $310 as expected values.
10. **Plan and manual conflicts (the branch follows the manual).** Lump sums: plan 1.9 checks “One-time lump-sum payments, such as rebates/credits, winnings from lotteries, refund deposits, etc.”; the manual excludes “Income tax refunds”, “Lump-sum inheritances” and “One-time insurance payments” and counts “Net gambling or lottery winnings”. The branch counts net gambling winnings and no refunds or rebates. Insurance: plan 1.9 leaves “Insurance payments made directly to the insured” unchecked; the manual counts “Regular insurance or annuity payments” and “Workers’ compensation insurance”. The branch counts `pension_income`, `disability_benefits` and `workers_compensation`. “General Assistance benefits” (unchecked, not in the manual) is not counted. Plan “Income from employment through Workforce Investment Act (WIA)” is checked.
11. **Social Security gross (Alabama's rule).** Plan 1.9 checks “Including MediCare deduction” (render) and the manual counts receipts “before taxes” with no Medicare netting, so the branch counts `social_security` as is and subtracts no `medicare_part_b_premium` (test 16(a)).
12. **Income simplifications.** Self-employment uses the model's net inputs with no further deduction (“Net receipts from non-farm or farm self-employment”). Each source is floored at zero and gambling is netted, per member (settled). `estate_income` stands for “Periodic receipts from estates or trusts” and `financial_assistance` for “Financial support from family or friends”. Interest counts in full. Unemployment compensation is the reported amount, else modeled Alabama UI (monetary eligibility and regular benefits only). Training stipends, military family allotments, royalties, severance pay, contract income outside self-employment and WIA earnings have no input and are not counted. TANF is read through the take-up-gated `tanf` (settled).
13. **Years and dates.** All parameters start at `2025-10-01` (the supplement drops to $0 at `2026-10-01`), but the chart on the 2025 guidelines took effect February 17, 2025 (Clearinghouse header) and the one on the 2026 guidelines May 15, 2026 (draft FY2027 plan page 53), after the FY2026 heating season. Annual periods read 1 January values, so these dates change no annual result; a monthly encoding would need both, and the unaccepted draft adopts the 2027 guidelines on release.
14. **Other gaps, kept explicit.** Applicant rules 4(c), (d), (g) and (h), the once-per-season limit, priority periods for vulnerable households, tribal LIHEAP households (page 5) and pre-pay accounts are not modeled. Plan 2.3's No for subsidized renters and utilities in rent agrees with manual 6.1.1 through rule 4(f): only tenants with no out-of-pocket cost are denied.
15. **Alabama State Supplementary Payment (user decision, 2026-10-07).** The branch counts `al_ssp` in full, every category, beside `ssi`. Section 5.5.1 counts cash receipts “from all sources”; its SSA row names Supplemental Security Income, and the SSP, paid from state funds and administered by the Department of Human Resources (rules 660-2-4-.01 and .02), counts as an unlisted source. Page 18 excludes “Foster care benefits”; the branch reads that as payments for the care of a foster child, matching the unchecked plan 1.9 box “Funds received by household for the care of a foster child”, so the $110 supplement to an adult living in a foster home counts. The plan has no state-supplement box.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-al-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-al-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [us-al-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-al-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml)
- [us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml)
- [us-al-admin-code-660-2-4.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-al-admin-code-660-2-4.yaml) and [us-ssa-cola-2026-official-documents.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ssa-cola-2026-official-documents.yaml) (SSP and SSI amounts, tests 15, 16 and 20)
- [us-al-benefits-w6-ui-statute.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-al-benefits-w6-ui-statute.yaml) (Alabama UI law, test 17)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-al/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the FY2026 limits for sizes 1 to 15 and the inclusive ceiling, the income levels at every printed boundary for sizes 1 to 4 and the plan-method boundaries for sizes 5 and 15, all 48 chart cells and the four-person rule, the shared wood, coal and kerosene column and fuels without a column, heat in rent, subsidized or public housing and the NONE heating type, the HUD deduction before the $100 supplement and its end on 2026-10-01, mixed-status households, the under-18 earned-income exclusion, every listed unearned source (reported or modeled UI, gross Social Security, the Alabama SSP with SSI), SSI under the income test, per-source loss floors, TANF take-up, and any 2025 or 2027 period kept in scope. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: pe-parity: SSA 2027 COLA (3.6%) and automatic determinations (PE-US #10225)

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
PolicyEngine-US PR: https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/pull/10225 (SSA's 2027 COLA and automatic determinations, announced 2026-10-14).

## Modules to add

Each module mirrors its 2026 counterpart from #40 and the 2026 COLA module.

| Module | Corpus citation (needs ingest) | Required 2027 output |
|---|---|---|
| `us/policies/ssa/cola/2027.yaml` | `us/guidance/ssa/cola/2027/block-1` | `social_security_cola_2027_applicable_increase_percentage` = 0.036 |
| `us/policies/ssa/contribution-and-benefit-base/2027.yaml` | `us/guidance/ssa/contribution-and-benefit-base/2027/block-1` | contribution and benefit base = 192,300 |
| `us/policies/ssa/quarter-of-coverage/2027.yaml` | `us/guidance/ssa/quarter-of-coverage/2027/block-1` | quarter of coverage amount = 1,970 |
| `us/policies/ssa/retirement-earnings-test/2027.yaml` | `us/guidance/ssa/retirement-earnings-test/2027/block-1` | under FRA: $25,560/yr ($2,130/mo); year reaching FRA: $67,920/yr ($5,660/mo) |
| `us/policies/ssa/substantial-gainful-activity/2027.yaml` | `us/guidance/ssa/substantial-gainful-activity/2027/block-1` | non-blind $1,770/mo; blind $2,950/mo |
| `us/policies/ssa/pia-bend-points/2027.yaml` | `us/guidance/ssa/pia-bend-points/2027/block-1` | first and second bend points (official values not yet captured; see blockers) |

**Computation-year AWI.** The 2026 modules compute from `computation_year_average_wage_index` = 69,846.57, which is AWI(2024). The 2027 modules need AWI(2025), published 2026-10-14 at https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/AWI.html. The announced amounts limit it to roughly 72,772–72,837. That range is consistent with the 192,300 base under 42 USC 430(b), the 1,970 quarter of coverage under 42 USC 413(d)(2), and the earnings test and SGA amounts.

**SSI.** The year-general `us/statutes/42/1382f/a` takes the applicable increase percentage as an input. With the 2027 COLA of 3.6%, it should yield the announced 2027 federal payment standard: $1,029 individual and $1,544 couple per month.

## Sources

- **2027 COLA fact sheet:** https://www.ssa.gov/news/en/cola/factsheets/2027.html (COLA, base, quarter of coverage, earnings test, SGA, SSI amounts, student exclusion $2,500/mo and $10,080/yr)
- **SSA press release:** https://www.ssa.gov/news/en/press/releases/2026-10-14.html
- **OACT pages:**
  - https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html
  - https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/QC.html
  - https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/rtea.html
  - https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/sga.html
  - https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/bendpoints.html
  - https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/AWI.html
- **COLA check:** the BLS CPI-W series CWUR0000SA0 gives a July–September 2026 average of 328.746 (327.104, 328.481, 330.654). Over the 2025Q3 average of 317.265 that is 1.0362, which rounds to 3.6%.

## Companion tests

Use the same external source as PE-US #10225's `test_social_security_parameters_include_latest_official_2027_values`, which is the 2027 fact sheet:

- COLA 0.036
- Base 192,300
- Quarter of coverage 1,970
- Earnings test 25,560 / 67,920
- SGA 1,770 / 2,950
- SSI 1,029 / 1,544

Add the bend-point cases once the official values are captured.

## Blockers

1. **Corpus:** the 2027 SSA guidance was published 2026-10-14 and is not in the pinned corpus release. Each `us/guidance/ssa/*/2027` path needs ingest, and so does the AWI series row for 2025.
2. **Source text:** ssa.gov returned 403 to every automated request from our network on 2026-10-14. We could not capture the source text verbatim. The values above come from SSA's fact sheet as indexed by search, and each one checks out against the statutory indexing formulas. The verbatim excerpts for the proof atoms must come from the ingested pages.
3. **Encoder approval:** each billed signed-encoder run needs separate approval.
