items.body:
## Objective

Ship Georgia LIHEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 2a, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9968 (branch `ga-liheap`), open, not merged; DTrim99 approved `c60610f7f7` (2026-10-20) and PavelMakarchuk `10ff85eddb` (2026-10-21). Head `a9dae48466` (2026-10-21). The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

- **Sources need ingest.** The payment amounts, Level I cutoffs and printed limits come only from the FY2025 and FY2026 Georgia Benefit Matrix PDFs, in no axiom-corpus manifest on `main` (`liheap-agent-queue.yaml`: `matrix_status: absent`). Also in no manifest: the FY2025 state plan, the FY2025 and FY2026 HHS state median income and poverty guideline tables (IM 2024-02 and IM 2025-02, Attachments 4 and 2), the FY2024 matrix, the PAMMS export and the DFCS page. 42 U.S.C. 8624 is in a statute ingest scope, not a manifest. The FY2026 plan and the 2022 manual are in manifests.
- **Release admission not checked.** Presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not checked for any source.
- **Encoder approval.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval. No Georgia run has been approved or started.
- **No merged oracle revision.** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9968 is approved but not merged, so there is no revision to pin.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9968, open, not merged. Branch `ga-liheap`, head `a9dae48466` (comment wording and main). Since PavelMakarchuk's 2026-10-20 review, a main heating fuel bill, like an electric bill, overrides the direct payment (`ga_liheap.yaml` Cases 23, 24; matrix Case 8; no prior expectation changed), and the income files start 2024-10-01; the source lists and minimum age cite FY2025 plan item 1.9 (same values). Everything below describes `a9dae48466`.
- **Scope:** Georgia LIHEAP regular heating assistance: residence, the 60% of state median income test with the federal 110% poverty floor, household size without nonqualified noncitizens, countable income, the energy-burden test (heat in rent, subsidized housing), and Benefit Matrix step 1 (Level I or II by size and income) and step 2 (amount by main heating fuel), with the level's lowest amount when rent includes all utilities and no separate bill is reported (plan page 30). Out of scope: crisis assistance and pre-pay crisis rules, cooling and the matrix “COOLING BENEFIT” column, weatherization, cooling units, heating equipment, the PSC Energy Assistance and Senior Match components, categorical eligibility, the $1,000 utility-credit screen, and the elderly and homebound priority period.
- **Policy periods:** Program year N is federal fiscal year N (October 1 of N-1 to September 30 of N); each Georgia variable is annual and reads the value in force on 1 January, so period 2025 is FY2025 and 2026 is FY2026. `payment/lower_income_limit` has `2024-10-01` and `2025-10-01` values (the two matrices); the limit reads `gov.hhs.smi.amount` (Georgia $105,893 from `2024-10-01`, $110,736 from `2025-10-01`). `eligibility/fpg_year_lag` (1 from `2024-10-01`) makes the floor read the prior calendar year's guidelines, which HHS makes mandatory for the fiscal year. `eligibility/smi_rate`, `payment/base_amount`, `payment/lower_income_uplift`, `payment/maximum_table_size` and the four `income/` files start at `2024-10-01` (FY2025 prints the same values as FY2026; the manual dates from January 2022). The registry records `verified_years: "2025-2026"`; 2027 and later are unverified estimates (interpretation 20), with only a draft FY2027 plan (“Report Status: Saved”) and no FY2027 matrix found.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/ga/dfcs/liheap/`: `ga_liheap`; `ga_liheap_household_size`; `eligibility/ga_liheap_eligible`, `eligibility/ga_liheap_income_limit`; `income/ga_liheap_income`; `payment/ga_liheap_matrix_amount`. `eligibility/_ga_liheap_housing.py` holds the two route functions, which YAML cannot assert. The limit calls the shared helper in `variables/gov/hhs/hhs_smi.py` (`gov.hhs.smi`); eligibility calls `fpg` in `variables/gov/hhs/tax_unit_fpg.py` (`gov.hhs.fpg`).
- **Parameters:** `gov.states.ga.dfcs.liheap` (`eligibility/smi_rate` 0.6, `eligibility/fpg_year_lag` 1; `income/minimum_age` 18, `income/monthly_interest_disregard` $25, `income/sources/person` (24 sources), `income/sources/household` (`tanf`); `payment/base_amount` (Level II amount for five fuels), `payment/lower_income_limit` (sizes 1 to 16), `payment/lower_income_uplift` $100, `payment/maximum_table_size` 16). 10 files. Federal: the shared `gov.hhs.liheap.fpg_floor` (1.1 from `1985-10-01`, the same file as PR 10279) and the existing `gov.hhs.fpg`.
- **Tests:** 65 YAML cases in 6 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/ga/dfcs/liheap/` (`ga_liheap.yaml` 24, `ga_liheap_household_size.yaml` 2, `eligibility/ga_liheap_eligible.yaml` 12, `eligibility/ga_liheap_income_limit.yaml` 4, `income/ga_liheap_income.yaml` 15, `payment/ga_liheap_matrix_amount.yaml` 8). Every benefit, eligibility and matrix-amount case sets `heating_type`. Not run locally; CI validates them.

## Module paths and corpus citations

Manifest presence on axiom-corpus `main` was checked with `gh api .../contents/manifests/<file>?ref=main` (404 = absent) on 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-15 (`2137e79bec`); presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not checked. rulespec-us (`d8511cca76`) holds `us-ga/policies/dfcs/` (medicaid, snap, tanf) and `us-ga/statutes/`, but no LIHEAP module, `us-ga/regulations/`, `us/statutes/42/8624` or `us/` state median income or poverty guideline module. The manual manifest captures the cited file (89 PDF pages, `pdf_page` granularity, `expression_date: '2022-01-01'`; every page has text, so `page-N` should equal the PDF page, unchecked). The plan manifest captures the FY2026 file (`expression_date: '2025-10-01'`), segmented by headings with `start_after_pattern` matching “Plan Attachments” (pages 1 and 47), so confirm sections 1, 2 and 16 and the page 43 assurances were kept. Its text layer has no check-box states.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-ga/policies/dfcs/liheap-policy-manual/section-100/basic-consideration` | 101.2: the three requirements; one payment per component; amount by annual gross income and size; subsidized housing and renters' bills (pages 3 to 4) | `us-ga/manual/dfcs/liheap-policy-manual` | In manifest `us-ga-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml`. Official copy: [Georgia LIHEAP Policy Manual, revised January 2022, pages 3, 4, 50-52, 56, 57, 62-70, 75, 76, 81-83, 85, 89](https://liheapch.acf.gov/sites/default/files/webfiles/docs/2023/manuals/GA_PolicyManual_2023.pdf#page=3) (all manual pages below). |
| `.../section-1100/basic-eligibility-criteria`, `.../citizenship`, `.../categorically-eligible`, `.../ineligible-households` | 1100.3 (page 50); 1100.4: undocumented adults' income counted, not in size (page 51); 1100.5 a and b: legal and non-legal immigrants and the undocumented-parent note (pages 51 to 52); 1100.12 categorical eligibility (page 56); 1100.14 ineligible households (page 57) | same | In manifest. |
| `.../section-1200/basic-considerations`, `.../calculation-of-income`, `.../income-table` | 1200.1 and 1200.2: all income, under-18 income not considered, ineligible immigrants' income counted (pages 62 to 63); 1200.6 monthly conversion and self-employment (page 64); 1200.7 Include/Exclude table, including “Contribution/ Cash Gift” (pages 65 to 69) | same | In manifest. The Include/Exclude reading rests on the X column position in the text layer. |
| `.../section-1300/payment-methods`, `.../section-1500/glossary`, `.../section-1600/application-instructions` | 1300.2 payment methods (page 70); glossary: categorically eligible, children, household, ineligible households (pages 75 to 76); application items 10, 12, 24, 26 and 27 (pages 81 to 85) | same | In manifest. |
| `.../section-1700/energy-burden-table` | Energy Burden Table: heat situation, burden, type of payment (page 89) | same | In manifest. Multi-line cells: read the non-layout text or the rendered page. |
| `us-ga/policies/dfcs/liheap-benefit-matrix/fy2026` | Step 1 Level I and Level II income ranges for sizes 1 to 16; step 2 heating benefit by main heating fuel for each level | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [Georgia Benefit Matrix, FY2026 income guidelines](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/benefits-matricies/GA_BenefitMatrix_Heat-Cool_2026.pdf) (1 page, PDF created 2025-08-05). |
| `us-ga/policies/dfcs/liheap-benefit-matrix/fy2025` | The same two steps for FY2025 | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [Georgia Benefit Matrix, FY2025 income guidelines](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2025/benefits-matricies/GA_BenefitMatrix_2025.pdf) (1 page, PDF created 2024-08-20). |
| `us-ga/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-1`, `.../section-2`, `.../section-16`, `.../assurances` | 1.4, 1.4a and 1.6 categorical eligibility; 1.8 gross income; 1.9 countable income, including SSA benefits “Excluding MediCare deduction” (pages 5 to 7); 2.1 60% of state median income; 2.3 renters and subsidized housing; 2.5 benefit variables and the fuel-credit rule; 2.6 minimum $400 and maximum $810 (pages 8 to 9); 16.1 lowest benefit for direct payment to the applicant (page 30); assurance (2), the 110% proviso (page 43) | `us-ga/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | In manifest `us-ga-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml`: [FY2026 state plan, pages 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 30, 43](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/state-plans/GA_Plan_2026.pdf#page=5) (report status “Submission Accepted by CO”). |
| `us-ga/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2025/section-1`, `.../section-2`, `.../section-16`, `.../assurances` | 1.9 countable income, with the same boxes as FY2026 (pages 5 to 7); 2.1 60% of state median income (page 8); 2.6 minimum $400 and maximum $810 (page 9); 16.1 the same lowest-benefit sentence (page 30); assurance (2) (page 43) | none | Not in a corpus manifest (`us-ga-liheap-state-plan-fy2025.yaml` is a 404); needs ingest. Official copy: [FY2025 state plan, pages 5 to 9, 30, 43](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2025/state-plans/GA_Plan_2025.pdf#page=5) (Revision 2, report period 10/01/2024 to 09/30/2025). |
| `us/` state median income module (FFY2025 and FFY2026) | Georgia four-person median ($105,893 FFY2025, $110,736 FFY2026), the 60% amounts for sizes 1 to 12, and the footnote size method | none for FFY2025 or FFY2026 | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copies: [LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 4 (FY26 mandatory), pages 1, 3, 4](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_IM2025-02_SMIStateTable_Att4.pdf#page=1) and [LIHEAP IM 2024-02 Attachment 4 (FY25 mandatory), pages 1, 3, 4](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_IM%202024-02_Att4SMITable.pdf#page=1). `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml` holds IM 2026-01 Attachment 4 (FY2027 mandatory), used only by the carried-forward 2027 period. |
| `us/statutes/42/8624/b/2/B` | The 110% poverty floor on income-only exclusion | expected `us/statute/42/8624/b/2/B` | Not in a manifest file; `liheap-agent-queue.yaml` records the statute scope `2026-09-13-liheap-statute-chapter-94-title-42` (42 U.S.C. 8621 to 8630, OLRC release point 119-103). Quoted from [42 U.S.C. 8624, GovInfo, 2023 edition](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2023-title42/html/USCODE-2023-title42-chap94-subchapII-sec8624.htm). |
| `us/` LIHEAP poverty guideline module (FY2025 and FY2026 mandatory) | 110% of the guidelines for sizes 1 to 12 and the increment per further member | none for FY2025 or FY2026 | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest (`us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml` holds only IM 2026-01 Attachment 2, FY2027 mandatory, which backs only the carried-forward 2027 lag). Official copies: [LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 2, page 1](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_IM2025-02_FPGSte-Table_Att2.pdf#page=1) and [LIHEAP IM 2024-02 Attachment 2, page 1](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_IM%202024-02_Att2FPGTables_States.pdf#page=1). |

The matrices print the 60% limits for sizes 1 to 16 (sizes 1 to 12 equal the HHS tables to the dollar), so a module can take the limits from the matrix and cross-check them against HHS. | Output | policyengine-us variable | Entity, period | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Household size | `ga_liheap_household_size` | SPM unit, year | Members who are citizens or qualified noncitizens (`is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`, the 8 USC 1641 list, no waiting-period bar), children included; undocumented and DACA members do not count. |
| Countable income | `ga_liheap_income` | SPM unit, year | For each member aged 18 or over, nonqualified adults included: the 24 person sources in the Inputs line (`employment_income` through `child_support_received`; railroad benefits gross), each floored at zero, plus max(Social Security - `medicare_part_b_premium`, 0). Then max(the adults' total interest - $300, 0) and `tanf` (after take-up), each once per unit. Members under 18 contribute nothing. |
| Income limit | `ga_liheap_income_limit` | SPM unit, year | floor(floor(0.6 x SMI4) x factor(size)), where SMI4 is the HHS Georgia four-person median in force on 1 January ($105,893 for FFY2025, $110,736 for FFY2026) and factor is 0.52 plus 0.16 for each of persons two to six plus 0.03 for each further person; 0 when size is 0. Reproduces all 16 printed limits in each year. |
| Eligible | `ga_liheap_eligible` | SPM unit, year | Georgia only: size > 0, income at or below the limit or below round(1.1 x the HHS poverty guideline for the size, 2) (guideline year = model year - 1; income exactly at the floor fails), `heating_type` not NONE, and an energy burden: `has_heating_expense`, or a positive bill for `heating_type` (even with heat in rent or a subsidy), or the all-utilities-in-rent route (heat in rent, `tenant_pays_utilities` false, rent > 0, no housing assistance, not public housing), or the heat-in-rent electric route (heat in rent, rent > 0, `pre_subsidy_electricity_expense` > 0, subsidized or not, whatever `tenant_pays_utilities` says). |
| Matrix amount | `ga_liheap_matrix_amount` | SPM unit, year | Step 2 amount, not gated by eligibility: the Level II amount for `heating_type` (ELECTRICITY $400, NATURAL_GAS $560, FUEL_OIL $710, PROPANE $580, WOOD $400; every other fuel $0), plus $100 when income is at or below the Level I cutoff for min(size, 16). On the all-utilities-in-rent route with no positive `pre_subsidy_electricity_expense` or bill for `heating_type`, the base is the lowest Level II amount ($400) for any `heating_type` other than NONE, so Level I pays $500; with either bill the main-fuel amount applies (unpriced fuels and UNSPECIFIED: $0). $0 when the base is $0. |
| Benefit | `ga_liheap` | SPM unit, year | `ga_liheap_matrix_amount` when eligible, else 0. Not capped at the bill. |

### SBP companion

[Pavel, October 22](#issuecomment-6349320620): `military_retirement_income` = `military_retirement_pay` + `military_retirement_pay_survivors`, counted once. Existing retiree-only tests are unchanged.

| Case | Inputs | Expected | Derivation |
|---|---|---|---|
| SBP-1 | period 2026; Georgia; one citizen adult aged 62; `military_retirement_pay_survivors` $9,600; no other income; NATURAL_GAS with `gas_expense` $1,200; heat not in rent; no housing assistance; `ssi` 0; `ga_tanf` 0 | income $9,600; limit $34,549; matrix $660; eligible; `ga_liheap` $660 | An SBP annuity is an unearned payment received regularly as a retirement benefit (page 66), and no Exclude row covers it: $9,600. $9,600 is in “$0 - $13589” (size 1): Level I NATURAL GAS $660 (FY2026 matrix). |

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Income limit arithmetic (rounding inferred).** The HHS footnote fixes the order (60% of the four-person median, then the size percentage) but states no rounding. Flooring after each step reproduces all 16 printed limits in FY2025 and FY2026; floor(SMI x factor x 0.6) misses 11 FY2026 and 14 FY2025 sizes by $1 (FY2026 size 2: 45,180, printed 45,179).
2. **Sizes above 16 (coverage limit).** No source prints a size 17 limit or Level I cutoff. The model adds 3 points per person to the limit (size 17: floor(66,441 x 1.65 = 109,627.65) = 109,627) and uses the size 16 Level I cutoff ($42,336) for larger sizes (`ga_liheap.yaml` Case 15: 17 people with $40,000 get $660; matrix Case 7). Both are provisional, and the federal floor ($114,015 for 17 in FY2026, interpretation 21) exceeds that limit.
3. **Size 4 Level I cutoff.** Every printed Level I top is 39.33% of the same size's Level II top except size 4, at 38.33% ($25,469 of $66,441 in FY2026; $24,355 of $63,535 in FY2025). Keep the printed values.
4. **Whole-dollar ranges.** The matrices print whole dollars with no gap rule (“$0 - $13589”, “$13590 - $34549”). The model reads Level I and eligibility as income at or below the printed top, so cents above a top move up a level or fail; branch tests use one cent above.
5. **Level I as Level II plus $100 (inferred pattern).** The branch stores the five Level II amounts and a $100 uplift, which reproduces all ten printed cells on both sheets, but the sheets print two columns, not a rule. Encode the printed columns.
6. **Heat in rent and a separate bill (user decision 2026-10-06; `ga_liheap.yaml` Cases 16, 17, 23, 24; eligible Cases 8, 9; matrix Case 8).** Page 89 row 3 pays an unsubsidized heat-in-rent renter billed for electric through the electric vendor; page 4 makes subsidized renters eligible “if their utility bill is in their name”, and page 57 bars them only if they “cannot verify an energy burden”. Route: heat in rent, rent > 0 and `pre_subsidy_electricity_expense` > 0, subsidized or not, whatever `tenant_pays_utilities` says. Page 57 limits the unsubsidized all-in-rent class to rent with “no separate bill for heating/cooling costs”, so this route and a positive bill for `heating_type` (row 1, “Paid to vendor”) override the all-utilities direct payment (PavelMakarchuk S4, S8). Both pay the main fuel's step 2 amount (the FY2024 note), not the page 30 lowest. One adult at $12,000: natural gas $660 with either bill ($560 at $24,000), electric at $24,000, $400, fuel oil $810, propane $680; UNSPECIFIED and kerosene $0. No rent entered means no route (eligible Case 8, unit 6), which also misses a tenant whose subsidy covers the whole rent.
7. **Rent including all utilities.** The direct-payment route pays the lowest amount only with neither an electric bill nor a bill for `heating_type` (otherwise interpretation 6 applies) and, since the amount does not depend on fuel, pays UNSPECIFIED (the settled exception). Other direct-pay cases (page 89 rows 4 and 7; vendors without an agreement, page 4) have no inputs; they get their main-fuel amount if they report a bill.
8. **Which bill shows an energy burden.** `has_heating_expense` or a positive bill for the selected `heating_type` qualifies, even with heat in rent or a subsidy (companion test 11); an unrelated bill does not (eligible Case 5: natural gas with only an electric bill fails, a $1 gas bill qualifies), as PAMMS page 4 words it. Page 82's public or subsidized housing whose “rent includes utilities” is read as all utilities in rent with no bill of the household's own (pages 4, 57). Heat in rent with a primary-fuel bill (`ga_liheap.yaml` Case 6) resolves in the household's favor. Eligible Case 3, unit 2 (unsubsidized, heat in rent, no bill, no rent) fits neither route; page 89 row 2 needs rent > 0 and `tenant_pays_utilities` false. Plan item 2.3 (page 8) answers No to differing policies for subsidized renters and renters with utilities in rent; the branch follows manual pages 4, 57, 82 and 89.
9. **Fuels without a step 2 row (coverage limit; settled).** `heating_type` is required. Step 2 prices only ELECTRIC, NATURAL GAS, OIL, PROPANE and WOOD, so kerosene, coal, solar, other and unspecified fuels pay $0 on every vendor route (eligible with a bill, paid $0; not a legal denial). Only the all-utilities-in-rent route pays them, with no separate bill; reporting an electric or fuel bill takes the award from $500 to $0 (`ga_liheap.yaml` Case 17, unit 3; Case 24). Unspecified fuel with heat outside rent has no burden (Case 14, unit 3). PolicyEngine/policyengine-us issue 9754 tracks the default.
10. **Plan and manual conflicts (the branch follows the manual).** Lottery: page 66 includes “Lottery Winnings”; plan 1.9 leaves the lump-sum box (“winnings from lotteries”) unchecked. The branch counts `gambling_winnings`, which includes other gambling (income Case 13: 30,000 + 6,000 = 36,000, negatives floor to 0, a 17-year-old's are excluded; `ga_liheap.yaml` Case 18: 12,000, Level I electric $500). Cash gifts: page 65 includes “Contribution/ Cash Gift”; the FY2026, FY2025 and FY2022 plans (page 6) leave “Cash gifts” unchecked; the FY2022 plan covers the manual's issue year, so the later boxes show no policy change. The branch counts adults' `financial_assistance` (outside cash; transfers between members have no input) and cites the FY2022 plan (companion test 15). PAMMS has no income chapter, so the 2022 manual is the newest income rule located; PAMMS page 5 still prints $350 to $400 with a senior maximum, which plan 16.1 says the matrix removed, and the branch follows the matrices. Disability and workers' compensation: pages 65 and 68 include them, plan 1.9 leaves the insurance-payments box unchecked, and the branch counts them (companion test 18). Capital gains: page 65 includes them; the plan has no box. Minors: page 62 excludes all income under 18, while page 68 (“Minor Income”) and plan 1.9 name only a child's earnings; the branch follows page 62.
11. **Interest disregard once per household.** Pages 66 and 69 do not say whether the $25 applies per person or per account. The branch subtracts $300 once from the adults' combined interest (income Case 4: 200 + 200 - 300 + 600 dividends = 700; per person, 600). Annualizing the monthly $25 as $300 is a simplification.
12. **Per-source floors (settled).** Each source is floored at zero, so a business, farm, rental or capital loss offsets nothing (income Case 11: $40,000, $36,000, $0; `ga_liheap.yaml` Case 7: $6,000 wages with an $18,000 self-employment loss, Level I wood $500; Case 13: both units over the limit). No Georgia source addresses offsets between sources.
13. **Social Security net, railroad gross (settled, Georgia-specific).** Both plans check “Excluding MediCare deduction” and page 69 excludes the premiums, so Social Security counts as max(benefit - `medicare_part_b_premium`, 0) per adult, although page 67 says to use the award letter “for gross amount of check”; `medicare_part_b_premium` excludes any Medicare Savings Program share. Railroad retirement counts gross: application item 12 groups it with Social Security, but no source nets it (`ga_liheap.yaml` Case 12: $36,000 military and $36,000 railroad retirement, both over the limit).
14. **TANF (settled).** Read through the take-up-gated `tanf` aggregate, once per unit, so TANF counts when received.
15. **Household composition (simplification).** The SPM unit stands in for the page 76 household. Roomers and boarders (out of size; rent over $30 or $70 a month counted), foster children, group quarters and institutions (page 57) are not identified.
16. **Lawful noncitizens in the household size (manual conflict; user decision 2026-10-07).** 101.2 (page 3), 1100.3 (page 50), the 1100.5 a list, “CITIZENS ELIGIBLE FOR PROGRAM CONSIDERATION” (page 51), and 1100.4 and the 1100.5 b note (pages 51 to 52) leave only undocumented members out of the size. Against them, 1100.14 (page 57) lists as ineligible “Applicants where ALL household members are non-U.S. citizens.”, and the glossary (page 76) says under “Household” “U.S. Citizenship (applicant must be a U.S. citizen. If other household members are non-citizens use this/these persons income in determining eligibility but do not include in the household size.” and under “Ineligible Households” “households where all persons are not U.S. Citizens”. The branch follows the eligibility sections, as do PAMMS page 4 and the DFCS page: size counts `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`; undocumented, DACA (not on the page 51 list) and other nonqualified members do not (`ga_liheap_household_size.yaml` Case 1: LPR, asylee, citizen, size 3). Page 57 is read as a unit with no citizen or qualified noncitizen (size 0: ineligible, limit $0 in limit Case 4), so lawful immigrants alone can qualify. Under the glossary reading, lawful noncitizens would leave the size (a permanent resident with $16,000 wages and a citizen child: size 1, $560, not size 2, $660; two permanent residents alone: ineligible).
17. **Annual income (simplification).** The manual computes gross monthly income (pages 62, 64); the matrix and page 4 use annual income, and annual inputs stand in. The page 64 unemployment rule (“Multiply by 14 weeks, then divide by 12”) is not applied; annual `total_unemployment_compensation` counts as reported.
18. **Categorical eligibility (not applied).** Plan 1.4 answers Yes for TANF, SSI and SNAP, 1.4a limits it to “pure public assistance”, and manual 1100.12 and the glossary require that assistance be the only income or that every member receive it. Aggregate inputs cannot establish this, so every household takes the income test; plan 1.6 says the benefit is the same, and such income is far below the limit.
19. **Other gaps.** Not modeled: the $1,000 fuel-account credit screen (plan 2.5), one payment per program year, vendor agreements and the Approved Vendor List, the elderly and homebound priority period, the PSC components, Include rows without inputs (adoption assistance, other annuities, contract and mortgage-sale income, WIA and training allowances, military allotments, donations, roomer and boarder income).
20. **Carried-forward years.** Before 2025: that year's HHS median with the FY2025 cutoffs and amounts. 2027 and later: the FFY2027 median ($115,118) with the FY2026 cutoffs and amounts; the floor (2026 guidelines) binds from size 17 (size 16: floor(69,070 x 1.62) = 111,893 against 1.1 x 101,160 = 111,276). All are unverified estimates.
21. **Federal 110% poverty floor (`ga_liheap.yaml` Case 22; eligible Cases 10 to 12).** 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B) bars excluding a household on income alone below 110% of the poverty level, and both plans assure it (page 43), so the floor governs over the printed size-16 rows. Georgia names no guideline, so the branch uses the HHS-mandatory one (Attachment 2: 2024 guidelines for FY2025, 2025 for FY2026) at `ga_liheap_household_size`: eligible when income <= the printed limit or < round(1.1 x guideline, 2). Float64 gives 1.1 x 98,150 = 107,965.00000000001, so the floor is rounded to the cent and income exactly at 110% fails “less than 110 percent”. The printed limits fall below the floor from size 16: FY2025 $102,926 against 1.1 x 95,760 = $105,336; FY2026 $107,634 against 1.1 x 98,150 = $107,965 (size 15: $105,641 against $101,915). The limit keeps the printed table; a protected household above it gets Level II. Companion tests 16 and 19 pin the exact floor, the guideline lag and the Georgia size. In-force calendar guidelines would make FY2025 bind from size 15 ($101,020 against $101,915).

## Existing corpus starting points

- [FY2026 state-plan manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ga-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [Policy manual manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ga-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission. The sources listed under Why queued need ingest before the modules above can be proved.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-ga/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the income limits and Level I cutoffs for sizes 1 to 16 in FY2025 and FY2026, the five fuel amounts at both levels, the lowest-amount payment for rent including all utilities, the heat-in-rent electric and fuel-bill routes with and without a subsidy, subsidized housing, mixed immigration status, the under-18 exclusion, every counted income source including unemployment and cash gifts, Social Security net of the Medicare premium, the interest disregard, TANF receipt/take-up and the 110% poverty floor from size 16 at the exact cent, with the HHS-mandatory guideline year and the Georgia household size. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Florida LIHEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 2a, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9969 (branch `fl-liheap`), open and ready for review, not merged. Head `ba61f132b2` (pushed 2026-10-19). The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

- **Sources need ingest.** No axiom-corpus manifest on `main` holds the FloridaCommerce payment matrices that set the amounts and bands (FFY 2026; updated FY 2024/2025), the FY2025 state plan, the statewide application or portal FAQ (the minor-income rule), the FFY2025 and FFY2026 HHS state median income tables, the 2024 and 2025 poverty guidelines with the LIHEAP IM 2024-02 and 2025-02 guideline tables (the one-year lag), or 42 U.S.C. 8624 (the 110% floor). Each needs ingest.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-06, 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-19 (git tree of `manifests/`, 1,714 entries on 2026-10-19, not truncated), not in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run requires separate approval. None has been requested or approved for Florida.
- **No reviewed PE revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. DTrim99 requested changes on `7c5688f9ec` (2026-10-14), fixed at `f2f6f3f706`; PavelMakarchuk approved `f2f6f3f706` with comments (2026-10-19), applied at `ba61f132b2`. DTrim99's re-review is pending and the PR is unmerged, so no revision can be pinned.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9969, open and ready for review, not merged; branch `fl-liheap`, head `ba61f132b2` (2026-10-19). Commits from `2da6d77e44` (2026-10-03) to `f2f6f3f706` built the program and applied two local reviews and DTrim99's 2026-10-14 review. `ba61f132b2` addresses PavelMakarchuk's 2026-10-19 review: the floor is rounded to cents before the strict comparison, so income exactly at 110% is not protected (interpretation 18); the shared `fpg_floor.yaml` matches PR 10279 and links 42 U.S.C. 8624 at `#b_2_B`; the guideline lag cites LIHEAP IM 2024-02, 2025-02 and 2026-01; code notes record the plan item 2.6 and contract G(1), G(7)d, G(8)a and G(8)c conflicts; tests 19 to 22 add size 14, a 15-member household built from people, the 2027 floor edge and a six-household `integration.yaml`. Everything below describes `ba61f132b2`; oracle fixtures pin the merged revision.
- **Scope:** the regular Home Energy Benefit (manual 700.01) for heating, paid once a year from the payment matrix. Out of scope: crisis (700.02), weather-related or supply-shortage assistance (700.03), cooling, weatherization, in-kind benefits and heating equipment (FY2025 plan 2.7), the Elderly Home Energy Assistance Program, the SNAP nominal payment (none is paid) and data-match enrollment (FY2026 plan 1.5).
- **Policy periods:** FY2025 and FY2026 (October 1 to September 30). Florida variables are annual and read the value in force on 1 January, so period `2025` is FY2025 and `2026` FY2026. Every Florida file starts at 2024-10-01; three change at 2025-10-01: `payment/base_amount` ($1,000/$750/$550/$400, then $350/$300/$250/$200), `eligibility/fpg_rate` (1.5, then 0) and `eligibility/truncates_smi_limit` (false, then true). The limit reads `gov.hhs.smi.amount` (Florida $98,038, then $103,063) with `household_size_adjustment` (FY2026 via `liheap_smi_limit`) and `gov.hhs.fpg` lagged one year; the shared `gov.hhs.liheap.fpg_floor` (1.1 from 1985-10-01) sets the 110% floor, compared in cents. `programs.yaml`: status `partial`, no `verified_years`. Earlier years backfill FY2025, and 2027 on keeps the FY2026 rules with the FFY2027 median ($108,122) and the 2026 guidelines; both are unverified estimates, and no FY2027 matrix is published.

- **Parameters:** `gov.states.fl.commerce.liheap` (`eligibility/`: `categorical_programs`, `fpg_rate`, `fpg_year_lag`, `smi_rate`, `truncates_smi_limit`; `income/`: `adult_age`, `sources/earned`, `sources/unearned`, `sources/household`; `payment/`: `base_amount` (keyed by band 1 to 4), `child_max_age`, `elderly_min_age`, `income_band_fraction`, `income_band_fpg_rate`, `supplement`). 15 files, plus the shared federal `gov.hhs.liheap.fpg_floor`.

The FY2026 plan assurances (page 45) print the same clause. | Countable income | `fl_liheap_countable_income` | SPM unit, year | Members 18 and over, students included (under 18 count nothing): each person-level source in Inputs from `employment_income` to `alimony_income` (the branch's earned and unearned lists; Social Security gross), floored at zero separately, plus max(gambling winnings - losses, 0); plus the unit's take-up-gated `tanf` (including `fl_tca`) once. Nonqualified members' income counts. |
| Categorical eligibility | `fl_liheap_categorically_eligible` | SPM unit, year | The unit's `snap` + `tanf` + `ssi` (each after take-up) is positive. Florida only. |
| Income limit | `fl_liheap_income_limit` | SPM unit, year | Before rounding. FY2026: floor(floor(0.6 x SMI4) x f(size)). FY2025: max(0.6 x SMI4 x f(size), 1.5 x the 2024 guideline for the size). f(size) = 0.52 + 0.16 x min(size - 1, 5) + 0.03 x max(size - 6, 0). Zero for size 0. FY2025 SMI amounts are unrounded (30,587.856 for one person); eligibility compares income with the limit rounded half up. |
| Eligible | `fl_liheap_eligible` | SPM unit, year | Size above 0, and (countable income at or below the rounded limit, strictly below 1.1 x the one-year-lagged guideline for the size rounded to cents, or categorical), and heating responsibility, and a qualifying fuel. Responsibility: with heat in rent, the unit is not subsidized (`receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing`) or has a positive heating bill; otherwise `has_heating_expense` (default: a positive primary-fuel bill; an explicit false is respected). Fuel: `heating_type` is not NONE; UNSPECIFIED qualifies only with heat in rent. Florida only. |
| Benefit | `fl_liheap` | SPM unit, year | When eligible: base(band) + $100 if any member is 60 or over + $100 if any member is disabled + $150 if any member is under 6. Where 1.5 x guideline is at least the limit (FY2025 sizes 9 and above): below 75% of the guideline is band 1, up to 100% band 2, up to 125% band 3, else band 4. Elsewhere: up to round-half-up(0.5, 0.7 and 0.85 x limit) bands 1 to 3, else band 4 (including categorical or floor-protected income above the limit). Bases: FY2025 $1,000, $750, $550, $400; FY2026 $350, $300, $250, $200. Fuel and the bill do not matter. |

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Rounding (inferred).** No source states a rounding rule. FY2026 floors 60% of the four-person median, then each size (test 2), and rounds band tops (50%, 70%, 85% of the limit) half up (tests 3, 16, 19). FY2025 rounds the 60% amount and each band top half up (test 13; the HHS FFY2025 page prints $30,587, the matrix $30,588). No source covers cents between a printed top and the next start ($16,078.50); the branch puts them in the next band, and its tests use the next cent (`fl_liheap.yaml` Cases 1, 17, 24, 26; `eligible` Cases 1, 6).
2. **FY2025 first poverty-guideline band.** The printed band 1 top is one dollar below 75% at every size from 9 to 20 ($43,574 against 0.75 x 58,100 = 43,575), although the heading reads "75% of FPG or Less"; band 2 is headed "At least 75% but no more than 100% FPG". The branch follows the printed dollars: band 1 is income below 75% (test 14).
3. **Limit rule (source conflict, unresolved).** Manual 900.01D (page 39) sets 60% of SMI for sizes 1 to 8 and 150% of the poverty guidelines for 9 or more; 1100.03D (page 47), 1200.01A (page 49) and 1200.03A(2)(a) (page 51) set 150% for all. FY2025: plan, matrix and 900.01D agree; the branch takes the greater (SMI for 1 to 8, the guideline for 9 to 20). FY2026: plan 2.1, the matrix footnote, the Clearinghouse, the portal for sizes 1 to 12 and the draft FFY2027 plan give 60% of SMI (size 9: $87,190, $7,266 a month, against $89,475 at 150% of the 2025 guideline); the branch uses it for every size, as Part 200 Q.4 directs. Amendment 0001 conflicts (G(8)c: 150% from 9 people; G(7)d: 150% for all), but its own D(10)b and G(1) (page 11) adopt the current matrix, which umbrella section 33A's precedence order leaves intact. The owner kept 60% of SMI on 2026-10-07; the 110% floor (interpretation 18) protects the lowest incomes from 15 people.
4. **FY2026 size 13 and above (source anomaly).** The matrix prints $157,686 for size 13, 100% of SMI (103,063 x 1.53 = 157,686.39), with band tops at 50%, 70% and 85% of it; the portal prints $13,141 a month (157,686 / 12). The footnote, plan 2.1 and the draft FFY2027 plan state 60% of SMI, and 8624(b)(2)(B) caps eligibility at the greater of 150% of poverty ($122,475 for 13) and 60% of SMI ($94,610). The branch applies 60% of SMI to the size 13 limit and bands (test 16), departing from the portal: 13 people with $60,000 get $300, as do 12 and 14. Larger sizes follow the federal factors unchecked.
5. **FY2026 plan 2.6 against the matrix (source conflict).** The FY2026 plan estimates $400 to $1,350, the FY2025 figures; the FFY2026 matrix pays $200 to $700. The manual (700.01C; Part 200 Q.4, page 9) and contract D(10)b (page 9) require the current matrix, so the branch follows it; the draft FFY2027 plan estimates $200 to $700.
6. **Income above the limit (estimate).** Receipt (plan 1.4a, 1.6; manual G(9)) and the 110% floor admit income above the limit, but no located source prints a band above it. The branch pays the smallest base ($200 in FY2026, $400 in FY2025) plus additions (`fl_liheap.yaml` Case 7: wages $100,000, SNAP $1,200, $200; Cases 25, 27, 28).
7. **Categorical receipt.** Receipt is positive take-up-gated `snap`, `tanf` or `ssi` for any member; FY2025 veterans programs have no input. A minor's SSI qualifies the household though the minor's income is excluded (`categorically_eligible` Case 3). Receipt waives no other condition (test 8). Manual 900.04C and 1100.03 treat SNAP, SSI, SSD or TANF receipt as proof of citizenship, read as documentation rules.
8. **Minors' income (statewide application).** The application and FAQ exclude minors' income, plan 1.10 names floridaliheap.com as the statewide application, and plan 1.9 leaves a child's earned income unchecked; manual 1200.01D instead counts 16 and 17 year olds not in school full time. The branch follows the application: members 18 and over count, students included; members under 18 do not (tests 12, 22). Minors are undefined; under 18 follows 1200.01D and plan 1.9. The application PDF (created 2025-03-21) has no effective date, so the rule is backfilled through FY2025. An 8 year old's Social Security and a minor's SSI stay excluded (`countable_income` Cases 14, 15).
9. **Social Security gross (Florida's rule).** Plan 1.9 checks "Including MediCare deduction" and manual G(5)(a) adds the premium back to a net check, so the branch counts `social_security` as is, without subtracting `medicare_part_b_premium` (test 9); the manual's SSI-recipient exception needs no rule.
10. **Gross income and losses (settled).** Plan 1.8 and 1200.01B count gross income. Each earned and unearned source, rental and farm rent included, is floored at zero separately, so a loss offsets nothing; net business inputs get no further expense deduction (G(12)); net gambling is floored at zero. Dependent cases: `countable_income` Case 2 (12,000 + max(-6,000, 0) + 600 = 12,600), 3 (1,200), 17 (wages 1,200, winnings 4,000, losses 4,000, 5,000 or 10,000: 1,200 each), 19 (30,500); `fl_liheap.yaml` Case 19 (40,000 and 34,000, both ineligible).
11. **Income-source mapping.** No plan row names workers' compensation or disability benefits; the branch counts both (nearest rows: insurance paid to the insured; retirement or pension). Military and railroad retirement and survivor benefits count as retirement or pension; estate income as receipts from estates or trusts. Checked forms with no input: contract income, mortgage or sales-contract payments, one-time lump sums, work study, royalties, VISTA and training stipends, Independent Living Program payments and Social Security garnishes; WIA earnings and commissions are inside wages. Florida Optional State Supplementation (`fl_oss`) is not counted: 900.02B (page 39) and 900.03B(1) (page 40) exclude its recipients' settings.
12. **Household.** The SPM unit stands in for the economic unit of 900.02. Qualified status follows `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant` (no input for the domestic-abuse category; 900.01B read through 900.04B). A unit with no qualified member is ineligible (900.04A, D item 2). Applicant rule (source conflict): 900.04A (page 41) accepts a household when one member, preferably an adult, qualifies, but 900.04D item 1 denies an illegal alien applicant; no input names the applicant, so a qualified member is assumed to apply (test 5(b)). Not modeled: separate households in one dwelling (900.02A), state-paid foster or residential residents (900.02B), boarders, whose landlord's income is not counted (Part 200 G), and absent members (900.06).
13. **Heating responsibility.** Source conflict: heat in non-subsidized rent qualifies under 900.01A (page 39) and 100.01 (page 4), but 1100.04B item 1 (page 47) asks renters for a landlord statement that "Home energy costs are not included in their rent", and 1100.04C (page 48) denies an application without a fuel bill or such a statement. FY2025 plan 2.3 repeats the statement under Renters (page 8) yet answers Yes for utilities in rent (page 9); the FY2026 plan answers No to all three renter rows (page 8). The branch follows 900.01A and 100.01. With heat in subsidized rent, a positive heating bill stands for an obligation to pay a portion (900.08A); outside rent, `has_heating_expense` does (test 18). A bill or heat in rent stands for the 900.01C energy burden; no HUD utility allowance is deducted (900.08B to C, test 7); landlord statements and account ownership are assumed.
14. **Fuel (settled).** `heating_type` is a required input; the amount does not depend on fuel (plan 2.5). NONE is ineligible. UNSPECIFIED qualifies only with heat in rent: non-subsidized rent pays it, as core's `HeatingType` guidance intends for heat in rent with an unknown fuel (`fl_liheap.yaml` Case 22, $350); subsidized rent has no bill to show a residual charge ($0); outside rent pays $0 even with `has_heating_expense` or `heating_expense` set (Case 21). PolicyEngine/policyengine-us issue 9754 tracks the default; the national datasets carry no heating inputs, so microsimulation totals are about $0.
15. **Additions.** Elderly is 60 and over; disabled is `is_disabled` for any member; the child addition applies to a member under 6, so a child aged 5.5 qualifies (`fl_liheap.yaml` Case 12).
16. **Periods and editions.** Annual income stands in for 30 days annualized or the current situation, whichever is lower (1200.03A, contract G(8)a); the portal's rounded monthly maximums differ from the annual values by at most $6 a year ($2,680 x 12 = 32,160 against $32,155). One award per year is modeled; previous awards (900.05, Part 200 Q.1) are not inputs. The FY2025 matrix ("effective ASAP", PDF created 2024-06-28) is dated 2024-10-01; period 2025 reads it either way. No post-DEO manual was located.
17. **Other gaps.** Residency of at least six months, institutions and dormitories (900.03), Poarch Creek Band members (900.07) and fund-availability limits are not modeled.
18. **110% poverty floor (federal).** 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B), the FY2026 plan assurances (page 45) and Amendment 0001 G(8)e (page 13) bar excluding a household on income below 110% of the poverty level. Income strictly below 1.1 x the guideline, rounded to cents, is income-eligible; the limit still reproduces the matrix. The guideline lags one year (LIHEAP IM 2024-02, 2025-02, 2026-01: each January's guidelines are mandatory from the next October 1; test 19). FY2025 limits are at least 150% of the guideline. The floor binds from 15 people in FY2026 (98,320 against 101,915; 16: 100,175 against 107,965; 14 clears it, 96,465 against 95,865) and the 2027 estimate (103,148 against 105,028; test 21); protected income above the limit gets the band 4 base (tests 17, 20). 1.1 x 92,650 is 101,915.00000000001 in float64, so the branch rounds the floor to cents and exactly $101,915 is not protected, as the statute's "less than" requires (tests 17, 21).

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-fl-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-fl-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [us-fl-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-fl-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-fl/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the FY2025 and FY2026 limits and bands (FY2025 sizes 9 to 20 on the guidelines; FY2026 sizes 1 to 14, size 13 at 60% of SMI), the 110% floor from 15 people (not at the exact floor; also 2027), end-to-end FY2026 households, the three additions, categorical receipt and TCA take-up, nonqualified members, heat in rent and subsidized housing, a reported obligation outside rent, an unspecified fuel only with heat in rent, per-source income floors, net gambling, gross Social Security and excluded minors' income. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: LIHEAP wave 2a: encode South Dakota LIEAP regular heating assistance

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Objective

Ship South Dakota LIEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 2a, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9974 (branch `sd-liheap`), open, not merged. Head `f88aa84a78` (2026-10-19) addresses PavelMakarchuk's review of `cd74fd52d6`. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder cannot run for this program yet:

- **Sources need ingest.** On 2026-10-06 axiom-corpus `main` manifests captured three of the branch's official sources: the FY2026 state plan, the FY2026 benefit matrix and the 2018 Office of Energy Assistance manual. No manifest captures South Dakota Administrative Rules (ARSD) chapter 67:15:01, the FY2024 state plan (item 9.1), the FY2025 state plan, the FY2022 to FY2024 benefit matrices, the Department of Social Services (DSS) income-limit tables for 2024-2025 and 2025-2026, application form EA-297, the 2023 to 2025 HHS poverty guidelines, the FFY2024 to FFY2026 HHS state median income tables, or 45 CFR 96.85(b).
- **Release admission unchecked.** Presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not checked, including for the three manifests that exist.
- **Encoder runs need approval.** Each billed encoder run requires separate approval. None has been requested for this program.
- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9974 is not merged: PavelMakarchuk's 2026-10-19 review requested changes (one critical finding, the kerosene payment method), fixed at `f88aa84a78`; DTrim99's 2026-10-15 request for changes, answered at `cd74fd52d6`, also awaits re-review.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9974, branch `sd-liheap`. Head `f88aa84a78` (2026-10-19) answers PavelMakarchuk's review of `cd74fd52d6`: kerosene is paid to the supplier and capped at unpaid charges like fuel oil (interpretation 4; plan item 9.1, ARSD 67:15:01:40 and :43.01); comments correct the FY2026 size 6 plan figure to $22,013 and cite statute and DLR URLs. `cd74fd52d6` (2026-10-15) merged upstream/main `9560e7f183` and answered DTrim99's review of `ee24e71ea5`. Earlier commits (from `d3b03217a6`, 2026-10-03) built the program and adopted the shared `liheap_smi_limit` helper (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us PR 10019). Everything below describes `f88aa84a78`.
- **Scope:** the regular heating benefit of South Dakota's Low Income Energy Assistance Program (LIEAP) for FY2024 to FY2026: residence; a household size counting citizens and eligible aliens (at least one); the income limit by that size, or categorical eligibility when every member receives SNAP; heating-cost responsibility; countable income; four heating regions; the two-tier direct-payment matrix by fuel group and region, capped at unpaid heating charges (kerosene included, priced from Fuel Oil) except for wood and coal (paid in full); and heat in rent, 30% of monthly tenant rent for seven months up to the regional amount. Out of scope: the Energy Crisis Intervention Program (ECIP), cooling (South Dakota operates none), weatherization, furnace repair and replacement, the SNAP nominal payment (plan item 1.7a: No), and households served by tribal LIHEAP grantees.
- **Policy periods:** three seasons (FY N runs October 1 of N-1 to September 30 of N; plan item 1.1). Annual variables read the value in force on 1 January: model period `2024` carries FY2024, `2025` FY2025, `2026` FY2026. `payment/direct` has entries at `2021-10-01` (FY2022 and FY2023 cells) and `2023-10-01` (FY2024 electricity, fuel oil and propane cells, which FY2026 repeats). `income/limits/table/amount` holds the printed FY2025 limits for sizes 1 to 10 at `2024-10-01`, applied by `income/limits/table/in_effect` (false `2023-10-01`, true `2024-10-01`, false `2025-10-01`). Limit and tier rates start at `2024-01-01`; age limits, income-source lists, regions and heat-in-rent parameters start at `2025-10-01` and backfill. `programs.yaml` lists South Dakota LIEAP as `status: partial` with no `verified_years`; its note names the gaps in interpretations 7 and 2. Model years 2022 and 2023 read the FY2022 and FY2023 cells, but the rule misses some printed limits; they and earlier years are unverified estimates. Model year 2027 carries the FY2026 rule; the FY2027 draft is not encoded (interpretation 1).
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/sd/dss/liheap/`: `sd_liheap`; `eligibility/sd_liheap_eligible`, `sd_liheap_household_size`, `sd_liheap_income_limit`; `income/sd_liheap_countable_income`; `payment/sd_liheap_base_payment`, `sd_liheap_heat_in_rent_payment`, `sd_liheap_income_threshold`, `sd_liheap_region`. No new inputs. The limit and threshold reuse `fpg` (`gov.hhs.fpg`, one-year lag) and the shared `liheap_smi_limit` helper (`gov.hhs.smi.amount`, size-adjusted).
- **Parameters:** `gov.states.sd.dss.liheap` (`income/`: `earned_income_min_age` 18, `secondary_school_age_limit` 19, `fpg_year_lag` 1, `sources/earned`, `sources/unearned`, `limits/fpg_lower_rate` 1.5, `limits/fpg_upper_rate` 2, `limits/smi_rate` 0.6, `limits/table/amount`, `limits/table/in_effect`; `payment/`: `direct` (fuel group, region, tier), `heat_in_rent/amount` (by region), `heat_in_rent/months` 7, `heat_in_rent/rent_share` 0.3, `income_threshold_rate` 1.25, `regions/region_1` to `region_4`). 19 files.
- **Tests:** 78 YAML cases in 10 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/sd/dss/liheap/` (`sd_liheap.yaml` 14; `integration.yaml` 5; `eligibility/`: `sd_liheap_eligible.yaml` 7, `sd_liheap_household_size.yaml` 4, `sd_liheap_income_limit.yaml` 5; `income/`: `sd_liheap_countable_income.yaml` 23; `payment/`: `sd_liheap_base_payment.yaml` 7, `sd_liheap_heat_in_rent_payment.yaml` 8, `sd_liheap_income_threshold.yaml` 3, `sd_liheap_region.yaml` 2). The 72 cases at `cd74fd52d6` passed CI. The new and changed cases (`sd_liheap.yaml` Case 2, kerosene $1, and new Case 14; income Case 23, modeled UI; eligible Case 3 awards; `integration.yaml`) were not run locally; CI validates them.

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence in a manifest on axiom-corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-06: the five manifests named below were read; likely names for other South Dakota LIHEAP manifests returned 404; a code search for `67:15` found nothing; a 2026-10-19 listing of `manifests/` shows no new one. “Needs ingest” marks a source no corpus manifest captures. Presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not checked. rulespec-us `main` has only `us-sd/policies/cms` and `us-sd/policies/income_tax` for South Dakota, and no `us/` poverty-guideline, state-median-income or 45 CFR part 96 module.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-sd/regulations/arsd/67-15-01/definitions-and-household` | 67:15:01:01(1) categorically income eligible, (4) gross income, (5) independent living arrangement; :06 vulnerable households; :08.01 institutions; :09 proof of liability for heating expenses | none | Needs ingest. Official: [ARSD chapter 67:15:01](https://sdlegislature.gov/Rules/Administrative/67:15:01) (HTML per section; local copy from the JSON API, `https://sdlegislature.gov/api/Rules/67%3A15`). |
| `us-sd/regulations/arsd/67-15-01/income` | :10 three calendar months, tax return for the self-employed, categorical eligibility; :11; :18 exclusions (1) to (22); :18.01 self-employed households | none | Same source. |
| `us-sd/regulations/arsd/67-15-01/benefits` | :20 benefit levels; :35 regions; :39 Native American households; :40 wood and coal; :41 to :41.02 heat in rent; :43.01 payment limits (payment to the energy supplier or landlord) | none | Same source. |
| `us-sd/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-1`, `.../section-2`, `.../section-9`, `.../section-17` | 1.1 dates and claim windows (page 4); 1.4, 1.4a, 1.5 (page 5); 1.8, 1.9 (pages 6 to 7); 2.1 to 2.3 (page 9); 2.5, 2.6 (page 10); 9.1 supplier payments and exceptions (page 22); 17.3 (page 34) | `us-sd/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | In manifest `us-sd-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml`, segmented by Section headings. Official copy: [FY2026 state plan, pages 4-7, 9-10, 22, 34](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/state-plans/SD_Plan_2026.pdf#page=4). Check-box states come from renders of pages 5-7, 9-10, 22 and 34. |
| `us-sd/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2025/section-2`, `.../section-9`; `.../fy2024/section-9` | FY2025: 1.1 dates (page 4); 2.1 thresholds (page 8); 2.6 minimum and maximum (page 9); 9.1 (page 21). FY2024: 9.1 (page 21) | none | Needs ingest. Official: [FY2025 state plan, pages 4, 8-9, 21](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2025/state-plans/SD_Plan_2025.pdf#page=4); [FY2024 state plan](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2024/state-plans/SD_Plan_2024.pdf#page=21). |
| `us-sd/policies/dss/liheap-benefit-matrix/fy2026` | Own and Rent Cases (five fuel groups, four regions, two tiers) and Heat in Rent Cases | `us-sd/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026-benefit-matrix` | In manifest `us-sd-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml` (one page, PDF dated 2025-09-02, as cached). Its `access_note` gives the 2018 manual's 1,984,214 bytes, not this file's 52,140. Official: [FY2026 benefit matrix](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/benefits-matricies/SD_BenefitMatrix_2026.pdf). |
| `us-sd/policies/dss/liheap-benefit-matrix/fy2024`, `.../fy2023`, `.../fy2022` | Cells and Maximum Income (Annual, 3-Month) for sizes 1 to 15; FY2022 and FY2023 have lower electricity, fuel oil and propane cells | none | Needs ingest. Official: [FY2024 benefit matrix, pages 1-5](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2024/benefits-matricies/SD_BenefitMatrix_2024.pdf#page=1), [FY2023, pages 1-5](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2023/benefits-matricies/SD_BenefitMatrix_2023.pdf#page=1), [FY2022, pages 1-5](https://liheapch.acf.gov/sites/default/files/webfiles/docs/SD_BenefitMatrix_2022.pdf#page=1). |
| `us-sd/policies/dss/energy-assistance-page/income-limits-2025-2026` and `.../income-limits-2024-2025` | Maximum three-month income for sizes 1 to 10; gross income; responsibility for heating costs | none | Needs ingest. Official: [DSS energy assistance page, archived January 1, 2026](https://web.archive.org/web/20260101052007/https://dss.sd.gov/economicassistance/energy_weatherization_assistance.aspx) (2025-2026 table) and [the same page archived January 14, 2025](https://web.archive.org/web/20250114001211/https://dss.sd.gov/economicassistance/energy_weatherization_assistance.aspx) (2024-2025 table). The live page changes each season; ingest each dated version. |
| `us-sd/policies/dss/oea-policies-and-procedures-manual/chapter-1` to `.../chapter-4` | Pages 2-3 eligibility and household; 7-9 citizenship and mixed households; 12-13 time frame and categorical eligibility; 17-18 ineligible members' income and household count; 24-28 income chart; 30-32 payment, heat in rent, wood, coal and kerosene | `us-sd/manual/dss/oea-policies-and-procedures-manual` | In manifest `us-sd-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml` (60 pages, PDF dated 2017-12-05, 1,984,214 bytes like the cached copy). Its `benefit_matrix_pdf_pages: '50'` is the unused 2016-2017 limits page; the 2016-2017 matrix (page 51) and region map (page 52) are images. Corpus `page-N` suffixes count text-bearing pages only, so they can differ from the PDF pages quoted below. Official copy: [2018 manual, pages 2-3, 7-9, 12-13, 17-18, 24-28, 30-32, 52](https://liheapch.acf.gov/sites/default/files/webfiles/docs/SD_Policy-and-Procedures-Manual2018.pdf#page=2). |
| `us-sd/policies/dss/energy-assistance-application/ea-297` | Page 2 claim windows and uses not paid; page 4 heating-source categories, payment of heat-in-rent, wood and coal awards; page 5 gross income to report | none | Needs ingest. Official: [Application EA-297 (08/25), pages 2, 4-5](https://dss.sd.gov/formsandpubs/docs/ENERGY/energyassistanceapplication.pdf#page=2). |
| `us/policies/hhs/poverty-guidelines/2023` to `.../2025` | Contiguous-states guidelines $14,580 plus $5,140 per added person (2023), $15,060 plus $5,380 (2024), $15,650 plus $5,500 (2025), read with a one-year lag | `us/guidance/hhs/aspe/poverty-guidelines` (current page only) | `us-hhs-poverty-guidelines.yaml` and `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml` hold only the 2026 guidelines (model year 2027). The tier and award are not given here: they rest on interpretation 2. |

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Income-limit rule (inferred) and plan conflict.** No source states how DSS computes its limits. The branch rule (Required outputs) reproduces all fifteen FY2024 and all ten FY2026 published limits; floor(floor(0.6 x M) x S) equals the HHS tables' printed 60% amounts (FFY2026 size 7 $90,057, so $22,514 a quarter). FY2025 departs from it (sizes 1 to 3 at 200% of the 2024 guideline; sizes 4 to 9 the HHS FFY2025 60% column over 4, rounded half up, $73,582 / 4 = $18,395.50 giving $18,396, above the 200% cap for sizes 4 and 5; size 10 at 150%), so the branch prints that table (companion test 5). The plans disagree with DSS: FY2026 item 2.1 lists 60% of state median income for sizes 4 to 9 (HHS FFY2026 $66,709, $77,382 and $88,055 for sizes 4 to 6: $16,677, $19,345 and $22,013 a quarter, floored as the model does), but DSS publishes $16,075, $18,825 and $21,575, 200% of the 2025 guideline; FY2025 lists 60% for sizes 1 to 3, where DSS publishes 200%. The branch follows DSS, as `sd_liheap_income_limit` and `fpg_upper_rate` comments record. Rule values with no published counterpart: FY2026 sizes 11 to 15 (`sd_liheap_income_limit.yaml` Case 3: 105,972; 114,224; 122,472; 130,724; 138,972) and FY2025 size 11 (Case 5: 103,288). The rule misses some FY2022 and FY2023 limits (FY2023 size 7: printed 18,485 a quarter, rule 18,484). Income at the limit is eligible (“may not exceed”). Every limit is at least 149% of the guideline, so the federal 110% floor (42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B)) never binds. For sizes 4 to 6 the FY2027 draft's 60% of the $118,003 median (70,800; 82,128; 93,456) exceeds the 200% rule that model year 2027 carries (66,000; 77,360; 88,720); its size 1 to 3 rates equal 200% of the 2026 guideline.
2. **First-tier threshold (Mid).** FY2022 to FY2024 print it; FY2026 names “0-Mid” and “Mid-Max” without a number; FY2025 has no matrix. The branch uses 4 x round-half-up(1.25 x G / 4), which reproduces every printed FY2022 to FY2024 three-month Mid (FY2024 size 2: 1.25 x 19,720 / 4 = 6,162.50 gives 6,163) and gives $19,564 for one person in FY2026 and $18,824 in FY2025. Cases resting on it: `sd_liheap.yaml` Cases 3 (20,000, $792), 7 (FY2025, threshold 39,000, $792) and 10 ($792 at 29,565.20; $880 at 18,565.20); `integration.yaml` Cases 1 (24,648 ≤ 33,312: $1,007) and 3 (24,648 ≤ 26,436: $854); `sd_liheap_income_threshold.yaml` Case 2; `sd_liheap_base_payment.yaml` Cases 4 and 6 and the tier 2 half of Case 1. FY2024 also prints an Annual Mid, the unrounded 125% (18225, 24650), which differs from 4 x the 3-Month figure for twelve of fifteen sizes; the branch uses the 3-Month figure because the program tests three months of income (`sd_liheap_base_payment.yaml` Case 3: 18,224.01 tier 2, 24,652 tier 1, 24,652.01 tier 2; `sd_liheap_income_threshold.yaml` Case 1). A 2026-10-08 search of the DSS forms, online application and vendor portal found no FY2026 Mid schedule.
3. **FY2025 cells (carried forward).** No FY2025 matrix is published (Clearinghouse checked 2026-10-03). The branch carries the FY2024 cells; the FY2025 plan's $668 minimum and $3,437 maximum equal the FY2024 Coal & Wood Region 1 tier 2 and Fuel Oil Region 4 tier 1 cells. `sd_liheap.yaml` Case 7 rests on this.
4. **Kerosene (source conflict; the branch follows the plan and rules).** No kerosene row exists; EA-297's “Fuel Oil/Kerosene” category supports pricing it from Fuel Oil. Plan item 9.1 (every claimed year and the FY2027 draft), ARSD 67:15:01:40 and :43.01, EA-297 page 4 and the DSS page (Source text) pay the supplier for every fuel except wood, coal and heat in rent; only manual page 31 (2018) pays kerosene “the entire benefit amount”. The branch treats that page as superseded for kerosene and caps kerosene at unpaid charges like fuel oil (`sd_liheap` comment; companion tests 3, 7 and 15(b)); `sd_liheap_base_payment.yaml` Cases 2 and 7 price it from Fuel Oil.
5. **Fuels without a row (coverage limit; settled).** `heating_type` is a required input. SOLAR, OTHER and UNSPECIFIED direct-pay households get $0 because the matrix has no row, not because a source denies them (manual page 31 names corn and pellet stoves among heat sources paid by check). NONE is ineligible. Heat in rent pays an UNSPECIFIED fuel because its amount does not depend on fuel. Cases: `sd_liheap.yaml` Case 5 (eligible, $0); `sd_liheap_base_payment.yaml` Case 5. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us issue 9754 tracks the unspecified default.
6. **County (coverage limit).** An explicit `UNKNOWN` or out-of-state county gives region 0 and $0 (`sd_liheap.yaml` Case 6; `sd_liheap_region.yaml` Case 2; `sd_liheap_heat_in_rent_payment.yaml` Case 8). With no `county` input the model uses the state's alphabetically first county, Aurora (Region II), so fixtures must always send a county.
7. **Mixed-status households (settled) and ineligible members' income (overstated).** Manual pages 9 and 18 make mixed households eligible and count only citizens and eligible aliens; the household size counts members with `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant` and must be at least 1 (companion test 9). Page 17 counts only “a portion” of an ineligible member's income, through a Citizenship Income Calculator whose formula is unpublished (none found 2026-10-08); its one example (adjusted income $6,200) matches neither full counting ($7,000) nor SNAP-style pro rata ($3,000 + $4,000 x 3/4 = $6,000). The model counts that income in full, overstating it. `sd_liheap.yaml` Case 13 rests on this and on interpretation 2: a citizen adult earning $18,000, an undocumented adult earning $9,000 and a citizen child give size 2, income $27,000, limit $42,300, Mid $26,436: tier 2, $792; proration to $26,436 or less would pay tier 1, $880. The branch counts every qualified noncitizen (`sd_liheap_household_size.yaml` Case 1; `sd_liheap_eligible.yaml` Case 3: LEGAL_PERMANENT_RESIDENT and REFUGEE adults, $938 each); whether manual page 8's TANF time limits for refugees and post-1996 permanent residents (Source text) apply to LIEAP is unsettled, and `immigration_status` has no entry date.
8. **Categorical eligibility (source conflict; the branch follows the rule over the manual).** ARSD 67:15:01:01(1) and plan 1.4a require every individual on the application to receive SNAP; manual page 12 also covers members whose income SNAP considered, Medicare Savings Program households and SSI recipients. The branch follows the rule and the plan, approximating receipt as Required outputs states. Manual page 13 sets a categorical household's benefit level from SNAP income times 3; the branch uses its own countable income.
9. **Income items.** Workers' compensation: no plan 1.9 row or manual chart entry names it, but EA-297 page 5 lists it as gross income and ARSD :18 does not exclude it, so it counts (`sd_liheap_countable_income.yaml` Case 22). Gambling winnings (plan unchecked, manual page 27 counts; the branch follows the manual): Case 17 (17,000). Trusts as `estate_income`: Cases 20 and 21 (26,000; a loss floors at 0, 20,000). Cash gifts (source conflict; the branch follows the rule and manual over plan 1.9's unchecked “Cash gifts”): ARSD :18(17) excludes only occasion gifts, manual page 25 counts gifts listed for all three months and EA-297 page 5 lists money from family or friends; `financial_assistance` counts as regular help (Case 8: 14,400; `sd_liheap.yaml` Case 14: $0). Medicare premiums: the branch nets only Part B from Social Security; the manual also nets Part D from Social Security and SSI, Parts A and D from pensions and Parts B and D from VA benefits, all counted gross here, as is railroad retirement. No model input exists for jury duty pay, foster care payments, long-term care insurance or tribal per capita payments over $2,000. Each business, farm, partnership, rental and farm-rent result is floored at zero separately, so one source's loss does not offset another's gain (ARSD :18.01 is silent on netting); net inputs omit the depreciation add-back (manual page 24) and the tax-return basis. Overpayment withholding (ARSD :18(21)) is not separable from the inputs.
10. **Vendor cap (simplification).** `heating_expense` is read as the eligible unpaid charges in the claim window; the model cannot see charge dates, balances or bills already paid. A negative bill floors at 0 (`sd_liheap.yaml` Case 6). Heat billed by the landlord on top of rent is a vendor bill (manual page 31). Kerosene is a vendor fuel (interpretation 4).
11. **Heat in rent (simplification).** min(regional amount, 7 x 30% of monthly tenant rent) assumes steady rent for October to April, a signed landlord agreement (ARSD :41.01) and approval by October. `rent` is the net tenant share after modeled housing assistance.
12. **Household, period and administration.** The SPM unit stands in for the LIEAP household. Annual income stands in for four times three calendar months and is compared with four times the three-month limits and thresholds. Institutions (ARSD :08.01), tribal service areas (ARSD :39), duplicate payments, funding availability (ARSD :11, :20(5)) and verification are not modeled.
13. **Years.** No year is verified. The [FY2021 plan, page 9](https://liheapch.acf.gov/sites/default/files/webfiles/docs/SD_Plan_2021.pdf#page=9), item 2.6, prints a $334 minimum ($668 from FY2022), so cells backfilled before October 2021 are unverified. The regions and heat-in-rent amounts that backfill from `2025-10-01` are unchanged in the FY2022 to FY2026 matrices and the rule. The 2018 manual (PDF dated 2017-12-05) is the latest published.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [FY2026 state-plan manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-sd-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [FY2026 benefit-matrix manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-sd-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml)
- [Policies and procedures manual manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-sd-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml)
- [LIHEAP annual figures 2026 manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission. The sources marked “needs ingest” above must be ingested before the modules can be proved.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-sd/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the FY2024 to FY2026 income limits (rule-based FY2024 and FY2026, the printed FY2025 table), first-tier thresholds, the 40 direct-payment cells and four heat-in-rent amounts (with FY2022 and FY2023 cells where encoded), the vendor cap on unpaid charges, full payment for wood and coal, the vendor cap for kerosene, heat in rent with zero and subsidized tenant shares, categorical SNAP eligibility, mixed-status household size and income, county regions, and countable income (Social Security net of Part B, unemployment insurance, regular cash help). Set heating type and county explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.body:
## Encoding debt

Vermont's Aid to the Aged, Blind or Disabled (AABD) program has no RuleSpec module. SSA administers the optional state supplement (rule 2761; an agreement under 33 V.S.A. § 1309(a)); the Department for Children and Families (DCF) pays the Essential Person (AABD-EP) grant (rule 2743). On `rulespec-us` `main` (`d8511cca7`, 2026-10-15), `us-vt/` holds only `policies/` (`cms/`, `income_tax/`).
