items.body:
Dispatch-ready encoding debt for the SSI spousal-deeming benefit rule and the definitions that classify SSI couples. Companion PolicyEngine work: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10138 (issue) and the pull request that cites this issue as `axiom: <this issue> queued`. Related: #1626, which queues 416.1202 and 416.1205 (resource deeming) and has the same corpus blocker. No handwritten RuleSpec has been created.

## Encoding debt and search evidence

PolicyEngine-US capped SSI under spousal income deeming at the individual Federal benefit rate, so a claimant with income of their own could get more with deeming than without it. 20 CFR 416.1163(e)(2) makes the benefit the lesser of the couple computation and the individual rate less the claimant's own countable income. PolicyEngine-US also found SSI couples (joint claims, and the ineligible spouse whose income is deemed) through tax-unit head and spouse roles, which do not appear in 416.1801(c), 416.1806 or 416.1160(d).

I listed the tracked tree of rulespec-us `origin/main` at `16a667719` (`git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main -- us/statutes/42 us/regulations`). The SSI modules present are `us/statutes/42/1382/a/1-3`, `1382/b`, `1382/e/1`, `1382a/b/2`, `1382a/b/4`, `1382b/a`, `1382c/a/1-2`, `1382f/a` and `1382f/c`. None is under `us/regulations/20-cfr/416/`. `us/statutes/42/1382/b.yaml` encodes the statutory benefit with and without an eligible spouse and reads income as a supplied input. It has no deeming rule and does not say who is an eligible spouse. An issue search for 416.1163, spousal deeming and eligible spouse found only #1626 and LTSS issues (#1578, #1588-#1592), which concern Medicaid spousal impoverishment rather than SSI.

New modules and companion fixtures:

- `us/regulations/20-cfr/416/1163.yaml` and `1163.test.yaml`, corpus citation `us/regulation/20/416/1163`. Pinned corpus line 6 of `data/corpus/provisions/us/regulation/2026-07-23-title-20-part-416.jsonl`.
- `us/regulations/20-cfr/416/1801.yaml` and `1801.test.yaml`, corpus citation `us/regulation/20/416/1801` (line 12), for the eligible-spouse definition in 416.1801(c).
- `us/regulations/20-cfr/416/1806.yaml` and `1806.test.yaml`, corpus citation `us/regulation/20/416/1806` (line 14), for who is a spouse.
- The ineligible-spouse definition in 416.1160(d), corpus citation `us/regulation/20/416/1160` (line 4). Encode it as a rule in a `1160.yaml` module, or in `1163.yaml` with a 416.1160(d) proof excerpt.
- Import the Federal benefit rates from `us/statutes/42/1382/b` and `us/statutes/42/1382f/a`. Treat countable income after 416.1112 and 416.1124 and the 416.1163(b)-(c) allocations as exact, legally scoped leaf inputs until those sections are encoded. Do not substitute tax-unit roles or tax dependency for spouse or household relationships.

## Corpus and signed encoder blocker

The same blocker as #1626. The rulespec-us toolchain pins corpus release `us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap`, corpus ref `8f7d60aaced28ee4252b9237f9d6e02360dc34bc`. At that ref, `2026-07-23-title-20-part-416.jsonl` has rows for 416.1160, 416.1163, 416.1801, 416.1802 and 416.1806 (source format `ecfr-xml`, source as of 2026-07-14). The pinned release manifest `manifests/releases/us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap.json` does not include the `2026-07-23-title-20-part-416` scope, so these rows are not dispatchable from the pinned release. Generated content must come from the signed encoder with its protected signer, and the billed run needs its own approval (#1403, #1416). The `.axiom/workflow-toolchain.toml` pins are axiom-encode `0.2.2092` (`3bf5a2af`), rules engine `89571cc2` and corpus `8f7d60aa`. Refresh and verify all refs at dispatch time.

## Regulation (verbatim, pinned corpus rows)

### 20 CFR 416.1163(d), (e) and (f)(5)

https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/chapter-III/part-416/subpart-K/section-416.1163

> (d) Determining your eligibility for SSI. (1) If the amount of your ineligible spouse's income that remains after appropriate allocations is not more than the difference between the Federal benefit rate for an eligible couple and the Federal benefit rate for an eligible individual, there is no income to deem to you from your spouse. In this situation, we subtract only your own countable income from the Federal benefit rate for an individual to determine whether you are eligible for SSI benefits.
>
> (2) If the amount of your ineligible spouse's income that remains after appropriate allocations is more than the difference between the Federal benefit rate for an eligible couple and the Federal benefit rate for an eligible individual, we treat you and your ineligible spouse as an eligible couple. We do this by:
>
> (i) Combining the remainder of your spouse's unearned income with your own unearned income and the remainder of your spouse's earned income with your earned income;
>
> (ii) Applying all appropriate income exclusions in §§ 416.1112 and 416.1124; and
>
> (iii) Subtracting the couple's countable income from the Federal benefit rate for an eligible couple. (See § 416.2025(b) for determination of the State supplementary payment amount.)
>
> (e) Determining your SSI benefit. (1) In determining your SSI benefit amount, we follow the procedure in paragraphs (a) through (d) of this section. However, we use your ineligible spouse's income in the second month prior to the current month. We vary this rule if any of the exceptions in § 416.1160(b)(2) applies (for example, if this is the first month you are eligible for payment of an SSI benefit or if you are again eligible after at least a month of being ineligible). In the first month of your eligibility for payment (or re-eligibility), we deem your ineligible spouse's income in the current month to determine both whether you are eligible for a benefit and the amount of your benefit. In the second month, we deem your ineligible spouse's income in that month to determine whether you are eligible for a benefit but we deem your ineligible spouse's income in the first month to determine the amount of your benefit.
>
> (2) Your SSI benefit under the deeming rules cannot be higher than it would be if deeming did not apply. Therefore, your benefit is the lesser of the amount computed under the rules in paragraph (d)(2) of this section or the amount remaining after we subtract only your own countable income from an individual's Federal benefit rate.
>
> (5) You become subject to the $30 Federal benefit rate. If you become a resident of a medical care facility and the $30 Federal benefit rate applies, we do not deem your ineligible spouse's income to you to determine your eligibility for SSI benefits beginning with the first month for which the $30 Federal benefit rate applies. In determining your benefit amount beginning with the first month for which the $30 Federal benefit rate applies, we use only your own countable income in a prior month, excluding any income deemed to you in that month from your ineligible spouse.

### 20 CFR 416.1163(g), Examples 2 and 3 (September 1986 rates: $336 individual, $504 couple)

> Example 2. In September 1986, Mr. Jones, a disabled individual, lives with his ineligible spouse, Mrs. Jones, and ineligible child, Christine. Mr. Jones and Christine have no income. Mrs. Jones has earned income of $401 a month and unearned income of $252 a month. Before we deem any income, we allocate $168 to Christine. We take the $168 allocation from Mrs. Jones' $252 unearned income, leaving $84 in unearned income. Since Mrs. Jones' total remaining income ($84 unearned plus $401 earned) is more than $168, which is the difference between the September Federal benefit rate for an eligible couple and the September Federal benefit rate for an eligible individual, we compute the combined countable income as we do for a couple. We apply the $20 general income exclusion to the unearned income, reducing it further to $64. We then apply the earned income exclusion ($65 plus one-half the remainder) to Mrs. Jones' earned income of $401, leaving $168. We combine the $64 countable unearned income and $168 countable earned income, and compare it ($232) with the $504 September Federal benefit rate for a couple, and determine that Mr. Jones is eligible. [...]
>
> Example 3. In September 1986, Mr. Smith, a disabled individual, lives with his ineligible spouse, Mrs. Smith, who earns $201 per month. Mr. Smith receives a pension (unearned income) of $100 a month. Since Mrs. Smith's income is greater than $168, [...] we deem all of her income to be available to both Mr. and Mrs. Smith and compute the combined countable income for the couple. We apply the $20 general income exclusion to Mr. Smith's $100 unearned income, leaving $80. Then we apply the earned income exclusion ($65 plus one-half of the remainder) to Mrs. Smith's $201, leaving $68. This gives the couple total countable income of $148. This is less than the $504 September Federal benefit rate for a couple, so Mr. Smith is eligible based on deeming. [...]

### 20 CFR 416.1801(c) (definitions)

https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/chapter-III/part-416/subpart-R/section-416.1801

> Eligible spouse means a person— (1) Who is eligible for SSI, (2) Whom we consider the spouse of another person who is eligible for SSI, and (3) Who was living in the same household with that person on— (i) The first day of the month following the date the application is filed (for the initial month of eligibility for payment based on that application); (ii) The date a request for reinstatement of eligibility is filed (for the month of such request); or (iii) The first day of the month, for all other months. An individual is considered to be living with an eligible spouse during temporary absences as defined in § 416.1149 and while receiving continued benefits under section 1611(e)(1) (E) or (G) of the Act.
>
> Spouse means a person's husband or wife under the rules of §§ 416.1806 through 416.1835 of this part.

### 20 CFR 416.1806

https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/chapter-III/part-416/subpart-R/section-416.1806

> (a) We will consider someone to be your spouse (and therefore consider you to be married) for SSI purposes if— (1) You are legally married under the laws of the State where your and his or her permanent home is (or was when you lived together); (2) We have decided that either of you is entitled to husband's or wife's Social Security insurance benefits as the spouse of the other (this decision will not affect your SSI benefits for any month before it is made); or (3) You and an unrelated person of the opposite sex are living together in the same household at or after the time you apply for SSI benefits, and you both lead people to believe that you are husband and wife.
>
> (b) if more than one person would qualify as your husband or wife under paragraph (a) of this section, we will consider the person you are presently living with to be your spouse for SSI purposes.

### 20 CFR 416.1160(d) and 416.1802(b)(1)

> Ineligible spouse means someone who lives with you as your husband or wife and is not eligible for SSI benefits.
>
> (b) If you have an eligible spouse—(1) Counting income. If you apply for or receive SSI benefits and have an eligible spouse as defined in § 416.1801(c), we will count your combined income and calculated the benefit amount for you as a couple. [...]

Federal benefit rates for the companion cases are from SSA's "SSI Federal Payment Amounts" table (https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/SSIamts.html, read 2026-10-12): 1986 $336.00 and $504.00; 2026 $994.00 and $1,491.00.

## Required outputs and mapping

Period: Month. Entity: Person, with an explicit same-household spouse relationship.

1. `ssi_spousal_deeming_applies`, Judgment (416.1163(d)): the ineligible spouse's income remaining after 416.1163(b)-(c) allocations is more than the couple rate less the individual rate. "Not more than" is the no-deeming side, so equality means no deeming.
2. `ssi_benefit_under_couple_computation`, Money (416.1163(d)(2)): couple rate less the couple's combined countable income (both spouses' remaining unearned and earned income combined, with the 416.1112 and 416.1124 exclusions applied once to the combined amounts). Floor at zero.
3. `ssi_benefit_without_spousal_deeming`, Money (416.1163(e)(2), second limb): individual rate less only the claimant's own countable income. Floor at zero.
4. `ssi_benefit_with_ineligible_spouse`, Money (416.1163(e)(2)): the lesser of outputs 2 and 3 when output 1 holds; output 3 otherwise.
5. (416.1163(f)(5)) While the $30 Federal benefit rate applies, no spousal income is deemed for eligibility or amount: the benefit is the $30 rate less only the claimant's own countable income. Import the $30 rate from `us/statutes/42/1382/e/1`.
6. `is_ssi_eligible_spouse`, Judgment (416.1801(c)): the person is eligible for SSI, is the spouse of another person eligible for SSI (416.1806), and lived in the same household with that person on the dates in (c)(3). Eligibility for SSI and the dated living-together facts are leaf inputs.
7. `is_ssi_spouse`, Judgment (416.1806): any of (a)(1)-(3), with (b) choosing the person presently lived with when more than one qualifies. Each condition is its own leaf input.
8. `is_ssi_ineligible_spouse`, Judgment (416.1160(d)): lives with the claimant as husband or wife and is not eligible for SSI. A spouse who is aged, blind or disabled but fails the citizenship or qualified-noncitizen condition is not eligible for SSI, so is an ineligible spouse.

Output 4 must never exceed output 3; this is the rule PolicyEngine-US lacked.

## Pasteable review_finding

```text
Encode 20 CFR 416.1163(d), (e)(2) and (f)(5) as a signed module at us/regulations/20-cfr/416/1163.yaml (corpus citation us/regulation/20/416/1163), and 416.1801(c), 416.1806 and 416.1160(d) at us/regulations/20-cfr/416/1801.yaml, 1806.yaml and 1160.yaml (corpus citations us/regulation/20/416/1801, /1806, /1160). No module for any 20 CFR part 416 section exists on rulespec-us origin/main 16a667719. Complete and sign the source bundle before dispatch: the pinned corpus ref 8f7d60aac has these rows in 2026-07-23-title-20-part-416.jsonl (lines 4, 6, 12, 14), but the pinned release us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap does not include that scope. Do not create unsupported citations.

Required Person/Month outputs, each with a verbatim proof excerpt: ssi_spousal_deeming_applies (Judgment, 416.1163(d): remaining spouse income after allocations is more than the couple rate less the individual rate; equality is no deeming); ssi_benefit_under_couple_computation (couple rate less combined countable income, floored at 0); ssi_benefit_without_spousal_deeming (individual rate less only own countable income, floored at 0); ssi_benefit_with_ineligible_spouse (the lesser of the two when deeming applies, per 416.1163(e)(2) 'cannot be higher than it would be if deeming did not apply', otherwise the no-deeming amount); the 416.1163(f)(5) rule that no spousal income is deemed while the $30 rate applies; is_ssi_spouse (416.1806(a)(1)-(3) and (b)); is_ssi_eligible_spouse (416.1801(c)(1)-(3)); is_ssi_ineligible_spouse (416.1160(d)).

Import Federal benefit rates from us/statutes/42/1382/b and us/statutes/42/1382f/a, and the $30 rate from us/statutes/42/1382/e/1. Countable income under 416.1112/416.1124 and the 416.1163(b)-(c) allocations may be exact leaf inputs until those sections are encoded; say so in each leaf's description. Spouse, marriage and living-together facts are leaf inputs named for their legal conditions. Never use tax filing roles, tax dependency or the age order of adults in a tax unit as a proxy for them. A spouse who is aged, blind or disabled but not eligible for SSI (for example on citizenship) is an ineligible spouse.

Add every companion case in this issue. Expectations are hand-computed from the CFR text, the 416.1163(g) examples and SSA's published Federal benefit rates, not from either engine. Refresh rulespec/corpus/rules-engine/encoder refs at dispatch; generated content requires the protected signer and a separately approved billed encoder run. After encoding, register pending oracle coverage for the new outputs and point the PolicyEngine adapter at ssi_if_takes_up, uncapped_ssi_without_spousal_deeming and ssi_claim_is_joint.
```

## Companion cases

Monthly amounts. Claimants are aged, blind or disabled citizens with resources within the limits; no living-arrangement reduction unless stated; no ineligible children unless stated. Expectations are hand-computed from the quoted CFR and SSA rate table. None comes from an engine.

| ID | Case | Deeming applies | Couple computation | Without deeming | Benefit | Source |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| D1 | Sept. 1986, Mr. Smith: own pension $100; ineligible spouse earns $201 | yes ($201 > $168) | $504 − $148 = $356 | $336 − $80 = $256 | $256 | 416.1163(g) Ex. 3, (e)(2) |
| D2 | Sept. 1986, Mr. Jones: no own income; spouse earns $401, unearned $252; one ineligible child with no income (allocation $168) | yes ($485 > $168) | $504 − $232 = $272 | $336 | $272 | 416.1163(g) Ex. 2, (e)(2) |
| D3 | Jan. 2026, aged claimant own Social Security $743; ineligible spouse Social Security $100 and wages $400 | yes ($500 > $497) | $1,491 − $990.50 = $500.50 | $994 − $723 = $271 | $271 | 416.1163(d)(2), (e)(2) |
| D4 | D3 with Social Security $579 and $78 | no ($478 ≤ $497) | n/a | $994 − $559 = $435 | $435 | 416.1163(d)(1) |
| D5 | Jan. 2026, no own income; ineligible spouse wages $967.50 | yes | $1,491 − $441.25 = $1,049.75 | $994 | $994 | 416.1163(e)(2) |
| D6 | Jan. 2026, spouse remaining income exactly $497 (unearned) | no (not more than) | n/a | $994 − own | own-income only | 416.1163(d)(1) |
| D7 | Jan. 2026, $30 rate applies, no own income; ineligible spouse wages $2,000 | not deemed | n/a | $30 | $30 | 416.1163(f)(5) |
| C1 | Married aged citizens living together, both eligible, sharing a household (and a tax unit) with a 90-year-old who is neither spouse | eligible couple | n/a | n/a | both is_ssi_eligible_spouse holds; the 90-year-old not_holds | 416.1801(c), 416.1806(a)(1) |
| C2 | Married couple living together; spouse aged but fails the citizenship condition | not an eligible couple | n/a | n/a | spouse is_ssi_ineligible_spouse holds; claimant is_ssi_eligible_spouse not_holds | 416.1801(c)(1), 416.1160(d) |
| C3 | Legally married, both eligible, living in different households on the first of the month with no 416.1149 temporary absence | not an eligible couple | n/a | n/a | is_ssi_eligible_spouse not_holds for both | 416.1801(c)(3)(iii) |
| C4 | Unrelated opposite-sex adults living together who lead people to believe they are husband and wife | spouse | n/a | n/a | is_ssi_spouse holds | 416.1806(a)(3) |
| C5 | Two people would qualify as spouse; the claimant presently lives with one | spouse is the one lived with | n/a | n/a | is_ssi_spouse holds only for that person | 416.1806(b) |

Properties to add as tests: output 4 ≤ output 3 for every input; with other inputs fixed, the benefit never rises when the claimant's or the spouse's income rises; output 4 equals output 3 whenever output 1 does not hold.

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Kentucky LIHEAP in Axiom, covering the agreed scope and effective periods of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with signed RuleSpec encodings and reproducible oracle validation.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9725 (branch `ky-liheap`), open and not yet merged. Scope, policy periods, module paths, source text, required outputs and companion tests are in the sections below. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## PolicyEngine implementation (historical snapshot)

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9725, open and not yet merged. Head `7bd0a99968` on 2026-10-03 (adds the Medicare premium deduction and military retirement pay, plus a merge of `main`). The merged commit will be recorded here once it exists.
- **Scope:** the regular heating subsidy component only. Winter crisis, spring and summer cooling subsidies, air conditioner units, weatherization, in-kind benefits and the Preventive Assistance Program are out of scope.
- **Policy periods:** federal fiscal years 2025 (2024-10-01 to 2025-09-30) and 2026 (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). The model reads FY2025 for period `2025` and FY2026 for period `2026`: the annual period stands for the heating season that ends in that year. Every parameter is dated `2024-10-01` with FY2025 and FY2026 references; the two benefit workbooks publish the same 384 heating amounts, so no second dated value is needed. The registry records `verified_years: "2025-2026"`. Earlier years use parameter backfilling and are unverified estimates.
- **Variables:** `ky_liheap`, `ky_liheap_eligible`, `ky_liheap_income_eligible`, `ky_liheap_income` and `ky_liheap_fpg`, under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/ky/dcbs/liheap/`. No new input variables.
- **Parameters:** `gov.states.ky.dcbs.liheap` (`earned_income_age`, `earned_income_sources`, `unearned_income_sources`, `social_security_medicare_premium_deduction`, `fpg_year_lag`, `income_limit`, `maximum_table_size`, and `payment/` with `coal_adjustment`, `dollars_per_point`, `fuel_points`, `income_bands`, `income_points/subsidized`, `income_points/unsubsidized`, `maximum_household_points`, `subsidized_housing_rate`).
- **Tests:** 31 YAML cases in five files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/ky/dcbs/liheap/` (`integration.yaml`, `ky_liheap.yaml`, `ky_liheap_eligible.yaml`, `ky_liheap_income.yaml`, `ky_liheap_income_eligible.yaml`).

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence in a manifest on axiom-corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-02 against the saved manifest list (`corpus-manifests.txt`, 1,000 names) and the saved Kentucky and federal LIHEAP manifests. Presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not checked. No manifest name contains "kar" or "921": there is no 921 KAR 4:116 manifest. `us-ky-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml` is the only Kentucky LIHEAP manifest. rulespec-us has no `us-ky/regulations/` tree yet; the paths below follow `us-nc/regulations/10a-ncac/71u/0210` and `us-ny/regulations/18-nycrr/387/12`.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-ky/regulations/921-kar/4/116/section-1` | Definitions: 1(5) economic unit, 1(8) gross household income, 1(10) household, 1(12) level of poverty, 1(15) subsidy component | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [921 KAR 4:116, engrossed PDF, pages 1-3 and 5](https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/downloads/docs/10174/document.engrossed.pdf#page=1) (6 pages, last amended effective 2021-11-23). The HTML page at apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/titles/921/004/116/, which the PR cites, carries the same text without page numbers. |
| `us-ky/regulations/921-kar/4/116/section-2` | 2(1)(a)-(d) application contents, including a Social Security number or permanent residency card for each member; 2(2) incomplete application | none | Same document, page 2. |
| `us-ky/regulations/921-kar/4/116/section-3` | 3(1) income at or below 130 percent of poverty unless the cabinet approves an increase; 3(2) responsible for heating or for heating as an undesignated portion of rent | none | Same document, page 2. |
| `us-ky/regulations/921-kar/4/116/section-4` | 4(1)(a)-(e) subsidy benefit rule; lower benefits in federally assisted housing or with a utility allowance | none | Same document, page 3. |
| `us-ky/regulations/921-kar/4/116/section-8` | 8(1) five-working-day determination; 8(3) denial when required information is not provided | none | Same document, page 5. |
| `us-ky/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-1` | 1.8 gross income; 1.9 countable income checklist (pages 5-7) | `us-ky/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | In manifest `us-ky-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml` (report period 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Official copy: [Kentucky FY2026 LIHEAP plan, pages 5-9 and 33-34](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/state-plans/KY_Plan_2026.pdf#page=5). The checkbox states are visible only in the PDF rendering; a plain text extraction does not carry them. |
| `us-ky/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-2` | 2.1 150 percent threshold; 2.3 renters with utilities in rent; 2.4-2.6 benefit variables and the $15-$250 range (pages 8-9) | `us-ky/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | Same manifest. |
| `us-ky/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-17` | 17.2 identification documents; 17.3 citizenship or qualified non-citizen verification; 17.4 income verification (pages 33-34) | `us-ky/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | Same manifest. |
| `us-ky/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2025/section-1` and `/section-2` | FY2025 edition of 1.8-1.9 (pages 5-6) and 2.1-2.6 (pages 8-9). Differences from FY2026: the Social Security sub-box "Including MediCare" (deduction) is checked, "Legal settlements" is unchecked, minimum benefit $134 | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [Kentucky FY2025 LIHEAP plan, pages 5-6 and 8-9](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2025/state-plans/KY_Plan_2025.pdf#page=5) (51 pages, report period 2024-10-01 to 2025-09-30). |
| `us-ky/policies/dcbs/liheap-benefit-matrix/fy2026/heating` | Worksheet `rev benefit income range`: monthly income ranges and heating amounts for sizes 1-8, six fuels, unsubsidized (rows 5-43) and subsidized (rows 52-90); `Subsidy points` and `Points Description`: the point rule behind the cells. The `if no funding FFY26` worksheet is a contingency and is not used. | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [FY2026 benefit workbook](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/benefits-matricies/KY_BenefitMatrix_Heat-Cool_2026.xlsx) (SHA-256 `819fedc9…9cf6`, saved under `sources/ky/`). |
| `us-ky/policies/dcbs/liheap-benefit-matrix/fy2025/heating` | Worksheet `subsidy benefits` (unsubsidized rows 3-41, subsidized rows 45-83) with `Subsidy points` and `points` | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [FY2025 benefit workbook](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2025/benefits-matricies/KY_BenefitMatrix_2025.xlsx). Its 384 heating amounts equal the FY2026 cells; only the income ranges differ (2024 guidelines), and five of them are mistyped (see Interpretations and gaps). |
| `us-ky/policies/dcbs/liheap-fact-sheet/fy2025-2026/eligibility` | Monthly gross income limits for sizes 1-8; $688 per additional member; heating-responsibility and document requirements | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [DCBS FY2025-2026 LIHEAP fact sheet](https://www.capky.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/2025-2026-LIHEAP-Fact-Sheet-V2.pdf) (1 page, hosted by the statewide contracted administrator). |
| `us-ky/policies/dcbs/liheap-fall-subsidy-announcement/2025-10-30` | Benefit depends on housing category, fuel and income; benefit may be credited to the account | none | Not in a corpus manifest; supporting only. [Community Action Kentucky announcement, 2025-10-30](https://www.capky.org/news/liheap-fall-subsidy-one-time-heating-assistance-in-kentuckys-120-counties/). |
| `us/` poverty guidelines module | 2025 guidelines ($15,650 for one person, $5,500 per additional person) for FY2026; 2024 guidelines ($15,060 and $5,380) for FY2025 | none for 2024 or 2025 | `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml` holds the 2026 guidelines only; it notes that the undated path in `us-hhs-poverty-guidelines.yaml` was never extracted (that manifest's contents were not saved for this review). Official notices: [FR Doc. 2025-01377, 90 FR 5917, page 1](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-17/pdf/2025-01377.pdf#page=1) and [FR Doc. 2024-00796, 89 FR 2961, page 2](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2024-01-17/pdf/2024-00796.pdf#page=2). |
| `us/statutes/8/1611` | 8 U.S.C. 1611(a): an alien who is not a qualified alien is not eligible for any Federal public benefit | none found | rulespec-us already has `us/statutes/8/1641` and `us/statutes/8/1641/b` (qualified alien). No section 1611 module and no U.S. Code manifest name was found in `corpus-manifests.txt`. Official copy: [8 U.S.C. 1611 (2023 edition)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2023-title8/html/USCODE-2023-title8-chap14-subchapI-sec1611.htm). |

## Source text (verbatim)

Local copies of every file quoted here are under `output/liheap-axiom-issues-2026-10-02/sources/ky/`. Line-break whitespace is collapsed; nothing else is changed.

**Household.** 921 KAR 4:116 Section 1(10) (page 1):

> "Household" means an individual or group of individuals who are living together in the principal residence as one (1) economic unit and who purchase energy in common.

Section 1(5) (page 1):

> "Economic unit" means one (1) or more persons sharing common living arrangements.

**Gross household income.** Section 1(8) (page 1):

> "Gross household income" means all earned and unearned income, including lump sum payments received by a household during the calendar month preceding the month of application.

**Level of poverty.** Section 1(12) (page 1):

> "Level of poverty" or "poverty level" means the degree to which a household's gross income matches the official poverty income guidelines published annually in the Federal Register by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, under authority of 42 U.S.C. 9902(2).

**Subsidy component.** Section 1(15) (page 2):

> "Subsidy component" means the heating or cooling component that provides an eligible household with: (a) A payment to the household's energy provider; or (b) A payment to a landlord, if utilities are included in the rent.

**Application.** Section 2(1) (page 2): "A household or authorized representative applying for LIHEAP shall provide to an agency the following: (a) Proof of household income; (b) Most recent: 1. Heating bill; 2. Cooling bill; or 3. Verification that heating or cooling is included in the rent; (c) Statement of household demographics; and (d) A Social Security number, or a permanent residency card, for each household member." Section 2(2) (page 2): "An application shall not be considered complete until the required information, as specified in subsection (1) of this section, is received by the agency."

**Income limit.** Section 3(1) (page 2): "Income. Gross household income shall be at or below 130 percent of the official poverty income guidelines updated annually in the Federal Register by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services pursuant to 42 U.S.C. 9902(2), unless: (a) Program funding is enhanced through a federal or state award; or (b) The cabinet approves an increase to the poverty income guidelines due to funding availability."

FY2026 plan, Section 2.1 (page 8), the single row under "2.1 Designate the income eligibility threshold used for the heating component:" reads "All Household Sizes", "HHS Poverty Guidelines", "150.00%". The FY2025 plan, Section 2.1 (page 8), carries the same row.

Fact sheet (1 page), "ELIGIBILITY: 1) Household income must be at or below the following, relative to household size:"

| Household Size | Gross Monthly Income | Household Size | Gross Monthly Income |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | $ 1,957 | 5 | $ 4707 |
| 2 | $ 2644 | 6 | $ 5394 |
| 3 | $ 3332 | 7 | $ 6082 |
| 4 | $ 4019 | 8 | $ 6769 |

followed by "Add $688 for each additional family member".

2025 poverty guidelines, FR Doc. 2025-01377 (page 1): one person $15,650, two $21,150, three $26,650, four $32,150, five $37,650, six $43,150, seven $48,650, eight $54,150; "For families/households with more than 8 persons, add $5,500 for each additional person." 2024 guidelines, FR Doc. 2024-00796 (page 2): $15,060, $20,440, $25,820, $31,200, $36,580, $41,960, $47,340, $52,720; "For families/households with more than 8 persons, add $5,380 for each additional person."

**Countable income.** FY2026 plan, Section 1.8 (page 5): "1.8. In determining a household's income eligibility for LIHEAP, do you use gross income or net income?" The "Gross Income" box is checked. | Gross household income | `ky_liheap_income` | SPM unit, year | Sum over members of the earned sources (wages, net self-employment, specified-service business, partnership and S-corporation, farm operations) for members aged 18 or over, plus the unearned sources listed in `unearned_income_sources` (unemployment, strike pay, SSI, Kentucky State Supplementation, pensions, military retirement income (retiree pay plus SBP annuities), railroad benefits, retirement distributions, financial assistance, gambling winnings, rental and farm rent income, alimony, child support, interest, dividends, workers' compensation, disability benefits, veterans' benefits, state tax refunds), each source floored at zero, plus Social Security, counted gross for FY2025 and net of the Medicare Part B premium the person pays (`medicare_part_b_premium`, zero when not enrolled or when a Medicare Savings Program pays it) from FY2026, plus annual `tanf`. |
| Income eligible | `ky_liheap_income_eligible` | SPM unit, year | Income divided by 12 is at or below ceil(1.5 × guideline / 12) for sizes 1-8; above 8 the size-8 limit plus ceil(1.5 × additional-person amount / 12) per extra member ($688 for FY2026). |
| Eligible | `ky_liheap_eligible` | SPM unit, year | Income eligible; a positive heating bill for the reported fuel or heat included in rent; at least one member who is a citizen or qualified noncitizen (8 U.S.C. 1641); and every member either has a Social Security number (`ssn_card_type` not `NONE`) or is a lawful permanent resident. |
| Heating payment | `ky_liheap` | SPM unit, year | Points = min(size, 5) + income points + fuel points, less 1 for a two-person coal household. Income band from monthly income against ceil(guideline × 0.75, 1, 1.25 / 12); unsubsidized points 4, 3, 2, 1 by band, subsidized 1, 2, 3, 4. Fuel points: electricity 6, propane 5, fuel oil or kerosene 4, natural gas 3, coal 2, wood 1; other fuels 0 and pay $0. Amount = ceil(points × 16.66); in subsidized housing (`receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing`) ceil(amount × 0.3). Not capped at the bill. |
