Plan 1.9 checks SSI and TANF; Section 17.4 lists the DCBS award letter for KTAP and State Supplementation. 11,928 + 744 + 3,516. | income $16,188 | 921 KAR 4:116 Section 1(8); FY2026 plan pages 6 and 34 |

## Interpretations and gaps

- **Subsidized ordering conflicts with the regulation.** 921 KAR 4:116 Section 4(1)(c) and plan Section 2.4 give the highest benefit to the lowest income. The workbook's subsidized rows take 30 percent of the unsubsidized rows in reverse order (E52 `=ROUNDUP(E8*0.3,0)`, E55 `=ROUNDUP(E5*0.3,0)`), so the published subsidized payment rises with income. Both workbooks do this. The PR reproduces the published cells (subsidized income points 1, 2, 3, 4). Under the regulation's ordering a one-person natural gas household at $0 would get ceil(134 × 0.3) = $41, not $26. Every subsidized companion case (7, 8, 9) depends on this choice. Which ordering agencies pay is unconfirmed.
- **Two-person coal.** `Subsidy points` H8 is `=2+1+4` (one fuel point, which is wood's) and H9:H11 are typed to match, so the two-person coal cells equal the wood cells (117, 100, 84, 67; subsidized 21, 26, 30, 36). Every other size gives coal two points. The PR keeps the published cells through a −1 adjustment at size 2 (`coal_adjustment`). Case 7 includes these cells as published.
- **Additional-member increment.** The fact sheet says "Add $688 for each additional family member". The workbook's own C45 reads 687 (`=D43-D38`, 6,769 − 6,082), and its "Adjusted POP" table T37:T42 rounds each whole limit (7,457; 8,144; 8,832; 9,519; 10,207; 10,894). The PR follows the fact sheet: ceil(5,500 × 1.5 / 12) = 688 per member, giving 7,457; 8,145; 8,833; 9,521; 10,209; 10,897. The three readings agree at size 9 only. `ky_liheap_income_eligible.yaml` Case 1 (size 10 at $8,145 a month, eligible) and Case 3 (size 12 at $9,521 eligible, $9,522 not) rest on the fact sheet reading.
- **Household-size points above five.** `Points Description` B10:B16 lists size points 1 to 6 with "6 and above" 6, but every published cell caps size points at 5 (`Subsidy points` E28 `=5+6+4`, label "5 and above", maximum 15 points = $250 = plan Section 2.6). The PR caps at 5.
- **Income bands above size 8.** The matrix prints rows only to size 8. For larger households the PR uses ceil(guideline × 0.75, 1, 1.25 / 12), which matches Q37:T42. Case 6 depends on this.
- **Band boundaries and rounding.** FY2026 bands end at ceil(guideline × rate / 12) with the next band starting one cent higher (`=D7+0.01`). FY2025 bands are labelled "76-100%" and start one dollar higher (`=D3+1`), leaving cents between 942 and 943 unassigned; the PR treats any income above the rounded end as the next band in both years. The FY2025 `subsidy benefits` worksheet also mistypes several ranges: D16 = 2828 (T11 holds 2827.5; 3,228 under the 2024 guideline), D20 = 2850 (S12; 3,250), the size-6 unsubsidized block repeats the size-2 ranges (D28 `=Q28`), D33 = 2935 (Q15 holds 2934.75; 2,959) and D38 = 2895 (Q16; 3,295). The FY2025 `Subsidy points` worksheet carries the consistent ranges. The PR derives every band from the guideline, so it reproduces the amounts but not those five mistyped ranges. Case 2 (size 1) is unaffected.
- **Guideline year.** The fact sheet does not name the guideline year; $1,957 = ceil(15,650 × 1.5 / 12) identifies the 2025 guidelines for FY2026, and the FY2025 workbook's 1,883 identifies 2024. The FY2026 worksheet title "LIHEAP Benefit Matrix 2024-2025" and its P column (1255 = 15,060 / 12) are stale; Q11:T11 use 15,650. The `if no funding FFY26` worksheet is not used.
- **Income limit base.** The regulation's base is 130 percent (Section 3(1)); the plans set 150 percent under 3(1)(b). The PR stores 1.5 and the one-year lag as parameters.
- **Social Security and Medicare.** The FY2026 plan checks "Excluding MediCare deduction"; the FY2025 plan checks "Including MediCare" (deduction). A dated parameter (`social_security_medicare_premium_deduction`: false from 2024-10-01, true from 2025-10-01) switches the treatment. From FY2026 the PR subtracts the Part B premium the person pays, `medicare_part_b_premium`, which is zero for a person who is not enrolled and excludes the share a Medicare Savings Program pays, since that share is not withheld from the check; no Part D premium variable exists. `ky_liheap_income.yaml` Case 3 (2026: a $12,000 retiree whose premium an MSP covers keeps $12,000; a $23,600 retiree is counted at $21,165.20; a $2,000 benefit is floored at $0) and Case 9 (2025: $22,700 counted gross); `integration.yaml` Case 8 ($23,600 retiree eligible for $84 only because of the deduction) and Case 9 (FY2025, $22,700, over the limit).
- **At least one citizen or qualified member.** No Kentucky text states a household-level immigration rule. The PR requires one member who is a citizen or qualified alien, resting on 8 U.S.C. 1611(a) and plan Section 17.3, and counts every member in size and income because Section 1(10) has no carve-out. `ky_liheap_eligible.yaml` Case 2 depends on this: a DACA parent with a work-authorized number, wages $29,120, and a citizen child aged 4, electricity with a $1,440 bill, is eligible; $2,426.67 a month is above 2,204 and not above 2,644 (size 2, row 13), E13 = $150. The qualified-alien test is the shared `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant` (8 U.S.C. 1641 statuses; no five-year bar, no SAVE check).
- **Per-member Social Security number or residency card.** Section 2(1)(d) names each household member; plan Section 17.2 requires the card from all adults and only requests it from other members. The PR applies the regulation to every member, so a child with neither a number nor permanent residence makes the household ineligible. No PR test isolates a child; Case 11 is the same under both readings. The default `ssn_card_type` is CITIZEN, so a caller must send NONE to trigger the rule.
- **Utility allowance.** Section 4(1)(e) lowers benefits for "federally assisted housing or receiving a utility allowance". The PR selects the subsidized schedule by `receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing`; a `hud_utility_allowance` amount alone does not (`integration.yaml` Case 2, household 3, $134).
- **Heat in rent.** A household with `heat_expense_included_in_rent` is responsible under Section 3(2)(c) and gets the full table amount for its fuel; the landlord verification in plan Section 2.3 is not modelled. `heating_type` is a required input; heat in rent with an unspecified fuel is eligible and paid $0 (`ky_liheap_eligible.yaml` Case 5).
- **Not capped at the bill.** Section 4(1) pays "the full benefit amount" and the announcement says the subsidy "can be applied as a credit on utility account"; `integration.yaml` Case 1 household 1 pays $134 on a $10 bill.
- **Fuels.** Kerosene takes the fuel oil column (`Points Description` I5 "Fuel Oil/Kerosene"; Section 7(1)(c) prices kerosene for the subsidy component): `ky_liheap.yaml` Case 6, $150. OTHER, SOLAR, NONE and UNSPECIFIED have no column and pay $0.
- **Income sources.** The PR counts existing net self-employment, specified-service, partnership and farm inputs once, each floored at zero, so a loss in one source does not offset another (`ky_liheap_income.yaml` Cases 1, 4, 8); Section 1(8) says "gross" and plan 17.4 lists "Records of income and expenses on farm or rental income". `rental_income` is assumed non-negative (settled). Workers' compensation and employer disability benefits are counted under "Insurance payments made directly to the insured". Military retirement income is separate from `pension_income`: count `military_retirement_income` (retiree pay plus SBP annuities) once beside pensions. State tax refunds (`salt_refund_income`) stand for "Income tax refunds"; `financial_assistance` for "Cash gifts"; `gambling_winnings` for lottery winnings. Jury duty pay, commissions, legal settlements, other lump sums and the WIA and work-study exclusions cannot be isolated with existing inputs. TANF uses the annual `tanf` aggregate (includes `ky_ktap` and take-up).
- **Household and period.** The SPM unit stands for the household that purchases energy in common (Section 1(10)); annual income divided by 12 stands for "the calendar month preceding the month of application" (Section 1(8)). Application windows (November 3 to December 12, 2025), pre-registration priority and the five-working-day rule are not modelled.
- **Plan minimum.** The FY2025 plan's $134 minimum benefit (Section 2.6) contradicts its own workbook, whose lowest heating cell is $15 (I45). The FY2026 plan states $15.
- **Crisis, cooling, weatherization** and in-kind benefits (Sections 3(3), 3(4), 4(2), 4(3), 10(3)) are out of scope.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [FY2026 state-plan manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ky-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)

These FY2026 manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Link the PE PR and agree the component scope, effective periods, inputs, and outputs. Cover the eligibility and benefit-calculation behavior actually in scope; identify any excluded program components explicitly.
- [ ] Audit official sources and reuse existing corpus content. Ingest missing official documents with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance; obtain signed ingest/release admission. Keep any toolchain or corpus-pin change in its own gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state rule modules with the approved encoder, placing state content under `us-ky/` in the canonical layout. Include source-grounded proofs, benefit parameters where applicable, and companion tests for representative cases, boundaries, and ineligibility. Every test supplies all local inputs.
- [ ] Use personal-Codex local generation followed by exact-commit reviewed-candidate promotion for eligible modules: review the rule/test bytes, obtain the protected allowlist entry for the commit/base branch, and run protected validation/signing with the required approval. Retain the signed manifests and evidence that rule/test bytes are unchanged.
- [ ] Assemble and validate a runnable program with the required indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing blocker before declaring the complete program shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) is currently open.
- [ ] Add concept/input/output mappings and reproducible fixtures in axiom-oracles against the merged PE implementation, pinned to an exact commit. Record units and periods, compare representative and boundary cases, and resolve or explicitly disposition mismatches against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, and oracle PRs and successful CI/promotion evidence. Record the shipped scope and any remaining gaps.

## Contribution route

Use the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion contract](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion), added by [axiom-encode#1696](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/pull/1696). It validates and signs explicitly admitted reviewed content without regenerating it; it does not authenticate the original generating runtime. The [planned personal-Codex experiment](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1622#issuecomment-5940016560) records the process. The five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs are not prerequisites for testing this route.

This issue tracks work to ship; it does not claim the encoding, promotion experiment, or PE parity validation is already complete.

items.title: [pe-parity] Count military Survivor Benefit Plan annuities in 26 state benefit income definitions: MO and TX TANF, MO SAB and 23 child care programs (PE-US #10317)

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Encoding debt: military Survivor Benefit Plan annuities in 26 state benefit income definitions

**Parity status: queued.** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10317 makes 26 state benefit programs count a military Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) annuity as income: Missouri TANF, Texas TANF, Missouri Supplemental Aid to the Blind and 23 child care subsidy programs. rulespec-us has no module for any of these income definitions. The signed encoder is blocked for two reasons:

- **Sources.** Several sources are not on axiom-corpus `main` or not in the signed release that rulespec-us pins. Each program block below says where its source is: the corpus citation, whether the manifest is at the pinned corpus ref `4cf99d445019a97e260514de5533bbc3e1baacaf`, and what needs ingest.
- **Approval.** Each signed encoder run is billed and needs separate approval, which a PolicyEngine session cannot give.

No encoder or workflow was run. RuleSpec must come from the signed encoder; never hand-write it.

## PolicyEngine change

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10317 (branch `fix-sbp-benefit-income-sources`, head `f297b6ac67`), open.
- **Background:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10182 moved SBP annuities out of `military_retirement_pay` (a retiree's own pay) into a new input, `military_retirement_pay_survivors`, and added `military_retirement_income`, which adds the two. The benefit income lists still named only `military_retirement_pay`, so an SBP annuity counted as $0.
- **The fix:** #10317 replaces `military_retirement_pay` with `military_retirement_income` in 43 entries of 41 benefit income lists. This issue covers the 26 lists that have no other open pe-parity issue. The other lists are covered by notes on their own issues: the LIHEAP issues #1532 (AL), #1533 (GA), #1534 (FL), #1535 (OK), #1537 (RI), #1538 (AR), #1539 (SD), #1540 (OH), #1465 (KY), #1468 (IN), #1479 (OR) and #1482 (MD), and the child care issues #1757 (HI), #1737 (PA) and #1736 (MO CCS).
- **Tests:** `tx_tanf_gross_unearned_income.yaml` (Texas TANF, retiree pay plus an SBP payment), `ny_ccap_countable_income.yaml` Case 16 and `mo_sab_countable_income.yaml` Case 39 set an SBP annuity. The new code-health check `policyengine_us/tests/code_health/test_military_retirement_readers.py` fails if a benefit income list names `military_retirement_pay` without the survivor annuity input, so it pins the other lists.

## What Axiom has (rulespec-us `main` `fa533144`, 2026-10-22)

No module encodes any of the 26 income definitions. Each block below says what `us-<state>/` holds. Searches for "military retirement", "Survivor Benefit Plan", "SBP" and "<state> child care" found no open issue for these programs.

## Required outputs

For each program: the countable (unearned) income output that its block names, with the entity and period the program uses. Military retired pay and an SBP annuity each count in full and once. An SBP annuity is paid by the Department of Defense to a retiree's surviving spouse or child; it is not a Social Security survivor benefit and not a VA payment.

## Companion tests

Each block gives one case: one adult (the person whose income the program counts), an SBP annuity of $800 a month and no other income. The expected countable income is $800 a month, or $9,600 a year for an annual program, with any rounding or conversion that the program's rule prescribes. Each value comes from the quoted rule text; none uses PolicyEngine output.

## Interpretations and limits

- **Massachusetts CCFA from 2023-10-01.** The closed source lists name "Retirement income" and do not define it. PolicyEngine reads an SBP annuity as retirement income. If EEC does not, the 2023 and 2025 periods count $0.
- **Oregon ERDC.** OAR 414-175-0035(52)(a)(A) names benefits that "employees receive"; a survivor's annuity counts through the residual rule in 414-175-0030(1)(c).
- **Minnesota CCAP.** Minn. Stat. 256P.06 subd. 3(2)(ix) counts "retirement benefits" with no tax condition. Item (xi), income from members of the armed forces "unless excluded from income taxes", is not applied to an SBP annuity, which is paid to a survivor, not a member.
- **Stale PolicyEngine references** that the blocks note: Ohio's rule is now OAC 5180:6-1-03 (eff. 2026-08-01), not 5180:2-16-03; Colorado's list is 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111(I) (3.105.1(I) in the 2023 text), not Section 7.105; Rhode Island's Income definition is 29, not 30; Pennsylvania Part I.J is on file page 60; West Virginia 5.2.4.4 is on file page 55.

## Dispatch

For each program, after its source is in the pinned signed release, paste a `review_finding` of this form, with the block's citation, quote and test:

> Encode <program> countable income (corpus <citation>, file page <N>) at <module path>: count military retired pay and a military Survivor Benefit Plan annuity, each in full and once, under "<quoted item>". Output <entity> <period> countable income. Add the companion case: an SBP annuity of $800 a month and no other income gives $800 a month.

## Programs

In this body: Missouri TANF, Missouri SAB, Texas TANF, Arkansas SRA, Colorado CCCAP, DC CCSP, Delaware POC, Florida School Readiness, Idaho ICCP, Kansas CCAP, Kentucky CCAP, Massachusetts CCFA and Maryland CCS. In the first comment: Maine CCAP, Michigan CDC, Minnesota CCAP, Nebraska CCS, New Mexico CCAP, Nevada CCDP, New York CCAP, Ohio PFCC, Oregon ERDC, Rhode Island CCAP, Vermont CCFAP, Washington WCCC and West Virginia CCAP.

The blocks name each program's list under `policyengine_us/parameters/gov/states/`. Pages are file pages (1-indexed). Sources were read on 2026-10-22 against axiom-corpus `main` `e26ec7b`.

## Program blocks (1 of 2)

### MO TANF (Temporary Assistance) — `mo/dss/tanf/income/sources/unearned.yaml`

- **Existing rulespec-us issue:** none. #1444 covers Missouri TA unit composition and Appendix B, not income sources.
- **Existing rulespec-us module:** none. `us-mo/` holds only SNAP manual modules (`policies/dss/snap/...`, `manual/dss/snap/...`), CMS Medicaid/CHIP levels and income tax.
- **Proposed module path:** `us-mo/policies/dss/tanf/0210-015-05/block-1.yaml`. This follows `us-mo/policies/dss/snap/1105-000-00/1105-015-00/1105-015-04/block-1.yaml`, which mirrors its corpus path.
- **Corpus citation:** `us-mo/manual/dss/tanf/0210-015-05` in `manifests/us-mo-tanf-state-policy-manual.yaml` (expression date 2023-09-13; at pinned ref: yes). Official copy: [Missouri TA/Case Management Manual 0210.015.05](https://dssmanuals.mo.gov/temporary-assistance-case-management/0210-015-05/) (HTML, no pages).
- **Law (verbatim):** "Possible sources of Unearned Income include but are not limited to: … annuities (AN-include) … military retirement (MR-include)". The same list has "union fund/pension benefits/retirement (UF-include)".
- **Exclusions checked:** I read the 0210.015.05 exclude codes, 0210.015.35 Income Excluded, .35.40 Governmental Payments and .35.50 Other Income (HTML). No item excludes a military survivor annuity. The closest item is a recipient rule in .35.50: "The income of any SSI, SSI-SP, SP or SAB recipient living in a Temporary Assistance household except the income, other than SSI, of an SSI child who is applying for or receives Title XIX."
- **Required output:** the assistance group's gross unearned income per month, including military retirement pay and SBP annuities (PE `mo_tanf_gross_unearned_income`, SPMUnit, MONTH).
- **Companion test:** Inputs: one adult in the assistance group (not an SSI or SAB recipient) with a military SBP annuity of $800 a month and no other income. Expected gross unearned income: $800 a month. Derivation: "annuities (AN-include)". Unearned income gets no disregard, so the result needs no arithmetic.
- **Notes:** The signed release does not carry this source; #1444 says the same about this manifest. Its us-mo manual scopes are `2026-05-27-mo-snap-manual-r2026-07-15-self-contained` and `2026-07-13-recovery`. The newest memo cited on the page is IM-162 (October 10, 2019). The page title has a "Protected:" label, but the text is public. An SBP recipient who also receives SSI or SAB has all income excluded under .35.50.

### MO SAB (Supplemental Aid to the Blind) — `mo/dss/ssp/sab/income/sources/unearned.yaml`

- **Existing rulespec-us issue:** none.
- **Existing rulespec-us module:** none. `us-mo/` has no SAB or SSI-supplement module; only SNAP, CMS and income-tax modules are present.
- **Proposed module path:** `us-mo/policies/dss/sab/0410-000-00/0410-015-00/0410-015-10/block-1.yaml`. This follows the nested SNAP layout `us-mo/policies/dss/snap/1105-000-00/1105-015-00/...`.
- **Corpus citation:** `us-mo/manual/dss/sab/0410-000-00/0410-015-00/0410-015-10` in `manifests/us-mo-ssi-state-supplement.yaml` (expression date 2026-09-11; at pinned ref: yes). Official copy: [Missouri SAB Manual 0410.015.10 Unearned Income](https://dssmanuals.mo.gov/supplemental-aid-to-the-blind/0410-000-00/0410-015-00/0410-015-10/) (HTML, no pages).
- **Law (verbatim):** "Unearned income includes the following: … Annuities, Pensions, and Compensations: … Military retirement … Annuities." In 0410.020.00, the rule budgets monthly: "After exclusions, standard exemptions, and other deductions are allowed, total the remaining monthly income."
- **Exclusions checked:** I read 0410.015.15 Income Excluded (HTML). No item excludes a military survivor annuity. The closest item covers VA pensions only: "Any benefits designated for a veteran’s dependent."
- **Required output:** the claimant's countable unearned income per month, including military retirement pay and SBP annuities (PE `mo_sab_countable_income`, Person, MONTH).
- **Companion test:** Inputs: one SAB claimant with a military SBP annuity of $800 a month and no other income. Expected countable unearned income: $800 a month. Derivation: "Annuities." (item 11 of the "Annuities, Pensions, and Compensations" list). SSI does not apply because the claimant has no SSI.
- **Notes:** The signed release does not carry this source; its us-mo manual scopes are listed under MO TANF. The expression date is the fetch date, because the manual sections carry only IM memo dates (latest IM-162, October 10, 2019). The page lists are unlabeled HTML ordered lists, so "C2" and "C11" in the PE notes are positional (third list, items 2 and 11).

### TX TANF — `tx/tanf/income/sources/unearned.yaml`

- **Existing rulespec-us issue:** none. Merged PRs #507 and #516 encoded the TANF grant tables and proration only.
- **Existing rulespec-us module:** none for A-1320. Related modules are `us-tx/policies/hhs/texas-works-handbook/c-110-tanf.yaml`, `c-110-tanf/block-2.yaml` and `a-1340-income-limits/block-16.yaml`.
- **Proposed module path:** `us-tx/policies/hhs/texas-works-handbook/a-1320-types-income/block-<n>.yaml`, where `<n>` is the corpus row that holds A-1324.20. This follows `a-1340-income-limits/block-16.yaml`.
- **Corpus citation:** `us-tx/manual/hhs/texas-works-handbook/a-1320-types-income` in `manifests/us-tx-manuals.yaml` (expression date 2026-05-27; at pinned ref: yes). Official copy: [Texas Works Handbook A-1320 Types of Income, A-1324.20 Veterans Benefits](https://fhb.hhs.texas.gov/handbooks/texas-works-handbook/a-1320-types-income) (HTML, no pages).
- **Law (verbatim):** In A-1324.20 (Revision 15-4, effective October 1, 2015), TANF and SNAP: "Surviving spouses and/or children of service members who die while on active duty may be entitled to SBP payments made by DFAS-CL." and "The gross amount of any SBP payment is counted as unearned income." The same section says of military retirement: "The gross payment is counted as unearned income."
- **Exclusions checked:** I read A-1320 (A-1321 to A-1326, HTML), whose TANF and SNAP intro says "Income that is not specifically listed in this section must be counted." No TANF exclusion covers SBP. The closest item is "All veterans benefits are exempt from income", which is under the "Medical Programs" heading only.
- **Required output:** each certified-group member's gross unearned income per month, including gross military retirement pay and the gross SBP payment (PE `tx_tanf_gross_unearned_income`, Person, MONTH, summed for the budget group).
- **Companion test:** Inputs: one adult with a military SBP annuity of $800 a month and no other income. Expected gross unearned income: $800 a month. Derivation: "The gross amount of any SBP payment is counted as unearned income." A monthly payment needs no conversion.
- **Notes:** This source is probably in the signed release. Its scope `us-tx/manual/2026-05-27-tx-manuals-r2026-07-15-self-contained` comes from this manifest, and the c-110-tanf module already cites it; I did not confirm the A-1320 row itself. The manifest URL is on www.hhs.texas.gov, and the PE reference URL is on fhb.hhs.texas.gov. The same section says the SBP is reduced by VA DIC, and DIC is counted separately as a VA benefit. The SBP input must therefore be the payment after the DIC offset, before tax withholding.

### AR SRA (child care, School Readiness Assistance) — `ar/ade/oec/sra/income/sources.yaml`

- **Existing rulespec-us issue:** none.
- **Existing rulespec-us module:** none. `us-ar/` holds DHS TEA manual modules (`policies/dhs/tea/manual/2024/*`), income tax and CMS; it has no child-care module.
- **Proposed module path:** `us-ar/policies/ade/oec/sra/manual/2023/countable-unearned-income.yaml`. This follows `us-ar/policies/dhs/tea/manual/2024/income-eligibility-budget.yaml`.
- **Corpus citation:** none; needs ingest. The FSU Procedural Manual is in no manifest; the corpus holds only the AR CCDF Plan (`us-ar/policy/acf/ccdf-plan/fy2025-2027`). Official copy: [FSU Procedural Manual (June 2023), page 20](https://dese.ade.arkansas.gov/Files/FSU-Procedural-Manual-June-2023_UPDATED_20230629075344.pdf#page=20).
- **Law (verbatim):** 4.3.2 (page 20): "In a Low Income or ESS case, all unearned income is counted in the budget unless specifically excluded. The following types of unearned income shall be included but not limited to: … Pensions, interest, and annuities". 4.3 (page 19): "Countable income from all household parents or custodians age eighteen (18) years and over, or less than eighteen (18) years, and legally emancipated must be considered in the budget."
- **Exclusions checked:** I read 4.3.3 Excluded Income (page 20). No item excludes a military survivor annuity paid to an adult. A survivor child is caught by "Earned/unearned income of a child under eighteen (18) years of age unless an emancipated minor".
- **Required output:** the eligibility group's countable income per month, including the unearned income of parents or custodians age 18 or older, which includes military retirement pay and SBP annuities (PE `ar_sra_countable_income`, SPMUnit, MONTH).
- **Companion test:** Inputs: one adult parent (age 18 or older) with a military SBP annuity of $800 a month and no other income. Expected countable unearned income: $800 a month. Derivation: "Pensions, interest, and annuities". A monthly amount needs no conversion; the 4.3.6 "Yearly income / (divided by) 12" rule is for self-employment only.
- **Notes:** An SBP paid to a non-emancipated child under 18 does not count (4.3.3). The PE list comment that "annuities" has no matching variable is now out of date.

### CO CCAP (CCCAP) — `co/ccap/income/countable_income/sources.yaml`

- **Existing rulespec-us issue:** none. Merged PR #417 encoded the CCAP income limits only.
- **Existing rulespec-us module:** `us-co/regulations/8-ccr-1403-1/3.111/h-low-income-eligibility-guidelines.yaml` (3.111(H) income limits). It does not encode income inclusions.
- **Proposed module path:** `us-co/regulations/8-ccr-1403-1/3.111/i-income-inclusions.yaml`. This follows the existing `3.111/h-...` module.
- **Corpus citation:** two manifests hold this rule. `us-co/regulation/8-ccr-1403-1-eff-2026-08-14` is in `manifests/us-co-state-benefits-w7-regulation.yaml` (expression date 2026-08-14, ruleVersionId 12658; at pinned ref: yes). `us-co/regulation/8-ccr-1403-1` is in `manifests/us-co-ccap-8-ccr-1403-1.yaml` (expression date 2023-08-14, ruleVersionId 11042; at pinned ref: yes). Official copy: [8 CCR 1403-1 (eff. 08/14/2026), page 50](https://www.sos.state.co.us/CCR/GenerateRulePdf.do?ruleVersionId=12658&fileName=8%20CCR%201403-1#page=50).
- **Law (verbatim):** 3.111(I) (page 46): "Each of the following are considered countable income and are taken into consideration for eligibility for child care." Item (8) (page 50): "Pensions and annuities (minus the amount deducted for penalties, if early payouts are received from these accounts) … e. Any other payment from an account meant to provide for a retired person or their survivors." Item (7)(a) (page 49) counts "Retirement or pension payments paid by defense finance and accounting services (DFAS) to retired members of the Armed Forces;".
- **Exclusions checked:** I read 3.111(J) items 1–29 (pages 51–54); the 2023 text has the same 29 items at 3.105.1(J). No item excludes a military survivor annuity. The closest item covers earnings only: "Earnings of a child in the household when not a teen parent".
- **Required output:** the adult caretakers' or teen parents' countable gross income per month, including military retirement pay and SBP annuities (PE `co_ccap_countable_income`, SPMUnit, MONTH).
- **Companion test:** Inputs: one adult caretaker with a military SBP annuity of $800 a month and no other income. Expected countable income: $800 a month. Derivation: 3.111(I)(8), "Pensions and annuities", item e. No early-payout penalty applies.
- **Notes:** The PE reference title "Section 7.105" is out of date. In ruleVersionId 11042 the list is 3.105.1(I) (I. on page 22, item 8 on page 25), and in 12658 it is 3.111(I). Neither manifest version is a scope of the signed release. The existing 3.111(H) module cites `us-co/regulation/8-ccr-1403-1/3.111` through the release scope `us-co/regulation/2026-07-13-recovery-r2026-09-11-tanf-consolidated`, and its text has October 2025 values. The 11042 manifest metadata (3.111 = Parent Fees) does not match that text. Before encoding, confirm which version the 3.111 row holds.

### DC CCSP — `dc/dhs/ccsp/income/countable_income/sources.yaml`

- **Existing rulespec-us issue:** none.
- **Existing rulespec-us module:** none. `us-dc/` holds SSA POMS OSSP levels (`policies/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/2026/*`), statutes 4-205 and 47-1806, income tax and CMS.
- **Proposed module path:** `us-dc/policies/osse/child-care-subsidy-policy-manual/2.5.2.yaml`. This follows the agency/document/section layout of `us-dc/policies/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/...`.
- **Corpus citation:** `us-dc/manual/osse/child-care-subsidy-policy-manual` in `manifests/us-dc-child-care-subsidy-manual.yaml` (expression date 2026-07-19; at pinned ref: yes). The manifest segments by section label, so the row is probably `.../2.5.2`. Official copy: [DC Child Care Subsidy Program Policy Manual, page 13](https://osse.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/osse/publication/attachments/DC%20Child%20Care%20Subsidy%20Program%20Policy%20Manual.pdf#page=13).
- **Law (verbatim):** 2.5.2 (page 13): "Pension and retirement benefits including regular distributions from various sources such as government employee pensions, military retirement/pensions, railroad retirement, private pensions, annuities, Individual Retirement Arrangement (IRA) accounts, or 401(k) plans; and". 2.5.1 (page 12): "All income is converted to an annual figure."
- **Exclusions checked:** I read 2.5.3 Exempt Income (pages 13–14). No item excludes a military survivor annuity. The survivor exclusion covers Social Security only: "Social Security payments, including survivor’s benefits and Supplemental Security Income (SSI);". The catch-all "Any source of income not included in the above definition of countable income" does not apply, because annuities are listed.
- **Required output:** the family's gross annual countable income, including military retirement pay and SBP annuities (PE `dc_ccsp_countable_income`, SPMUnit, MONTH, equal to 1/12 of the annual figure).
- **Companion test:** Inputs: one parent with a military SBP annuity of $800 a month and no other income. Expected countable income: $9,600 a year ($800 × 12, by the 2.5.1 annual conversion). Derivation: "military retirement/pensions … annuities".
- **Notes:** The signed release does not carry this source; its only us-dc manual scope is `2026-07-17-dc-snap-manual`. The PE reference `#page=12` opens 2.5 Income, but the pension bullet is on page 13. The PDF was last modified 2024-09-30; the manifest expression date is the fetch date. An SBP paid to a child could fall under "Income of others in the household who do not have financial responsibility for the child", so the test uses a parent.

### DE POC (Purchase of Care) — `de/dss/poc/income/countable_income/sources.yaml`

- **Existing rulespec-us issue:** none.
- **Existing rulespec-us module:** none. `us-de/` holds DSSM 4000 TANF modules (`regulations/title-16/4000-financial-responsibility/4007-*`, `4008-*`, `4008/1/2`), statute 30 (tax) and SSP POMS levels.
- **Proposed module path:** `us-de/regulations/title-16/11000-child-care-subsidy-program/11003/9/1.yaml`. This follows `us-de/regulations/title-16/4000-financial-responsibility/4008/1/2.yaml`.
- **Corpus citation:** none; needs ingest. No manifest holds DSSM 11000/11003; only `policyengine-source-coverage.yaml` lists the URL as discovered. Official copy: [16 Del. Admin. Code 11000 Child Care Subsidy Program (PDF), page 18](https://regulations.delaware.gov/api/AdminCode/title16/11000/d4a60754-55cf-4996-beda-0fc4138caea4#page=18). The HTML page is https://regulations.delaware.gov/AdminCode/title16/11000.
- **Law (verbatim):** 11003.9.1(4) (page 18): "DSS considers all gross earned and unearned income received by the family when determining child care eligibility." (5)(B) (page 18): "Unearned income, including, but not limited to: … vii. Pensions; viii. Railroad retirement; ix. Annuities; and".
- **Exclusions checked:** I read 11003.9.1(6)(A)–(U) (pages 18–19). No item excludes a military survivor annuity. The closest item covers earned income only: "E. The earned income of a child under the age of 18 years old who is a student;".
- **Required output:** the family's gross countable income per month, including military retirement pay and SBP annuities (PE `de_poc_countable_income`, SPMUnit, MONTH). The rule compares "gross monthly income" with the FPL limit in (4)(B).
- **Companion test:** Inputs: one adult with a military SBP annuity of $800 a month and no other income. Expected countable unearned income: $800 a month. Derivation: "ix. Annuities", under (4) "all gross … unearned income".
- **Notes:** The PE reference URL (`…/Division%20of%20Social%20Services/11003.shtml`) now loads an empty app shell, and the second PE reference (24 DE Reg 704) also no longer returns its text. 11003.9.1 was last amended by 29 DE Reg. 533 (12/01/25). The current text has 200% FPL in (4)(B) and a new exclusion (6)(U); the (5)(B) list is unchanged. Under 11003.9.2, the income of children in the family size also counts, so an SBP paid to a survivor child counts too.

### Florida School Readiness — `fl/doe/sr/income/sources.yaml`

- **Existing rulespec-us issue:** none.
- **Existing rulespec-us module:** none. `us-fl/` holds DCF ESS manual pages (SNAP/TCA), FAC 65A-1 rules, and CMS and income tax policies. It has no `statutes/` folder and nothing for School Readiness.
- **Proposed module path:** `us-fl/statutes/1002/81.yaml` (+ `.test.yaml`). It uses the chapter/section layout of `us-mn/statutes/290/067.yaml` (Minn. Stat. 290.067), because `us-fl/` has no statute module.
- **Corpus citation:** none; needs ingest. The Florida statute rows in the corpus cover only ch. 220, s. 414.095 and HB 5001 (`us-fl-tanf-ccdf-w6-statutes.yaml`, `us-fl-state-benefits-w7-statute.yaml`, `us-fl-benefits-w6-statute.yaml`). Official copy: [The 2026 Florida Statutes, s. 1002.81 (Online Sunshine, HTML, no pages)](https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=1000-1099/1002/Sections/1002.81.html).
- **Law (verbatim):** s. 1002.81(7): "“Family income” means the combined gross income, whether earned or unearned, that is derived from any source by all family or household members who are 18 years of age or older who are currently residing together in the same dwelling unit."
- **Exclusions checked:** the rest of s. 1002.81(7) excludes only the earnings of some enrolled students and "food stamp benefits or federal housing assistance payments issued directly to a landlord or the associated utilities expenses". No exclusion covers a military survivor annuity.
- **Required output:** family income (family/household unit, members aged 18 or older), with military retired pay and an SBP annuity counted as unearned income "derived from any source". The statute sets no period; PolicyEngine's `fl_sr_countable_income` is SPMUnit, month.
- **Companion test:** one household member aged 18 or older, an SBP annuity of $800 a month and no other income. Expected family income: $800 a month, or $9,600 a year (800 × 12) if the module is annual. Derivation: s. 1002.81(7), "unearned … derived from any source"; no exclusion applies.
- **Notes:** the PE list cites the 6M-4.400 FAQ and the unofficial flrules.elaws.us copy of 6M-4.200. flrules.org returned 403, so the text of 6M-4.200 was not checked. The statute governs.

### Idaho ICCP — `id/dhw/iccp/income/unearned_sources.yaml`

- **Existing rulespec-us issue:** none.
- **Existing rulespec-us module:** none. `us-id/` holds income tax statutes (63-30xx), IDAPA 16.03.04 SNAP pages, `regulations/idapa/16/03/05/514.yaml` (AABD), a DHW food stamp policy and CMS policies.
- **Proposed module path:** `us-id/regulations/idapa/16/06/12/071.yaml` (+ `.test.yaml`), following `us-id/regulations/idapa/16/03/05/514.yaml`. The module also needs the .011.13 definition, as an input or a companion module.
- **Corpus citation:** `us-id/regulation/idapa/16/06/12` in `manifests/us-id-ccdf-subsidy-rules.yaml` (expression date 2023-04-06; `numbered_sections` segmentation; at pinned ref: yes). Official copy: [IDAPA 16.06.12, Idaho Child Care Program, page 7](https://adminrules.idaho.gov/rules/current/16/160612.pdf#page=7).
- **Law (verbatim):** page 7, .071: "All gross earned and unearned income is counted in determining eligibility and the child care benefit amount, unless specifically excluded under Section 072 of these rules." Page 6, .011.13: "Unearned Income. Unearned income includes retirement, interest child support, and any income received from a source other than employment or self-employment."
- **Exclusions checked:** .072.01–.17, pages 7–8. No item covers a military survivor annuity. The nearest item is .072.04, "Assistance. Assistance to meet a specific need from other organizations and agencies." An SBP annuity is not paid on the basis of need.
- **Required output:** the countable unearned income of the family (family, month), including military retired pay and an SBP annuity.
- **Companion test:** one parent in the family, an SBP annuity of $800 a month and no other income. Expected countable unearned income: $800 a month. Derivation: .071 with .011.13 ("any income received from a source other than employment"), and .077.04, "Use the exact monthly income if it is expected for each month of the certification period."
- **Notes:** the source prints .011.13 with no comma between "interest" and "child support"; the quote keeps that. By the 16.03.05 precedent, the section row is probably `.../16/06/12/071` (not verified). The corpus file SHA-256 is the same as that of the official PDF fetched 2026-10-22.

### Kansas CCAP — `ks/dcf/ccap/income/countable_income/unearned.yaml`

- **Existing rulespec-us issue:** none. (#1800 "KS1" is about Kansas tax credits, not CCAP.)
- **Existing rulespec-us module:** none for child care income. `us-ks/` holds `policies/dcf/keesm/keesm7410.yaml` (TANF budgetary standards), `keesm7400/cash-proration-rounding.yaml`, a KHPA SSP memo and CMS policies.
- **Proposed module path:** `us-ks/policies/dcf/keesm/keesm6220.yaml` (+ `.test.yaml`), following `us-ks/policies/dcf/keesm/keesm7410.yaml`.
- **Corpus citation:** `us-ks/manual/dcf/keesm/keesm6220` in `manifests/us-ks-keesm.yaml` (expression date 2026-04-01; at pinned ref: yes). The companion rows `.../keesm6200` and `.../keesm6410` are in the same manifest. Official copy: [KEESM 6220 Types of Countable Unearned Income (HTML, no pages)](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/EES/KEESM/Current/keesm6220.htm).
- **Law (verbatim):** KEESM 6220: "Annuities, Pensions - Annuities, pensions, retirement, veterans, or disability benefits, old-age, survivors, Social Security benefits, or strike benefits are countable." KEESM 6200: "Gross unearned income shall be considered unless exempt as noted below."
- **Exclusions checked:** all entries in KEESM 6410. No entry exempts military retired pay or a survivor annuity. The nearest military entry is "Combat Pay (All Programs) - Additional pay received by military personnel as a result of deployment to a combat zone is exempt." (Hostile fire pay is exempt in the same way.)
- **Required output:** the countable unearned income of the child care family (family, month), including military retired pay and an SBP annuity.
- **Companion test:** one adult in the family, an SBP annuity of $800 a month and no other income. Expected countable unearned income: $800 a month. Derivation: KEESM 6220 "Annuities, Pensions"; the annuity is regular unearned income under 6211.
- **Notes:** a vendor-payment paragraph in 6220 removes only a court-ordered ex-spouse share of military retirement from the retiree's income. It does not apply to an SBP annuity. The live pages carry the manual revision mark "10-26", but the corpus scope is the 2026-05-27 snapshot (`2026-05-27-ks-keesm-r2026-07-15-self-contained`). Compare the "Annuities, Pensions" paragraph before encoding (the Wayback Machine was offline). The monthly basis for child care is in KEESM Appendix F-1 (`us-ks/manual/dcf/keesm/appendix/f-1-monthly-family-income-and-family-share-deduction-schedule`, `us-ks-tanf-ccdf-w6-manual.yaml`).

### Kentucky CCAP — `ky/dcbs/ccap/income/countable_income/sources.yaml`

- **Existing rulespec-us issue:** none. (#1802 "KY1" is about Kentucky tax care credits, not CCAP.)
- **Existing rulespec-us module:** none. `us-ky/` holds KRS 141 tax statutes (`statutes/11/141/*.yaml`) and CMS policies.
- **Proposed module path:** `us-ky/regulations/kar/922/002/160.yaml` (+ `.test.yaml`), with dated versions. `us-ky/` has no regulation module, so the path copies the corpus segments, in the same way that `us-fl/regulations/fac/65a-1/400/block-1.yaml` copies `us-fl/regulation/fac/65a-1/400/block-1`.
- **Corpus citation:** `us-ky/regulation/kar/922/002/160/document-15544` (effective 2024-11-18) in `manifests/us-ky-tanf-ccdf-w6-rules.yaml` (expression date 2026-10-06; at pinned ref: yes). The earlier versions `.../document-13685` (effective 2022-11-15) and `.../document-10239` (effective 2019-05-31) are in the same manifest. Official copy: [922 KAR 2:160, LRC document 15544, page 7](https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/kar/downloads/docs/15544/document.engrossed.pdf#page=7).
- **Law (verbatim):** page 7, Section 8(2): "Except for a child who is eligible as specified in Section 5 of this administrative regulation, gross income received or anticipated to be received by the applicant and responsible adult shall be considered when the cabinet or its designee determines the family's eligibility for the CCAP." Page 9, Section 8(6)(c)1: "Using the gross monthly amount of continuing, stable unearned income received on a monthly basis;"
- **Exclusions checked:** Section 8(4)(a)–(ll), pages 7–9. No item covers pensions, annuities or military survivor payments. The nearest item is "(ff) A payment made, pursuant to 38 U.S.C. 1815 by the Veteran's Administration, to children of female Vietnam veterans;"
- **Required output:** the gross income of the applicant and the responsible adult (family, month), including military retired pay and an SBP annuity.
- **Companion test:** the applicant is the only adult, with an SBP annuity of $800 a month and no other income. Expected gross unearned income: $800 a month. Derivation: Section 8(2) (gross income) and 8(6)(c)1 (the gross monthly amount of stable unearned income).
- **Notes:** the regulation does not define "gross income" and does not list pensions, so the result depends on 8(2) and on the absence of an 8(4) exclusion. The text of 8(2) is the same in documents 10239, 13685 and 15544. The 2021-12-15 version (48 Ky.R. 693) is not in the corpus. The PE reference links document 10239 (the 2019 version). The current version is 15544: the history on the LRC title page ends "51 Ky.R. 420; eff. 11-18-2024". The corpus file SHA-256 is the same as that of the LRC PDF fetched 2026-10-22.

### Massachusetts CCFA — `ma/eec/ccfa/income/countable_income/sources/unearned.yaml`

- **Existing rulespec-us issue:** none.
- **Existing rulespec-us module:** none. `us-ma/` holds MGL c. 62 tax statutes, 106 CMR 362–365 DTA rules, DTA SNAP COLA policies and CMS policies. It has nothing from EEC.
- **Proposed module path:** `us-ma/policies/eec/ccdf/income-eligible-countable-income.yaml` (+ `.test.yaml`), with three dated versions. The prefix copies the corpus `us-ma/policy/eec/ccdf/...` rows, in the same way that `us-ma/policies/dta/snap-cola/2025-10-01/standard-deduction.yaml` copies its DTA row.
- **Corpus citation:**
  - 2020-01-01 period: `us-ma/policy/eec/ccdf/financial-assistance-policy-guide-2022-02-01` in `manifests/us-ma-tanf-ccdf-w6-docs.yaml` (expression date 2026-10-06; at pinned ref: yes). Official copy: [EEC Financial Assistance Policy Guide, February 1, 2022, page 39](https://www.mass.gov/doc/eecs-financial-assistance-policy-guide-february-1-2022/download#page=39).
  - 2023-10-01 period: none; needs ingest (the Interim Income Eligible policies of October 1, 2023). Official copy: [Interim Income Eligible CCFA Program Policies, October 1, 2023, page 12](https://www.mass.gov/doc/interim-income-eligible-child-care-financial-assistance-program-policies-october-1-2023/download#page=12); PE uses the web.archive.org copy of 2023-10-18. CCFA-25-03 (`us-ma/policy/eec/ccdf/policy-advisory-interim-income-eligible-state-library-copy`, expression date 2025-04-01, at pinned ref: yes) keeps these interim policies in effect, but it does not repeat the income list.
  - 2025-04-01 period: `us-ma/policy/eec/ccdf/eec-ccfa-2026-04-income-eligible-consolidated-policies-2026-05-06` in the same manifest (expression date 2026-10-06; at pinned ref: yes). Official copy: [EEC CCFA Income Eligible Policies, May 6, 2026, page 21](https://www.mass.gov/doc/eec-ccfa-2026-04-income-eligible-consolidated-policies-may-6-2026/download#page=21).
  - Regulation for all periods: `us-ma/regulation/eec/606-cmr/10` in `manifests/us-ma-tanf-ccdf-w6-rules.yaml` (expression date 2026-10-06; at pinned ref: yes).
- **Law (verbatim):**
  - 2022 guide, page 37 (4.2.B.3): "submit documentation of all relevant sources of earned income, … as well as any unearned income, unless income is excluded below." Page 39 (4.2.C.3.d): "RETIREMENT INCOME. For Parents aged 65 and claiming retirement, any pension or other retirement related income must be verified by submitting copies of award letters or retirement pay stubs."
  - Oct 2023 interim policies, page 12: "Only the following income sources are used when calculating a family’s income eligibility: … Retirement income;"
  - May 2026 policies, page 21: "When evaluating income eligibility, the FAA will verify the income of parents residing with the child to include the following income sources: … Retirement income"
- **Exclusions checked:**
  - 2022: the 4.2.C.4 list (pages 40–41) has no pension, annuity or military survivor item. The nearest items are "Military Housing Allowance" and Agent Orange payments "made to Vietnam veterans or their survivors".
  - 2023 (page 12) and 2026 (page 22): the lists of sources that are not considered exclude "Social Security Income, including but not limited to survivor’s benefits or SSDI" and "Veterans Disability Benefits". Neither list names a military or employer survivor annuity.
- **Required output:** the countable unearned income of each parent who lives with the child (Person, month), summed into the total gross monthly household income. Military retired pay and an SBP annuity enter as "any unearned income" (2022) or as "Retirement income" (from 2023-10-01).
- **Companion test:** one parent who lives with the child, an SBP annuity of $800 a month and no other income. Expected countable unearned income in each period:
  - 2020-01-01 (2022 guide): $800 a month. Derivation: 4.2.B.3, "any unearned income, unless income is excluded"; no 4.2.C.4 item applies.
  - 2023-10-01 and 2025-04-01: $800 a month only if EEC reads an SBP annuity as "Retirement income". Otherwise $0, because the list is closed.
- **Notes:** 606 CMR 10.04(2)(a)3 (EEC copy effective January 1, 2026, file page 13) counts "the income of the parents living with the child receiving financial assistance". It also says: "EEC may exclude additional forms of income for determining financial eligibility as detailed in EEC Policy." So the closed policy list controls, and the policies do not define "Retirement income". The October 2023 text of 606 CMR 10 was not checked. In the 2022 guide, C.3.d is a verification rule for parents aged 65 or older; the count depends on B.3. The PE period starts on 2020-01-01, before the February 2022 guide; earlier guides were not checked. The corpus files for the 2022 guide and the 2026 policies are stored as `.html`, but their SHA-256 values are the same as those of the official PDFs; the CCFA-25-03 file also matches.

### Maryland CCS — `md/msde/ccs/income/countable_income/sources.yaml`

- **Existing rulespec-us issue:** none.
- **Existing rulespec-us module:** none. `us-md/` holds Tax-General 10-105 and 10-211, DHS FIA SNAP and TCA policies, and CMS policies. It has no COMAR module.
- **Proposed module path:** `us-md/regulations/title-13a/subtitle-14/chapter-06/regulation-02.yaml` (+ `.test.yaml`). The path copies the corpus path, in the same way that `us-ma/regulations/106-cmr/365/150/block-1.yaml` copies its row. The annualization rule is in regulation-03.
- **Corpus citation:** `us-md/regulation/title-13a/subtitle-14/chapter-06/regulation-02` and `.../regulation-03` in `manifests/us-md-tanf-ccdf-w6-rules.yaml` (expression date 2026-10-06; at pinned ref: yes). Official copies (HTML, no pages): [COMAR 13A.14.06.02 Definitions](https://regs.maryland.gov/us/md/exec/comar/13A.14.06.02) and [COMAR 13A.14.06.03 Eligibility](https://regs.maryland.gov/us/md/exec/comar/13A.14.06.03).
- **Law (verbatim):** .02B(28)(b): "“Gross income” includes, but is not limited to: … (v) Pensions and annuities; … (vii) Military entitlements, bonuses, and allowances;". .03F(4): "Annualization of gross income shall be performed by multiplying: … (d) Monthly income by 12;"
- **Exclusions checked:** .02B(28)(c)(i)–(xxvi). No item excludes a pension, an annuity or a military survivor payment. The nearest item is "(xxiii) Veterans Administration payments to children with birth defects born to female Vietnam veterans;"
- **Required output:** the annual or annualized gross income of the family (family, year; .03F(3)), including military retired pay ((v) or (vii)) and an SBP annuity ((v)).
- **Companion test:** one adult in the family, an SBP annuity of $800 a month and no other income. Expected annual gross income: $9,600. Derivation: .02B(28)(b)(v), "Pensions and annuities", and .03F(4)(d): 800 × 12 = 9,600. PolicyEngine's monthly `md_ccs_countable_income` shows $800.
- **Notes:** .02B(28)(a) defines gross income as "the sum of earnings, … received by an individual for compensation of services rendered on a regular or recurrent basis". A survivor did not render the services, but (b) expressly includes annuities, so the count depends on (b)(v). .03F(3) refers to ".02B(30)" for gross income, but the definition is now at B(28) (B(30) is "Infant"); this cross-reference in COMAR is stale. The PE list comment says that annuities and military entitlements are not modeled. After this PR, `military_retirement_income` carries the SBP annuity, so that comment is partly stale. The corpus HTML is not byte-identical to the live page (the page is dynamic); the quotes come from the live page of 2026-10-22. The PE period starts on 2022-05-01, and earlier COMAR versions were not checked.

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Rhode Island LIHEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 2a, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9972 (branch `ri-liheap-wave2a`), open and ready for review, not merged. Head `d58c4a21f9` (2026-10-19) addresses PavelMakarchuk's review of 2026-10-19 (approved with comments; DTrim99's request for changes of 2026-10-14 stands). ## Why queued
