| C18 | Positive farm income (`income/ok_liheap_countable_earned_income.yaml` Case 8) | period 2026; age 50; wages $12,000; `farm_operations_income` $1,200 | Self-employment is earned; the net farm input stands in for receipts less the 50% deduction (interpretation 5): 13,200. | countable earned $13,200 | OAC 340:20-1-11(a)(2), (c)(4) |
| C19 | SSDI receipt and the medical deduction (`ok_liheap.yaml` Case 14) | period 2026; age 50; medical $1,200; `social_security_disability` $9,000, then employer disability insurance (`disability_benefits`) $9,000 | Both count (340:50-7-29(c)(2)-(3)): 750 a month <= 1,696. SSDI meets 340:50-5-4(a)(2): net 7,800 (650 a month), row $401 - $700: $265. Employer disability is on no 340:50-5-4 list: no deduction, net 9,000 (750): $235. | deductions $1,200, $0; net $7,800, $9,000; $265, $235 | OAC 340:20-1-11(c)(1); 340:50-5-4(a); C-7 10/1/2025; C-7-A |
| C20 | Five households (`integration.yaml` Cases 1-5) | 1: 2025; age 68, Medicare enrolled; Social Security $12,000; Part B $2,220; other medical $1,800; PROPANE. 2: 2026; wages $31,200; children 9, 6, 3; child care subsidy, copay $2,268. 3: 2026; age 45; SSI $11,928; medical $600; roomer, heat in rent, `gas_expense` $300. 4: 2026; one tax unit: undocumented parent, wages $24,000; citizen parent, wages $12,000; children 9, 4. 5: 2027; nine members; wages $52,000; ELECTRICITY | All under the limit. Net a month: 1: (12,000 - 4,020) / 12 = 665, LP gas. 2: size 4; (31,200 - 2,880 - 2,268) / 12 = 2,171, size 4-6. 3: SSI meets (a)(2); (11,928 - 600) / 12 = 944, roomer. 4: size 3; deemed 24,000 - 2,880 - 4,776 = 16,344; gross 2,362 <= 2,888; net 2,122. 5: limit 6,037 + 616 = 6,653; net 4,093, size 7+. | $350; $259; $40; $235; $277 | C-7; C-7-A; C-1 IX-A; OAC 340:20-1-11(a)(4), (c); 340:20-1-19(d); 340:50-5-4(a) |

### SBP companion

[Pavel, October 22](#issuecomment-6349321879): `military_retirement_income` = `military_retirement_pay` + `military_retirement_pay_survivors`, counted once. Existing retiree-only tests are unchanged.

| Case | Inputs | Expected | Derivation |
|---|---|---|---|
| SBP-1 | period 2026; Oklahoma; one citizen adult aged 62; `military_retirement_pay_survivors` $9,600; no other income; NATURAL_GAS with `gas_expense` $1,200; heat not in rent; no housing assistance; `ssi`, `ok_tanf` and child care inputs 0 | countable and gross income $9,600; eligible; net income $9,600; `ok_liheap` $235 | An SBP annuity is an annuity and a retirement benefit, so it is unearned income (340:50-7-29(c)(2); 340:20-1-11(a)(3)). 9,600 / 12 = 800, at or below the size 1 limit $1,696 (C-7 10/1/2025). No earned income, child support or medical expense to deduct: net 800 a month, row “$701 - ineligible”, size 1-3, utility: $235 (C-7-A). |

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Plan and OAC.** The OAC stands in for a manual. Where the plan and the OAC differ, the branch follows the OAC; where the OAC is silent, it follows the plan.
   - *Child earnings.* Plan 1.9 leaves "Earned income of a child under the age of 18" unchecked (all such earnings excluded). OAC 340:20-1-11(b) applies 340:50-7-22(9), which excludes only a school student 17 or younger under parental control; the branch excludes a member under 18 in K-12 school who is a tax dependent. Companion cases (`income/ok_liheap_countable_earned_income.yaml` Cases 2-7): 0 for a 10-year-old and a 17-year-old dependent in school; $7,200 for a 17-year-old dependent out of school, a 17-year-old non-dependent in school, an 18-year-old in school and a 20-year-old in college. The plan reading gives both 17-year-olds $0.
   - *Heat in rent (settled 2026-10-06).* The branch follows OAC 340:20-1-19(d)(1)-(2), 340:20-1-13(2)(B)-(C), 340:20-1-10(h) and plan 2.3: heat-in-rent renters and roomers need a verified surcharge, subsidized or not, and a positive `heating_expense` for the household's `heating_type` stands for it. Reading not followed: 340:20-1-10(c) counts "undesignated payments for energy in the form of rent" and (f)(3) lists only "subsidized households whose heating or cooling costs are included in the rent" as non-vulnerable; the branch reads (c) as defining the household and (f) as examples. The 2025 edition's 340:20-1-19(d)(1) text layer adds "unsubsidized" (struck or inserted is unclear); either way it names only surcharge payers. Companion case C10.
   - *Resources.* The 2025 edition (model period 2026) kept the resource wording of 340:20-1-10(h)(2) and 340:20-1-11(e) (Register PDF pages 576 and 581, quoted above), but the 10/1/2024 and 10/1/2025 C-7 editions print no level, FY2025 and FY2026 plan item 2.3 answer No (page 9), and the 2026 edition drops both. The branch has no asset test; a comment in `ok_liheap_eligible` says why. Companion case `eligibility/ok_liheap_eligible.yaml` Case 5 (2026): gross $18,000 (1,500 a month) with $1,000,000 or $0 in the bank: limit $20,352, eligible both times.
   - *Medicare premium.* All three plans check "Excluding MediCare deduction" for SSA benefits (item 1.9, page 6). OAC 340:20-1-11(a) and (c), the plan narrative (page 7) and Quest allow deductions only after the gross test, and the deductions include Medicare premiums (340:50-7-31(a)(3)(A)(vi), by analogy); the branch follows them, not item 1.9. Companion cases: `ok_liheap.yaml` Case 7 (2026, age 70, enrolled, Social Security $21,360, premium $2,434.80; then no premium): 1,780 a month > 1,696, $0 for both (net 18,925.20 and 21,360); netting would count 1,577 and pay $235. `income/ok_liheap_countable_income.yaml` Case 2: Social Security $1,200 with that premium plus a $12,000 pension counts $13,200 (netting: $12,000).
   - *Medical expenses.* 340:20-1-11(c)(1) does not define "verified non-reimbursed medical expenses". The branch uses SNAP's list in 340:50-7-31(a)(3)(A) (`snap_allowable_medical_expenses`) without SNAP's $35 threshold (C15).
2. **Rounding (inferred).** The OAC rounds each source's monthly amount to the nearest dollar; the branch rounds only the monthly gross and net totals, half up (floor(x + 0.5)), so separately rounded sources can differ. Companion cases: `ok_liheap.yaml` Case 9, second household (2026, wages $20,358: 1,696.50 rounds to 1,697 > 1,696): $0; `eligibility/ok_liheap_eligible.yaml` Case 1, third value (2027, gross $20,754, 1,729.50): not eligible; `payment/ok_liheap_matrix_amount.yaml` Case 2 (2026, annual net): 4,800.12 and 4,805.88 give $365, 4,806 and 4,811.88 $265, 8,400.12 and 8,405.88 $265, 8,406 and 8,411.88 $235; `income/ok_liheap_net_income.yaml` Case 3 (2027, gross $20,754: over the limit; net $17,874).
3. **Limit formula (inferred, verified).** No source states how C-7 rounds. Rounding 130% of the prior year's guideline up to the dollar, separately for the base and the per-member increment, reproduces all 27 printed figures in float32 and float64 (1.3 x 15,960 / 12 must give exactly 1,729.00, not $1,730). The limit is inclusive ("equal to or less than"). The one-year lag follows the LIHEAP IMs cited above (`fpg_year_lag` cites them); plan 2.1 names only the HHS Poverty Guidelines. C-7 confirms it: 1.3 x 15,060 / 12 = 1,631.50 gives the printed FY2025 $1,632; the 2025 guideline would give $1,696.
4. **Deeming details.** The tax unit stands in for the ineligible member and the dependents "claimable for federal personal income taxes"; actual claiming can differ. (a)(4)(A) subtracts the earned income deduction and (D) subtracts "all applicable deductions per (c)", which include the same deduction; the branch subtracts it once. Companion cases:
   - `ok_liheap.yaml` Case 1 (2027): undocumented adult with wages $13,200, citizen child 10. Deemed 13,200 - 2,880 - 12 x 398 = 5,544; size 1; gross and net 462 a month: $265 (deducted twice: $365).
   - `ok_liheap.yaml` Case 5 (2027): citizen wages $18,000, undocumented adult wages $12,000, one tax unit. Deemed 12,000 - 2,880 - 4,776 = 4,344; gross 22,344 (1,862 a month) > 1,729: $0 (net 19,464; deducted twice: $235).
   - `ok_liheap.yaml` Case 4 (2027): undocumented adult 60 (wages $12,000, medical $600, child support paid $1,200), citizen adult (wages $6,000, child support paid $600), citizen child, TANF $1,200, subsidized copay $600. Deemed 12,000 - 2,880 - 600 - 1,200 - 4,776 = 2,544; gross 9,744; net 9,744 - 2,880 - 600 - 600 = 5,664 (472 a month), size 2: $265.
   - `income/ok_liheap_deemed_income.yaml` Case 8 (2025): undocumented children 15 and 10 in their own tax unit (survivor benefits $3,600 and $2,400), citizen adult with wages $6,000. IX-B for two, $380: 6,000 - 4,560 = 1,440; gross 7,440 (620 a month) <= 1,632; net 4,560 (380): $365. Case 7 (2027): a 17-year-old with $3,600 uses IX-B $193 (1,284 deemed); an 18-year-old uses IX-A $398 (0).
5. **Self-employment and losses (settled).** OAC 340:20-1-11(c)(4) deducts 50 percent of gross self-employment income before the gross test. The branch uses the net business inputs with no further deduction and floors every source at zero separately, rental, farm rent and estate income included. Companion cases: `income/ok_liheap_countable_earned_income.yaml` Case 1 (2026): 12,000 + 2,400 + 600 + 1,200 with a $1,200 farm loss floored: $16,200; `income/ok_liheap_countable_income.yaml` Case 3 (2026): wages $12,000 with rental -$6,000 counts $12,000; pension $5,000 with farm rent -$3,000 and estate -$2,000 counts $5,000; gross $17,000.
6. **Immigration status (settled 2026-10-06).** OAC 340:20-1-10(d)(3) cites "OAC 340:50-67", read as 340:50-5-67, the SNAP rule incorporating 7 CFR 273.4. The branch follows SNAP alien eligibility, P.L. 119-21 section 10108 included, through `is_snap_immigration_status_eligible` for January of each year (C11). Reading not followed: the eCFR text of 7 CFR 273.4(a)(6) still lists refugees and asylees. Gaps: Compact of Free Association residents, noncitizen nationals and the 273.4(a)(3)-(5) groups have no `immigration_status` value; `years_since_us_entry` stands in for time in qualified status; PolicyEngine dates the list change 2025-07-01 (the statute: July 4, 2025), which no January read reaches.
7. **Directly billed fuels without a table (settled coverage limit).** A directly billed OTHER, SOLAR or UNSPECIFIED household stays eligible with $0, a coverage gap (OAC 340:20-1-10(b)(1) also names butane). The heat-in-rent tables price any fuel except NONE, but the award needs a positive bill for the household's `heating_type` (interpretation 8), so UNSPECIFIED fuel, which has no bill, gets $0. Companion cases: `payment/ok_liheap_matrix_amount.yaml` Case 7 (2026, size 1, net 0): OTHER, SOLAR, UNSPECIFIED $0; natural gas $365. `ok_liheap.yaml` Case 15 (2026, wages $12,000, net 760 a month): SOLAR and OTHER, each with a $1,200 bill, are eligible with $0; natural gas $235. The unspecified default is tracked in PolicyEngine/policyengine-us issue 9754.
8. **Responsibility proxies.** A positive `heating_expense` stands for the verified surcharge of every heat-in-rent renter or roomer; the `has_heating_expense` flag alone qualifies only a direct payer. Housing-assistance inputs are not read. The roomer's written agreement and unrelatedness (340:20-1-10(c)(3)) have no input and are assumed.
9. **Other gaps.** Not modeled: another program's gross income when every member receives SNAP, TANF, SSP, ABD Medicaid or a child care subsidy (340:20-1-11(a)(1)(B)); those programs' own exclusions (SNAP's apply to everyone); the Social Security number rule (340:20-1-10(h)(5)); tribal LIHEAP dual participation (340:20-1-4); institutions (340:20-1-10(f)(1)); pre-authorization; mid-year funding adjustments. Income forms with no input (mortgage contracts, settlements, insurance payments, irregular gifts) are not separated. The SPM unit stands in for the household, annual income / 12 for the application month; the copay is deducted once per SPM unit. `is_usda_elderly` and `is_usda_disabled` represent 340:50-5-4 (7 CFR 271.2): age 60 or benefit receipt. The veteran flags stand in for (a)(6)-(9), so an (a)(7) aid-and-attendance or housebound veteran is entered as `is_permanently_disabled_veteran`; (a)(3)-(5) and (a)(10)-(11) have no inputs, and `is_disabled` shows no receipt. Part B counts only with `medicare_enrolled`. `partnership_s_corp_income` counts as earned, as in other states' LIHEAP lists, though 340:50-7-29(c)(8) makes S corporation and passive partnership shares unearned; the input cannot split them, and only the $240 deduction differs. Oklahoma's state supplement is not modeled (`ssi` is federal).
10. **Earlier years.** Model period 2025 carries back the income rule effective 2025-09-15. The rule in force on 1 January 2025 (a 38-item exclusion list, struck on Register PDF pages 578-580) gives the same result for every modeled source, including item (14) on a full-time student's earnings; its (c) differed only by a struck *may* (page 580). FY2024 and earlier also had a liquid-resource test; Quest: "Effective October 1, 2024, the Energy Assistance program does not consider resources for eligibility determination." Those years are unclaimed and not encoded.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [FY2026 state-plan manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ok-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [Appendix C-7-A manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ok-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml)
- [OAC chapter 340:50 manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ok-snap-rules.yaml)
- [Appendix C-1 manifest (SNAP policy appendices)](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ok-snap-policy.yaml)
- [Federal LIHEAP annual figures manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission. The sources that "Why queued" names as missing, and the 2024 and 2025 poverty guidelines with their IM attachments, need ingest before the modules above can be proved.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-ok/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the FY2025 to FY2027 income limits (sizes 1 to 8 and the additional-member amounts), the $240 deduction, all 36 cells of the four C-7-A tables, the fuel-to-table mapping, heat in rent with and without a surcharge, SNAP alien eligibility before and after P.L. 119-21, deeming with the Schedule IX standards, gross Social Security in the income test, the deductions after it (premiums of members 60 or over or disabled under 340:50-5-4), unemployment compensation, retirement distributions, farm income, monthly rounding, and TANF take-up. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: Encode MCL 206.508(4) Michigan total household resources (net business and rental loss add-backs)

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Encoding debt

Nothing in rulespec-us encodes Michigan's "total household resources" (MCL 206.508(4)), the income measure for the homestead property tax credit (MCL 206.520) and the home heating credit (MCL 206.527a). `us-mi/` on `main` encodes only MCL 206.30, 206.51 and chapter 206 section 272 (`us-mi/statutes/206.30/*`, `206.51/*`, `206/272`), plus policy pages. `git ls-tree` of `main` finds no `us-mi/statutes/206.508*` path, and a code search of TheAxiomFoundation for `206.508` or "household resources" finds no module.

The section is in the pinned corpus: `axiom-corpus` `data/corpus/provisions/us-mi/statute/2026-09-14-income-tax-chapter-us-mi-chapter-206.jsonl` has the row `us-mi/statute/206.508` (expression date 2026-09-14, id `50d98f41-c54a-5ca6-b7fa-a4c3e3676600`). Its subsection (4) text is identical to the Legislature's page (below).

PolicyEngine-US got this definition wrong. It floored each business and rental source at zero separately, and then subtracted every federal above-the-line deduction, including `loss_ald` (the business, rental and capital losses just floored away). PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9790 fixes it. This issue is that PR's `pe-parity` side. The companion tests below use the same law and forms as that PR's tests.

## Blocker (why this is queued, not encoded)

The signed encoder run (`axiom-encode encode us-mi/statute/206.508 --apply`) is OpenAI-billed and needs Max's approval. No ingestion is needed: the corpus row exists.

## Law (verbatim)

MCL 206.508(4), from corpus row `us-mi/statute/2026-09-14 ... /206.508`, checked against https://www.legislature.mi.gov/Laws/MCL?objectName=mcl-206-508 on 2026-10-05:

> (4) "Total household resources" means all income received by all persons of a household in a tax year while members of a household, excluding for tax years beginning after December 31, 2018 any compensation received pursuant to the wrongful imprisonment compensation act, 2016 PA 343, MCL 691.1751 to 691.1757, and increased by the following deductions from federal gross income:
>
> (a) Any net business loss after netting all business income and loss.
>
> (b) Any net rental or royalty loss.
>
> (c) Any carryback or carryforward of a net operating loss as defined in section 172(b)(2) of the internal revenue code.

MCL 206.508(3): "'Household' means a claimant and spouse."

**Michigan Treasury implementation** (cross-check, not a corpus citation). 2025 MI-1040 book (https://www.michigan.gov/taxes/-/media/Project/Websites/taxes/Forms/IIT/TY2025/MI-1040-Book.pdf):
- Page 26, "Total Household Resources": "They are AGI, excluding net business and farm losses, net rent and royalty losses, and any carryover of a net operating loss, plus all income exempt or excluded from AGI."
- Page 31, MI-1040CR line 16: "Enter amounts to the extent included in AGI from: U.S. Schedule C ...; Part II (Ordinary Gains and Losses) of the U.S. Form 4797; Part II (Income or Loss from Partnerships and S Corporations) and Part III (Income or Loss from Estates and Trusts) of the U.S. Schedule E; U.S. Schedule F ... If the total is negative enter '0.'"
- Line 17 does the same for Schedule E Part I (rents and royalties), Part IV (REMICs) and Part V (Form 4835 farm rental).
- Page 32, line 30: "Enter total adjustments from your U.S. Form 1040, Schedule 1." The list is IRA, student loan interest, self-employment tax, self-employed health insurance, early withdrawal penalty, alimony, HSA and similar items. It has no losses.
- The 2024 book (`TY2024/MI-1040-Instructions.pdf`) has the same text.

## Plan

Encode `us-mi/statutes/206.508.yaml` through the signed encoder. `review_finding`:

> Encode MCL 206.508(4) (corpus us-mi/statute/206.508) in us-mi/statutes/206.508.yaml. Inputs (household = claimant and spouse, 206.508(3); Money, tax year): `household_income_received` (all income received by the household's members while members, excluding wrongful imprisonment compensation for tax years beginning after 2018, with business, rental and NOL deductions taken as in federal gross income), `household_net_business_income` (the household's business income and loss netted: U.S. Schedule C, Form 4797 Part II, Schedule E Parts II and III, Schedule F; may be negative), `household_net_rental_or_royalty_income` (rents and royalties netted; may be negative), `household_net_operating_loss_carryover_deduction` (the section 172(b)(2) carryback or carryforward deducted). Derived rules, each with its verbatim excerpt: `net_business_loss_increase` = max(0, -household_net_business_income), source 206.508(4)(a) "Any net business loss after netting all business income and loss"; `net_rental_or_royalty_loss_increase` = max(0, -household_net_rental_or_royalty_income), source 206.508(4)(b); `net_operating_loss_increase` = household_net_operating_loss_carryover_deduction, source 206.508(4)(c); `total_household_resources` = household_income_received + the three increases, source 206.508(4). A business loss must not offset rental income or the reverse: each is netted within its own group and only a net loss is added back.

## Required outputs

- `us-mi:statutes/206.508#total_household_resources`
- `us-mi:statutes/206.508#net_business_loss_increase`
- `us-mi:statutes/206.508#net_rental_or_royalty_loss_increase`

## Companion tests

Expected values come from MCL 206.508(4) and MI-1040CR lines 14, 16, 17 and 33. That is the same ground truth as the PolicyEngine-US tests in `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/mi/tax/income/mi_household_resources.yaml` (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9790). The household has wages and the listed business and rental items, and nothing else. `household_income_received` is wages plus business and rental income with the losses taken (federal AGI here), and the NOL deduction is 0.

| case | wages | business items | rental items | income received | net business | net rental | total household resources |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| business loss | 100,000 | Schedule C −50,000 | — | 50,000 | −50,000 | 0 | 100,000 |
| rental loss | 50,000 | — | Schedule E Part I −30,000 | 20,000 | 0 | −30,000 | 50,000 |
| loss netted within business | 50,000 | Schedule C −10,000; S corporation 30,000 | — | 70,000 | 20,000 | 0 | 70,000 |
| net business loss | 50,000 | Schedule C −40,000; S corporation 30,000 | — | 40,000 | −10,000 | 0 | 50,000 |
| business loss, rental income | 50,000 | Schedule C −20,000 | rents 15,000 | 45,000 | −20,000 | 15,000 | 65,000 |
| loss netted within rental | 50,000 | — | rents −10,000; Form 4835 farm rent 25,000 | 65,000 | 0 | 15,000 | 65,000 |
| rental loss, business income | 50,000 | S corporation 20,000 | rents −30,000 | 40,000 | 20,000 | −30,000 | 70,000 |
| estate loss netted | 50,000 | Schedule E Part III −5,000; S corporation 20,000 | — | 65,000 | 15,000 | 0 | 65,000 |
| Form 4797 loss netted | 50,000 | Form 4797 Part II −8,000; S corporation 20,000 | — | 62,000 | 12,000 | 0 | 62,000 |

## Extension: federal exclusions count as income received; only U.S. Schedule 1 adjustments come off (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9795)

PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9795 (stacked on #9790) fixes MI-1040CR line 30. This section is its `pe-parity` side. Before #9795, PolicyEngine-US subtracted four federal exclusions from gross income as if they were Schedule 1 adjustments. The encoding has to make the same distinction.

### Law (verbatim)

MCL 206.508(4), quoted above, starts from "all income received by all persons of a household". It adds back only the three listed "deductions from federal gross income". An exclusion is not a deduction: the amount never enters federal gross income, but it is still income received. Federal deductions from gross income other than (a) to (c) stay subtracted:

- IRC 62(a): "the term 'adjusted gross income' means, in the case of an individual, gross income minus the following deductions". U.S. Schedule 1 Part II (lines 11 to 26, "Adjustments to Income") reports them.
- IRC 135(a): "no amount shall be includible in gross income by reason of the redemption during such year of any qualified United States savings bond".
- IRC 137(a)(1): "Gross income of an employee does not include amounts paid or expenses incurred by the employer for qualified adoption expenses in connection with the adoption of a child by an employee if such amounts are furnished pursuant to an adoption assistance program."
- IRC 931(a): "gross income shall not include— (1) income derived from sources within any specified possession, and (2) income effectively connected with the conduct of a trade or business by such individual within any specified possession."
- IRC 933: "The following items shall not be included in gross income and shall be exempt from taxation under this subtitle: (1) ... income derived from sources within Puerto Rico".

**Michigan Treasury implementation** (cross-check, not a corpus citation). 2025 MI-1040 book:
- Page 26: total household resources are "AGI, excluding net business and farm losses, net rent and royalty losses, and any carryover of a net operating loss, plus all income exempt or excluded from AGI."
- MI-1040CR line 14: "Enter all compensation received as an employee. ... and any other amounts reported to you on Form W-2."
- Line 15 (form): "All interest and dividend income (including nontaxable interest)".
- Line 30: "Enter total adjustments from your U.S. Form 1040, Schedule 1."
- The 2025 W-2 instructions say employer adoption benefits "are not reportable in box 1" and must be reported "in box 12 with code T".

### `review_finding` (addendum to the one above)

> In us-mi/statutes/206.508.yaml (MCL 206.508(4), corpus us-mi/statute/206.508), derive `household_income_received` = `household_federal_adjusted_gross_income` + `household_income_excluded_from_federal_gross_income`, source 206.508(4) "all income received by all persons of a household in a tax year while members of a household". Inputs (household = claimant and spouse; Money; tax year):
> - `household_federal_adjusted_gross_income`: federal gross income minus the IRC 62(a) deductions, that is, after the U.S. Schedule 1 Part II adjustments, with business, rental and NOL deductions taken.
> - `household_income_excluded_from_federal_gross_income`: income received that federal law excludes from gross income, for example savings bond interest under IRC 135, employer adoption assistance under IRC 137, possession income under IRC 931 and Puerto Rico income under IRC 933, other than wrongful imprisonment compensation.
>
> An exclusion is not one of the "deductions from federal gross income" in (a) to (c), so excluded income is never subtracted. IRC 62(a) deductions other than (a) to (c) stay subtracted. `total_household_resources` is unchanged: `household_income_received` plus the three increases.

### Required outputs (added)

- `us-mi:statutes/206.508#household_income_received`

### Companion tests (added)

Expected values come from MI-1040CR lines 14, 15, 30 and 33 and the 2025 MI-1040 book page 26. They match the PolicyEngine-US tests added in `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/mi/tax/income/mi_household_resources.yaml` (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9795). Each household is one person with no business or rental items, so the three increases are 0.

The last PolicyEngine case also has 1,200 of health insurance premiums (line 31). Premiums are outside 206.508(4)'s text, so the companion test drops them: line 33 = 53,000 − 3,300 = 49,700. PolicyEngine-US, with line 31, gives 48,500.

| case | household | federal AGI | excluded from gross income | income received | total household resources |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| savings bond interest (IRC 135) | wages 30,000; interest 2,000, of which 1,500 excluded (Form 8815) | 30,500 | 1,500 | 32,000 | 32,000 |
| employer adoption benefits (IRC 137) | wages 60,000, of which 5,000 adoption benefits (W-2 box 12 code T, not box 1) | 55,000 | 5,000 | 60,000 | 60,000 |
| Puerto Rico income (IRC 933) | wages 45,000, of which 15,000 earned in Puerto Rico | 30,000 | 15,000 | 45,000 | 45,000 |
| possession income (IRC 931) | wages 40,000, of which 8,000 from a specified possession | 32,000 | 8,000 | 40,000 | 40,000 |
| exclusions and Schedule 1 adjustments | wages 50,000 (4,000 adoption benefits); interest 3,000 (1,000 excluded under IRC 135); IRA 2,000, early withdrawal penalty 300, student loan interest 1,000 (Schedule 1 line 26 = 3,300) | 44,700 | 5,000 | 49,700 | 49,700 |

In every case, total household resources = federal AGI + excluded income. Subtracting the excluded income again, as PolicyEngine-US did before #9795, gives 30,500, 55,000, 30,000, 32,000 and 44,700. That is wrong.

## Related

- PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9790 (this fix), stacked on PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9788 (capital losses on line 19).
- Templates: #1403, #1416, #1490.
- PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9795 (MI-1040CR line 30: federal exclusions stay in household resources), stacked on #9790; see the extension above.

## Extension: household membership (MCL 206.508(3))

The plan, required outputs and companion tests are extended in https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us/issues/1491#issuecomment-5999062372, for PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9796. Per-member inputs `claimant_income_received` and `spouse_income_received` replace `household_income_received`, which becomes a derived output (206.508(3): "'Household' means a claimant and spouse"). Amounts received for dependents count, as in MI-1040CR lines 21, 22 and 27; a dependent's own income does not. There are 8 more companion tests.

items.title: Encode South Dakota's optional state supplements (ARSD 67:12:14; ARSD 67:46; POMS SI DEN01415.011 B.5.b): the $15 independent living payment and the assisted living and adult foster care payment (PE-US PR 10169)

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Encoding debt

South Dakota's two optional state supplements have no RuleSpec module: the independent living payment (Senate Bill 32, ARSD 67:12:14) and the assisted living and adult foster care payment (Senate Bill 201, ARSD 67:46 long-term care assistance). Both are state-administered (POMS SI DEN01415.011 B: "The State administers its optional supplementary payments"). On `rulespec-us` `main` (`d8511cca7`, 2026-10-15), `us-sd/` holds only `policies/` (`cms/`, `income_tax/`). Issue searches for "South Dakota SSP", "South Dakota supplement", "South Dakota state supplement", "South Dakota optional", "67:12:14", "67:46", "28-5A" and "DEN01415" find no SSP issue.

PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10169 (open) adds the program to PolicyEngine-US:

- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/sd/dss/ssp/`, all Person and monthly: `sd_ssp` (the sum), `sd_ssp_independent`, `sd_ssp_care`, and the inputs `sd_ssp_care_certified`, `sd_ssp_care_setting` (`ASSISTED_LIVING` / `ADULT_FOSTER_CARE` / `NONE`), `sd_ssp_approved_care_cost`, `sd_ssp_care_income_deductions`, `sd_ssp_care_partial_month_days` (0 = full month), `sd_ssp_care_died_or_transferred` and `sd_ssp_care_joint_entry`.
- **Parameters** under `gov.states.sd.dss.ssp`: `individual_amount` ($15), `couple_first_amount` ($8), `couple_second_amount` ($7), `minimum_age` (18), `assisted_living_daily_rate` ($77.16, uprated with `gov.ssa.uprating` to the nearest $0.01), `resource_limit` ($2,000) and `joint_entry_resource_limit` ($3,000).
- **Wiring:** `sd_ssp` counts as SNAP and HUD unearned income and in `household_state_benefits` and `spm_unit_benefits`.
- **Tests** under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/sd/dss/ssp/`: `sd_ssp.yaml` (34 cases) and `integration.yaml` (11).
- **Scope:** 2026. The daily rate and resource limits start 2026-01-01; the other values start in 1978. Earlier years are out of scope.

## Module paths and corpus citations

| Proposed module | Provisions | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|
| `us-sd/regulations/arsd/67-12-14/` | :01(2), :02(1)-(4), :03(1)-(2), :04 | In the corpus as `us-sd/regulation/arsd/67/12/14` (manifest `manifests/us-sd-ssi-state-supplement.yaml`, LRC API, one record per section) |
| `us-sd/regulations/arsd/67-46/` | 04:02(2), 04:10(6)-(7), 04:13(2), 04:15, 05:30, 06:03, 06:05, 06:09, 06:10; co-cite 01:14, 05:42(7)-(8) | In the corpus as `us-sd/manual/dss/medicaid/67-46-01` to `67-46-06` (manifest `manifests/us-sd-medicaid-eligibility-manual.yaml`, one record per chapter, as of 2026-09-10) |
| `us-sd/policies/ssa/poms/si-den01415-011/sd-optional-supplement-amounts.yaml` | B.5.b | In the corpus as `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/den01415.011` (manifest `manifests/us-ssa-poms-si-2026-09-10.yaml`) |
| `us-sd/policies/dhs/ltss-fee-schedule/2026/state-optional-supplemental-assisted-living.yaml` | Service 08054 row; note 2 | Needs ingest: the [January 2026 schedule](https://dhs.sd.gov/content/dam/digital/united-states/south-dakota/sdo/pdf/long-term-services-and-supports/provider-portal/fee-schedules/LTSS-Fee-Schedule-and-In-Home-Services-Fee-Schedule-Effective-1-1-26.pdf) (the [July 2026 schedule](https://dhs.sd.gov/content/dam/digital/united-states/south-dakota/sdo/pdf/long-term-services-and-supports/provider-portal/fee-schedules/LTSS-Fee-Schedule-Effective-7-1-2026.pdf) repeats it) |
| Co-cited: SDCL 28-5A-1 | Authority | Needs ingest (no manifest) |

I checked the manifests on axiom-corpus `main` (`2137e79be`), not the signed release that rulespec-us pins.

## Source text (verbatim)

ARSD text is from the LRC rules API (`sdlegislature.gov/api/Rules/<rule>`), fetched 2026-10-15.

**[SDCL 28-5A-1](https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/28-5A-1):**

> [...] to provide, under such rules as may be promulgated by the department, for supplementary payments to qualified residents of South Dakota who are receiving or would be eligible to receive supplemental security income [...]

**ARSD 67:12:14** (independent living payment):

> (2) "Other income," any earned or unearned income except SSI and in-kind support and maintenance which may include but is not limited to wages from employment, social security retirement, survivors and disability benefits, [...]

> A person must meet all the following criteria to be eligible to receive benefits under the optional state supplemental program: (1) The person is receiving SSI and may be receiving in-kind income; (2) The person is an adult of at least 18 years of age and not in school; (3) The person is a resident of South Dakota; and (4) The person has independent living arrangements, such as a home, apartment, hotel room, or room in a boarding house, or resides in the household of another who provides in-kind support or maintenance. Institutionalized individuals or couples living in adult foster care or assisted living arrangements are not eligible.

> The optional supplemental payment shall be discontinued in the month the department is notified of one or more of the following: [...] (2) The person is receiving other income in addition to SSI benefits;

> Persons eligible for the state optional supplemental program shall receive benefits at a rate approved by the department based on the annual appropriation by the state Legislature.

**[POMS SI DEN01415.011](https://secure.ssa.gov/poms.nsf/lnx/0501415011DEN) B.5.b** (Senate Bill 32 column):

> Only those individuals and couples on the SDX who are in LA A or B and in current pay status who have no other income. An individual will receive $15 per month and each member of a couple will receive $8 and $7 respectively.

**ARSD 67:46** (care payment):

- 04:02(2): "'Income,' unless specifically excluded in § 67:46:04:03, any money or in-kind payments before deductions;"
- 04:10(6)-(7):

  > (6) For a married couple, if both spouses enter a long-term care facility during the same calendar month, the department considers the couple's combined income available to each other and shared equally in the calendar month of entry regardless of room occupancy. After the calendar month of entry, the department treats the couple as separate individuals and considers only that income which is actually available to the individual; and (7) For a married couple living together during the calendar month that one spouse enters assisted living or adult foster care, the department considers the couple's combined income available to each other in the calendar month of entry.

- 04:13(2) (52 SDR 125, effective July 1, 2026):

  > The department must refer an individual to the Social Security Administration to apply for supplemental security income if the individual's income, minus twenty dollars, is less than: [...] (2) The supplemental security income standard benefit amount of nine hundred ninety-four dollars, if the individual is not institutionalized but living in an adult foster care home or an assisted living facility.

- 04:15:

  > An individual not receiving home and community based waiver services and who is in an assisted living facility or in adult foster care is ineligible to receive assistance under this article when the individual's net income exceeds the monthly care rates after application of the budgeting regulations contained in §§ 67:46:06:03 to 67:46:06:07, inclusive.

- 05:30: "The resource limit, including both liquid and nonliquid resources, for long-term care assistance is $2,000 for an individual and $3,000 for an individual with a spouse if both spouses begin receiving long-term care services in the same month."
- 06:03: "For purposes of determining the amount of long-term care assistance, income is considered according to subdivisions 67:46:04:03(1) to (5), inclusive; §§ 67:46:04:04, 67:46:04:06 and 67:46:04:08 to 67:46:04:10, inclusive."
- 06:05: "An applicant or recipient residing in a nursing or intermediate care facility is allowed: (1) A deduction of one hundred dollars per month to cover personal needs;"
- 06:09: "Whenever the residence period in a long-term care facility is less than a full month, the recipient's income shall not be applied toward the cost of care unless the recipient died or transferred to another long-term care facility."
- 06:10: "Payment for program benefits shall be based on the difference between the individual's available income and the monthly rate for the provider of the individual's choice [...]"
- 01:14: "An individual applying for or receiving medical assistance must take advantage of all income and resources to which the individual is entitled, including items such as social security, SSI, [...] Failure or refusal by the individual to take the necessary action to take advantage of the income and resources makes the individual ineligible for medical assistance."

**LTSS fee schedule, January 2026** (one page), "LTSS State-Funded KIND Program Service Codes" column:

| Service | Code | Rate | Frequency |
|---|---|---|---|
| State Optional Supplemental Assisted Living 2. | 08054 | $77.16 | per day |

> 2. This rate includes Room and Board. The State Optional Supplemental Assisted Living service rate is adjusted annually in January based on the Social Security Administration (SSA) Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA). The State Optional Supplemental Assisted Living service, also known as the Regular Assisted Living Program, rate is effective 01/01/2026.

## Required outputs

All Person, monthly.

| Output | PolicyEngine-US | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| Independent amounts (Money parameters) | `individual_amount`, `couple_first_amount`, `couple_second_amount` | $15; $8 and $7 (B.5.b; rate set under 67:12:14:04) |
| Daily rate (Money parameter) | `assisted_living_daily_rate` | $77.16 a day (08054), COLA-indexed each January (note 2) |
| Resource limits (Money parameters) | `resource_limit`, `joint_entry_resource_limit` | $2,000; $3,000 for an individual whose spouse begins care in the same month (05:30); PE pools the couple's |
| Independent eligible (Judgment) | in `sd_ssp_independent` | Receives SSI AND age 18+ AND not in school AND living arrangement A or B AND no other income (:01(2); pooled for an eligible couple) AND not in assisted living or adult foster care (setting set or certified) |
| Independent payment (Money) | `sd_ssp_independent` | $15; eligible couple (joint SSI claim, both qualify) $8 and $7 |
| Care eligible (Judgment) | in `sd_ssp_care` | Certified nonwaiver placement AND aged, blind or disabled AND citizen or SSI qualified noncitizen AND resources within the limit AND not incarcerated AND (takes up SSI OR federal SSI would be 0) (04:13(2), 01:14) |
| Care payment (Money) | `sd_ssp_care` | max(0, min(approved charge, days × rate) − max(0, income − deductions)); no daily cap in adult foster care; income = gross earned and unearned income plus SSI (04:02(2)), shared equally for a joint-entry couple in the entry month (04:10(6)); income set to 0 in a partial month unless the recipient died or transferred (06:09) |

## Companion tests

From the sources above, not from PolicyEngine-US output. South Dakota residents aged 65, January 2026 (FBR $994), resources within limits unless listed, only the income listed; F-I are certified nonwaiver assisted living residents.

| Case | Derivation | Expected | Source | PolicyEngine-US case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. SSI-only adult at home | — | 15 | B.5.b | `sd_ssp.yaml` "Case 1, SSI is the only cash income." |
| B. Eligible couple, SSI only | — | 8 and 7 | B.5.b | `integration.yaml` "Case 1, eligible SSI couple receives eight and seven dollars." |
| C. SSI recipient with $500 of Social Security | other income > 0 | 0 | :01(2), :03(2) | `sd_ssp.yaml` "Case 2, small Social Security benefit disqualifies despite an SSI payment." |
| D. Household of another, in-kind support | ISM is not other income | 15 | :02(1), (4) | `sd_ssp.yaml` "Case 3, in-kind support does not disqualify." |
| E. Age 17, or a student | — | 0 | :02(2) | `sd_ssp.yaml` "Case 4, child is not eligible for independent supplement." and "Case 5, student is not eligible for independent supplement." |
| F. Full January, $3,000 charge, SSI $994 | 31 × 77.16 − 994 | 1,397.96 | 06:10, 08054 | `sd_ssp.yaml` "Case 10, actual care bill capped at January daily reimbursement." |
| G. 10 days in January, $1,500 charge | min(1,500, 771.60), income not applied | 771.60 | 06:09 | `sd_ssp.yaml` "Case 16, certified partial month without income contribution." |
| H. Joint-entry couple, resources $3,200 | 3,200 > 3,000 | 0 each | 05:30 | `integration.yaml` "Case 5, joint entry pools spouses' resources against the joint limit." |
| I. Joint-entry couple, full month, incomes $1,200 and $800, $2,200 charges | 2,200 − (1,200 + 800) / 2 | 1,200 each | 04:10(6) | `integration.yaml` "Case 7, joint entry within the pooled limit shares the couple's income equally." |

## Interpretations that change a result

- **Couple income (independent).** PE pools an eligible couple's other income (B.5.b), so either spouse's income excludes both; 67:12:14:03(2) reads per person. Integration Case 3 ([0, 0]); see the first comment.
- **Joint-entry sharing comes before deductions.** Each spouse's own deductions come off half the combined income; no source states the order. Integration Cases 7 ([1,200, 1,200]), 9 (incomes $2,500 and $500: [700, 700]) and 12 (a $100 deduction for one spouse: [800, 700]).
- **Joint-entry resources are pooled.** 05:30 does not say whose resources meet $3,000; PE pools the couple's, as 05:42(8) does in nursing facilities. Integration Case 5: [0, 0] on 3,200 pooled; own 1,800 and 1,400 would pass.
- **Joint entry is the entry month only, and needs both spouses.** `sd_ssp_care_joint_entry` drives the $3,000 pooled limit and income sharing in that month; later months, or a flag on one spouse only, use $2,000 and own income. Integration Cases 6, 8 and 13; see the first comment.
- **Partial months still apply 04:15.** Income isn't applied in a partial month (06:09), but a resident whose net income exceeds the monthly rate (the covered-days charge scaled to the month) is ineligible, since 06:01 applies chapter 04 first. `sd_ssp.yaml` Case 35 (0).
- **Not modeled:** the month only one spouse enters care (04:10(7), 05:42(7) combine the couple's income and resources); PE uses the entrant's own.
- **Care setting.** Any assisted living or adult foster care resident, including waiver and private-pay residents, loses the $15 (:02(4)); the care payment goes only to residents certified for the nonwaiver program (04:15: "not receiving home and community based waiver services"). `sd_ssp.yaml` Cases 33, 34 and 36 (a private-pay medical facility) (0).
- **SSI pursuit.** A resident who would qualify for SSI but does not take it up gets no care payment (`sd_ssp.yaml` Case 32, 0); one over the SSI income limit need not apply (Case 23, 700). PE uses the federal SSI income test, not 04:13(2)'s income − $20 < $994.
- **Daily rate forward.** $77.16 follows `gov.ssa.uprating` to the cent until the next fee schedule (PE projects $79.32 for 2027). No PE case.
- **History** is out of scope; earlier months reuse $77.16 (the July 2025 schedule shows $75.05 from 01/01/2025).
- **Federal SSI.** Care income includes PE's own SSI; parity checks should take SSI as an input.

Source conflicts are in the first comment.

items.title: [pe-parity] Pennsylvania CCW Appendix A: include employee pretax premiums in qualifying medical expenses (PE-US #10046)

labels.name: pe-parity

items.body:
<!-- premium-input-contract:10046:pa-ccw -->

## Encoding gap and scope

**Parity status: queued.** Filed by the US + core hub under Max's standing go d1142.

Mirror [PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10046](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/pull/10046), exact head `b5a0b3cc588d95f00768d6e664e3d3075f851313`. Pennsylvania Child Care Works counts employee wages before health-insurance deductions, and allows qualifying unreimbursed health-care premiums in its medical deduction without a tax-status exclusion. Add the separate employee pretax payments to the non-pretax medical-premium aggregate once.

Against main `d97b9164c69f3295da44f3ace67985cc5bcf2fbd`, annual medical expenses in the two new cases change **2400 to 6000** (mixed payment methods) and **0 to 6000** (all pretax). Adjusted annual income changes **36000 to 33600** in each case. The medical expense threshold is 10% of gross income; wages remain $36,000 annually.

## Target and existing-coverage search

Proposed module `us-pa/regulations/55/3042/appendix-a.yaml`, companion `us-pa/regulations/55/3042/appendix-a.test.yaml`. Target Part I(A) and Part II(C). Keep unrelated income inclusions, stepparent deduction charts, household eligibility and subsidy schedules outside this correction.

All-state searches on 2026-10-13 by `Pennsylvania Child Care`, `Child Care Works`, `CCW`, `pa_ccw`, `3042`, and `10046` found no covering CCW issue. The rulespec-us main tree `4b35d0872d92308ef7c41cc00cb17c7610be882b` contains no Chapter 3042 or CCW module. Pennsylvania LIHEAP [#1536](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us/issues/1536) is a different program and does not cover this rule.

## Operative official text (verbatim)

[55 Pa. Code Chapter 3042 Appendix A Part I(A), official PDF p.59](https://www.pacodeandbulletin.gov/secure/pacode/data/055/chapter3042/055_3042.pdf#page=59):

> before deductions

Part I(A) includes a parent/caretaker's employee compensation before the listed deductions, expressly including health insurance.

[Appendix A Part II(C), official PDF p.61](https://www.pacodeandbulletin.gov/secure/pacode/data/055/chapter3042/055_3042.pdf#page=61):

> A medical expense not reimbursed through medical insurance that exceeds 10% of the family gross monthly income.
>
> health care premiums

The expense must arise in the 90 days preceding notification and be expected to continue for six months after it began. The rule uses monthly expenses, a monthly payment plan, or both, and expressly lists health-care premiums among qualifying medical expenses.

Part I(A) supplies the gross wage inclusion; Part II(C) supplies the premium deduction and its conditions. A qualified pretax salary reduction remains part of this gross-wage base and its employee-paid premium is a medical payment. Employer contributions are not an expense incurred by the family. Do not import federal Schedule A exclusions into this program.

## Corpus contract and named blocker

**Blocker: admit official 55 Pa. Code Chapter 3042 Appendix A Parts I(A), II(C).** At corpus ref `8f7d60aaced28ee4252b9237f9d6e02360dc34bc`, the complete tree has Pennsylvania SNAP/tax sources but no Chapter 3042/CCW source or provision artifact. Proposed ingestion targets are `us-pa/regulation/55/3042/appendix-a/part-i/a` and `us-pa/regulation/55/3042/appendix-a/part-ii/c`, subject to the corpus maintainers' canonical identifiers.

Capture the official PDF, the exact operative excerpts on 1-based PDF pages 59 and 61, effective dates and hash; admit them and verify their presence in the signed release selected for generation. Existing pin: `us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap`, SHA256 `0d69a0cdbe024fc2276f3c261c00402bb0a47488ac5f482cc20bd3404980adbc`. The signed encoder is unavailable in this workspace; each billed run requires separate approval. No run or handwritten RuleSpec is authorized by this filing.

## Required outputs and companion expectations

Expose gross wages before payroll health-premium deductions, qualifying employee-paid medical expenses including both disjoint payment methods, the amount above 10% of gross monthly income, and adjusted monthly income (with explicit annual-unit conversion for the PE bridge). Native tests must supply facts establishing the Part II(C) unreimbursed, recent-incurrence and expected-continuation conditions. PE's current annual proxy does not independently model those administrative dates; these companions assume those conditions hold.

Expected values come from the PR's [pa_ccw_adjusted_income.yaml at the pinned head](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/blob/b5a0b3cc588d95f00768d6e664e3d3075f851313/policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/pa/dhs/ccw/pa_ccw_adjusted_income.yaml), with arithmetic independently established by the same official provision. Period `2026`, one Pennsylvania employee, steady payments, all expenses qualifying and unreimbursed, no other income/deductions, employer premium payments zero:

| Companion | Annual PE inputs | Expected annual outputs |
|---|---|---|
| Pretax and after-tax premiums both count toward the medical deduction | `state_code=PA`, `employment_income=36000`, `health_insurance_premiums=2400`, `pre_tax_health_insurance_premiums=3600` | `pa_ccw_medical_expenses=6000`; `pa_ccw_adjusted_income=33600` |
| Moving all premiums to pretax payroll leaves the medical deduction unchanged | `state_code=PA`, `employment_income=36000`, `health_insurance_premiums=0`, `pre_tax_health_insurance_premiums=6000` | `pa_ccw_medical_expenses=6000`; `pa_ccw_adjusted_income=33600` |

For either case: monthly gross income $3,000, employee medical payments $500, floor $300, deductible excess $200, adjusted income $2,800/month = $33,600/year. Preserve this transfer invariant while holding wages, expense conditions and other deductions fixed. Applicable non-pretax aggregate/decomposed inputs are alternative representations; do not add overlapping components.

items.title: LIHEAP wave 1b: encode Maryland MEAP regular heating assistance

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Maryland MEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1b, covering the scope and effective period of the corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

Comparison: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9746 (`md-meap`); see the historical snapshot below. Pin the final reviewed revision for oracle validation.

## PolicyEngine implementation (historical snapshot)

- **PR history:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9746; recorded comparison head `906c7855b0` (2026-10-06). Its review fixes and scope are detailed in the outputs, source interpretations and tests below. This is a historical reference; pin the final reviewed revision for oracle validation. October 20 and 22 requirements are incorporated below.
- **Scope:** the regular heating benefit of the Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP), paid once per program year from the FY25, FY26 and FY27 MEAP Benefit Matrices: residence, income and categorical eligibility, household size under the manual's rule (children under 18 always count), countable income, the seven payment levels by fuel, the subsidized and submetered housing level, the heat-in-rent denial, and the Garrett County multiplier. Out of scope: the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP) and its matrix, arrearage retirement (EARA, GARA), crisis assistance, cooling, weatherization, heating-equipment repair or replacement, the $21 SNAP nominal payment, shelters, the medical-expense waiver and any supplemental benefit increase.
- **Policy periods:** three seasons. State fiscal year N runs July 1 of N-1 to June 30 of N (COMAR 07.03.21.02B(6)); every Maryland variable is annual and reads the value in force on 1 January of the model year, so model period `2025` carries FY25, `2026` FY26 and `2027` FY27. B(20): "“Qualified alien” means an individual who is not a citizen of the United States who: (a) Is lawfully admitted for permanent residence under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA); (b) Is admitted to the United States as a refugee under §207 of the Immigration and Nationality Act; (c) Is granted asylum under §208 of the Immigration and Nationality Act; (d) Has had deportation or removal withheld under §234(h) or 241(b)(3) of the Immigration and Nationality Act; (e) Has been granted status as a Cuban or Haitian entrant as defined in §501(e) of the Refugee Education Assistance Act of 1980; (f) Is paroled into the United States under §212(d)(5) of the Immigration and Nationality Act for a period of at least 1 year; (g) Is granted conditional entry pursuant to §203(a)(7) of the Immigration and Nationality Act as in effect before April 1, 1980; or (h) Is a battered spouse, battered child, or parent or child of a battered individual." ## Required outputs

| Output | policyengine-us variable | Entity, period | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qualified household size | `md_meap_household_size` | SPM unit, year | Members who are citizens or federal qualified noncitizens (`is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`) plus every member under 18 (`adult_age`) regardless of status, following manual page 108; nonqualified adults are not counted, but every member's income is. |
| Countable earnings | `md_meap_countable_earned_income` | Person, year | Wages plus net self-employment, SSTB self-employment and farm operations income, each floored at zero (`income/sources/earned`). Zero for a person under 18 (`adult_age`) or a full-time student (COMAR .04E(3)). |
| Countable income | `md_meap_countable_income` | SPM unit, year | Earnings of every member, plus max(Social Security + railroad benefits - the computed Medicare Part B premium, 0) per member (COMAR .04D(3), D(26), E(20); plan 1.9), plus each `income/sources/unearned` item floored at zero at the unit level (SSI, TANF, ordinary dividends, interest, estate income, pensions, military retirement income (retiree pay plus SBP), survivor benefits other than Social Security survivor benefits (`survivor_benefits`, under D(12), D(13) and D(18)), retirement distributions, child support received, alimony, workers' compensation, unemployment compensation, veterans' benefits, strike benefits, rental income, farm rental income), less child support paid, floored at zero. |
| Poverty guideline | `md_meap_fpg` | SPM unit, year | HHS guideline of the prior calendar year (`fpg_year_lag` 1) for max(qualified size, 1). |
| Income limit | `md_meap_income_limit` | SPM unit, year | Size 1-10: 2 x guideline, the guideline of the calendar year before the model year (2024 for FY25, 2025 for FY26, 2026 for FY27). Size 11 and over: floor(F(size) x floor(0.6 x four-person SMI)), where F is the 45 CFR 96.85(b) factor (52% + 16% per person 2-6 + 3% per further person); this reproduces the rows ACF IM 2025-02 Attachment 4 prints for sizes 7 to 12. |
| Categorically eligible | `md_meap_categorically_eligible` | SPM unit, year | Computed `snap`, `tanf` or `ssi` greater than zero in the year (receipt after take-up; no receives-style input). Means-tested VA benefits are not identified. |
| Eligible | `md_meap_eligible` | SPM unit, year | (categorically eligible or countable income at or below the limit or strictly below 110% of `md_meap_fpg`, rounded to cents), at least one citizen or qualified-alien member (a child counted regardless of status does not satisfy this), a heating cost (`has_heating_expense`) or heat in rent, not (heat in rent and (housing assistance or public housing)), and not assisted living. Maryland only. |
| Payment level | `md_meap_level` | SPM unit, year | Ratio of countable income to the guideline (divisor 1 where the guideline is zero, outside Maryland) against inclusive band tops 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2 gives levels 1-5 and 7 (`income_level`); when the level is not 7 and the unit has housing assistance, is in public housing or is submetered, level 6 (`subsidized_level`). |
| Dwelling arrangement (input) | `md_meap_dwelling_type` | SPM unit, year | `STANDARD` (default), `SUB_METERED` (level 6), `ASSISTED_LIVING` (denied). |
| Benefit | `md_meap` | SPM unit, year | When eligible: the program year's matrix cell for the fuel row (ELECTRICITY, SOLAR: Electric; NATURAL_GAS: Gas; WOOD, COAL: Wood/Coal; FUEL_OIL, KEROSENE: Oil; PROPANE: Propane; OTHER, NONE, UNSPECIFIED: $0) at max(level, 1); times 1.1 in Garrett County when the level is not 7; floor(x + 0.5). Zero otherwise. |
