| 30 | Medicare deduction in the full calculation (`integration.yaml` Case 11) | retiree aged 70, Baltimore County, `social_security_retirement` $32,000, gas with a $1,150 bill; no SNAP, TCA or SSI | $32,000 is over the $31,300 one-person limit, but the model's 2026 Part B premium for this retiree is $202.90 a month ($2,434.80 a year, no Medicare Savings Program at this income): 32,000 - 2,434.80 = 29,565.20, at or below $31,300; 29,565.20 / 15,650 = 1.889, "151-200% FPL": Level 5, Gas $300. | income $29,565.20; limit $31,300; Level 5; eligible; $300 | COMAR .04D(3); IG26; matrix Gas row |
| 31 | Categorical eligibility from computed SNAP (`integration.yaml` Case 12; nothing forced) | parent aged 30 with `employment_income_before_lsr` $18,000 (the input the TANF earned-income list reads, so TCA computes as $0), child aged 6, Baltimore City, gas with a $1,150 bill; SNAP, TCA and SSI computed | The model's SNAP for this household is positive, which plan p. 5 and manual p. 62 treat as categorical eligibility; TCA is $0, so countable income is $18,000 (D(1)); 18,000 / 21,150 = 0.851: Level 3, Gas $400. | categorical; income $18,000; Level 3; eligible; $400 | plan p. 5; manual p. 62; matrix Gas row |

## Interpretations and gaps

- **Nonqualified children in household size (settled 2026-10-06: the manual).** COMAR .04C(1) excludes every nonqualified member from the count; manual p. 108 counts "All children under 18 ... regardless of citizenship" and excludes only ineligible adults. The owner chose the manual, the operating rule: `md_meap_household_size` counts qualified members plus every child under `adult_age`, and `md_meap_eligible` still requires one citizen or qualified-alien member (manual p. 108: "the household must have at least one eligible member"). Test 1 now reads $400 at size 2 and test 22 covers four mixed-status households. The conflict is recorded in the variable and the PR body; no amendment reconciling it was found.
- **Level for unsubsidized heat in rent (gap).** No source read states which matrix level applies when heat is included in rent outside public or subsidized housing. Plan p. 10 covers payment to the landlord and COMAR .07A(2) the delivery; plan 2.5 says the program considers "whether the utility bill is in the name of the customer or the landlord". The draft pays the ordinary income level and fuel row (test 3, $880) and labels it an inference. Missing evidence: an FY26 OHEP benefit-determination instruction for landlord-paid heat.
- **Sizes 9 and 10 (interpretation).** Rows 1-8 equal twice the 2025 guideline exactly. The sheet's "For each additional HH member add $11,004" line gives $119,304 and $130,308; twice the guideline gives $119,300 and $130,300, which the draft computes and test 15 asserts. The two readings of one page differ by $4 and $8 at sizes 9 and 10 only.
- **Garrett County (interpretation).** The 1.1 multiplier is express in plan 2.5 of the FY2025 and FY2026 plans. Half-up rounding of the half-dollar products and the flat $25 at Level 7 follow the FY27 Garrett table and are not stated for FY25 or FY26 (tests 5, 11, 24). The FY27 Garrett table equals 1.1 times the statewide cells, rounded half up, in every cell except oil Level 4, which prints $1,210 (1.1 times the FY26 oil Level 1) where 1.1 times $980 is $1,078; the model keeps the multiplier and pays $1,078 (test 26), documented in `md_meap`. Plan 2.6's "Maximum Benefit $1,100" still conflicts with $1,210 for FY26 Garrett oil at Level 1; the model pays $1,210.
- **Level 7 over Level 6 (interpretation).** Manual p. 63 pays "CE applicants assessed at Level 6 (household exceeds 200% FPL)" a nominal benefit, numbering the over-200% column 6 where the FY26 matrix numbers it 7 ("Level 7 Over 200%FPL"; FY27: "Over 200%CE"). The draft uses the matrix numbering and lets Level 7 take precedence over the subsidized or submetered Level 6 (tests 2, 13, 16). The nominal level applies only above 200% of the guideline, not above the SMI limit (test 8, Case 10).
- **Fuel rows (interpretation).** Gas and Wood/Coal are separate parameters since 2026-10-06 (`amount/gas`, `amount/wood_coal`) because the FY25 and FY27 matrices print different amounts although the FY26 cells coincide. Kerosene is mapped to the Oil row (labeled Oil/Kerosene from FY27; manual p. 6 lists kerosene as a MEAP fuel). A grid-tied solar home is paid from the Electric row (manual 1.1.1, page 6, lists solar subscriptions; the bill `heating_expense` reads for it is the electricity bill). Other fuels and no heating have no row and pay $0 (test 12).
- **Dwelling arrangement input (interpretation).** `md_meap_dwelling_type` adds `SUB_METERED` because the matrix column is "Subsidized/Sub metered" and no existing input identifies a submetered home, and `ASSISTED_LIVING` for the COMAR .06D(3)(k) denial, which no published schedule requires and no existing input covers. Ordinary subsidized homes use `receives_housing_assistance` and `is_in_public_housing`, although COMAR .02B(24) defines subsidized housing as privately owned complexes and B(19) public housing separately; the Level 6 treatment of public housing rests on plan p. 9's wording.
- **Out-of-state table lookup (defect found in review, fixed at head `9e139912b6`).** At the first head `md_meap` indexed the amount tables with the raw level, and units outside Maryland carry level 0, which is not a key; any simulation mixing an eligible Maryland unit with another state raised. The level is floored to 1 before the lookups, which cannot change a Maryland result, and since 2026-10-06 `md_meap_level` divides by 1 where the guideline is zero so the rows `defined_for` masks produce no 0 / 0; test 14 covers the two-state case.
- **Not modeled (limitations).** Means-tested VA categorical eligibility (`veterans_benefits` cannot identify the subset); the Medicare Part D premium (no variable; the Part B premium is deducted since 2026-10-06 under COMAR .04D(3), D(26), E(20) and plan 1.9 "Excluding MediCare deduction", tests 28 and 30, using the computed out-of-pocket premium, zero when a Medicare Savings Program pays it); COMAR .04D items without an input (TDAP, royalties, monetary gifts and loans, mine worker's benefits, armed forces dependent allowances, Criminal Injuries Compensation Board payments, fellowship stipends, live-in home-care payments); the court-order cap on the child support deduction (`child_support_expense` is assumed court-ordered); the 30-day income window (annual income is used for the limit and the level); COMAR .02B(20)(h) battered spouse or child (no status input); the once-per-program-year rule (.09D); the medical-expense waiver (.03C); and any supplemental increase (.07B(2)). Chapter 207 enrolls households whose member "MEETS THE FINANCIAL ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS" of the four programs; the draft, like the plan and manual, uses receipt after take-up. Plan 1.9 differs from COMAR in leaving "Interest, dividends, or royalties" unchecked and checking "Cash gifts" and "One-time lump-sum payments", and Attachment A lists "Inheritance and lottery winnings" and "AmeriCorps or VISTA payments" as countable; the draft follows COMAR (interest and dividends count; lump sums and AmeriCorps or VISTA do not). Plan 2.1 states the thresholds as SMI percentages (39.00% to 58.70%) that approximate the dollar rows; the draft follows the Income Guidelines dollar rows for sizes 1-10 and derives 11+ from the federal SMI table, whose vintage (FFY2026, $154,117) is the model's choice, not a Maryland publication. An unknown county is treated as outside Garrett County. The SPM unit stands in for the COMAR .02B(16) household.
- **Coverage limits and exclusions.** `heating_type` is a required input; an unspecified fuel is eligible but pays $0 (test 9), and the national datasets carry no heating inputs, so microsimulation totals are $0 (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us issue 9754). EUSP and its matrix, EARA and GARA arrearages, crisis assistance, cooling, weatherization, equipment and the $21 SNAP nominal payment (plan 1.7b) are out of scope; nothing from them is in the PR.
- **FY25 and FY27 (encoded 2026-10-06).** The five amount tables carry `2024-07-01` (FY2025 matrix, Clearinghouse copy), `2025-07-01` (FY26) and `2026-07-01` (FY27 statewide table) entries, change-only; the level, multiplier, county, poverty-rate and lag parameters start at `2024-07-01`; the income-source lists, `adult_age` and the SMI parameters stay at `2025-07-01`. FY25 Level 6 is $102 for every fuel and the FY25 plan prints the $750 maximum (oil Level 1). The FY25 limits are twice the 2024 guideline, matching the FY2025 matrix's monthly 151-200% FPL tops (test 27); no FY27 OHEP income-guidelines sheet was found on the OHEP site, so the FY27 limits follow the rule with the 2026 guideline and are not independently published. Every unearned source is floored at zero at the unit level (test 29). `military_retirement_income` counts retiree pay plus the separate SBP input once under D(12)–(13); SBP is not included in `survivor_benefits`.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-md-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-md-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [us-md-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-md-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml)
- [us-md-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-md-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml)

Manifest presence is not proof that all attachments are captured, the source is complete, or it is admitted in the corpus release pinned by rulespec-us. Verify the signed release and fill the actual gaps rather than duplicating existing ingestion: the FY2025 and FY26 MEAP Benefit Matrices, the FY2025 plan, the FY2026 Income Guidelines, COMAR 07.03.21 and 2023 Chapter 207 have no manifest; the attachments manifest holds the FY27 tables, which are now encoded.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-md/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover every statewide payment cell for FY25 to FY27, Garrett and nominal payments, the manual household rule, the Medicare Part B deduction, submetered/assisted-living treatment, income boundaries and larger households, mixed-status membership, categorical receipt/take-up, and explicit fiscal-year mapping. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: LIHEAP wave 2b: encode Washington LIHEAP regular heating assistance

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Washington LIHEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 2b, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10345 (branch `wa-liheap-wave2b`), open, not merged. Head `329eb32148` (2026-10-23), a comment fix on top of the merge of policyengine-us `main` at `ee6c90961d`; this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **Sources missing from the corpus.** axiom-corpus `main` captures the accepted FFY2026 state plan, the FY2026 benefit calculation worksheet, the 2024, 2025 and 2026 HHS poverty guidelines and the CY2026 Medicare Part B premium notice. No manifest holds the other sources the branch cites: the Department of Commerce Washington State Weatherization Manual (July 2026), whose Policies 1.1.1 and 1.1.2 tie weatherization income rules to the LIHEAP guidelines and are the branch's only Commerce text for the 20% wage allowance, the 10% retirement and unemployment deductions and the mixed-status count; the Commerce PY27 LIHEAP Eligibility Guidelines (heating responsibility, the program year and the period 2027 limits); the Byrd Barr Place Program Year 2025-2026 application packet (assessment window, payroll deduction, heat-in-rent documents, self-employment, FY2026 monthly limits); the Kitsap Community Resources (KCR) self-employment worksheet (monthly loss floor); the CACLMT LIHEAP FAQ (the child support paid deduction the branch does not apply); and the draft FFY2027 plan (not adopted). These need ingest. The Commerce LIHEAP operating manual sits behind a State of Washington staff sign-in, so no public source exists to ingest for the household definition, a mixed-status rule, the surrogate heat cost schedule or the worksheet's rounding.
- **Program bundle scope.** The LIHEAP program bundle on corpus `main` (`manifests/program-bundles/liheap.yaml`, as of 2026-10-06) marks both Washington FY2026 documents `scope: excluded` with the reason `Back-year table: not current law`, while FY2026 is the branch's only verified year.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-23; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.
- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10345 was a draft from 2026-10-21 and is marked ready for review on 2026-10-23 with no reviews yet, so there is no revision to pin.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10345, branch `wa-liheap-wave2b`, head `329eb32148` (2026-10-23), which closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10339. Commit `b92d806562` (2026-10-23) applies the 2026-10-21 review fixes: military Survivor Benefit Plan annuities count through `military_retirement_income` with the 10% retirement deduction; Social Security counts net of the computed `medicare_part_b_premium` (plan item 1.9); the deduction for child support paid, sourced only to a subgrantee FAQ, is removed; a comment records that `wa_ssp` is not counted because item 1.9 names only SSI; the wage-rate file gains the Commerce Policy 1.1.2 reference and the income-limit variable a page anchor; duplicate cases are deleted, two test comments are corrected and documentation is reworded. Commit `45755acd5d` replaces the built-in `sum()` over person calls with explicit loops (no behavior change). Merge `a4e881b4b0` brings in policyengine-us `main` at `ee6c90961d`, and commit `329eb32148` corrects the `retirement_deduction_rate` comment to name all three `retirement_sources` (no behavior change). Everything below describes that head; oracle fixtures will pin the merged commit.
- **Scope:** Washington LIHEAP regular heating assistance, administered by the Department of Commerce through local agencies, one grant a program year, for FY2026: Washington residence; household size from citizens and qualified noncitizens, with every member's income counted; countable income (earnings only from members 18 and over) with a 20% allowance on wages, 10% deductions on pensions, retirement distributions, military retirement income and unemployment compensation, Social Security net of the Part B premium, and TANF and State Family Assistance once per unit; the inclusive 150% poverty-guideline limit; heating responsibility (a heating bill or heat paid through rent); the Actual and Surrogate Heat Cost Benefit Calculation Worksheet with its 24 household adjusters; the $250 minimum and $1,250 maximum; and a final cap at the reported annual heating cost. Out of scope: year-round crisis assistance, weatherization and the Policy 1.4.2 repairs and services in plan item 2.7 (blankets, space heaters, air conditioners, generators, window and roof repair), cooling, the $20.01 SNAP nominal payment, the State Home Energy Assistance Program and Puget Sound Energy HELP that subgrantees run beside LIHEAP, the surrogate heat cost schedule (not recovered), priority scheduling, funding availability and the once-per-program-year limit.
- **Policy periods:** one verified season, FY2026: the plan's report period October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026 (page 1), within heating-assistance dates of operation from 10/01/2025 to 09/30/2027 (item 1.1, page 4); the PY27 sheet gives the program year as October 1 through September 30. Washington variables are annual and read 1 January values, so period `2026` is FY2026 on the 2025 HHS guidelines (`fpg_year_lag` 1); the Byrd Barr FY2025-26 monthly maximums are 150% of those guidelines divided by 12 and rounded. All 16 parameter files date every value `2025-10-01`. `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2026"`. Earlier periods take the same Washington values by backfilling, on the lagged guideline (period `2025` on the 2024 guidelines): unverified estimates. Later periods carry the FY2026 worksheet forward on the lagged guideline: period `2027` uses the 2026 guidelines, whose 150% limits equal the PY27 sheet (income-limit Cases 13 and 14), but its awards are carried-forward estimates. The draft FFY2027 plan keeps 150%, $250 and $1,250 and changes several income boxes; the branch does not adopt it (interpretation 17).
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/wa/commerce/liheap/`: `wa_liheap`, `wa_liheap_countable_income`, `wa_liheap_eligible`, `wa_liheap_household_size`, `wa_liheap_income_limit`. No new input variable. The award reads the shared `heating_expense` (the bill for the primary `heating_type`); the limit calls `fpg` in `variables/gov/hhs/tax_unit_fpg.py`.
- **Parameters:** 16 files under `gov.states.wa.commerce.liheap`: `fpg_rate` (1.5), `fpg_year_lag` (1); `income/` `earned_income_min_age` (18), `wage_deduction_rate` (0.2), `retirement_deduction_rate` (0.1), `unemployment_deduction_rate` (0.1), `business_sources` (4 sources), `retirement_sources` (3), `unearned_sources` (12); `payment/` `household_adjuster` (single-amount scale, sizes 1 to 24), `income_constant` (3,648.10 a month), `quotient_numerator` (1,460.80 a month), `multiplier_constant` (1.3), `intermediate_rounding_increment` (0.01), `minimum` (250), `maximum` (1,250). Plus a `programs.yaml` entry (status partial) and a changelog fragment.
- **Tests:** 118 YAML cases in 5 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/wa/commerce/liheap/` at the head (`wa_liheap.yaml` 67, `wa_liheap_countable_income.yaml` 23, `wa_liheap_eligible.yaml` 10, `wa_liheap_household_size.yaml` 4, `wa_liheap_income_limit.yaml` 14). The review fixes added three cases (`wa_liheap.yaml` Cases 66 and 67, `wa_liheap_countable_income.yaml` Case 23) and deleted 23 duplicates (eight per-fuel and three heating-cost award cases, ten income-limit cases, two child-support-paid cases). Every benefit and eligibility case sends `heating_type`. Local runs before the 2026-10-21 review fixes passed; the fixes were not run locally; CI validates.

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence on axiom-corpus `main` (`3666647728`, 2026-10-24T01:37Z) was checked on 2026-10-23 against the full manifest list, by reading the Washington LIHEAP, poverty-guideline, LIHEAP annual-figures, CMS 2026 and LIHEAP program-bundle manifests, and by GitHub code search of `manifests/` for the Commerce, Byrd Barr and KCR URLs; the signed release was not checked. rulespec-us `main` (`5db28f7e1f`, 2026-10-24T02:39Z) has `us-wa/policies/` (cms: CHIP and Medicaid eligibility levels; income_tax), `us-wa/regulations/388` (DSHS rules, including WAC 388-478-0020) and `us-wa/statutes/82`; none is LIHEAP, there is no Commerce module and no `us/` poverty-guideline module. The paths below follow that layout. Pages are physical PDF pages; they equal the printed numbers in the plan and the weatherization manual, and worksheet pages 1-2 are printed pages 10-11.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-wa/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-1` | Report period and status (page 1); 1.1 dates of operation and the funding note (page 4); 1.4 no categorical eligibility, 1.7 the SNAP nominal payment (out of scope), 1.8 gross income (page 5); 1.9 countable-income boxes, Social Security with “Excluding MediCare deduction” checked, and the Other note (pages 5-7) | `us-wa/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | In manifest `us-wa-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml` (the Clearinghouse file the branch cites, expression date 2025-10-01). Official copy, for every plan row: [FFY2026 Detailed Model Plan, pages 1, 4-10 and 37](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/state-plans/WA_Plan_2026.pdf#page=1) (52 pages). Check boxes and radio buttons read from renders of pages 5 to 9 and 37. |
| `us-wa/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-2` | 2.1 150% of the HHS poverty guidelines; 2.2 additional requirements answered Yes, none described; 2.3 no assets test, no differing policy for renters, subsidized renters or utilities in rent; priority scheduling (pages 8-9); 2.5 benefit variables (page 9); 2.6 minimum and maximum (page 10) | `us-wa/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | Same manifest. |
| `us-wa/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-17` | 17.3 citizenship and qualified non-citizen verification (page 37) | `us-wa/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | Same manifest. |
| `us-wa/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026-benefit-matrix/worksheet` | Worksheet lines (a) to (d), the $336 example and the adjusters for sizes 1-24 (pages 1-2); the 150% monthly FPL column (page 2); the benefit-percentage table and curve, not used by the branch (pages 3-5) | `us-wa/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026-benefit-matrix` | In manifest `us-wa-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml` (5 pages, expression date 2025-10-01, PDF dated 2025-12-22; not on a Clearinghouse index page). Official copy: [FY2026 benefit matrix, pages 1-5](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/benefits-matricies/WA_BenefitMatrix_2026.pdf#page=1). |
| `us-wa/policies/commerce/weatherization-manual/2026-07/policy-1-1` | Title and date (page 1); Policy 1.1.1 item 1 (page 13); Policy 1.1.2 item 1.a (page 14); items 4.a(1)-(2), 5.a income exclusions and the citizenship item (page 15) | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. [Washington State Weatherization Manual, July 2026, pages 1 and 13-15](https://deptofcommerce.app.box.com/s/5a32797ex8tz2blo8nwtifecokpya37j#page=13) (579 pages; Policy 1.1.2 effective March 2025). A weatherization manual: its LIHEAP cross-reference is the branch's only Commerce text for these deductions. |
| `us-wa/policies/commerce/liheap-eligibility-guidelines/py27` | Items 1-3 (once a program year; heating paid directly or through rent; 150% on average monthly income), the deductions note, annual and monthly limits for sizes 1-12 | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. [Commerce PY27 LIHEAP Eligibility Guidelines](https://deptofcommerce.app.box.com/s/3fp0xz4y2x2p4hedw9ww4sk7ma36srlx) (one page, linked from the [Commerce LIHEAP page](https://www.commerce.wa.gov/community-opportunities/liheap/)). No FY2026 edition was recovered. |
| `us-wa/policies/byrd-barr-place/energy-assistance-application/py2025-2026` | Page 1: 150% limit and monthly maximums for sizes 1-5, the 1, 3 or 12 month assessment, the 20% payroll deduction, utility account or heat in rent; page 2: heat-in-rent documents, citizenship documents, income documents for members 18 and over, the 50% self-employment standard deduction; page 13: self-employed declaration | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. A Seattle subgrantee's form, not a Commerce rule. [Byrd Barr Place Program Year 2025-2026 Energy Assistance Application Packet, pages 1, 2 and 13](https://drive.google.com/file/d/18fvR5CL8UKpTj4Vsm7KlkitKUJclAvkR/view#page=1) (17 pages). |
| `us-wa/policies/kcr/liheap-self-employment-worksheet` | Disallowed IRS deductions and the monthly net-loss floor (pages 1-2) | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest; subgrantee form. [KCR self-employment income worksheet, pages 1-2](https://www.kcr.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/Self-Employment-Form.pdf#page=1). |
| No module (conflict record) | CACLMT income list, including the deduction for child support paid; grant factors | none | Not in a manifest; subgrantee page whose direct request returns a bot challenge (read through a text reader on 2026-10-23). [CACLMT LIHEAP FAQ](https://www.liheapcalendar.com/CACLMT/FAQ). Needed only to record the reading the branch does not follow (interpretation 5). |
| `us-wa/policies/acf/liheap-plan/ffy2027-draft` | Template note (page 1); 1.5 two-year certification, 1.9 boxes (pages 5-6); 2.1 (page 8); 2.6 (page 9) | none | Not in a manifest; needed only if period 2027 is kept in scope. [COMM LIHEAP Model Plan 2027 - Draft 05.04.26, pages 1, 5-6, 8 and 9](https://deptofcommerce.app.box.com/s/5jgeglnyyzvqd0iikydlxiswsnf57pzh#page=1) (49 pages; not accepted). |
| `us/` poverty guidelines module | 2025 guidelines for the 48 contiguous states ($15,650, plus $5,500 for each additional person) behind every FY2026 limit; 2024 (period 2025) and 2026 (period 2027) for the estimates | `us/guidance/hhs/aspe/poverty-guidelines/2025/federal-register` and `.../2024/federal-register`; `.../2026/federal-register` | `us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml` holds 89 FR 2961 and 90 FR 5917; `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml` holds 91 FR 1797. (h) 10,000. | (a) 21,600; (b) 9,600; (c) 5,000; (d) 0; (e) 0; (f) 45,000; (g) 11,600; (h) 10,000 | plan pp. 5-7; Byrd Barr p. 2; KCR p. 1 |
| 12 | Retirement, unemployment and military retirement (`wa_liheap.yaml` Cases 29, 65 and 66; `wa_liheap_countable_income.yaml` Cases 6, 7 and 17) | (a) age 65, pension $10,000 and retirement distributions $2,000; then taxable private pension $10,000 and taxable public pension $2,000. (b) age 40, unemployment $12,000; then size 1 with countable income $10,800 (supplied), ELECTRICITY, cost $400. (c) age 40, `military_retirement_pay` $26,000, ELECTRICITY $1,000. (d) age 70, `military_retirement_pay_survivors` $26,000, NATURAL_GAS $1,000 | 10% retirement and unemployment deductions (Policy 1.1.2 item 5.a; interpretation 3). (a) 12,000 x 0.9 = 10,800. (b) 12,000 x 0.9 = 10,800; 900.00; denominator 2,748.10; quotient 0.532, to 0.53; multiplier 0.77; 400 x 0.77 = 308. (c) 26,000 x 0.9 = 23,400 <= 23,475; 1,950.00; denominator 1,698.10; quotient 0.860, to 0.86; multiplier 0.44; 440. (d) A Survivor Benefit Plan annuity is military retirement income (settled): the same 23,400 and 440. | (a) 10,800 both ways; (b) 10,800, then $308; (c) 23,400, eligible, $440; (d) 23,400, eligible, $440 | Wx manual p. 15; plan p. 6 |
| 13 | Social Security and SSI (`wa_liheap.yaml` Case 67; `wa_liheap_countable_income.yaml` Cases 8, 9 and 23) | (a) age 70, Social Security $24,000, `medicare_part_b_premium` $2,434.80; NATURAL_GAS $1,000. (b) age 65, Social Security $12,000, premium $0 (paid by a Medicare Savings Program). (c) age 40, Social Security disability $12,000, `ssi` $2,400 a year. (d) age 70, pension $30,000, Social Security $1,800, premium $2,434.80 | Social Security counts net of the Part B premium (settled reading of “Excluding MediCare deduction”; interpretation 4); premium 12 x 202.90 = 2,434.80. (a) 24,000 - 2,434.80 = 21,565.20 <= 23,475; 1,797.10; denominator 1,851.00; quotient 0.789, to 0.79; multiplier 0.51; 510. (b) 12,000. (c) 12,000 + 2,400; SSI counts in full, with no retirement deduction. (d) 30,000 x 0.9 = 27,000; Social Security max(1,800 - 2,434.80, 0) = 0, and the excess premium reduces nothing else. | (a) 21,565.20, eligible, $510; (b) 12,000; (c) 14,400; (d) 27,000 | plan p. 6; 90 FR 52063 |
| 14 | TANF and State Family Assistance (`wa_liheap.yaml` Case 64; `wa_liheap_countable_income.yaml` Cases 11 and 21) | parent 40 and child 10, no other income, ELECTRICITY $1,000: (a) TANF not received; (b) TANF received $6,840 a year. Then one adult with TANF $1,200 and State Family Assistance $2,400; then a parent and child with TANF $6,000 | Item 1.9 counts TANF; received cash counts, once per unit. (a) Size 2, income 0: quotient 0.40, multiplier 0.90, 900. (b) $6,840 = 12 x $570, the two-person standard in WAC 388-478-0020; 6,840 / 12 / 1.36 = 419.118, to 419.12; denominator 3,228.98; quotient 0.452, to 0.45; multiplier 0.85; 850. 1,200 + 2,400 = 3,600. $6,000 once, not once per member. | (a) $900; (b) income 6,840, eligible, $850; 3,600; 6,000 | plan p. 6; WAC 388-478-0020 |

No branch test disagrees with these derivations. Tests 5 and 6 depend on interpretations 9 and 10; tests 2, 9 to 14 on interpretations 2 to 8.

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Annual income (simplification).** Byrd Barr assesses 1, 3 or 12 months of income and bases eligibility on the month before the signature date; the PY27 sheet speaks of average monthly income, and the worksheet starts from monthly income. The branch uses annual amounts divided by 12, which equals a 12-month average.
2. **Household and mixed status (convention).** No public Washington LIHEAP household definition or mixed-status rule was located; the Commerce operating manual is behind a staff sign-in. The SPM unit stands in for the household sharing heating costs. Size counts `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`, which approximates the 17.3 documentation test (DACA and TPS holders are not counted); every member's income counts, with no further proration. This matches weatherization Policy 1.1.2 item 4.a, which is not a LIHEAP rule; the code also notes it follows other states' LIHEAP implementations. Infants exempt from verification, documentation refusals and the weatherization opt-out are not modeled.
3. **The 20% and 10% deductions (source reading).** Plan item 1.8 selects gross income and item 1.9 lists no deduction. The branch takes the 20% wage allowance and the 10% retirement and unemployment deductions from weatherization Policy 1.1.2 item 5.a, reading “(1) For 150% FPL” as applying all current exclusions, including (a) to (c), at the LIHEAP threshold, and “except” in item (2) as withholding (a) to (c) only at the higher weatherization thresholds. Byrd Barr takes 20% from earned income taxed at payout; the PY27 sheet names no deduction. The branch applies 20% to all `employment_income` and nothing to net business income. The sources do not say which payments the 10% retirement deduction covers; the branch applies it to `pension_income`, `retirement_distributions` and `military_retirement_income`, not to Social Security, SSI, `railroad_benefits` or `survivor_benefits`, so a civilian survivor benefit counts in full while a military survivor annuity gets 10% (companion tests 12 and 13).
4. **Social Security and the Medicare deduction (settled reading).** Item 1.9 checks “Excluding MediCare deduction” and leaves “Including MediCare deduction” unchecked. The branch reads this as counting Social Security net of the Part B premium: per person, max(max(`social_security`, 0) - `medicare_part_b_premium`, 0), using the premium policyengine-us computes (0 when not enrolled or when a Medicare Savings Program pays it). The label can also be read as excluding the deduction, that is, counting gross Social Security. Only the Part B premium is deducted, and a premium larger than the benefit reduces no other income (companion test 13).
5. **Child support paid (source conflict, settled).** The CACLMT FAQ, a subgrantee page, says support paid “can be deducted”; the plan, the Commerce manual, the PY27 sheet and the Byrd Barr form list no such deduction. The branch follows the plan and manual and deducts nothing (companion test 11(c)). The branch adds no `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml` entry for Washington and no source-conflict marker.
6. **SSI, the state supplement and other assistance (encoded reading).** `ssi` counts in full. The Washington State Supplementary Payment (`wa_ssp`) is not counted because item 1.9 names only SSI; refugee cash assistance (`wa_rca`) has no box and is not counted. `tanf` is TANF received (it follows `takes_up_tanf_if_eligible`) and `wa_sfa` is State Family Assistance; both count once per SPM unit. `general_assistance` stands for other cash aid such as ABD. CACLMT's “TANF or any other Federal or State support” would reach further.
7. **Income items without a matching input (simplification).** Repayable loans, jury duty pay, royalties, structured legal settlements, third-party payments for living expenses and foster care payments are checked but have no dedicated input; commissions and work-study pay count only when reported as `employment_income`. One-time lump sums are unchecked but cannot be separated from `retirement_distributions` or other annual inputs. VA benefits are unchecked, so `veterans_benefits` is not counted. `disability_benefits` and `life_insurance_benefits` are read as insurance payments made directly to the insured (unchecked). Contract income and mortgage or sales-contract payments are unchecked and not counted. Rental and farm rental losses offset nothing (settled).
8. **Self-employment (simplification).** Byrd Barr and KCR take gross receipts less allowable expenses month by month, with no negative month, and Byrd Barr offers a 50% standard deduction without receipts. The branch counts the model's annual net `self_employment_income`, `sstb_self_employment_income`, `farm_operations_income` and `partnership_s_corp_income`, each floored at zero, with no further deduction; monthly loss floors, the KCR list of disallowed IRS deductions and the 50% option are not reproduced.
9. **Worksheet rounding (inferred).** The worksheet prints two-decimal values on lines (a) to (d) and a whole-dollar benefit but states no rounding rule. Full precision gives 400 x (1.30 - 1,460.80 / 3,148.10) = $334.39 for the printed example, not $336, so rounding matters. The branch rounds line (a) to the cent, line (c) to 0.01 and the award to the dollar, each half up, which reproduces $336. The tie cases in companion tests 5 and 6 rest on the half-up choice.
10. **Floor, ceiling and cost cap (convention).** Plan item 2.6 sets $250 and $1,250; the worksheet prints neither, and no source orders them against the heating cost. The branch applies the floor and ceiling and then caps the award at the reported annual cost, so a $100 cost pays $100 (an approved modeling choice). A reading that always pays at least $250 would change the $249.50 and $100 values in companion test 6.
11. **Heating cost and the surrogate cost (gap).** The worksheet multiplies an Annual Heat Cost, and CACLMT bases the grant on 12 months of previous heat usage. The branch uses `heating_expense`, the annual bill for the primary fuel. The worksheet's title names a surrogate heat cost, but no surrogate schedule was recovered: heat in rent with no supplied cost is eligible and pays $0, an unsupported amount rather than ineligibility (companion test 8(c)). Secondary fuels, baseload splits, partial-year residence, self-supplied fuel and Byrd Barr's split between two utilities are not modeled.
12. **Fuel, dwelling type and the heating type input (coverage limit).** Item 2.5 checks fuel type and dwelling type as benefit variables, and CACLMT names housing type, but the worksheet uses neither; the branch's award varies by fuel only through the bill. `heating_type` is a required input: NONE is no heating, and UNSPECIFIED has no bill in `heating_expense` and pays $0 (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the default). `wa_liheap_eligible.yaml` Case 5 is eligible with UNSPECIFIED and heat in rent, and `wa_liheap.yaml` Case 51 pays $336 with UNSPECIFIED only because it supplies `heating_expense` directly. SOLAR reads the electricity bill.
13. **Worksheet constants and vintage (gap).** The worksheet is the FY2026 attachment (PDF dated 2025-12-22), but its 150% monthly column uses the 2024 guidelines ($15,060 x 1.5 / 12 = $1,882.50, printed $1,883). Whether the constants 3,648.10, 1,460.80 and 1.30 were recalibrated for FY2026 is not stated; the branch uses them as printed, with the limit on the 2025 guidelines. The benefit-percentage table on pages 3-5 is not used; a hand check found its rows do not all follow from the worksheet arithmetic on the 2024, 2025 or 2026 guidelines (17% prints 88.00%, while 0.17 x 15,060 / 12 = 213.35 gives a quotient of 0.43 and 87%).
14. **Households over 24 (gap).** The adjuster table stops at 24; larger households keep income eligibility, and the branch pays $0 rather than extrapolate (companion test 4). A line (b) at or below zero also pays $0; at every FY2026 limit line (a) stays under $1,957, so this happens only when eligibility is overridden (`wa_liheap.yaml` Case 54).
15. **Other requirements (not modeled).** Item 2.2 answers Yes to additional eligibility requirements but describes only priority scheduling and targeted intake, which are not modeled. The once-per-program-year limit (PY27 item 1), funding availability, application dates, verification and documents are not modeled. Subsidized housing and assets change nothing (item 2.3; companion test 8).
16. **Exact annual limits (convention).** The branch compares annual income with 1.5 times the annual guideline, unrounded and inclusive. Provider monthly displays round: Byrd Barr's $2,644 for two people is 31,725 / 12 = 2,643.75. A monthly test against the rounded display can differ near the limit by under a dollar a month.
17. **Years and dates (simplification).** All parameters start `2025-10-01`; annual periods read 1 January values, so period 2026 applies FY2026 to the whole calendar year, including October to December 2026, which fall in FY2027. Period 2025 (2024 guidelines) and period 2027 (2026 guidelines) are estimates. The period 2027 limits match the PY27 sheet, but the draft FFY2027 plan (not accepted; it counts combat-related VA benefits, insurance paid to the insured and contract income, drops work study and allows two-year certification for fixed incomes) is not adopted.
18. **Program bundle scope (corpus).** The corpus LIHEAP program bundle excludes both Washington FY2026 documents as back-year tables. Encoding FY2026 needs them admitted, or the release scope limited.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-wa-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-wa-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [us-wa-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-wa-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml)
- [us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml) (2024 and 2025 guidelines; the 2025 ones set every FY2026 limit)
- [us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml) (2026 guidelines, period 2027 estimate)
- [us-cms-annual-notices-2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-cms-annual-notices-2026.yaml) (CY2026 Part B premium, a test input)
- [program-bundles/liheap.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/program-bundles/liheap.yaml) (Washington entries excluded as back-year)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-wa/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the FY2026 150% limits for sizes 0 to 25 and the inclusive ceiling, the qualified-member count with every member's income, the exclusion of earnings under 18, the 20% wage allowance, the 10% retirement (pensions, distributions, military retirement and Survivor Benefit Plan annuities) and unemployment deductions, Social Security net of the Part B premium, SSI, TANF and State Family Assistance once per unit, every checked and unchecked income box that has an input, per-source loss floors, worksheet lines (a) to (d) with all 24 adjusters and the intermediate rounding, the $250 floor, $1,250 ceiling and final cost cap, heat in rent with and without a cost, subsidized housing, every heating type including none and unspecified, sizes over 24, and any 2025 or 2027 period kept in scope. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: [pe-parity] Encode Wis. Stat. 71.52(4)-(6) homestead household income: claimant and spouse only, $500 per dependent (PE-US #10191)

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Encoding debt

rulespec-us has no Wisconsin homestead credit module. `us-wi/` holds only `policies/income_tax/2026_form1es_estimated_schedule.yaml` and `policies/income_tax/2026_full_year_resident_core.yaml`, and neither encodes Wis. Stat. 71.52–71.55. So nothing encodes the rule PolicyEngine-US got wrong: homestead household income counts only the claimant's and spouse's income, never a dependent's, and a dependent instead brings a $500 deduction.

PolicyEngine-US made three mistakes, fixed in PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10191:
- **Dependents' tax-exempt amounts.** `wi_homestead_income` summed the person-level tax-exempt income items, SSI and 2020 excluded unemployment compensation over every tax unit member, dependents included.
- **Dependents' Social Security.** It took Social Security from `tax_exempt_social_security`, a tax-unit amount that includes dependents' benefits.
- **Earned income test.** `wi_homestead_eligible` counted a dependent's earnings toward the earned income test.

## Statute (verbatim, pinned corpus)

The pinned release `us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap` includes the whole-section row `us-wi/statute/71.52`, from lock `.axiom/corpus-locks/us-wi/statute/2026-07-16-pit-west-chapter-71.json` (`source_as_of` 2026-04-03). It reads:

> (4) "Household" means a claimant and an individual related to the claimant as husband or wife.
>
> (5) "Household income" means all income received by all persons of a household in a calendar year while members of the household, less $500 for each of the claimant's dependents, as defined in section 152 of the internal revenue code, who have the same principal abode as the claimant for more than 6 months during the year to which the claim relates.
>
> (6) "Income" means the sum of Wisconsin adjusted gross income and the following amounts, to the extent not included in Wisconsin adjusted gross income: maintenance payments …, support money, cash public assistance …, the gross amount of any pension or annuity (including railroad retirement benefits, all payments received under the federal social security act and veterans disability pensions), nontaxable interest received from the federal government or any of its instrumentalities, …

The 2026-09-23 lock `.axiom/corpus-locks/us-wi/statute/2026-09-23-income-tax-subunits-chapter-71.json` also has subsection rows `us-wi/statute/71.52/4`, `/5` and `/6` (`source_as_of` 2026-09-04), but these are on `main` only and not in the pinned release.

The ground truth for the companion tests is outside the corpus: the 2024 Schedule H instructions (https://www.revenue.wi.gov/TaxForms2024/2024-ScheduleH-inst.pdf).
- File page 8: "A household is a claimant and the claimant's spouse living in the claimant's homestead."
- File page 13: "do not include your children's social security or SSI benefits, whether paid to them directly or to you on their behalf."
- File page 10: "Only one spouse must have earned income to qualify for the homestead credit. The spouse that meets this definition must be the claimant."

Wis. Admin. Code Tax 14.03(5)(a)6 (https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/code/admin_code/tax/14.pdf) excludes "Social security or SSI payments received on behalf of a claimant's children". I did not find the Schedule H instructions in any us-wi form lock whose rows are readable, so that is a corpus gap: the 2026-09-15 and 2026-10-06 form locks carry no `git_blob`.

## Why this is not a PR

Content must come from the signed encoder (`axiom-encode encode` with `--apply`, or `targeted-signed-reencode.yml`); hand-written RuleSpec fails the generated-guard. A signed run is OpenAI-billed and needs Max's approval, which a PolicyEngine session cannot give itself, so this is queued for the Axiom eng hub's next dispatch wave.

## Dispatch

Encode corpus citation `us-wi/statute/71.52` at `us-wi/statutes/71.52.yaml`. Paste this as `review_finding`:

> Encode Wis. Stat. 71.52(4)-(6) (corpus us-wi/statute/71.52) at us-wi/statutes/71.52.yaml: the homestead credit household and household income.
>
> Outputs:
> - `homestead_household_member` (Person, bool, Year): true for the claimant and for the claimant's spouse living in the claimant's homestead. False for everyone else, including the claimant's dependents.
> - `homestead_income_of_person` (Person, Money, Year): the person's income under (6). That is the person's Wisconsin adjusted gross income plus the listed amounts to the extent not in it, including the gross amount of any pension or annuity, all payments received under the federal Social Security Act, nontaxable interest, support money and cash public assistance. Leaf inputs per item.
> - `homestead_household_income` (TaxUnit, Money, Year): the sum of `homestead_income_of_person` over persons where `homestead_household_member` is true, less $500 × the number of the claimant's section 152 dependents who share the claimant's principal abode for more than 6 months.
>
> A dependent's own income, such as Social Security, SSI, unemployment compensation or wages, never enters household income. The dependent instead brings the $500 deduction.
>
> Proof excerpts:
> - "a claimant and an individual related to the claimant as husband or wife"
> - "all income received by all persons of a household"
> - "less $500 for each of the claimant's dependents"
>
> Companion tests are TY2024, from the 2024 Schedule H instructions, file pages 8, 10 and 13.

Companion tests are the same cases as the PolicyEngine-US YAML tests in #10191: `wi_homestead_income.yaml` Cases 6–7 and `wi_homestead_credit.yaml` Case 5.

- **A. A grandchild's survivor benefits are left out (TY2024).**
  - Claimant aged 70: Social Security 18,000; taxable pension 6,000. None of the Social Security is taxable, so Wisconsin AGI is 6,000.
  - Dependent grandchild aged 17, same abode all year: survivor benefits 12,000.
  - Expected: `homestead_household_income` = 6,000 + 18,000 − 500 = 23,500. The grandchild's 12,000 is excluded.
- **B. A child's SSI and excluded unemployment compensation are left out (TY2020).**
  - Claimant aged 66: Social Security 15,000; pension 5,000.
  - Dependent child: unemployment compensation 8,000 (excluded on the child's own federal return under IRC 85(c)); SSI 3,000.
  - Expected: 5,000 + 15,000 − 500 = 19,500.
- **C. No dependents.** Claimant aged 70 with Social Security 18,000 and pension 6,000: 24,000.

If the encoder also takes the 71.53 eligibility rule, add this test:

- **D. A dependent's wages do not meet the earned income test (TY2024).**
  - Claimant aged 40: unemployment compensation 6,000 and no earnings.
  - Dependent child aged 17: wages 4,000.
  - Expected: not eligible. Unemployment compensation is not earned income (Schedule H instructions, file page 7), and the dependent's wages do not count.

## Oracle

PolicyEngine-US after #10191:
- `wi_homestead_income`: household income, less $500 per dependent;
- `wi_homestead_eligible`;
- `wi_homestead_credit`;
- `filer_tax_exempt_social_security`.

PolicyEngine starts from federal AGI rather than Wisconsin AGI, so compare only the cases above, where the two are equal.

items.body:
## Objective

Ship New Jersey LIHEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1b, covering the agreed scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with signed RuleSpec encodings and reproducible oracle validation.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9745 (branch `nj-liheap`), open and under review, not yet merged. Scope, policy period, module paths, source text, required outputs and companion tests are in the sections below. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## PolicyEngine implementation (historical snapshot)

- **PR history:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9745; recorded head `ee00db7d60` (2026-10-07), following `f4d535357b`. Its five-band FY2027 grid, FY2022 in-effect gate, rounding and source conflicts are described in the outputs, interpretations and tests below. This is a historical reference; pin the final reviewed revision for oracle validation. October 20 and 23 requirements are incorporated below.
- **Scope:** the regular heating benefit of New Jersey's Home Energy Assistance program (LIHEAP) for FFY2026 and FFY2027: residency and household rules, heating responsibility or heat included in rent, the subsidized-housing and dependent-student exclusions, the 60% of State Median Income monthly income test, countable income net of the Medicare Part B premium, the county, fuel, income and household-size benefit grid including its Renters panel, and the renter level for subsidized tenants who pay their own heating bill. Out of scope: medically necessary cooling ($300), emergency energy assistance, supplemental heating emergency benefits, furnace repair and restart, the Universal Service Fund, Lifeline, weatherization, and payment mechanics (direct utility transfers, two-party checks).
- **Policy periods:** two seasons. Federal fiscal year 2026 (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30; applications 2025-10-01 to 2026-06-30) is read at model period `2026` and FFY2027 (applications 2026-10-01 to 2027-06-30) at `2027`; every formula is undated and every variable annual. The FY2027 handbook, matrix, fact sheet and plan state the same rules, panels and cells as FY2026 except one renters cell, which carries `2026-10-01: 474`; every other grid value is dated `2025-10-01` only, and the FY2027 limits follow from the FFY2027 state median income through the limit formula. The registry records `verified_years: "2026-2027"`. The 60% SMI test has applied since FY2022 (BPU, 2021-10-19): `eligibility/in_effect` is `false` before `2021-10-01` and `true` from it, `smi_rate` is dated `2021-10-01`, so periods before 2022 pay nothing (test 28) and 2022 to 2025 are unverified estimates.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/nj/dca/liheap/`: `nj_liheap`; `eligibility/nj_liheap_eligible`, `nj_liheap_household_size`, `nj_liheap_income_limit`; `income/nj_liheap_countable_income`, `nj_liheap_countable_income_person`; `payment/nj_liheap_income_band`, `nj_liheap_region`. No new input variable.

Handbook quotations are from the FY2026 LIHEAP Handbook (running title "Home Energy Assistance Program’s Guideline"); page numbers are PDF pages. Regulation quotations are from the Cornell LII copy of N.J.A.C. 5:49. Local copies are in `liheap-sources/wave1b/NJ/sources/`.

**Residency, household and strikers.** Handbook 2.2 (page 5): "The household members shall be residents of New Jersey." "1. The term "household" means any individual or group of individuals who are living together as one economic unit for whom home energy is customarily provided in common or who make undesignated payments for energy in the form of rent." "3. Strikers and households that include striking members are ineligible for Home Energy Assistance benefits, in accordance with N.J.A.C. 10:90 2.8(c)." Handbook 2.3.F.3 (page 10): "For the purpose of this program, the household shall consist of all persons residing within a single residential unit." 2.3.F.4: "Tax dependent college students who are absent from the household solely because of college attendance must be included in the household size for the determination of eligibility." 2.3.F.6: "Roomer-boarders residing with an applicant household are not to be included in the household size, and the income of such individuals is not to be considered in the eligibility determination. However, any income provided to the HEA applicant household by the roomer-boarder in excess of $250.00 per month shall be considered in determining the household's gross monthly income."

**Nonqualified members.** Handbook 2.2.4 (page 6): "In most cases, non-qualified citizens are not eligible for Home Energy Assistance benefits. Qualified citizens defined in Section 431 of the Federal Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act (PRWORA) of 1996, P.L. 104-193, if otherwise eligible, may receive LIHEAP benefits (see N.J.A.C. 10:90-2.10 and 10.3)." 2.2.4.a: "Qualified citizens are defined as legal immigrants, including but not limited to legal permanent residents, refugees, asylees, individuals paroled into the United States for a period of at least one year, individuals whose deportation has been withheld, individuals granted conditional entry, and certain individuals who are victims of domestic abuse." 2.2.5: "In cases where a non-qualified citizen resides within an applicant household, the non-qualified citizen must be excluded from the HEA household size. If the non-qualified citizens have a monthly income of more than $500.00, the amount in excess of $500.00 shall be counted as income to the household and must be added to all other household income in determining the household's gross monthly income." N.J.A.C. 5:49-2.2(a)5: "In cases where a non-qualified alien resides within an applicant household, the non-qualified alien must be excluded from the HEA household size. ## Interpretations and gaps

Each item is marked as an interpretation the draft makes, an inference from published figures, a convention, or a gap it leaves.

- **Codified rule against handbook, three conflicts (interpretation; owner decision pending).** (1) Income ceiling: N.J.A.C. 5:49-2.3(a) sets 175% of the Federal Poverty Index capped at 60% SMI; handbook 2.3.A, plan 2.1 and the fact sheet use 60% SMI alone (175% of the 2025 guideline for one person is $27,387.50 a year against the published $50,005). (2) Disregard: 5:49-2.2(a)5 says $268 a month; handbook 2.2.5 says $500 (a nonqualified earner at $1,000 a month counts $732 under the rule and $500 under the handbook). (3) Subsidized tenant with a heating bill in their name: 5:49-2.2(d)1.i pays "a renter's benefit level"; handbook 3.2.F.1 pays by fuel and does not repeat that exception (a 1 to 4 person electric household in the 19 counties, top row, is paid $234 on Renters where the handbook's fuel rule would pay $529 on Electric). The readoption notice keeps the chapter in force without change from September 22, 2025 and does not reconcile them. The model follows the handbook on (1) and (2) and, since the owner's call of 2026-10-06, the regulation on (3) (test 18): the handbook copies (d)1 without subparagraph (i) and prints no contrary rule. Public housing with its own bill (eligible under 2.3(b)1) is read with the rent subsidy because 2.2(d)1 treats the two as one class, although (d)1.i names only the subsidy. The codified text was read from the Cornell LII copy only.
- **Categorical eligibility (interpretation; owner decision pending).** Plan 1.4a calls a household with a TANF, SNAP or PAAD member "categorically eligible"; handbook 3.1.a.2 requires automatic SNAP cases to have "a current monthly income that is less than or equal to the program’s standards" and handbook 2.2 makes households over the standard ineligible "including any TANF, GA or SSI grants". The draft applies the income test to every household (test 10). A SNAP household over 60% SMI is ineligible in the draft and would be eligible under a literal reading of the plan.
- **Pre-FY2022 standard (gated 2026-10-07).** The BPU announcement of 2021-10-19 names a move from 200% FPL to 60% SMI, but its $4,039 monthly figure for four reproduces at 185% of the 2020 poverty guideline ($26,200 x 1.85 / 12 = 4,039), not 200% ($4,367), so no pre-FY2022 rule is encoded. Instead `eligibility/in_effect` is `false` before 2021-10-01 (an explicit early value, since the model backdates the earliest entry) and `true` from it, `nj_liheap_eligible` requires it (test 28), and `smi_rate` is dated 2021-10-01.
- **FY2027 plan 1.9 (conflict; the handbook controls).** The FY2027 plan (page 6) leaves Strike Pay, General Assistance and TANF unchecked where the FY2026 plan checks all three. Handbook 2.2 (page 6) counts TANF and GA grants toward the standard and 2.2.3 makes striker households ineligible, so the model counts all three; noted in `unearned.yaml`, at the `tanf` add in `nj_liheap_countable_income` and in the PR conflict table.
- **Grid income unit (inference).** The grid does not say whether its rows are monthly or annual. Monthly is inferred because the income test is monthly and because the three upper breakpoints equal the FFY2022 monthly 60% SMI limits for sizes 4, 8 and 12 computed with the limit formula above from the FFY2022 New Jersey SMI of $128,786: floor(0.6 x 128,786) = 77,271, and sizes 4, 8 and 12 give $6,439, $8,886 and $9,659. The breakpoints are fixed dollars not updated for FFY2026, so a 1 to 4 person household cannot reach the two lowest rows (the size 4 limit, $8,014, is below $8,887).
- **The $961 cell (kept as printed).** Deliverables, Warren & Sussex, "1 to 4", top three rows, prints 961 three times; the lower rows (613, 491, 366) and the grid's own ratios imply about 735. The FY2027 grid image prints 961 too. The draft stores 961 (test 1 depends on it). Two smaller irregularities are also kept as printed: Electric, Warren & Sussex, "5 to 8", top rows, 821; Gas, Warren & Sussex, "13 or More", "$8887 - $9659", 445.
- **Two rows stored as one band (interpretation).** The rows "$0 - $1000" and "$1001 - $2000" print identical amounts in every column of both years and are combined; since 2026-10-07 the "$2001 - $6439" row is its own band, so `income_band` has five bands (0, 2,001, 6,440, 8,887, 9,660) over 160 cells and the FY2027 Renters, Warren & Sussex, "13 or More" cell carries 474 from 2026-10-01 (test 23). An Axiom encoding may key all six printed rows; every value agrees.
- **Unknown county (coverage limit).** `county: UNKNOWN` or an out-of-state county gives region 0 and a $0 payment while `nj_liheap_eligible` stays true (test 12, part 4); the grid has no column to read, and no source denies the benefit. With no county input the model falls back to the first county in the state, Atlantic County, region 1, so the default path is paid (test 21). `region_1` lists the 19 counties as the complement of the printed "Warren & Sussex Counties".
- **Unspecified fuel (coverage limit).** `heating_type` is a required input. A direct payer with UNSPECIFIED, OTHER or NONE receives $0 (test 7); since 2026-10-06 SOLAR reads the Electric panel, the pairing `heating_expense` uses. Only the Renters panel, reached through `heat_expense_included_in_rent` or the subsidized direct-payer rule, pays without a fuel (tests 2 and 18). Datasets carry no heating inputs, so population totals are $0 until the default changes (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us issue 9754).
- **Out-of-state table lookup (defect found in review, fixed at head `1c87f6ae57`).** `nj_liheap_income_band` is defined for New Jersey only, so units in other states carry band 0, which is not a grid key; at head `3b7e373` the grid lookup raised in a simulation holding one eligible New Jersey unit and one unit elsewhere. The fix floors the band at 1 before the lookup, as region and size already were, and test 5 covers the mixed-state case. No New Jersey result changes.
- **Household, period and business income (interpretation).** The SPM unit stands in for "all persons residing within a single residential unit"; the handbook's apartment, boarding-home and roomer-boarder splits need correct SPM membership. Calendar year 2026 stands in for the FFY2026 season, and annual inputs divided by 12 stand in for the four-week income verification window. Self-employment, SSTB and farm income are the model's net inputs with no further deduction, each floored at zero (handbook 2.3.C.1 nets business expenses but says nothing about a loss); since 2026-10-06 every unearned source is floored the same way per person (tests 22 and 24), under plan 1.8 (gross income) and handbook 2.3.D (receipts from rental property).
- **Survivor benefits (interpretation).** Handbook 2.3.D (page 8) counts "benefits and pensions, annuities", so survivor pensions and annuities count. 2.3.E.10 (page 9): "Veteran’s benefits shall also be excluded from the household income, provided the proof of veterans’ benefits is provided." The model's `survivor_benefits` is one amount across every non-Social-Security survivor source, VA survivor payments included, so that slice cannot be excluded; the whole amount counts, over-counting households with VA survivor income relative to the handbook. Added 2026-10-03 at head `0f47f9cd32`.
- **Not modeled (gaps).** The Medicare Part D premium (no variable; the Part B premium is deducted since 2026-10-06, tests 15 and 27); the Tenants Lifeline supplement inside SSI (2.3.F.7(b); the SSI variable carries no supplement, so there is nothing to remove); the utility-allowance detail of a rent subsidy (every subsidized direct payer gets the renter level); strikers; residents of medical facilities, community residences and treatment centers; heating costs paid by non-members; a separate fuel charge paid to the landlord (indistinguishable from a vendor bill); roomer-boarders and the $250 rule; foster-care allowances, contract income, commissions, legal settlements, cash gifts, lump sums and VISTA stipends (no input); the PAAD screen for automatic payments.
- **FY2027 (encoded 2026-10-06).** The FY2027 handbook, plan, fact sheet and grid are in scope: 60% SMI, the $500 disregard, the $118 minimum and the $1,278 maximum are unchanged, the heating dates move to 2026-10-01 to 2027-06-30, the limits rise with the FFY2027 state median income (test 9) and the grid differs from FY2026 in the one cell named above, which the model stores from 2026-10-01 (test 23); nothing else changes in FY2027.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [FY2026 state-plan manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-nj-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [FY2026 handbook manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-nj-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml)
- [FY2026 benefit-grid manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-nj-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml)

These FY2026 manifests are discovery starting points; the FY2027 handbook, grid, fact sheet and plan and the N.J.A.C. 5:49 text have no manifest and need ingest. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-nj/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover all distinct payment-grid combinations, the FY2026 and FY2027 published income limits and rounding, mixed-status member income, the Medicare Part B deduction, heat-in-rent and the renter level for subsidized direct payers, unknown county/fuel, and TANF receipt/take-up. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: Encode 7 CFR 273.9(b)–(c) income itemization: SNAP takes total unearned income as one input slot today

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## What is missing

The federal SNAP composition (`us/policies/usda/snap/state-plan-composition.yaml`) defines countable unearned income as `max(0, snap_total_monthly_unearned_income)`, and `snap_total_monthly_unearned_income` is a single input slot (`us:regulations/7-cfr/273/10#input.snap_total_monthly_unearned_income` in the tests). The itemization in 7 CFR 273.9(b)(1)–(2) (earned income; unearned income including assistance payments such as SSI and TANF, general assistance, annuities and pensions, Social Security, unemployment compensation, workers' compensation, child support, alimony) and the exclusions in 273.9(c) are not encoded. `us/regulations/7-cfr/273/9.yaml` exists at section granularity only.

## Why it matters

- A program certificate for SNAP must declare its boundary facts per source. With one aggregate slot the certificate cannot say which amounts it takes from other programs' administration (SSI including a state's optional supplement, TANF cash, unemployment compensation, Social Security) and which it excludes.
- A composed certificate (SNAP computed together with TANF, SSI and UI) binds those slots to the other modules' outputs through composition bridge rules. That binding needs one slot per source.
- 7 CFR 273.9(b)(2)(i) counts assistance payments from federal or federally aided public assistance programs and other need-based assistance, so a state's optional SSI supplement counts; the aggregate slot hides that.

## Ask

Encode 7 CFR 273.9(b) and (c) with the supervised encoder (`axiom-encode encode <corpus citation> --backend codex --apply`; no hand-authored YAML), one input slot per income source named in the regulation, and rewire the composition's `snap_countable_earned_income` / `snap_countable_unearned_income` to the itemized rules. Companion tests per source and exclusion.

Context: the cross-program dependency matrix in the private plan graph (program-dependencies.json) records SNAP → SSI/TANF/UI as counted income; this issue is the encoding side of that boundary.

items.title: LIHEAP wave 1c: encode Virginia EAP regular Fuel Assistance

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Virginia Energy Assistance Program (EAP) Fuel Assistance, the regular LIHEAP heating benefit, in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1c, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10303 (branch `va-liheap-wave1c`), open and ready for review, not merged. Head `ae989becf3` (2026-10-23) adds the review fixes (commit `9f0caea3ca`) and merges `main` (`6a92d6a983`); this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **Sources missing from the corpus.** No axiom-corpus manifest on `main` holds 22VAC40-680, the Virginia Energy Assistance Program regulation (sections 10, 20 and 30 define the terms, the eligibility criteria and the point method). Also missing: the FY2024 and FY2025 Virginia plans (item 2.5 values per point for FFY2023 and FFY2024, needed only for periods before 2025), the EAP Information Sheet 032-03-0661-26 (05/25) and the Fuel Assistance Application (living arrangement codes, the Medicare Part B or D question and the fuel list). The manual, the FY2026 plan, the FY2026 benefit matrix and the 2024 and 2025 HHS poverty guidelines are captured.
- **Bundle scope.** The LIHEAP program bundle on corpus `main` (`manifests/program-bundles/liheap.yaml`, as of 2026-10-06, fiscal year 2027) marks the Virginia FY2026 plan and the FY2026 benefit matrix as excluded (“Back-year table: not current law”); only the manual is in scope. The benefit matrix carries the 05/21 Appendix B page (150% basis) that the manual compilation lacks. An FY2026 release needs that scope reconciled. No FY2027 Virginia plan or benefit matrix is posted (both Clearinghouse URLs returned 404 on 2026-10-23).
- **Unpublished point values.** VDSS does not publish the primary fuel points, the vendor-survey average fuel costs behind the energy burden, or the FFY2026 value per point. The branch uses PolicyEngine placeholders and the FFY2025 value (interpretations 1 and 2).
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-23; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.
- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. DTrim99 requested changes on 2026-10-21 at `1396baf7fe`; head `ae989becf3` has not been re-reviewed, so there is no revision to pin.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10303, branch `va-liheap-wave1c`, head `ae989becf3`, which closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10291. Commit `9f0caea3ca` deducts each member's out-of-pocket Medicare Part B premium from household gross income (exemption 15), floors every unearned source per person and source, counts the Auxiliary Grant (`va_ag`), adds the plan item 2.5 benefit range to the placeholder files, points 22VAC40-680 references at section pages and adds five test cases. Oracle fixtures will pin the merged commit.
- **Scope:** Fuel Assistance, the once-a-season regular heating benefit, for FFY2026: Virginia residence, household size counting citizens and qualified aliens, gross countable income of all members with per-source loss floors, the exemption 15 Medicare Part B deduction and the $50 elderly or disabled deduction, the 150% income limit with the all-SSI exception, eligible fuels and the heating-expense and housing rules, the Appendix B point tables (size, income, climate zone, vulnerability, living arrangement), two placeholder point values (primary fuel, energy burden) and points times the value per point. Out of scope: Crisis Assistance, Cooling Assistance, weatherization, equipment repair or purchase and security deposits.
- **Policy periods:** one verified season, FFY2026 (October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026; plan page 1 “Report Period: 10/01/2025 to 09/30/2026”). Variables are annual and read 1 January values, so period `2026` is FFY2026 on the 2025 guidelines (`fpg_year_lag` 1, matrix page 1). `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2026"`. Earlier periods use parameter backfilling and are unverified estimates (interpretation 12).
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/va/dss/eap/` (11, no new input): `va_eap`, `va_eap_climate_zone`, `va_eap_countable_income`, `va_eap_disabled` (person), `va_eap_eligible`, `va_eap_household_size`, `va_eap_income_eligible`, `va_eap_income_limit`, `va_eap_income_points`, `va_eap_points`, `va_eap_vulnerability_points`.
- **Parameters:** 26 files under `gov.states.va.dss.eap`: `age/elderly` (60); `benefit/value_per_point` ($4.226444 from 2022-10-01, $4.957075 from 2023-10-01, $4.531665 from 2024-10-01); `climate_zone/` six locality lists (133 localities, 2017-06-01); `eligibility/` `fpg_rate` (1.5), `fpg_year_lag` (1), `heating_types` (7 fuels), `max_table_size` (20); `income/` `child_earnings_age_limit` (18), `medical_disregard` ($50 a month), `sources/earned` (5 sources), `sources/unearned` (21); `points/` `climate_zone` (by zone), `household_size` and `income` (single-amount scales on band starts), `living_arrangement` (20), `primary_fuel` (10, placeholder), `energy_burden` (13, placeholder), `vulnerability/` `elderly` (20), `disabled` (15), `child` (12), `child_age_limit` (6). Plus a `programs.yaml` entry and a changelog fragment.
- **Tests:** 129 YAML cases in 12 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/va/dss/eap/`: `integration.yaml` 7, `va_eap.yaml` 10, `va_eap_climate_zone.yaml` 10, `va_eap_countable_income.yaml` 22, `va_eap_disabled.yaml` 10, `va_eap_eligible.yaml` 23, `va_eap_household_size.yaml` 6, `va_eap_income_eligible.yaml` 9, `va_eap_income_limit.yaml` 6, `va_eap_income_points.yaml` 7, `va_eap_points.yaml` 7, `va_eap_vulnerability_points.yaml` 12. Every payment case sends `heating_type`. All 129 pass locally at this head.

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence on axiom-corpus `main` (`5117fb3fad`, 2026-10-23) was checked on 2026-10-23 against the full manifest tree and by GitHub code search for each missing source's URL or file name; the signed release was not checked. rulespec-us `main` (`829d85e9c8`, 2026-10-23) has `us-va/policies/` (`cms`, `income_tax`) and `us-va/statutes/`, but no `us-va/regulations/`, no LIHEAP module in any jurisdiction and no `us/` poverty-guideline module. The paths below follow the `us-ak/regulations/aac/title-7/chapter-45/...` and `us-<st>/policies/<agency>/<document>/...` layouts. Pages are physical PDF pages. The manual's page bodies number Non Public Assistance Households as Chapter C section 4 (page 36) and Citizenship and Alien Status as section 5 (page 41); the manual's index and the branch label the income provisions C.5.a, and this issue follows the branch labels with page locators.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
