Official copy: [22VAC40-680-10](https://law.lis.virginia.gov/admincode/title22/agency40/chapter680/section10/) (last amended effective December 20, 2000). Corpus layout as in `us-va-tanf-ccdf-w6-regulation.yaml`: `us-va/regulation/title-22/agency-40/chapter-680/section-10`. |
| `.../chapter-680/680-20-eligibility-criteria` | 20(A) purpose; 20(B)(1) income at or below the limits; 20(B)(2) qualified alien status; 20(B)(3) ineligible households | none | Same. [22VAC40-680-20](https://law.lis.virginia.gov/admincode/title22/agency40/chapter680/section20/) (last amended effective February 26, 2003). |
| `.../chapter-680/680-30-benefits` | Benefit levels, the six climate zones, the point factors, the value per point and the benefit amount | none | Same. [22VAC40-680-30](https://law.lis.virginia.gov/admincode/title22/agency40/chapter680/section30/) (last amended effective December 10, 1997). |

Official copy, for every manual row: [Energy Assistance Manual, Volume IX, pages 25-32, 35-41, 50, 52-53 and 62-66](https://www.dss.virginia.gov/media/vdss/benefit-programs/documents/eap/Complete_Manual.pdf#page=25). |
| `.../chapter-b/income` | B.6 gross income (page 28); B.6.a FFY2026 limits, 05/25 (page 28); B.6.b exemptions 1 to 27 (pages 28-31); B.6.c $50 deduction (page 31) | same | Same file. |
| `.../chapter-b/citizenship-and-other-criteria` | B.7 citizenship and qualified alien statuses (pages 31-32); B.8.a residence and B.8.c Social Security number (page 32) | same | Same file. |
| `.../chapter-c/income-verification` | C.1.a applicant's statement, including the Medicare premium (page 35); C.2.c Medicare premium deducted (page 36); C.5.a.1 rounding, conversion and the prior calendar month (page 37); C.5.a.3 countable income (page 38); C.5.a.4.b self-employment profit, including rental property (pages 38-40); C.5.a.4.c unearned income (page 40); section 5.a income of undeclared members counted (page 41) | same | Same file. |
| `.../chapter-d/benefit-determination` | D.1.a-c primary heat system, primary fuel type, heating expense (page 50); D.4 screening and the medical deduction (page 52); D.5 benefit factors and points (pages 52-53) | same | Same file. |

Official copy: [FY2026 Detailed Model Plan, pages 1, 5-6 and 8-9](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/state-plans/VA_Plan_2026.pdf#page=1). [FY2024 plan, page 9](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2024/state-plans/VA_Plan_2024.pdf#page=9); [FY2025 plan, page 9](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2025/state-plans/VA_Plan_2025.pdf#page=9). |

[Information Sheet 032-03-0661-26 (05/25)](https://www.dss.virginia.gov/media/vdss/benefit-programs/documents/eap/032-03-00661-26_EAP_Information_Sheet_eng.pdf) (1 page). |

[Fuel Assistance Application, pages 1-2](https://www.dss.virginia.gov/media/vdss/benefit-programs/documents/403-errors/FUEL-ASSISTANCE-APPLICATION.pdf#page=1). |
| `us/` poverty guidelines module | 2025 guidelines for the 48 contiguous states ($15,650 for one person, $5,500 for each additional person) behind every FFY2026 limit; 2024 guidelines ($15,060, $5,380) for the period 2025 estimate | `us/guidance/hhs/aspe/poverty-guidelines/2025/federal-register` and `.../2024/federal-register` | In manifest `us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml` (90 FR 5917 and 89 FR 2961). |

Companion tests take `medicare_part_b_premium`, `ssi`, `tanf` and `va_ag` as inputs, so no Medicare, SSI, TANF or Auxiliary Grant module is needed. TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us#1787 covers the Auxiliary Grant itself.

## Source text (verbatim)

Quotations come from the official files above (pdftotext -layout, line breaks collapsed). The benefit matrix is a scan; its quotations were read from renders. Plan check-box and radio states come from renders of plan pages 5, 6, 8 and 9.

**22VAC40-680-10.** “"Disabled person" means a person receiving Social Security disability, Railroad Retirement disability, 100% Veterans Administration disability, Supplemental Security Income as disabled, or an individual who has been certified as permanently and totally disabled for Medicaid purposes.” “"Elderly person" means anyone who is 60 years of age or older.” “"Energy burden" means the average fuel cost for the primary fuel type used by a household divided by the income of the household.” “"Household" means an individual or group of individuals who occupies a housing unit and functions as an economic unit by purchasing residential energy in common (share heat), or making undesignated payments for energy in the form of rent (heat is included in the rent).” “"Poverty guidelines" means the Poverty Income Guidelines as established and published annually by the Department of Health and Human Services.” “"Primary fuel" means the fuel used to operate the primary heating system currently used to heat the majority of the house.” “"Vulnerability factor" means an individual is a child under the age of six or meets the definition of an elderly or disabled person.”

**22VAC40-680-20.** “A. The purpose of the fuel assistance component is to provide heating assistance to eligible households to offset the costs of home heating energy that are excessive in relation to household income. B. Eligibility criteria are set out in this subsection. 1. Income limits. Maximum income limits shall not exceed the maximum allowed by federal law. In order to be eligible for fuel assistance, a household's income must be at or below the maximum income limits. 2. Alien status. An alien who meets a qualified status as defined by the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 (PRWORA), P.L. 104-193, regardless of when he entered the United States, is eligible to receive assistance and services under the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) if he meets other program requirements. 3. Ineligible households. The households that are ineligible to receive fuel assistance are: a. Subsidized households whose total heating costs are included in their rent. b. Persons living in institutions. c. Persons living in temporary shelters or group homes who have no heating expense or who pay a nominal fee to live there. d. Persons who reside in only one room within a larger dwelling. e. Subsidized households who are responsible for payment of individual excess fuel usage charges even though heating expenses are included in their rent.”

**22VAC40-680-30.** “Benefit levels shall be established based on income in relation to household size, fuel type, and geographic area, with the highest benefit given to households with the least income and the highest energy need. Geographic areas are the six climate zones for Virginia recognized by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the United States Department of Commerce. The six climate zones are: Northern, Tidewater, Central Mountain, Southwestern Mountain, Eastern Piedmont, and Western Piedmont. Each year the benefit amounts for each household shall be determined by state computer using the following method: 1. The following factors for each household will be assigned a point value: a. Gross monthly income; b. Living arrangements; c. Primary heat type; d. Climate zone; e. Vulnerability: (1) Person 60 years of age or older; (2) Disabled person in household; (3) Child under six; and f. Energy burden. Point values will be determined by department staff in accordance with guidelines established by the State Board of Social Services. 2. The total points of all households will be determined. 3. The available benefit dollars will be divided by the point total to determine a point dollar value. 4. The household's benefit amount will be calculated by multiplying the household's point total by the value per point.”

No branch test disagrees with these derivations. Every payment total depends on interpretations 1 and 2.

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Primary fuel and energy burden points (placeholders).** Appendix B sets the fuel points each year from a vendor price survey and the Virginia Tech study (the highest-cost fuel gets 20) and scores the burden, the survey's average fuel cost divided by household income, from 0 to 25. VDSS publishes neither the survey results nor the points. The branch gives every eligible household 10 fuel points and 13 burden points (the 50% to 69% band). Plan item 2.5 prints the FFY2025 range, $181.26 to $634.43, which equals 40 and 140 points at $4.531665 (40 x 4.531665 = 181.2666, printed truncated; 140 x 4.531665 = 634.4331). The five published factors sum to between 37 points (9 + 0 + 8 + 0 + 20) and 100 points (15 + 25 + 20 + 20 + 20), so in FFY2025 the fuel and burden points totaled at most 3 for the lowest benefit and at least 40 for the highest. With the placeholders, the model ranges from 60 points ($271.90, an all-SSI household over the limit in Tidewater with no vulnerable member) to 123 points ($557.39). 22VAC40-680-30 bases benefit levels on “income in relation to household size, fuel type, and geographic area, with the highest benefit given to households with the least income and the highest energy need”; the placeholders remove the fuel and burden variation. Encode both values as named inputs or placeholders with the Appendix B method recorded; companion tests supply 10 and 13.
2. **Value per point (latest published).** VDSS computes the value in December and reports it in the next year's plan. The FFY2026 value is unpublished, and no FY2027 plan is posted. The branch carries the FFY2025 value, $4.531665 (dated 2024-10-01), into period 2026. Earlier values: $4.226444 from 2022-10-01 (FFY2023) and $4.957075 from 2023-10-01 (FFY2024). Annual periods read 1 January values, so period 2025 uses $4.531665 and period 2024 uses $4.957075.
3. **Heating type (settled model input rule).** `heating_type` is a required input. The branch lists only the seven fuels of B.5.c.1.a, so UNSPECIFIED is ineligible, including a household with heat in unsubsidized rent; D.1.b requires the household to designate a primary fuel type. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the `heating_type` default. Companion tests set `heating_type` explicitly.
4. **Medicare premiums (Part B only).** The branch subtracts each member's out-of-pocket `medicare_part_b_premium` from household gross income before the $50 deduction and the zero floor, for any member who pays it, under exemption 15. The model's premium is net of Medicare Savings Program coverage and zero for non-enrollees; it stands in for the applicant's statement of the amount (C.1.a). Part D premiums, which application question 10 also asks about, have no premium input and are not deducted.
5. **Per-source loss floors (encoded reading).** Every earned and unearned source is floored at zero per person, so a business, rental or farm rent loss offsets no other income. C.5.a.3 counts the income “received” and self-employment “Profit”, and C.5.a.4.b lists rental property among the self-employment profit determinations; no provision lets a loss in one source reduce another.
6. **Interest, dividends and cash contributions (manual over plan).** Plan item 1.9 leaves “Interest, dividends, or royalties” and “Cash gifts” unchecked. The manual counts all gross unearned income (C.5.a.3.c), names “cash contributions” (C.5.a.4.c), and none of the 27 exemptions covers interest or dividends; exemption 19 excludes only non-recurring income such as one-time gifts. The branch counts `interest_income`, `ordinary_dividend_income` and recurring `financial_assistance`.
7. **Auxiliary Grant and TANF (inputs).** B.5.a names “auxiliary grants to the aged, blind and disabled” as public assistance and no exemption covers them, so `va_ag` counts. Most Auxiliary Grant recipients live in licensed assisted living or adult foster care settings, which B.5.c.2.b excludes; the model has no licensed-facility input. TANF counts through the SPM unit's take-up-gated `tanf` (which includes `va_tanf`).
8. **Income limit (reconciled pattern).** floor(1.5 x 2025 guideline / 12) reproduces all 20 B.6.a amounts and the $687 increment; this is a numerical pattern, not an express rounding rule. The one-year guideline lag follows the June adoption note (matrix page 1). The 05/21 Appendix B page (150%) controls over the manual's 01/03 copy (130%).
9. **Income percent (inference).** Appendix B prints whole-percent bands with no fraction rule. The branch rounds the percent to four decimals and floors it, so a one-person income of $23,473 (100.004%) scores 1 point; incomes above 100%, reachable only through the all-SSI exception, score 0. The percent uses countable income after the premium and the $50 deduction (D.4: “to determine the countable income for screening purposes”).
10. **Climate zones (source pages).** Salem city (775) appears in Central Mountain on the 01/03 Appendix A page 1 but not on the 06/17 page 1; the branch keeps Central Mountain. Bedford City (515, now part of Bedford County) and Clifton Forge (560, now a town in Alleghany County) have no county code of their own. A household without a listed Virginia county defaults to Tidewater.
11. **Simplifications without inputs.** Annual amounts stand for twelve times the prior calendar month's income; the 4.3 and 2.15 conversions, irregular-income averaging and per-member rounding to the dollar (C.5.a, page 37) are not modeled. The SPM unit stands for the B.5.a household. `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant` approximates B.7. The Social Security number rule (B.8.c), live-in attendants, licensed facilities, group homes, one-room occupants, persons without a physical address, the code F excess-usage arrangement and roomer or boarder profit rules have no inputs. `is_disabled` stands for railroad retirement disability and Medicaid permanent and total disability. The vendor-payment limit to charges through March 31 is not applied, and benefits are not truncated to the cent as VDSS prints them.
12. **Years (backfill).** Only FFY2026 is verified. `fpg_rate` 1.5 starts 2021-05-01 and backfills earlier years, although the 01/03 Appendix B page names 130%; the FFY2023 value per point backfills before 2022-10-01. Earlier periods are unverified estimates.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-va-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-va-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml) (Energy Assistance Manual, 138 pages)
- [us-va-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-va-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml) (FY2026 benefit matrix, OCR)
- [us-va-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-va-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml) (2024 and 2025 guidelines)
- [us-va-tanf-ccdf-w6-regulation.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-va-tanf-ccdf-w6-regulation.yaml) (layout for Virginia Administrative Code sections; holds no 22VAC40-680 section)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-va/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the FFY2026 limits for sizes 1 to 20 and the $687 step, the at-or-below test and the all-SSI exception, household size (citizens and qualified aliens, income of others counted), the under-18 earnings exemption, every listed countable source with per-source loss floors, the exemption 15 Part B deduction, the $50 deduction once per elderly or disabled member, the seven eligible fuels and UNSPECIFIED, SOLAR, NONE and OTHER, heat in rent with and without a subsidy, homelessness, every Appendix B table and band edge, all 133 climate-zone localities, the placeholder fuel and burden points, and the value per point for each period kept in scope. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: Encode SSI spouse and parent resource deeming under 20 CFR 416.1202 and the 416.1205 resource limits (PE-US #3557 parity)

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
Dispatch-ready encoding debt for the regulation. The statute it implements, 42 USC 1382c(f)(1) and (f)(2), was dispatched to the signed encoder on 2026-10-09 (axiom-encode runs [37983146825](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/actions/runs/37983146825) and [37983156312](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/actions/runs/37983156312)); both runs were told to defer the statute's "inequitable under the circumstances" exception to `us/regulation/20/416/1202`, which is this issue. No handwritten RuleSpec has been created.

## Encoding debt and search evidence

PolicyEngine-US currently tests a person's own SSI-countable resources against the individual limit, except that it combines resources for an SSI joint claim. It omits resources of an ineligible spouse and parent-to-child resource deeming. The companion PolicyEngine change implements 20 CFR 416.1202(a), (b), and 416.1205; see PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#3557.

I searched the tracked tree of rulespec-us `origin/main` at `16a6677190194da2431a78fcaa5b6548cd0e2845` with `git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main`, filtering for SSI, Supplemental Security Income, 20 CFR, part 416, and the relevant section numbers. A bounded `git grep` of tracked federal modules and manifests found no encoding of 20 CFR 416.1202 or 416.1205. The existing `us/regulations/42-cfr/435/120/ssi-mandatory-group.yaml` only encodes the Medicaid obligation for people receiving or deemed to receive SSI; its SSI status is a supplied input. It does not compute SSI resources or SSI resource eligibility. `us/statutes/42/416/l.yaml` concerns a different provision and is not the requested CFR provision.

New modules and companion fixtures:

- `us/regulations/20-cfr/416/1202.yaml` and `1202.test.yaml`; corpus citation `us/regulation/20/416/1202`.
- `us/regulations/20-cfr/416/1205.yaml` and `1205.test.yaml`; corpus citation `us/regulation/20/416/1205`.
- Referenced definitions: 20 CFR 416.1856 (child), 416.1851 (household), 416.1806 (spouse), 416.1167 (temporary absence), and 416.1207 (first-moment-of-month resource determination). Import signed modules where available; otherwise declare exact, legally scoped leaf inputs and deferred dependencies. Do not substitute tax filing or tax dependency definitions for these relationships.
- SSA POMS companion guidance: SI 01330.100, .200, .280, .310, and .340. Give any rule that depends on POMS rather than directly on the CFR a POMS proof source.

## Corpus and signed encoder blocker

The rulespec-us toolchain pins corpus release `us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap` and corpus ref `8f7d60aaced28ee4252b9237f9d6e02360dc34bc`. At that git ref, `data/corpus/provisions/us/regulation/2026-07-23-title-20-part-416.jsonl`, line 9, is `us/regulation/20/416/1202`, source format `ecfr-xml`, source as of `2026-07-14`. Its operative text matches the eCFR XML retrieved for `2026-10-05` on `2026-10-09`. However, the pinned release manifest `manifests/releases/us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap.json` does not include the `2026-07-23-title-20-part-416` regulation scope. Existence at the pinned git ref does not make this provision dispatchable from the pinned release.

That partial part-416 corpus snapshot also includes 416.1167, 416.1207, and 416.1806. It contains no section row for 416.1205, 416.1851, or 416.1856. A bounded search of all federal regulation JSONL files at the pinned ref found no alternate 416.1205 or 416.1856 row. POMS proof sources also need ingestion or confirmation in the dispatch source bundle. The signed encoder is therefore blocked on completing the corpus source bundle and making it available in the pinned signed release. Do not dispatch with an invented citation or replace the legally necessary definitions with an opaque aggregate.

The current rulespec-us `.axiom/workflow-toolchain.toml` names axiom-encode `0.2.2092`, ref `3bf5a2afbff0391261ad65bd7497f1b0efaaff85`, and rules engine ref `89571cc2a938707fd60a5489b951135345697296`. Refresh and verify all refs at dispatch time. Follow issues #1403 and #1416: generated content must come from the signed encoder with its protected signer, and the billed encoder run needs its own approval.

The companion PolicyEngine pull request cites this issue as `axiom: <this issue> queued`, with the corpus blocker above.

## Regulation (verbatim)

The primary source is eCFR, title 20 current through `2026-10-05`, retrieved `2026-10-09` using the versioner XML API. Official SSA CFR pages provide an independently accessible copy:

- https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/chapter-III/part-416/subpart-L/section-416.1202
- https://www.ssa.gov/OP_Home/cfr20/416/416-1202.htm
- https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/chapter-III/part-416/subpart-L/section-416.1205
- https://www.ssa.gov/OP_Home/cfr20/416/416-1205.htm

### 20 CFR 416.1202

> (a) Married individual. In the case of an individual who is living with a person not eligible under this part and who is considered to be the husband or wife of such individual under the criteria in §§ 416.1802 through 416.1835 of this part, such individual's resources shall be deemed to include any resources, not otherwise excluded under this subpart, of such spouse whether or not such resources are available to such individual. In addition to the exclusions listed in § 416.1210, we also exclude the following items:
>
> (1) Pension funds that the ineligible spouse may have. Pension funds are defined as funds held in individual retirement accounts (IRA), as described by the Internal Revenue Code, or in work-related pension plans (including such plans for self-employed persons, sometimes referred to as Keogh plans);
>
> (2) For 9 months beginning with the month following the month of receipt, the unspent portion of any retroactive payment of special pay an ineligible spouse received from one of the uniformed services pursuant to 37 U.S.C. 310; and
>
> (3) For 9 months beginning with the month following the month of receipt, the unspent portion of any retroactive payment of family separation allowance an ineligible spouse received from one of the uniformed services pursuant to 37 U.S.C. 427 as a result of deployment to or service in a combat zone (as defined in § 416.1160(d)).
>
> (b) Child—(1) General. In the case of a child (as defined in § 416.1856) who is under age 18, we will deem to that child any resources, not otherwise excluded under this subpart, of his or her ineligible parent who is living in the same household with him or her (as described in § 416.1851). We also will deem to the child the resources of his or her ineligible stepparent. As used in this section, the term “parent” means the natural or adoptive parent of a child, and the term “stepparent” means the spouse (as defined in § 416.1806) of such natural or adoptive parent who is living in the same household with the child and parent. We will deem to a child the resources of his or her parent and stepparent whether or not those resources are available to him or her. We will deem to a child the resources of his or her parent and stepparent only to the extent that those resources exceed the resource limits described in § 416.1205. (If the child is living with only one parent, we apply the resource limit for an individual. If the child is living with both parents, or the child is living with one parent and a stepparent, we apply the resource limit for an individual and spouse.) We will not deem to a child the resources of his or her parent or stepparent if the child is excepted from deeming under paragraph (b)(2) of this section. In addition to the exclusions listed in § 416.1210, we also exclude the following items:
>
> (i) Pension funds of an ineligible parent (or stepparent). Pension funds are defined as funds held in IRAs, as described by the Internal Revenue Code, or in work-related pension plans (including such plans for self-employed persons, sometimes referred to as Keogh plans);
>
> (ii) For 9 months beginning with the month following the month of receipt, the unspent portion of any retroactive payment of special pay an ineligible parent (or stepparent) received from one of the uniformed services pursuant to 37 U.S.C. 310; and
>
> (iii) For 9 months beginning with the month following the month of receipt, the unspent portion of any retroactive payment of family separation allowance an ineligible parent (or stepparent) received from one of the uniformed services pursuant to 37 U.S.C. 427 as a result of deployment to or service in a combat zone (as defined in § 416.1160(d)).
>
> (2) Disabled child under age 18. In the case of a disabled child under age 18 who is living in the same household with his or her parents, the deeming provisions of paragraph (b)(1) of this section shall not apply if such child—
>
> (i) Previously received a reduced SSI benefit while a resident of a medical treatment facility, as described in § 416.414;
>
> (ii) Is eligible for medical assistance under a Medicaid State home care plan approved by the Secretary under the provisions of section 1915(c) or authorized under section 1902(e)(3) of the Act; and
>
> (iii) Would otherwise be ineligible because of the deeming of his or her parents' resources or income.
>
> (c) Applicability. When used in this subpart L, the term individual refers to an eligible aged, blind, or disabled person, and also includes a person whose resources are deemed to be the resources of such individual (as provided in paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section).

An individual who is living with an ineligible spouse is eligible for benefits under title XVI of the Act if his or her nonexcludable resources, including the resources of the spouse, do not exceed $2,250 prior to January 1, 1985, and all other eligibility requirements are met.

### Definitions and timing

20 CFR 416.1856, https://www.ssa.gov/OP_Home/cfr20/416/416-1856.htm:

> We consider you to be a child if—
>
> (a)(1) You are under 18 years old; or
>
> (2) You are under 22 years old and you are a student regularly attending school or college or training that is designed to prepare you for a paying job;
>
> (b) You are not married; and
>
> (c) You are not the head of a household.

416.1202(b) additionally requires age under 18; the student extension in 416.1856 does not extend parent resource deeming to ages 18–21.

20 CFR 416.1207(a), https://www.ssa.gov/OP_Home/cfr20/416/416-1207.htm:

> Resources determinations are made as of the first moment of the month. A resource determination is based on what assets an individual has, what their values are, and whether or not they are excluded as of the first moment of the month.

20 CFR 416.1167(a), (b), (c), https://www.ssa.gov/OP_Home/cfr20/416/416-1167.htm:

> (a) General. During a temporary absence, we continue to consider the absent person a member of the household. A temporary absence occurs when—
>
> (1) You, your ineligible spouse, parent, or an ineligible child leaves the household but intends to and does return in the same month or the month immediately following; or
>
> (2) You enter a medical treatment facility and are eligible for either benefit payable under § 416.212. We consider your absence to be temporary through the last month benefits under § 416.212 were paid unless you were discharged from the facility in the following month. In that case, we consider your absence to be temporary through the date of discharge.

> If you are an eligible child who is away at school but comes home on some weekends or lengthy holidays and if you are subject to the control of your parents, we consider you temporarily absent from your parents' household. However, if you are not subject to parental control, we do not consider your absence temporary and we do not deem parental income (or resources) to you. Being subject to parental control affects deeming to you only if you are away at school.
>
> If your ineligible spouse or parent is absent from the household due solely to a duty assignment as a member of the Armed Forces on active duty, we continue to consider that person to be living in the same household as you, absent evidence to the contrary. If we determine that during such an absence, evidence indicates that your spouse or parent should no longer be considered to be living in the same household as you, then deeming will cease. When such evidence exists, we determine the month in which your spouse or parent should no longer be considered to be living in the same household as you and stop deeming his or her income and resources beginning with the month following that month.

Do not equate physical absence with termination of household membership. In particular, a medical-facility residence does not stop deeming if it is an absence qualifying under 416.1167(a)(2). An adjudicated temporary-absence input must certify one of these exact conditions, rather than merely labelling a move as temporary.

## Required outputs and mapping

Period: Month. Entity: Person for individual outputs, with an explicit same-household parent/spouse relationship group where needed. The PolicyEngine adapter may use its existing tax-unit parent roles and marital-unit spouse roles, but those adapter conventions are not legal definitions.

1. `ssi_individual_resource_limit` and `ssi_couple_resource_limit`, Money, from 416.1205(c), including the effective dates above. The couple limit applies both to two eligible spouses and to an eligible individual with an ineligible spouse.
2. `ssi_spouse_resources_subject_to_deeming`, Money: same-household ineligible spouse's otherwise countable resources, removing the additional 416.1202(a)(1)–(3) exclusions. The result is nonnegative and does not depend on whether the resources are available to the eligible individual.
3. `ssi_parent_resources_subject_to_deeming`, Money: resources of legally qualifying parents/stepparents in the same household, applying the general exclusions and additional 416.1202(b)(1)(i)–(iii) exclusions. An SSI application or aged/blind/disabled status alone does not establish an eligible parent; apply SI 01330.310 before classifying the parent.
4. `ssi_parent_resource_allowance`, Money: individual limit for one resident parent; couple limit for two resident parents or one parent plus resident stepparent. Read the same 416.1205 outputs as the final resource test, so a counterfactual limit change changes the allowance too.
5. `ssi_resources_deemed_from_parents`, Money: nonnegative parental excess over the allowance; zero when the parent(s) meets the resource requirement under SI 01330.310; zero for a child outside the 416.1856 definition/under-18 requirement or excepted under all three conjunctive elements of 416.1202(b)(2). Split excess equally across SSI-eligible children, redetermining the remaining set when a child is ineligible, following SI 01330.200(B) and the Goode example. Declare any non-resource SSI eligibility classification dependency instead of treating all disabled children as eligible automatically.
6. `ssi_resources_for_resource_test`, Money: individual own countable resources plus applicable spouse or parent deemed resources; combined own resources for an eligible couple. Do not double-count a spouse in both the combined resource base and the deemed resource addend.
7. `meets_ssi_resource_test`, Judgment: compare the resource base with the appropriate limit using inclusive `<=`. An eligible individual living with an ineligible spouse uses the couple limit even when no joint SSI claim is made. Children use the individual limit.

The pension exclusion applies to the ineligible deemor's pension funds; it is not a general exclusion of the eligible individual's own retirement assets. The two military payment exclusions last nine months beginning with the month after receipt. They must be treated as excluded asset amounts, not current military income, and cannot reduce deemed resources below zero.

## Adapter scope and points requiring explicit treatment

The PolicyEngine model is annual and uses tax-unit parents/marital-unit spouses. These entities approximate the legal same-household and natural/adoptive/stepparent relationships; tax-unit inclusion does not prove them. Make exact legal predicates explicit in RuleSpec, and document the annual adapter limitations. Do not manufacture a regulation authorizing automatic deeming from any adult tax-unit member.

Full SSI eligibility also depends on income, citizenship, residence, and other criteria. Resource formulas must not recursively call final child eligibility when forming the parent resource pool or eligible-child denominator. SI 01330.310 and .340 establish how to test applying/eligible parents' resources without that recursion. Aged/blind/disabled status is an existing PolicyEngine proxy, not the complete legal meaning of “eligible.”

416.1202(b)(2) is a precise exception for qualifying disabled children returning to home care; ordinary institutional residence alone is not that exception. Model household membership/temporary absences and the specified waiver conditions separately. A medical-facility flag stops parental deeming only when residence removes the child from the parent's legally defined household; 416.1167(a)(2)-qualified temporary medical absence preserves that membership and deeming. Temporal questions should be adjudicated monthly in RuleSpec; do not infer a cessation date from an annual age snapshot. The PolicyEngine Month formula reads the annual `age` input at `period.this_year`, because age is a level and must not be apportioned across months.

| Spousal resources at the combined couple limit pass | `{"pass":[true,true]}` | 1202(a),1205(a),(c) |

The parent adapter-isolation case separates a child and adult into different tax units inside one household. It pins the present adapter's isolation, not a federal rule that tax units determine parental relationships. Legal RuleSpec must still deem from a qualifying parent in another tax unit; the PolicyEngine adapter requires an explicit deemed-resource input in that unsupported relationship configuration.

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Arizona LIHEAP Standard benefit in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1c, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10293 (branch `az-liheap-wave1c`), open for review, not merged. Head `406a5efe6a` (2026-10-23), which adds the 2026-10-23 review fixes (commit `49fa4c2f47`), a merge of `main` and the Medicare premium follow-up; this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **Sources missing from the corpus.** No axiom-corpus manifest on `main` holds the editions the branch encodes: the DES LIHEAP Policy revision 13, effective August 25, 2025 (household, eligibility, countable income, benefit rules and the FY2026 Appendix A limits), and revision 15, effective March 23, 2026 (the under-18 income change). `us-az-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml` holds revision 16A, effective July 1, 2026: its Appendix A carries the FY27 limits (period 2027 only) and its Appendix B reprints the point worksheet. It also carries the other revision 13 provisions the branch cites (page map under Source text). Also missing: the worksheet behind every point table, the DES program page, the FY2026 state median income table and the 2025 HHS poverty guidelines (rows below; `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml` holds the FY2027 table and the 2026 guidelines). These need ingest before the modules below can be proved.
- **Bundle scope.** The LIHEAP program bundle on corpus `main` (`manifests/program-bundles/liheap.yaml`, as of 2026-10-06, fiscal year 2027) marks the FY2026 Arizona plan, the FY2026 SMI table and the 2025 guidelines as excluded back-year material. An FY2026 release needs that scope reconciled, or the release limited to period 2027 under revision 16A.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-20; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.
- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10293 is not approved: the 2026-10-21 review requested changes, and the fixes at head `406a5efe6a` await re-review, so there is no revision to pin.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10293, branch `az-liheap-wave1c`; it closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10290. Since head `c12ed6dbd4`, commits `cc76cdf244` and `8c9c5f1f8d` read `total_unemployment_compensation` and count `military_retirement_income`, commit `49fa4c2f47` floors every unearned source at zero, adds `farm_rent_income` and `gambling_winnings`, reads the take-up-gated `tanf` and cites revision 16A wherever it carries revision 13's text, and the head commit subtracts members' `medicare_part_b_premium` from household gross income. Oracle fixtures will pin the merged commit.
- **Scope:** Arizona's single annual Standard LIHEAP benefit for the FY2026 season, the regular benefit (interpretation 1). Covered: residence, household size counting citizens and qualified noncitizens, categorical eligibility through SNAP or Cash Assistance receipt, gross countable income (each source floored at zero, less members' Medicare Part B premiums) with the under-18 rules of revisions 13 and 15, the Appendix A limit (the greater of 60% of state median income and 150% of the HHS poverty guidelines), the energy-expense requirement (a bill or energy included in rent), the worksheet's income, energy-burden and energy-need points with +2 for portable fuel, and the $160, $320, $480 and $640 payment bands. Out of scope: Regular and Life-Threatening Crisis Assistance ($5.01 to $500), water for evaporative cooling, Temporary Emergency Shelter, weatherization, energy-related repair and equipment, and the closed state Power AZ program. Rules in scope but without inputs: interpretation 16.
- **Policy periods:** one verified season, FY2026 (October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026; plan item 1.1, page 4). Variables are annual and read 1 January parameter values, so period `2026` applies revision 13 with the FY2026 SMI (`gov.hhs.smi.amount` AZ `2025-10-01`: 107,983) and the 2025 guidelines (`fpg_year_lag` 1). Parameter dates: worksheet values `2024-10-12` (point scales, payment, the child age limit, portable-fuel and per-category points); revision 13 values `2025-08-25` (all other values); `income/child_unearned_income_counted` false from `2025-08-25` and true from `2026-03-23` (revision 15). `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2026"`. Period `2027` (revision 15's child income rule, kept in revision 16A, the FY2027 SMI of 112,946 and the 2026 guidelines) reproduces every revision 16A Appendix A cell but is not claimed. Earlier periods use parameter backfilling and are unverified estimates.
- **Variables:** the 14 in Required outputs, under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/az/des/liheap/` (with `eligibility/`, `income/` and `points/` subfolders). No new input variable. The limit reuses the shared `liheap_smi_limit` helper (`variables/gov/hhs/hhs_smi.py`, PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10019) and `fpg()` with `gov.hhs.smi` and `gov.hhs.fpg`.
- **Parameters:** 16 files under `gov.states.az.des.liheap`: `eligibility/` `smi_rate` (0.6), `fpg_rate` (1.5), `fpg_year_lag` (1), `max_table_size` (12) and `categorical_programs` (`snap`, `tanf`); `income/` `adult_age` (18), `child_unearned_income_counted`, `sources/earned` (5 sources) and `sources/unearned` (19); `points/` `income_ratio` and `energy_burden` (band-top `single_amount` scales read with `right=True` and a `-.inf` first threshold), `portable_fuel` (2), `elderly_age` (60), `child_age_limit` (7) and `vulnerable_member` (1); `payment/amount` (`single_amount` keyed at 0, 5, 9 and 13 points). Plus a `programs.yaml` entry and a changelog fragment.
- **Tests:** 124 YAML cases in 13 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/az/des/liheap/` at head `406a5efe6a`. Since `c12ed6dbd4`, the branch adds seven cases (countable unearned Cases 10-13, countable income Cases 3-4, energy burden Case 18; those files now hold 13, 4 and 18), and the Medicare premium changes three countable incomes (integration Case 2, now $320; countable unearned Case 7; `az_liheap.yaml` Case 14). Every case sends `heating_type`. All 124 cases pass locally on the head (2026-10-23).

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence on axiom-corpus `main` (`e019e44563`, 2026-10-19) was checked on 2026-10-20; the signed release was not checked. rulespec-us `main` (`874bce4fea`, 2026-10-19) has `us-az/policies/`, `us-az/regulations/aac/` and `us-az/statutes/` but no LIHEAP module, and `us/` has no state median income or poverty-guideline module. The paths below follow that layout. Pages are physical PDF pages; in the three DES policy editions they equal the printed page footers (for example “8 of 37” and “39 of 41”). The corpus `page-N` suffix counts text-bearing pages only.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-az/policies/des/liheap-policy/rev-13/section-v/definitions` | Categorical Eligibility (pages 3-4); Disability, Eligible Household Member, Eligibility Period, Energy Utility, Gross Income, Household (page 4); Ineligible Household Member, Mixed-Status Household, Portable Fuel, Qualified Noncitizen, SUAP, Standard LIHEAP (page 5) | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. Official copy, for every revision 13 row: [DES LIHEAP Policy revision 13 (effective August 25, 2025), Wayback capture of October 17, 2025, pages 1, 3-10, 13-14, 29-34 and 37](https://web.archive.org/web/20251017id_/https://des.az.gov/sites/default/files/dl/CCSD-LIHEAP-Policy.pdf#page=1) (37 pages). des.az.gov now serves revision 16A. The branch cites the October 30, 2025 capture (`20251030203752`) only for Appendix A (page 37) and the under-18 sentence (page 9). |
| `.../rev-13/section-vi-a/eligibility` | VI.A.1 energy-related expenses and VI.A.2 subsidized housing (page 6); VI.A.3 eligible member (pages 6-7); VI.A.4 residence, VI.A.5 Tribal members, VI.A.6.a-b categorical eligibility (page 7); VI.A.6.c income eligibility, VI.A.6.d mixed status, VI.A.6.e.i-ii.D countable income (page 8); VI.A.6.e.ii.E-F under 18 and the plan cross-reference, VI.A.7 costs paid by another program (page 9) | none | Same file. |
| `.../rev-13/section-vi-b/standard-liheap-assistance` | VI.B.1: the matrix and the four benefit factors (page 10) | none | Same file. |
| `.../rev-13/section-vii-a/verification-of-income` | VII.A.1.c.ii: members 18 and older, self-employment profit or loss (page 13), the Medicare note (page 14); VII.A.1.c.v: the monthly income formula (page 14) | none | Same file. |
| `.../rev-13/section-vii-b/benefits` | VII.B.1.a: up to $640, once per Eligibility Period (page 30); VII.B.1.c-d: income of categorically eligible households, LIHEAP not income (page 31); VII.B.3.a.ii.B: payment to the applicant when utilities are in rent (page 32); VII.B.3.b.iii: the $5.00 vendor minimum and the remainder rule (pages 33-34); VII.B.4.b: the $640 limit and SUAP (page 34) | none | Same file. |
| `.../rev-13/appendix-a/income-eligibility` | Monthly limits for sizes 1 to 12 and +$687 per person over 12 (page 37) | none | Same file. |
| `us-az/policies/des/liheap-policy/rev-15/section-vi-a/countable-income` | Effective date (page 1); VI.A.6.e.ii.E: only earned income of members under 18 is excluded (page 9) | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [DES LIHEAP Policy revision 15 (effective March 23, 2026), Wayback capture of April 4, 2026, pages 1 and 9](https://web.archive.org/web/20260404182400id_/https://des.az.gov/sites/default/files/dl/CCSD-LIHEAP-Policy.pdf?time=1775327031204#page=1). |
| `us-az/policies/des/liheap-policy/rev-16a/appendix-a/income-eligibility` and `.../rev-16a/appendix-b/benefit-matrix` | Revision notes (pages 1-2); the other revision 13 provisions above, which the branch now cites here (page map and wording changes under Source text); FY27 monthly limits for sizes 1 to 12 and +$710 (page 39); the benefit matrix (pages 40-41) | `us-az/manual/des/liheap-policy` | In manifest `us-az-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml` (revision 16A, expression date 2026-07-01, 41 pages). Its `benefit_matrix_pdf_pages: '39'` points at Appendix A, the income table; the matrix itself is Appendix B on pages 40-41. Supports the period 2027 limits and the matrix, not the FY2026 limits or revision 13's under-18 rule. Official copy: [DES LIHEAP Policy revision 16A (effective July 1, 2026), pages 1-10, 13-14, 31-35 and 39-41](https://des.az.gov/sites/default/files/dl/CCSD-LIHEAP-Policy.pdf#page=1); the bytes fetched on 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-23 match the corpus lock (sha256 `85508bbb4c9d...`). |
| `us-az/policies/des/liheap-eligibility-worksheet/640-limit` | Section 1 income points, section 2 energy burden and the +2 portable-fuel note, section 3 energy need, section 4 payment matrix; effective October 12, 2024 | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [LIHEAP Eligibility Worksheet, $640 Limit (the Clearinghouse FY2026 heating matrix; the cooling matrix file is byte-identical)](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/benefits-matricies/AZ_BenefitMatrix_Heating_2026.pdf) (1 page). |
| `us-az/policies/des/liheap-program-page` | The income-ratio formula and its 2,000 / 4,535 example; the burden formula and its 350 / 2,000 example; the portable-fuel note; the payment table; the leftover-credit rule; categorical income on file; the October 12, 2024 effective statement | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [DES LIHEAP program page](https://des.az.gov/liheap) (Wayback capture of September 21, 2026; the live page fetched on 2026-10-20 carries the same text). Interpretive support; the policy and worksheet carry the rules. |
| `us-az/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-1` | 1.1 dates and 1.2 funding shares (page 4); 1.4 and 1.4a categorical eligibility, 1.6 equal treatment (page 5); 1.8 gross income (pages 5-6); 1.9 countable income, with “Excluding MediCare deduction” checked (pages 6-7) | `us-az/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | In manifest `us-az-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml` (Clearinghouse copy, expression date 2025-10-01); the program bundle marks it excluded as back-year. Official copy: [FY2026 state plan, pages 1, 4-7 and 9-10](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/state-plans/AZ_Plan_2026.pdf#page=1) (54 pages). |
| `us-az/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-2` | 2.1 the two threshold rows, 2.2 no additional requirements, 2.3 no asset test, the subsidized-housing rule, no differing renter rules (page 9); 2.4 one point per category, 2.5 benefit variables, 2.6 minimum $160 and maximum $640 (page 10) | `us-az/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | Same manifest. |
| `us/` state median income module | FY2026: Arizona four-person SMI $107,983 and 60% amounts for sizes 1 to 12 (Attachment 4 pages 1 and 4), with the 45 CFR 96.85 size percentages in its footnote; FY2027 ($112,946) for period 2027 | `us/guidance/acf/ocs/liheap-im/2026-01/attachment-4-smi-table` (FY2027 only) | `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml` holds the FY2027 table. The FY2026 table needs ingest: [LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 4, pages 1 and 4](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_IM2025-02_SMIStateTable_Att4.pdf#page=1); the bundle lists it with no citation path as excluded back-year. The branch also cites the Clearinghouse FFY 2026 Arizona SMI table (`azsmi.htm`, in no manifest; same 60% amounts, no four-person SMI). The bundle lists `us/regulation/45/96/85` in scope; whether a manifest captures it was not checked. |
| `us/` poverty guidelines module | 2025 guidelines ($15,650 for one person, $5,500 for each additional person) behind every FY2026 FPG arm; 2026 guidelines ($15,960, $5,680) for period 2027 | `us/guidance/hhs/aspe/poverty-guidelines/2026/federal-register` (2026 only) | `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml` holds the 2026 guidelines (91 FR 1797); the undated `us-hhs-poverty-guidelines.yaml` was never extracted. The 2025 guidelines need ingest: [FR Doc. 2025-01377 (90 FR 5917), page 1](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-17/pdf/2025-01377.pdf#page=1); the bundle lists it as excluded back-year. |

Companion tests take `snap` and `tanf` receipt as inputs, so no SNAP or Cash Assistance module is needed. Wage and benefit amounts are inputs; no expected value depends on their provenance. The branch also cites the [Clearinghouse FFY 2026 poverty guideline table](https://liheapch.acf.gov/profiles/povertytables/FY2026/popstate.htm) (in no manifest), which repeats the 2025 guidelines.

## Source text (verbatim)

Quotations come from the official files above (pdftotext -layout; the Federal Register notices in reading order; line breaks collapsed). Plan check-box and radio states come from 300 DPI renders of plan pages 5, 6, 7, 9 and 10.

**Editions and dates.** Revision 13, page 1: “Effective Date: 08/25/2025”, “Revision Number: 13”. Revision 15, page 1: “Effective Date: 03/23/2026”, “Revision Number: 15”. Revision 16A, pages 1-2: “Effective Date: 07/01/2026”, “Revision Number: 16A (Rescinds and supercedes Rev. 16)”, with the revision 16 notes “Updates program income limits for FY27” and “Incorporates the DES LIHEAP Benefit Matrix in Appendix B”. Plan page 1: “Report Period: 10/01/2025 to 09/30/2026” and “Report Status: Submission Accepted by CO”. Plan page 4, item 1.1: heating assistance and cooling assistance each from “10/01/2025” to “09/30/2026”; item 1.2: heating “16.80%”, cooling “38.12%”; and “The above dates are based on the calendar year. Funding for the Federal Fiscal Year is not affected by the heating and cooling months listed above.” Policy page 4: “Eligibility Period: The 12-month period for which an Applicant is eligible for an annual Standard and Crisis LIHEAP benefit.” Page 5: “Standard LIHEAP: Assistance that requires basic eligibility requirements be met and calculated based on the Benefit Matrix. This assistance is distinct from Crisis Assistance.” Page 10, VI.B.1: “Payments will be calculated using the LIHEAP Heating/Cooling Benefit Matrix as set by the current LIHEAP State Plan.” Worksheet: “LIHEAP ELIGIBILITY WORKSHEET - $640 Limit” and “Effective October 12, 2024”. Program page: “The information contained on this page is effective for applications received on or after October 12, 2024.”

**Revision 16A locators.** The branch cites revision 16A for all policy text below except the FY2026 Appendix A and revision 13's under-18 sentence. It moves the Household definition to page 5, VI.A.2-3 to page 7, VI.A.6.b.i.A to page 8, VI.A.6.e.ii.B-D to page 9 and each VII.B citation one page later (pages 31-35); Appendix A is page 39 and Appendix B (the worksheet tables) pages 40-41. Other cited pages are unchanged. Every other quoted policy passage is verbatim in revision 16A except the Portable Fuel and VI.A.6.e.ii.E changes noted below and these: Energy Utility (page 4) names “vendors of electricity or gas; Portable Fuel for purposes of heating or cooling; or water for the purposes of evaporative cooling”; VI.A.6.e.i (page 8) reads “30-day”, and VI.A.6.e.ii.A drops the list of documents; VI.A.6.e.ii.B (page 9): “Unearned income, including Social Security and TANF benefits, alimony, child support, gambling profits, and retirement income;”; VII.A.1.c.ii.B (page 13): “Income from self-employment or sole-proprietorship;”, with VII.A.1.c.iii.B.1 (page 14): “Form 1040 or 1099, plus Schedule C (Profit and Loss Statement) for self-employment;”; VII.B.1.c.i (page 32): “actively enrolled in DES Cash Assistance or Nutrition Assistance”; VII.B.4.b (page 35): “a Standard LIHEAP payment of up to $640 per Eligibility Period”. Revision 16A adds VI.A.1.c.i (page 7): “Uses of Portable Fuel beyond heating/cooling (e.g., cooking, powering outdoor tools or equipment) are ineligible for LIHEAP.”

**Household and immigration.** Policy page 4: “Household: Any individual or group of individuals who are living together as one (1) economic unit for whom residential Energy Utilities are customarily purchased in common or who make undesignated payments for Energy Utilities in the form of rent.” And: “Eligible Household Member: A member of a Household that is a U.S. citizen or Qualified Noncitizen”. Page 5: “Nonqualified noncitizens are not eligible for LIHEAP benefits, but their income will be counted toward total Household income and they may apply on behalf of Eligible Household Members”. And: “Qualified Non-Citizens may fall into any of the following categories: Lawful/legal permanent residents; asylees; refugees; ... battered noncitizen spouses, battered noncitizen children ...; Cuban/Haitian entrants; Compacts of Free Association citizens lawfully residing in the U.S.; or victims of a severe form of trafficking.” Pages 6-7, VI.A.3: “An Applicant, or a Household member, must be an Eligible Household Member.” ... “limits eligibility for benefits to citizens and Qualified Noncitizens, and prohibits benefits to other noncitizens ...” Page 8, VI.A.6.d: “Only Eligible Household Members will be considered as part of the Household size; and” “Income from all Household members aged 18 and older - regardless of eligibility - is considered Household income.”

**Eligibility.** Page 6, VI.A.1: “An Applicant must require assistance with payment of energy-related expenses.” VI.A.2: “An Applicant living in subsidized housing, and receiving an Energy Utility allowance or reimbursement greater than or equal to their monthly Energy Utility cost, is not eligible for LIHEAP assistance.” Page 7, VI.A.4: “The Applicant and Household must reside within Arizona at the time of application.” VI.A.5: members of Tribal nations “Are eligible to apply for LIHEAP assistance if they have first applied for benefits with their Tribal nation and are:” denied, or approved with a remaining balance. VI.A.6.a: “A Household must either meet Categorical Eligibility or Income Eligibility requirements for the purposes of verifying Household income.” VI.A.6.b.i: “If one (1) Household member’s current enrollment in Cash Assistance or Nutrition Assistance is verified, the Household will be considered categorically eligible.” And: “Categorical Eligibility exempts the Household from Verification of Income requirements, however, the Household must still meet and validate all other eligibility criteria to receive LIHEAP benefits.” Page 9, VI.A.7: “A Household may not receive LIHEAP benefits for costs already paid by any other assistance program.” Plan page 5, item 1.4: “Do you consider households categorically eligible if at least one household member receives ...” answered Yes, with the heating column TANF Yes, SSI No, SNAP Yes, Means-tested Veterans Programs No. Item 1.4a: “Categorical Eligibility is a determination that a Household meets income eligibility for LIHEAP assistance based upon one (1) or more Household member’s active enrollment in either DES Cash Assistance (CA) under Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) or DES Nutrition Assistance (NA) under the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).” Item 1.6: “In both cases, the reported income of the household is used to determine benefit amounts per the LIHEAP Matrix.” Plan page 9: item 2.2 (additional requirements) No; item 2.3 “Do you require an Assets test?” No; “Renters?” No; “Renters Living in subsidized housing?” Yes, with “Renters living in subsidizing housing, who receive a utility reimbursement, are not eligible for LIHEAP if the amount of the reimbursement exceeds the amount of their monthly utility bill.”; “Renters with utilities included in the rent?” No. Program page: “Your existing income information on file with DES will be used from your prior application.”

**Income limit.** Policy page 8, VI.A.6.c.i: “When Categorical Eligibility does not apply, the Household’s Gross Income must be at or below the greater of:” “60% of the SMI; or” “150% of the FPL.” “Note: See Appendix A for current SMI and FPL calculations.” Plan page 9, item 2.1: household size 1 to “9”, “State Median Income”, “60.00%”; household size “10”, “HHS Poverty Guidelines”, “150.00%”. Revision 13, page 37, “APPENDIX A - Income Eligibility by Household Size” (unchanged in revision 15), and revision 16A, page 39, “APPENDIX A - LIHEAP Income Eligibility by Household Size”, columns “Household size” and “Monthly Gross Income Limit”:

| Household size | Revision 13 (page 37) | Revision 16A (page 39) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | $2,807 | $2,936 |
| 2 | $3,671 | $3,840 |
| 3 | $4,535 | $4,743 |
| 4 | $5,399 | $5,647 |
| 5 | $6,262 | $6,550 |
| 6 | $7,126 | $7,454 |

## Required outputs

| Output | policyengine-us variable | Entity, period | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Household size | `az_liheap_household_size` | SPM unit, year | Number of members for whom `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant` is true. Arizona only. |
| Countable earned income | `az_liheap_countable_earned_income` | Person, year | For members aged 18 or over, the sum of `employment_income`, `self_employment_income`, `sstb_self_employment_income`, `partnership_s_corp_income` and `farm_operations_income`, each floored at zero; 0 under 18 in every period. |
| Countable unearned income | `az_liheap_countable_unearned_income` | Person, year | The sum of `total_unemployment_compensation`, `strike_benefits`, `social_security` (gross), `ssi` (twelve monthly amounts), `pension_income`, `military_retirement_income`, `retirement_distributions`, `railroad_benefits`, `veterans_benefits`, `alimony_income`, `child_support_received`, `rental_income`, `farm_rent_income`, `interest_income`, `ordinary_dividend_income`, `general_assistance`, `gambling_winnings`, `disability_benefits` and `workers_compensation`, each floored at zero, so no loss offsets other income. Counted for members aged 18 or over, and for younger members only when `child_unearned_income_counted` is true at the period start (false in period 2026, true in 2027). |
| Countable income | `az_liheap_countable_income` | SPM unit, year | max(members' countable earned and unearned income + the unit's annual `tanf` (take-up gated; includes `az_tanf`) - the members' `medicare_part_b_premium` total, 0). Each premium is out of pocket (0 if not enrolled, net of Medicare Savings Program coverage). Includes members who are not counted in size. |
| Income limit | `az_liheap_income_limit` | SPM unit, year | 12 x max(S, P), or 0 when size is 0. S = floor(floor(floor(0.6 x SMI4) x f) / 12), with SMI4 the Arizona four-person SMI in force at the period start (107,983 for 2026; 112,946 for 2027) and f = 0.52 + 0.16 x min(size - 1, 5) + 0.03 x max(size - 6, 0). P = floor(1.5 x G(c) / 12) + max(size - 12, 0) x floor(1.5 x (G(c + 1) - G(c)) / 12), with c = min(size, 12) and G the prior calendar year's HHS guideline for the household's state group. Reproduces both Appendix A tables. |
| Income eligible | `az_liheap_income_eligible` | SPM unit, year | Countable income <= income limit. |
| Categorically eligible | `az_liheap_categorically_eligible` | SPM unit, year | Annual `snap` + `tanf` > 0. |
| Energy cost | `az_liheap_energy_cost` | SPM unit, year | `pre_subsidy_electricity_expense` + `gas_expense` + `bottled_gas_expense` + `wood_expense` + `coal_expense` + `fuel_oil_expense` + `other_heating_fuel_expense`. |
| Eligible | `az_liheap_eligible` | SPM unit, year | Arizona; size > 0; categorically or income eligible; energy cost > 0 or `heat_expense_included_in_rent`; `heating_type` is not UNSPECIFIED. |
| Income points | `az_liheap_income_points` | SPM unit, year | r = countable income / income limit (unbounded when the limit is 0): 5 if r <= 0.2, 4 if <= 0.4, 3 if <= 0.6, 2 if <= 0.8, 1 if <= 1, otherwise 0. |
| Energy burden points | `az_liheap_energy_burden_points` | SPM unit, year | b = energy cost / countable income (0 when the cost is 0; unbounded when income is 0 and the cost is positive): 0 if b <= 0.05, 1 if <= 0.10, 2 if <= 0.15, 3 if <= 0.20, 4 if <= 0.25, 5 if <= 0.30, otherwise 6; plus 2 when `heating_type` is PROPANE, WOOD or COAL. |
| Energy need points | `az_liheap_energy_need_points` | SPM unit, year | One point for each category any member meets: age >= 60; `is_disabled`, positive `social_security_disability`, or positive `ssi` with `is_blind` or `is_ssi_disabled`; `is_veteran`; age < 7. |
| Total points | `az_liheap_points` | SPM unit, year | Income points + energy burden points + energy need points (at most 17). |
| Benefit | `az_liheap` | SPM unit, year | If eligible: $160 for 0 to 4 points, $320 for 5 to 8, $480 for 9 to 12, $640 for 13 or more; not capped at the energy cost. Otherwise $0. |

Inputs: `state_code`, `age`, `immigration_status`, `is_disabled`, `is_blind`, `is_ssi_disabled`, `is_veteran` (set explicitly; interpretation 11), the earned and unearned sources above (`social_security` sums `social_security_retirement`, `_disability`, `_survivors` and `_dependents`; `retirement_distributions` sums taxable and tax-exempt distributions; `military_retirement_income` sums `military_retirement_pay` and `military_retirement_pay_survivors`; `total_unemployment_compensation` passes a reported `unemployment_compensation` through), `medicare_part_b_premium`, `ssi` and `snap` (monthly variables; tests give annual totals), `tanf` (annual), `heating_type` sent explicitly, the seven bills above, and `heat_expense_included_in_rent`. Unit tests also set `az_liheap_household_size` directly.

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **One Standard benefit (settled).** Arizona pays one Standard payment per 12-month Eligibility Period, up to $640 (pages 4, 30, 34). The plan's heating (16.80%) and cooling (38.12%) components are funding shares with county months “based on the calendar year”; the policy names one “LIHEAP Heating/Cooling Benefit Matrix”. The branch pays it once per model year as the regular benefit.
2. **Zero points pay $160 (settled reconciliation, not an express rule).** The worksheet's first row is “1 - 4”, and plan 2.6 states a $160 minimum. Only a categorically eligible household above 100% of the limit with no burden or need points can score 0; the branch pays it $160 (`payment/amount` keyed from 0). Test 8(b) depends on this.
3. **Band edges between printed whole percents (interpretation).** The worksheet prints whole-percent bands with gaps (“0% - 20%”, “21% - 40%”; “5% or less”, “6% - 10%”), and the program-page examples use unrounded 44% and 17.5%. The branch forms each ratio in float64, keeps a printed top in its band and moves any excess to the next band (`right=True` with a `-.inf` first threshold). Rounding to whole percents would keep 20.002% and 5.004% in the lower band. Tests 1, 4 and 5 depend on this.
4. **Monthly test from annual inputs (simplification).** The policy tests income for the 30 days up to the application (VI.A.6.e.i) and builds monthly income as average gross pay times frequency over 12 (VII.A.1.c.v). The branch compares annual income with 12 times the monthly limit and uses annual over annual ratios for both point scales.
5. **Income-limit rounding (inferred).** The policy states the “greater of” rule but no rounding. Appendix A reproduces as the larger of floor(60% SMI amount / 12) and floor(1.5 x guideline / 12), with floor(1.5 x 5,500 / 12) = 687 per person over 12, for both tables. Rounding half up fails (test 2). Computed from the four-person SMI, the 60% amount must be floored first (0.6 x 107,983 = 64,789.80, printed $64,789; without the floor, size 5 gives $6,263 instead of $6,262). Plan 2.1's two rows (sizes 1 to 9 on SMI, 10 and up on the guidelines) are where the two arms cross for FY2026; the branch computes the maximum, which also matches FY27. Tests 2 and 3 depend on this.
6. **Household (simplification).** The SPM unit stands in for the economic unit (page 4). Size counts `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`, which has no status for Compacts of Free Association citizens, battered noncitizens or trafficking victims (page 5).
7. **Categorical eligibility and its income (simplification).** Any modeled `snap` or `tanf` in the year stands for “current enrollment”. Both are take-up gated, and `tanf` includes `az_tanf`, so a family that does not take up Cash Assistance gets neither the eligibility nor the income. For categorically eligible households the branch uses the whole household's countable income, not “the reported income of the Household member who is actively enrolled” (VII.B.1.c), and such a household above the limit scores 0 income points.
8. **Under-18 income and revision timing (settled).** Revision 13 excludes all income of members under 18; revisions 15 and 16A exclude only their earned income, and plan 1.9 leaves “Earned income of a child under the age of 18” unchecked. Counting children's unearned income is a labeled inference: no revision says so, and VI.A.6.d.ii still names the income of members aged 18 and older as household income. `child_unearned_income_counted` turns true on 2026-03-23 and annual periods read 1 January, so period 2026 follows revision 13 throughout and period 2027 follows revision 15. Test 11 depends on this.
9. **Medicare premiums off household income (encoded reading).** The policy says Medicare expenses “should be subtracted when determining gross income” (page 14 in revisions 13, 15 and 16A), and plan 1.9 checks “Excluding MediCare deduction”. The branch counts `social_security` gross and subtracts the members' `medicare_part_b_premium` total from household gross income, floored at zero, so a premium also reduces a pension (test 15(c)); netting it from Social Security alone gives the same result when the benefit covers the premium. Part D and other Medicare expenses have no input. Tests 8(a), 12(e), 12(l), 15(a) and 15(c) depend on this.
10. **Disability need point (encoded reading).** The definition (page 4, quoted above) covers Title II and XVI recipients. The branch reads “other ... disability benefits” as making the Title II and XVI benefits disability benefits: it credits `is_disabled`, `social_security_disability`, or SSI paid to a recipient who `is_blind` or `is_ssi_disabled`. Social Security retirement or survivor benefits and SSI paid on age alone give no disability point. Read literally, every Title II or XVI recipient would qualify: test 8(a) would score 6 points (still $320), the pair aged 68 and 66 in test 13 would score 3, and the aged SSI recipient 2. State-administered disability benefits have no input.
11. **Veteran input.** The branch reads `is_veteran`, which policyengine-us derives from `veterans_benefits` > 0 when unset; VA benefits paid to a survivor would then add the point, and a veteran without VA benefits needs the flag.
12. **Energy cost and portable fuel (interpretation).** For the worksheet's “Total Monthly Cost”, the branch adds the pre-subsidy electric bill, metered gas, bottled gas, wood, coal, fuel oil and other heating fuel, and excludes water for evaporative cooling (out of scope) and sewer, trash and phone. The +2 applies when `heating_type` is PROPANE, WOOD or COAL; generator fuel and pellets have no heating type, and FUEL_OIL, KEROSENE, SOLAR and OTHER get no bonus. A secondary propane or wood bill does not add the 2 points. Revision 16A's narrower Portable Fuel use (pages 5 and 7) is not modeled; bills count in full.
13. **Heating type required (settled).** `heating_type` is a required input; UNSPECIFIED makes the household ineligible and pays $0, even with energy in rent, so a heat-in-rent household must send its fuel. NONE stays eligible because the Standard benefit pays any Energy Utility bill, cooling included. policyengine-us issue 9754 tracks the unspecified default.
14. **Zero income and zero cost (interpretation).** The worksheet does not address them. A positive cost with no income takes the top burden band (6 points); no cost scores 0 burden points, even with energy in rent. Tests 5, 9(a) and 14(a) depend on this.
15. **Income sources (encoded reading and gaps).** Workers' compensation is an encoded reading: plan 1.9 neither lists nor excludes it, and the branch counts it through the Gross Income definition and “Consistent income received from other sources” (test 12(g)). Military retirement pay and Survivor Benefit Plan annuities are “retirement income”, and farm rent is “Rental income” (tests 12(m)-(o)). Every source is floored at zero one by one, so no loss offsets other income (tests 12(h) and 15(b)). The policy counts “gambling profits”, while plan 1.9 leaves lottery winnings (one-time lump sums) unchecked; `gambling_winnings` does not separate them, so all of it counts (test 12(o)). Not counted: capital gains (plan 1.9 is silent) and the plan 1.9 items with no input (cash gifts over $50, jury duty, legal settlements, other insurance payments to the insured, mortgage or sales-contract payments, foster and adoption care payments, royalties). WIA, work-study and commission income count as wages.
16. **Rules without inputs (not modeled).** The subsidized-housing allowance test (“greater than or equal to” in the policy, “exceeds” in plan 2.3), the Tribal first-apply rule (VI.A.5), the bar on costs paid by another program (VI.A.7), the SUAP $640 at recertification (pages 5, 19, 34), obligation-to-pay verification and the $5.00 vendor minimum.
17. **Years, editions and dates.** The worksheet is dated October 12, 2024 (its PDF title says SFY25), yet it is the matrix the Clearinghouse posted for FY2026, and revision 16A Appendix B reprints it. Revision 14 was never captured. Revision 16A adopts the FY27 limits on July 1, 2026, inside FY2026; annual periods read 1 January, so period 2026 uses the FY2026 limits all year. A monthly encoding would need 2025-08-25 (revision 13), 2026-03-23 (revision 15) and 2026-07-01 (revision 16A). Period 2027 assumes revision 16A stays in force through calendar 2027; the live policy was still revision 16A on 2026-10-23.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-az-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-az-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml) (revision 16A; period 2027 limits and the matrix)
- [us-az-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-az-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml) (FY2027 SMI table and 2026 guidelines; test 14(c))
- [program-bundles/liheap.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/program-bundles/liheap.yaml) (fiscal year 2027 scope; see Why queued)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-az/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover companion tests 1 to 15, keeping the revision 16A limits for period 2027 only if that period stays in scope. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable Standard-benefit program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: Encode New Hampshire's adult category financial assistance (OAA, ANB, APTD): He-W 600 grant, SPA NH-26-0001 and SR 26-01 standards, 8 U.S.C. 1622(b) (PE-US PR 10156)

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Encoding debt

New Hampshire's optional state supplement is its state-administered adult category financial assistance: Old Age Assistance (OAA), Aid to the Needy Blind (ANB) and Aid to the Permanently and Totally Disabled (APTD), under RSA 167:6 and He-W 600. The grant is the standard of need minus the assistance group's (AG's) net income. The federal SSI payment counts as unearned income (He-W 654.04(c)), so the state pays the whole difference, including to people who get no SSI. The program has no RuleSpec module.

On `rulespec-us` `main` (`172bf04e4`, 2026-10-14), `us-nh/` holds only `policies/cms/`, `policies/income_tax/` and `regulations/he-w-700/` (SNAP): no He-W 600 module and no `us-nh/statutes/`. `us/statutes/8/` holds `1612/b/2/G`, `1613`, `1641` and `1641/b` (output `qualified_alien`), but nothing for 8 U.S.C. 1621, 1622 or 1645. The shared module `us/policies/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/2026/federally-administered-optional-supplement-common.yaml` holds the 2026 FBRs the standard of need is built from (`federal_code_a_individual_fbr` 994.00, `federal_code_a_couple_fbr` 1,491.00).

Issue searches (among them "New Hampshire SSP", "New Hampshire supplement", "He-W 600", "He-W 658", "Old Age Assistance", "APTD", "RSA 167", "NH-26-0001", "nh_ssp" and "us-nh") find no issue for this program, and no issue has "New Hampshire" in its title. Related `pe-parity` issues: SSPs #1450, #1708, #1709, #1766 and #1767; adult assistance #1716, #1717, #1720, #1721, #1722 and #1727 (CO), #1519 (IL) and #1735 (MN).

PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10156 (open) adds the program as `nh_ssp`, verified for 2026, without medical assistance:

- **Variables** (Person, month unless noted) under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/nh/dhhs/ssp/`: `nh_ssp_eligible`, `nh_ssp_assistance_group_size`, `nh_ssp_countable_income`, `nh_ssp`, `nh_ssp_living_arrangement` (`INDEPENDENT` by default, `SUBSIDIZED_COMMUNITY_RESIDENCE`, `NONSUBSIDIZED_COMMUNITY_RESIDENCE`, `ENHANCED_FAMILY_CARE`, `RESIDENTIAL_CARE`; `NONE` for an SSI medical treatment facility), `nh_ssp_disability_eligible` (year), `nh_ssp_resources_deemed_from_parents`, `nh_ssp_employment_expenses` and `nh_ssp_other_income_deductions`; inputs `nh_ssp_has_essential_person`, `nh_ssp_essential_person_countable_income`, `nh_ssp_essential_person_resources` and `nh_ssp_grant_reduction_applies`. The helper `_nh_ssp_couple.py` puts spouses in one AG only when both live independently.
- **Parameters** under `gov.states.nh.dhhs.ssp`, dated 2026-01-01 unless noted: `minimum_payment_level.one_person` by arrangement (in the order above 27, 89, 149, 207, 207; `NONE` 0) and `.two_person` (21), both dated 1998-01-01; `three_person_need` 1,976; `standard_disregard` by AG size (13, 20, 25); `earned.*`, `resource_limit`, `minimum_payment`, `grant_reduction_fraction`, `disabled_minimum_age`; `immigration.waiting_period` 5, `.exempt_statuses` (refugee, asylee, Cuban/Haitian entrant, deportation withheld) and `.permanent_resident_qualifying_quarters` 40.
- **Tests** under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/nh/dhhs/ssp/`: `nh_ssp.yaml` (61 cases), `integration.yaml` (10), `nh_ssp_assistance_group_size.yaml` (6) and `nh_ssp_resources_deemed_from_parents.yaml` (3).

## Module paths and corpus citations
