| `us/statutes/8/1622.yaml` (subsection (b)), importing `us:statutes/8/1641/b#qualified_alien` | Exceptions making qualified aliens eligible for State public benefits; co-cite 1621(c)(1)(B) and 1645 | 1645: `us/statute/8/1645` | 1645: lock `.axiom/corpus-locks/us/statute/2026-10-12-w7-federal-usc-closure-title-8.json`. 1621 and 1622: in no manifest or lock on `main` that I found; need ingest: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2024-title8/html/USCODE-2024-title8-chap14-subchapII-sec1622.htm and the same URL ending `sec1621.htm` |

> I. For the purposes hereof, a person shall be eligible for old age assistance who is 65 years of age and a resident of this state. No person shall be eligible to receive such aid while receiving aid to the needy blind, aid to the permanently and totally disabled, or aid to families with dependent children.

> IV. For the purposes hereof a person shall be eligible for aid to needy blind who has no vision or whose vision with correcting glasses is so defective as to prevent the performance of ordinary activities for which eyesight is essential and is a resident of the state.

From VI (its first three sentences):

> VI. For the purposes hereof, a person shall be eligible for aid to the permanently and totally disabled who is between the ages of 18 and 64 years of age inclusive; is a resident of the state; and is disabled as defined in the federal Social Security Act, Titles II and XVI and the regulations adopted under such act, except that the minimum required duration of the impairment shall be 48 months, unless and until the department adopts a 12-month standard in accordance with RSA 167:3-j. In determining disability, the standards for "substantial gainful activity" as used in the Social Security Act shall apply, including all work incentive provisions including Impairment Related Work Expenses, Plans to Achieve Self Support, and subsidies. Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, eligibility for state cash assistance and medical assistance shall be conditioned upon the person filing an application or applications for any federal cash benefits for which the individual may be entitled and pursuing all appeals available for those federal cash benefits.

X(a):

> X. (a) For purposes hereof, an individual is ineligible for cash assistance benefits under the aid to the needy blind, aid to the permanently and totally disabled, and old age assistance programs for any month during which he or she is:
> (1) Fleeing to avoid prosecution for a crime which is a felony under the laws of the place from which the individual flees, or which, in the case of the state of New Jersey, is a high misdemeanor under the laws of that state; or
> (2) Fleeing to avoid custody or confinement after conviction for a crime, or an attempt to commit a crime, which is a felony under the laws of the place from which the individual flees, or which, in the case of the state of New Jersey, is a high misdemeanor under the laws of that state; or
> (3) Violating any condition of probation or parole imposed under federal or state law.

**8 U.S.C. 1621, 1622 and 1613** (United States Code, 2024 edition, from GovInfo: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2024-title8/html/USCODE-2024-title8-chap14-subchapII-sec1622.htm). The edition's notes list no amendment to 1621 or 1622 after 1998.

1621(c)(1)(B):

> (1) Except as provided in paragraphs (2) and (3), for purposes of this subchapter the term "State or local public benefit" means—

> (B) any retirement, welfare, health, disability, public or assisted housing, postsecondary education, food assistance, unemployment benefit, or any other similar benefit for which payments or assistance are provided to an individual, household, or family eligibility unit by an agency of a State or local government or by appropriated funds of a State or local government.

1622(a) and (b)(1) to (3) (footnote markers omitted; the edition's note says 1612(a)(2)(A)(i)(V) was redesignated 1612(a)(2)(A)(v)):

> Notwithstanding any other provision of law and except as provided in subsection (b), a State is authorized to determine the eligibility for any State public benefits of an alien who is a qualified alien (as defined in section 1641 of this title), a nonimmigrant under the Immigration and Nationality Act [8 U.S.C. 1101 et seq.], or an alien who is paroled into the United States under section 212(d)(5) of such Act [8 U.S.C. 1182(d)(5)] for less than one year.

> Qualified aliens under this subsection shall be eligible for any State public benefits.

> (1) Time-limited exception for refugees and asylees
> (A) An alien who is admitted to the United States as a refugee under section 207 of the Immigration and Nationality Act [8 U.S.C. 1157] until 5 years after the date of an alien's entry into the United States.
> (B) An alien who is granted asylum under section 208 of such Act [8 U.S.C. 1158] until 5 years after the date of such grant of asylum.
> (C) An alien whose deportation is being withheld under section 243(h) of such Act [8 U.S.C. 1253] (as in effect immediately before the effective date of section 307 of division C of Public Law 104–208) or section 241(b)(3) of such Act [8 U.S.C. 1231(b)(3)] (as amended by section 305(a) of division C of Public Law 104–208) until 5 years after such withholding.
> (D) An alien who is a Cuban and Haitian entrant as defined in section 501(e) of the Refugee Education Assistance Act of 1980 until 5 years after the alien is granted such status.
> (E) An alien admitted to the United States as an Amerasian immigrant as described in section 1612(a)(2)(A)(i)(V) of this title.

> (2) Certain permanent resident aliens
> An alien who—
> (A) is lawfully admitted to the United States for permanent residence under the Immigration and Nationality Act [8 U.S.C. 1101 et seq.]; and
> (B)(i) has worked 40 qualifying quarters of coverage as defined under title II of the Social Security Act [42 U.S.C. 401 et seq.] or can be credited with such qualifying quarters as provided under section 1645 of this title, and (ii) in the case of any such qualifying quarter creditable for any period beginning after December 31, 1996, did not receive any Federal means-tested public benefit (as provided under section 1613 of this title) during any such period.

> (3) Veteran and active duty exception
> An alien who is lawfully residing in any State and is—
> (A) a veteran (as defined in section 101, 1101, or 1301, or as described in section 107 of title 38) with a discharge characterized as an honorable discharge and not on account of alienage and who fulfills the minimum active-duty service requirements of section 5303A(d) of title 38,
> (B) on active duty (other than active duty for training) in the Armed Forces of the United States, or
> (C) the spouse or unmarried dependent child of an individual described in subparagraph (A) or (B) or the unremarried surviving spouse of an individual described in clause (i) or (ii) who is deceased if the marriage fulfills the requirements of section 1304 of title 38.

1613(a), which governs federal SSI and not the state grant:

> Notwithstanding any other provision of law and except as provided in subsections (b), (c), and (d), an alien who is a qualified alien (as defined in section 1641 of this title) and who enters the United States on or after August 22, 1996, is not eligible for any Federal means-tested public benefit for a period of 5 years beginning on the date of the alien's entry into the United States with a status within the meaning of the term "qualified alien".

## Interpretations and gaps

- **8 U.S.C. 1622(b)(2) against AAM 305.13.** AAM 305.13 keeps "lawfully admitted permanent residents regardless of work history" out for 5 years; He-W 616.02(a) has the same wait, and AAM 305.11 lists the other 1622(b) classes but not (b)(2). PolicyEngine-US follows 1622(b)(2): 1622(a) lets a State set eligibility only "except as provided in subsection (b)", under which those aliens "shall be eligible for any State public benefits", and the grant is a State-funded welfare benefit under 1621(c)(1)(B) (SPA C.1: "Solely by the state"). Encode 1622(b) as an override of 616.02(a) and record AAM 305.13 as conflicting guidance, with 8 U.S.C. 1624 as its possible basis (see the conflicts comment), as `nh_ssp_eligible` does.
- **Federal SSI during the wait.** 1613(a) still bars SSI for 5 years (POMS SI 00502.100 A.3.b, B), so the grant is the whole standard minus other income (Case H). PolicyEngine-US's `is_ssi_qualified_noncitizen` ignores 1613(a), so `nh_ssp.yaml` Case 51 supplies `ssi` of 0; otherwise it would pay SSI of $994 and a $27 grant. That federal issue is outside PR 10156.
- **Entry dates and other classes.** He-W 616.02 treats entry "before August 22, 1996" as unrestricted, AAM 305.13 "on or before 8/22/96"; PolicyEngine-US counts years since entry (`nh_ssp.yaml` Case 48: exactly 5 is eligible). Cite AAM 305.11 for COFA migrants, Native Americans and trafficking victims. PolicyEngine-US has no `immigration_status` value for them or Amerasians and doesn't read `is_veteran` or `is_military`, so a 1622(b)(3) veteran permanent resident within 5 years gets $0.
- **Standard of need.** No rule prints the minimum supplemental payment levels that He-W 658.03(e) and 648.04(b) add; SR 26-01 gives them by subtraction (1,008 − 994 + 13 = 27; 1,492 − 1,491 + 20 = 21), taking no 658.03(e)(1) excluded increase, as PolicyEngine-US does; POMS SI 02001.020 A.2.a lets a State "maintain supplementary payment levels". SSA's *State Assistance Programs for SSI Recipients* prints the same amounts for January 1998 (https://www.ssa.gov/policy/docs/progdesc/ssi_st_asst/1998/nh.pdf#page=3) and 2011, and DHHS's January releases fit them from 1998 (SR 97-44) to 2026 (against the FBRs DHHS printed); I didn't check these against the corpus. AG 2 uses the couple FBR, which SR 26-01 calls the maximum "for an individual and either a spouse or needy essential person". AG 3 is DHHS's stated maximum for "a couple and needy essential person" − 12; DHHS states $1,988 for 2026 where POMS gives 1,491 + 498 = 1,989, so encode the published $1,976 and update it each January. He-W 648.04(a) names "Family residences", not enhanced family care; I assume it is one. `nh_ssp.yaml` Cases 52 to 54 check that 2027 grants to SSI-only recipients stay $27, $207 (residential care) and $21 (couple).
- **Minimum grant and the reduction.** 670.03(a)(4) sets the $2 minimum "after rounding", and (c) reduces "The adult category grant pursuant to (a) above"; neither says whether the minimum or rounding applies again. AAM 617 orders rounding, minimum, reduction. PolicyEngine-US applies the minimum first and rounds again, half up: $2 pays $1, $358 pays $239 (`nh_ssp.yaml` Case 46). Case F avoids both questions.
- **The reduction's SNAP condition.** 670.03(c)(1)c. requires that the person "Does not receive" SNAP; AAM 617.03 also exempts "Individuals who are either receiving SNAP benefits or included in a SNAP household", and "ANB cases in which parental income and resources have been deemed to the case". SNAP counts the grant, so PolicyEngine-US keeps the reduction as an input. Under the separate federal one-third reduction, SSI is $662.67 and the grant $358 (`nh_ssp.yaml` Case 45).
- **APTD and He-W 652.07.** AAM 209 requires an impairment that "can be expected to last for a continuous period of not less than 48 months". PolicyEngine-US's duration proxy, `is_permanently_and_totally_disabled`, defaults to false, so microsimulation pays APTD only where the data set it. `takes_up_ssi_if_eligible` stands in for the SSI application (`nh_ssp.yaml` Case 22); Title II and the other applications have no input. An SSI denial for excess income or the 1613(a) bar isn't a refusal or failure under 652.07(f) (Cases E and H).
- **Essential persons.** AAM 227 adds that the person must not meet "the categorical requirements for OAA, ANB, or APTD", and that the applicant chooses whether to include them; their earnings get the 654.15(f) disregard, and their unearned income (654.02(d)(3)) and resources (AAM 403) count. PolicyEngine-US takes their countable income and resources as inputs, in independent living only. He-W 652.03(e) also compares the group-size standard with available income to deem income; decide whether that adds anything to the 654.02 budget.
- **Wages.** He-W 654.02(c)(1) counts "countable gross earned income, as defined in He-W 601.04(m)-(n)", and 601.04(m) takes wages "prior to payroll deductions". POMS SI 00820.102 C.2 treats a cafeteria-plan salary reduction as "not the employee's wages", but no He-W 600 rule or AAM 511 entry excludes one, and 654.18(c)(6) allows a payroll deduction as an OAA or APTD employment expense only if it "is not elective". So PolicyEngine-US keeps pre-tax health premiums in the state wage count for the applicant, an applicant spouse and a nonapplicant spouse, while federal SSI, an input here, keeps SSA's exclusion. Pinned by `nh_ssp.yaml` "Case 60, pre-tax health premiums still count as New Hampshire wages." (case M: net income 1,031, $0) and "Case 61, a nonapplicant spouse's pre-tax health premiums still count as New Hampshire wages." ([0, 0]); with the premiums netted out they give $27 and [21, 0]. The blind-child path reuses federal parental deeming, so the parents' wages there are net of these premiums; 652.03(f)(2) uses "combined earned income, as defined in He-W 601.03(k)", which names no exclusion.
- **Blind children.** PolicyEngine-US reuses `ssi_unearned_income_deemed_from_ineligible_parent` for 652.03(f)-(g) (`integration.yaml` Case 10). 652.03(j) cites "He-W 656.06(c)", which doesn't exist; the limit is 656.06(b). AAM 615.01 says that with several eligible ANB children "the parental ADI is divided equally", states no division for resources (PolicyEngine-US gives each child the full excess, `nh_ssp.yaml` Case 36), and skips deeming when the parents get FANF or SSP. The month after the 18th birthday (652.03(q)) needs an override input.
- **Couples.** The rules don't say how the AG grant is issued; PolicyEngine-US splits it between applicant spouses (`nh_ssp.yaml` Cases 41, 49 and 50 test couples under 670.03(c), 654.15(d)-(e) and 654.02(e)).
- **Other gaps.** An SSI medical treatment facility maps to `NONE` (`nh_ssp.yaml` Case 42); AAM 601 Table A gives nursing facilities "N/A" and treats "licensed but uncertified facilities" as independent living. PolicyEngine-US excludes incarcerated people (Case 43), though no adult-category inmate exclusion was found in He-W 600 or RSA 167:6. 654.02(d)(2) cites a nonexistent "He-W 654.15(h)" (the disregard is (f)); 654.02(e)(2) cites 654.15(c) and (d) for the ANB disregard in (b) and (c). The encoding can start at 2026-01-01.

labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Parity context

PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9916 fixes Los Angeles County General Relief (GR) in PolicyEngine. The model counted the SPM unit's CalWORKs grant once per member: a $150/month grant in a three-person unit was budgeted as $450, which put an applicant over the $221 single-applicant net income limit. The PR counts the grant once. It does not change which people or sources count.

The written DPSS manual counts different people:

- **Who counts.** GR counts the income of the **GR household**: the participant, their spouse or registered domestic partner, and eligible GR family members at the same address. Anyone receiving State or Federal public assistance is excluded (44-203). Adult children, other relatives and unrelated adults are aided on separate cases (44-203). A legally married, non-aided spouse's income counts above the spouse's needs per the GR Basic Budget table (44-101; 43-100).
- **Public assistance.** None of the income of a person in the home who receives public assistance (SSI/SSP, CAPI, CalWORKs) counts (44-101). That covers all of that person's income, not only the grant.
- **Social Security.** Social Security (RSDHI) is not public assistance in these sections. 44-101 and 43-100 list SSI/SSP and RSDHI as available income that the applicant/participant must claim.

PolicyEngine instead sums every SPM unit member's `veterans_benefits`, `unemployment_compensation`, `ca_state_disability_insurance`, `irs_employment_income`, `self_employment_income`, `sstb_self_employment_income`, `ssi` and `social_security`, plus the unit's `tanf`. `tanf`, `ssi` and `social_security` were added on informal DPSS advice (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#4114, #4123). Whether PolicyEngine moves to the GR household is queued as Max's decision d1027.

Axiom should encode the written rule. In both PolicyEngine test households (T1 and T2 below), eligibility and the grant come out the same under both readings. Only the intermediate countable income differs.

## Encoding debt

Nothing in rulespec-us encodes Los Angeles County GR. On `main` `f468c8dae`, no path matches `general.?relief`, `los.?angeles` or `dpss`. `us-ca/` has only `policies/{cdss,cms,dor,income_tax}`, `regulations/{cdss,mpp}` and `statutes/{rtc,wic}`. Issue searches for "general relief" and "Los Angeles" across TheAxiomFoundation found nothing.

**Blocker:** the sources are not in the corpus. TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus#784 asks to ingest them. Until it lands and the toolchain is re-pinned, the signed encoder has no citation to bind.

## Sources (verbatim from the 2026-10-06 snapshots; glyphs as published)

**DPSS ePolicy GR 44-101 Income**, release 11/06/2017 (https://my.dpss.lacounty.gov/public/en/home/epolicy/program/gr/income/income.html). Policy:

> After approval, all net income to the General Relief (GR) household is deducted from the GR grant.
> All income of a legally married, non-aided spouse with whom the GR participant is living, in excess of the spouse’s needs per the GR Basic Budget table, is considered income to the GR household.
> If any person in the home receives State or Federal public assistance, (e.g., SSI/SSP, CAPI, CalWORKs) none of the income of the public assistance recipient is considered available to meet the needs of the GR household.

> Income is available if the applicant/participant only has to apply for, claim, or accept the income to obtain it.
> Examples of available income are:
> Relative’s offer of a contribution;
> Unemployment Insurance Benefits (UIB)/Disability Insurance Benefits (DIB); and
> Supplemental Security Income (SSI)/State Supplemental Program (SSP) or Retirement Survivors Disability and Health Insurance (RSDHI) benefits, including benefits available by appealing SSI/SSP discontinuances and denials.
> The entire GR household is ineligible if any member of that household refuses to accept or apply for available income.

Definitions:

> Net Income
> Net income is the amount remaining after deducting allowable expenses from gross income.

> Earned Income Disregards
> Earned Income Disregards (EID) is the sliding scale amount of an applicant/participant’s earning that is disregarded in calculating the earnings to be deducted from the grant.

**DPSS ePolicy GR 44-203 Household Composition and Living Arrangement**, release 03/19/2019 (https://my.dpss.lacounty.gov/public/en/home/epolicy/program/gr/emergency-aid/household-composition-and-living-arrangement.html):

> GR Household
> The GR household is composed of the participant, their spouse or registered domestic partner, and any eligible GR family members living at the same address, excluding those receiving State or Federal public assistance.

> The following individuals may be aided on the same case:
> Legal spouses;
> Registered domestic partners;
> Sponsored Alien Families; and
> GR eligible families, including the parents, and 18-year-old children attending high school or trade/technical school full-time who expect to complete the school program before their 19th birthday.
> Note:
> Supplemental Security Income (SSI) recipients are not aided in the case as those individuals listed above.
> The following individuals are aided on separate cases:
> Adult children;
> Relatives who do not meet the above description of individuals aided on the same case; and
> Non-related adults.

> All GR households exclude those receiving State or Federal public assistance.

**DPSS ePolicy GR 43-100 Responsible Relatives for General Relief**, release 02/06/2023 (https://my.dpss.lacounty.gov/public/en/home/epolicy/program/gr/responsible-relatives/responsible-relatives-for-general-relief.html):

> In GR family cases, the public assistance income of any other family member is not considered available to meet the needs of the GR family.

> When an individual resides with a spouse, that spouse is also required to apply for GR unless the spouse receives SSI/SSP, Cash Assistance to Immigrants, or CalWORKs.

> All GR household members are responsible for providing information necessary for income determination and for taking necessary action to obtain available income. All income of a legally married, non-aided spouse with whom the GR participant is living, more than the spouse’s needs per the GR Basic Budget table, is considered available income.

**DPSS ePolicy GR 44-301 Aid Payments**, release 11/01/2017, Basic Budget Table, Maximum GR Grant column: household size 1 is $221, 2 is $375, 3 is $450, and so on up to 10 or more at $951.

**ABP 392, General Relief Information Sheet.** Two copies agree on every figure below:

- rev. 10/2019, inside the DPSS intake packet https://file.lacounty.gov/SDSInter/dpss/1147883_intake-packet-calfresh-gr-english.pdf (sha256 `3f38fb3f8fc407463932ccbee7dd06afa27fcb6fb943be59f4c51d8c09aa8e7d`);
- rev. 07/2021, the Google Drive copy PolicyEngine cites (sha256 `01391df6e05eebf573e76db159ab30d4dda2b634ad49c265a06e2cd7788d77b2`).

Page 1, Eligibility, item 3 (rev. 07/2021):

> 3. Your monthly net income* is less than:
> o For 1-person: $221.
> o For 2-people who apply together: $375.
> * Net income is any income you earn after all state and federal deductions and includes:
> • Income from a job of any type.
> • Unemployment Insurance Benefits (UIB).
> • State Disability Insurance (SDI).
> • Veteran’s benefits.

Page 3, Income and savings, item 1:

> 1. You may continue to receive GR if your monthly net income (without your GR grant) is less than:
> o For 1-person: $621 per month.
> Note: If your monthly income is between $201 and $620, the amount of your grant will be lower than $221/month.

## Module path and oracle coverage

The module path follows the citations axiom-corpus#784 assigns. Agency manuals elsewhere use the `manual` class, for example `us-nc/manual/dhhs/fns/...` encoded at `us-nc/policies/...`. So 44-101 at `us-ca/manual/la-county-dpss/gr/44-101-income` would be encoded at `us-ca/policies/la-county-dpss/gr/44-101-income.yaml`. If the corpus maintainers choose a different jurisdiction or class, use theirs.

Oracle coverage needs no `oracle-coverage-pending` declaration. axiom-oracles `axiom_oracles/bridges/mappings/us.yaml` (`main` `d3419010d`) maps the `us-ca:` prefix as `not_comparable`. Exact mappings to PolicyEngine's `la_general_relief_net_income` and `la_general_relief_net_income_eligible` are optional follow-up work in axiom-oracles.

## `review_finding` (paste into the signed dispatch)

> Encode Los Angeles County DPSS General Relief countable net income and the net income tests. Corpus citations: CORPUS_CITATIONS, covering ePolicy GR 44-101, 44-203, 43-100 and 44-301, and ABP 392 pages 1 and 3. Module at MODULE_PATH. No rulespec-us module covers LA County GR today. Use effective_from 2019-10-01. That is the month of ABP 392 rev. 10/2019, the earliest revision found; the sheet states no effective date, and rev. 07/2021 has the same amounts. Whether the amounts are still current after 2021 is unverified. All amounts are monthly.
>
> Entity: each person in the home of the GR applicant/participant. Leaf inputs per person:
> - `is_gr_household_member`: the applicant/participant, their spouse or registered domestic partner, or an eligible GR family member at the same address (44-203). Adult children, other relatives and non-related adults are not members (44-203).
> - `is_non_aided_spouse`: a legally married spouse living with the participant who is not aided on the GR case.
> - `receives_public_assistance`: receives State or Federal public assistance, for example SSI/SSP, CAPI or CalWORKs.
> - `net_income`: income after all state and federal deductions, before EID.
> - `spouse_needs`: for a non-aided spouse, the spouse's needs per the GR Basic Budget table. Keep this a leaf input. Which Basic Budget row applies is not stated. 43-100's separate Responsible Relative Need Scale (MBSAC) governs support liability, not this clause; record that as an open point.
>
> Required outputs, each with verbatim proof excerpts from the corpus provisions:
>
> 1. `gr_household_countable_net_income` (Money). The sum over persons in the home of:
>    - `net_income` if `is_gr_household_member` and not `receives_public_assistance`;
>    - max(0, `net_income` − `spouse_needs`) if `is_non_aided_spouse` and not `receives_public_assistance`;
>    - 0 otherwise.
>
>    A public assistance recipient contributes 0, including all their non-assistance income (44-101: "none of the income of the public assistance recipient"; 44-203: "excluding those receiving State or Federal public assistance").
> 2. `gr_applicant_net_income_eligible` (Judgment). `gr_household_countable_net_income` < 221 for one person, and < 375 for two people who apply together (ABP 392 p. 1). The comparison is strict ("less than"). For three or more people, ABP 392 gives no applicant limit, so make that a deferred dependency rather than inferring it from the 44-301 table.
> 3. `gr_recipient_net_income_eligible` (Judgment). Countable net income without the GR grant < 621 for one person (ABP 392 p. 3), strict. ABP 392 gives no two-person recipient limit, so make that a deferred dependency.
>
> Do not encode the grant amount. Under 44-101, net income is deducted from the grant after approval, with earnings first reduced by the EID sliding scale. That scale is not in this source set; it was not found in the GR ePolicy income, household and aid-payment sections. ABP 392 p. 3 says only that income between $201 and $620 lowers the grant. Make the grant a deferred dependency on the EID table, and the $201–$620 note an open point. Do not adopt PolicyEngine's linear $201–$620 phase-out (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#3269); that is an engine placeholder, not a source formula.
>
> Open points, with no output: an applicant/participant who personally receives public assistance (ABP 392 p. 1: GR "is for people who do not qualify for other State or federal cash assistance programs"; 40-106.5), and the `spouse_needs` row.

## Companion tests

Every expected value is hand-computed from the quoted text. None comes from an engine. Period 2026-01, monthly amounts, the applicant is "A", and unlisted amounts are 0. Unless a test says otherwise, A is the only GR household member and nobody receives public assistance. T1 and T2 are the two PolicyEngine households from PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9916 (`integration.yaml`).

| # | Case | Countable | Limit | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | A has no income. A's sister B and B's child C live with A and receive CalWORKs of $150. | 0. B and C are not GR household members (44-203: relatives on separate cases), and they receive public assistance. | 221 | applicant: holds |
| T2 | A is a continuing recipient with no income. Another adult in the home receives CalWORKs of $200. | 0 | 621 | recipient: holds |
| T3 | A has UIB of $220. | 220 | 221 | holds |
| T4 | A has UIB of $221. | 221 | 221 | not_holds (strict) |
| T5 | A has no income. A's mother lives with A and receives SSI/SSP of $1,100. | 0 | 221 | holds |
| T6a | A and A's spouse apply together, with combined net wages of $374. | 374 | 375 | holds |
| T6b | The same couple, with combined net wages of $375. | 375 | 375 | not_holds |
| T7a | Recipient A has veterans' benefits of $620. | 620 | 621 | holds |
| T7b | Recipient A has veterans' benefits of $621. | 621 | 621 | not_holds |
| T8 | A has SDI of $100. B in the home receives CalWORKs and has wages of $500. | 100 | 221 | holds |
| T9a | A has no income. A's non-aided spouse has net income of $521 and `spouse_needs` of $221, and no public assistance. | 300 | 221 | not_holds |
| T9b | The same as T9a, but the spouse receives SSI/SSP. | 0 | 221 | holds |
| T10 | A receives RSDHI of $500. RSDHI is available income and not public assistance. | 500 | 221 | not_holds |
| T11 | A has no income. A non-related adult roommate has wages of $500 and no public assistance. | 0 (44-203: non-related adults are on separate cases) | 221 | holds |

T9b fails if the public-assistance exclusion is left off the spouse clause. T8 and T5 fail if a recipient's income is counted. T11 fails if non-members' income is counted.

**Known divergence from PolicyEngine,** pending decision d1027. PolicyEngine counts every SPM unit member's income, with `tanf` once per unit after PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9916. Where the other people in the home share A's SPM unit:

- T1: PolicyEngine counts $150 instead of $0. Eligibility and the grant are the same.
- T2: PolicyEngine counts $200 instead of $0. Eligibility and the grant are the same.
- T5: PolicyEngine counts the mother's SSI and denies A.
- T8: PolicyEngine counts B's wages and CalWORKs and denies A.
- T11: PolicyEngine counts the roommate's wages and denies A.
- T9a/T9b: PolicyEngine counts all of the spouse's income, with no needs offset and no public-assistance exclusion.

These companion tests follow the written rule.

**Properties to pin for every input:**

- Countable income does not depend on any income of a person flagged `receives_public_assistance`.
- Countable income does not depend on the income of a person who is neither a GR household member nor a non-aided spouse.
- Countable income is non-decreasing in each counted person's `net_income`, and non-increasing in `spouse_needs`.
- The eligibility judgments are monotone: raising countable income never turns not_holds into holds.

## Related

- PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9916 (this fix).
- PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#4123: the SSI/Social Security/TANF source. 44-101's available-income passage is a primary source for the applicant's own SSI/SSP and RSDHI, but not for TANF.
- PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#3269: the phase-out formula.
- TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus#784: source ingest, the blocker.
- Templates: #1403 and #1416.

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Arkansas LIHEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 2a, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9973 (branch `ar-liheap`), open, not merged; DTrim99 and PavelMakarchuk approved `e1b597400c` (2026-10-21). Head `55c4f217ac` (2026-10-21). The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

- **Sources missing from the corpus.** On axiom-corpus `main` (checked 2026-10-06, 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-19), Arkansas has three LIHEAP manifests: the FY2026 state plan, the FFY 2026 matrices and eligibility chart, and, since TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus#718 (merged 2026-10-12), the adopted 190-page FFY 2025 manual, which the branch now cites (interpretation 1). No manifest captures: the FY2025 state plan; the FFY 2025 chart and five matrices; application AEO-9495, forms R 01/FY2025 and R 11/2025 (work income, fuel groups); the 2024 and 2025 poverty guidelines; the FFY 2025 and FFY 2026 state median income tables; 45 CFR 96.85(b); and two corroborating pages. They need ingest.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence in the signed corpus release pinned by rulespec-us was not checked for any source, including the three manifests on `main`.
- **Billed encoder runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval. None has been requested for this program.
- **No merged PE revision.** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9973 is approved but not merged, so there is no revision to pin.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9973, open, not merged. Head `55c4f217ac` (comment wording, countable Case 29 tax units and main). Since the change requests at `f2a1172c0f`, high-school enrollment reads `is_in_secondary_school` or `is_in_k12_school`, the manual's full-time-student definition also excludes dependent high-school students up to age 23 (interpretation 3(c)), countable Case 27 becomes 18,300, and countable Cases 29-33 (companion test 13) and `ar_liheap.yaml` Case 20 (interpretation 9) are new. Everything below describes `55c4f217ac`.
- **Scope:** the winter Regular Assistance benefit (“Rate Reduction (Regular Assistance) Program”): Arkansas residence; at least one citizen or qualified noncitizen; household size counting only those members, with every member's income counted; monthly countable income (MCI) at or below the eligibility chart; an energy burden (a direct bill, heat in unsubsidized rent, or heat in subsidized rent with an excess energy charge); no asset test and no categorical eligibility; and the benefit read from one of five fuel matrices by MCI row (39 rows) and size column (“1&2”, “3&4”, “5 & UP”). Out of scope: Crisis Assistance, summer Regular Assistance on the electric matrix (cooling), Assurance 16, weatherization and its emergency HVAC services, disaster relief and additional-funding supplements, split or secondary-fuel benefit requests, and the proposed FY2027 plan.
- **Policy periods:** FFY 2025 and FFY 2026 (FFY N: October 1 of N-1 to September 30 of N). Every variable is annual and reads the value in force on 1 January, so period `2025` carries FFY 2025 and `2026` carries FFY 2026. At `2025-10-01` the matrices change 63 of 585 cells, `income_band` changes its top five lower bounds, `smi_max_size` goes from 6 to 7 and `additional_member_amount` from $672 to $688; everything else starts at `2024-10-01`. Federal inputs: the state median income in force on 1 January (`gov.hhs.smi.amount`) and the previous calendar year's poverty guideline (`fpg_year_lag` 1). Other periods are unverified estimates (interpretation 11).
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/ar/ee/aeo/liheap/`: `ar_liheap`, `ar_liheap_household_size`; `eligibility/ar_liheap_eligible`; `income/ar_liheap_countable_income`, `income/ar_liheap_income_limit`; `payment/ar_liheap_matrix_amount` (the ungated table amount). The limit reuses the federal `smi()` and `fpg()` helpers (`gov.hhs.smi`, `gov.hhs.fpg`), the latter with a year lag.
- **Parameters:** `gov.states.ar.ee.aeo.liheap` (`income/`: `earned_disregard` 0.2, `interest_disregard` $200 a month per member, `earned_minimum_age` 18 (earnings of younger members excluded), `full_time_student_age_limit` 23 (dependent full-time college and high-school students, inclusive), `high_school_student_age_limit` 18 (any high-school student), `sources/earned` (with `rental_income` and `farm_rent_income`), `sources/unearned` (with `total_unemployment_compensation`); `income/limit/`: `smi_rate` 0.6, `smi_max_size`, `fpg_rate` 1.5, `fpg_year_lag` 1, `max_table_size` 20, `additional_member_amount`, `rounding_increment` 1; `payment/`: `income_band` (39 lower bounds), `household_size_group` (1-2, 3-4, 5 and up), and five `matrix/` files keyed by band and size group). 21 files.
- **Tests:** 89 YAML cases in 7 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/ar/ee/aeo/liheap/`: `ar_liheap.yaml` 20, `ar_liheap_household_size.yaml` 2, `eligibility/ar_liheap_eligible.yaml` 7, `income/ar_liheap_countable_income.yaml` 33, `income/ar_liheap_income_limit.yaml` 4, `payment/ar_liheap_matrix_amount.yaml` 18 and `integration.yaml` 5. Below, eligible, countable, limit and matrix Case N name cases in the third to sixth files. Expected values are hand computations; tests were not run locally; CI validates them.

## Module paths and corpus citations

Manifest presence on axiom-corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-06, 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-19; signed-release presence was not checked. rulespec-us has `us-ar/policies/` (cms, dhs/tea, income_tax), no `us-ar/regulations/` or `us-ar/statutes/` tree, and no LIHEAP, poverty-guideline or state-median-income module on `main` (2026-10-06). Manifests cite `us-ar/policy/...`; the module paths follow the rulespec-us `us-ar/policies/` layout.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-ar/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-1` | 1.4 categorical eligibility answered No; 1.8 work income less 20%, non-work income gross; 1.9 countable income boxes, Social Security “Excluding MediCare deduction”, the lottery-only lump-sum note (pages 5 to 7) | `us-ar/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | In manifest `us-ar-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml` (segmented by “Section N” headings, expression date 2025-10-01). Official copy: [FY2026 state plan, pages 5-7 and 9-11](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/state-plans/AR_Plan_2026.pdf#page=5) (55 pages; the footer `Page N of 55` equals the PDF page). |
| `.../fy2026/section-2` | 2.1 60% of state median income for sizes 1 to 7, 150% of the HHS poverty guidelines for sizes 8 to 15; 2.3 no asset test, subsidized and unsubsidized heat in rent; energy-burden explanation; 2.5 benefit variables; 2.6 minimum $60, maximum $570 (pages 9 to 11) | same | In manifest. |
| `us-ar/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2025/section-1`, `.../section-2` | 1.8 and 1.9 (pages 5 to 7); 2.1 state median income for sizes 1 to 6, poverty guidelines for sizes 7 to 15, 2.3 renters (page 8); 2.6 minimum $50, maximum $475 (page 9) | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [FY2025 state plan, pages 5-9](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2025/state-plans/AR_Plan_2025.pdf#page=5) (51 pages). |
| `us-ar/policies/aeo/liheap-eligibility-chart/ffy2026` | Maximum monthly countable income for sizes 1 to 20, “ADD $688 FOR EACH ADDITIONAL HOUSEHOLD MEMBER”, heat-in-rent lease note | `us-ar/policy/aeo/liheap-benefit-matrix/ffy2026/eligibility-chart` | In manifest `us-ar-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml` (host `adeq.state.ar.us`; the branch cites `www.adeq.state.ar.us`). Official copy: [FFY 2026 eligibility chart](https://www.adeq.state.ar.us/energy/assistance/pdfs/LIHEAP_Eligibility-Chart_2026.pdf) (1 page). |
| `us-ar/policies/aeo/liheap-eligibility-chart/ffy2025` | Sizes 1 to 20, “ADD $672 FOR EACH ADDITIONAL HOUSEHOLD MEMBER” | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [FFY 2025 eligibility chart](https://www.adeq.state.ar.us/energy/assistance/pdfs/LIHEAP_Eligibility-Chart_2025.pdf) (1 page). |
| `us-ar/policies/aeo/liheap-benefit-matrix/ffy2026/electric`, `.../natural-gas`, `.../propane`, `.../fuel-oil`, `.../other-wood-pellets` | 39 MCI rows by three household-size columns per fuel; rows “0-69” to “1390-1449” on page 1, “1450-1509” to “5237-Max” on page 2 | `us-ar/policy/aeo/liheap-benefit-matrix/ffy2026/<fuel>` | In manifest `us-ar-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml` (`page_count: 2`; the corpus `page-N` suffix counts text-bearing pages only). The branch's PDFs match Wayback captures by SHA-1; the manifest records no hash. Official copies: [electric, pages 1-2](https://www.adeq.state.ar.us/energy/assistance/pdfs/LIHEAP_Benefit-Matix_2026_Electric.pdf#page=1), [natural gas, pages 1-2](https://www.adeq.state.ar.us/energy/assistance/pdfs/LIHEAP_Benefit-Matix_2026_Natural-Gas.pdf#page=1), [propane, pages 1-2](https://www.adeq.state.ar.us/energy/assistance/pdfs/LIHEAP_Benefit-Matix_2026_Propane.pdf#page=1), [fuel oil, pages 1-2](https://www.adeq.state.ar.us/energy/assistance/pdfs/LIHEAP_Benefit-Matix_2026_Fuel-Oil.pdf#page=1), [other, pages 1-2](https://www.adeq.state.ar.us/energy/assistance/pdfs/LIHEAP_Benefit-Matix_2026_Other-Wood-Pellets.pdf#page=1). |

## Required outputs

| Output | policyengine-us variable | Entity, period | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Household size | `ar_liheap_household_size` | SPM unit, year | Number of members with `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant` (citizens and the federal qualified-noncitizen statuses). Other members are not counted; their income still counts. |
| Countable income | `ar_liheap_countable_income` | SPM unit, year | 12 x round_half_up(A / 12), where A = 0.8 x (sum over counted workers of employment, self-employment, SSTB self-employment, farm operations, partnership or S corporation, rental and farm rent income, each floored at zero) + (sum over all members of `total_unemployment_compensation` (reported, else modeled state UI; Arkansas has none), strike benefits, SSI, pension income, `military_retirement_income`, survivor benefits, alimony, child support received, ordinary dividends, veterans' benefits, `financial_assistance`, workers' compensation, gambling winnings and capital gains, each floored at zero) + (per member, max(interest − 12 x $200, 0)) + (per member, max(max(Social Security, 0) + max(railroad benefits, 0) − `medicare_part_b_premium`, 0)) + `tanf` (take-up gated; includes `ar_tea`). A counted worker is a member aged 18 or older who is neither a tax-unit dependent (`is_tax_unit_dependent`) aged 23 or younger who is a full-time college student (`is_full_time_college_student`) or in high school (`is_in_secondary_school` or `is_in_k12_school`), nor a high-school student aged 18 or younger. |
| Income limit | `ar_liheap_income_limit` | SPM unit, year | 0 when the size is 0; otherwise 12 x (round_half_up(B) + max(size − 20, 0) x the per-member amount), where B = 0.6 x SMI(size) / 12 for sizes up to 6 (FFY 2025) or 7 (FFY 2026), and 1.5 x FPG(min(size, 20), previous calendar year) / 12 above; per-member amount $672 (FFY 2025) or $688 (FFY 2026). Reproduces every printed row of both charts. |
| Eligible | `ar_liheap_eligible` | SPM unit, year | Arkansas only: size > 0, countable income at or below the limit, `heating_type` not NONE, and a heating responsibility: with heat in rent, unsubsidized or `heating_expense` > 0; without heat in rent, `has_heating_expense` (default: a positive primary-fuel bill with heat not in rent; an explicit false is respected). Subsidized means `receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing`. |
| Matrix amount | `ar_liheap_matrix_amount` | SPM unit, year | Arkansas only, ungated: the cell for the fuel schedule (electric for ELECTRICITY; natural gas; propane; fuel oil for FUEL_OIL and KEROSENE; other for WOOD, COAL and OTHER), the MCI row (largest printed lower bound at or below MCI) and the size column (1&2, 3&4, 5 & UP). Zero for SOLAR, UNSPECIFIED, NONE and size 0. Not capped by the bill. |
| Benefit | `ar_liheap` | SPM unit, year | The matrix amount when eligible, else zero. |

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Manual (authority).** The branch cites the adopted 190-page FFY 2025 manual for both program years. No FY2026 manual was found. Earlier revisions cited the 167-page August 2024 draft; a word-level comparison (2026-10-19) of Appendix F and sections 4.4-4.4.1 and 4.7.3-4.9 found every encoded rule unchanged.
2. **Plan against manual, branch follows the manual (owner decision, 2026-10-06).** Workers' compensation: plan item 1.9 leaves “Insurance payments made directly to the insured” unchecked; manual pages 155 and 168 and the application count it. TEA: the plan leaves TANF unchecked; manual page 155 and the application count it. Capital gains and gambling: the plans count lottery winnings as the only one-time lump sum (page 7), and manual page 163 excludes nonrecurring lump sums, including the sale of personal property; Appendix F pages 157 and 160 count both, and the branch follows Appendix F. Dependent cases: countable Case 11 (military retirement $24,000, workers' compensation $15,600, gambling $1,200, capital gains $3,000: each in full), Cases 12 and 13 (TEA $2,448: 2,448 with take-up, 0 without), and `ar_liheap.yaml` Case 14 (five citizens with TEA $3,432: MCI 286, fuel oil “250-309”, “5 & UP”: $497). Loans: plan item 1.9 checks “Loans that need to be repaid”; manual page 163 excludes all loans, and the branch counts none.
3. **Plan or application against manual.** (a) and (b) follow the manual (owner decision, 2026-10-06); (c) follows the application read with the manual's definition (owner decisions, 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20).
   - (a) Interest. Plan item 1.9 (page 6) counts “Interest, dividends, or royalties” with no threshold; manual page 162 counts the “amount over $200.00”. Readings: the $200 is monthly (unearned income is the month's receipts, page 57; Appendix E, pages 154 to 155, converts other frequencies); only the excess counts; and it applies to each person, a chosen reading since the manual names no unit. Countable Case 17 (spouses with $2,400 of interest each and a $12,000 pension) gives 12,000; one household-wide $200 would give 12,000 + (4,800 − 2,400) = 14,400.
   - (b) Rental income. Plan item 1.8 (page 5) takes 20% off work income only and item 1.9 lists “Rental income” on its own; manual page 165 says “Ownership of rental property will be considered a self-employment enterprise.” `rental_income` and `farm_rent_income` are earned sources: 20% off, floored per source, subject to the worker exclusions. Farm rent is read as rental property (landlord rent), not farming. Page 166's extra 10% for operating costs is not applied to these net inputs (item 7).
   - (c) Minors and full-time students. The forms' “full-time student” is undefined, so the branch applies the manual's definition (page 141; Appendix F, page 159), reading “up to age 23” as inclusive, and section 4.7's high-school rule (page 56). It excludes the earnings of every member under 18 (`earned_minimum_age`; the forms' rule, wider than page 158's half-time attendance condition); of an `is_tax_unit_dependent` member aged 23 or younger (`full_time_student_age_limit`) who is an `is_full_time_college_student` or in high school (`is_in_secondary_school` or `is_in_k12_school`); and of any high-school student aged 18 or younger (`high_school_student_age_limit`). Their unearned income counts. Readings: a tax-unit dependent stands for a dependent of a household member (without supplied roles, age-ordered inference can make an adult student the spouse; countable Case 31 supplies them); the glossary's sentence on high-school students over 18, read within the definition's “up to age 23, who is a dependent” terms, places dependent ones among full-time students (countable Cases 27 and 30); `is_in_k12_school` is false by default from 18, so `is_in_secondary_school` carries older students (countable Case 29). The full-time-work and emancipation exceptions are not modeled.
4. **Half dollars (inferred tie rule).** “Round MONTHLY COUNTABLE INCOME (MCI) to the nearest whole dollar amount” (manual page 58) does not place $0.50; the branch rounds half up. `ar_liheap.yaml` Case 12 second household (pension $28,170: 2,347.50, rounded up to 2,348 > 2,347, not eligible, $0; half down would pay $68) and the second households of `ar_liheap.yaml` Case 13 and countable Case 15 (alimony $834: 834 / 12 = 69.50, rounded up to 70, row “70-129”) depend on it.
5. **Limit rounding and per-member amounts (inferred pattern).** No source states how the chart rounds. Half-up monthly rounding of 0.6 x median x size factor / 12 and 1.5 x guideline / 12 reproduces all 40 printed rows. The per-member amounts are stored as printed: 1.5 x 5,500 / 12 = 687.50 matches $688, but 1.5 x 5,380 / 12 = 672.50 would round to $673, not the printed $672. The plans list sizes 1 to 15 only; the charts run to 20 plus the per-member amount.
6. **Social Security (settled; Arkansas nets it).** Plan item 1.9 checks “Excluding MediCare deduction” in both years, manual section 4.7.2 excludes the Part B premium, and Appendix F lists “Medicare insurance premiums” as No. Two general statements point the other way: page 167 (“(Note: The gross amount is counted.)”) and page 58 (100% of award-letter income). The branch nets `medicare_part_b_premium` per member against Social Security plus railroad benefits, floored at zero; it is zero when not enrolled and excludes Medicare Savings Program coverage, which stands in for “not eligible for Medicaid”. Other medical deductions are not modeled.
7. **Self-employment (simplification).** The manual allows actual costs (page 62), a standard 10% (page 155), or 20% plus 10% from gross (page 166); the plan takes 20% off work income. The branch takes 20% off the existing net business inputs (rental included), each floored at zero; their expense netting stands in for the 10% allowance. Countable Case 5 (net business income $20,000): 16,000, MCI 1,333.33, rounded: 15,996; as gross under page 166: 14,004.
8. **Energy-burden inputs (conventions).** With subsidized heat in rent, a positive `heating_expense` is the excess energy charge. A direct bill counts through `has_heating_expense`; a caller sets it false when an allowance fully reimburses the bill (companion test 16). The reimbursement test itself (manual page 63) is not modeled. `has_heating_expense` set true without a positive bill counts as an obligation (eligible Case 3: true, false).
9. **Fuels (coverage).** `heating_type` is a required input. COAL reads the “OTHER (WOOD, PELLETS, ETC.)” schedule ($410 at size 5, income 0, matrix Case 8); coal is not named in the matrix, and the application offers “OTHER:”. SOLAR and UNSPECIFIED have no schedule and pay $0 (matrix Case 15; `ar_liheap.yaml` Case 20), also with heat in rent, because the amount depends on the fuel; PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the unspecified default. The grant uses the primary fuel's matrix.
10. **FY2025 benefit levels.** FY2025 plan item 2.6 estimates a $50 minimum and $475 maximum; the FFY 2025 matrices, headed “HOUSEHOLD SIZE BENEFIT PAYMENT (20% OVER BASE)”, print $60 to $570, and the branch follows them. The electric file (PDF metadata: October 7, 2024) is byte-identical to a [Wayback capture of December 6, 2024, page 1](https://web.archive.org/web/20241206194455id_/https://www.adeq.state.ar.us/energy/assistance/pdfs/liheap_benefit-matix_2025_electric.pdf#page=1), before the January 6, 2025 opening. 1.2 times the [Clearinghouse “2025” matrix, pages 1-5](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2025/benefits-matricies/AR_BenefitMatrix_2025.pdf#page=1) amounts (its 2024 base; electric “$ 0-69”: $202, $240, $287), rounded, gives the AEO FY2025 cells in the 35 rows whose lower bounds run from $0 to $2,250. The FFY 2025 “OTHER” row “5,140-Max” prints $0.00 in every column, so an eligible other-fuel household of six or more there gets $0 (matrix Case 14).
11. **Years (estimates).** `programs.yaml` lists no `verified_years`; its note says the income rules follow the FFY 2025 manual (no FY2026 manual) and other years are unverified. Earlier periods backfill FFY 2025 values: a one-person gas household with no income gets $308 in 2024; the Clearinghouse 2024 matrix pays $257. 2027 and later carry the FFY 2026 tables forward with the FFY 2027 median income and 2026 guideline (one-person limit $2,460). The [proposed FY2027 plan, page 11](https://www.adeq.state.ar.us/energy/assistance/pdfs/proposed-fy2027-liheap-model-plan.pdf#page=11) raises item 2.6's range to $70-$665; it has no published matrix or chart (2026-10-06) and is not encoded. The federal floor in 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B) (110% of poverty) never binds: every limit is at least 32% above it at every size in 2025-2027.
12. **Household and period (simplifications).** The SPM unit stands for the LIHEAP household (manual page 53); shared-meter rules (pages 55 to 56) are not derived. Annual inputs divided by 12 stand for the month before application (pages 56 to 57). One winter grant per program year.
13. **Yes rows without an input.** No input carries these Appendix F Yes rows, so none is counted: adoption assistance, cryptocurrency, crowd-fund accounts, executor fees, foster care payments, HUD utility payments (from $50 in Appendix E; the application's “Housing Utility Assistance Payment”), inheritance, jury duty pay, royalties and Trade Adjustment Assistance (pages 155-168, quoted above); nor is contract income (plan item 1.9). `financial_assistance` counts every reported gift, though Appendix F counts only regular gifts (three or more consecutive months) and excludes irregular ones (page 157). The irregular-income and odd-job exclusions are not modeled.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [FY2026 state-plan manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ar-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [FFY 2026 benefit-matrix and eligibility-chart manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ar-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml)
- [FFY 2025 policy manual manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ar-liheap-policy-manual-manual.yaml) (the manual the branch cites)
- [2026 federal annual figures manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml) (used only by carried-forward periods)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission. The sources listed as missing under Why queued need ingest before the modules above can be proved.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-ar/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the FFY 2025 and FFY 2026 income limits (median-income and poverty-guideline sizes, the per-member amounts above 20), MCI rounding at the limit and at row edges, every row and size column of the ten fuel matrices, the kerosene/wood/other fuel groups, heat in rent and subsidized housing, qualified-member household size with full income of other members, the 20% work-income deduction (rental included) and per-source loss floors, interest over $200 a month, the earnings exclusion for minors, dependent full-time college and high-school students to age 23 and 18-year-old high-school students, Social Security and railroad retirement net of Part B, TEA take-up, each listed unearned source (split dividends; unemployment through the reported-or-modeled total), and an explicit direct-obligation false. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: LIHEAP wave 1d: encode Minnesota EAP regular heating assistance

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Minnesota Energy Assistance Program (EAP) regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1d, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10433 (branch `mn-liheap-wave1d`), open, not merged. Head `8ef6ef80e5` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983`; this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **Sources missing from the corpus.** No axiom-corpus manifest on `main` holds the branch's main sources: the EAP Policy Manual FFY26 (program year October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026) and FFY27 (October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027), chapters 3 and 4, and the two editions of Appendix 4A, the Primary Heat Benefit Calculator workbook, which is the only published source of the pay-share constants and the backup matrix. `us-mn-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml` holds the FFY 2024 manual (expression date 2023-10-01), which describes the same benefit method and the same $200 and $1,400 limits, but whose income table rests on the FY2024 state median income and which carries no pay shares. Also missing: the FY2026 state median income table (LIHEAP IM 2025-02, Attachment 4), behind every FFY26 limit for sizes 1 to 18, and 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B), the 110% poverty floor behind sizes 19 and up. These need ingest. The FY2026 state plan, the 2025 and 2026 poverty guidelines and the FY2027 state median income table are captured. Minnesota's FY2027 plan was not posted at the Clearinghouse path on 2026-10-21 (HTTP 404).
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-23; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.
- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10433 opened on 2026-10-23 with no reviews yet, so there is no revision to pin.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10433, branch `mn-liheap-wave1d`, head `8ef6ef80e5` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983` and closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10423. A 2026-10-22 review (no critical findings) led to fixes on the same branch: Minnesota Paid Leave counts from FFY2026 (one source list dated 2025-10-01 instead of two), a comment on early retirement withdrawals was reworded as a documented limitation, five cases were removed (four that repeated other cases, with two pay-share assertions moved into `mn_eap.yaml` Cases 1 and 2, and the FFY2026 Paid Leave control case), and the retirement-age test now uses ages 59 and 59.5. Everything below describes the branch with those fixes; oracle fixtures will pin the merged commit.
- **Scope:** Minnesota EAP Primary Heat, the state's single regular benefit, for FFY2026 and FFY2027: Minnesota residence; household size from citizens and eligible non-citizens, with ineligible members' income counted; gross countable income against the one-month maximum (50% of state median income for sizes 1 to 18, 110% of the prior year's poverty guideline for sizes 19 and 20, and the federal floor above 20); vulnerability to energy costs (an energy bill, heat in unsubsidized rent, or heat in subsidized rent with an electric bill); annual energy cost from the household's bills for every fuel including non-heat electricity, or the backup matrix for heat in unsubsidized rent, or the electric bill for heat in subsidized rent; the Appendix 4A pay share, falling linearly with the income percentile; Qualified Eligibility; whole-dollar rounding, the $200 minimum and the $1,400 maximum. Out of scope: Crisis, Energy Related Repair (ERR), weatherization, Assurance 16 services, the application deadline, the one-grant-per-year rule, first-come first-served processing, payment routing, the eHEAT consumption rules described under interpretation 6, and Minnesota's FY2027 plan (not posted).
- **Policy periods:** two verified seasons, FFY2026 and FFY2027. Heating assistance runs October 1, 2025 to May 31, 2026 (plan item 1.1, page 4); the program year runs October 1 to September 30 (FFY26 manual page 72). Minnesota variables are annual and read 1 January values. Period `2026` is FFY2026: the 2025-10-01 parameter entries, Minnesota's FY2026 state median income ($143,998 for four, `gov.hhs.smi.amount` at 2025-10-01) and the 2025 HHS guidelines (`fpg_year_lag` 1). Period `2027` is FFY2027: the 2026-10-01 entries, the FY2027 state median income ($147,939) and the 2026 guidelines. Eleven parameter files (the four pay-share constants and the seven backup-matrix rows) hold entries dated 2025-10-01 and 2026-10-01; the other 13 hold one 2025-10-01 entry. `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2026-2027"`. Earlier periods take the FFY26 Minnesota values by backfilling, on the earlier state median income and guidelines (period `2025`: FY2025 state median income $137,690 and the 2024 guidelines): unverified historical estimates. Later periods carry the FFY27 values forward on uprated state median income and uprated guidelines: carried-forward estimates. No user-approved estimate replaces a published value; the user's decisions are listed under interpretations.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/mn/commerce/eap/`: `mn_eap`, `mn_eap_household_size`; `eligibility/` `mn_eap_eligible`, `mn_eap_income_limit`; `income/` `mn_eap_countable_income`; `payment/` `mn_eap_energy_cost`, `mn_eap_pay_share` and the new input `mn_eap_housing_type` (APARTMENT, DUPLEX, TRIPLEX, FOURPLEX, TOWNHOUSE, HOUSE, MOBILE_HOME, OTHER; default HOUSE). The branch also removes a stale comment in the shared `pfml_benefits` input saying only Massachusetts uses it.
- **Parameters:** 24 files under `gov.states.mn.commerce.eap`: `eligibility/` `smi_rate` (0.5), `fpg_year_lag` (1); `income/` `sources/earned` (7 sources), `sources/unearned` (12), `sources/investment` (2), `qualified_eligibility_sources` (`tanf`, `general_assistance`, `ssi`), `investment_minimum` ($50 a month), `gift_minimum` ($100 a month), `retirement_age` (59.5), `student_age_limit` (19); `payment/` `minimum` (200), `maximum` (1,400), `energy_cost_sources` (7 expenses), `share/` `maximum`, `minimum`, `slope_start`, `slope_end`, and `backup_cost/` `oil`, `propane`, `steam`, `natural_gas`, `electricity`, `district_heating`, `metered_propane`, each by housing type. The income limit reuses the shared `gov.hhs.smi` amount and size adjustments, `gov.hhs.fpg` and `gov.hhs.liheap.fpg_floor` (1.1). Plus a `programs.yaml` entry and a changelog fragment; no `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml` entry.
- **Tests:** 36 YAML cases in 7 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/mn/commerce/eap/` at the head (`mn_eap.yaml` 8, `mn_eap_household_size.yaml` 1, `eligibility/mn_eap_eligible.yaml` 5, `eligibility/mn_eap_income_limit.yaml` 2, `income/mn_eap_countable_income.yaml` 9, `payment/mn_eap_energy_cost.yaml` 5, `payment/mn_eap_pay_share.yaml` 6). Every case sends `heating_type`. The 41 cases of the earlier version passed locally on 2026-10-21, before the 2026-10-22 review fixes, which were not re-run; CI validates.

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence on axiom-corpus `main` (`dce8e44665`, 2026-10-23) was checked on 2026-10-23 against the full manifest list and by reading the Minnesota LIHEAP, poverty-guideline and LIHEAP annual-figure manifests; GitHub code search of the corpus for the manual, workbook and calculator file names found nothing. Presence in the signed release was not checked. rulespec-us `main` (`115bad3183`, 2026-10-23) has `us-mn/policies/` (cms, dhs combined-manual and income_tax) and `us-mn/statutes/290`, but no Minnesota Commerce, EAP or LIHEAP module and no `us/` poverty-guideline or state-median-income module; the paths below follow that layout. Pages are physical PDF pages. FFY26 manual chapter footers restart at 1 (chapter 3 page 1 is PDF page 71, chapter 4 page 1 is PDF page 117); in the FFY27 manual chapter 3 starts on PDF page 73 and chapter 4 on PDF page 119.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-mn/policies/commerce/eap-policy-manual/ffy2026/chapter-3/eligibility-policies` | One grant per program year (page 71); program year, deadline, residence, vulnerability (page 72); eligible non-citizen documents (pages 73-75); ineligible non-citizens (pages 80-81); household size and definition (pages 82-83); institutions and dwellings (pages 84-85); PCA income (pages 85-86); foster care (page 87) | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. Official copy, for every FFY26 row: [EAP Policy Manual FFY26, pages 71-102, 107-111, 114 and 117-126](https://mn.gov/commerce-stat/pdfs/ffy26-eap-policy-manual.pdf#page=71) (328 pages, modified 2025-10-01). |
| `.../ffy2026/chapter-3/income-definition` | Gross cash receipts, one calendar month, prior-year profit divided by 12, 2026 Maximum EAP Income Guidelines (pages 88-89) | none | Same file. |
| `.../ffy2026/chapter-3/income-inclusions-and-exclusions` | Income Inclusions and Exclusions table (pages 89-99); List of Excluded Income (pages 99-101) | none | Same file. The standalone Appendix 3A at its live URL is the FFY27 edition. |
| `.../ffy2026/chapter-3/income-verification` | Qualified Eligibility (page 102); self-employment, rental and farm income (pages 107-109); retirement and PERA notes (page 111); gifts (page 114) | none | Same file. |
| `.../ffy2026/chapter-4/primary-heat` | All energy costs (page 117); consumption window and backup matrix (page 118); consumption exceptions (pages 119-123); financial need, $200 and $1,400 (page 124); both methods (page 125); which method, heat in rent, subsidized housing, business use (page 126) | none | Same file. |
| `.../ffy2026/appendix-4a/primary-heat-benefit-calculator` | `Formula Parameters!C2:C7`, `Calculator!D2:I21`, `Income Guidelines!A2:B21`, `Backup Matrix Values!A2:C57` | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [MN_BenefitMatrix_2026.xlsx](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/benefits-matricies/MN_BenefitMatrix_2026.xlsx) (Clearinghouse, workbook modified 2025-12-01, sha256 `c7362efb...`). The state URL held the same cells until Commerce replaced them with FFY27. |
| `us-mn/policies/commerce/eap-policy-manual/ffy2027/...` (same sections) | Change log (pages 9, 11-12, 14); vulnerability (page 74); ineligible non-citizens and household (pages 82-84); 2027 guidelines (page 90); income table with Paid Leave (pages 91-100); Qualified Eligibility (page 103); retirement and PERA (page 113); Paid Leave (page 116); chapter 4 (pages 119-128) | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. [EAP Policy Manual FFY27, pages 9, 11-12, 14, 74, 82-84, 90-100, 103, 113, 116 and 119-128](https://mn.gov/commerce-stat/pdfs/ffy27-eap-policy-manual.pdf#page=9) (333 pages, modified 2026-09-02). |
| `.../ffy2027/appendix-4a/primary-heat-benefit-calculator` | FFY27 constants, income guidelines and backup matrix (same cells) | none | Not in a manifest; needs a dated capture because the URL is reused each year: [phb-calculator.xlsx](https://mn.gov/commerce-stat/xls/phb-calculator.xlsx) as served 2026-10-21 (workbook modified 2026-10-14, sha256 `43a5ad35...`). |
| `us-mn/policies/commerce/eap-policy-manual/ffy2024` (not needed) | FFY 2024 edition: 2024 Maximum EAP Income Guidelines (PDF page 84); $200 and $1,400 (page 113) | `us-mn/manual/commerce/eap-policy-manual` | In manifest `us-mn-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml` (309 pages, expression date 2023-10-01): no FFY26 or FFY27 value. Its limits use 50% of state median income for sizes 1 to 16 and 110% of guidelines for 17 to 20. Its `benefit_matrix_pdf_pages: none printed in this document` is accurate. Official copy: [EAP Policy Manual FFY24, pages 84 and 113](https://mn.gov/commerce-stat/pdfs/eap/providers/2024/FINAL-FFY24-EAP-Policy-Manual.pdf#page=84). |
| `us-mn/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-1` | Report period and status (page 1); 1.1 dates and the May 31 deadline (page 4); 1.4 no categorical eligibility, 1.7a no SNAP nominal payment, 1.8 gross income (page 5); 1.9 countable-income boxes (pages 6-7) | `us-mn/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | In manifest `us-mn-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml` (the Clearinghouse file the branch cites, expression date 2025-10-01). Official copy: [FY2026 Detailed Model Plan, pages 1 and 4-9](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/state-plans/MN_Plan_2026.pdf#page=1). Check boxes read from 110 DPI renders of pages 5 to 9. The LIHEAP program bundle (as of 2026-10-06) lists both Minnesota manifests as excluded, with the reason that each is a back-year table and not current law. |
| `us-mn/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-2` | 2.1 50% of state median income, sizes 1 to 10; 2.2; 2.3 no asset test, subsidized renters (page 8); explanations, 2.5 benefit variables, 2.6 $200 and $1,400 (page 9) | `us-mn/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | Same manifest. |
| `us/statutes/42/8624/b/2/B` | The greater of 150% of poverty or 60% of state median income, and the 110% floor | none | No source manifest found; the LIHEAP program bundle cites only `us/statute/42/8621`; coverage by any bulk United States Code ingest was not checked. Official copy: [42 U.S.C. 8624, 2024 edition](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2024-title42/html/USCODE-2024-title42-chap94-subchapII-sec8624.htm). |
| `us/` state median income module | FY2026 Minnesota four-person median $143,998 (period 2026); FY2027 $147,939 (period 2027); the 45 CFR 96.85(b) size factors | `us/guidance/acf/ocs/liheap-im/2026-01/attachment-4-smi-table` (FY2027 only) | FY2027 table in `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml`. The FY2026 table needs ingest: [LIHEAP IM 2025-02, Attachment 4, page 2](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_IM2025-02_SMIStateTable_Att4.pdf#page=2) (the bundle lists it as excluded, back-year). 45 CFR 96.85 appears in the bundle with no manifest. Needed only to derive the table rather than encode the published cells. |
| `us/` poverty guidelines module | 2025 guidelines ($15,650, $5,500 each additional person) for FFY26 sizes 19 and up; 2026 guidelines ($15,960, $5,680) for FFY27 | `us/guidance/hhs/aspe/poverty-guidelines/2025/federal-register`; `.../2026/federal-register` | 2025 (and 2024, period 2025 estimate) in `us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml`; 2026 in `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml`. [90 FR 5917](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-17/html/2025-01377.htm); [91 FR 1797](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-01-15/html/2026-00755.htm). The branch also cites LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 2 (110% table, in no manifest) and the IM 2026-01 page (`us/guidance/acf/ocs/liheap-im/2026-01`, captured). |

## Source text (verbatim)

Quotations come from the official files above (pdftotext, layout and raw modes, line breaks collapsed) and from cell dumps of the two Appendix 4A workbooks; plan check-box and radio states come from renders of plan pages 5 to 9. Where FFY27 repeats FFY26 word for word, the FFY27 page is given in brackets.

**Program and dates.** Plan page 1: “Report Period: 10/01/2025 to 09/30/2026” and “Report Status: Submission Accepted by CO”; page 4, item 1.1: heating assistance “10/01/2025” to “05/31/2026”, and “Applications must be received or postmarked by May 31”. Manual page 71 [73]: “A household is eligible for one Primary Heat grant during the program year. Once determined eligible, a household is eligible until September 30, the end of the program year.” Page 72: “The EAP year is from October 1 of one year through September 30 of the next. The application deadline is typically May 31, but is sometimes extended beyond that date.” FFY27 page 74: “Applications must be postmarked or received by EAP on or before the application deadline.”

**Residence, categorical eligibility and assets.** Page 72 [74]: “Anyone applying for Primary Heat or requesting Crisis or ERR must be living in Minnesota.” Plan page 5: item 1.4 (categorical eligibility) No; 1.7a (SNAP nominal payment) No; 1.8 “Gross Income” checked. Plan page 8: 2.2 (additional eligibility requirements) Yes; “Do you require an Assets test?” No.

**Household and members.** Page 82 [84]: “Household size means the number of people who reside in the household on the date a household member signs the application.” and “Household is defined in 42 U.S.C. 8622(5) as any individual or group of individuals who live together as one economic unit for whom residential energy is customarily purchased in common or who make undesignated energy payments in the form of rent.” Page 73 [75]: “Eligible non-citizens must provide documentation of their immigration status.” Pages 80-81 [82-83]: “If an ineligible non-citizen is a household member on an EAP application, their income is counted but they are not counted as a household member” and “Calculate the one month income from all sources (both eligible and ineligible non-citizens)”. Page 81 also denies the application “If no household member can document citizenship or eligible non-citizen status”. Plan page 9: “Minnesota does not count ineligible non-citizens as household members but counts their income.” Page 84: “Residents of institutions are not eligible for EAP.” and “To be eligible for Primary Heat benefits, a dwelling unit must be used as a primary residence and be designed for year-round human habitation.” Page 87: “Do not count Northstar Care for Children or foster care income.” and adult foster care: “Households may choose to include individuals in adult foster care as household members or not, whichever is the most beneficial”.

**Income limit.** Page 88: “Income means a household’s gross cash receipts, before taxes.”; “The income guidelines equal up to 50 percent of the Minnesota state median income.”; “Gross payments for the one complete calendar month prior to signing the application for most earned and unearned income.”; “The previous year’s profit divided by 12 for self-employment and certain regular annual payments.”; and a household “may be over-income for EAP based on” the one-month column “even though the household’s yearly income is less than” the annual column. Pages 88-89, “2026 Maximum EAP Income Guidelines”, and FFY27 page 90, “2027 Maximum EAP Income Guidelines”, each headed “Based on 50% of State Median Income (SMI) for household sizes 1-18 and on 110% of Federal Poverty Guidelines for household sizes 19-20.” FFY27 page 90 opens: “Maximum EAP income guidelines are defined according to estimates of the state median income and poverty level provided by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.” The “1 Month Max. Guidelines” column (the companion tests use sizes 1 to 4, 18, 19 and 20):

| Size | FFY26 | FFY27 | Size | FFY26 | FFY27 | Size | FFY26 | FFY27 | Size | FFY26 | FFY27 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | $3,119 | $3,205 | 6 | $7,919 | $8,136 | 11 | $8,819 | $9,061 | 16 | $9,719 | $9,985 |
| 2 | $4,079 | $4,191 | 7 | $8,099 | $8,321 | 12 | $8,999 | $9,246 | 17 | $9,899 | $10,170 |
| 3 | $5,039 | $5,177 | 8 | $8,279 | $8,506 | 13 | $9,179 | $9,431 | 18 | $10,079 | $10,355 |
| 4 | $5,999 | $6,164 | 9 | $8,459 | $8,691 | 14 | $9,359 | $9,616 | 19 | $10,509 | $10,835 |
| 5 | $6,959 | $7,150 | 10 | $8,639 | $8,876 | 15 | $9,539 | $9,800 | 20 | $11,013 | $11,355 |

The “Annual Income” column prints, for example, $37,439 and $132,165 (FFY26 sizes 1 and 20) and $38,464 and $136,268 (FFY27). Appendix 4A `Income Guidelines!B2:B21` holds the same one-month cells in each edition. Plan page 8, item 2.1: sizes 1 to 10, “State Median Income”, “50.00%”.
