## Required outputs

| Output | policyengine-us variable | Entity, period | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Household size | `mn_eap_household_size` | SPM unit, year | Number of members with `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`; 0 outside Minnesota. |
| Income limit | `mn_eap_income_limit` | SPM unit, year | 12 x max(floor(round(0.5 x SMI x size factor, 2) / 12), floor(round(1.1 x guideline, 2) / 12)); SMI is Minnesota's four-person median (`gov.hhs.smi`, 45 CFR 96.85(b) factors 0.52, +0.16 to six, +0.03 after); guideline is the prior year's 48-state guideline for the size; 0 when size is 0. Equals 12 x the published one-month cell for sizes 1 to 20. |
| Countable income | `mn_eap_countable_income` | SPM unit, year | Sum over all members, counted in size or not: earned sources (`employment_income`, `self_employment_income`, `sstb_self_employment_income`, `partnership_s_corp_income`, `farm_operations_income`, `farm_rent_income`, `rental_income`, each floored at 0) plus `total_unemployment_compensation` (floored), both 0 for a member aged 19 or under with `is_in_k12_school`; unearned sources (`ssi` summed over months, `general_assistance`, `military_retirement_income`, `railroad_benefits`, `veterans_benefits`, `workers_compensation`, `disability_benefits`, `pfml_benefits`, `alimony_income`, `strike_benefits`, `estate_income`, `survivor_benefits`, each floored); `retirement_distributions` from age 59.5; max(`social_security` + `pension_income` - `medicare_part_b_premium`, 0) per person. Plus household `interest_income` + `ordinary_dividend_income` when that total / 12 >= $50; household `financial_assistance` when its total / 12 >= $100; SPM-unit `tanf` (includes MFIP cash). |
| Energy cost | `mn_eap_energy_cost` | SPM unit, year | Heat not in rent: sum of `pre_subsidy_electricity_expense`, `gas_expense`, `fuel_oil_expense`, `bottled_gas_expense`, `wood_expense`, `coal_expense`, `other_heating_fuel_expense`. Heat in rent and subsidized (`receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing`): `pre_subsidy_electricity_expense`. Heat in unsubsidized rent: the backup-matrix cell for `mn_eap_housing_type` in row Oil (FUEL_OIL, KEROSENE), Propane (PROPANE), Natural Gas (NATURAL_GAS) or Electricity (ELECTRICITY); 0 for other heating types. |
| Eligible | `mn_eap_eligible` | SPM unit, year | Minnesota; size > 0; countable income <= limit; `heating_type` not UNSPECIFIED or NONE; heat in unsubsidized rent, or energy cost > 0. |
| Pay share | `mn_eap_pay_share` | SPM unit, year | p = 0 under Qualified Eligibility (the members' `tanf`, `general_assistance` and `ssi` total > 0 and countable income does not exceed it, compared to the cent); otherwise countable income / limit (0 when the limit is 0). Share = Pay Max - (Pay Max - Pay Min) x clip((p - Slope Start) / (Slope End - Slope Start), 0, 1). FFY26 0.439, 0.108, 0, 0.896; FFY27 0.452, 0.113, 0, 0.891. |
| Benefit | `mn_eap` | SPM unit, year | If eligible and energy cost > 0: min(max(floor(share x cost + 0.5), $200), $1,400); otherwise $0. |

Inputs: `state_code`, `age`, `immigration_status`, `is_in_k12_school`; the earned, unearned, retirement and investment sources above (`ssi` is monthly; `social_security` or its components; `unemployment_compensation`; `taxable_ira_distributions` and the other `retirement_distributions` parts); `medicare_part_b_premium`; `financial_assistance`; `tanf` (SPM unit, sent as an input in every test); `heating_type` sent explicitly with the matching bills; `heat_expense_included_in_rent`, `receives_housing_assistance`, `is_in_public_housing` (household) and `mn_eap_housing_type`.

Age 70, `social_security_retirement` $6,000 and `ssi` $6,168, no premium (2026) | Percentile 0: Pay Max 0.439, 0.452. 35,000 / 37,428 = 0.935 and 36,000 / 38,460 = 0.936, past the slope ends: 0.108, 0.113. SSI only: “eligible at the lowest level of income” (page 102), percentile 0 (interpretation 4): 0.439 (0.321 otherwise). With Social Security, not SSI only: 12,168 / 37,428 = 0.3251042; 0.439 - 0.331 x 0.3251042 / 0.896 = 0.3189001. | 0.439, 0.452, 0.108, 0.113, 0.439, 0.3189001 | pp. 102, 124; Appendix 4A C4:C7 |
| 13 | Two households end to end (`mn_eap.yaml` Cases 7, 8) | (a) 2026: adults 38 (wages $37,440) and 36 ($14,040), member 16 in K-12 (wages $4,000), child 9; NATURAL_GAS, gas $1,050, electric $1,000, DUPLEX. (b) 2027: parent 31, wages $27,000, `child_support_received` $3,000; child 6; PROPANE, heat in unsubsidized rent, MOBILE_HOME | (a) Size 4; 37,440 + 14,040 = 51,480 (student wages excluded); limit 12 x 5,999 = 71,988; cost 2,050; 51,480 / 71,988 = 0.7151192; 0.439 - 0.331 x 0.7151192 / 0.896 = 0.1748209; x 2,050 = 358.38, to 358. (b) Size 2; 27,000; limit 12 x 4,191 = 50,292; FFY27 Propane, Mobile Home 3,342; 27,000 / 50,292 = 0.5368647; 0.452 - 0.339 x 0.5368647 / 0.891 = 0.2477383; x 3,342 = 827.94, to 828. | (a) size 4, income 51,480, limit 71,988, cost 2,050, share 0.1748209, $358; (b) size 2, income 27,000, limit 50,292, cost 3,342, share 0.2477383, $828 | pp. 88-91, 117, 124-126; FFY27 p. 90; both Appendix 4A editions |

No branch test disagrees with these derivations. Some depend on readings the text does not settle: test 5 at size 21 (interpretation 2), 6(b) and 6(e) (interpretation 7), the $209 in 8(b) and 10(b) (interpretation 9), the loss floor in 9(b) (interpretation 11), 10(c) (interpretation 10) and the SSI-only share in 12 (interpretation 4).

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **One month and annual amounts (simplification).** EAP counts gross receipts for one calendar month, or prior-year profit divided by 12 (page 88). The branch compares annual income with 12 times the one-month cell, not the annual column, which is $0 to $11 higher (FFY26 size 1: $37,439 against $37,428). This follows the manual's note that a household can be over the one-month limit with yearly income under the annual column. The FFY26 and FFY27 annual columns at size 19 ($126,116 and $130,021) are $1 above 110% of the guideline; the one-month cells match it.
2. **How the limit is built (inferred, and a settled decision for sizes over 20).** The manual prints cells, not a rounding rule. The branch reproduces all 40 one-month cells as the larger of floor(round(50% x size-adjusted median, 2) / 12) and floor(round(110% x prior-year guideline, 2) / 12); the shared `liheap_smi_limit` helper would give $9,615 at FFY27 size 14 against the printed $9,616. The plan lists only sizes 1 to 10 at 50% of state median income. The table stops at 20; above it the branch applies the 110% floor of 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B) through the shared `fpg_floor` (settled), because 50% of median is lower there. Axiom can encode the printed cells directly and needs the median and guideline modules only for sizes over 20.
3. **Pay-share constants (user decision).** The manual gives only the shape of the share and says the percentages are set when funds are awarded. The branch takes Pay Max, Pay Min, Slope Start and Slope End from Appendix 4A `Formula Parameters!C4:C7` of each edition, which the FFY27 manual calls an optional estimating tool; eHEAT, the system of record, is not public. The FFY27 workbook was posted on 2026-10-14; if Commerce reposts it after the federal award, C4:C7 need a recheck. Rounding follows `ROUND(G2*C2, 0)` (half away from zero; equal to floor(x + 0.5) for these positive amounts), and the $200 and $1,400 limits apply after rounding, as in I2.
4. **Qualified Eligibility (user decision).** “Eligible at the lowest level of income” (page 102) is read as an income percentile of 0, the Pay Max share. The branch finds it when the members' `tanf`, `general_assistance` and `ssi` total is positive and countable income does not exceed it at the cent. MFIP is part of `tanf`; DWP has no input. The income limit still applies.
5. **Household and members (simplification).** The SPM unit stands in for the economic unit. `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant` approximates eligible non-citizen status (the documents on pages 74-75); SSNs and their exceptions, institutions, the dwelling-eligibility tools, minors claimed by two households, students away, the adult-foster-care election and the live-in PCA exclusion are not identified.
6. **Energy cost basis (simplification).** Current-year expense inputs stand in for up to 12 months of prior-year consumption inside the 16-month window. A zero expense is no cost, so an own-paying household without consumption data does not get the backup matrix (page 120), and a subsidized heat-in-rent household that pays electricity with no recorded use is treated as not paying it, ineligible instead of the $200 minimum (page 126). eHEAT's larger-of rule for partial data, lower-of rule for business use, shared meters, outbuildings and rented-out rooms, fuel-change invalidation, the biofuel worksheet, the $1 extended-absence entry and the solar-garden rules are not modeled. An unsubsidized heat-in-rent household that also pays its own electric bill gets the matrix cost only; the manual does not say to combine them.
7. **Backup matrix and heating types (settled decisions).** All seven rows are stored; `heating_type` selects Oil for FUEL_OIL and for KEROSENE (by inference, as the heating-expense grouping does), Propane for PROPANE, Natural Gas and Electricity. No heating type selects Steam, District Heating or Metered Propane (Metered Propane matches Propane in every cell of both editions). WOOD, COAL, SOLAR and OTHER have no row, so heat in rent with those fuels is eligible at $0 (page 123: the matrix “does not include biofuels”). `mn_eap_housing_type` defaults to HOUSE; Mobile Home equals House in every row of both editions.
8. **Housing proxies (simplification).** Subsidized housing is `receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing`; tribal subsidized housing has no separate input. HUD 236 and FHA 515 tenants, vulnerable through rent (page 72), are subsidized whenever `receives_housing_assistance` is set. A positive `pre_subsidy_electricity_expense` stands in for paying electric costs. Households not required to pay rent, heat or electricity, and the FFY27 lot-rent and HOA rule, are not identified. `heating_type` is a required input (settled): UNSPECIFIED and NONE pay $0, including with heat in rent, because the matrix needs a fuel (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the default).
9. **Social Security, pensions and Medicare (settled).** The manual counts Social Security net of Medicare and Part D (page 96), excludes “Medicare deductions from Social Security” (page 100) and nets Medicare paid out of a PERA pension (page 111); plan item 1.9 checks “Excluding MediCare deduction”. The branch subtracts the computed `medicare_part_b_premium` once from each person's Social Security plus pension, floored at 0; no Part D input exists, and other annuities are not netted. Companion test 10(b) depends on this.
10. **Minnesota Paid Leave (user decision, 2026-10-22).** Benefits began January 1, 2026. The FFY26 table has no Paid Leave row; the FFY27 manual counts it and its change log describes the row as an addition. The branch counts `pfml_benefits` from FFY2026 under the FFY26 definition of income as gross cash receipts, with the closest FFY26 row (wage-replacement disability pay) also counted. Companion test 10(c) depends on this.
11. **Self-employment and losses (simplification).** The manual takes Schedule 1 lines 3 to 6 per return and does not net one return's loss against another; without a return it counts 50% of gross receipts. The branch counts net business, SSTB, partnership and S corporation, farm, farm rent and rental income, each floored at zero per person (settled), so a loss on one line does not offset another line of the same return either. The 50% gross-receipts route has no input; `rental_income` is assumed nonnegative.
12. **Retirement withdrawals (inference).** `retirement_distributions` count from age 59.5; unpenalized early benefits under 59½, which the manual counts, have no input and are excluded. `pension_income` counts at any age and also carries life insurance and endowment payments, which the manual excludes.
13. **Thresholds (inference).** The $50 test applies to the household's combined interest and ordinary dividends, as one-month equivalents of annual amounts; the $100 test to the household's `financial_assistance`. Royalties have no input of their own; `estate_income`, counted in full as trust disbursements, carries only royalties received through an estate or trust.
14. **Students (simplification).** The exclusion uses `is_in_k12_school` at age 19 or under; equivalency programs such as GED, home schooling and alternative learning centers are identified only if that input is set. Social Security of minors and students counts, as page 96 says.
15. **Inputs the model lacks, and plan boxes (gap and source difference).** DWP, MFIP housing assistance grants, Housing Support, tribal per capita and judgment payments, irregular income, jury pay, inheritances, lump sums, training allowances, Trade Adjustment Act payments, contract-for-deed interest and payments on behalf of the household have no input. Military pay counts only through `employment_income`; the separate `military_basic_pay` input is not listed. Plan item 1.9 checks foster-care funds and leaves child earnings unchecked, while the manual excludes Northstar and foster care income (page 87) and counts the earnings of minors who are not K-12 students; the branch follows the manual and adds no conflict-register entry.
16. **Years and dates (simplification).** Annual periods read 1 January values, so period 2026 applies FFY26 to all of calendar 2026, including October to December 2026, which fall in FFY27. Period 2025 and earlier, and period 2028 and later, are estimates (see Policy periods).
17. **Other gaps.** The application deadline, one grant per program year, first-come first-served order, funding, the $10 benefit-fix threshold, vendor payment routing, Crisis and ERR are not modeled.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-mn-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-mn-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [us-mn-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-mn-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml) (FFY 2024 edition)
- [us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml) (2025 guidelines, period 2026; 2024, period 2025 estimate)
- [us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml) (2026 guidelines and FY2027 state median income, period 2027)
- [us-hhs-poverty-guidelines.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-hhs-poverty-guidelines.yaml) (undated, never extracted)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-mn/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the FFY26 and FFY27 one-month limits for sizes 1 to 20 and the floor above 20, the inclusive limit, the Appendix 4A pay share at percentile 0, between the ends and past the slope end in both years, whole-dollar rounding, the $200 floor and $1,400 cap, Qualified Eligibility, own-bill totals with non-heat electricity, every backup-matrix row the branch selects (Oil for fuel oil and kerosene, Propane, Natural Gas, Electricity) across the eight housing types with the House default, the unselected Steam, District Heating and Metered Propane rows, wood, coal, solar and other with heat in rent, heat in subsidized rent through the electric bill, unspecified and no heat, ineligible non-citizens (income counted, size not), the K-12 student exclusion at 19, Social Security and pension net of Medicare, retirement withdrawals at 59½, the $50 and $100 thresholds, Paid Leave, MFIP, child support excluded, per-source loss floors, and any 2025 or 2028 period kept in scope. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Oregon LIHEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1b, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9743 (branch `or-liheap`), open and under review, not yet merged. Scope, policy period, module paths, source text, required outputs and companion tests are in the sections below. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## PolicyEngine implementation (historical snapshot)

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9743, open and under review, not merged. Head `bbb8ce05c7` (2026-10-08 UTC): a merge of `upstream/main` `e19f75c510`, which carries the merged New Jersey (PR 9745) and New York (PR 9744) programs; only `programs.yaml` changed, so the policy content equals `9872ebbdf5`. Previous head `9872ebbdf5` (2026-10-08 UTC): the round 3 commit `ea08858e80` changes references only. The five amount tables cite the Region 1 and the Region 2 matrix page of each manual (PY2025 pages 58 and 59, PY2026 pages 78 and 80, PY2027 pages 72 and 74), the income band parameter and variable add the pages that hold the larger household sizes (PY2026 page 79, PY2027 page 73), the region variable cites both regions' county pages, single-page titles carry no page text, and the unearned source description says person-level. No value, formula or test changed. Merged with `upstream/main` `023cb8292e`, which includes Maryland MEAP. Previous head `34bf42ca56` (2026-10-07): the round 2 commit floors each member's unearned sources before the household sum (TANF added at the unit level), adds the even-size FY2026 limit case, the PY2027 size-12 Region 2 row and a two-member rental case, puts the PY2025 and PY2027 pages on four variables, and moves the reference titles to the `#page a-b` form; the per-page splitting David asked for (S6) was declined because the table pages are consecutive; round 3 then added one entry per table section instead (see the current head). Earlier head `5d4e3a5b15` (2026-10-06): commit `7d4079fe85` applies DTrim99's round 1 review (PY2025 and PY2027 tables, the kerosene and solar columns, a float64 ceiling, two added income sources, per-source flooring, a per-member interest case, reference and test fixes) and is merged with `upstream/main`. History: first head `f7b04fa1b0` (2026-10-02); the 2026-10-02 review fixes pushed as `1898b48807` (2026-10-03); the author's `6c8020e7da` added `farm_rent_income` and `survivor_benefits` (head `dfb2b8230b`); a tidy pass pushed as `06b38abd60` (2026-10-06). Everything below describes head `bbb8ce05c7`; its policy content is identical to `34bf42ca56`. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges; oracle fixtures pin that revision.
- **Scope:** the "Regular/Standard Payment" of Oregon LIHEAP for program years 2025 to 2027 (PY2025 effective 2024-10-01, PY2026 as corrected by OHCS 44-2025, PY2027 effective 2026-10-01): gross income at or below 60% of state median income, the energy-burden test with its subsidized heat-in-rent exclusion, the county region, heating fuel, household size and income band payment matrices, and the 50% payment for a roomer, boarder or owner applying separately. Out of scope: the matrix "COOLING" column, crisis and combo payments, the bulk-fuel "Fuel Payment", heating and cooling equipment repair or replacement, portable air conditioners, health and safety, supplemental and agency-pay payments, the SNAP nominal payment, OEAP, and weatherization.
- **Policy periods:** three seasons. Program year N is federal fiscal year N (October 1 of N-1 to September 30 of N) and is read at model period `N`: every Oregon variable is annual and reads the value in force on 1 January. The five amount tables and `income_band` carry change-only entries at `2024-10-01` (PY2025 manual, pages 58 to 59), `2025-10-09` (PY2026 as corrected by OHCS 44-2025, pages 78 to 81) and `2026-10-01` (PY2027 manual, pages 72 to 75). The ten non-matrix files start at `2024-10-01` because the PY2025, PY2026 and PY2027 manuals state the same scalar rules ($200 interest, age 18, 50% roomer share, subsidized heat in rent, size 6 and 12 limits, county lists). The registry records `verified_years: "2025-2027"`. Years before 2025 backfill the PY2025 values and are unverified estimates. Interpretation 1 is closed.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/or/ohcs/liheap/`: `or_liheap`, the input `or_liheap_dwelling_type`; `eligibility/or_liheap_eligible`, `or_liheap_income_limit`; `income/or_liheap_countable_income`, `or_liheap_countable_earned_income`; `payment/or_liheap_income_band`, `or_liheap_region`. The limit reuses the federal `hhs_smi` variable (`gov.hhs.smi.amount`, `household_size_adjustment`, `additional_person_threshold`).
- **Parameters:** `gov.states.or.ohcs.liheap` (`eligibility/`: `smi_rate`; `income/`: `earned_income_min_age`, `interest_threshold`, `sources/earned` (now including `partnership_s_corp_income`), `sources/unearned` (person-level sources, review requirement: `military_retirement_income`; TANF is added in the formula); `payment/`: `income_band`, `max_household_size`, `max_payment_size`, `roomer_rate`, `regions/region_1`, `regions/region_2`, and `amount/electricity`, `amount/fuel_oil`, `amount/natural_gas`, `amount/propane`, `amount/wood`, all five keyed by region, household size and band). 16 files.
- **Tests:** 40 YAML cases in 6 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/or/ohcs/liheap/` at head `bbb8ce05c7`, unchanged since `34bf42ca56` (`or_liheap.yaml` 25, `integration.yaml` 3, `income/or_liheap_countable_income.yaml` 6, `income/or_liheap_countable_earned_income.yaml` 1, `eligibility/or_liheap_eligible.yaml` 1, `eligibility/or_liheap_income_limit.yaml` 4). Run locally on 2026-10-07 before the round 2 commit: all passed; the round 3 commit changed no test.

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence in a manifest on axiom-corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-02 against the manifest copies saved in `corpus/`. Presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not checked. The manual manifest captures the oregon.gov PDF (95 pages, PDF dated 2026-06-30) at `pdf_page` granularity; its `benefit_matrix_pdf_pages: 77-80` is one page off the file (page 77 holds the income limits, the matrices are on pages 78 to 81), and its own note says the corpus `page-N` suffix counts text-bearing pages only, so corpus page numbers may differ from the PDF pages quoted below. The 2026-06-30 file prints the same 96 matrix rows as the manual edition created 2025-10-07 and as the OHCS 44-2025 filing attachment. The OAR 813-200 rule text and the OHCS 44-2025 filing are in no manifest. rulespec-us already has `us-or/policies/` (cms, income_tax) and `us-or/statutes/`; the paths below follow that layout.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-or/policies/ohcs/energy-assistance-manual/py2026/section-two/income-definition` | Page 36: gross income before any deductions; number of household members; income exchanged within the household not counted | `us-or/manual/ohcs/energy-assistance-intake-operations-policy-manual` | In manifest `us-or-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml`. Official copy: [PY2026 manual, page 36](https://www.oregon.gov/ohcs/energy-weatherization/Documents/2026%20Final%20Energy%20Assistance%20Intake%20Operations%20%26%20Policy%20Manual.pdf#page=36) (the same file serves every manual page cited below). |
| `.../section-two/income-and-income-exclusion-chart` | Pages 37 to 49: the "Considered Income?" Yes/No chart, including the under-18 and high-school rows (page 41) and the $200 interest note (page 43) | same | In manifest. The Yes/No reading rests on the X column position in the text layer. |
| `.../section-two/proof-of-income` and `.../section-two/what-is-not-income` | Page 49: count income for all residents; page 50: interest counted only over $200 a year and withdrawn; page 53: earnings of minors and of high-school enrollees 18 and over | same | In manifest. |
| `.../section-one/self-employed-clients` and `.../section-two/private-disability-insurance` | Page 35: self-employment net of the cost of doing business, no carry-forward; pages 54 to 56: private disability with a Social Security offset | same | In manifest. |
| `.../section-one/unusual-eligibility-situations` | Page 30: roomer/boarder definition; co-habitants are one economic unit | same | In manifest. |
| `.../section-three/payment-types` and `.../section-three/standard-benefits-primary-heating-source` | Pages 61 to 62: regular payment, energy burden, subsidized heat in rent, the 50% roomer/boarder/owner payment, Fuel Payment; page 67: primary heating source, direct pays to renters | same | In manifest. |
| `.../section-five/eligibility-income-guidelines` | Page 77: 60% of state median income for sizes 1 to 12 and each additional member | same | In manifest. |
| `.../section-five/benefit-matrix-region-1` and `.../section-five/benefit-matrix-region-2` | Pages 78 to 79: Region 1 county list and matrix; pages 80 to 81: Region 2 | same | In manifest (`benefit_matrix_pdf_pages: 77-80` there; the matrices are PDF pages 78 to 81). |
| `us-or/policies/ohcs/energy-assistance-manual/py2025/...` and `.../py2027/...` | PY2025 manual (final 2024-09-27): income limits page 57, Region 1 and 2 matrices pages 58 to 59, roomer rule page 47, income chart pages 31 to 41, interest pages 34 and 40, minors pages 33 and 41. PY2027 manual (posted 2026-09-23): income limits page 71, matrices pages 72 to 75, roomer rule page 59, income chart pages 38 to 53, interest pages 43 and 51, minors pages 42 and 54 | none | Not in a saved manifest (not checked against corpus main on 2026-10-06); needs ingest. Official copies: [PY2025 manual, page 58](https://www.oregon.gov/ohcs/energy-weatherization/Documents/PY25%20EA%20Operations%20%20Policy%20Manual-%20FINAL%209-27-24.pdf#page=58) and [PY2027 manual, page 72](https://www.oregon.gov/ohcs/energy-weatherization/Documents/manuals/09-23-2027-PY-2027-EA-Operations-Policy-Manual.pdf#page=72). |
| `.../section-seven/energy-burden-table` | Pages 93 to 94: which heat situations carry an energy burden | same | In manifest. |
| `us-or/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-1` and `.../section-2` | 1.4 categorical eligibility; 1.8 gross income; 1.9 countable forms, including SSA benefits "Including MediCare deduction" (pages 5 to 6); 2.1 60% of state median income; 2.3 no asset test; 2.5 benefit variables; 2.6 minimum $250 and maximum $750 (pages 8 to 9) | `us-or/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | In manifest `us-or-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml`, segmented by "Section N" headings. Official copy: [FY2026 state plan, pages 5-9](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/state-plans/OR_Plan_2026.pdf#page=5). The text layer carries no check-box states; those were read from rendered pages. |
| `us-or/policies/ohcs/oar-813-200/0005-definitions`, `.../0008-manuals`, `.../0020-household-eligibility` | 813-200-0005(3) energy burden, (6) household, (7) household income, (8) 60% of state median income; 0008 manual adopted by reference, with filing history; 0020(1) income threshold and energy burden, (2) 30-day to 12-month income period, (5) institutions | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official: [OAR chapter 813, division 200](https://secure.sos.state.or.us/oard/displayDivisionRules.action?selectedDivision=3649) (HTML; the site answers plain clients with a bot challenge). On 2026-10-02 the live 0008 text already adopts the PY2027 manual "dated October 1, 2026" under OHCS 29-2026, so the PY2026 adoption must be taken from the filing history. |
| `us-or/policies/ohcs/oar-813-200/filings/ohcs-44-2025` | Temporary order filed 2025-10-09 correcting the payment matrices; rule text adopting the manual dated October 1, 2025 | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. ## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Parameter dates (closed 2026-10-06).** The five amount tables and `income_band` carry `2024-10-01` (PY2025), `2025-10-09` (PY2026 as corrected by OHCS 44-2025) and `2026-10-01` (PY2027); the ten scalar and list files start at `2024-10-01` because the three manuals state the same rules. Whether the PY2026 band tops changed between the 2025-10-01 adoption and the 2025-10-09 correction was still not checked; no result depends on it. Take effective dates from the sources.
2. **Roomer/boarder/owner input (owner decision pending).** `or_liheap_dwelling_type` is an application arrangement, not a dwelling type: the matrix has no dwelling dimension and plan item 2.5 leaves "Dwelling type" unchecked. The 50% rule itself is manual text (pages 61 to 62). Plan item 2.6 states a "$250" minimum while half of the lowest cell is $125 and the PE test pays $232.50; the manual does not say whether the half payment is floored. Whether the input stays, what it is called, and whether the plan minimum applies are the owner's call; do not treat the PE draft's $232.50 as the settled rule.
3. **Interest per person (interpretation).** The $200 test is applied to each member's interest and the amounts over $200 are summed. Pages 43 and 50 name neither person nor household. Two members with $150 each count $0 in PE and $300 under a household reading. The "and is withdrawn" condition is assumed met; the test that pins this (test 14) uses one-person units only.
4. **Missing county (corrects the earlier body).** The earlier body said a missing county yields zero. With no `county` input the model's county defaults to the alphabetically first county of the state, Baker County, which is in Region 2 (page 80), so a household sent without a county is paid at Region 2 rates (natural gas $560 instead of $670 for a Region 1 resident; electricity $515 instead of $465). Only an explicit `UNKNOWN` county or an out-of-state county gives region 0 and $0. Case 22 (test 20) pins the fallback. Oracle fixtures must always send a county.
5. **Sizes above 12 (coverage limit).** Page 77 extends the limit by "Each Additional Member" "$2,115" (its monthly "$184.58" times 12 is $2,214.96, so the page is inconsistent with itself; the model's 3% step gives about $2,214), but pages 78 to 81 end at size 12. PE leaves such a household eligible and pays $0.
6. **Ceiling (inferred).** No source states a rounding rule. The ceiling of 0.6 times the HHS size-adjusted median reproduces all twelve limits on page 77; floor or half-up rounding do not. `income <= limit` follows OAR 813-200-0005(8) "at or below".
7. **Out-of-state lookup defect (found in review, fixed at head `1898b48807`).** At head `f7b04fa` the payment formula indexed the amount tables with the raw income band, which is 0 for units outside Oregon, so a simulation holding one eligible Oregon unit and any other-state unit raised `ParameterNotFoundError`. The fix floors the band at 1 (`max_(..., 1)`), as the region already was, and test 1 covers the mixed-state case; no Oregon result changes.
8. **Fuels without a matrix column (coverage limit, not a legal rule).** `heating_type` is a required input. The program is fuel blind (page 5), so kerosene is paid from the Heating Oil column and a grid-tied solar home from the Electricity column, the pairings `heating_expense` uses (test 8). Coal, other, none and unspecified pay $0 because the matrix prints only five heating columns, not because the manual denies them; page 67 bases the standard benefit on "the energy type where the majority of assistance will be applied". Fixtures must send `heating_type` with the matching bill; the unspecified default is tracked in PolicyEngine/policyengine-us issue 9754.
9. **Social Security gross (Oregon's own rule).** Plan item 1.9 checks "Including MediCare deduction" and the page 58 worksheet adds the premium back ("Adds lines a and b"), so PE counts `social_security` as is and wires in no Medicare premium variable. Private disability is entered net of the SSA offset so the manual's examples (pages 55 to 56) are reproduced without counting the offset twice.
10. **Other gaps, kept explicit.** Institutional residence (OAR 813-200-0020(5)), tribal duplicate awards, the 30-day to 12-month income window (annual income stands in), categorical eligibility (plan item 1.4 answers No, so none is encoded), the SNAP nominal payment, Yes rows without a model input (adoption assistance, contract for deed, foster care, informal income, royalties, tribal per capita payments, work study, regular cash gifts, jury duty, legal settlements), the Fuel Payment, supplemental and agency payments, and OEAP are not modeled. Self-employment uses the model's net inputs with no further deduction and each source floored at zero (page 35 bars carry-forward only); every unearned source is floored the same way for each member (tests 23 and 27), so one member's rental or estate loss offsets neither other income nor another member's rent. Subsidized housing, public housing included, with heat in rent is excluded even when the household pays a separate non-heating utility bill (test 12). The SPM unit stands in for the economic household; the co-habitant and roomer verification rules on page 30 are not derived. Page 36 "Income that exchanges hands within a household is not counted" is satisfied by not having an intra-household transfer input.
11. **PY2025 and PY2027 (encoded 2026-10-06).** In PY2025 the Heating Oil, Liquid Gas and Wood/Pellets columns differ by region (size 1 third row heating oil $680 in Region 1 against $745 in Region 2), so all five tables carry the region level; in PY2026 and PY2027 those three columns are identical in both regions. In PY2027 the Electricity and Natural Gas columns and the band tops change while the Heating Oil, Liquid Gas and Wood/Pellets cells equal FY2026 in every cell, so they carry no `2026-10-01` entry. The FFY2027 four-person median is $129,250, which makes six PY2027 limits exact dollars; the ceiling must be taken after rounding to cents in float64 (test 5).

## Existing corpus starting points

- [FY2026 state-plan manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-or-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [PY2026 manual manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-or-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml)

These FY2026 manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission. The OAR 813-200 text, the OHCS 44-2025 filing, the PY2025 and PY2027 manuals and the FFY2025 and FFY2026 HHS state median income tables are not in any manifest and need ingest before the modules above can be proved (FFY2027 is in `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml`).

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-or/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover income limits, payment-band boundaries and the county/fuel tables for each of PY2025 to PY2027, heat-in-rent and subsidized housing, separate-application adjustments, mixed households, TANF receipt/take-up, and private-disability/Social Security income interactions. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: LIHEAP wave 1d: encode Wisconsin WHEAP regular heating assistance

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Wisconsin WHEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1d, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10434 (branch `wi-liheap-wave1d`), open, not merged. Head `00b8d56388` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983`; this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10434 opened on 2026-10-23 with no reviews yet, so there is no revision to pin.
- **Sources missing from the corpus.** No axiom-corpus manifest on `main` holds the HE+ Benefit Calculator for FFY2026, the only source of the benefit formula constants, the heat proxy table and the income limits for sizes 9 to 20 (`liheap-agent-queue.yaml` records `matrix_status: absent` for Wisconsin). Also missing: the agency-posted FFY2026 plan (the $2,580 maximum the branch uses), LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 4 (the FY2026 state median income, $123,148 for four), and, for the period 2027 estimate only, the PY27 manual and the FFY2027 plan. These need ingest. The FFY2026 plan and the 2025 guidelines are in manifests; Wis. Stat. 16.27 and 42 U.S.C. 8624 sit in statute scopes without per-document manifests.
- **Different edition in the corpus.** `us-wi-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml` holds the June 2026 re-issue of the PY26 manual; the branch cites the February 2026 edition through a Wayback capture (the agency URL now returns 404). The cited passages read the same; three page numbers differ.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-23; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10434, branch `wi-liheap-wave1d`, head `00b8d56388` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983` and closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10424. It includes the 2026-10-22 review fixes: household size also counts non-citizens who receive Social Security (manual 3.2.2.4), exact-edge cases for the federal 110% floor, a minor's self-employment income, and comments on FoodShare receipt and court-placed foster children. No `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml` entry is added.
- **Scope:** the WHEAP regular heating benefit (the LIHEAP heat benefit) for FFY2026: household size, gross countable income, the 60% SMI limit, the federal 110% floor, categorical eligibility and its benefit at the limit, the energy burden (a heating bill, or heat in rent without rental assistance), the fuel, and the HE+ formula (poverty ratio between 0.60 and 2.15, constants 2.66667 and 2.94269, heating cost between 0.75 and 2 times a heat proxy by fuel, dwelling type and rooms, 60% electric baseload, truncation, $30 minimum, $2,580 maximum). Out of scope: the state-funded non-heating electric (Public Benefits) benefit, crisis assistance, weatherization, HE+ Program Services, supplemental benefits, the February 1 reduction and the $1 SNAP benefit of Wis. Stat. 16.27(5)(e).
- **Policy periods:** one verified season, FFY2026: heating applications October 1, 2025 to May 15, 2026 (plan item 1.1, page 4; manual Definitions, page 14; Wis. Stat. 16.27(4)(a)) in the program year October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026 (plan page 1). Wisconsin variables are annual and read 1 January values, so period `2026` is FFY2026 on the 2025 HHS guidelines (`fpg_year_lag` 1; the calculator's 15,650 and 5,500) and the FY2026 SMI (`gov.hhs.smi.amount` WI, $123,148 from 2025-10-01). All 31 parameter files hold one `2025-10-01` entry. `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2026"`. Earlier periods take the same values by backfilling, with the FY2025 SMI and the 2024 guidelines: unverified estimates. Later periods carry the FFY2026 constants forward with the FY2027 SMI ($127,769) and the 2026 guidelines: carried-forward estimates, since no FFY2027 calculator is published. The user approved FFY2026 only and the $2,580 maximum (interpretations 5 and 15).

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Annual income for a prior-month test (simplification).** Wisconsin tests one month of gross income, annualized (Appendix E; 3.3.2 item 1; calculator C5 and C13 compare one-month income with the one-month column). The branch compares annual income with the annual column, which equals 12 times the one-month figure within 4 cents (size 2: 12 x 4,186.92 = 50,243.04). The 12-month periods, the present-month option and the extra-paycheck rule are not modeled. The limit is the shared `liheap_smi_limit`: floor(share x floor(0.6 x SMI)), which reproduces all 20 printed sizes; the order of flooring is inferred, and plan 2.4 says only that Wisconsin rounds down.
2. **Household, case head and size (settled reading and simplification).** The SPM unit stands in for the economic unit. Size counts members with `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant` or positive `social_security` (3.2.2.4); a FoodShare-receiving non-citizen is counted only through immigration status, because FoodShare receipt has no person-level input. Ineligible non-citizens' income counts but they are not counted in size (4.4.26.2), which also sets the guideline; 3.2.6.2 and the calculator's “include all” are read as data-entry instructions. A household with no counted member has no case head and is ineligible (3.2.1). Court-placed foster children are counted (no input identifies them), and the other 3.2.6.4 exclusions are not identified. The SSN and student case head rules are not modeled.
3. **Categorical eligibility (simplification).** Receipt in any month of the year stands in for receipt for the entire prior month (3.3.1 item 2(e)). FoodShare covers a member in the SNAP unit (`is_snap_excluded_member` false) of a unit with positive `snap`; W-2 covers citizens and qualified non-citizens of a unit with positive `tanf` (the assistance group is assumed to include them); SSI is `ssi` or `receives_ssi`. Under the model's SNAP rules after Pub. L. 119-21, a refugee is outside the FoodShare group (companion test 7(g)). The Caretaker Supplement and Wisconsin's state SSI supplement, both named as categorical (3.3.1 item 2(c); Wis. Stat. 16.27(5)(c)), have no variable at this base.
4. **Categorical households above the limit (settled; source conflict).** Manual 2.3.1 item 1 and plan item 1.6 compute the benefit at the 60% SMI limit. The calculator has no such step: C10 to C12 hold the actual ratio at 2.15 and C40 pays the categorical household on it. The two agree for sizes 1 to 6, where the limit is above 215% of the guideline (245.5% for one person), and differ from size 7 (limit 205.0% of the guideline; size 8 188.3%). The branch follows the manual and plan (user decision); companion test 6 gives $306 against the calculator's $291.
5. **Maximum benefit (settled; source conflict).** Plan item 2.6 prints $2,147, the agency-posted plan $2,580 and calculator C17 $2,575. The branch uses $2,580 (user decision). The largest award the FFY2026 constants can produce is $2,574 (companion test 8(e)), so $2,575 and $2,580 never bind; $2,147 would bind only for fuel oil single-family homes of five to nine rooms with costs at twice the proxy and low ratios (uncapped $2,192 to $2,574). The FFY2027 agency plan prints $2,784.
6. **Proxy bounds (settled; source conflict).** Manual 2.3.1 items 2 to 5 call the proxy 75% of the average cost, cap actual cost at two times the proxy and raise it to the proxy. The calculator floors at 0.75 times and caps at 2 times the table value (C30, C31); on the manual's wording the cap would be 1.5 times the table value. The branch follows the calculator (user decision).
7. **Electric baseload (inference).** The calculator removes 60% of the bill only when the electric meter serves both heat and other use (C22, usage “b”), and D19 asks for the entire annual bill. The model's electric bill is the whole bill, so the branch removes 60% for every ELECTRICITY household; heat-only electric meters are not identified. Manual item 6 concerns the non-heating benefit.
8. **Rooms (simplification).** `bedrooms`, held between 1 and 9, stands in for the 4.4.17 room count, which also counts kitchens, living and dining rooms; most homes are therefore undercounted and their proxy is lower. A studio counts one room (the calculator rejects zero). A motel or camper counts one room.
9. **Dwelling type (new input).** `wi_wheap_dwelling_type` defaults to SINGLE_FAMILY, so a caller that omits it gets the single-family proxy. MOTEL_OR_CAMPER uses the calculator's rooming-house row; the Help Desk approval motels need (4.4.13) is not modeled. Cells flagged IsFake are used as published; the mobile home fuel oil per-room amount is negative (-13).
10. **Fuels (coverage limit and inference).** `heating_type` is a required input (settled); UNSPECIFIED and NONE pay $0 (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the default). Kerosene, wood and OTHER use the wood-and-other row (4.4.28.3); coal is not named in any Wisconsin source and joins that row by inference. SOLAR has no calculator class, so its heating cost is 0; a SOLAR household with a bill stays eligible with a $0 award. Heat pumps go to the Help Desk (4.4.28.3).
11. **Energy burden and housing (simplification).** Burden is `has_heating_expense` (a positive bill for the named fuel, heat not in rent) or heat in rent without `receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing`. Section 42 tenants keep the burden (3.2.5.1 note) but cannot be told apart if they report rental assistance. Separate payments to a landlord, shared and business meters (proxy floor, C35), in-kind rent, group homes and institutions have no input. A known fuel with a $0 bill and no heat in rent has no burden here; 4.4.28.4 processes a paying household that lacks bills with “zero” costs on the proxy, which is not modeled.
12. **Countable income items (simplification).** Self-employment, farm, partnership, rental and royalty income are netted across sources and members and floored at zero (3.3.5); the S-GIRF route, net operating losses, rent paid by household members and the $120 land-rent threshold are not separable; a minor's or student's self-employment is excluded with wages. Other sources are floored one by one (settled); `rental_income` is assumed nonnegative (settled). High school students are `is_in_k12_school`; 3.3.2 says full-time and Table 3.6 says full or part-time. Withdrawals count from age 73 only; regular withdrawals before 73 and inherited IRAs cannot be identified. Inaccessible interest (IRAs, CDs) is not identified. `general_assistance` cannot separate Interim Assistance, which Table 3.6 ignores; `financial_assistance` stands in for gifts; tribal per capita, land contract interest and the state SSI line have no input; voluntary child support paid is not separated. Plan item 1.9 checks one-time lump sums and leaves General Assistance unchecked; the branch follows the manual, which ignores most lump sums and counts General Relief.
13. **Social Security and Medicare (settled).** Plan item 1.9 checks “Excluding MediCare deduction” and Table 3.5 deducts Part B, C and D premiums. The branch counts `social_security` plus `railroad_benefits`, less the computed `medicare_part_b_premium`, floored at zero per person; Part C and D premiums and the deduction from federal civil service retirement pay have no input. Companion tests 13 and 14(e) use premiums of $0 and $2,434.80 as inputs.
14. **Federal 110% floor (federal law).** No Wisconsin source states the floor. The branch applies 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B) with the 2025 guideline at the program size, rounded to cents, and a strict “less than”. It binds only from size 20 (size 19: limit 126,348 above the 126,115 floor).
15. **Years and dates (simplification).** All parameters start `2025-10-01`; annual periods read 1 January values, so period 2026 applies FFY2026 to the whole calendar year, including October to December 2026, which fall in FFY2027. Period 2027 keeps the FFY2026 constants with the FY2027 SMI and 2026 guidelines; its limits differ by $1 from PY27 Appendix E at sizes 1, 5 and 6 (39,863, 88,926 and 101,192 against 39,864, 88,927 and 101,193), PY27 ignores gambling winnings, and the PY27 maximum is $2,784. Period 2025 uses backfilled values with the FY2025 SMI and 2024 guidelines.
16. **Plan editions and the manual (source wording).** The ACF-accepted plan answers item 1.4 Yes; the agency-posted plan answers No; both narratives and the manual require every member to be a recipient, which the branch follows.
17. **Other gaps.** Funding availability, the February 1 reduction (Wis. Stat. 16.27(4)(b)), supplemental benefits, one benefit per season, the application window, automated applications, the $1 SNAP benefit of 16.27(5)(e) (plan item 1.7a: none) and payment routing are not modeled. The calculator's unused 215% flag (C14) is not modeled.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-wi-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-wi-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [us-wi-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-wi-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml) (PY26 manual, June 2026 re-issue)
- [us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml) (2025 guidelines; 2024 for the period 2025 estimate)
- [us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml) (2026 guidelines and FY2027 SMI, period 2027 estimate)
- [state-statutes.current.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/state-statutes.current.yaml) (whole-code source `us-wi-statutes`, Wis. Stat. 16.27)
- [liheap-agent-queue.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/liheap-agent-queue.yaml) (42 U.S.C. 8621 to 8630 statute scope; Wisconsin `matrix_status: absent`)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-wi/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the PY26 limits for sizes 1 to 20 and the inclusive limit, the federal 110% floor and its strict edge, categorical eligibility of every member and the benefit at the limit, household size with ineligible non-citizens and non-citizens receiving Social Security, every counted, deducted and ignored income rule the branch encodes, the poverty ratio floor 0.60 and cap 2.15, the 2.66667 and 2.94269 constants, all 25 proxy pairs, rooms from 1 to 9 and the motel rule, the 0.75 and 2 times bounds, the electric baseload, heat in rent and subsidized housing, truncation, the $30 minimum and the maximum, the fuel mapping (kerosene, wood, coal, other, solar, none and unspecified), and any 2025 or 2027 period kept in scope. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Kansas LIHEAP in Axiom, covering the agreed scope and effective periods of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with signed RuleSpec encodings and reproducible oracle validation.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9663 (branch `ks-liheap`), open and not yet merged. Scope, policy periods, module paths, source text, required outputs and companion tests are in the sections below. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## PolicyEngine implementation (historical snapshot)

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9663, open and not yet merged. Head `67d231acd5` on 2026-10-02. The merged commit will be recorded here once it exists.
- **Scope:** the regular heating benefit of the Kansas Low Income Energy Assistance Program (LIEAP), which KEESM 13100 defines as a "Heating Only" program paid as a single annual benefit. Out of scope: crisis assistance, cooling, weatherization, heating-equipment purchase or repair, the end-of-season supplement DCF may issue if funds allow, and the auto-issuance path (KEESM 13350).
- **Policy periods:** two seasons. Federal fiscal year 2025 (2024-10-01 to 2025-09-30) is read at model period `2025`; parameters are dated `2024-10-01`. Federal fiscal year 2026 (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30) is read at model period `2026`; parameters are dated `2025-10-01`. Every Kansas variable is annual and reads the value in force on 1 January of the model year, so period `2026` carries the FY2026 limits, exemption and matrix. The registry records `verified_years: "2025-2026"`.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/ks/dcf/liheap/`: `ks_liheap`, `ks_liheap_household_size`, `ks_liheap_fuel_category`, the inputs `ks_liheap_dwelling_type` and `ks_liheap_utility_rate_tier`; `eligibility/ks_liheap_eligible`, `ks_liheap_income_eligible`, `ks_liheap_income_limit`, `ks_liheap_energy_vulnerable`; `income/ks_liheap_countable_income`, `ks_liheap_countable_earned_income`, `ks_liheap_countable_unearned_income`, `ks_liheap_countable_interest_dividend_income`; `payment/ks_liheap_income_band`, `ks_liheap_household_size_group`, `ks_liheap_matrix_amount`.
- **Parameters:** `gov.states.ks.dcf.liheap` (`eligibility/`: `fpg_rate`, `fpg_year_lag`, `max_table_size`, `rounding_increment`; `income/`: `earned_income_min_age`, `interest_income_min_age`, `regular_interest_dividend_exemption`, `sources/earned`, `sources/unearned`; `payment/`: `income_band`, `household_size_group`, `min_benefit`, and `matrix/natural_gas`, `matrix/electricity`, `matrix/propane`, `matrix/other`).
- **Tests:** 131 YAML cases in 14 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/ks/dcf/liheap/`.

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence in a manifest on axiom-corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-02 against the manifest copies saved in `corpus/`. Presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not checked. The KEESM manifest holds one edition only: the undated "Current" manual captured 2026-05-27 with expression date 2026-04-01. The PR cites the edition-pinned October 2024, July 2025 and January 2026 copies instead. On 2026-10-02 the April 2026 edition on DCF's site is word-for-word the January 2026 edition for every section below apart from the edition stamp, and the "Current" URL now serves the October 2026 edition, whose 13362 table already carries the FY2027 limits ($1,995 for one person, $710 per additional person). Pin ingests to the edition folders.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-ks/policies/dcf/keesm/keesm13000/program-summary` | 13100: single annual "Heating Only" benefit; the four eligibility criteria; application period ends the last business day of March | `us-ks/manual/dcf/keesm/keesm13000` | In manifest `us-ks-keesm.yaml` (April 2026 edition). Same text in the October 2024 and January 2026 editions the PR cites: [KEESM 13000, October 2024](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo10-24/Robo_10_01_24/keesm13000.htm) and [January 2026](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo01-26/Robo_01_01_26/keesm13000.htm). |
| `us-ks/policies/dcf/keesm/keesm13200/proof-of-information` | 13230: gross income anticipated for the month of application | `us-ks/manual/dcf/keesm/keesm13200` | In manifest `us-ks-keesm.yaml`. Same text in [KEESM 13200, October 2024](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo10-24/Robo_10_01_24/keesm13200.htm) and [January 2026](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo01-26/Robo_01_01_26/keesm13200.htm). |
| `us-ks/policies/dcf/keesm/keesm13300/household-definition`, `.../citizenship-and-alienage`, `.../energy-vulnerability` | 13310 one regular benefit per program year; 13320 household; 13330 citizen or qualified alien, excluded members; 13340 heating responsibility, shared heat, own-cut wood, subsidized housing | `us-ks/manual/dcf/keesm/keesm13300` | In manifest `us-ks-keesm.yaml`. 13310 to 13340 read the same in [KEESM 13300, October 2024](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo10-24/Robo_10_01_24/keesm13300.htm) and [January 2026](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo01-26/Robo_01_01_26/keesm13300.htm); the January 2026 edition adds 13350 auto issuance, which was "Reserve" in October 2024. |
| `us-ks/policies/dcf/keesm/keesm13360/income-eligibility`, `.../exempt-income`, `.../income-guidelines` | 13360 gross income of all persons at the address, 150% of poverty, self-employment, deemed income eligible, no asset test; 13361 exempt income; 13362 monthly limit table | `us-ks/manual/dcf/keesm/keesm13360` | In manifest `us-ks-keesm.yaml` for FY2026 only (the April 2026 copy matches [KEESM 13360, January 2026](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo01-26/Robo_01_01_26/keesm13360.htm) and [July 2025](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo07-25/Robo_07_01_25/keesm13360.htm), the first edition with the FY2026 table). FY2025 needs ingest of [KEESM 13360, October 2024](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo10-24/Robo_10_01_24/keesm13360.htm): its 13362 table holds the FY2025 limits ($1,882.50 to $6,590.00, $672.50 per additional person) and its 13361 holds the $50-a-month interest and dividend exemption. |
| `us-ks/policies/dcf/keesm/keesm13400/benefit-levels` | 13410: benefit varies by household income, dwelling type, primary heating fuel, household size and utility rates | `us-ks/manual/dcf/keesm/keesm13400` | In manifest `us-ks-keesm.yaml`. 13410 reads the same in [KEESM 13400, October 2024](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo10-24/Robo_10_01_24/keesm13400.htm) and [January 2026](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo01-26/Robo_01_01_26/keesm13400.htm); 13421 vendor-name wording differs between the two. |
| `us-ks/policies/dcf/keesm/keesm6300` | Earned income definition (wages, salary, profit from services including managerial responsibilities) | `us-ks/manual/dcf/keesm/keesm6300` | In manifest `us-ks-keesm.yaml`. Same text in [KEESM 6300, October 2024](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo10-24/Robo_10_01_24/keesm6300.htm) and [January 2026](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo01-26/Robo_01_01_26/keesm6300.htm). |
| `us-ks/policies/dcf/keesm/keesm6313` | Self-employment; rental property income unearned unless managed 20 hours a week; a loss cannot offset other income | `us-ks/manual/dcf/keesm/keesm6313` | In manifest `us-ks-keesm.yaml`. Same operative text in [KEESM 6313, October 2024](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo10-24/Robo_10_01_24/keesm6313.htm) and [January 2026](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo01-26/Robo_01_01_26/keesm6313.htm) (one cross-reference to the definitions appendix changed). |
| `us-ks/policies/dcf/keesm/keesm7122` | 7122.1: 25% standard income-producing cost deduction or actual costs; no loss offset | `us-ks/manual/dcf/keesm/keesm7122` | In manifest `us-ks-keesm.yaml`. Same text in [KEESM 7122, October 2024](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo10-24/Robo_10_01_24/keesm7122.htm) and [January 2026](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/KEESM/Robo01-26/Robo_01_01_26/keesm7122.htm). |
| `us-ks/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026-benefit-matrix` | FY2026 "Benefit Adjustment @ 80%" tables: natural gas (page 1), electricity (page 2), propane (page 3), other (page 4) | `us-ks/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026-benefit-matrix` | In manifest `us-ks-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml` (4 pages, PDF dated 2025-09-09). Same file the PR cites: [FY2026 benefit matrix, pages 1-4](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/benefits-matricies/KS_BenefitMatrix_2026.pdf#page=1). Each page prints the unadjusted table on the left and the adjusted table on the right. |
| `us-ks/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2025-benefit-matrix` | FY2025 "Ben Adj 100.0%" tables: natural gas and electricity tiers A-I of the first band (page 1), the rest of electricity and propane bands 1-2 (page 2), propane bands 3-4 and other (page 3) | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [FY2025 benefit matrix, pages 1-3](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2025/benefits-matricies/KS_BenefitMatrix_2025.pdf#page=1) (3 pages, PDF dated 2024-09-23). |
| `us-ks/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-1` and `.../section-2` | 1.4 categorical eligibility; 1.8 gross income; 1.9 countable income forms (pages 5-7); 2.1 150% of the HHS poverty guidelines; 2.3 no asset test, subsidized renters; 2.5 benefit variables; 2.6 minimum $130, maximum $4,301 (pages 8-9) | `us-ks/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | In manifest `us-ks-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml`, segmented by "Section N" headings. Same file the PR cites: [FY2026 state plan, pages 5-9](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/state-plans/KS_Plan_2026.pdf#page=5). The text layer does not carry the check-box states; those were read from the rendered pages. |
| `us-ks/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2025/section-1` and `.../section-2` | Same questions; 2.6 minimum $100, maximum $2,232 (page 9); different boxes in 1.9 (page 6) | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [FY2025 state plan, pages 5-9](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2025/state-plans/KS_Plan_2025.pdf#page=5). |
| `us/` poverty guidelines module | 2024 guidelines ($15,060 for one person, $5,380 per additional person) for FY2025; 2025 guidelines ($15,650 and $5,500) for FY2026 | none for 2024 or 2025 | `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml` holds the 2026 guidelines only; `us-hhs-poverty-guidelines.yaml` is named in `corpus-manifests.txt` but its contents were not saved here and the 2026 manifest notes its undated path "was never extracted". Official notices: [FR Doc. 2024-00796, page 2](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2024-01-17/pdf/2024-00796.pdf#page=2) and [FR Doc. 2025-01377, page 1](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-17/pdf/2025-01377.pdf#page=1). |

The PR also cites the [LIHEAP Clearinghouse Kansas profile](https://liheapch.acf.gov/profiles/Kansas.htm) for the $130 minimum and the [DCF Energy Assistance page](https://www.dcf.ks.gov/services/ees/Pages/EnergyAssistance.aspx) for the possible end-of-season supplement. Neither is in a saved manifest; neither carries a rule the modules need.

## Source text (verbatim)

KEESM quotations are from the January 2026 edition unless marked; the October 2024 edition is identical except where quoted separately. Local copies are in `sources/ks/`.

**Program.** KEESM 13100: "The Low Income Energy Assistance Program (LIEAP) is federally funded assistance which helps qualifying households pay home energy costs through the issuance of a single annual benefit. The Kansas LIEAP program is defined as a "Heating Only" program based on federal program definitions and is designed to assist households with their winter heating costs." The criteria: "Combined income of all persons living at the address must not exceed 150% of the federal poverty level;" "An adult household member must be personally responsible for purchasing heating fuel costs incurred at the current residence, payable either to the landlord or to the fuel vendor;" "The household must meet citizenship or lawful residency requirements; and" "The household must meet application requirements." Period: "While the start date will vary in any given year, the application period ends the last business day of March in the program year."

KEESM 13310: "No person or household may receive a regular LIEAP benefit more than once in a program year."

**Household.** KEESM 13320: "household" means any individual or group of individuals who are living together as one economic unit for whom residential energy is customarily purchased in common or who make undesignated payments for energy in the form of rent. And: "The application shall include all persons that normally reside in the household. The income of all household members living together, is used to determine eligibility. If a household member is or turns eighteen in the month of application, his/her income is countable."

**Citizenship.** KEESM 13330: "Households must contain at least one member who is a U.S. Citizen or "qualified alien." Applicants currently receiving Food Assistance, cash or medical assistance will categorically meet the alienage requirement for energy assistance." Then: "Qualified aliens include: legal permanent residents, refugees, asylees, individuals paroled into the U.S. for a period of at least one year, individuals whose deportation has been withheld, individuals granted conditional entry, and certain individuals who are victims of sexual harassment and survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking." And: "Household members who are not citizens or lawful permanent residents will not be considered in determining household size, although the income from such members will be counted in determining total household income."

**Income limit.** KEESM 13360: "The combined gross income of all persons living at the residence address shall not exceed 150% of the federal poverty level. (See 13362.) Countable income includes earnings by adults, unearned income of adults and children, public assistance benefits, social security benefits, interest earnings and most other income. In determining income eligibility, gross income received or intended for the month of application is countable." And: "There are no asset or resource tests."

KEESM 13362: "The gross income (before deductions) of all persons living at the residence address is considered in determining household income. The following eligibility limits represent 150% of the federal poverty level:" Column headings "Number in Household" and "One Month Income at 150% of Poverty Level".

| Number in household | October 2024 edition (FY2025) | July 2025 and January 2026 editions (FY2026) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | $1,882.50 | $1,956 |
| 2 | $2,555.00 | $2,644 |
| 3 | $3,227.50 | $3331 (printed without a comma) |
| 4 | $3,900.00 | $4,019 |
| 5 | $4,572.50 | $4,706 |
| 6 | $5,245.00 | $5,394 |
| 7 | $5,917.50 | $6,081 |
| 8 | $6,590.00 | $6,769 |
| For each additional person | $672.50 | $688 |

FY2026 state plan, section 2.1 (page 8): "All Household Sizes", "HHS Poverty Guidelines", "150.00%". Section 2.3 (page 8): "Do you require an Assets test?" is answered No.

**Categorical eligibility.** FY2026 state plan, section 1.4 (page 5): TANF, SSI and SNAP are marked Yes for heating; 1.4a: "If a household member receives one of the benefits listed above, they are considered income eligible, and we use the income already verified through that program for the LIEAP case." KEESM 13360: "Individuals on a LIEAP application may be "Deemed Income Eligible" if they have an active Food Assistance or TANF case in the month that they apply for LIEAP and the income reflected in the Food Assistance/TANF case has been verified. Any adults not deemed income eligible would be subject to income verifications as detailed earlier in 13360. It is possible that the combination of countable verified income for those deemed income eligible and the income of any adults not deemed income eligible could still exceed the allowable income guidelines." And: "Since gross income of all adult household members is a factor in determining the benefit level, verified countable income for each deemed income eligible individual in addition to countable income for any individuals not deemed income eligible must be determined to allow for the calculation of an appropriate benefit."

**What income counts.** FY2026 state plan, section 1.8 (page 5): "In determining a household's income eligibility for LIHEAP, do you use gross income or net income?" with "Gross Income" checked.
