Every FY2026 amount above depends on this choice.
- **FY2026 minimum.** The plan's "Minimum Benefit $130" is applied as a floor to the 63 adjusted cells below $130; KEESM 13410 has no minimum. `integration.yaml` Case 9 (propane, tier A, trailer/other, wages $21,600: cell $75, paid $130) and `ks_liheap.yaml` Case 1 (other fuel, trailer/other, five members, wages $30,000: cell $128, paid $130) depend on it; `ks_liheap.yaml` Case 2 (natural gas, tier A, trailer/other, five members, wages $9,600: cell $138, paid $138) does not. In FY2025 the lowest cell ($100, `integration.yaml` Case 12) equals the $100 minimum, so that season does not exercise the floor. The plan's $4,301 maximum is unexplained and never binds.
- **Categorical eligibility.** FY2026 plan 1.4a says a household with a TANF, SSI or SNAP member is "considered income eligible". KEESM 13360 says deemed-eligible individuals' verified income still counts and the household total "could still exceed the allowable income guidelines". The PR follows KEESM: `integration.yaml` Case 5 (two retirees, Social Security $20,000 and $15,000, SSI $1,200: total $36,200 above the size 2 limit $31,728, not eligible), `eligibility/ks_liheap_income_eligible.yaml` Cases 7-9 and `eligibility/ks_liheap_eligible.yaml` Case 6 rest on that reading.
- **Household size and qualified aliens.** KEESM 13330's size sentence names "citizens or lawful permanent residents"; its list of qualified aliens is broader. The PR counts every federal qualified status (LPR, refugee, asylee, deportation withheld, Cuban or Haitian entrant, conditional entrant, paroled one year or more). Kansas does not name Cuban or Haitian entrants, and its "victims of sexual harassment and survivors of domestic violence" category has no input. `ks_liheap_household_size.yaml` Case 7 (refugee with a citizen child counts two) depends on this. The rule that Food Assistance, cash or medical assistance recipients "categorically meet the alienage requirement" is not modeled. An excluded member's income counts in full with no proration, as 13330 states.
- **Self-employment.** KEESM 13360 and 7122.1 count gross receipts less a 25% standard deduction (or actual costs), averaged. The PR counts the model's net self-employment, SSTB, farm and partnership or S corporation inputs as they are, with no further deduction, and floors each source at zero (6313, 7122.1). Treating partnership or S corporation income as earned rests on the 6300 definition ("profit resulting from the performance of services, including managerial responsibilities"). Rental and farm rental income are counted as unearned (6313) without the 25% deduction that 6313's note describes; `rental_income` is assumed non-negative.
- **Interest and dividends.** FY2026: the exemption for interest and dividends "received irregularly, are unpredictable and are less than $30 in a quarter" cannot be identified from annual inputs, so every positive amount counts (`income/ks_liheap_countable_interest_dividend_income.yaml` Case 3: $120 of interest counts). FY2025: the $50-a-month test is applied to annual interest plus dividends divided by 12, and when exceeded the dividends count along with the interest although the text says "the full amount of interest". Children's interest is excluded at every age under 18; their dividends count. Burial-fund interest is not modeled. The FY2026 plan leaves "Interest, dividends, or royalties" unchecked in 1.9 while the FY2025 plan checks it; the PR follows KEESM 13360 ("interest earnings") in both seasons.
- **Income sources without a matching input.** The plan checks "Contract Income", "Payments from mortgage or Sales Contracts", "Commissions", "Legal settlements" and, for FY2026, "Cash gifts" and "Jury duty compensation". Contract and mortgage payments, legal settlements and adoption support have no model input. Cash support from outside the household (`financial_assistance`) is not counted because KEESM 13361 exempts only irregular gifts up to $50 a month and the input cannot separate regular from irregular. KEESM 13361 (January 2026) exempts "jury duty payments", contrary to the plan; there is no input. The FY2025 plan checks "One-time lump-sum payments"; KEESM 13361 exempts lump sums; none is modeled. "Insurance payments made directly to the insured" is represented by `workers_compensation`. Social Security counts gross, Medicare premium included (the plan checks the "Including MediCare" box). SNAP is in-kind and not counted. IRA and 401(k) withdrawals are exempt and not counted.
- **Income period.** KEESM 13360 and 13230 count gross income received or intended for the month of application, with weekly and biweekly conversion factors and a prior-month rule for strikers. The PR uses annual income divided by 12 for both the limit and the band. The matrix prints whole-dollar bands ("0 - 899", "900 - 1,199"); the PR compares unrounded monthly income with thresholds 900, 1,200 and 1,700, so $899.50 stays in band 1. Negative countable income is floored to band 1 (`payment/ks_liheap_income_band.yaml` Case 11).
- **Income limit arithmetic.** The one-year guideline lag and the rounding are inferred from the published tables, not stated: FY2025 prints cents and equals 150% of the 2024 guidelines; FY2026 prints whole dollars that match half-up rounding of 150% of the 2025 guidelines, with the additional-person increment rounded separately ($687.50 to $688). The limit is derived from the guideline parameters rather than stored; `eligibility/ks_liheap_income_limit.yaml` Cases 3-8 are reform and fallback regressions, not Kansas policy.
- **Household and period mapping.** The SPM unit stands in for "all persons living at the residence address"; KEESM 13320's exceptions (paid live-in attendants, landlord and tenant in room-and-board arrangements, students, congregate living) are not modeled. "Is or turns eighteen in the month of application" is read as age 18 or older in the model year. Calendar year 2026 stands in for the FY2026 season (applications run from autumn 2025 to the last business day of March 2026); the FY2025 rules apply to calendar 2025.
- **Energy vulnerability facts.** Shared unmetered heat, homeless households with prior-address heating debt, HUD "excess" utility charges, FHA projects, and landlord-billed purchases cannot be derived; `ks_liheap_energy_vulnerable` can be set directly (`eligibility/ks_liheap_energy_vulnerable.yaml` Cases 5-7). A zero wood bill is the proxy for cutting one's own wood. Heat included in unsubsidized rent is treated as responsibility under 13340 even with no separate bill: the benefit is then the table for the reported fuel at the input tier, or, when the fuel is unspecified, the other-fuel table (`eligibility/ks_liheap_energy_vulnerable.yaml` Case 3: $639). Outside that case `heating_type` is a required input and an unspecified fuel pays $0 because no bill is read (`eligibility/ks_liheap_energy_vulnerable.yaml` Case 2).
- **Fuel, tier and dwelling.** Solar maps to the electricity table; fuel oil, kerosene, wood, coal and other map to the other-fuel table (`ks_liheap_fuel_category.yaml`). The utility range tier is a provider attribute from DCF's rate survey that no public document lists; it is an input defaulting to E. Dwelling type is an input defaulting to house/modular/mobile.
- **Not modeled.** 13310 (Kansas residence beyond `state_code`, legal capacity, tribal LIHEAP exclusivity, once per program year), 13350 auto issuance, 13420 payment splitting and vendor rules, 13450 overpayment recovery, the application period, and any end-of-season supplement.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [FY2026 state-plan manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ks-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [Benefit-matrix attachments manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ks-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml)

These FY2026 manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Link the PE PR and agree the component scope, effective periods, inputs, and outputs. Cover the eligibility and benefit-calculation behavior actually in scope; identify any excluded program components explicitly.
- [ ] Audit official sources and reuse existing corpus content. Ingest missing official documents with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance; obtain signed ingest/release admission. Keep any toolchain or corpus-pin change in its own gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state rule modules with the approved encoder, placing state content under `us-ks/` in the canonical layout. Include source-grounded proofs, benefit parameters where applicable, and companion tests for representative cases, boundaries, and ineligibility. Every test supplies all local inputs.
- [ ] Use personal-Codex local generation followed by exact-commit reviewed-candidate promotion for eligible modules: review the rule/test bytes, obtain the protected allowlist entry for the commit/base branch, and run protected validation/signing with the required approval. Retain the signed manifests and evidence that rule/test bytes are unchanged.
- [ ] Assemble and validate a runnable program with the required indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing blocker before declaring the complete program shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) is currently open.
- [ ] Add concept/input/output mappings and reproducible fixtures in axiom-oracles against the merged PE implementation, pinned to an exact commit. Record units and periods, compare representative and boundary cases, and resolve or explicitly disposition mismatches against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, and oracle PRs and successful CI/promotion evidence. Record the shipped scope and any remaining gaps.

## Contribution route

Use the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion contract](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion), added by [axiom-encode#1696](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/pull/1696). It validates and signs explicitly admitted reviewed content without regenerating it; it does not authenticate the original generating runtime. The [planned personal-Codex experiment](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1622#issuecomment-5940016560) records the process. The five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs are not prerequisites for testing this route.

This issue tracks work to ship; it does not claim the encoding, promotion experiment, or PE parity validation is already complete.

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Indiana EAP in Axiom, covering the agreed scope and effective periods of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with signed RuleSpec encodings and reproducible oracle validation.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9728 (branch `in-eap`), open and not yet merged. Scope, policy periods, module paths, source text, required outputs and companion tests are in the sections below. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## PolicyEngine implementation (historical snapshot)

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9728, open and not yet merged. Head `2a04f374f4` on 2026-10-03 (branch `in-eap`; adds the Medicare premium deduction and military retirement pay, plus a merge of `main`). The merged commit will be recorded here once it exists.
- **Scope:** regular heating assistance and its winter electric allowance only (manual Section 8.7 ties the allowance to operating the heating system). Crisis assistance, cooling, weatherization, Emergency Repair and Replacement, credit-balance holds and discretionary supplements are out of scope.
- **Policy period:** federal fiscal year 2026 (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30); the state plan runs the heating component from 10/01/2025 to 04/20/2026. The model reads it for period `2026` (parameter values dated 2025-10-01). Period `2025` reads the six values dated 2024-10-01 from the PY2024-25 benefit matrix (income points 6, 4, 2; electric $100, $75, $50; zero fuel points for natural gas and electric heat) and the FY2025 state median income; every other FY2025 value is backfilled from FY2026. The registry records `verified_years: "2026"`.
- **Variables:** `in_eap`, `in_eap_eligible`, `in_eap_income`, `in_eap_smi`, `in_eap_household_size` and the input `in_eap_dwelling_type` (`SINGLE_FAMILY`, `MOBILE_HOME`, `MULTI_UNIT`), under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/in/ihcda/eap/`.
- **Parameters:** `gov.states.in.ihcda.eap` (21 files): `eligibility/` (`adult_age`, `income_limit`, `minimum_monthly_rent`), `income/` (`calculation_months`, `sources`, `student_age_limit`) and `benefit/` (`amount_per_point`, `dwelling_points`, `fuel_points`, `heating_award_fuels`, `income/lower_points`, `middle_points`, `higher_points`, `lower_rate`, `middle_rate`, `electricity/lower_income`, `middle_income`, `higher_income`, `vulnerability/elderly_age`, `points`, `young_child_age_limit`). State median income comes from the shared `gov.hhs.smi` tree.
- **Tests:** 38 YAML cases in `in_eap.yaml` (16), `in_eap_eligible.yaml` (5), `in_eap_income.yaml` (8) and `integration.yaml` (9) under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/in/ihcda/eap/`.

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence in a manifest on axiom-corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-02. Presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not checked.

The only Indiana manual in the corpus is a different edition from the one the PR cites. Manifest `us-in-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml` holds the Program Year 2024 manual, version 1.0 (`us-in/manual/ihcda/liheap-intake-and-operations-manual`, 111 PDF pages, created 2023-09-07). Its benefit sections sit on PDF pages 64-71 (income charts 65-66, dwelling and fuel 66-67, at-risk and electric 67, total benefit 70-71; the manifest records `benefit_matrix_pdf_pages: 60-71`) and carry different values: income points 8, 6, 4; dwelling 2, 2, 1; fuel 12, 3, 3; at-risk 4; a flat $150 electric benefit; FFY 2023 state median income of $89,193. It cannot ground FY2026 or FY2025. The PR cites the PY2026 manual (122 PDF pages; printed page numbers are two less than PDF pages; income charts on PDF pages 69-70, dwelling and fuel 71, vulnerable and electric 72-73, total benefit 77). Three documents need ingest: the PY2026 manual, the PY2025-26 benefit matrix and the PY2024-25 benefit matrix.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-in/policies/ihcda/liheap-intake-and-operations-manual/py2026/3-1-who-can-get-eap-benefits` | Section 3.1: annual income at or below 60% of state median income; Indiana residency and active utility service; pending eviction writ | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [IHCDA PY2026 Intake and Operations Manual, PDF pages 10, 23-27, 29, 32-33, 47-62 and 68-78](https://www.in.gov/ihcda/files/Indiana-LIHEAP-Intake-and-Operations-Program-Manual-PY2026.pdf#page=69) |
| `.../py2026/3-2-who-is-part-of-the-household` | Sections 3.2-3.3: three-month residence, pregnancy counted, roommates counted, excluded persons (PDF pages 23-25) | none | Same document; needs ingest |
| `.../py2026/3-4-who-is-vulnerable` | Section 3.4: disability by SSA or listed benefit receipt, elderly 60 or older, veterans, child five or under, pregnancy; points awarded once (PDF pages 26-27) | none | Same document; needs ingest |
| `.../py2026/4-4-citizenship` | Section 4.4: citizens, nationals and qualified non-citizens under 8 U.S.C. 1641(b); ineligible members excluded from size but their income counted; applicant aged 18 (PDF page 29) | none | Same document; needs ingest. The qualified-alien definition already exists in rulespec-us as `us/statutes/8/1641/b`; its corpus manifest was not identified in `corpus-manifests.txt` |
| `.../py2026/4-7-direct-benefit-payment` | Section 4.7: utilities in rent keep regular-benefit eligibility; $1 monthly rent minimum; renter benefit table; self-cut firewood has no heating burden (PDF pages 32-33) | none | Same document; needs ingest |
| `.../py2026/6-income-computations` | Section 6 and 6.1: members 18 and above; most recent three months, times four for eligibility; counted sources, gross wages, gross business income, Social Security net of Medicare premiums, child SSA benefits (PDF pages 47-57) | none | Same document; needs ingest |
| `.../py2026/6-2-what-is-not-counted-as-income` | Section 6.2: under-18 income, dependent students, child support received, lump sums, capital gains, tax refunds, TANF, Medicare Part B premium; child support paid deducted (PDF pages 57-62) | none | Same document; needs ingest |
| `.../py2026/8-3-income-level-determination` | Section 8.3: 9, 5, 2 income points by three-month income against 30%, 45% and 60% of SMI, sizes 1-10; heat in rent gets 2 points (PDF pages 69-70) | none | Same document; needs ingest |
| `.../py2026/8-4-dwelling` | Section 8.4: 3, 2, 1 dwelling points; 0 when heat is in rent; manufactured home on a foundation is single-family (PDF pages 70-71) | none | Same document; needs ingest |
| `.../py2026/8-5-primary-heating-fuel-source` | Section 8.5: bulk fuels 6, natural gas 1, electric 1, heat in rent 0 (PDF page 71) | none | Same document; needs ingest |
| `.../py2026/8-6-vulnerable-populations` | Section 8.6: 2 points once per household (PDF pages 71-72) | none | Same document; needs ingest |
| `.../py2026/8-7-electric-utility-payments` | Section 8.7: $125, $100, $50 by the same income chart; $50 when electricity is in rent (PDF pages 72-73) | none | Same document; needs ingest |
| `.../py2026/8-11-total-benefit` | Section 8.11: points times $25 plus electric; no electric service, no electric benefit; with Section 1.1 (kerosene barred, PDF page 10), 8.8 (utility burden, PDF page 74) and 8.13 (unsafe or inoperable heat gets the electric credit only, PDF page 78) (PDF page 77) | none | Same document; needs ingest |
| `us-in/policies/ihcda/eap-benefit-matrix/py2025-2026` | Form MTRX-2026 (revised 2025.08.05): sizes 1-8 one-month and three-month ceilings; 9, 5, 2 points; $125, $100, $50; utility-in-rent column 2 points and $50; instructions | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [PY2025-26 benefit matrix and instructions, pages 1-2](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/benefits-matricies/IN_BenefitMatrix_Heat-Crisis_2026.pdf#page=1) |
| `us-in/policies/ihcda/eap-benefit-matrix/py2024-2025` | PY2024-25 matrix (revised 2024.07.24): 6, 4, 2 points; $100, $75, $50; natural gas and electric 0 fuel points; sizes 1-8 ceilings; source of the six FY2025 values | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [PY2024-25 benefit matrix and instructions, pages 1-2](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2025/benefits-matricies/IN_BenefitMatrix_2025.pdf#page=1) |
| `us-in/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-2` | Plan section 2.1 (60% SMI, all sizes), 2.3 (renters with utilities in rent need out-of-pocket rent), 2.4-2.5 (vulnerable 2 points, electric benefit), 2.6 ($100 minimum, $625 maximum); section 1.8-1.9 countable-income checkboxes (gross income; SSA benefits excluding the Medicare deduction) | `us-in/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | In manifest `us-in-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml` (plan PDF pages 5-9). The 1.8-1.9 checkboxes are images, not extractable text |
| `us/policies/acf/ocs/liheap-im/2025-02/attachment-4-smi-table` | FY2026 state median income: Indiana four-person $107,555; 60% by size 1-12; the household-size percentages (52, 68, 84, 100, 116, 132, then 3 points per person) | none for FY2026 | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml` holds IM 2026-01 Attachment 4 (`us/guidance/acf/ocs/liheap-im/2026-01/attachment-4-smi-table`), the table for mandatory use in FY2027 and optional use in FY2026, where Indiana is $111,012; the PR uses the FY2026 mandatory table. Official copy: [LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 4, pages 1 and 4](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_IM2025-02_SMIStateTable_Att4.pdf#page=1) |
| `us/policies/acf/ocs/liheap-im/2024-02/attachment-4-smi-table` | FY2025 state median income: Indiana four-person $103,324, used by the period-2025 cases | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [LIHEAP IM 2024-02 Attachment 4, pages 1 and 4](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_IM%202024-02_Att4SMITable.pdf#page=1) |
| `us/regulations/45-cfr/96/85` | 45 CFR 96.85(b): household-size adjustment of state median income, used for sizes above the printed chart | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [45 CFR 96.85](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-A/part-96/subpart-H/section-96.85) |

## Source text (verbatim)

All manual citations are to the PY2026 Intake and Operations Manual by PDF page.

**Program.** Section 1.1 (PDF page 10): "An additional amount between $50-$125 for electricity is added to keep the heating system operational." and "Regular EAP funds can be used for connection, reconnection, and direct energy, fuel, or delivery costs. EAP funds may not be used for heating methods or fuels that are considered unsafe in residential settings, including, but not limited to, ovens, cooking stoves, portable space heaters, or kerosene."

**Income limit.** Section 3.1 (PDF page 23): "EAP benefits are available to households with a combined annual income at or below 60% of State Median income (see Section 8.3)."

State plan, section 2.1 (PDF page 8): eligibility threshold "All Household Sizes", "State Median Income", "60.00%".

**Household.** Section 3.2 (PDF page 23): "Anyone living in the household continuously for the past three (3) months must be listed on the application, except as provided in 3.3." Births: "If a household member is pregnant, the unborn child can be considered part of the household, regardless of the projected date of birth. The household will be awarded points under the vulnerable population category based on this child." Roommates: "Any roommates or housemates must be counted as household members if they are living in the household at the time of application, even if they are not related to other household members or are not direct parties to a lease or mortgage. Their income must be calculated as part of the household income."

**Citizenship.** Section 4.4 (PDF page 29): "In addition to the above criteria, eligible household members must be United States (U.S.) citizens, U.S. Nationals or qualified non-U.S. citizens (aliens) as defined by 8 U.S.C§1641(b)." "Persons who are not citizens or qualified non-US citizens are considered to be ineligible household members. Ineligible household members living with eligible household members do not disqualify the family from receiving assistance." "An applicant must only be eighteen (18) to apply." "In order to calculate the household’s eligibility, an LSP will exclude the ineligible household members from the total number of household members (total household size) when calculating the benefit amount. The income of the ineligible household member, however, must be counted when determining the total household income eligibility."

**Vulnerable members.** Section 3.4 (PDF pages 26-27): "Vulnerable population points are only awarded once per household; however, all applicable vulnerable population categories must be recorded in the statewide database." "A person is determined to be living with a disability if they receive benefits from the Social Security Administration (SSA)." "A household member may automatically be considered to be a person with a disability if the receive one or more of the following benefits:" SSI, SSDI, Veterans Disability, Medicaid Disability, MAABD, Railroad Retirement Disability, Vocational Rehabilitation Services, Black Lung Disability. "If the person with a disability does not receive any of the above benefits, they may present a doctor’s statement, along with a pending SSA application or appeal for benefits." "EAP considers households with elderly persons to be households containing a member sixty (60) years or older." "A Veteran household is defined as a household where any member of the household served or is serving for any length of time in any military service branch (Army, Navy, AirForce, Marines or Coast Guard) and received an honorable discharge if no longer participating in active services." "Households with at least one child age five (5) or under are considered vulnerable population households. This includes households with a member that is pregnant at the time of application."

**Utilities in rent.** Section 4.7 (PDF page 32): "If a household’s rent payment includes utilities in the rent, the applicant is eligible for an EAP regular benefit. Households with heating or electric utilities included in the rent will not be eligible for a crisis benefit." "Clients must be paying a minimum of $1 monthly in rent to receive an EAP benefit when utilities are included in the rent." "LSPs will calculate the benefit using the benefit matrix, whose details can be found in Section 8: EAP Benefits, in the same way as applicants whose utilities are not included in the rent." The renter table (PDF page 33) pays the electric vendor and the client when heat is in rent, the heating vendor and the client when electricity is in rent, and the client for both when all utilities are in rent. Firewood (PDF page 33): "If an applicant who heats with firewood discloses or is known by the LSP to cut their own firewood, this applicant does not have a heating burden, as their heating expenses are $0. Therefore, such applicants will be eligible for an electric benefit, but not a heating benefit."

State plan, section 2.3 (PDF page 8): "Applicants who rent their home and have utilities included in the rent must have an out-of-pocket rent responsibility (i.e., their rent is not 100% subsidized) in order to establish that an energy burden exists."

**Income period.** Section 6 (PDF page 47): "The household income is the total income received by all household members aged eighteen (18) and above during the application period. The total household income is used to determine financial eligibility for benefits. Households are eligible with an income up to 60% of State Median Income. Income computation is used to compute points on the benefit matrix." "In order to calculate income, LSPs will consider the most recent three (3) consecutive months or thirteen (13) consecutive weeks of income." "The statewide database will treat this three-month income as a representative sample, and will multiply the three-month income by four in order to calculate the annual income for eligibility determination." "Any income amount of one dollar ($1.00) or less (e.g., an interest accrual on a bank account of ten cents [$0.10]) may be excluded from income calculations."

**Counted income.** Section 6.1 (PDF page 47): "Income from employment may be gross wages, salaries, commissions, bonuses, profit-sharing, cashed-out vacation or sick pay, tips, military allotments, pensions, self-employment and other retirement payments such as private retirement plans." (PDF page 49): "LSPs are to calculate employment income based on the gross amount paid; however, if total gross and federal taxable gross income are both provided, the federal taxable gross income is to be used for the calculation." Self-employment (PDF page 51): "Self-employment income is an individual's income from a private trade or business (including farming)." "For the purposes of determining eligibility for LIHEAP benefits, LSPs will consider gross income and profits before allowable business expenses and other adjustments are applied." (PDF page 52) Schedule C: "Use line 5, Gross profit"; Schedule F: "Use line 9, Gross income." Pensions (PDF page 54): "Ongoing pension payments are counted as income." Life insurance (PDF page 54): "Life insurance payments issued on a regular basis to a surviving household member should be counted as income. Lump sum payments, however, should not be counted." Railroad (PDF page 55): "Railroad benefits should be calculated based on the net amount." Social Security (PDF page 55): "Only benefits paid during the three-month calculation period should be counted. The net amount of the Social Security check, after the deduction for Medicare Part B premiums and/or Part D, overpayment recovery, tax withholdings, and child support garnishments, is to be used to compute income. Social Security benefits paid to a surviving spouse in the name of the surviving children are counted as income to the household." "While EAP generally excludes income received by individuals under 18, any SSA benefits received by a household are to be included as income."

**Excluded income and deductions.** Section 6.2 (PDF pages 57-61): "The income of any household member under 18 years old at the time of application is excluded from the household’s eligibility determination." "Income for high school students who are a dependent member of the household is not counted. High school student’s income should not be counted, even if the student is over 18." "Income from a full-time college student, up to age 23, who is a dependent of a member of the household should not be counted." "When an applicant receives child support, payments are excluded as income." "When an applicant is paying child support, payments can be deducted from income." "A lump sum pension or retirement payment that represents the employee's contribution and/or interest is excluded as income." "Capital Gains are not considered income." "Income tax refunds and Earned Income Tax Credits are excluded as income." "TANF should not be calculated as income." "The premium for Medicare Part B is not included as income."

## Interpretations and gaps

- **Three months from annual income.** The manual places a household by its most recent three months of income (Sections 6, 8.3) and multiplies that by four for eligibility. The PR uses annual income: times 3/12 against the three-month chart for points, and whole against the 12-month 60% limit for eligibility. The 12-month column is not always four times the three-month column (size 1: $16,778 against 4 × $4,194 = $16,776; size 2: $43,882 against 4 × $10,970 = $43,880), so an annual input near a boundary can land differently depending on which column an encoder keys. The companion cases use amounts that give the same answer under both columns.
- **Rounding.** The manual prints the charts without a rounding rule. Truncating household-adjusted SMI to a whole dollar, then truncating the 30%, 45% and 60% products, reproduces all 90 printed values. The federal FY2026 table (IM 2025-02 Attachment 4) prints $33,557 for one person and $74,858 for five; the manual prints $33,556 and $74,857. The PR follows the manual. Sizes 2, 3, 4 and 6-10 agree.
- **Sizes above 10.** The manual prints sizes 1-10 and refers larger households to Community Programs. The PR applies the 45 CFR 96.85(b) 3-percentage-point steps (size 11: 147%); the federal table prints $94,863 for an 11-person household, which `in_eap_eligible.yaml` Case 3 reproduces. `in_eap.yaml` Case 14 derives size 11 three-month ceilings of $11,857 and $17,786 the same way; those are not printed anywhere.
- **Points text.** Section 8.3 says "Points range from 2-6"; its chart headings, the PY2025-26 matrix and the Section 8.11 table give 2, 5 and 9. The PR uses 2, 5 and 9. The FY2026 state plan, section 2.5, says the electric benefit "will be $50-$100"; the manual (Sections 1.1, 8.7) and the matrix give $50 to $125, and the plan's own $625 maximum equals 20 × $25 + $125. The PR uses $125.
- **Household.** The SPM unit stands in for the residence-based household; Section 3.2 counts unrelated roommates, which SPM units separate. Reported pregnancies are added to size (Section 3.2). Foster children, exchange students, drop-in guests, absent members, deaths and separations within the three months, and residence changes are not modeled.
- **Ineligible members.** Section 4.4 excludes non-qualified members from size and counts their income "when determining the total household income eligibility". The PR also counts that income when assigning income points. The shared qualified-status flag stands in for citizen, national and 8 U.S.C. 1641(b) status; SSN refusal (Section 4.5), the 30-day residency (Section 4.3), eviction writs (Section 3.1) and emancipated minors are not modeled. The PR requires a member aged 18 or older (Section 4.4) and at least one eligible member.
- **Social Security and Medicare.** Section 6.1 counts the net check after Medicare Part B and Part D premiums, overpayment recovery, withholding and garnishment; the plan's section 1.9 checks "Excluding MediCare deduction". The PR subtracts the Part B premium the person pays, `medicare_part_b_premium`, which is zero for a person who is not enrolled and excludes the share a Medicare Savings Program pays, since that share is not withheld from the check. No Part D premium variable exists, and withholding, overpayment recovery and garnishment are not modeled. `integration.yaml` Case 7 (widow aged 72, Social Security $21,600, pension $5,000, wood heat): countable income $2,196.67 a month is above the MSP limit, so the $2,434.80 premium is paid; income (21,600 − 2,434.80) + 5,000 = $24,165.20, three-month $6,041.30, band 2, 16 points, $500 (gross it would be band 3 and $375). `in_eap_income.yaml` Case 9 covers an MSP-covered retiree ($12,000 counted in full), the floor ($2,000 benefit with a larger premium counts $0) and a 40-year-old on SSDI who is not enrolled.
- **Gross business income.** Section 6.1 asks for Schedule C gross profit, Schedule F gross income and the Schedule E lines before expenses. The PR counts the existing net self-employment, farm, partnership and S corporation, estate, farm rent and rental inputs, each floored at zero per person so a loss does not offset wages (`in_eap_income.yaml` Case 6). Counted income is understated for those households.
- **Other income simplifications.** Railroad benefits are to be computed on the net amount and unemployment from the DWD "NET" column; the PR counts the gross inputs. All retirement distributions count, though Section 6.2 excludes a lump sum of the employee's contribution and interest. Amounts of $1 or less, in-kind payments, and the Section 6.3 zero-income statement are not modeled. Student exclusions use `is_tax_unit_dependent` for "a dependent member of the household"; the secondary-school exclusion has no age cap and the college exclusion stops after age 23.
- **Vulnerability proxies.** Disability is read from an SSI payment, a reported SSI receipt, SSDI, or a disability flag with Medicaid receipt; the doctor's statement with a pending SSA claim, Veterans Disability, Railroad Retirement Disability, Vocational Rehabilitation and Black Lung receipt have no exact inputs. Veteran status is `is_veteran` (veterans benefits received) or `is_military`; the honorable-discharge condition is not checked. Ages compare `age` at the period: 60 or older, child 5 or younger. The monthly SSI-receipt flag is read for December when the period is a year.
- **Utilities in rent.** `tenant_pays_utilities: false` places both heat and electricity in rent (2 income points, 0 dwelling, 0 fuel, $50 electric); `heat_expense_included_in_rent` places heat alone in rent and keeps the income-based electric allowance when an electric bill is reported. Electricity alone in rent cannot be expressed. The $1 monthly rent rule is tested as annual `rent` of at least $12, where `rent` is pre-subsidy rent less housing assistance, matching the plan's out-of-pocket requirement. The waiver of a direct-pay benefit to a billed utility (Section 4.7) changes the payee, not the amount, and is not modeled.
- **Fuel.** `heating_type` is a required input. Kerosene receives no heating award (Section 1.1) but keeps the electric allowance (Sections 8.7, 8.13 by analogy). `OTHER` is treated as a bulk fuel (6 points) because the only named fuels the input cannot separate are wood pellets, corn and biofuels; `SOLAR` earns no points and no award; `UNSPECIFIED` and `NONE` earn no heating award. None of those four is addressed by the manual. A fuel with a zero bill earns no heating award, which also covers the Section 4.7 self-cut firewood rule.
- **Electric allowance.** Paid when an electric bill is reported or the home heats with electricity with a bill (Section 8.11: no electric service, no electric benefit). Section 8.7 bars shifting regular dollars from heat to electricity; the PR never does.
- **Benefit eligibility conditions not modeled** (Sections 4.6, 8.8, 8.12, 8.13): utility account in a household member's name or an exception, commercial account coding, inoperable or unsafe heating equipment, credit balances above $250 (regulated) or $500 (bulk fuel), prior awards in the program year. Regular awards are not capped at the current bill.
- **FY2025.** Only the six values that the PY2024-25 matrix changes are dated 2024-10-01. Dwelling 3, 2, 1; bulk fuels 6; vulnerable 2; $25 per point; and the 30%, 45%, 60% rates are backfilled from FY2026 and happen to match the PY2024-25 matrix page 1, but the PY2025 manual was not checked and the registry does not claim FY2025.
- **Datasets.** Microsimulation datasets carry no heating inputs, so population totals are near $0 until the default `heating_type` changes (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754).

## Existing corpus starting points

- [FY2026 state-plan manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-in-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [Benefit-matrix manual manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-in-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml)

These FY2026 manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Link the PE PR and agree the component scope, effective periods, inputs, and outputs. Cover the eligibility and benefit-calculation behavior actually in scope; identify any excluded program components explicitly.
- [ ] Audit official sources and reuse existing corpus content. Ingest missing official documents with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance; obtain signed ingest/release admission. Keep any toolchain or corpus-pin change in its own gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state rule modules with the approved encoder, placing state content under `us-in/` in the canonical layout. Include source-grounded proofs, benefit parameters where applicable, and companion tests for representative cases, boundaries, and ineligibility. Every test supplies all local inputs.
- [ ] Use personal-Codex local generation followed by exact-commit reviewed-candidate promotion for eligible modules: review the rule/test bytes, obtain the protected allowlist entry for the commit/base branch, and run protected validation/signing with the required approval. Retain the signed manifests and evidence that rule/test bytes are unchanged.
- [ ] Assemble and validate a runnable program with the required indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing blocker before declaring the complete program shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) is currently open.
- [ ] Add concept/input/output mappings and reproducible fixtures in axiom-oracles against the merged PE implementation, pinned to an exact commit. Record units and periods, compare representative and boundary cases, and resolve or explicitly disposition mismatches against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, and oracle PRs and successful CI/promotion evidence. Record the shipped scope and any remaining gaps.

## Contribution route

Use the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion contract](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion), added by [axiom-encode#1696](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/pull/1696). It validates and signs explicitly admitted reviewed content without regenerating it; it does not authenticate the original generating runtime. The [planned personal-Codex experiment](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1622#issuecomment-5940016560) records the process. The five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs are not prerequisites for testing this route.

This issue tracks work to ship; it does not claim the encoding, promotion experiment, or PE parity validation is already complete.

items.body:
## Objective

Ship North Carolina LIEAP in Axiom, covering the agreed scope and effective periods of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with signed RuleSpec encodings and reproducible oracle validation.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9726 (branch `nc-lieap`), open and not yet merged. Scope, policy periods, module paths, source text, required outputs and companion tests are in the sections below. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## PolicyEngine implementation (historical snapshot)

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9726, open and not yet merged. Head `53e9ee801f` on 2026-10-05 (fix commit `d76e933755` plus a merge of `main`). The merged commit will be recorded here once it exists.
- **Scope:** regular LIEAP heating assistance only. The Crisis Intervention Program (heating and cooling crisis), supplement payments, weatherization and equipment are out of scope. December priority processing, automatic re-enrollment, tribal administration (Lumbee Tribe, EBCI) and county fund-balance rules are not modeled.
- **Policy periods:** federal fiscal year 2026 (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30) and federal fiscal year 2027 (2026-10-01 to 2027-09-30). The model year is the heating season ending in that year: period `2026` reads the FY2026 limits and bands (EP-300 Change 2-2026, May 1, 2026), period `2027` reads the FY2027 limits and bands (Change 3-2026 and Change 04-2026, October 1, 2026) and applies the resource test, whose waiver parameter ends 2026-07-01. The registry records `verified_years: "2026-2027"`.
- **Variables:** `nc_lieap`, `nc_lieap_eligible`, `nc_lieap_income`, `nc_lieap_income_limit`, `nc_lieap_earned_income`, `nc_lieap_gross_income_person`, `nc_lieap_household_size`, and the reported inputs `nc_lieap_is_daas_disabled`, `nc_lieap_has_paid_excess_heating_costs`, `nc_lieap_nonbank_resources`, `nc_lieap_bank_account_exclusions`, under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/nc/ncdhhs/lieap/`.
- **Parameters:** `gov.states.nc.ncdhhs.lieap` (`income_limit`, `special_income_limit`, `elderly_age`, `fpg_year_lag`, `earned_income_sources`, `rental_income_sources`, `unearned_income_sources`, `earned_income_deduction`, `earned_income_deduction_threshold`, `earned_income_deduction_rate`, `medical_deduction`, `resource_test`, `resource_limit`, `special_resource_limit`, and `payment/lower_income`, `payment/higher_income`, `payment/lower_income_share`, `payment/coal_wood`).
- **Tests:** 49 YAML cases in six files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/nc/ncdhhs/lieap/` (`integration.yaml`, `nc_lieap.yaml`, `nc_lieap_eligible.yaml`, `nc_lieap_income.yaml`, `nc_lieap_income_limit.yaml`, `nc_lieap_household_size.yaml`).

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence in a manifest on axiom-corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-02 against the saved manifests in `output/liheap-axiom-issues-2026-10-02/corpus/`. Presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not checked. Existing rulespec-us North Carolina modules use `us-nc/policies/dhhs/fns/<section>/page-N` and `us-nc/regulations/10a-ncac/71u/<rule>/`, so the Energy Programs manual is proposed under `us-nc/policies/dhhs/energy-programs/`.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-nc/policies/dhhs/energy-programs/ep-300/300-02-application-requirement` | Special population: a member aged 60 or over, or a disabled person (SSI, SSA or VA disability) receiving DAAS services (page 1) | `us-nc/manual/dss/energy-programs/ep-300` | In manifest `us-nc-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml` as Change 2-2026 (May 1, 2026), the same print the PR cites for FY2026. The manifest records `benefit_matrix_pdf_pages: '19'`; the payment charts actually run over PDF pages 19-20 and the income-limit tables over pages 14-15. All 22 pages carry text, so the corpus `page-N` suffix should equal the PDF page. The manifest's citation path says `dss`; existing modules use `dhhs`. |
| `us-nc/policies/dhhs/energy-programs/ep-300/300-08-vulnerability` | Heating source billed separately; private vs public housing; heat in rent; Section 8; institutions (page 9) | same | same manifest |
| `us-nc/policies/dhhs/energy-programs/ep-300/300-09-income-and-deductions` | 130% and 150% limits; base period; FNS income types; care, child support, earned-income and medical deductions; self-employment expenses; maximum countable income tables (pages 10-15) | same | same manifest |
| `us-nc/policies/dhhs/energy-programs/ep-300/300-10-households-with-an-ineligible-alien` | Gross test, proration, deductions for excluded members (pages 15-17) | same | same manifest |
| `us-nc/policies/dhhs/energy-programs/ep-300/300-11-resources` | Waiver dates, $4,500 and $3,000 limits, counted resources (pages 17-18) | same | same manifest |
| `us-nc/policies/dhhs/energy-programs/ep-300/300-12-benefit-determination` | $300/$400/$500 charts, coal and wood $300 (pages 18-20) | same | same manifest |
| FY2027 expression of the two modules above (`300-09`, `300-12`), expression date 2026-10-01 | FY2027 maximum countable income (pages 14-15) and payment charts (pages 19-20 of Change 3-2026; pages 20-21 of Change 04-2026) | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copies: [Change Notice 03-2026, page 1](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/EP-CN-03-2026.pdf#page=1); its EP-300 attachment [Change 3-2026, October 1, 2026, pages 14-15 and 19-20](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/EP-CN-03-2026a1.pdf#page=14); and the current manual the PR's tests cite, [EP-300 Change 04-2026, October 1, 2026, pages 14-15 and 20-21](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/EP-300_10.1.2026.pdf#page=14). A word-level comparison of the three prints found no change to sections 300.08-300.12 other than the FY2027 figures and page shifts. |
| `us-nc/policies/dhhs/energy-programs/ep-150/150-01-who-must-be-included` | Household is everyone at the residence; ineligible alien excluded from the count; foster-child option | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [EP-150 Household Composition, Change 2-2023, page 1](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/eps150.pdf#page=1) |
| `us-nc/policies/dhhs/energy-programs/ep-175/175-01-citizenship-requirement` and `.../175-05-alien-eligibility-status` | At least one citizen or eligible alien; illegal aliens not eligible; USCIS document chart (pages 1 and 4-6); 175.06 D treatment of undocumented members (page 6) | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. Official copy: [EP-175 United States Citizenship, Change 1-2011, pages 1, 4-6](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/eps175.pdf#page=4) |
| `us-nc/policies/dhhs/fns/fns-350-whose-income-is-counted/page-1` and `page-2` | Count all non-excluded gross income; non-qualified ineligible aliens; K-12 student earnings excluded | `us-nc/manual/dhhs/fns/fns-350-whose-income-is-counted` | In manifest `us-nc-fns-manuals.yaml`; modules already exist in rulespec-us. The live PDF prints Change 20-2021, November 1, 2021; the manifest's `source_as_of` is 2026-05-27. |
| `us-nc/policies/dhhs/fns/fns-300-sources-of-income/page-1`, `page-5`, `page-21`, `page-26` | Earned and unearned definitions; lump sums not income; college work study not counted; student earned income not counted; wages counted | `us-nc/manual/dhhs/fns/fns-300-sources-of-income` | In manifest `us-nc-fns-manuals.yaml`; modules exist. Live PDF prints Change 01-2022, January 11, 2022. |
| `us-nc/policies/dhhs/fns/fns-315-special-budgeting-income/page-8` | 315.09 Title IV college work-study not counted | `us-nc/manual/dhhs/fns/fns-315-special-budgeting-income` | In manifest `us-nc-fns-manuals.yaml`; module exists. |
| `us-nc/policies/dhhs/fns/fns-225-citizenship` | Qualified and non-qualified alien definitions that EP-300.10 A.1 incorporates | `us-nc/manual/dhhs/fns/fns-225-citizenship` | In manifest `us-nc-fns-manuals.yaml`; modules exist (pages 1-4). The PR does not cite FNS 225; it uses the federal qualified-noncitizen list (8 USC 1641). |
| `us-nc/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-1` and `section-2` | 1.4 categorical eligibility (SNAP, heating); 1.5 automatic enrollment of the special population; 1.8 gross income; 1.9 countable income checklist; 2.1 thresholds 130% and 150%; 2.3 no assets test, renters, older adults and disability; 2.5 benefit variables; 2.6 $300 minimum and $500 maximum | `us-nc/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | In manifest `us-nc-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml`. The checkbox states on pages 5, 6 and 9 are images, not text; the manifest's `labeled_sections` extraction will not carry them. |
| FY2026 heating benefit matrix (same figures as EP-300 pages 14-15 and 19-20) | 130% and 150% limits and bands, sizes 1-26 and 1-15/1-11 | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest if wanted. Official copy: [NC FY2026 benefit matrix, pages 1-3](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/benefits-matricies/NC_BenefitMatrix_Heat-Cool_2026.pdf#page=1). It prints the size-6 special lower band as $2,697 where EP-300 page 20 prints $2,267, and labels the special population age 65. |
| `us/` poverty guidelines module | 2025 guidelines ($15,650 for one person, $5,500 per additional person) for FY2026; 2026 guidelines ($15,960 and $5,680) for FY2027 | `us/guidance/hhs/aspe/poverty-guidelines/2026/federal-register` for 2026 | `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml` holds the 2026 notice only. The 2025 notice is not in a saved manifest: [FR Doc. 2025-01377, page 1](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-17/pdf/2025-01377.pdf#page=1). The 2026 notice: [FR Doc. 2026-00755, page 1](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-01-15/pdf/2026-00755.pdf#page=1). |

Change notices EP-CN-05-2025 (FY2026 poverty level, effective October 1, 2025), EP-CN-02-2026 (May 1, 2026, terminated income and processing), EP-CN-03-2026 and EP-CN-04-2026 are in no saved manifest. EP-150, EP-175 and the FY2026 benefit matrix are in no saved manifest. The only NC LIHEAP manifests on `main` are the two named in the issue.

## Source text (verbatim)

Page numbers are PDF pages of EP-300 Change 2-2026 (May 1, 2026) unless another document is named. In that print the PDF page equals the printed page.

**Eligibility criteria.** EP-300.07 (page 9): "Eligibility for the Low-Income Energy Assistance Program is based on certain non-financial and financial requirements. Each applicant’s household must meet all requirements. Eligibility criteria is discussed in Sections 300.08 through 300.10, and 300.13."

**Household.** EP-150.01 (page 1): "Include in the application everyone who lives at the same residence unless it is known to be a boarding house or contain separate apartments. If it is a known boarding house or separate apartment with a separate heat source, there must be a written or lease agreement." and "Special Note: Do not include an ineligible alien in the number in the household but do count his reserve and prorate his income into the budget." and "Households have the option to include or exclude foster children in the Low Income Energy Assistance Program case."

**Citizenship.** EP-175.01 (page 1): "A. A household must include at least one: 1. U. S. citizen, or 2. Eligible alien." and "D. Illegal aliens are not eligible." EP-175.05 (page 4): "The following chart lists USCIS documents, the alien status, and the household members' eligibility or ineligibility for LIEAP." The chart marks "Permanent Resident" (page 4), and "Cond. Entrant", "Refugee", "Granted Asylum", "Parolee" and "Deportation withheld (PRUCOL)" (page 5), as "Eligible for Energy Programs". EP-175.06 D (page 6): "If he refuses or does not provide documentation, consider him an ineligible alien. 1. Count his prorated income when determining eligibility. 2. Count his total countable reserve in the household's reserve. 3. Exclude him from the eligible number in the household."

**Special population.** EP-300.02 A (page 1): "1. Households containing an elderly person aged 60 and above or 2. Households containing persons with disabilities that receive services through the Division of Aging and Adult Services (DAAS). Disabled persons are defined as receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI), Social Security Administration (SSA), or Veterans Administration (VA) disability."

**Vulnerability (heating responsibility).** EP-300.08 (page 9): "To be eligible, a household must be vulnerable at the time of application. A household is vulnerable if it has a heating source billed separately and it is subject to the rising cost of heating for the heat expense. Accept the applicant’s statement about the vulnerability status for the household." Items: "1. If a household lives in a private living arrangement with a heating source and heat costs are billed separately, it is fully vulnerable." "2. If a household lives in public housing where heat costs are billed separately from the rent, it is fully vulnerable." "3. An applicant who lives in a private living arrangement who does not receive a separate bill from the energy provider, they are not vulnerable." "4. A household living in public housing where utilities for heat are billed separately from the rent or where utilities for heat are included in the rent, and the household has paid an excess in utilities for heat in the last 12 months at the current address, is fully vulnerable." "5. A person living in an institution is not vulnerable." Note: "Receipt of a utility allowance does not affect vulnerability status. Section 8 households are considered in a private living arrangement."

**Income eligibility limit.** EP-300.09 (page 10): "Households meet income eligibility if the total household members' countable income for the base period (month(s) prior to application) is equal to or less than 130% of the current poverty level. Households containing individuals in the elderly population age 60 and above with income up to one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the federal poverty level and disabled persons receiving services through the Division of Aging and Adult Services. Households with this special population will meet income eligibility if the total household members' countable income for the base period (month(s) prior to application) is equal to or less than 150% of the current poverty level. FNS base periods and income conversions do not apply to LIEAP. LIEAP base period is the month prior to the month of application for all sources of income including child support and self-employment. Income calculations are actual income received in the base period, unless the income source has terminated. If the applicant reports terminated income, count actual income received in the month of application."

FY2026 state plan, section 2.1 (page 9), eligibility threshold rows: "1 All Household Sizes HHS Poverty Guidelines 130.00%" and "2 All Household Sizes HHS Poverty Guidelines 150.00%". Section 2.3 (page 9): "the special population group (60+ older and disabled) is evaluated on a 150% FPL vs non-special population households with no members 60+ or older and disabled, which are evaluated on a 130% FPL for the heating program. The special population group consist of households with an indivudal aged 60 or older or disabled."

**What income counts.** EP-300.09 A (pages 10-11): "Refer to the following Food and Nutrition Services Manual sections for types of income to count, how to verify income and budgeting guidance to apply:" followed by "FNS 300 Sources of Income", "FNS 305 Rules for Budgeting Income", "FNS 315 Special Budgeting Income", "FNS 310 Budgeting New, Changed, and Terminated Income", "FNS 350 Whose Income is Counted".

FNS 350.01 (page 1): "Count all non-excluded gross income in a FNS unit whether earned or unearned, unless special circumstances exist as indicated below." FNS 350.01 D.1 (page 2): "For a child age 17 or younger, exclude his entire gross earned income only if the child is: a. A student attending any elementary or secondary school recognized, operated, or supervised by the state or local school district (including home-school) or attending classes at least half-time to obtain a GED, and b. Not the head of the FNS unit."

FNS 300.01 (page 1): "Earned income is payment for labor or services rendered from paid employment or business ownership. Some common examples of earned income include wages, salaries, tips, and self-employment." and "Unearned income is all income that is not earned from one’s job or from one’s business. Some common examples of unearned income include contributions, railroad retirement, Social Security, and Veteran’s benefits." and "Earned or unearned income from any source that is received in a lump sum payment is not countable as income." FNS 300.02 chart: "College Work Study" is marked N (page 5); "Student Earned Income" "(Students age 17 and younger who are attending elementary or secondary school and are not the head of household)" is marked N (page 21); "Wages" is marked Y E and "Work Study" N (page 26); "Social Security Benefits" is marked Y U, with a note to count the gross amount when the benefit is reduced by a federal offset (page 20); "Rental Income" is marked Y E/U (page 17); "Self-Employment" Y E (page 19); "Farm Income" Y E (page 8).

FNS 315.09 (page 8): "Do not count College Work Study as a source of income when administered under Title IV of the Higher Education Act or the Bureau of Indian Affairs. Count other College Work Study benefits as earned income."

FY2026 state plan, item 1.8 (page 5): "In determining a household's income eligibility for LIHEAP, do you use gross income or net income?" with the "Gross Income" box checked. Item 1.9 (page 6) checks, among others, "Wages", "Self - Employment Income", "Social Security Administration (SSA ) benefits" with "Including MediCare" (deduction) checked, "Rental income", "Income from work study programs", "Child support", "Earned income of a child under the age of 18"; it leaves "One-time lump-sum payments, such as rebates/credits, winnings from lotteries, refund deposits, etc." unchecked. Item 1.6 (page 5): "The Energy program policy is aligned with FNS policy which makes categorically eligibility easy and fair."

**Deductions.** EP-300.09 B.1 a) (page 11): "Determine whether a household member has out of the pocket childcare expenses in the base period. If so, allow the full amount of out-of-pocket expenses to be paid to the day care provider. Do not allow any amount to be paid by or reimbursed by other parties." B.1 b): "Verify actual childcare costs paid in the base period for each household member with earned income." The heading of B.1 is "Child & Adult Care Expenses."

B.2 a) (page 12): "Determine whether a household member is required to pay legally obligated child support to a non-household member." B.2 d): "Allow as a deduction the child support is actually paid (including arrearages) by the household member. This includes court ordered payments or rent, mortgage, or other shelter expenses to the custodial parent and child in lieu of child support and court ordered payments for health insurance coverage for the child."

B.3 a) (page 12): "The Energy System allows automatically for each household member with earned income the standard deduction from the table below for all types of earned income including farm, self-employment, and rental income. (The table includes an allowance for hospital insurance premiums, FICA, State retirement, etc.)" Table (pages 12-13), "Gross Income Level" and "Standard Deduction":

| Gross income level (monthly) | Standard deduction |
|---|---|
| $1 - $50 | $10 |
| $51 - $100 | $20 |
| $101 - $150 | $30 |
| $151 - $200 | $40 |
| $201 - $300 | $60 |
| $301 - $400 | $80 |
| $401 + | 20% |

B.4 a) (page 13): "Each specified person will receive a standard medical deduction of $85, regardless of whether they have an expense. A specified person is an individual 60 years of age or older, or one of the following:" then "i. Who receives SSI or disability or blindness payments under Title one, two, fourteen or sixteen of the Social Security Act. These individuals may have been approved but have not received their initial payment." through "vii. Receives Medicaid based on disability." and "viii. Receives SSI based on presumptive eligibility."

B.5 (page 13): "Self-Employment Expenses. Include but are not limited to:" a list of business taxes, fees, interest, loan principal, rent, insurance, labor, utilities, repairs, supplies, transportation, meals and professional costs (pages 13-14).

**Maximum countable monthly income tables.** EP-300.09 (pages 14-15): two tables keyed by the number eligible in the household, one headed as maximum countable income at 130% and one at 150% for the special population.
