Annual limits 15,960 × 1.3 = $20,748; × 1.5 = $23,940; (15,960 + 5 × 5,680) × 1.5 = $66,540. | aged 40: $400; $300; $300; not eligible. aged 60: $400; $300; $300; not eligible. size 6: $500; $400 | Change 3-2026 pp. 14-15, 19-20 (Change 04-2026 pp. 14-15, 20-21); FR Doc. 2026-00755 |

## Interpretations and gaps

- **Coal and wood for the special population between 130% and 150%.** EP-300.12 A (page 18) says: "Households that heat with coal and/or wood will receive a benefit of $300 regardless of household size; however, the income will still need to be at or below the 130% income limit." The same paragraph opens: "The income limit is 130% of the federal poverty level." EP-300.09 (page 10) says: "Households with this special population will meet income eligibility if the total household members' countable income for the base period (month(s) prior to application) is equal to or less than 150% of the current poverty level." Plan section 2.1 (page 9) lists "2 All Household Sizes HHS Poverty Guidelines 150.00%". The PR reads the 300.12 A sentence as restating income eligibility, which 300.09 and the plan set at 150% for the special population, so a coal or wood household with a member aged 60 or over or DAAS-disabled is paid $300 up to its 150% limit. Taken literally, the sentence says 130%. Cases: `nc_lieap.yaml` Case 5 households 3-4 ($20,340 and $20,352 a year, aged 60, wood and coal: $300), Case 7 households 3-4 (DAAS-disabled: $300), Case 8 households 1-2 (aged 62, wood: $23,472 pays $300; $23,484 is ineligible).
- **Unspecified fuel with heat in rent.** `heating_type` is a required input; `NONE` and an unspecified fuel pay $0. The exception is a household whose heat is included in the rent, which under EP-300.08 item 4 is a public-housing tenant who may not know the building's fuel; the payment depends only on size and income, so `integration.yaml` Case 4 (the Case 5 family with `heating_type: UNSPECIFIED`) expects $400, and `nc_lieap.yaml` Case 6 expects $0 for an unspecified fuel without heat in rent. The manual does not speak of unknown fuels.
- **Who is vulnerable.** The model reads "billed separately" as a positive bill for the reported heating fuel with heat not in the rent (`has_heating_expense`). Private living arrangements with heat in the rent, including Section 8, are never vulnerable. Public housing with heat in rent needs the reported fact `nc_lieap_has_paid_excess_heating_costs`. The vendor-contract and account-number conditions, the applicant's-statement rule, bills in another person's name (300.02 H), institutions (item 5) and closed accounts (300.12 note) are not modeled.
- **Household.** The SPM unit stands in for everyone living at the residence (EP-150.01). The foster-child option and boarding-house or separate-apartment arrangements are not modeled.
- **Immigration status.** EP-175.05 lists USCIS documents and marks PRUCOL and other categories "Eligible for Energy Programs" with no waiting period; EP-300.10 A.1 points to FNS 225 for qualified and non-qualified aliens. The PR counts citizens and the federal qualified-noncitizen statuses of 8 USC 1641 (`is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`) and treats everyone else as a non-qualified ineligible alien subject to the unprorated gross test of 300.10 A.2.b. The qualified-but-ineligible pathway of 300.10 A.2.a (prorated income, no gross test), PRUCOL, Temporary Protected Status (`nc_lieap_income_limit.yaml` Case 2 treats TPS as not qualified) and document-specific cases are not resolved. EP-175.06 D (a member who refuses documentation) is not modeled.
- **Special income limit and an excluded member.** 300.09 speaks of "Households containing individuals in the elderly population age 60 and above" and does not say whether an ineligible alien can confer the 150% limit. The PR requires the qualifying member to be in the eligible count (`nc_lieap_income_limit.yaml` Case 2: an excluded DAAS-disabled member leaves a one-person household at $20,345). The resource limit, by contrast, looks at every member (300.11 counts ineligible aliens' assets) and at any disabled member (`is_usda_disabled`), not only a DAAS-served one.
- **DAAS disability.** 300.02 A.2 and 300.09 require both disability benefits (SSI, SSA or VA) and DAAS services. This is the reported input `nc_lieap_is_daas_disabled`; generic disability does not activate the 150% limit (`nc_lieap_eligible.yaml` Case 5, `integration.yaml` Case 7 household (c)).
- **Income period.** Annual income divided by 12 stands in for "the month prior to the month of application". Terminated income (300.09, Change Notice 02-2026) and the FNS budgeting sections (305, 310) are not modeled.
- **Gross versus net.** Plan item 1.8 checks "Gross Income"; the manual deducts care, child support, the earned-income standard deduction and $85 per specified person. The model follows the manual.
- **Student and work-study earnings.** FNS 350.01 D.1, FNS 300.02 and FNS 315.09 exclude a K-12 student's earnings (aged 17 or under, not head of unit) and Title IV work-study; plan item 1.9 checks "Earned income of a child under the age of 18" and "Income from work study programs" as countable. The model follows the manual through the shared SNAP earner flag, which does not test head-of-unit status and excludes all earnings of a federal work-study participant (`nc_lieap_income.yaml` Case 4).
- **Social Security.** Counted gross; the Medicare premium is not deducted (FNS 300.02 page 20; plan item 1.9 checks "Including MediCare").
- **Self-employment, farm and rental income.** 300.09 B.3 applies the standard deduction to "all types of earned income including farm, self-employment, and rental income", and B.5 lists deductible business expenses. The model uses the existing net self-employment, SSTB and farm inputs and `rental_income`, each floored at zero, with no separate expense itemization; rental income is treated as earned (B.3) rather than under the FNS 300 E/U split, and the student and work-study exclusions are not applied to it. Form 4835 farm rent (`farm_rent_income`) is not named in the manual and is counted with rental income. The income sources are North Carolina's own lists and do not follow `gov.usda.snap.income.sources`. `rental_income` is assumed non-negative. (`nc_lieap_income.yaml` Cases 2, 4, 7, 10, 11 and 12.)
- **Deduction table gaps and the earnings floor.** The table runs "$1 - $50", "$51 - $100" and so on; it does not say what a fractional amount such as $50.01 gets or what happens when earnings are under $10. The PR keys the bands at their tops ($50.01 gets $20; `nc_lieap_income.yaml` Case 1 fractional points) and caps the deduction at the earnings so it cannot offset unearned income (Case 9: $7 a month of wages leaves $13,380 a year for a retiree with $1,200 a month of Social Security).
- **Care and child support deductions.** B.1 b) verifies childcare "for each household member with earned income"; the model allows childcare without that condition and deducts adult care on the strength of the B.1 heading "Child & Adult Care Expenses." Child support is deducted from `child_support_expense` without checking that it is legally obligated (B.2 a). Transportation for dependent care is not modeled.
- **Excluded member's deductions.** 300.10 B.1 denies the medical deduction; B.2 bases the work deduction on the prorated income; B.3 prorates "childcare, etc." paid by the ineligible alien. The model prorates that member's child support and adult care payments (`nc_lieap_income.yaml` Case 8: aged 61, undocumented, wages $19,200, support $2,400, adult care $1,200 → $8,820) but cannot attribute unit-level `childcare_expenses` to a payer, so childcare is never prorated. Room and board paid within the unit (A.2.c) is not modeled.
- **Resources.** 300.11 waives resources "for FY July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026". The PR applies the $3,000/$4,500 limits from 2026-07-01, so period 2027 tests them (`nc_lieap_eligible.yaml` Cases 7, 10-12, 14; `integration.yaml` Case 9: FY2027 one-person households with $2,400, $3,600 (aged 45) and $3,600, $4,800 (aged 67) in resources expect $400, $0, $300, $0). The October 1, 2026 prints still carry the expired waiver sentence and no FY2027 plan was posted, so the PR calls the FY2027 value provisional. Bank balances are reduced by the reported `nc_lieap_bank_account_exclusions` (outstanding withdrawals and funds already counted as income); `nc_lieap_nonbank_resources` carries cash and retained lump sums; both are new reported inputs.
- **Band boundaries and extrapolation.** The manual publishes limits for 1-26 members and bands for 1-15 (130%) and 1-11 (150%); the rule that the lower band ends at half the monthly limit, rounded half up, is inferred from the published tables, and the model extends it to larger households (`nc_lieap.yaml` Case 10: sizes 16, 12 and 27). The FY2026 size-6 special lower band uses the matrix's $2,697, not the manual's "$0-$2,267" (`nc_lieap.yaml` Cases 3-4, size 6).
- **Source typos noted, not followed.** EP-300 page 20 "$0-$2,267" (size 6, 150%); matrix page 3 "$8,1444" (size 10 upper band; the limit is $8,144); matrix page 2 "aged 65 or older"; the 150% chart heading "(Represents 76 - 130% of 100%)"; FY2027 "$4.864" (size 14).
- **Payment not capped at the bill.** 300.12 contemplates credit balances; the model pays the chart amount whatever the bill. The county fund-balance rule (even $200 approvals) and funds exhaustion are not modeled.
- **Categorical eligibility and automatic enrollment.** Plan item 1.4 marks SNAP households categorically eligible for heating but leaves 1.4a blank, and 1.6 says the policy "is aligned with FNS policy"; the model applies the manual's financial tests to every household and does not infer a SNAP waiver. Plan item 1.5 automatic enrollment of the special population is not modeled.
- **Backfill.** Years before FY2026 use the FY2026 schedule with each year's lagged guideline and are unverified estimates (`integration.yaml` Case 3: 2022 limit 12,880 × 1.3 = $16,744).

## Existing corpus starting points

- [FY2026 state-plan manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-nc-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [Benefit-matrix manual manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-nc-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml)

These FY2026 manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Link the PE PR and agree the component scope, effective periods, inputs, and outputs. Cover the eligibility and benefit-calculation behavior actually in scope; identify any excluded program components explicitly.
- [ ] Audit official sources and reuse existing corpus content. Ingest missing official documents with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance; obtain signed ingest/release admission. Keep any toolchain or corpus-pin change in its own gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state rule modules with the approved encoder, placing state content under `us-nc/` in the canonical layout. Include source-grounded proofs, benefit parameters where applicable, and companion tests for representative cases, boundaries, and ineligibility. Every test supplies all local inputs.
- [ ] Use personal-Codex local generation followed by exact-commit reviewed-candidate promotion for eligible modules: review the rule/test bytes, obtain the protected allowlist entry for the commit/base branch, and run protected validation/signing with the required approval. Retain the signed manifests and evidence that rule/test bytes are unchanged.
- [ ] Assemble and validate a runnable program with the required indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing blocker before declaring the complete program shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) is currently open.
- [ ] Add concept/input/output mappings and reproducible fixtures in axiom-oracles against the merged PE implementation, pinned to an exact commit. Record units and periods, compare representative and boundary cases, and resolve or explicitly disposition mismatches against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, and oracle PRs and successful CI/promotion evidence. Record the shipped scope and any remaining gaps.

## Contribution route

Use the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion contract](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion), added by [axiom-encode#1696](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/pull/1696). It validates and signs explicitly admitted reviewed content without regenerating it; it does not authenticate the original generating runtime. The [planned personal-Codex experiment](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1622#issuecomment-5940016560) records the process. The five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs are not prerequisites for testing this route.

This issue tracks work to ship; it does not claim the encoding, promotion experiment, or PE parity validation is already complete.

items.title: Encode New Jersey's Optional State Supplementation: POMS SI 01415.058 J levels by living arrangement, SI NY01415.025 code rules, SI 01320.430 D deeming (PE-US PR 10157)

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Encoding debt

New Jersey's federally administered Optional State Supplementation (OSS) has no RuleSpec module. On `rulespec-us` `main` (`172bf04e4`, 2026-10-14), `us-nj/` holds only:

- `policies/cms/` (CHIP and Medicaid eligibility levels)
- `policies/income_tax/`
- `regulations/njac-10-90/` (WorkFirst New Jersey)
- `statutes/54a:4-7` (the New Jersey earned income tax credit)

There is no `us-nj/policies/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/` tree like the DC and Delaware ones, and no SSI module under `us-nj/statutes/`. The shared module `us/policies/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/2026/federally-administered-optional-supplement-common.yaml` already holds the 2026 federal amounts New Jersey's tables use: FBR 994.00 and 1,491.00 (`federal_code_a_individual_fbr`, `federal_code_a_couple_fbr`), the federal code C individual FBR 994.00, FBR less VTR 662.67 and 994.00, the Title XIX caps 30.00 and 60.00, and the code Y waiver (`optional_supplement_waived_os_code_applies`). No module encodes the federal OSS computation in 20 CFR 416.2025, and there is no `us/regulations/20-cfr/` tree.

Issue searches for "New Jersey supplementary", "New Jersey SSP", "New Jersey state supplement", "New Jersey optional", "New Jersey SSI", "44:7-86", "01415.058", "NY01415.025", "nj_ssp" and "us-nj" SSP find no issue for this program. "01415.058" finds #1450 and #1767 and the closed DC and Delaware issues #519, #520 and #532; "New Jersey SSI" finds only #1481 (New Jersey LIHEAP). The SSP `pe-parity` issues cover California (#1450), New Mexico (#1708), Texas (#1709), Wyoming (#1766), Nevada (#1767) and New Hampshire (#1769).

PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10157 (open, not merged) adds the program to PolicyEngine-US:

- **Variables** (Person, monthly), under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/nj/njdhs/ssp/`:
  - `nj_ssp_care_setting`, an input: `CONGREGATE_CARE`, `RESIDENTIAL_HEALTH_CARE`, `EXCLUDED` (publicly operated community residences, emergency shelters, and institutionalized children whose care private insurance pays) or `NONE`.
  - `nj_ssp_living_arrangement`, the OS code: `CONGREGATE_CARE` (A), `LIVING_ALONE_OR_WITH_OTHERS` (B), `LIVING_ONLY_WITH_INELIGIBLE_SPOUSE` (C), `HOUSEHOLD_OF_ANOTHER` (D), `RESIDENTIAL_HEALTH_CARE` (I), `MEDICAID_INSTITUTION` (G) or `NONE` (Z). It reads the care setting, the federal living arrangement, the medical-facility input, `is_ssi_ineligible_spouse`, and whether anyone outside the marital unit lives in the household. It can also be set directly.
  - `nj_ssp`, the payment. It calls the shared helper `ssi_state_supplement` (`policyengine_us/variables/gov/ssa/ssi/_ssi_state_supplement.py`, which PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10001 also adds). The helper computes the level before income internally; no output variable holds that level.
- **Parameters,** dated 2026-01-01:
  - `gov.states.nj.njdhs.ssp.amount.individual` and `.couple`, broken down by `nj_ssp_living_arrangement`. The couple file's code C cell is a 25.35 placeholder (see "Interpretations and gaps").
  - The federal `gov.ssa.ssi.state_supplement.minimum_payment`, $1.
- **Tests** under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/nj/njdhs/ssp/`: `nj_ssp.yaml` (17 cases), `nj_ssp_living_arrangement.yaml` (11) and `integration.yaml` (9), 37 in total.
- **Aggregates:** `nj_ssp` is added to `household_state_benefits`, `spm_unit_benefits`, SNAP unearned income and HUD unearned income.
- **Scope:** 2026 only. Earlier years and mandatory (grandfathered) supplementation are out of scope; the registry status is `partial`.
- **Changes after the first review:**
  - The files moved from `nj/dhs/ssp` to `nj/njdhs/ssp`, so the parameters are now `gov.states.nj.njdhs.ssp.*`.
  - `integration.yaml` Cases 2 and 6 were renamed and given comments; their inputs are unchanged. Case 2 now describes a congregate care couple in a small household-scale facility; no input holds the facility's size or institution status. Case 6 now describes a couple living only with a foster child; the child is a 12-year-old tax-unit dependent with no foster-care input, and code C is entered directly. Case 7 also checks `spm_unit_benefits`, and Case 8 (congregate care spouses paid as individuals after the month of entry) and Case 9 (code B under deeming, with a spouse earning $34,590 a year and a 12-year-old) are new.
  - `nj_ssp.yaml` Case 17 (a disabled child living with parents) is new.

## Module paths and corpus citations

| Proposed module | Provisions | Corpus citation | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-nj/policies/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/2026/nj-ssp-living-arrangement-variations.yaml` | OS codes A, B, C, D, I, G and Z and the Lifeline NOTE (SI 01415.058 J.1). Code Y comes from the shared module | `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/01415.058/block-34` | In axiom-corpus manifest `manifests/us-ssa-poms-si-2026-09-10.yaml`: source id `ssa-poms-si-01415-058` (TN 95, expression date 2026-08-28) |
| `us-nj/policies/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/2026/nj-ssp-individual-state-supplement-levels.yaml` | J.2.a, all 9 rows and both footnotes | `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/01415.058/block-35` and `block-36` | Same manifest |
| `us-nj/policies/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/2026/nj-ssp-couple-state-supplement-levels.yaml` | J.2.b, all 6 rows and footnotes 1 to 3 | `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/01415.058/block-35` and `block-37` | Same manifest |
| `us-nj/policies/ssa/poms/si-ny01415-025/nj-oss-codes.yaml` | SI NY01415.025: code C (the household rule, the separate-household and foster-child exceptions, transients); the NOTE under codes A and I (couple status after entry into a facility); code Z's privately insured children | `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/ny01415.025/block-2` | Same manifest: source id `ssa-poms-si-ny01415-025` (expression date 2022-09-13). The New Jersey row of `manifests/ssi-agent-queue.yaml` (`agent_ready`) names this section and SI 01415.058 J |
| `us-nj/statutes/44:7-86.yaml` (the `us-nj/statutes/54a:4-7.yaml` path style) | N.J.S.A. 44:7-86, which SSA gives as New Jersey's "Statutory basis for payment" | none | Not in any `us-nj` manifest or corpus lock on `main`; needs ingest from the New Jersey Legislature's statutes database (`lis.njleg.state.nj.us`, the source of `us-nj/statutes/54a:4-7`). I couldn't retrieve the section, so this issue doesn't quote it |
| Co-cited source | SSA, State Assistance Programs for SSI Recipients, January 2011, New Jersey: SSA administration, the statutory basis and the scope of coverage | none | Not ingested. `manifests/us-ssa-w6-federal-guidance.yaml` holds other states' 2011 pages (for example `us/guidance/ssa/state-assistance-programs-for-ssi-recipients/2011/de`) but not New Jersey's; needs ingest: https://www.ssa.gov/policy/docs/progdesc/ssi_st_asst/2011/nj.html |
| `us-nj/policies/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/2026/nj-ssp-payment.yaml` | Federal administration (SI 01415.058 A; SI NY01415.025 A). The federal computation: 20 CFR 416.2025(b) and 416.2020(c); SI 02001.005 A.2 and B.2; SI 02001.010 A.1 to A.3; SI 02005.030 A.1 and G; SI 01320.430 C.5, C.7, D and example G.4 | `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/01415.058/block-1`; `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/ny01415.025/block-1`; `us/regulation/20/416/2025`; `us/regulation/20/416/2020`; `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/02001.005/block-2` and `block-7`; `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/02001.010/block-1` to `block-3`; `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/02005.030/block-1`, `block-14` and `block-15`; `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/01320.430/block-7`, `block-9`, `block-11` to `block-13` and `block-35` | The POMS sections are in `manifests/us-ssa-poms-si-2026-09-10.yaml`. 20 CFR 416.2020 and 416.2025 are not listed in a `manifests/*.yaml` document file. Part 416 is the eCFR extraction scope `us/regulation/2026-09-11-title-20-part-416` (row in `manifests/ssi-agent-queue.yaml`; corpus lock `.axiom/corpus-locks/us/regulation/2026-09-11-title-20-part-416.json`); its provisions are section-level, with no blocks |

- **Block numbers.** I took them from the provisions JSONL git blobs named in the corpus locks on `main`: `831feb4ce2` (`data/corpus/provisions/us/manual/2026-09-10-ssi-poms-si.jsonl`) and `9fa9a51e6f` (`data/corpus/provisions/us/regulation/2026-09-11-title-20-part-416.jsonl`). Both downloads match the sha256 in their lock. Blocks 34, 36 and 37 of SI 01415.058 and block 2 of SI NY01415.025 match the live pages word for word, apart from spacing and footnote markers.
- **Second copy of SI 01415.058.** The DC run also holds the section as `us/guidance/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/2026` (TN 94, `manifests/us-dc-ossp-ssa-poms.yaml`, `source_as_of` 2025-12-09); the shared module cites that copy. Its New Jersey subsection is `block-35` to `block-38`. Its two tables are identical to blocks 36 and 37 above. Its J.1 text differs only in quotation marks (for example OS code "A" and a separate "household") and one apostrophe ("Department of Human Services' Division"). The New Jersey row of `manifests/ssi-agent-queue.yaml` names the manual-family paths used above.
- **The payment module.** As in #1767, the last module holds federal rules that every federally administered state shares. If #1767's encoder builds a shared module instead (for example `us/regulations/20-cfr/416/2025.yaml`), the New Jersey module should import it. The outputs and tests below don't change either way.

I checked presence in the manifests on axiom-corpus `main` (`437198d6c`). I did not check the signed release that rulespec-us pins.

## Source text (verbatim)

**POMS SI 01415.058, Federally Administered Optional Supplementary Payment Programs for January 2026** (TN 95, "Effective Dates: 08/28/2026 - Present"), https://secure.ssa.gov/poms.nsf/lnx/0501415058

Subsection A:

> The following states participate in federally administered optional supplementary payment programs:

The table that follows lists "New Jersey" with the reference "SI 01415.058J".

Subsection J.1, "Definitions of State living arrangement variations for New Jersey":

> **A** Congregate care
> Apply OS code A to recipients in Federal living arrangement A. The living arrangement includes:
> • recipients in residential facilities who are under the supervision of the Department of Human Services;
> • children and adults in residential facilities (both inside and outside of NJ) who are under the supervision of, or placed by the NJ Department of Human Services Division of Developmental Disabilities (DDD) or Division of Youth and Family Services (DYFS); and
> • recipients living in assisted living residences or comprehensive personal care homes (CPCH) licensed by the Department of Health and Senior Services.
>
> **B** Living alone or with others
> Use OS code B for recipients whose Federal living arrangements are A or C and who do not meet the requirements defined in other supplementation categories.
> You must consider any eligible recipient who meets the requirement for a Federal code A to be in optional supplement B unless they are residing in a residential health care facility or living alone with an ineligible spouse.
> Likewise, any child meeting the criteria for a Federal code C is automatically entitled to optional supplement B.
> This category includes, but is not limited to, recipients who are in one of the following situations:
> 1. Living physically alone;
> 2. Living with others in a private dwelling, but meet some criteria for Federal living arrangement A; or
> 3. Placed in a transitional residency program by the Division of Mental Health and Hospitals, Department of Human Services.
> Optional supplement code B is the proper code to use with an intervening Federal code A. For State supplement codes, see SM 01301.535.
> Use OS code B to address Section 1619 cases.
>
> **C** Living alone with an ineligible spouse
> Use OS code C when a recipient lives with ONLY their ineligible spouse and NO other persons are part of the household. Use Federal criteria to determine an ineligible spouse for State supplementation purposes (i.e., a spouse, either by marriage or holding out as spouses) who is either not eligible for SSI or who chooses not to apply. If other persons, even minor children, are present in the household, you cannot apply this OS code.
> It is possible that a claimant and the ineligible spouse live with others and allege that they are a separate household by virtue of the fact that they eat their meals out or have separate purchase and preparation of food. In this instance, you may consider an optional supplement C as long as no other person is considered part of the household. There is no couple counterpart in this category.
> A transient recipient who co-exists only with an ineligible spouse also qualifies as OS code C.
> Always consider parent(s) with minor children to be in the same household and code the case OS code B.
>
> **D** Living in the household of another
> Apply OS code D to recipients who are living in the household of another for Federal purposes.
>
> **I** Licensed residential health care facilities (RHCF)
> Apply OS code I to recipients living in:
> • attached nursing homes;
> • assisted living residence;
> • CPCH; or
> • free-standing licensed residential health care facilities. We paid residents of these facilities the OS A rate prior to January 1, 2006.
> We must base our authorization for this payment on the recipient's verified residence at a facility listed in the New Jersey Congregate Care Directory.
> Only the RHCF section of a multipurpose facility is eligible for the OS code I rate. Pay residents of the assisted living resident (ALR or CPCH section of a multipurpose facility) at the OS code A rate. Nursing home residents are in living arrangement (D or G) if Medicaid pays more than 50 percent of the cost of care.
>
> **G** Apply OS code G effective September 1, 1988, when the State elected Federal administration of an optional State supplementary payment to residents of Title XIX facilities.
>
> **Z** No supplement cases
> Apply OS code Z to recipients:
> • in licensed medical facilities where Medicaid is paying less than 50 percent of the cost of care;
> • in publicly operated community residences having 16 or less residents; and
> • residing throughout a month in publicly operated emergency shelters.

C.7, "OSS Payment Category for Ineligible Spouse", with its NOTE:

> Effective October 1, 1988, to determine the OSS for a couple, the ineligible spouse is considered to be in the same category (i.e., aged, blind or disabled) as the eligible individual. (Currently, four States vary their payment rates by category: California, Iowa, Massachusetts, and Nevada.) The State supplement rate used is the greater of: • The eligible couple rate for the category for which the eligible individual qualifies; or • the eligible individual rate (including the special rate for an eligible individual living with an ineligible spouse) for the category for which the eligible individual qualifies.

D.1, "Determine Eligibility/Payment as an Individual":

> a. Subtract the eligible individual's own countable income from the FBR for an individual. The remainder is the Federal benefit as an individual, or excess countable income.
> b. If a Federal Benefit is due under a. above, use the full OSS for an individual, or the OSS for an individual with an ineligible spouse, in those States which provide such an OSS.
> c. If there is excess countable income remaining in a. above, subtract the excess from the OSS for an individual. The remainder is the State supplement due as an individual. (If no Federal or State benefit is due, deeming is not applicable.)

D.2, "Follow Spouse-to-Spouse Deeming Rules" (a., second sentence; b. to d.):

> If the ineligible spouse's total income after allocations is more than the difference between the FBR for an eligible couple and the FBR for an eligible individual, combine the eligible individual's and ineligible spouse's incomes and treat as an eligible couple.
> b. Subtract the couple's countable income (after applying appropriate exclusions and allowances) from the FBR for a couple. The remainder is the Federal benefit due a couple using the deeming rules. Where the couple's countable income is greater, excess countable income results, and no Federal benefit is payable.
> c. If a Federal benefit is due based on use of the ineligible spouse's income, the State supplement used is the full OSS for a couple who are both aged, both blind, or both disabled (depending on the category of the eligible individual's SSI benefit).
> If the State provides different payment variations, select the variation that applies to the eligible individual, and use the corresponding OSS for a couple.
> However, if the State has an individual supplement rate (including a special rate for an eligible individual living with an ineligible spouse) which is greater than the State supplement for an eligible couple, use the higher individual State supplement.
> d. If there is excess countable income remaining in step 2.b., subtract the excess from the OSS for a couple (or the individual State supplement, if greater). The remainder is the State supplement due a couple using the deeming rules. (If no Federal or State benefit is due, the individual is ineligible due to excess income.)

D.3, "Determine Federal Benefit/State Supplement Amounts":

> a. The Federal benefit amount is the lesser of: • The Federal benefit due as an individual (step 1.a.); or • The Federal benefit due using the deeming rules (step 2.b.).
> b. The State supplement amount is the lesser of: • The State supplement due as an individual (step 1.b. or c.); or • The State supplement due using the deeming rules (step 2.c. or d.).

**20 CFR 416.2025(b), Optional supplementation: Countable income,** https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/chapter-III/part-416/subpart-T/section-416.2025

> (b) Effect of countable income on payment amounts. Countable income of an eligible individual or eligible couple is determined in the same manner as such income is determined under the title XVI supplemental security income program. Countable income will affect the amount of the State supplementary payments as follows:
> (1) As provided in § 416.420, countable income will first be deducted from the Federal benefit rate applicable to an eligible individual or eligible couple. In the case of an eligible individual living with an ineligible spouse with income (the deeming provisions of § 416.1163 apply), the Federal benefit rate from which countable income will be deducted is the Federal benefit rate applicable to an eligible couple, except that an eligible individual's payment amount may not exceed the amount he or she would have received if he or she were not subject to the deeming provisions (§ 416.1163(e)(2)).
> (2) If countable income is equal to or less than the amount of the Federal benefit rate, the full amount of the State supplementary payment as specified in the Federal agreement will be made.
> (3) If countable income exceeds the amount of the Federal benefit rate, the State supplementary benefit will be reduced by the amount of such excess. In the case of an eligible individual living with an ineligible spouse with income (the deeming methodology of § 416.1163 applies), the State supplementary payment rate from which the excess income will be deducted is the higher of the State supplementary rates for an eligible couple or an eligible individual, except that an eligible individual's payment amount may not exceed the amount he or she would have received if he or she were not subject to the deeming provisions (see § 416.1163(e)(2)). For purposes of determining the State supplementary couple rate, the ineligible spouse is considered to be in the same category as the eligible individual.
> (4) No State supplementary payment will be made where countable income is equal to or exceeds the sum of the Federal benefit rate and the State supplementary payment rate.

The monthly payment formula:

- **Individual:** `max(0, level − max(0, countable income − FBR))`. The FBR is 994.00 for federal codes A and C, 662.67 for code B and the 30.00 payment cap for code D (416.2025(b)(2)-(4); J.2.a).
- **Eligible couple living together:** the same formula on the couple's combined countable income, the couple FBR (1,491.00; 994.00 for code B; 60.00 for code D) and the J.2.b level. The result is divided by 2 (SI 02005.030 G.1).
- **Eligible individual with deemed income from an ineligible spouse:** the lesser of two amounts (SI 01320.430 D.3.b; 416.2025(b)(3)):
  - the individual computation, with the person's own countable income and the individual FBR, using the code C level when code C applies (D.1.a-c);
  - the couple computation, with the couple's countable income, the couple FBR, and the higher of the couple level for the person's variation and the individual level (C.7, D.2.b-d).
  - In New Jersey the individual level is the higher one for code B (31.25 against 25.35) and code C (152.99; no couple level). The couple level is higher for codes A, I, D and G.
- **Rounding:** each person's amount is raised to the next cent using the third decimal digit only (SI 02001.010 A.1-A.3). Halving the A, B and I couple levels leaves a half cent, so each member gets 309.18, 12.68 or 369.18 (J.2.b footnote 1).
- **Minimum:** a positive amount below $1 is paid as $1.00, per member for a couple (416.2020(c); SI 02001.005 A.2, B.2).

Inputs: State of residence; SSI category facts (aged, blind, disabled; age); SSI eligibility for the month apart from income (resources, immigration status, residence); federal living arrangement (A, B, C or D); facility facts (a facility listed in the Congregate Care Directory and which section; a licensed medical facility and Medicaid's share of the cost of care; a publicly operated community residence and its size; a full month in a publicly operated emergency shelter; a child whose facility care private insurance pays; federal code D before January 1988); marital or holding-out status, living together, and whether the spouse is eligible for SSI or chooses not to apply; whether anyone other than the spouse and foster children is part of the household; the State's separate-household determination; transient status; waiver of the supplement; the month of entry into a facility and whether the facility is an institution; whether ineligible-spouse deeming applies; monthly countable income under the federal SSI rules (own, couple, or with deemed income).

## Interpretations and gaps

- **Code C has no couple level.** J.1 says "There is no couple counterpart in this category", and J.2.b has no C row.
  - PolicyEngine-US's `couple.yaml` holds 25.35 (the B couple level) for `LIVING_ONLY_WITH_INELIGIBLE_SPOUSE`, with a comment that it never affects results. A code C claimant is never part of an eligible couple, and under deeming the helper uses `max(couple, individual)` = 152.99 (Case L).
  - The encoding should leave the C couple cell undefined and use the individual level in the deeming computation directly (D.2.c, "use the higher individual State supplement"). A parity check should skip that parameter cell.
- **The code C household test.** PolicyEngine-US gives code C when the person's marital unit holds an SSI-ineligible spouse and nobody outside the marital unit lives in the household.
  - Neither exception can be derived: foster children (SI NY01415.025, effective 7/1/90) and the separate household for couples who eat out or buy and prepare food separately. Both go through an explicit `nj_ssp_living_arrangement` input (the variable's documentation says so). Transients are covered when the household holds only the couple.
  - `integration.yaml` Case 6 enters code C directly for a couple living only with a foster child (12) and pays 152.99. It is the PolicyEngine-US case for the foster-child exception through the explicit input.
  - The encoding should take "other persons in the household, excluding foster children" and the State's separate-household determination as inputs.
- **A spouse who chooses not to apply.** J.1 counts a spouse "who is either not eligible for SSI or who chooses not to apply" as an ineligible spouse; SI NY01415.025 says "who is either ineligible for SSI or who chooses not to apply".
  - PolicyEngine-US's `is_ssi_ineligible_spouse` covers only a spouse who is not aged, blind or disabled, and `ssi_claim_is_joint` ignores take-up. So when one aged spouse doesn't apply, the couple is computed jointly and the applicant gets half the B couple level (12.68) instead of the C level (152.99, subject to deeming). An aged, blind or disabled spouse who is ineligible for another reason is treated the same way.
  - A NOTE in `nj_ssp.py` documents this. No PolicyEngine-US case covers it. The encoding should follow J.1.
- **Couples in a facility.** The SI NY01415.025 NOTE gives a couple entering a Level 2 facility "the couple FBR and couple OSS D for the month of change only"; after that, the spouses are two individuals, except in a small-scale facility that is not an institution.
  - PolicyEngine-US has no month-of-change or institution input, so it computes congregate care spouses in one marital unit jointly. `integration.yaml` Case 8 enters congregate care spouses as separate marital units to pay 150.05 each (Case K).
  - `integration.yaml` Case 2 pays the A couple level (309.18 each) in a small household-scale facility where couple status continues (Case J).
  - The month of entry itself has no PolicyEngine-US case and is not modelled. Read literally, the NOTE names "couple OSS D" (93.08 in J.2.b, a federal code B row) for that month, although J.2.b prints A and I couple levels under federal code A. The encoding should record which reading it takes for the month of entry.
  - The helper averages the two members' couple levels when spouses in one marital unit have different codes (NOTE in `nj_ssp.py`). SI 02005.030 G.1 says to "average their individual OSS payment" for multi-living-arrangement couples living together. No New Jersey case covers a mixed couple.
- **Code B under deeming.** The B individual level exceeds the B couple level (31.25 against 25.35); the C.7 NOTE names New Jersey and Washington. Code B with an ineligible spouse arises when someone else is in the household, such as a child.
  - Under deeming, the couple computation uses 31.25 (D.2.c) instead of the 25.35 couple level: the full 31.25 when the couple's countable income after the child's allocation is at or below 1,491, and 31.25 less the excess when it is above 1,491 (D.2.d), reaching $0 at 1,522.25. The payment is the lesser of that and the individual computation (D.3.b), so this reading pays 31.25 rather than 25.35 whenever own countable income is at most 994 and couple countable income is at most 1,491. PolicyEngine-US follows this reading. `integration.yaml` Case 9 (an aged recipient, a spouse earning $34,590 a year and a 12-year-old) has couple countable income of 1,150.25 and pays 31.25; no companion test covers it.
  - C.5 says the payment rate "is the lower of the rate for an eligible couple or individual". D.3.b and example G.4.c read that as the lesser of the two computed amounts, not the lower rate; G.4 pays Washington's 192.00 special rate rather than its 22.00 couple rate. Case L follows D.3.b.
- **The Lifeline.** The J.1 NOTE puts a Lifeline utility payment inside every rate except the Medicaid-facility rate. POMS doesn't print the Lifeline share. Encode the levels as published, with no Lifeline output. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10230 tracks counting New Jersey LIHEAP income net of the Lifeline; the LIHEAP draft #1481 lists a Lifeline exclusion in its N.J.A.C. 5:49-2.3 row.
- **J.2.b footnote 1.** Halving the A, B and I couple levels gives 309.175, 12.675 and 369.175, which SI 02001.010 A.2 raises per member (Cases I and J). The footnote also marks the B/D total 1,087.08, which halves evenly (543.54), and it doesn't say which part carries the half cent.
  - The January 2014 to 2020 charts (SI 01415.046 to .052) printed these couple levels one cent higher (618.36, 25.36, 738.36, 93.09), without the footnote. From January 2021 (SI 01415.053) they read 618.35, 25.35, 738.35 and 93.08 with the footnote. Per member, A, B and I pay the same either way.
  - Encode the 2026 levels as printed and round per member.
- **Facility codes are inputs.** Codes A and I depend on the Congregate Care Directory and the section of a multipurpose facility. PolicyEngine-US takes them from `nj_ssp_care_setting`.
  - The Z settings other than a medical facility (a publicly operated community residence, a public emergency shelter all month, privately insured children) share one input, `EXCLUDED`. A medical facility where Medicaid pays less than half is derived from `ssi_lives_in_medical_treatment_facility` without `ssi_medicaid_pays_majority_of_care`. Cases that were federal code D before January 1988 have no input.
  - J.1 gives Z where Medicaid pays "less than 50 percent" and G where it pays "more than 50 percent". PolicyEngine-US puts exactly 50 percent in Z.
- **Order of the codes.** PolicyEngine-US checks Z, then G, A, I, D and C, and defaults to B. J.1 code I supports G before A and I for nursing home units. `nj_ssp_living_arrangement.yaml` Cases 9 and 10 pin the order with conflicting inputs and are not source cases.
- **Mandatory and essential-person supplementation are not modelled.** SSA's 2011 description lists mandatory minimum supplementation administered by SSA. Its 2011 table has a "Living with an essential person" C row (state supplement 25.36). J.2 prints no such row for 2026. The registry note says "Mandatory grandfathered supplementation is not modeled". Leave both out.
- **Take-up gate.** The helper pays only when `is_ssi_eligible` and `takes_up_ssi_if_eligible` hold; `nj_ssp.yaml` Case 15 pins take-up false at $0. Take-up is a modelling device. The encoding's eligibility input should be SSI eligibility apart from income, not receipt of a federal payment: New Jersey pays when federal SSI is $0 (Cases L, O and R).
- **Rounding and the $1 minimum.** PolicyEngine-US drops digits after the third decimal, then raises to the cent (`np.ceil(np.floor(x * 1_000) / 10) / 100`, SI 02001.010 A.1), and applies the $1 minimum per member after rounding (SI 02001.005 B.2). For an individual, a positive supplement below $1 arises only when federal SSI is $0, so 416.2020(c) and A.2 agree (Case P). No New Jersey case has a couple below $1.
- **Code Y and out-of-state placements.** PolicyEngine-US has no waiver input (code Y) and pays only New Jersey residents; SI NY01415.025 F's rule for New Jersey placements in out-of-state facilities is not modelled.
- **History (out of scope).** The encoding starts at 2026-01-01. The G levels were 10.00 (individual) and 20.00 (couple) in the January 2014 to 2018 charts (SI 01415.046 to .050), and 20.00 and 40.00 from January 2019 (SI 01415.051).

## Plan

**Step 1. Encode** the three SI 01415.058 J modules, the SI NY01415.025 module and the payment module above through the signed encoder. Co-cite N.J.S.A. 44:7-86 and SSA's January 2011 New Jersey description once they are ingested. Paste this as `review_finding`:

> Encode New Jersey's federally administered Optional State Supplementation as Person-level monthly modules from POMS SI 01415.058 J (corpus us/manual/ssa/poms/si/01415.058, blocks 34-37) and POMS SI NY01415.025 (corpus us/manual/ssa/poms/si/ny01415.025, blocks 1-2). Co-cite N.J.S.A. 44:7-86 once ingested. Take the computation from 20 CFR 416.2025(b) and 416.2020(c) (corpus us/regulation/20/416/2025 and us/regulation/20/416/2020), POMS SI 02001.005 A.2 and B.2, SI 02001.010 A.1-A.3, SI 02005.030 A.1 and G, and SI 01320.430 C.5, C.7, D and G.4. Required outputs, each with verbatim proof excerpts:
> 1. Money parameters, effective 2026-01-01: the 9 individual rows of J.2.a and the 6 couple rows of J.2.b. Code C has no couple level.
> 2. Judgments for the month:
>    - Code Z: in a licensed medical facility where Medicaid pays less than 50 percent of the cost, OR in a publicly operated community residence with 16 or fewer residents, OR in a publicly operated emergency shelter throughout the month, OR a child under 18 in a facility whose care private health insurance pays (from December 1, 1996), OR a case that was federal code D before January 1988.
>    - Code G: federal living arrangement D (Title XIX facility, Medicaid pays more than 50 percent), and not code Z.
>    - Code C: lives with an ineligible spouse (federal criteria: married or holding out, and not eligible for SSI or choosing not to apply) AND no other person is part of the household, where foster children don't count and a documented State determination of eating out or separate purchase and preparation of food makes the claimant and spouse a separate household. Never when parents live with minor children.
> 3. The OS code for the month: Z or G as above; Y if waived; otherwise A in a congregate care setting (a residential facility supervised by the Department of Human Services, a DDD or DCF placement, or an assisted living residence or comprehensive personal care home in the New Jersey Congregate Care Directory), I in the RHCF section of a licensed residential health care facility in the Directory, D in federal living arrangement B, C as above, and B for anyone else in federal living arrangement A or C.
> 4. A Money output, the monthly payment for each person:
>    - max(0, level − max(0, countable income − FBR)), zero when countable income is at or above FBR + level (416.2025(b)(2)-(4)).
>    - An eligible couple living together is computed jointly with the couple FBR and the J.2.b level, and the result is divided by 2 (SI 02005.030 G.1). Spouses in an institution are two individuals after the month of change unless the facility is a small-scale household (SI NY01415.025 NOTE).
>    - Under ineligible-spouse deeming, the payment is the lesser of the individual computation (with the code C level where code C applies) and the couple computation with the higher of the couple level and the individual level (SI 01320.430 C.7, D.1-D.3; 416.2025(b)(3)).
>    - Each person's amount is raised to the next cent using the third decimal only (SI 02001.010 A.1-A.3). A positive amount below $1 is paid as $1.00, per member for a couple (416.2020(c); SI 02001.005 A.2, B.2).
>
> Companion tests, each assigning every leaf input: cases A to R in the issue's Companion tests table.

**Step 2. Oracle coverage.** Map the outputs to these PolicyEngine-US variables, all monthly:

- `nj_ssp_living_arrangement` (the OS code; codes Z, G and C are its `NONE`, `MEDICAID_INSTITUTION` and `LIVING_ONLY_WITH_INELIGIBLE_SPOUSE` values);
- `nj_ssp` (the payment; no output variable holds the per-person level);
- the parameters `gov.states.nj.njdhs.ssp.amount.individual` and `.couple`, skipping the couple file's code C placeholder.

Record the readings under "Interpretations and gaps" as known modelling choices rather than encoding them: the code C couple placeholder, the explicit-input route for the code C exceptions, the spouse who chooses not to apply, couples in a facility (separate marital units after entry, the month-of-entry level), the code B deeming reading, the Lifeline, the input-only facility codes, mandatory supplementation, and the take-up gate.

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Mississippi LIHEAP in Axiom, covering the agreed scope and effective periods of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with signed RuleSpec encodings and reproducible oracle validation.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9727 (branch `ms-liheap`), open and not yet merged. Scope, policy periods, module paths, source text, required outputs and companion tests are in the sections below. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## PolicyEngine implementation (historical snapshot)

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9727, open and not yet merged. Head `e8df6fff93` on 2026-10-02 (branch `ms-liheap`). The merged commit will be recorded here once it exists.
- **Scope:** regular assistance under the LIHEAP benefit matrix: the main heating fuel bill paid up to that fuel's column, plus the electric bill of a home not heated by electricity paid up to the Electric column (Rule 7.8 C-D), capped at the bills (Rule 7.4 A). The model returns one program-year amount; it does not split the heating component (10/01/2025 to 04/30/2026) from the cooling component (05/01/2026 to 09/30/2026), which use the same matrix and the same $1,500 program-year maximum. Out of scope: the Energy Crisis Intervention Program, heating or cooling equipment, in-kind goods (blankets, fans), weatherization, the $100-per-intake payment for heat in rent (Rule 6.4 B), and propane 100-gallon requests (Rule 7.8 E).
- **Policy period:** federal fiscal year 2026 (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). State parameters are dated 2025-10-01 and the four-person state median income is the FY2026 figure. The model reads them for period `2026`. The registry records `verified_years: "2026"`.
- **Variables:** `ms_liheap`, `ms_liheap_eligible`, `ms_liheap_income`, `ms_liheap_income_limit`, `ms_liheap_household_size`, under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/ms/mdhs/liheap/`.
- **Parameters:** `gov.states.ms.mdhs.liheap` (`adult_age`, `income_limit`, `maximum_table_size`, `income_bands/1` to `income_bands/20`, `maximum_payment` and `payment_reduction` by `heating_type`, `electric_maximum_payment`, `electric_payment_reduction`, `propane_exception_amount`, `propane_exception_household_size`, `propane_exception_income_band`, `unearned_income_sources`). Federal inputs: `gov.hhs.smi.amount[MS]` ($85,708 from 2025-10-01), `gov.hhs.smi.household_size_adjustment`, `gov.hhs.smi.additional_person_threshold`.
- **Tests:** 39 YAML cases under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/ms/mdhs/liheap/`: `integration.yaml` (6), `ms_liheap.yaml` (19), `ms_liheap_eligible.yaml` (4), `ms_liheap_income.yaml` (8), `ms_liheap_income_limit.yaml` (2).

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence in a manifest on axiom-corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-02 against the manifest list in `corpus-manifests.txt`. Presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not checked. rulespec-us holds only `us-ms/policies/...` modules today (CHIP, Medicaid, income tax); the regulation paths below follow the `us-nc/regulations/...` and `us-ny/regulations/...` layout.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-ms/regulations/title-18/part-24/chapter-2/rule-2-1` | Definitions P (household) and Q (income) | `us-ms/regulation/title-18/part-24` | In manifest `us-ms-liheap-benefit-matrix-rule.yaml` (source_id `us-ms-liheap-title-18-part-24`, expression date 2026-01-01, 64 PDF pages). Same edition the PR cites: [Title 18 Part 24, LIHEAP Policy Manual, revised January 2026; PDF pages 11, 22-24, 29-33, 36, 39, 58-64](https://www.sos.ms.gov/adminsearch/ACCode/00000693c.pdf#page=22). PDF page = printed page + 1. |
| `us-ms/regulations/title-18/part-24/chapter-6/rule-6-1` | Eligibility: energy bill obligation, citizenship or LPR status, 60% SMI, age 18 | same | Same manifest. PDF page 22. |
| `us-ms/regulations/title-18/part-24/chapter-6/rule-6-3` | Immigration status: undocumented head, documented members, non-applicant income counted and excluded from size | same | Same manifest. PDF page 23. |
| `us-ms/regulations/title-18/part-24/chapter-6/rule-6-4` | Renters: utility in rent, itemized charge, $100 per intake | same | Same manifest. PDF page 24. |
| `us-ms/regulations/title-18/part-24/chapter-6/rule-6-11` | Income: gross, 30 days, countable list, exempt list, unearned list, self-employment net profit or loss, minors | same | Same manifest. PDF pages 29-33. |
| `us-ms/regulations/title-18/part-24/chapter-7/rule-7-4` | Household benefit: pay the amount of the bill; credit balances | same | Same manifest. PDF page 36. |
| `us-ms/regulations/title-18/part-24/chapter-7/rule-7-8` | Benefit matrix: $1,500 program year cap, cap by energy type, Total Electric column, electric plus main fuel | same | Same manifest. PDF page 39. The manifest's `benefit_matrix_pdf_pages: '39'` points at this rule text, not at the tables. |
| `us-ms/regulations/title-18/part-24/appendix/income-guidelines` | 60% State Median Income column, sizes 1-20, effective 10/1/2025 | same | Same manifest, but PDF page 58 is an image with no text layer (pdftotext yields only "LIHEAP Benefit Matrix" and "57"). The manifest says image-only pages are skipped in its page numbering, so the table is probably not in the extracted text. Needs OCR or the federal table below. |
| `us-ms/regulations/title-18/part-24/appendix/benefit-matrix` | 2026 LIHEAP Benefit Matrix (Fuel Types), sizes 1-20 | same | Same manifest, but PDF pages 59-64 are images with no text layer, as above. The same tables with a text layer are the standalone attachment below. |
| `us-ms/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/benefit-matrix` | Standalone FY2026 benefit matrix attachment (6 pages, text layer): the tables the PR's parameters encode | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. No `us-ms-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml` exists. Official copy: [MS FY2026 benefit matrix (Heat-Cool), pages 1-6; page 1 holds sizes 1-3, 2 holds 4-6, 3 holds 7-9, 4 holds 10-13, 5 holds 14-17, 6 holds 18-20](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/benefits-matricies/MS_BenefitMatrix_Heat-Cool_2026.pdf#page=1). |
| `us-ms/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-1` | 1.1 component dates; 1.8 gross income; 1.9 countable income checklist | `us-ms/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | In manifest `us-ms-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml` (48 pages). Checkbox states are graphics; the text layer does not say which boxes are checked. Official copy: [MS LIHEAP Detailed Model Plan FY2026, pages 4-6 and 8-9](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/state-plans/MS_Plan_2026.pdf#page=9). |
| `us-ms/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-2` | 2.1 60% SMI; 2.3 renters and subsidized housing; 2.5 bills paid up to the matrix; 2.6 $1 to $1,500 | same | Same manifest. Pages 8-9. |
| `us/regulations/45-cfr/96/96-85` | 96.85(b) household-size percentages (52, 68, 84, 100, 116, 132, plus 3 points per person above six) | none | No manifest name in `corpus-manifests.txt` refers to 45 CFR part 96; needs ingest. Official copy: [45 CFR 96.85, 2024 edition, page 1](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2024-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2024-title45-vol1-sec96-85.pdf#page=1). |
| `us/` state median income module (FY2026) | LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 4: Mississippi four-person SMI $85,708 and the 60% column for sizes 1-12 | none for FY2026 | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml` holds only IM 2026-01 Attachment 4 (mandatory FY2027, optional FY2026), whose Mississippi figure is $90,025 and does not match the manual's limits. Official copy: [SMI by Household Size for Mandatory Use in LIHEAP for FY26, pages 2 and 5](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_IM2025-02_SMIStateTable_Att4.pdf#page=2). |

## Source text (verbatim)

Manual page numbers are PDF pages of the January 2026 Title 18 Part 24 PDF (printed page + 1).

**Program and components.** Chapter 6 introduction (page 22): "Households that consume energy for residential purposes and meet the requirements of the program will be eligible for assistance. Energy bills may include electricity, natural gas, propane/butane, wood, kerosene, and coal." and "The maximum amount of financial assistance and the cost of the energy-related products given to eligible households may be up to $1,500, unless a client needs heating and/or cooling equipment." and "LIHEAP has two (2) components: program assistance known as regular assistance and the Energy Crisis Intervention Program (ECIP) that provides emergency assistance."

FY2026 plan, section 1.1 (page 4): "Heating assistance 10/01/2025 04/30/2026" and "Cooling assistance 05/01/2026 09/30/2026". Cover page: "Report Period: 10/01/2025 to 09/30/2026".

**Household.** Rule 2.1 P (page 11): "Household - Any individual or group of individuals who are living together as one economic unit for whom residential energy is customarily purchased."

Rule 6.6 A (page 24): "A. A live-in attendant should not be counted as a household member. The income of a live-in attendant will not count against an applicant applying for services when the live-in attendant is in the home solely for the applicant to be able to stay in the home."

**Eligibility conditions.** Rule 6.1 (page 22): "An applicant must meet the following requirements to receive a LIHEAP benefit: A. Have an obligation to pay an energy bill directly to a utility company, in subsidized housing where the energy cost is billed separate from rent or can provide evidence from the landlord stating utility is an undesignated portion of the rent, B. Be a U.S. citizen or have legal permanent resident status, C. Have income at or below the 60% state median income guidelines, and D. Be eighteen (18) years of age or older or an emancipated minor (through court action) who is considered head of household."

FY2026 plan, section 2.1 (page 8): "2.1 Designate the income eligibility threshold used for the heating component: Add Household size Eligibility Guideline Eligibility Threshold 1 All Household Sizes State Median Income 60.00%".

**Immigration status.** Rule 6.3 (page 23): "A. If the head of household is undocumented and is a single member of the household, the application must be denied. B. If the head of household is undocumented and has documented member(s) in the household, the application shall not be denied for the entire household. The application must be determined eligible by using the household size of the documented household members and the income for all household members eighteen (18) years of age and older. C. If an individual within the household is undocumented and does not disclose citizenship or establish satisfactory immigration status, ineligibility exists only for the individual, but not the entire household. This individual is considered a “non-applicant” and should not be questioned about citizenship/alien status. However, this individual must disclose and verify income and other information needed to establish the eligibility of the household. The income of this individual must be included in determining the household’s total income; however, this individual will not be counted in determining the household size. D. Eligibility cannot be determined when a “non-applicant” fails to disclose income; therefore, the application should be denied for the entire household."

**Renters and heat in rent.** Rule 6.4 A-B (page 24): "A. If the utility bill is included in the applicant’s rent, the applicant must provide either a copy of the applicants’ lease agreement or the “Landlord Verification Form” must be completed by the landlord detailing the heating/cooling arrangement with the renter. The lease agreement/Landlord Verification Form must include the amount of the utility cost as part of rent and the breakdown of the charges that make up the bill. All energy- related costs included in the bill will be the amount to be paid by LIHEAP to the energy vendor. B. If the lease agreement/verification form does not include an amount, the LIHEAP program will pay $100 per intake until the amount of the benefit matrix has been met."

FY2026 plan, section 2.3 explanations (page 9): "The applicant should provide either a copy of their lease; a notarized statement from the landlord detailing the heating/cooling arrangement with the client; or contract with the landlord that verifies the heating/cooling arrangement that the landlord has with the household. Persons/ households residing in public/subsidized housing dwellings unless their rent/mortgage includes utilities and they are not being billed separately for energy cost." (The second sentence is incomplete in the source.)

**Income.** Rule 2.1 Q (page 11): "Income - Income is money received on a regular and recurring basis by any household member. Income may be earned or unearned."

Rule 6.11 A-C (page 29): "A. Income is money received on a regular and recurring basis by any household member. Income may be earned or unearned. B. A household’s total gross income shall be used to determine eligibility. The total gross income received for the thirty (30) days prior to application date must be verified. C. Countable Income is income (earned or unearned) that must be included when determining eligibility for LIHEAP. The following types of income shall be used: 1) Salaries and wages, including overtime, tips, bonuses, commission, and 13th check; 2) Self-employment income; 3) Contract income; 4) Unemployment insurance; 5) Social Security benefits (including Medicare deduction); 6) SSI,; 7) SSDI; 8) Retirement benefits; 9) Alimony; 10) VA benefits; 11) Workers Compensation; 12) Private Disability (Short/Long Term Disability); 13) Money given to household; and 14) Any income whereas a W2 or 1099 is not received or otherwise documented."

Rule 6.11 D (pages 29-30): "D. Exempt income is income that should not be included when determining eligibility for LIHEAP. The following types of income shall not be considered: 1) Loans/Grants; 2) In-kind income;" then "3) Earnings from employment of a child under the age of 18, unless emancipated; 4) Infrequent income- if an individual receives it only once during a calendar year from a single source and the individual did not receive that type of income in the month immediately before that month or in the month immediately following that month (Examples of this would also be repayment of personal loans, etc.); 5) Reimbursement for business or medical expenses; 6) Payments made by others on behalf of household, unless payments were directly received by household; 7) Benefits received that must be excluded by federal law or incentives paid by TANF or Workforce Investment, earnings and allowances paid under Title IV-A, benefits received under Title VII, HUD, and educational grants; 8) Child support; 9) Payments made to the household for the care of a foster child; 10) Adoption assistance payments; and 11) Refunds such as energy refunds, income tax refunds and EITC, insurance refunds, etc."

Rule 6.11 F(1)-(3) (page 31): "F. Unearned Income - is all income that is not earned. Unearned income shall be used in determining eligibility. Some common examples are: 1) Money and Inheritances given to an individual, a contribution statement is required; 2) Private pensions and annuities; 3) Payments such as Social Security benefits, Railroad Retirement benefits, Department of Veterans Affairs benefits, civil service annuities, workers' compensation, unemployment insurance, retirement benefits, and payments based on need involving federal funds;" and F(7)-(8) (page 32): "7) Dividends and interest; 8) Rents and royalties (except those defined as earned income);"

Rule 6.11 I(1) (page 32): "1) The amount to be used in determining eligibility will be the net income available after deduction of business expenses. Subgrantee should include the amount on the Net Profit or (Loss) line from the Schedule C (Form 1040) Profit or Loss from Business (sole proprietorship), divided by 12."

Rule 6.11 J (page 33): "J. Income of Minors 1) Earned Income – A minor’s (under 18 years of age) income is excluded in the determination of income eligibility. 2) Unearned Income - A minor who receives unearned income such as Social Security or SSI must be included and is listed under the parent or legal guardian in the household."

## Interpretations and gaps

- **Household.** The SPM unit stands in for the economic unit of Rule 2.1 P. Live-in attendants (Rule 6.6) and roomers or boarders with separate bills (Rule 6.5) are not identified.
- **Documented member.** Rule 6.1 B says "U.S. citizen or have legal permanent resident status"; Rule 6.3 C speaks of "satisfactory immigration status" without defining it. The PR counts citizens and the qualified noncitizens of 8 U.S.C. 1641 through `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`, which is wider than LPR status. The existing status input stands in for the documentation requirement; Rule 6.3 D (non-applicant who will not disclose income) is not modeled.
- **Minor's unearned income under an undocumented head.** Rule 6.3 B uses "the income for all household members eighteen (18) years of age and older"; Rule 6.11 J(2) says a minor's Social Security or SSI "must be included and is listed under the parent or legal guardian". The PR counts a minor's unearned income in every household, including one whose only adult is undocumented (`ms_liheap_income.yaml` Case 3: undocumented adult wages $12,000 plus a 15-year-old's SSI $2,400 and Social Security $1,200, earnings excluded, gives size 1 and income $15,600). The reviewer raised this; the PR kept it. The text does not settle it.
- **Self-employment.** Rule 6.11 I(1) uses the Schedule C "Net Profit or (Loss) line". The PR counts the existing net self-employment, SSTB and farm inputs signed, so a loss offsets wages and other members' income, and floors only the household total at zero (`ms_liheap_income.yaml` Cases 1 and 7). Farm income is counted as self-employment on the strength of the farmer example in I(2). The source does not say whether a loss is floored, and does not mention Schedule F.
- **Countable income list and plan conflict.** The PR counts gifts (`financial_assistance`), interest, dividends and rental income per Rule 6.11 C(13), F(7)-(8) and K(1). Plan section 1.9 leaves "Cash gifts", "Rental income" and "Interest, dividends, or royalties" unchecked (checkbox states read from a page render). The PR follows the manual; `ms_liheap_income.yaml` Case 2 ($10,000 wages, $600 gifts, $400 interest, with child support, TANF and a tax refund excluded, gives $11,000) depends on this choice. Occasional versus recurring receipts (Rule 6.11 D(4)), insurance proceeds, prizes, royalties and jury duty pay are not separable in the existing inputs. Social Security is counted gross with the Medicare premium included (Rule 6.11 C(5); plan 1.9 "Including MediCare"); `rental_income` is assumed non-negative. These two are settled decisions.
- **Period.** Annual income stands in for the 30 days before application annualized under Rule 6.11 B and E. Annual bills stand in for the bills presented at each intake; Rule 7.8 C(1)(v) recalculates as income changes, and earlier awards in the program year are not tracked. Earlier years use parameter backfilling and are unverified historical estimates (`integration.yaml` Case 3 uses the FY2022 state median income with the FY2026 matrix).
- **Heating and cooling components.** Plan 1.1 runs heating from 10/01/2025 to 04/30/2026 and cooling from 05/01/2026 to 09/30/2026; both use the same matrix and $1,500 maximum (plan 2.5-2.6 and 3.5-3.6). The PR produces one program-year amount from annual bills and does not attribute it to a season.
- **Heat in rent.** Rule 6.4 A pays "All energy- related costs included in the bill" as itemized in the lease, and Rule 6.4 B pays "$100 per intake until the amount of the benefit matrix has been met" when no amount is itemized. Neither the itemized charge nor the number of intakes is an input, so the PR pays $0 for the main-fuel column of a heat-in-rent household and pays only its own electric bill up to the Electric column (`ms_liheap.yaml` Case 19: $0 with no electric bill, $540 with a $540 electric bill; Case 11 household 9: UNSPECIFIED fuel with heat in rent and a $1,000 electric bill gives $700). Under the text the rent portion would be at least $100 per intake. Eligibility of an unsubsidized renter with heat in rent rests on the landlord-evidence route of Rule 6.1 A.
- **Subsidized housing.** Rule 6.1 A accepts "subsidized housing where the energy cost is billed separate from rent"; plan 2.3's sentence on "public/subsidized housing dwellings unless their rent/mortgage includes utilities and they are not being billed separately" is incomplete. The PR reads both as: a household receiving housing assistance or in public housing qualifies only when its energy is billed separately, and the landlord-evidence route is for unsubsidized renters (`ms_liheap_eligible.yaml` Cases 2 and 4).
- **Income limit arithmetic.** The appendix table is reproduced by floor(floor(0.6 × 85,708) × share) = floor(51,424 × share). Without the inner truncation, floor(51,424.8 × share) differs from size 5 upward (59,652 against the published 59,651; 89,479 against 89,477 at size 20). No rounding rule is stated in the manual, the plan or 45 CFR 96.85. The formula also yields a limit above size 20, where the table says "Contact MDHS/DCS"; the matrix stops at 20, so payment is $0 there.
- **Matrix encoded as printed.** The PR keeps every printed band and cell (`income_bands/1` to `/20`, `propane_exception_*`). Anomalies kept as printed: size 3's fifth row ends at 31,313 where the other sizes' fifth rows end at 125% of the poverty guideline (33,313 for size 3); size 10's second row ends at 35,325 (the pattern gives 32,575); size 8's fifth row and size 12's fourth row run to the income limit; size 16's last row prints Propane 350 where the step pattern gives 650 (`ms_liheap.yaml` Cases 4, 6, 7, 8, 13, 17). Unprinted intervals (size 11: 17,634 to 17,663; size 15: 68,489 to 69,488), incomes above the last printed row but below the limit (size 10 above 72,507; size 18 above 84,849; size 20 above 60,075) and sizes above 20 pay $0 as coverage gaps, not findings of ineligibility (`ms_liheap.yaml` Cases 5, 15, 16). Neither the manual nor the plan states a band formula; Rule 7.8 A only says "See Benefit Matrix Attachment".
- **Manual example inconsistency.** Rule 7.8 C says "the overall cap is $1,200" and C(1) says the "maximum LIHEAP benefit for the program year of 2025 is $1,100" for the same one-person $14,500 household; the FY2026 matrix row prints Maximum Benefit 1200. The per-fuel caps in the example match the FY2026 row, and the PR follows the matrix.
- **Maximum Benefit column.** Not a separate parameter. In every row but one it equals Propane plus Electric and Total Electric Benefit, so the two caps of Rule 7.8 D never exceed it; in size 16's last row Propane 350 plus Electric 550 is 900, below the printed 1200. Rule 7.8 A's $1,500 program-year cap is met by construction.
- **Fuel mapping.** `heating_type` ELECTRICITY stands for a total electric household (Total Electric column, no second payment). COAL, FUEL_OIL, KEROSENE and OTHER use the Wood/Other Fuel column; the chapter 6 introduction names kerosene and coal as energy bills but the matrix has no column for them. SOLAR and NONE have no fuel column and receive the Electric column only. UNSPECIFIED pays $0, except that a household with heat included in rent receives the Electric column for its own electric bill (settled: `heating_type` is a required input). A known fuel with no bill reads as a zero bill.
- **Credit balance.** A negative main-fuel bill is treated as a credit balance under Rule 7.4 C ("Electric and natural gas bills should not be paid if there is a credit balance") and pays $0 without reducing the electric payment (`ms_liheap.yaml` Case 18).
- **Not modeled.** Emancipated-minor applicants (Rule 6.1 D; any member aged 18 or over stands in for the applicant); residency and institutional residents (Rule 6.2); zero-income verification (Rule 6.11 K); past-due amounts and fees, propane quotes and 100-gallon requests, budget plans and prepaid accounts (Rules 7.4 C-E, 7.8 E); the self-employment share of a bill (Rule 7.4 I); income changes during the year. `heating_type` must be sent by callers; the datasets carry no heating inputs, so microsimulation totals are $0 until the default changes (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754).

## Existing corpus starting points

- [FY2026 state-plan manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ms-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [Benefit-matrix rule manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ms-liheap-benefit-matrix-rule.yaml)

These FY2026 manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Link the PE PR and agree the component scope, effective periods, inputs, and outputs. Cover the eligibility and benefit-calculation behavior actually in scope; identify any excluded program components explicitly.
- [ ] Audit official sources and reuse existing corpus content. Ingest missing official documents with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance; obtain signed ingest/release admission. Keep any toolchain or corpus-pin change in its own gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state rule modules with the approved encoder, placing state content under `us-ms/` in the canonical layout. Include source-grounded proofs, benefit parameters where applicable, and companion tests for representative cases, boundaries, and ineligibility. Every test supplies all local inputs.
- [ ] Use personal-Codex local generation followed by exact-commit reviewed-candidate promotion for eligible modules: review the rule/test bytes, obtain the protected allowlist entry for the commit/base branch, and run protected validation/signing with the required approval. Retain the signed manifests and evidence that rule/test bytes are unchanged.
- [ ] Assemble and validate a runnable program with the required indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing blocker before declaring the complete program shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) is currently open.
- [ ] Add concept/input/output mappings and reproducible fixtures in axiom-oracles against the merged PE implementation, pinned to an exact commit. Record units and periods, compare representative and boundary cases, and resolve or explicitly disposition mismatches against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, and oracle PRs and successful CI/promotion evidence. Record the shipped scope and any remaining gaps.

## Contribution route

Use the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion contract](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion), added by [axiom-encode#1696](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/pull/1696). It validates and signs explicitly admitted reviewed content without regenerating it; it does not authenticate the original generating runtime. The [planned personal-Codex experiment](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1622#issuecomment-5940016560) records the process. The five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs are not prerequisites for testing this route.

This issue tracks work to ship; it does not claim the encoding, promotion experiment, or PE parity validation is already complete.
