items.body:
## Objective

Ship Ohio HEAP (LIHEAP) regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 2a, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9975 (branch `oh-liheap`), open and ready for review, not merged; head `259a6135e3` (2026-10-19) addresses PavelMakarchuk's review. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

- **Sources need ingest.** Only the FY2026 state plan, its attachment (the 2025 DRAFT workbook), the 2026 poverty guidelines and LIHEAP IM 2026-01 are in axiom-corpus manifests on `main` (checked 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-19); 42 USC 8624 is in an ingest-note statute scope. Every other source in the next section, the Guidelines (the program manual) included, needs ingest.
- **The manual copy was declined.** The benefit-matrix manifest declines the Guidelines copy the branch cites: “the Clearinghouse-listed manual is on a third-party CDN (irp.cdn-website.com) and is not taken”. Ingest needs an admissible copy of the manual or explicit admission of this one.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not checked.
- **Billing.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval.
- **No reviewed PE revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9975 is unmerged: PavelMakarchuk approved `a2cb1869c5` with comments, and DTrim99's re-review is pending.
- **2026 and later payments are estimates.** The FY 2026 matrix is unpublished; the branch fits its coefficients to the range in the accepted FY2027 plan (interpretation 3).

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9975, branch `oh-liheap`, head `259a6135e3` (2026-10-19). `a2cb1869c5` (2026-10-15) answered DTrim99's 2026-10-14 review; PavelMakarchuk approved it with comments. `259a6135e3` addresses his review: the 110% floor is rounded to the cent, so income of exactly 110% fails (interpretation 20); `fpg_floor.yaml` matches PR 10279 and 8624 links carry `#b_2_B`; HSA payroll deferrals are deducted (interpretation 12); the accepted FY2027 plan replaces its draft (interpretations 3, 9); LIHEAP IM 2024-02, 2025-02 and 2026-01 back the lag; seven new cases. Everything below describes `259a6135e3`.
- **Scope:** the regular Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP) credit, paid once a season to the main heating account: household size, countable income, the limit, heating responsibility and the benefit-matrix payment (fuel, region, targeted households). Out of scope: the Winter Crisis Program, emergency HEAP, the Summer Crisis Program (cooling), the Percentage of Income Payment Plan Plus (PIPP) and its award reduction (interpretation 16), weatherization (HWAP), the Electric Partnership Program, fuel tanks, heating-system repair or replacement.
- **Policy periods:** model year N is the season July N−1 to May N, credited from January N; every Ohio variable is annual and reads the value in force on 1 January of N. Payment entries: `2021-01-01` (2021 FINAL, also 2022; the 150% cap, all years), `2023-01-01` (2023 FINAL), `2024-01-01` and `2025-01-01` (DRAFT-cover estimates), `2026-01-01` (fitted estimate; carried into 2027 on). Eligibility entries: `2022-07-01` (175% of the prior year's guideline, all sizes; model year 2023, backfilling 2021 and 2022), `2024-07-01`, `2025-07-01`, `2026-07-01` (model years 2025 to 2027). Income-source and deduction lists and the adult age start at `2025-07-01` and backfill (countable-income Case 21 tests 2025); `gov.hhs.liheap.fpg_floor` is 1.1 from `1985-10-01`. `programs.yaml`: Ohio `partial`, no `verified_years`. 2021 and 2023 payments reproduce 4,793 of 4,848 non-PIPP cells (interpretation 6); 2022 carries 2021; 2024 on are estimates. Model year 2024 eligibility matches the July 2023 application.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/oh/odjfs/liheap/`: `oh_liheap`, `oh_liheap_household_size`; `eligibility/oh_liheap_eligible`, `eligibility/oh_liheap_income_limit`; `income/oh_liheap_countable_income`. The limit, the 110% floor and the payment use the federal `fpg()` helper with `year_lag`; the SMI limit uses the shared `liheap_smi_limit`.
- **Parameters:** 24 files under `gov.states.oh.odjfs.liheap`: `eligibility/` (FPG and SMI rates and year lags, `maximum_fpg_household_size`), `income/` (`adult_age`, `deductions`, earned and unearned `sources/`), `payment/` (`formula/` intercept, slope, poverty-ratio bounds; three `fuel_cost_ratio/` files; `regional/` factors and county lists; `targeted/` ages, multiplier, `young_child_in_effect`), plus the shared `gov.hhs.liheap.fpg_floor`.
- **Tests:** 75 YAML cases in 5 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/oh/odjfs/liheap/` at `259a6135e3` (`oh_liheap.yaml` 28, `oh_liheap_household_size.yaml` 2, `eligibility/oh_liheap_eligible.yaml` 16, `eligibility/oh_liheap_income_limit.yaml` 8, `income/oh_liheap_countable_income.yaml` 21). Every eligibility and payment case sends `heating_type`. PavelMakarchuk ran the 68 earlier cases at `a2cb1869c5`; the seven new ones were not run locally; CI validates them.

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence on axiom-corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-06, 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-19 (git tree of `manifests/`, 1,714 files; Ohio LIHEAP has only the two FY2026 manifests); presence in the signed release was not. Paths follow rulespec-us's `us-oh/policies/` and `us-oh/statutes/` layout with `odjfs`, the administering agency since 2026-04-06 (Development issued the Guidelines, workbooks and earlier applications). Pages are PDF pages, equal to printed numbers unless noted.

[2022–2023 Energy Assistance Programs Guidelines, pages 5 to 12, 56, 57 and 73 to 76](https://irp.cdn-website.com/aa88b0b1/files/uploaded/2022-24%20ATTACHMENT%202022-2023%20EAP%20Guidelines%20%281%29.pdf#page=5) |
| `.../eap-guidelines/2022-2023/e-4-utility-information` | E-4 (pages 11 to 12): heating and electric information, bills not in a member's name, eligible primary heat sources | none | Same file; needs ingest. |
| `.../eap-guidelines/2022-2023/appendix-xxiii-income` | Appendix XI (page 56): non-taxable Health Care Spending Accounts are allowable deductions; Appendix XII (page 57): pay stubs with pre-tax insurance deductions; Appendix XXIII (pages 73 to 76): countable income types, deductions, excluded income | none | Same file; needs ingest. |

| `us-oh/policies/odjfs/heap-benefit-matrix/2021-final/...` | Cover (page 1): target factor 1.50 (elderly, disabled), 50% floor, ±6% regions, PIPP offset, credits 61 and 50; Tables 1 (8), 2A (9 to 10), 2B (15 to 16), 2C (19 to 20; PIPP 22), 3A and 3B (23, 24, 26); formula (11) | none | Needs ingest. [2021 FINAL HEAP Benefit Matrix workbook, pages 1, 8 to 11, 15, 16, 19, 20, 22 to 24 and 26](https://liheapch.acf.gov/sites/default/files/webfiles/docs/OH_BenefitMatrix_2022.pdf#page=1) (Clearinghouse file names run a year ahead). |
| `.../heap-benefit-matrix/2023-final/...` | Cover (page 1): target factor 1.75 adding children 5 or under, credits 70 and 56; Tables 1 (8), 2A (9 to 10), 2B (15 to 16), 2C (19 to 20; PIPP 22), 3A and 3B (23 to 26), 4 (29); formula (11) | none | Needs ingest. [2023 FINAL LIHEAP Benefit Matrix workbook, pages 1, 8 to 11, 15, 16, 19, 20, 22 to 26 and 29](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2024/benefits-matricies/OH_BenefitMatrix_2024.pdf#page=1). |
| `.../heap-benefit-matrix/2024-draft/cover` | Credit percentages 46 and 38; maximum and minimum benefit by fuel | none | Needs ingest. [2024 DRAFT LIHEAP Benefit Matrix](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2025/benefits-matricies/OH_BenefitMatrix_2025.pdf). |
| `.../heap-benefit-matrix/2025-draft/cover` | Credit percentages 25 and 22; maximum and minimum benefit by fuel | `us-oh/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026-benefit-matrix` | In `us-oh-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml` (same URL), dated 2025-10-01 as the FY 2026 attachment; the branch applies it to model year 2025 (interpretation 2). [2025 DRAFT LIHEAP Benefit Matrix](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/benefits-matricies/OH_BenefitMatrix_2026.pdf). |

[Ohio Consumers' Counsel HEAP fact sheet, 2026–2027, page 1](https://occ.ohio.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/OCC-Home-Energy-Assistance-Program-HEAP_0.pdf#page=1); [Ohio Development IU-2025-5, January 16, 2025](https://wofb.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/IU-2025-5-HEAP-Customer-Benefit-Update.pdf); [HEAP FAQ for customers, January 2025, page 1](https://wofb.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/ATTACHMENT-2025-5-HEAP-FAQ-for-Customers.pdf#page=1); the last two on a West Ohio Food Bank host (no state copy found). |

Need ingest: the 2020 to 2025 guidelines ([ASPE prior HHS poverty guidelines and Federal Register references](https://aspe.hhs.gov/topics/poverty-economic-mobility/poverty-guidelines/prior-hhs-poverty-guidelines-federal-register-references)), [IM 2024-02 Attachment 2](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_IM%202024-02_Att2FPGTables_States.pdf#page=1) (FY25) and [IM 2025-02 Attachment 2](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_IM2025-02_FPGSte-Table_Att2.pdf#page=1) (FY26). |

## Source text (verbatim)

Quotations copy `pdftotext -layout` text of the official files, line breaks collapsed; “...” marks an interleaved column, [brackets] an editorial insertion. Check-box states come from page renders and are reported, not quoted.

**Program and benefit factors.** Guidelines E-1, page 5: “Clients at or below 175% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG) receive a benefit in the form of a credit directly to the client's main energy heating account beginning in the month of January.” and “The benefit amount depends on ... household poverty level, household main heating source, household location, if someone in the home is disabled, if a person in the home is 60 years of age or older, if there is a child in the home 5 years of age or younger, or if the household is enrolled in the Percentage of Income Payment Plan Plus (PIPP).” JFS 00330, page 1: “IMPORTANT: The HEAP Program runs from July 1, 2026 – May 30, 2027.”

**Household.** Guidelines E-2.1, page 6: “A household is defined by Section 2603 (5) ... as any individual or group of individuals who are living together as one economic unit for whom residential energy is customarily purchased in common or who make undesignated payments for energy in the form of rent (heat is included in the rent).” The “Counting Household Members” table (pages 6 to 7) marks “Tax dependents living in the household” Counted, foster and temporary-custody children Not Counted, and “Undocumented Alien*” Not Counted, with the note on page 7: “*Non-citizens, those who are not a Legal Resident or not a Qualified Alien in the home, shall have their income counted, but not their household membership.” E-2.8, page 10: “As long as there is one citizen in the household (whether adult or child) the household could be eligible for assistance.” and “The non-U.S. citizens/legal residents or qualified alien household members must be excluded from the total number of household members when calculating the benefit amount.” The three later applications (page 1) exclude residents of medical facilities and public community residences, adding: “Boarding/rooming houses, group homes or emergency shelters are also not eligible.”

**Income limit.** Guidelines E-2.2, page 7: “To be eligible, the total household Countable Income for the last 30 days or 12 months prior to the application date must be equal to or less than 175% of the FPG (150% for PIPP).” Its “12-Month Income Limit” 175% column prints size 1 “$23,782.50” through size 8 “$81,602.50”, then: “When determining 175% of the FPG, households with more than eight members must add $8,260 to the yearly income or $678.90 to the 30-day income for each additional member.” E-2, page 6: “At or below 175% FPG for the previous 30 days or 12 months for HEAP, SCP, and WCP.” and, for the benefit, “Lowest poverty level for either 30-day or 12-month period.”

FY2023 plan, page 8, item 2.1: household size “All Household Sizes”, “State Median Income”, “60.00%”, with: “Explanation of 2.1 Eligibility Threshold: Ohio uses 60% of the State Median Income as it best correlates to 175% of the HHS Federal Poverty level. Households must be at or below 175% of the Federal Poverty Level in order to be determined eligible.”

Application July 2023–May 2024, page 1: 175% limits from $25,515 (size 1) to $88,480 (size 8); “households with more than eight members must add $8,995 to the yearly income”.

Application July 2024–May 2025, page 1: “When determining households up to seven members for HEAP, SCP, and WCP, 175% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG) is used. For HEAP, SCP, and WCP households over eight members,60% State Median Income (SMI) is used.” FY2025 plan, page 8, item 2.1: one row, household size “8”, “State Median Income”, “60.00%”.

Application July 2025–May 2026, page 1: “When determining households up to eight members for HEAP, SCP, and WCP, 175% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG) is used. For HEAP, SCP, and WCP households over eight members, 60% State Median Income (SMI) is used.” FY2026 plan, page 8, item 2.1: one row, household size “9”, “State Median Income”, “60.00%”.

JFS 00330 (07/2026), page 1: “When determining households up to seven members for HEAP, 175% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG) is used. For HEAP, households over seven members, 60% State Median Income (SMI) is used.” Accepted FY2027 plan, page 9, item 2.1: household size “9”, “State Median Income”, “60.00%” (July 2026 draft, page 8: “8”). Consumers' Counsel fact sheet, page 1: income “must be at or below 175 percent of the federal income ... guidelines for households with up to seven people, ... and 60 percent of the State Median Income (SMI) for ... households of eight or more (see charts).”

Printed 175% limits (“Income Guidelines”, 12-month column, application page 1 of each season):

| Size | July 2024–May 2025 | July 2025–May 2026 | July 2026–May 2027 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | $26,355 | $27,387 | $27,930 |
| 2 | $35,770 | $37,012 | $37,870 |
| 3 | $45,185 | $46,637 | $47,810 |
| 4 | $54,600 | $56,262 | $57,750 |
| 5 | $64,015 | $65,887 | $67,690 |
| 6 | $73,430 | $75,512 | $77,630 |

Case 8: alimony and general assistance count (page 74; E-2.3 catch-all), child support received and TANF do not (pages 75 to 76): 12,000 + 1,200 + 1,200. Case 9: Child Support paid-out (page 74): 30,000 − 3,600 ≤ 27,387. Case 12: Medicare Premiums (page 74; application; plan 1.9): 28,000 − 2,434.80. Case 13: military pensions count (page 73); railroad retirement is Other Countable Income (E-2.3); 30,000 > 27,387. Case 16: landlord income is self-employment (page 73); each source is floored separately: 12,000 + 600. | 13,800; 14,400; 26,400 and eligible; 25,565.20; 30,000 and ineligible (both); 12,600 | Guidelines pp. 8, 73, 74; application p. 7; FY2026 plan p. 6 |
| 14 | Other unearned sources and premium deductions (`income/oh_liheap_countable_income.yaml` Cases 17, 18, 19, 20, 21) | period 2026, one adult per unit. Case 17, five units: wages 11,440 and unemployment 5,720; wages 20,240 and strike benefits 3,000; age 58, `is_disabled`, `veterans_benefits` (VA pension) 17,441; wages 17,600 and workers' compensation 5,124; wages 17,160 and `disability_benefits` 3,432. Case 18: wages 22,880, `pre_tax_health_insurance_premiums` 1,440. Case 19: the Case 12 unit (row 13) plus 467.88 of `health_insurance_premiums_without_medicare_part_b` (Part D). Case 20: wages 22,880, `health_savings_account_payroll_contributions` 1,700. Case 21: period 2025, age 70, Social Security 28,000, `medicare_part_b_premium` 2,220 | Unemployment and VA pensions (page 73), workers' compensation, disability payouts and strike benefits (page 74) count. Health premiums, including those withheld before tax (Appendix XII, page 57), prescription-plan and Medicare premiums are each deducted once (page 74; application p. 7). Health Care Spending Accounts (Appendix XI, page 56) are deducted; the list applies in 2025. | 17,160; 23,240; 17,441; 22,724; 20,592. 22,880 − 1,440 = 21,440. 28,000 − 2,434.80 − 467.88 = 25,097.32. 22,880 − 1,700 = 21,180. 28,000 − 2,220 = 25,780 | Guidelines pp. 56, 57, 73, 74; application p. 7 |
| 15 | Terminal 150+ rows (`oh_liheap.yaml` Cases 23, 24) | propane, `heating_expense` 1,200. Period 2021, wages: Ashtabula 19,140 and 22,330; Adams 19,140 and 22,330; age 60 with 22,330 in Ashtabula, then Adams; Ashtabula 22,331. Period 2023: the same with 20,385, 23,782 and 23,783 | Table 3B, size 1, 150% and 175%: 2021 $19,140 and $22,330 (page 26); 2023 $20,385 (page 25), limit $23,782.50 (Guidelines page 7). Row 150+ of Tables 2B (page 16) and 2C (page 20), PROPANE and PROPANE WEIGHTED; income above 175% is ineligible. | 2021: 403, 403, 357, 357, 604, 536, 0. 2023: 564, 564, 500, 500, 987, 875, 0 | 2021 and 2023 workbooks pp. 1, 16, 20, 25, 26; Guidelines p. 7 |
| 16 | Federal 110% floor and its threshold edges (`oh_liheap.yaml` Cases 25, 26; `eligibility/oh_liheap_eligible.yaml` Cases 15, 16) | `oh_liheap_household_size` set directly. (a) 2026, size 20, propane: wages 120,150, then 132,165. (b) 2026, size 17, propane: 114,014.99, then 114,015. (c) 2027, size 17, gas: 117,523.99, then 117,524. (d) 2026, 17 citizens: parents with wages 70,000 and 43,446, fifteen dependent children, gas | Limit floor(68,755 × size percentage), 68,755 = floor(0.6 × 114,593): 1.74 at size 20 (0.52 + 5 × 0.16 + 14 × 0.03), 119,633; 1.65 at 17, 113,445 (2026 and 2027). Floor round(1.1 × guideline, 2): 2025 guideline 15,650 + 5,500 per added member (120,150 at 20, floor 132,165; 103,650 at 17, floor 114,015); 2026 guideline at 17, 15,960 + 16 × 5,680 = 106,840, floor 117,524. Income below the floor passes above the limit; income at the floor fails. (d) 113,446 is $1 above the limit. Awards: interpretation 3. | (a) limit 119,633; true, false. (b) limit 113,445; true, false. (c) true, false. (d) size 17, income 113,446, true | 42 USC 8624(b)(2)(B); IM 2025-02 Att. 2; IM 2026-01; HHS FFY2026 Att. 4 pp. 2, 5 |

### SBP companion

[Pavel, October 22](#issuecomment-6349323971): `military_retirement_income` = `military_retirement_pay` + `military_retirement_pay_survivors`, counted once. Existing retiree-only tests are unchanged.

| Case | Inputs | Expected | Derivation |
|---|---|---|---|
| SBP-1 | period 2026; Ohio, Franklin County; one citizen adult aged 62, not a tax dependent, not disabled; `military_retirement_pay_survivors` $9,600; no other income or deductions; NATURAL_GAS, `gas_expense` $1,200; heat not in rent; no housing assistance | countable income $9,600; limit $27,387; eligible true | A military SBP annuity is a military pension paid to a widow or widower (page 73), counted gross (E-2.2, page 7): $9,600, at or below the size 1 limit $27,387 (application July 2025–May 2026). The award is not given here: the 2026 coefficients rest on interpretations 2 and 3. |

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Guideline lag.** Both FINAL workbooks' Table 3A income levels equal the prior year's guideline (2020, 2022), supporting the one-year lag.
2. **2024 and 2025 coefficients (DRAFT-cover estimates).** The covers print only credit percentages and award extremes; the branch applies the 2023 page 11 method and $950 high winter cost: B = (maximum − minimum credit) × 950 / 100 and A = maximum credit × 950 + 50 × B give A 475, B 0.76 (2024) and A 251.75, B 0.285 (2025). These reproduce every printed maximum (case 6), not interior awards; the printed minimums are PIPP awards (interpretation 16). No gas ratio is printed; 0.7236 to 0.7247 reproduces both gas maximums, and the branch uses 0.724. IU-2025-5 confirms both ranges despite the 2025 DRAFT's 5/1/2025 date. Dependent (`oh_liheap.yaml` Cases 16 and 17, other rows): 2025 Franklin propane at 15,060 (100% of the 2024 guideline): 251.75 − 28.5 = 223.25, $223; 2025 Franklin age 60 at the floor: gas 237.5 × 0.724 × 1.75 = 300.91, $301; propane $416; coal $249; 2024 Franklin at the floor: gas $316, propane $437, coal $262; Adams propane $411; 100% $399; 150% $361.
3. **2026 and later payments (estimate).** Accepted FY2027 plan items 2.5 and 2.6 (page 10) attach the unpublished FY 2026 matrix (used for model year 2026, as FY 2025 is for 2025) and print $31 and $546, as the July 2026 draft did. Credits of 31% and 28.5% give B = (0.31 − 0.285) × 9.5 = 0.2375 and A = 0.31 × 950 + 50 × 0.2375 = 306.375. 31% reproduces the maximum (294.5 × 1.06 × 1.75 = 546.30, $546); 28.5% lies in the 28.2% to 29.1% range whose coal minimum, 0.19 of the regular award (interpretation 16), rounds to $31 (270.75 × 0.6 × 0.19 = 30.87), so B could be about 0.18 to 0.27. The plan estimates FY2027 at the same range; 2027 carries the 2026 values. Dependent `oh_liheap.yaml` cases: 6 (2026, 15,650: 282.625, $283), 7 (2027, 15,960: $283), 8 (heat in rent, $0 income, base 294.5: Ashtabula fuel oil 312.17, $312; subsidized gas tenant with an electric bill 213.22, $213; subsidized with no bill, UNSPECIFIED and NONE, $0), 18 (interpretation 5), 19, 21, 22, 25 ($283, then $0), 26 (size 17, 114,014.99: 109.99999%, 280.25, $280), 27 (gas, 22,880 with no deduction, a 1,440 pretax premium or a 1,700 HSA deferral: 146.20%, 137.00%, 135.34%; $197, $198, $199), 28 (Ashtabula, age 60, propane, $0: $546).
4. **2022.** No 2022 FINAL workbook was found; 2022 carries 2021 (`oh_liheap.yaml` Case 15: 320, 464, 290, weighted propane 695; 12,880, the 2021 guideline, is 100%: 495.08 × 0.852 = 421.81, $422). FY2023 plan item 2.6 (page 9) prints “Minimum Benefit $50 Maximum Benefit $930” for the attached FY2022 matrix, above the 2021 maximum ($737); 2022 stays unclaimed.
5. **Above 150% of poverty.** The covers allow 175% (“Max Poverty”), but Tables 2B and 2C of both FINAL workbooks (pages 16, 20) end with “150+”, so the payment caps the poverty ratio at 1.5 (case 15). Table 4 (page 29) prints “>150” “0.00”; the branch follows the payment tables. Dependent: `oh_liheap.yaml` Case 5 (2026, guideline 15,650: 23,475, 23,475.01, 25,431.25 and 27,387 each pay 306.375 − 0.2375 × 150 = 270.75, $271; 27,388 is over the limit, $0) and Case 18 (age 70, Social Security 28,000 less Part B 2,434.80 = 25,565.20, 163.36%, capped: 270.75 × 1.75 = 473.81, $474; without the premium, $0).
6. **Workbook precision (branch test disagrees with the printed table).** With the printed four-decimal coefficients the branch reproduces 4,793 of 4,848 printed non-PIPP cells in Tables 2A to 2C; the 2023 gas ratio 0.5523 leaves 19 of 2,424 off by $1 (gas and electricity), the 2021 slope and ratios 36 of 2,424 (spread across every fuel group). Full precision (2023 gas 0.5523335; 2021 slope 0.981255, ratios 0.58821435, 0.85197, 0.532482) reproduces every cell; the branch keeps the printed values. `oh_liheap.yaml` Case 11 asserts $333 (income 13,046.40, 96%) and $578 (age 60, 13,590) where Table 2A prints $334 (row 96 GAS/ELEC, page 9) and $579 (row 100 GAS/ELEC WEIGHTED, page 10). The companion value is the printed cell.
7. **Poverty percentage.** The tables use whole percentages; no source says whether to truncate or round. The branch uses the continuous ratio, equal to the printed rows at whole percentages. Annual income stands in for the 30-day or 12-month choice and the “Lowest poverty level” rule.
8. **Limit rounding.** The applications print 175% limits floored to whole dollars (1.75 × 54,150 = 94,762.50, printed $94,762); the branch floors every limit. The Guidelines print cents ($23,782.50); with whole-dollar income (E-2.3) the floor is equivalent, so branch Case 6 asserts 23,782; 81,602; 89,862; 98,122.
9. **Size cutoffs.** 2023–2024: the July 2023 application (page 1) prints $25,515 through $88,480 plus $8,995 per member above eight, the all-sizes rule (`eligibility/oh_liheap_income_limit.yaml` Case 7: 25,515; 88,480; 97,475). 2024–2025: the application says FPG “up to seven members” and SMI “over eight members”; the branch follows the FY2025 plan (size 8 at SMI). 2025–2026: FPG through 8. 2026–2027: through 7 (JFS 00330, Consumers' Counsel, the July 2026 draft plan); the accepted FY2027 plan's item 2.1 (page 9) lists SMI from size 9, and the branch follows the application. The FY2023 plan explains its “All Household Sizes” SMI row as 175% of the FPL (`eligibility/oh_liheap_eligible.yaml` Case 14: nine members, 80,000 ≤ 89,862). From size 8 the printed 2022–2023 and 2023–2024 limits exceed the 8624(b)(2)(B) ceiling, max(150% FPG, 60% SMI) (size 8: $81,602.50 against max($69,945, $77,540); $88,480 against max($75,840, $82,886)); these unclaimed years keep them.
10. **SMI year and rounding (settled).** Ohio does not state the SMI year; the branch infers it from the 8624(b)(2)(B) cap (175% of the guideline at the last FPG size cannot exceed 60% of SMI): size 7 in 2024–2025 ($82,845) exceeds FFY2024 (100,106 × 0.6 × 1.35 = 81,086) but not FFY2025 ($88,547); size 8 in 2025–2026 ($94,762) exceeds FFY2025 ($90,515) but not FFY2026 ($94,881); the 2026–2027 Consumers' Counsel amounts match FFY2026. Truncating 60% of the four-person median, then the size-adjusted amount, reproduces every HHS FFY2025 and FFY2026 cell. Consumers' Counsel sizes 9 and 10 ($96,946, $99,010) exceed even the unrounded amounts (96,945.68, 99,008.35); the model uses HHS. Dependent (`eligibility/oh_liheap_income_limit.yaml`): Case 2 (2025: 65,591 × 1.38 = 90,515.58, $90,515; × 1.41, $92,483), Case 8 (2026, size 9: 68,755 × 1.41 = 96,944.55, $96,944).
11. **Minors' income (plan and manual conflict; the branch follows the manual).** The FY2026 plan and Consumers' Counsel exclude only minors' earnings; the Guidelines count members 18 or older plus a minor's SS/SSDI paid to an adult payee. The branch (settled 2026-10-06) excludes a dependent minor's income except `social_security`, whoever the payee is, and does not count a child's SSI. A nondependent 17-year-old counts as an adult, standing in for the emancipated minor (E-2.2, E-2.4). Dependent: `income/oh_liheap_countable_income.yaml` Case 5 (the case 12 child as a nondependent: 22,800).
12. **Gross versus net.** Plan item 1.8 checks “Gross Income”; the branch follows the Guidelines and the application and subtracts the five `income/deductions.yaml` inputs once per unit, against all income. The health inputs (premiums without Part B, user decision 2026-10-07; payroll premiums, Appendix XII, page 57; Part B; HSA payroll deferrals) are disjoint, so nothing is deducted twice. Employee HSA deferrals (gross in `employment_income`) stand in for Appendix XI's non-taxable Health Care Spending Accounts (page 56); no input holds health FSA deferrals. Disability premiums, spenddown, attorney fees and work-expense reimbursements have no input. Ohio nets Medicare (“Medicare Premiums”, the application, plan 1.9 “Excluding MediCare deduction”). Self-employment uses the net inputs.
13. **General assistance (settled: the manual's catch-all over the plan).** General assistance is in neither Guidelines list; E-2.3 counts “any income not listed above”, while plan 1.9 leaves it unchecked. The branch counts `general_assistance` (as railroad retirement). TANF and child support received are excluded by both sources and not read.
14. **Heat in rent (plan and manual conflict; the branch follows the manual).** Plan 2.3 requires renters with heat in the rent to prove they pay part of the electric bill; Guidelines E-4 (page 12) does not require the bill in a member's name. The branch follows E-4 for unsubsidized tenants (case 10 (c)) and requires a heating or electric bill for subsidized and public-housing tenants (application; plan 2.3). The award uses the reported primary fuel.
15. **Fuels and counties.** `heating_type` is required; an unspecified fuel pays $0 (default tracked in PolicyEngine/policyengine-us issue 9754), heat in rent included, because the amount depends on the fuel. SOLAR and OTHER have no column and are not primary heat sources (Guidelines page 12); like UNSPECIFIED they stay eligible with a $0 estimate (settled; `oh_liheap.yaml` Case 9 asserts the flags). An explicit UNKNOWN or non-Ohio county pays $0 (Case 20); an omitted county defaults to Adams, a southern county, paid at −6% (Case 19: propane 294.5 × 0.94 = 276.83, $277; gas 200.42, $200).
16. **PIPP.** E-1, the plans, every cover and the January 2025 FAQ (“75% HEAP reduction”) reduce the award for PIPP households; the covers project 76% to 82% of customers on PIPP. The cover minimums are the unweighted PIPP cells of row 150+ (Table 2C, page 22 of each FINAL workbook), in every workbook 0.19 of the regular central award at 150% (2021 to the cent: $49.85, $72.20, $45.13): 0.94 (the southern factor) less 0.75 (the “PIPP Plus Reduced Benefit Offset”). No input identifies enrollment; the branch computes the non-PIPP award.
17. **Household.** The SPM unit stands in for the economic unit; the counting table's custody, absence, foster, live-in aide and student rules and the ineligible residences are not derived. Qualified status has no waiting periods. The payment uses the qualified size (E-2.8): `oh_liheap.yaml` Case 21 (citizen 40 with wages 18,000, undocumented 38 with 12,000, citizen child 8: size 2, income 30,000 ≤ 37,012; 30,000 / 21,150 = 141.84%; 306.375 − 33.69 = 272.69, $273). `is_disabled` stands in for verified permanent and total disability.
18. **Sources.** Mapped: pensions to `pension_income` or `military_retirement_income`; military widow/widower SBP annuities to the latter, other widow's benefits to `survivor_benefits`, employment disability payouts to `disability_benefits`, IRA and annuity withdrawals to `retirement_distributions`, estate and trust payouts to `estate_income`, lottery winnings to `gambling_winnings`. Not modeled: utility assistance, Black Lung pensions, insurance payouts, other settlements. All `veterans_benefits` count, because the input cannot separate excluded VA disability. Every source is floored at zero separately (settled), so a loss offsets nothing (`oh_liheap.yaml` Case 22: a self-employment loss gives the floor, 294.5 × 0.724 = 213.22, $213; wages 15,650 with rental and capital losses stay at 100%, 282.625 × 0.724 = 204.62, $205).
19. **Guidelines edition.** Only the 2022–2023 Guidelines were found; the branch applies them to every season, checked against each application.
20. **Federal 110% floor.** 42 USC 8624(b)(2)(B) bars excluding a household on income below 110% of the poverty level; Ohio's plans repeat it (FY2026 page 48; FY2027 page 50). The 60% SMI limit falls below that floor for 17 or more members in 2025 to 2027 (2025: 108,225 < 111,254 at size 17; 2026: 113,445 < 114,015), never in 2021 to 2024. The branch ORs income < round(1.1 × FPG(N−1, size), 2) into the income test, keeping the printed limit and size > 0 outside the OR; unrounded, 1.1 × 103,650 = 114,015.00000000001 in float64 would admit income of exactly 110%. HHS makes each January's guidelines mandatory for LIHEAP from the next October 1 (IM 2024-02, 2025-02, 2026-01), so model years 2025 to 2027 use the 2024 to 2026 guidelines (companion test 16).

## Existing corpus starting points

- [FY2026 state-plan manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-oh-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [FY2026 plan benefit-matrix attachment manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-oh-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml)
- [LIHEAP annual figures 2026 manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml)
- [Federal statute layer ingest note](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/docs/ingest-runs/2026-09-13-federal-statute-layer.md) (42 USC 8621 to 8630 scope)

These FY2026 manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission. The sources listed under Why queued are not in any manifest and need ingest before the modules above can be proved.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-oh/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the 2022–2023 to 2026–2027 limits (175% of the guideline with dated size cutoffs, 60% of SMI above) and the 110% floor; the payment formula (2021 to 2025 coefficients, the 2026 estimate, the 150% cap) against the printed tables and maxima; county factors, fuel ratios and targeted households; heat in rent and subsidized housing; mixed-status households; dependent-minor income; and the child support, health, HSA and Medicare deductions. Set heating type and county explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: LIHEAP wave 1d: encode Louisiana LIHEAP regular heating assistance

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Louisiana LIHEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1d, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10429 (branch `la-liheap-wave1d`), open, not merged. Head `7c35019e79` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983`; this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **Sources missing from the corpus.** No axiom-corpus manifest on `main` holds the branch's main source for the FY2026 heating season, the Louisiana LIHEAP Service Delivery Guide revised January 1, 2024 (income, citizenship, responsibility, total energy cost, utility allowance, benefit and Appendix E rules). `us-la-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml` holds the edition effective April 1, 2026, which took effect after the FY2026 heating window closed. Also missing: the Clearinghouse copy of the FFY2026 benefit matrix that the branch cites (the same matrix is page 60 of the agency model plan in `us-la-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml`), Notice LHP-2025-01 (FY2026 income limits), the Service Delivery Guide FAQs of February 11, 2022 (answer A4), Memorandum LA LIHEAP 09 (edition dates), the final FFY2026 Plan Changes summary (heating dates), the HHS FY2026 state median income table (LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 4; the corpus holds the FY2027 table), the IM 2025-02 Attachment 2 poverty-guideline table and 42 U.S.C. 8624. These need ingest before the modules below can be proved. The accepted FY2026 state plan and the 2025 HHS poverty guidelines are captured.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-23; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.
- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10429 opened on 2026-10-23 with no reviews yet, so there is no revision to pin.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10429, branch `la-liheap-wave1d`, head `7c35019e79` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983` and closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10419. It adds the files below, a `programs.yaml` entry and a changelog fragment. Review fixes from 2026-10-22 add the April 1, 2026 guide beside every January 2024 guide reference, drop a floor on `ssi` that could never bind, and drop two duplicate income-limit cases (sizes 8 and 13); no expected value changed.
- **Scope:** Louisiana LIHEAP regular heating assistance, the single heating-season award of the Louisiana Housing Corporation (LHC) for FY2026: Louisiana residence, household size from citizens and qualified noncitizens (undocumented members' income still counts), gross countable income of members 18 and over plus Social Security and SSI of every member, the 60% state median income limit with the federal 110% poverty floor, responsibility for an energy bill or heat in rent, total energy cost across all energy bills less the HUD utility allowance for subsidized households without a member 60 or older, the energy burden band (total energy cost over income) by household size from the FFY2026 matrix ($200 to $700), the size maximum for zero income, and one $100 priority supplement. Out of scope: the summer cooling cycle (the same matrix applied in the cooling season), crisis assistance, weatherization, equipment repair or replacement, discretionary supplemental heating payments, credit balances from earlier assistance and first-come, first-served funding.
- **Policy periods:** one verified season, FY2026 heating: plan item 1.1 dates it November 15, 2025 to March 15, 2026 (page 4); LHC's final FFY2026 Plan Changes summary says December 15, 2025 to March 31, 2026 (page 1), in the program year October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026 (plan page 1). Louisiana variables are annual and read 1 January values, so period `2026` is FY2026: the HHS Louisiana four-person median of $98,137 (from `2025-10-01`) for the limit and the 2025 HHS guidelines (`fpg_year_lag` 1) for the federal floor. All 12 Louisiana parameter files hold one `2025-10-01` entry. `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2026"`. Earlier periods take the same Louisiana values by backfilling, with the federal median and guidelines of their own year (period `2025`: the $95,801 median, which reproduces all ten rows of Notice LHP-2024-01, and the 2024 guidelines): unverified estimates. Later periods carry the FY2026 Louisiana values forward (period `2027`: the FY2027 median of $100,636 and the 2026 guidelines): carried-forward estimates. Only a proposed FFY2027 plan exists (report status “Saved -- with Errors”); it keeps 60% of state median income and says “No Changes.” to the matrix, and the agency page as served on 2026-10-23 links no FFY2027 income notice. No user-approved estimate enters any amount.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/la/lhc/liheap/`: `la_liheap`, `la_liheap_household_size`, `la_liheap_energy_cost`; `eligibility/` `la_liheap_eligible`, `la_liheap_income_limit`; `income/` `la_liheap_countable_income`. No new input variable. The limit calls the shared `liheap_smi_limit` in `variables/gov/hhs/hhs_smi.py`; eligibility calls `fpg` in `variables/gov/hhs/tax_unit_fpg.py`.
- **Parameters:** 12 files under `gov.states.la.lhc.liheap`: `elderly_age` (60); `eligibility/` `smi_rate` (0.6), `fpg_year_lag` (1); `income/` `adult_age` (18), `sources/earned` (5 sources), `sources/unearned` (16 sources); `payment/` `amount` (4 burden bands by 2 size groups), `burden_band` (single-amount scale at 0, 0.10, 0.18 and 0.25), `size_group` (sizes 1-3 and 4 or more), `energy_cost_sources` (7 bills), `priority_supplement` (100), `young_child_max_age` (5). Federal parameters read: `gov.hhs.smi` (amount and size adjustments), `gov.hhs.fpg`, `gov.hhs.liheap.fpg_floor` (1.1).

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Monthly burden from annual amounts (simplification).** The guide divides one month's TEC (bills not more than 30 days old) by monthly income from the last 30 days of pay (4.1; 3.6 C.2). The branch divides annual bills by annual income, which equals the monthly ratio only when the application-month bills equal the annual average; winter heating bills usually exceed it. Pay-frequency conversion, unusual pay stubs and the rule that a recently terminated applicant has zero income (page 31) are not modeled. Plan 2.4 speaks of “The highest total energy cost (TEC)”; the guide adds every vendor's bill for one month, and the branch follows the guide.
2. **Band edges (inferred; settled).** The matrix prints “9.9% and Less”, “10% to 17.9%”, “18% to 24.9%” and “25% and Greater”, leaving gaps between 9.9% and 10%, 17.9% and 18%, and 24.9% and 25%; LHC publishes no rounding. The branch compares the unrounded burden with lower-inclusive cutoffs at 10%, 18% and 25%, which equals truncating the percentage to one decimal. A reading that rounds to one decimal would move a burden of 9.95% to 9.99% up a band; companion test 1 ($1,799 / $18,000 = 9.994%) depends on the branch reading.
3. **Zero income (source wording).** The guide and plan give zero-income households “the maximum benefit payment allowed for their family size”. The branch reads this as the top band ($650 or $700), plus the $100 supplement when a priority member is present, whatever the energy cost; income of zero after per-source floors counts as zero income.
4. **Heat in rent (settled).** Renters whose heating costs are in their rent are eligible (3.6 E.1; plan 2.3). The landlord states the unit's monthly heating cost on Appendix L, which has no model input, so the branch's burden counts only separately billed energy and the band is a lower bound; with no other bill the household gets the lowest band unless its income is zero. The landlord's rent reduction is not modeled.
5. **Fuels (coverage).** `heating_type` is a required input (settled). The matrix has no fuel column; the branch adds all seven bill inputs (4.1: “Any energy (or fuel) costs incurred to heat or cool a home”). NONE is not eligible. UNSPECIFIED pays $0 unless heat is in rent, the case where Louisiana pays without a fuel (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the default). SOLAR (read with the electric bill, plan 2.5 community solar), OTHER, wood, coal, fuel oil and kerosene are eligible like any fuel with a bill; the guide names natural gas, propane and electricity and does not address the others. Bill line items the guide includes or excludes (customer charge, franchise and infrastructure fees, tank rental, arrears, deposits, late fees) cannot be separated from the bill inputs, and the two editions disagree on four of them (Source text).
6. **Subsidized housing (simplification and readings).** Subsidized means `receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing`. `hud_utility_allowance` has no Louisiana schedule and is 0 unless supplied. The January 2024 edition compares the allowance with “the utility bill” and subtracts it from all vendors' costs; the April 2026 edition compares an allowance “for Heating or Cooling” with “the utility bill for that utility”; the branch subtracts the supplied allowance from all bills, and a code comment asks callers to supply only the heating or cooling allowance. An allowance equal to the bills (TEC 0) is read as no energy burden and ineligible, from “less that the Total Energy Costs” (3.6 E.1) and “must provide an energy bill to show an energy burden” (4.1 C.1); companion test 9(d) depends on this. The excess-utility-charge route has no separate input. The exemption reads “Applicants 60 years or older” in the guide and “Applicants over 60 years old” in plan 2.3; the branch follows the guide's 60 or older, and since no input names the applicant, any counted member of 60 or over exempts the household (settled). The April 2026 exclusion of Section 8 utility reimbursements from income has no input.
7. **Household and size (simplification).** The SPM unit stands in for the household. Size counts `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`, which approximates “a citizen of the United States, or a permanent legal resident who is eligible for federal benefits”. The January 2024 edition has no household definition; the April 2026 member exclusions (students away, foster placement, joint custody, live-in aides, incarceration, military duty, institutions) and the SSN requirement have no inputs. Undocumented members' income counts for the limit (D.3) and, by the branch's reading, in the burden denominator; the guide states it only for income eligibility.
8. **Priority supplement (settled).** Only counted members (citizens and qualified noncitizens) make the household a priority household, and only they exempt it from the utility allowance. `is_disabled` stands in for documented disability; “five years of age and younger” is read as under 6. One $100 per household.
9. **Income limit arithmetic (inferred rounding).** HHS states the order (60% of the four-person median, then the size percentage) but no rounding. Flooring after each step reproduces all ten Notice rows, the HHS sizes 11 and 12, and all ten FFY2025 rows of Notice LHP-2024-01 from $95,801. Sizes 13 and over extend the 3-point rule; neither Louisiana nor HHS prints them. The guide speaks of a “published monthly income limit”, but the Notice prints annual limits; the branch compares annual income with the annual limit.
10. **Federal floor (federal law).** 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B) bars excluding a household on income alone when its income is “less than 110 percent of the poverty level”. Louisiana's documents do not mention it. In FY2026 it first exceeds the 60% limit at size 14 ($95,865 against $91,855). The branch rounds 1.1 x guideline to cents and compares strictly; it registers no source conflict.
11. **Countable income (settled and readings).** Members 18 and over count (3.6 C.1). Social Security and SSI count for members of any age, from the Appendix E Social Security row (“benefits paid to minors”, SSI named in the row title) and FAQ A4; other income of minors does not (settled). Earnings of members 18 and over in high school do not count (`is_in_k12_school`). Social Security counts net of the computed `medicare_part_b_premium`, floored per person (settled). Every source is floored at zero separately and `rental_income` is assumed nonnegative (settled); net self-employment inputs get no further business-expense handling (the Appendix G depreciation rule is not applied). FITAP enters through the take-up-gated `tanf` of the SPM unit. Regular contributions are `financial_assistance`, which cannot separate regular from irregular gifts. “Insurance or annuity payments” are read through `pension_income`, which includes annuities and insurance contracts, and `disability_benefits` and `survivor_benefits` are counted. All interest counts; the Appendix E note “only if amount is over $200, and is withdrawn” is read as a proof rule. Royalties, jury duty pay, military family allotments, training stipends, informal income and KCSP have no input; `military_basic_pay` is not in the list, so military pay counts only as far as it is in `employment_income`. Child support received, capital gains, retirement-account withdrawals, tax refunds and SNAP are not counted.
12. **Plan and guide (manual followed).** Plan 1.9 checks one-time lump-sum payments and leaves commissions and cash gifts unchecked. The guide excludes “One – time cash payments” and “Lump sum inheritances”, counts only net gambling and lottery lump sums (Appendix E), counts commissions as earned income and counts regular contributions. The branch follows the guide (settled: manual over the plan checklist); it adds no `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml` entry, since no statute is on either side.
13. **Years, editions and dates (simplification).** All Louisiana parameters start `2025-10-01`; annual periods read 1 January values, so period 2026 applies FY2026 to the whole calendar year, including October to December 2026, which fall in FY2027. The heating window is November 15, 2025 to March 15, 2026 in plan 1.1 and December 15, 2025 to March 31, 2026 in the final Plan Changes summary; neither changes an annual amount. The January 2024 guide governed the FY2026 heating season and the April 2026 guide applies from April 1, 2026; for the rules encoded here they differ only in the TEC line items, the allowance comparison by utility type, the Section 8 reimbursement exclusion, the household-member definition and wording on room rental and rideshare self-employment. Earlier and later periods are estimates (see Policy periods).
14. **Other gaps.** One heating benefit per program year, credit balances from unused assistance (4.1 B), discretionary supplemental heating payments, first-come, first-served funding, application windows, active-account and SSN verification, and payment to the vendor or as a rent reduction are not modeled.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-la-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-la-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [us-la-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-la-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml) (agency model plan; matrix on page 60)
- [us-la-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-la-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml) (April 1, 2026 guide; no matrix)
- [us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml) (2024 and 2025 guidelines)
- [us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml) (2026 guidelines and the FY2027 SMI table, period 2027 estimate)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-la/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the FY2026 limits for sizes 1 to 10 and the inclusive limit, the extension above size 10 and the federal 110% floor, all four burden bands with their lower edges and both size groups, zero income, the $100 supplement for each priority group and once per household, undocumented members (income counted, size and supplement not), heat in rent, the fuel gates (NONE, UNSPECIFIED with and without heat in rent, solar and other fuels), the total energy cost across bills, the utility allowance with the age-60 exemption and the zero and negative TEC, the income of members under 18 and of high-school students, Social Security net of Medicare, SSI, FITAP, regular contributions, net gambling, every listed countable and excluded source, per-source loss floors, and any 2025 or 2027 period kept in scope. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Iowa LIHEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1c, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10292 (branch `ia-liheap-wave1c`), open for review, not merged. Head `cc2347fb3b` (2026-10-23), which adds the 2026-10-23 review fixes (commit `5108878aac`) and merges `main`; this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **Sources missing from the corpus.** No axiom-corpus manifest on `main` holds the branch's main source, the Iowa LIHEAP FY26 Policy and Procedures Manual effective October 1, 2025, with the Appendix I payment matrix. `us-ia-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml` holds the FY24 edition (expression date 2023-10-01), whose matrix and award amounts match FY26 but whose income table rests on the 2023 guidelines. Also missing: Program Notice 26-01 (the effective date), the LIHEAP Clearinghouse copy of Appendix I, the July 2025 public comment draft of the FFY2026 plan (page 48, the flat $800), the 2025 HHS poverty guidelines behind every FY26 limit and poverty-level band (`us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml` holds the 2026 ones), a dated capture of the agency page's FY26 income table (the live page now shows FY27), and Iowa Administrative Code 421 chapter 22, the LIHEAP rule in force during FY26, which incorporates the plan and manual by reference. These need ingest; the accepted FFY2026 plan is captured.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-20; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.
- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10292 is not approved: the 2026-10-21 review requested changes, and the fixes at head `cc2347fb3b` await re-review, so there is no revision to pin.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10292, branch `ia-liheap-wave1c`, head `cc2347fb3b` (2026-10-23), open for review; it closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10289. Commit `a5d1fea397` (2026-10-20) makes the fixed-income factor fail when any member has another recorded source, including child support received and FIP (new `income/sources/other_recorded.yaml`), treats railroad retirement as a fixed source and has kerosene follow fuel oil for the flat $800. Commits `8490f2e587` and `410a0a0241` read `total_unemployment_compensation` and count `military_retirement_income` as unearned and fixed income. Commit `5108878aac` (2026-10-23) counts Social Security net of `medicare_part_b_premium`, floors every unearned source at zero (in the countable amount and in the fixed-income test), and pays the flat $800 only to households that buy the deliverable fuel themselves. Everything below describes the code at the head; oracle fixtures will pin the merged commit.
- **Scope:** Iowa LIHEAP Regular Assistance, the once-a-year heating benefit, for FY26: Iowa residence, household size from citizenship or SSN documentation, gross countable income of members 18 and over (Social Security net of the Medicare Part B premium, each source floored at zero) less child support paid, the 200% income limit, the energy-burden condition (a bill for the heating fuel, heat in rent, subsidized housing), the heating fuel, the Appendix I matrix (poverty-level points, nine targeting factors, fuel points), $40 a point, the $80 minimum, the $800 maximum and the flat $800 for households that buy liquid propane or fuel oil themselves (kerosene included and the purchase condition, both by inference). Out of scope: ECIP crisis assistance (including heating equipment repair or replacement and emergency cooling), weatherization, Assurance 16 services, the automatically eligible verification waiver, funding availability and first-come first-served order, payment routing and the winter moratorium.
- **Policy periods:** one verified season, FY26: heating season October 1, 2025 to April 30, 2026 (plan item 1.1, page 4; manual Definitions, Heating Season, page 81) in the program year October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026 (Appendix B heading, page 89; Program Notice 26-01, effective October 1, 2025). Iowa variables are annual and read 1 January values, so period `2026` is FY26 on the 2025 HHS guidelines (`fpg_year_lag` 1); the printed limits equal exactly 2.0 times those guidelines. All 25 parameter files hold one `2025-10-01` entry. `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2026"`. Earlier periods take the same values by backfilling, on the lagged guideline (period `2025` on the 2024 guidelines): unverified estimates. Later periods carry the FY26 values forward on the lagged guideline (period `2027` on the 2026 guidelines): carried-forward estimates. The FY27 manual and Program Notice 27-01 (effective October 1, 2026) keep the FY26 matrix and award lines and set the limit at 200% of the 2026 guidelines, which period `2027` reproduces, but reword the fixed-income factor, a change a code comment notes as not modeled (interpretation 6).
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/ia/hhs/liheap/`: `ia_liheap`, `ia_liheap_household_size`, `ia_liheap_fuel_category` and the new input `ia_liheap_dwelling_type` (DETACHED, ATTACHED_2_TO_4_UNITS, ATTACHED_5_OR_MORE_UNITS; default DETACHED); `eligibility/` `ia_liheap_eligible`, `ia_liheap_fpg`, `ia_liheap_has_energy_burden`, `ia_liheap_income_eligible`, `ia_liheap_income_limit`; `income/` `ia_liheap_countable_earned_income` and `ia_liheap_countable_unearned_income` (person level), `ia_liheap_countable_income`, `ia_liheap_fixed_income_only`; `payment/` `ia_liheap_poverty_points`, `ia_liheap_targeting_points`, `ia_liheap_fuel_points`, `ia_liheap_points`.
- **Parameters:** 25 files under `gov.states.ia.hhs.liheap`: `eligibility/` `fpg_rate` (2), `fpg_year_lag` (1); `income/` `countable_min_age` (18), `sources/` `earned` (7 sources), `unearned` (15; the formula adds Social Security net of the premium, for 16 sources), `fixed` (6, with railroad and military retirement), `other_recorded` (`child_support_received`, `tanf`); `payment/` `amount_per_point` (40), `min_benefit` (80), `max_benefit` (800), `deliverable_fuel_amount` (800), `fuel_points` (by fuel category), `poverty_points` (single-amount scale on band tops, `right=True`, `-.inf` first threshold); `payment/targeting/` nine point values and `elderly_age` (60), `young_child_age` (6), `savings_threshold` (50,000). Plus a `programs.yaml` entry and a changelog fragment.
- **Tests:** 164 YAML cases in 16 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/ia/hhs/liheap/` at head `cc2347fb3b` (`ia_liheap.yaml` 17, `ia_liheap_fuel_category.yaml` 11, `ia_liheap_household_size.yaml` 5, `integration.yaml` 8, `eligibility/ia_liheap_eligible.yaml` 12, `eligibility/ia_liheap_fpg.yaml` 4, `eligibility/ia_liheap_has_energy_burden.yaml` 9, `eligibility/ia_liheap_income_eligible.yaml` 6, `eligibility/ia_liheap_income_limit.yaml` 5, `income/ia_liheap_countable_earned_income.yaml` 7, `income/ia_liheap_countable_income.yaml` 9, `income/ia_liheap_countable_unearned_income.yaml` 12, `income/ia_liheap_fixed_income_only.yaml` 19, `payment/ia_liheap_fuel_points.yaml` 10, `payment/ia_liheap_poverty_points.yaml` 11, `payment/ia_liheap_targeting_points.yaml` 19). Since `189af398b8`, the branch adds 11 cases: countable unearned Cases 10-12, fixed income Cases 16-19, `ia_liheap.yaml` Cases 16 and 17, countable earned Case 7 and countable income Case 9. Countable unearned Case 1 now expects $21,565.20 (Social Security net of a $2,434.80 premium). Every case sends `heating_type`. All 164 cases pass locally (2026-10-23).

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence on axiom-corpus `main` (`e019e44563`, 2026-10-19) was checked on 2026-10-20 against the full manifest list and by GitHub code search of `manifests/` for each source URL; the signed release was not checked. rulespec-us `main` (`874bce4fea`, 2026-10-19) has `us-ia/policies/` (cms and income_tax), `us-ia/regulations/iac/441/41` and `us-ia/statutes/422`, but no HHS, LIHEAP or Iowa Administrative Code 421 module and no `us/` poverty-guideline module; the paths below follow that layout. Pages are physical PDF pages; in the FY26 manual they equal the printed page numbers.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-ia/policies/hhs/liheap-policy-and-procedures-manual/fy2026/section-4/applications` | 4.20 once per program year (page 13); 4.40 items 3a and 4, a minor's Social Security as a fixed source and savings (page 14) | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. Official copy, for every FY26 manual row: [FY26 LIHEAP Policy and Procedures Manual, pages 1, 13-14, 18-22, 24-26, 31, 34, 42, 46-47, 79-82, 84-85, 89-90, 92, 94, 96-99, 102-103, 108-115, 117-119, 121-123 and 137](https://hhs.iowa.gov/media/17262/download?inline#page=1) (139 pages). |
| `.../fy2026/section-5/eligibility-requirements` | 5.10 income 200% or below (page 18); 5.30 residence and household membership (pages 18-19); 5.41 and 5.42 eligible and ineligible dwellings, heat in rent, subsidized housing (pages 20-21); 5.50 energy burden (page 22) | none | Same file. |
| `.../fy2026/section-6/income` | 6.00 under-18 sentence (page 24); 6.10 qualification periods and the SSA-1099 (pages 24-25); 6.20 gross income of members 18 and over, 30-day annualization (page 26) | none | Same file. |
| `.../fy2026/section-7/ssn-documentation` | 7.00 citizenship verification for household size (page 31); 7.30 ineligible members, income still counted (page 34) | none | Same file. |
| `.../fy2026/section-11/payments` | 11.00 benefit factors, matrix points, deliverable fuel raised to the state-set amount (page 42); 12.00 and 12.20 fuels supplied by vendors (pages 46-47) | none | Same file. |
| `.../fy2026/section-20/definitions` | Attached household (page 79); Detached household, Disabled, Elderly (page 80); FIP, Fixed Income Household, Heating Season (page 81); Household/Customer (page 82); Primary Heating Fuel Type and Subsidized Housing (pages 84-85); Young Child (page 85) | none | Same file. |
| `.../fy2026/appendix-b/poverty-guidelines` | FY26 Annual Gross Income table, sizes 1 to 8 and $11,000 for each additional member (page 89) | none | Same file. The [agency LIHEAP page](https://hhs.iowa.gov/programs/programs-and-services/liheap) printed the same table on 2026-10-04 and shows FY27 on 2026-10-20; a dated FY26 capture needs ingest. |
| `.../fy2026/appendix-c/income-source-guide` | Code key (page 90) and the counted and not-counted rows the branch uses (pages 90-121, listed under Source text) | none | Same file. |
| `.../fy2026/appendix-d/energy-burden-table` | Thirteen heat and electric situations with Yes or No energy burden and the type of payment (pages 122-123) | none | Same file. |
| `.../fy2026/appendix-i/benefit-maximums` | Regular Assistance Payment Matrix for FY26 and the award calculation (page 137) | none | Same file. The [Clearinghouse copy, IA_BenefitMatrix_Heat-Crisis_2026.pdf, page 1](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/benefits-matricies/IA_BenefitMatrix_Heat-Crisis_2026.pdf#page=1) (2 pages, modified 2025-12-10) prints the same text; in no manifest. |
| `us-ia/policies/hhs/liheap-policy-and-procedures-manual/fy2024/payment-matrix` | FY24 edition: the same matrix points and award amounts (PDF page 32, printed 26); limits $29,160 plus $10,280 for each additional member, 2.0 times the 2023 guidelines (Appendix A, PDF page 68) | `us-ia/manual/hhs/liheap-policy-and-procedures-manual` | In manifest `us-ia-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml` (114 pages, expression date 2023-10-01): no FY26 value. Its `benefit_matrix_pdf_pages: 22-23` are income pages (6.30 to 6.60); the matrix is on PDF page 32. Official copy: [FY24 LIHEAP Policy and Procedures Manual, pages 32 and 68](https://hhs.iowa.gov/media/2702/download?inline=#page=32). |
| `us-ia/policies/hhs/liheap-program-notice/26-01` | Effective date October 1, 2025; the FY26 change list updates the Appendix A and B income tables and lists no change to Appendix I (pages 1-3) | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. [Program Notice 26-01, pages 1-3](https://hhs.iowa.gov/media/17263/download?inline#page=1). |
| `us-ia/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-1` | Report period and status (page 1); 1.1 heating dates (page 4); 1.4 to 1.7a no categorical eligibility, automatic enrollment or SNAP nominal payment; 1.8 gross income; 1.9 countable-income boxes (pages 5-6) | `us-ia/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | In manifest `us-ia-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml` (the Clearinghouse file the branch cites, expression date 2025-10-01). Official copy: [FFY2026 Detailed Model Plan, pages 1, 4-6 and 8-9](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/state-plans/IA_Plan_2026.pdf#page=1). Check boxes and radio buttons read from 300 DPI renders of pages 5, 6, 8 and 9. |
| `us-ia/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-2` | 2.1 the printed 150.00% and the 200% note (pages 8-9); 2.2 no additional requirements; 2.3 no assets test, subsidized housing and utilities-in-rent policies (page 8); 2.4 matrix favors elderly, disabled and young children; 2.5 benefit variables; 2.6 $80 and $800 (page 9) | `us-ia/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | Same manifest. |
| `us-ia/policies/hhs/liheap-state-plan/ffy2026-public-comment-draft/payment-matrix` | The flat $800 for liquid propane and fuel oil (page 48, a manual page footed with an effective date of 10/01/24) | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. [FFY2026 plan, public comment draft of July 21, 2025, pages 1 and 48](https://hhs.iowa.gov/media/16690/download?inline#page=1); a hearing draft, not the accepted plan. |
| `us-ia/regulations/iac/421/22` | 22.2(1) income ceiling; 22.2(3) and 22.2(5) criteria and matrix in the plan and manual (page 1); 22.11 plan and manual incorporated by reference (page 3) | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest; not cited by the branch. [Iowa Administrative Code 421 chapter 22, as of July 23, 2025 (IAC 2/5/25), pages 1 and 3](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/iac/chapter/07-23-2025.421.22.pdf#page=1); rescinded effective October 1, 2026 by ARC 0495D ([IAC 421 chapter listing, IAC 8/19/26, page 2](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/iac/chapter/421.22.pdf#page=2)). |
| `us/` poverty guidelines module | 2025 guidelines for the 48 contiguous states ($15,650 for one person, $5,500 for each additional person) behind every FY26 limit and poverty-level band | `us/guidance/hhs/aspe/poverty-guidelines/2026/federal-register` (2026 only) | `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml` holds the 2026 guidelines (91 FR 1797), read by the period 2027 estimate; `us-hhs-poverty-guidelines.yaml` was never extracted. The 2025 guidelines need ingest: [FR Doc. 2025-01377 (90 FR 5917), page 1](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-17/pdf/2025-01377.pdf#page=1). The 2024 guidelines (period 2025 estimate) are in no manifest. |

FY27 documents, needed only if period 2027 is kept in scope, are in no manifest: [FY27 LIHEAP Policy and Procedures Manual, pages 89, 97 and 147](https://hhs.iowa.gov/media/19560/download?inline#page=89) (151 pages) and [Program Notice 27-01, pages 1 and 7](https://hhs.iowa.gov/media/19559/download?inline#page=1).

## Source text (verbatim)

Quotations come from the official files above (pdftotext, line breaks collapsed); plan check-box and radio states come from 300 DPI renders of plan pages 5, 6, 8 and 9.

**Program and dates.** Program Notice 26-01, page 1: “Effective Date: October 1, 2025”. Plan page 1: “Report Period: 10/01/2025 to 09/30/2026” and “Report Status: Submission Accepted by CO”; page 4, item 1.1: “Heating assistance” from “10/01/2025” to “04/30/2026”. Manual page 81, Definitions: “The Heating Season, in regard to the LIHEAP program, refers to the period of October 1 – April 30 and represents the timeframe in which applications for LIHEAP Regular Assistance benefits are accepted.” Page 13, section 4.20: “Households can only receive LIHEAP Regular Assistance once per program year unless the state decides to allow for supplemental payments due to increased funding levels for a particular year.”

**Household and members.** Manual page 82: “A household includes all the people who occupy a housing unit (such as a house or apartment) as their usual place of residence.” and “The key is: One Meter + One Bill = One Household”. Page 31, section 7.00: “Each household member listed on a LIHEAP application must verify their United States citizenship to be counted towards the total size of the household.” Page 34, section 7.30: “When a LIHEAP customer household contains a foreign national without the required documents or refuses to provide required documentation for that household member, that member becomes ineligible. Any household containing an ineligible member may apply as long as the ineligible member is not counted as an application participant (i.e., If there are two adults and one child and one of the adults is ineligible, the number of application participants is two). However, the ineligible member's income must be counted and documented for household eligibility determination.” Also: “A household comprised entirely of ineligible members is ineligible to receive LIHEAP.” Page 19, section 5.30, also lets two households claim the same children and excludes college students living away and incarcerated individuals.

**Residence, categorical eligibility and assets.** Page 18, section 5.30: “Anyone applying for LIHEAP Regular Assistance or ECIP Crisis Assistance must be living in Iowa, in their primary residence that has a legitimate address, and has an energy burden (see Appendix D).” Plan page 5: items 1.4 (categorical eligibility), 1.5 (automatic enrollment) and 1.7a (SNAP nominal payments) answered No. Plan page 8: item 2.2 (additional eligibility requirements) No; “Do you require an Assets test?” No.

**Income limit.** Page 18, section 5.10: “Financial eligibility is tied to the income of the household being 200% or below of the Office of Management and Budget’s federal poverty guidelines (FPG), revisions of which are published annually in the Federal Register (see Appendix B).” Page 89, Appendix B: “FY26 October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026.”, “Annual Gross Income” for sizes 1 to 8: “$31,300”, “$42,300”, “$53,300”, “$64,300”, “$75,300”, “$86,300”, “$97,300”, “$108,300”; “* Add $11,000 for each additional member.” and “** All income will be collected for a 30-day period and annualized”. Plan page 8, item 2.1: all household sizes, HHS Poverty Guidelines, “150.00%”. Plan page 9: “NOTE: Section 2.1 - Iowa's eligibility threshold is 200% FPG ($31,300 for a household of 1), which matches Iowa's Weatherization Assistance Program and is less than 60% of Iowa's SMI ($36,756 for a household of 1).” and “However, the OLDC report will not allow me to indicate 200% FPG without causing an error, so it had to be entered as 150%.” Agency page as served 2026-10-04: “The total household income for an applicant must be at or below 200% of the 2025 federal poverty guidelines. These guidelines are for October 1, 2025 - September 30, 2026.” 90 FR 5917, page 1: “2025 POVERTY GUIDELINES FOR THE 48 CONTIGUOUS STATES AND THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA”, size 1 “$15,650”, and “For families/households with more than 8 persons, add $5,500 for each additional person.” Iowa Administrative Code 421—22.2(1), page 1: “Households with incomes at or below the annually determined federal poverty guidelines, but not to exceed 150 percent of the guidelines, or an amount equal to 60 percent of the state median income for the state, according to DHHS, which are published annually in the Federal Register, may be eligible for assistance under LIHEAP.” 22.11, page 3: “The Iowa LIHEAP State Plan, the Iowa LIHEAP Policy and Procedures Manual, and assistance award criteria for the program are incorporated by reference as part of these rules.” The IAC 8/19/26 listing, page 2, marks chapter 22 “Rescinded ARC 0495D, IAB 8/19/26, effective 10/1/26”.

**Countable income.** Plan page 5, item 1.8: “Gross Income” checked. Manual page 24, section 6.00: “All income of individuals under age 18 is exempt from countable income, unless working full-time or the individual is emancipated and applying as head of household (see Section 5.30).” Section 6.10: “For purposes of qualifying for Energy Assistance, a LIHEAP customer may elect to use the most recent 30 calendar days, the most recent 12 months, or the most recent calendar year as a qualification period.” Page 26, section 6.20: “The gross income of all household members aged 18 and over residing in the household at the time of application shall be counted to determine eligibility.” and “When electing to use the most recent 30-day income period, income will be annualized”.

Appendix C, Income Source Guide (pages 90 to 121), the rows the branch uses. Code key, page 90: “B = Retirement Income (SSA retirement benefits, pensions, railroad retirement, etc.)”. Counted:

- Employment Income (page 97): “Wages, Salaries, Commissions, Tips, Vacation Pay, Overtime Pay, Paid Time Off (PTO), Sick Leave, Bonuses*, Profit Sharing*, Severance Pay*, Per Diem.” and “Earned income is not considered a fixed income source.”
- Military Pay (page 108): “Housing allowance is not considered income.”
- Self-Employment Income (page 113): “Income from a business, less business expenses.” Notes: “Filed Federal tax return required if deducting business expense, otherwise gross income is used. The LIHEAP program does NOT deduct business expenses.”
- Farm Income (page 98), X in the Yes column with code NA: “Proceeds from sale of crops, livestock or products” and “Proceeds from land rental”.
- Social Security Benefits (SSA, SSI, SSDI) (page 114): “*Only count for HH members 18 and older” and “If only source of HH income is SS benefits for member(s) under 18, record payment to capture source of income for AE fixed income criteria, but put amount received as $0.00”. Notes: “Count the net amount as income (gross minus benefits repaid to SSA (Box 4 of 1099 only).” and “If only a 1040 is provided and the amount on line 6a would cause the household to be over income for eligibility, agencies can request the SSA 1099 from the customer and utilize the “paid by check or direct deposit” as show on the SSA 1099.” Definition column: “Q: If a LIHEAP customer receives social security and is being reimbursed for Medicare Part B that was previously deducted, only count the amount received that applies to the verification period.”
- Medicare deduction, section 6.10 (page 25): “In the event that only a 1040 is provided and the amount in line 6a would cause the household to be over income for eligibility, agencies can request the SSA 1099 from the customer and utilize the “paid by check or direct deposit” as shown on the SSA 1099.” Plan item 1.9 (page 6) checks “Excluding MediCare deduction” beside “Social Security Administration (SSA ) benefits” (see below).
- Pensions (page 109): “Assistance, paid at regular intervals to a person or to the person’s surviving dependents in consideration of past services, age, merit, poverty, injury or loss sustained, etc.” IRA (page 103) and Retirement Income (page 111): “Note: An irregular withdrawal is not counted as income (withdrawals from savings or assets are excluded as income).”
- Railroad Retirement (page 110): box 5 of the RRB-1099 and box 7 of the RRB-1099-R, “Annuities or Pensions by the Railroad Retirement Board”, count as income.
- Unemployment Compensation (page 117): “Unemployment benefits are counted incomes.” Strike Benefits (page 115) and Workers’ Compensation (page 121).

**Targeting definitions.** Page 81, Fixed Income Household: “A household that receives only one or more of the following income types, and income may include: Social Security Administration (SSA) Benefits, Supplemental Security Income (SSI), Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI), Veterans’ Assistance, VA Service-Connected Disability Pension, VA Non-Service-Connected Disability Pension, and pensions.” It ends: “when that is the ONLY source(s) of income.” Page 14, section 4.40, item 3a: “Though no longer counted towards household income amounts, social security payments received by household members under age 18 can still qualify the household as AE eligible when that is the only source of income for the household.” Item 4: “Interest and dividend-bearing accounts (this includes high-interest bank accounts, cash on hand, CDs, and other investments that can be accessed without penalty to the household) are $50,000 or less.” Page 112, Savings: “Note – only count if Savings are over $50,000 as indicated on the LIHEAP application”.
