| Output | policyengine-us variable | Entity, period | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Household size | `ia_liheap_household_size` | SPM unit, year | Number of members with `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`; 0 outside Iowa. |
| Poverty guideline | `ia_liheap_fpg` | SPM unit, year | The HHS guideline of the year before the period for the household size and state group: in period 2026, $15,650 + $5,500 x (size - 1); 0 when size is 0. |
| Income limit | `ia_liheap_income_limit` | SPM unit, year | 2.0 x guideline, unrounded: $31,300 + $11,000 x (size - 1) in period 2026. |
| Countable earned income | `ia_liheap_countable_earned_income` | Person, year | For members aged 18 or over, the sum of `employment_income`, `military_basic_pay`, `self_employment_income`, `sstb_self_employment_income`, `partnership_s_corp_income`, `farm_operations_income` and `farm_rent_income`, each floored at zero; 0 under 18. |
| Countable unearned income | `ia_liheap_countable_unearned_income` | Person, year | For members aged 18 or over, max(`social_security` - `medicare_part_b_premium`, 0) plus `ssi` (twelve monthly amounts), `pension_income`, `military_retirement_income`, `retirement_distributions`, `railroad_benefits`, `total_unemployment_compensation`, `workers_compensation`, `strike_benefits`, `disability_benefits`, `veterans_benefits`, `alimony_income`, `rental_income`, `interest_income`, `ordinary_dividend_income` and `gambling_winnings`, each floored at zero per source, so a rental loss offsets nothing; 0 under 18. The premium is the person's own out-of-pocket Part B premium: 0 if not enrolled and net of Medicare Savings Program coverage. |
| Countable income | `ia_liheap_countable_income` | SPM unit, year | max(earned + unearned over all members, counted in size or not, minus the members' `child_support_expense`, 0). |
| Income eligible | `ia_liheap_income_eligible` | SPM unit, year | Countable income <= limit. |
| Energy burden | `ia_liheap_has_energy_burden` | SPM unit, year | `has_heating_expense` (a positive bill for the named fuel, heat not in rent); or `heat_expense_included_in_rent` and either unsubsidized or `pre_subsidy_electricity_expense` > 0. Subsidized means `receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing`. |
| Eligible | `ia_liheap_eligible` | SPM unit, year | Iowa; size > 0; income eligible; energy burden; `heating_type` not UNSPECIFIED, NONE or SOLAR. |
| Poverty points | `ia_liheap_poverty_points` | SPM unit, year | r = countable income / guideline: 8 if r <= 0.75, 6 if r <= 1.00, 5 if r <= 1.25, 4 if r <= 2.00, otherwise 0; 0 when the guideline is 0. |
| Fixed income only | `ia_liheap_fixed_income_only` | SPM unit, year | F = sum over all members, any age, of `social_security` (gross; the premium does not apply), `ssi`, `pension_income`, `military_retirement_income`, `railroad_benefits` and `veterans_benefits`; O = the members' earned sources and other unearned sources, each floored at zero per source, plus `child_support_received` and `tanf`; true when F > 0 and O = 0. |
| Targeting points | `ia_liheap_targeting_points` | SPM unit, year | +1 fixed income only; +1 a member aged 60 or over; +1 a member with `is_disabled`; +1 a member under 6; +1 DETACHED; -1 ATTACHED_5_OR_MORE_UNITS; -2 subsidized; -4 heat in rent; -4 `spm_unit_cash_assets` over $50,000. Each factor at most once. |
| Fuel category and points | `ia_liheap_fuel_category`, `ia_liheap_fuel_points` | SPM unit, year | NATURAL_GAS 4; ELECTRICITY 4; PROPANE 5; FUEL_OIL (FUEL_OIL and KEROSENE) 5; SOLID_FUEL (WOOD and COAL) 2; OTHER (every other `heating_type`) 0. |
| Total points | `ia_liheap_points` | SPM unit, year | Poverty + targeting + fuel points; may be zero or negative. |
| Benefit | `ia_liheap` | SPM unit, year | If eligible: $800 for fuel category PROPANE or FUEL_OIL (which includes KEROSENE) when `heat_expense_included_in_rent` is false; otherwise, including a household with heat in its rent in a propane or oil-heated building, min(max($40 x points, $80), $800). $0 if not eligible. |

Inputs: `state_code`, `age`, `immigration_status`, `is_disabled`; the earned sources above and the unearned sources above (`social_security` or its components; `ssi` is monthly; `military_retirement_pay` and `military_retirement_pay_survivors` through `military_retirement_income`; `unemployment_compensation` through `total_unemployment_compensation`); `medicare_part_b_premium`; `child_support_expense`; `child_support_received` and `tanf` (recorded, not counted); `heating_type` sent explicitly with the matching bill (`gas_expense`, `pre_subsidy_electricity_expense` for ELECTRICITY and SOLAR, `bottled_gas_expense`, `fuel_oil_expense` for FUEL_OIL and KEROSENE, `wood_expense`, `coal_expense`, `other_heating_fuel_expense`); `heat_expense_included_in_rent`, `receives_housing_assistance`, `is_in_public_housing`, `pre_subsidy_electricity_expense` (the electric account for heat in subsidized rent), `spm_unit_cash_assets` and `ia_liheap_dwelling_type`.

(e) age 66: Social Security $16,000 and taxable IRA distributions $3,000; age 67: Social Security $18,000, pension $6,000 and `medicare_part_b_premium` $2,434.80 (12 x $202.90, the 2026 standard premium). (f) age 52: wages $20,000, self-employment -$5,000, farm operations -$3,000, farm rent $2,000. (g) age 62: self-employment -$12,000 and Social Security $18,000. (h) age 31: military basic pay $28,000, partnership $4,000, SSTB self-employment $3,000 | Appendix C rows. (a) All count (interpretation 8). (b) Neither counts. (c) All count. (d) Railroad retirement counts; $35,000 exceeds $31,300. (e) The IRA distribution counts once; Social Security counts net of the premium (interpretation 5): 18,000 - 2,434.80 + 6,000. (f), (g) Losses offset nothing (page 113). (h) Military pay less housing allowance. | (a) $28,000; (b) $0; (c) $24,500; (d) $24,000, then not eligible; (e) $19,000, $21,565.20; (f) $22,000; (g) $18,000; (h) $35,000 | pp. 25, 90-121; plan p. 6 |
| 12 | Largest matrix totals and one point per factor (`integration.yaml` Case 7; `ia_liheap.yaml` Case 7; `payment/ia_liheap_targeting_points.yaml` Case 15; the natural gas award added here) | (a) age 68, `is_disabled`, Social Security $15,000; grandchild 4; KEROSENE, `fuel_oil_expense` $1,600; then the same with NATURAL_GAS. (b) ages 67 and 66, both disabled, Social Security $18,000 and $14,000; children 3 and 5; NATURAL_GAS | (a) Size 2: 15,000 / 21,150 = 70.9%, rounded up to 71%: 8. Fixed income only, elderly, disabled, child under 6 and detached: +5. Kerosene takes the fuel oil 5 (interpretation 9): 18 x $40 = $720, raised to the flat $800. With natural gas: 17 x $40 = $680. (b) Each factor once (interpretation 12): 5. | (a) 18 points, $800; natural gas 17 points, $680; (b) targeting 5 | pp. 80-81, 85, 89, 137 |
| 13 | Targeting thresholds (`payment/ia_liheap_targeting_points.yaml` Cases 1-13) | one adult aged 40, wages $30,000, NATURAL_GAS, ATTACHED_2_TO_4_UNITS; then DETACHED; age 60; age 59; `is_disabled` (age 45, wages $26,000, electric); an adult 30 with a child aged 5, then 6; ATTACHED_5_OR_MORE_UNITS; Section 8; public housing; heat in unsubsidized rent; savings $50,000; savings $50,001 | Two to four units score neither dwelling point. Detached +1; 60 or older +1, 59 none; disabled +1; under six +1, 6 none; five or more units -1; subsidized -2 (Section 8 and public housing, pages 84-85); heat in rent -4; only savings over $50,000 score: $50,000 none, $50,001 -4. | 0; 1; 1; 0; 1; 1; 0; -1; -2; -2; -4; 0; -4 | pp. 79-80, 84-85, 112, 137 |
| 14 | Farm couple heating with propane, savings over $50,000 (`integration.yaml` Case 3; `payment/ia_liheap_targeting_points.yaml` Case 19) | ages 55 (farm operations $22,000) and 53 (farm rent $6,000); PROPANE, `bottled_gas_expense` $2,400; `spm_unit_cash_assets` $60,000 | Farm income counts (page 98); no assets test (plan 2.3). 28,000 / 21,150 = 132.4%, rounded up to 133%: 4; detached +1, savings -4: -3; liquid propane 5; 6 x $40 = $240, raised to the flat $800. | income $28,000, limit $42,300, 6 points, $800 | pp. 42, 98, 112, 137; plan p. 8 |
| 15 | Medicare Part B premium (`ia_liheap.yaml` Case 16; `income/ia_liheap_countable_unearned_income.yaml` Case 11) | (a) age 66, `social_security` $33,000, `medicare_part_b_premium` $2,434.80 (12 x $202.90; $2,750 a month is above the Medicare Savings Program limits); NATURAL_GAS, `gas_expense` $1,200. (b) age 67, `social_security` $2,000, `pension_income` $24,000, `medicare_part_b_premium` $2,434.80 | (a) Plan item 1.9 counts SSA benefits “Excluding MediCare deduction”, and 6.10 uses the amount “paid by check or direct deposit” when the 1040 amount would put the household over income: 33,000 - 2,434.80 = 30,565.20, at or below 31,300 (gross, 33,000 is over income). 30,565.20 / 15,650 = 195.31%, rounded up to 196%: “126 – 200%” = 4. Fixed income only, elderly (66) and detached: 3. Natural gas 4. 11 x $40 = $440. (b) The deduction applies to the SSA benefit only, and the amount paid cannot fall below zero (interpretation 5): max(2,000 - 2,434.80, 0) + 24,000. | (a) income $30,565.20, income eligible, fixed income only true, points 4 + 3 + 4 = 11, $440; (b) $24,000 | pp. 25, 80-81, 89, 114, 137; plan p. 6 |
| 16 | Per-source loss floors (`income/ia_liheap_countable_income.yaml` Case 9; `income/ia_liheap_countable_unearned_income.yaml` Case 12; `income/ia_liheap_fixed_income_only.yaml` Case 18) | (a) age 40, wages $34,000, `rental_income` -$6,000; NATURAL_GAS. (b) age 62, pension $18,000, `rental_income` -$4,000. (c) age 67, Social Security $18,000, `rental_income` -$500, interest $500 | Rental income is “Income received from rental properties” (page 110), and 6.20 and plan item 1.8 count gross income, so a loss counts as 0 and offsets no other source (interpretation 7). (a) max(-6,000, 0) = 0; 34,000 exceeds 31,300 (netting would give 28,000: 4 + 1 + 4 = 9 points, $360). (b) 18,000 + 0 (a signed sum, or a floor on the total, gives 14,000). (c) Other sources 0 + 500 > 0, so not fixed income only (a signed sum gives 0). | (a) unearned $0, income $34,000, not income eligible, $0; (b) $18,000; (c) false | pp. 26, 81, 103, 110; plan p. 5 |
| 17 | Self-employment profit (`income/ia_liheap_countable_earned_income.yaml` Case 7; `income/ia_liheap_fixed_income_only.yaml` Case 19) | (a) age 45, wages $26,000, `self_employment_income` $4,000. (b) age 67, Social Security $18,000, `self_employment_income` $3,000 | Self-employment income counts (page 113). (a) 26,000 + 4,000. (b) Earned income “is not considered a fixed income source” (page 97), so the household is not fixed income only. | (a) $30,000; (b) false | pp. 81, 97, 113 |
| 18 | Military retirement (`income/ia_liheap_countable_unearned_income.yaml` Case 10; `income/ia_liheap_fixed_income_only.yaml` Cases 16 and 17) | (a) age 48, `military_retirement_pay` $26,400 ($2,200 a month). (b) age 60, `military_retirement_pay_survivors` $14,400 (a Survivor Benefit Plan annuity of $1,200 a month); ELECTRICITY, `pre_subsidy_electricity_expense` $1,400 | Pensions are “paid at regular intervals to a person or to the person’s surviving dependents in consideration of past services” (page 109), so retirement pay and the survivor annuity count (pages 109, 111) and are fixed sources (page 81). Each is the only source. | (a) unearned $26,400, income $26,400, fixed income only true; (b) income $14,400, fixed income only true | pp. 81, 109, 111 |
| 19 | Heat in rent in a propane-heated building (`ia_liheap.yaml` Case 17) | age 40, wages $28,000; PROPANE, `bottled_gas_expense` $0, heat in unsubsidized rent, ATTACHED_2_TO_4_UNITS | Unsubsidized heat in rent is an energy burden (5.41; Appendix D). 28,000 / 15,650 = 178.9%, rounded up to 179%: 4. Heat in rent -4, two to four units 0: -4. Liquid propane 5. 5 x $40 = $200. The tenant buys no fuel, so the flat $800 does not apply (interpretation 10). | energy burden true, fuel category PROPANE, targeting -4, 5 points, $200 ($800 under the other reading) | pp. 20, 42, 122, 137; draft plan p. 48 |

No branch test disagrees with these derivations. Tests 3 (the $11,738 case), 4 (kerosene, OTHER), 5, 8, 9, 11(a), 12, 15, 16 and 19 depend on interpretations 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 12.

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Poverty-level rounding and guideline (inferred).** Appendix I prints whole-percent bands with the note “*Note: Poverty levels of .01% are rounded up to the next percentage” and names no guideline. The branch divides annual countable income by the same lagged guideline as the limit (Appendix B is the manual's only table) and puts any excess over a band top in the next band. A reading that first rounds the percentage to two decimals would keep $11,738 for one person (75.003%) at 75% and 8 points; companion test 3's $11,738 case depends on the branch reading, its other cases do not.
2. **Annual income (simplification).** Iowa annualizes the 30-day, 12-month or calendar-year period the household elects (6.10, 6.20); Appendix I says “30-day, 60-day, or 12-month”. The branch uses annual amounts, which equal the calendar-year election. The 30-day look-ahead after a layoff (pages 24-25) and the limited-duration rule for unemployment (pages 79 and 117) are not modeled.
3. **Household and size (simplification).** The SPM unit stands in for the housing unit. Size counts `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`, which approximates Iowa's documentary test (SSN, I-94 or approved alternatives, one-time waivers). Members who refuse documentation, children claimed by two households, students away, incarcerated members, live-in caregivers, roomers and group-home bill shares are not identified.
4. **Members under 18 (settled).** All income of members under 18 is excluded, following 6.20, Appendix C (page 102 and the Social Security row, page 114) and plan item 1.9 (box unchecked). Section 6.00 (page 24) exempts under-18 income “unless working full-time or the individual is emancipated and applying as head of household”; that sentence conflicts and is recorded in branch comments. Emancipated minors applying as head of household are not identified. Companion test 8 rests on this decision.
5. **Social Security net of the Medicare Part B premium (settled).** Plan item 1.9 checks “Excluding MediCare deduction”; Appendix C counts the net amount after repayments, and section 6.10 and Appendix C use the amount “paid by check or direct deposit” when the 1040 amount would put the household over income. The branch counts each member's max(`social_security` - `medicare_part_b_premium`, 0). The premium is the out-of-pocket Part B amount: 0 for a person not enrolled and net of Medicare Savings Program coverage, which is not withheld from the check. A premium larger than the benefit does not reduce other income (companion test 15(b)). SSA repayments and Part D premiums have no input. The fixed-income factor keys on whether Social Security is present, so the premium does not change it.
6. **Fixed income only (encoded readings).** The factor is true only when a fixed source is present and no member, at any age, has another recorded source: the branch's earned and other unearned sources (each floored at zero), plus child support received and FIP (read through `tanf`), which Iowa does not count but calls not fixed (pages 92, 98). Railroad retirement and military retirement and survivor pay are pensions for the factor (Appendix C pages 109-110). Two readings of the FY26 wording “Fixed Income Only (no other sources of income)” remain: (a) non-countable receipts such as child support received and FIP defeat the factor (companion test 5: $480, or $520 with the point); (b) a working minor's wages, which are not countable, defeat it (`income/ia_liheap_fixed_income_only.yaml` Case 8), while a minor's Social Security identifies a fixed source (page 114; 4.40 item 3a). The FY27 manual and Program Notice 27-01 (effective October 1, 2026) reword the factor to “no other countable sources of income”; a code comment notes this as not modeled, since only FY26 is verified. Interest defeats the factor because all interest is counted (interpretation 8); receipts with no model input, such as gifts, cannot.
7. **Self-employment, farm income and losses (simplification).** Appendix C (page 113) uses the tax return for filers and gross income otherwise. The branch uses the model's net self-employment, partnership and farm inputs, each floored at zero (the filer route; a loss offsets nothing); the non-filer gross route is not represented. Farm rent counts as earned farm income (page 98). Unearned sources are floored the same way: Rental Income is “Income received from rental properties” (page 110), so a rental loss offsets nothing, and the fixed-income test floors each other source before checking for one (companion test 16).
8. **Income items without a matching input (simplification).** All `interest_income` counts, although Appendix C excludes bank-account interest (page 103); dividends count in full, without the $120 rule (page 96); `retirement_distributions` includes irregular withdrawals (page 111), `disability_benefits` short-term benefits (page 94) and `veterans_benefits` VA education and housing allowances (page 119), all excluded by Iowa. Royalties, trusts, tribal per capita payments, lump sums, cryptocurrency, legal settlements, work study and caregiver pay have no input. The Social Security row (page 114) also names “SSA (State Supplementary Assistance) - Fully state-funded”; the model has no Iowa state supplement at this head, so none is counted. Companion test 11(a) reads its $300 of interest as bond or investment interest; its $500 of dividends is over $120.
9. **Fuels (coverage limit and inference).** `heating_type` is a required input (settled). As a model input rule, not an Iowa rule, the branch treats UNSPECIFIED as ineligible, including when heat is in the rent, because the fuel row cannot be scored without a fuel (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the default). NONE is no heat, and SOLAR follows the Appendix D row for electricity from solar cells, wind power, an extension cord or a generator (no energy burden). Appendix I publishes points for natural gas, electric, liquid propane, fuel oil and solid fuel (wood, coal, corn). Kerosene follows fuel oil for both the 5 fuel points and the flat $800, by inference: the fuel row and the award rule use the same term, “Fuel Oil”; the draft plan (page 48) ties the flat amount to deliverable fuel customers lacking moratorium protection; and 12.20 (page 47) lists kerosene as a deliverable fuel. OTHER is eligible with 0 fuel points. The model has no corn heating type.
10. **Deliverable fuel amount (source wording and inference).** Appendix I calls $800 the minimum for liquid propane and fuel oil, 11.00 raises a lower matrix benefit to the state-set amount, and the draft plan's attachment calls it a flat amount that is both minimum and maximum. The general maximum is also $800, so all three give $800 in FY26; the branch pays `deliverable_fuel_amount` flat to the PROPANE and FUEL_OIL categories (kerosene included). By inference, the branch limits the flat amount to households that buy the fuel themselves: the draft plan (page 48) ties it to “deliverable fuel customers”, 11.00 (page 42) raises “the deliverable fuel benefit”, and Appendix D (page 122) pays a household with heat in its rent by “Direct pay to the LIHEAP customer” or to the electric vendor “because gas usage is indeterminate”. Such a tenant buys no fuel and takes the matrix amount, including the -4 heat-in-rent factor (companion test 19: $200). Paying $800 to every PROPANE or FUEL_OIL household would give $800 there. The draft page carries a manual footer dated 10/01/24 and belongs to a hearing draft, not the accepted plan.
11. **Energy burden and housing proxies (simplification).** A positive `pre_subsidy_electricity_expense` stands in for the Appendix D electric account of a household with heat in subsidized rent. Subsidized housing is `receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing`; the Definitions list is broader than either input. Appendix D rows for utilities billed by a landlord or trailer park, shared heat, disconnect notices, small propane tanks, dorms and households not charged by anyone have no separate input.
12. **Targeting factors (inference and proxies).** Appendix I lists each factor once; the branch scores each factor once per household however many members qualify (companion test 12(b)). `is_disabled` stands in for self-declared disability; `spm_unit_cash_assets` over $50,000 stands in for savings (4.40 item 4; ABLE accounts and trusts are not savings). The new `ia_liheap_dwelling_type` input defaults to DETACHED, so a caller that omits it gets the detached point; a mobile home occupied by one household is treated as detached by inference; “5-Plexes (or more than 5)” is read as five or more units.
13. **Minimum and maximum (arithmetic).** The $80 minimum applies to any approved customer, so zero and negative totals pay $80 (companion test 6). The matrix cannot reach $800 outside the flat amount: the largest other total is 8 + 5 + 4 = 17 points ($680); an 18-point kerosene household receives the flat $800.
14. **Income limit, plan field and administrative rule (source conflict).** Plan item 2.1 prints 150.00%; the plan's own note says the threshold is 200% and that the OLDC form would not accept it. The branch follows the manual's 200%. Iowa Administrative Code 421—22.2(1), in force during FY26 and not cited by the branch, limits incomes to 150 percent of the guidelines or 60 percent of state median income; the plan note states that 200% is below 60% of Iowa's SMI ($31,300 against $36,756 for one person), and 22.11 incorporates the plan and manual by reference. The rule was rescinded effective October 1, 2026.
15. **Years and dates (simplification).** All parameters start `2025-10-01`; annual periods read 1 January values, so period 2026 applies FY26 to the whole calendar year, including October to December 2026, which fall in FY27. Earlier and later periods are estimates (see Policy periods).
16. **Other gaps.** Funding availability, first-come first-served order, the once-per-program-year limit (4.20), application dates, the automatically eligible verification waiver (4.40), payment routing and the winter moratorium are not modeled. Railroad test households are aged 62 so the model imputes no SSI (its unearned income list omits `railroad_benefits`); companion tests take SSI as an input, $0 unless stated.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-ia-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ia-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [us-ia-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-ia-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml) (FY24 edition)
- [us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml) (2026 guidelines, period 2027 estimate)
- [us-hhs-poverty-guidelines.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-hhs-poverty-guidelines.yaml) (undated, never extracted)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-ia/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the FY26 limits for sizes 1 to 8 and the inclusive ceiling, the poverty-level band tops with the round-up note, every targeting factor and threshold (age 60, under 6, savings over $50,000, three dwelling types, subsidized housing, heat in rent, fixed income only with railroad retirement and recorded non-countable sources), the five published fuel rows and the treatment of kerosene (fuel oil points and the flat $800), other, solar, no heat and unspecified fuel, $40 a point with the $80 floor and $800 cap, the flat $800 for households that buy liquid propane or fuel oil and the matrix amount when heat is in the rent, heat in rent and subsidized housing, ineligible members (income counted, size not), the exclusion of income of members under 18, child support paid, Social Security net of the Medicare Part B premium, every listed countable and excluded source (including military retirement and survivor pay), per-source loss floors (including rental losses and the fixed-income test), and any 2025 or 2027 period kept in scope. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: LIHEAP wave 2b: encode New Hampshire Fuel Assistance Program regular heating assistance

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Objective

Ship New Hampshire Fuel Assistance Program regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 2b, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10343 (branch `nh-liheap-wave2b`), open, not merged. Head `a7d76c39d8` (2026-10-23), which follows the merge of policyengine-us `main` at `ee6c90961d`; this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **Sources missing from the corpus.** The branch's main source, the PY2027 Fuel Assistance Program Policy and Procedures Manual, is captured: `us-nh-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml` and its corpus lock hold the same file the branch read (SHA-256 `48d77fdaed2b6b33…`, 103 pages, PDF dated 2026-08-10). Attachment C, however, prints its heating-cost data as images with no text layer. The page 76 worked example and the page 77 tables (cost tiers, agency degree days, dwelling factors, fuel cost, efficiency and benefit multiplier) are absent from the extracted provisions, which contain none of 28.881, 6610, 7672 or 64.706; the page 75 illustration tables are absent too. A transcription of physical pages 75 to 77 needs admission before the heating-cost, tier and multiplier modules can be proved. Also missing: the Community Action Partnership of New Hampshire page that maps page 77's five agencies to counties; 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B), the 110% floor (the federal statute layer was extracted locally and not committed); 45 CFR 96.85(b), the size percentages (also printed in the captured HHS table's footnotes); and the FFY2027 draft state plan the PR body cites. These need ingest. The FY2026 state plan (which the LIHEAP program bundle marks as an excluded back-year document), the 2026 HHS poverty guidelines and the FY2027 HHS state median income table are captured; `us-nh-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml` holds the PY26 matrix, an earlier edition the branch does not use.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-23; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.
- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10343 was a draft from 2026-10-21 and is marked ready for review on 2026-10-23, with a review requested and none received yet, so there is no revision to pin.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10343, branch `nh-liheap-wave2b`, head `a7d76c39d8` (2026-10-23), which closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10337. Commit `3aceb16f27` (2026-10-23) applies the 2026-10-21 review fixes: military Survivor Benefit Plan annuities count through `military_retirement_income` (new `nh_fap.yaml` Case 84); `nh_fap_income_limit` calls the shared `liheap_smi_limit` helper instead of its own copy; one per-fuel `payment/benefit_multiplier.yaml` (page 77) replaces the scalar utility multiplier and the fuel sets in Python, with identical results; the cost-tier reference cites pages 76-78; 12 duplicate fuel-boundary and immigration-status cases were removed; and the candidate `us-nh:fap-income-floor-vs-smi-limit` was added to `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml`. Commit `8dc671f86e` sums the income sources with explicit loops instead of the built-in `sum()` (no behavior change), and `072d696aff` merges `main` at `ee6c90961d`. Commit `a7d76c39d8` adds `nh_ssp` (APTD, ANB and OAA) to the unearned sources, reading each source with `add()` so monthly `nh_ssp` sums over the year; treats a household `is_in_public_housing` as subsidized; corrects the countable-income test header to the combined $50 exclusion; adds two cases; and pins `nh_ssp: 0` for 15 aged or disabled members. Everything below describes that head; oracle fixtures will pin the merged commit.
- **Scope:** the New Hampshire Fuel Assistance Program (FAP), the state's LIHEAP regular heating benefit, for PY2027: New Hampshire residence, household size from citizens and qualified noncitizens (ineligible members' income still counts), countable gross income less child support paid and reported Medicare Part B premiums, the 60% state median income (SMI) limit with the federal 110% poverty floor, responsibility for heating costs directly or through unsubsidized rent, the annual heating cost (actual bill or the Attachment C estimate from dwelling type, rooms, county degree days and fuel), six income levels, four cost tiers, the Attachment D deliverable-fuel matrix and the 0.75 utility multiplier with whole-dollar rounding. Out of scope: energy emergency (crisis) assistance, cooling, weatherization, heating-equipment repair (including the option to apply up to $300 of the benefit to furnace repair or a service plan, page 57), the Supplemental Benefit Program and Senior Energy Assistance Services (page 40), priority intake order, funding limits and payment routing to vendors or landlords.
- **Policy periods:** one verified season, PY2027: the program year October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027 (manual glossary, page 8), with priority intake from July, intake for all from October and an April 30 application deadline (pages 10-11); the FFY2027 draft plan dates heating assistance 10/01/2026 to 09/30/2027 (item 1.1, page 4). New Hampshire variables are annual and read 1 January values, so period `2027` is PY2027 on the 2026 HHS guidelines (`fpg_year_lag` 1) and the FY2027 HHS four-person median of $156,134 (dated 2026-10-01 in `gov.hhs.smi.amount`). All 14 New Hampshire parameter files hold one `2026-10-01` entry. `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2027"`. Earlier periods take the same New Hampshire values by backfilling, with the guideline and median of their own year (period `2026`: the 2025 guidelines and the FY2026 median of $152,580): unverified historical estimates, which do not reproduce the PY26 matrix (interpretation 19). Later periods carry the PY2027 New Hampshire values forward with the model's projected guidelines and uprated median (the SMI parameter uprates from 2028): carried-forward estimates. Period 2027 also covers October to December 2027, which fall in PY2028.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/nh/doe/fap/`: `nh_fap`, `nh_fap_eligible`, `nh_fap_household_size`, `nh_fap_countable_income`, `nh_fap_income_limit`, `nh_fap_heating_cost` and the new input `nh_fap_dwelling_type` (SINGLE_FAMILY_OR_MODULAR, the default; MOBILE_HOME; APARTMENT_CONDO_OR_DUPLEX). ## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Rooms from bedrooms (approved approximation).** The estimate needs the dwelling's total rooms (page 17), excluding hallways, unfinished basements, garages, attics and closets, with oversized rooms counted by square feet. The branch uses `bedrooms` alone, so it usually counts fewer rooms than the agency (companion test 1: the manual's 7 rooms give AA and $825; 4 bedrooms give BB and $800). Zero or negative bedrooms give no estimate. Each SPM unit uses the whole household's bedrooms; rooms used only by foster individuals, a business or a roomer (pages 25-26, 31, 34) are not removed.
2. **Formula wording (source wording).** Page 76 labels step 1 “(Factor * # rooms + degree days)/1,000,000” but computes “(2000 * 7 * 7672) / 1000000”; the branch multiplies, as the example does.
3. **Actual or estimated cost (reading).** Page 18 says the system uses the estimate automatically, that actual costs “can be used for households with high energy usage” and that staff compare the two for “the best benefit”; page 76 asks for actual costs over 12 months. The branch takes the larger of the annual bill (floored at zero) and the estimate, which gives the better award because no matrix cell falls as cost rises.
4. **Counties and degree days (inference).** Page 77 lists degree days by agency; the county map comes from the CAPNH page, which names agencies by web domain. CAPHR is read as the Hillsborough and Rockingham agency by elimination (the manual's attachments call it SNHS). An unknown or out-of-state county gives no estimate; with no county input the model's fallback is Belknap County (6,610).
5. **Fuels (coverage).** `heating_type` is a required input (settled); UNSPECIFIED pays $0 (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the default). WOOD uses cordwood (0.63); wood pellets and bio bricks (21.650, 0.70) and winter blend (32.033, 0.78) have no `heating_type`. Coal is missing from page 78's deliverable heading but has a 1.000 multiplier on page 77; the branch treats it as delivered. SOLAR and OTHER have no page 77 row: the estimate is 0 and the multiplier 0, so an otherwise eligible household with a bill receives $0. Kerosene and fuel oil share `fuel_oil_expense`.
6. **Heat in rent (approved approximation).** The FY2026 plan says heat-in-rent “benefits are reduced”; page 76 shows the heat-in-rent multiplier only for “HIR = No” (1.0); the FFY2027 draft says such renters “are eligible for a benefit”. No reduction factor is published. The branch pays the ordinary schedule once, with the fuel multiplier, so these awards may be overstated. A heat-in-rent household with no positive actual or estimated cost receives $0. Payment as a rent reduction (page 57) is not modeled.
7. **Subsidized housing and dwelling facts (simplification).** `receives_housing_assistance` or the household's `is_in_public_housing` stands in for page 21's income-adjusted rent; public housing is read as subsidized because its rent is set by income. The new `nh_fap_dwelling_type` defaults to single family or modular; the agency's Room type (1,400) has no separate value. Campers and mobile homes not permanently attached (page 21) are not identified.
8. **Income levels and guideline year (reading).** Page 17's labels (“75.01-100%” and so on) leave gaps between levels; the branch compares income with 0.75 to 1.75 times the guideline, inclusive at each top, which reproduces page 74's dollar tops. Page 74 uses the 2026 guidelines, loaded on 1/16/26; page 10 loads new guidelines each February, so applications from February 2027 use the 2027 guidelines, which the branch does not model. The optional cut of level F to 200% of the guidelines (page 17) is not applied.
9. **Utility multiplier and rounding (inferred).** Page 78 prints utility cells; the branch stores the deliverable cells and the page 77 multiplier (0.750) and rounds half up to whole dollars, which reproduces all 24 utility cells. Page 76 has a rounding step but states no rule.
10. **Income limit arithmetic (inferred rounding).** HHS states the order (60% of the four-person median, then the size percentage) but no rounding. Flooring after each step reproduces page 74's eight amounts and the HHS amounts for sizes 9 to 12. Page 74 prints no SMI amount above eight; the branch extends the HHS rule. With floating point, the shared helper returns $238,883 at size 47, where exact arithmetic gives $238,884.
11. **Federal floor (statute; candidate `us-nh:fap-income-floor-vs-smi-limit`, follows statute).** The plan and manual apply 60% of SMI at every size; 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B) bars excluding on income alone below 110% of the poverty level. With the HHS size factors, the limit first falls below the floor at 28 counted members ($185,486 against $186,252). The branch rounds 1.1 x guideline to cents and compares strictly. Income in that gap still takes its level from the guideline.
12. **Annual income (simplification).** The agency counts current income, usually the month before application, annualized by ECOS (pages 13-14), with annual figures for self-employment, annuities and seasonal contracts. The branch uses annual amounts.
13. **Social Security and Medicare (encoded reading).** The branch counts `social_security` gross and subtracts each member's reported Part B premium (`medicare_part_b_premiums_reported`, floored at zero) from the household total, whether or not it was withheld from Social Security or railroad retirement. Part D premiums, Social Security and SSI overpayment recoveries (page 24), mandatory nursing-home payments (page 16) and employer mileage reimbursements (page 17) are not deducted. Plan item 1.9 checks “Excluding MediCare deduction”.
14. **Investment exclusion (approved convention).** Pages 15-16 exclude the first $50 of interest and the first $50 of dividends separately; page 17 allows “$50 of earned interest and/or dividends annually”. The branch applies one $50 exclusion to combined interest and ordinary dividends per SPM unit; whether the manual means per person or per household is not stated.
15. **Other income items (inputs and readings).** Child support received, capital gains, SSI under 18 and the earnings of members who are both full-time students and in secondary school (any age) are excluded. FANF counts through the take-up-gated `tanf`, once per unit. APTD, ANB and OAA count through `nh_ssp`, the New Hampshire state supplement, summed over the year; the model computes it for eligible aged, blind or disabled members unless supplied. RCA has no input. `general_assistance` is counted as state welfare, although plan item 1.9 leaves General Assistance unchecked and page 16 excludes one-time welfare-agency payments. `financial_assistance` stands in for regular support without the six-month test; `veterans_benefits` includes the excluded Aid and Attendance; `disability_benefits` and `pension_income` cannot separate one-time insurance payments. Adoption subsidies, military family allotments, royalties, tribal income, training stipends, assistantships and taxable grants have no input; military pay and tips count only within `employment_income`.
16. **Business and rental income (simplification).** The branch uses the model's net inputs, each floored at zero (settled), without adding back the depreciation, amortization and business-use-of-home deductions page 25 disallows; two businesses reported in one input cannot be floored separately. Rental and farm rental losses are floored (settled).
17. **Household (simplification).** The SPM unit stands in for the economic unit purchasing energy in common. Size counts `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`, which approximates page 35's list (F1, J1, F2 and J2 holders are ineligible under page 34). Students living away, foster individuals, live-in care providers, roomers, nursing-home residents, shared custody and the one-benefit-per-year rule are not identified.
18. **Plan, manual and manual examples (manual followed).** Plan item 1.9 checks one-time lump-sum payments; the manual excludes lump-sum inheritances and one-time compensation for injury or insurance; the branch follows the manual, with no candidate entry. Page 19's chart (“Up to $1,000” for DD) and example matrix (PY26 amounts) and page 75's illustration ($940 at CC/D and $425 at DD/E) differ from page 78 ($950, $440); page 78's utility labels overlap at $1,750 and $3,500. The branch follows page 77's cent tops and page 78's amounts.
19. **Years and editions (simplification).** All New Hampshire parameters start `2026-10-01`; annual periods read 1 January values, so period 2027 applies PY2027 to the whole calendar year. Period 2026 is an estimate that applies the PY2027 matrix: the PY26 matrix (corpus attachments manifest) used tiers starting at $1,000, $1,500 and $1,750 and amounts up to $2,177, and its 60% SMI table prints $62,251 for two persons where HHS prints $62,252.
20. **Other gaps.** The Supplemental Benefit Program (no amount, page 40), Senior Energy Assistance Services, the $300 furnace option, funding limits, priority and application windows, and vendor and landlord payment routing are not modeled.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-nh-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-nh-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml) (PY2027 manual, the branch's edition; pages 75-77 are images)
- [us-nh-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-nh-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml) (FY2026 plan; bundle-excluded)
- [us-nh-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-nh-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml) (PY26 matrix, earlier edition)
- [us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml) (2026 guidelines and the FY2027 SMI table)
- [us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml) (2025 guidelines, period 2026 estimate)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-nh/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the PY2027 limits for sizes 1 to 8 with the inclusive maximum, the HHS extension above eight and the federal 110% floor at 28 members, the five income-level tops, the four cost tiers at their cent edges, all 24 deliverable cells and the 0.750 utility multiplier with half-up rounding, the heating-cost estimate (dwelling factor, room proxy, county degree days, fuel cost and efficiency), the larger of actual and estimated cost with no cap, each mapped fuel and the treatment of other, solar, unspecified and no heat, heat in rent and subsidized or public housing, ineligible members (income counted, size not), child support received and paid, SSI under 18, the state supplement, high-school earnings, Social Security with reported Part B premiums, FANF, the combined $50 investment exclusion, per-source loss floors, and any 2026 or 2028 period kept in scope. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.body:
This issue mirrors a changed legal provision in [PolicyEngine-US PR #9184](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/pull/9184), head `b2e25f32656792a500a71eef9e2808baa402c19d` as fetched for wave 1. The PE implementation is an opt-in monthly **financial threshold screen**, separate from Medicaid enrollment and benefit values; functional eligibility and adjudication facts remain separate. Encode the operative law completely and expose the matching financial outputs without turning PE's disclosed partial scope into an assertion of full eligibility.

RuleSpec must be produced by the signed encoder; do not hand-write a module. This US hub issue is the research/test handoff. Max's d1142 ruling approves wave 1 billed runs; execution is assigned to the Axiom engineering hub.

## Module and corpus

- `us-tx/policies/hhsc/medicaid/mepd-j-7200.yaml` (target; preserve repository path conventions when dispatching).

Axiom corpus `us-tx/manual/2026-09-10-medicaid-state-eligibility-manual`; `us-tx/manual/hhsc/medicaid/mepd-j-7200/block-2` (JSONL line 1504, row id `6f592810-8dc7-5d55-8c00-6adb9931345c`); `us-tx/manual/hhsc/medicaid/mepd-j-7200/block-3` (JSONL line 1505, row id `9ff430fc-dd60-5974-8f7d-7d0cbed46f22`); `us-tx/manual/hhsc/medicaid/mepd-appendix-xxxi/block-2` (JSONL line 2127, row id `ec084968-57a3-5b1f-9637-f5ffba2ffaf5`)

## Existing-module and issue search

Rulespec-US main `207486d8b5194b46d52e54e2b1302ec36681f62b` was searched with `git ls-tree` and contents search. No module plus companion case covers this changed situation. The open `pe-parity` issue cache was searched for PR #9184, LTSS, each provision and state program; no matching open issue was found. Federal 1396p(f) and 435.217/.236 modules exist as dependencies, but their supplied-input or artificial-CPI cases do not establish the changed state/dated-dollar results here.

## Operative primary source (verbatim)

Fetched on 2026-10-09; HTML markup and PDF layout/page headers may be removed without paraphrasing operative wording.

Source: https://fhb.hhs.texas.gov/handbooks/medicaid-elderly-people-disabilities-handbook/j-7200-spousal-co-payment

> Body
> 
> Revision 26-3; Effective Sept.1, 2026
> 
> Budget Steps
> 
> Calculate the person and their spouse's net monthly earned income to determine the co-payment for a spousal companion case. Do this by subtracting the following mandatory payroll deductions:
> 
> income tax;
> 
> Social Security tax;
> 
> required retirement withholdings; and
> 
> required uniform expenses.
> 
> Note: Mandatory payroll deductions also apply to a dependent's earned income in spousal impoverishment cases.
> 
> Do not count in-kind support and maintenance income the spouse receives.
> 
> Do not allow a separate deduction for maintenance of the home in companion cases. The spousal allowance provides for home maintenance in those cases.
> 
> How to Determine Co-Payment for a Spousal Companion Case
> 
> Determine the countable net earned and gross unearned income of the person.
> 
> Subtract the personal needs allowance (PNA) of $75 for the person. Subtract the guardian fee allowance, if applicable.
> 
> Add the spouse's countable net earned and gross unearned income to the remainder. Count only the minimum monthly maintenance needs allowance (MMMNA) if the spouse’s income is more than the minimum monthly maintenance needs allowance MMMNA.
> 
> Subtract the spousal allowance.
> 
> If there are no dependents, go to step 6.
> If there are dependents, determine the dependent allowance.
> Subtract the dependent allowance.
> 
> Subtract incurred medical expenses. The remainder is the co-payment for the payment plan.
> 
> Notes:
> 
> Enter incurred medical expense deductions on the Medical Expense LUW in TIERS even if the payment plan is $0.
> 
> Follow procedures for an individual payment plan budget if:
> the person has signed a statement;
> 
> refuses to make the spousal allowance available; and
> 
> there are no dependents.
> 
> Count only the MMMNA in step 3 above if the community spouse's countable income is more than the MMMNA.
> 
> Examples
> 
> The following examples are for demonstration purposes only. They may not reflect the most recent protected resource amounts or dependent allowance.
> 
> A person and their spouse have the following monthly income:
> 
> Person
> $265 RSDI
> 
> +$200 Private retirement
> 
> =$465 Total
> 
> Spouse
> $350 RSDI
> 
> +$285 Teacher's retirement
> 
> = $635 Total
> 
> Co-payment calculation:
> $465 Person's gross income
> 
> – $75 PNA
> 
> = $390 Income available for diversion
> 
> + $635 Spouse's income
> 
> = $1,025 Total
> 
> – $4,066.50 Spousal allowance
> 
> = $0 Co-payment
> 
> Another person and their spouse have the following monthly income:
> 
> Person
> $490 RSDI
> 
> + $509 Private retirement
> 
> = $999 Total
> 
> Spouse
> $450 RSDI
> 
> + $300 Private retirement
> 
> + $750 Net earnings
> 
> = $1,500 Total
> 
> Co-payment calculation:
> $999 Person's gross income
> 
> – $75 PNA
> 
> = $924 Income available for diversion
> 
> + $1,500 Spouse's income
> 
> = $2,424 Total
> 
> – $4,066.50 Spousal allowance
> 
> = $0 Co-payment
> 
> A third person and their spouse have the following monthly income:
> 
> Person
> $1,250 RSDI
> 
> + $800 Private retirement
> 
> = $2,050 Total
> 
> Spouse
> $1,590 Net earnings
> 
> The person's dependent brother lives with the community spouse. The brother’s only income is $590 per month in RSDI disability benefits.
> 
> Brother’s dependent allowance calculation:
> $2,705Base amount of dependent allowance
> 
> – $590 Dependent's gross income
> 
> = $2,115Remainder
> 
> $2,115divided by 3
> 
> = $705 Dependent allowance
> 
> Co-payment calculation:
> $2,050 Person's gross income
> 
> – $75 PNA
> 
> = $1,975 Income available for diversion
> 
> + $1,590 Spouse's income
> 
> = $3,565 Total
> 
> – $4,066.50 Spousal allowance
> 
> = $0 Remainder
> 
> – $705 Dependent allowance
> 
> = $0.00 Co-payment
> 
> Related Policy
> 
> Co-Payment, Chapter H

Source: https://fhb.hhs.texas.gov/handbooks/medicaid-elderly-people-disabilities-handbook/appendix-xxxi-budget-reference-chart

> Individual or Couple Eligibility Budget
> 
> Special income limit — The special income limit for a person is equal to or less than 300% of the SSI federal benefit rate.
> 
> Income — Effective Jan. 1, 2026, total countable income must be no more than the special income limit:
> 
> Individual — $2,982
> 
> Couple — $5,964
> 
> Resources —Total countable resources must be no more than the limit:
> 
> Individual — $2,000
> 
> Couple — $3,000
> 
> Substantial home equity — $752,000
> 
> Transfer of assets (TOA) divisor — $262.37 daily rate effective Sept. 1, 2025.
> 
> Note: The transfer of assets daily rate is reviewed every other year.
> 
> Co-Payment
> 
> Individual or Couple Co-Payment Budget:
> 
> Personal Needs Allowance (PNA)
> $75 for a nursing facility recipient
> 
> $75 plus the Protected Earned Income (PEI) amount for a recipient in an ICF/IID facility
> 
> $85 for a recipient in foster care or assisted living
> 
> $2,901 for an HCBS waiver recipient
> 
> Guardianship Fees — Varies
> 
> Dependent Allowance — $967
> 
> Incurred Medical Expenses — Varies
> 
> Deduction for Home Maintenance — Up to $967
> 
> Spousal Co-payment Budget:
> 
> PNA
> $75 for a nursing facility recipient
> 
> $75 plus the PEI amount for a recipient in an ICF/IID facility
> 
> $85 for a recipient in foster care or assisted living
> 
> $2,901 for an HCBS waiver recipient
> 
> Guardianship Fees — Varies
> 
> Minimum Monthly Maintenance Needs Allowance (MMMNA) also known as Spousal Allowance — $4,066.50
> 
> Spousal Impoverishment Dependent Allowance — $2,643.75 effective July 1, 2025
> 
> Incurred Medical Expenses — Varies
> 
> Calculation of the Spousal Protected Resource Amount (SPRA):
> 
> SPRA is the greater of:
> one-half of the couple's combined countable resources; or
> 
> $32,532, the minimum resource amount set by federal law; but
> 
> cannot exceed $162,660, the maximum resource amount set by federal law.
> 
> Income-first MMMNA for SPRA expansion also known as Spousal Allowance — $4,066.50
> Related Policy
> Personal Needs Allowance (PNA), H-1500
> Guardianship Fees, H-1550
> Dependent Allowance, H-1600
> Deduction for Home Maintenance, H-1700
> Incurred Medical Expenses, H-2000
> Spousal Impoverishment Dependent Allowance, J-7400

## Required outputs

Expose the 2026 Texas standard of $4,066.50 regardless of shelter-expense facts. Distinguish this post-eligibility standard from the actual spouse allocation (which offsets the spouse's own income) and from applicant income eligibility. A nonapplicable/no-community-spouse scenario has no maintenance allowance.

## Companion cases and external expected values

These are prose test contracts for the encoder, not hand-written RuleSpec. Expected values are direct official-table entries or arithmetic dictated by the quoted primary law; no PolicyEngine output was used as an oracle. Use the same sources cited in PE's YAML metadata and the indicated cases. Assume all adjudicated nonfinancial prerequisites and valid reported classifications for the positive financial cases.

|Period|Input facts|Required result and external derivation|
|---|---|---|
|2026-01 and 2026-07|Qualifying applicant/community spouse; shelter expenses $0/$1,000/$3,000|Maintenance standard $4,066.50 in all scenarios; Appendix XXXI.|
|2026-07|No community spouse|No spouse maintenance allowance ($0).|
|2026-07|Applicant countable income $3,000; spouse shelter $3,000|Standard $4,066.50, but applicant is above $2,982 SIL and fails income threshold.|

PE YAML cross-checks under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/hhs/medicaid/eligibility/long_term_care/financial/`: `medicaid_ltss_mmmna.yaml Cases 1,4,8–9`; `is_medicaid_ltss_financial_threshold_eligible.yaml Case 1`.

## Queued blocker

The operative MEPD rows are present in the verified September manual scope but absent from both Texas manual scopes in `us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap` (May self-contained and July recovery). Select a signed release carrying the September rows, or publish a self-contained successor. The US hub is not authorized to run the encoder; dispatch belongs to the Axiom engineering hub under Max's d1142 approval.

Before closing, the engineering hub should attach the signed encoding PR, corpus release/fingerprints and passing companion case names, and replace this PR's corresponding `axiom:` item with `encoded` or a verified `encoded-correct` citation.

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Nevada Energy Assistance Program regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1d, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10432 (branch `nv-liheap-wave1d`), open, not merged. Head `4c554d9268` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983`; this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10432 opened on 2026-10-23 with no reviews yet, so there is no revision to pin.
- **Sources missing from the corpus.** No axiom-corpus manifest on `main` holds the branch's two main sources, the SFY2026 Energy Assistance Program (EAP) Manual (footer 27 Aug 25, MTL 01/25) and the SFY2027 manual (24 Aug 26, MTL 01/26). `us-nv-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml` holds the FY2024 edition (MTL 01/24, expression date 2024-06-25: a 2.63% burden, a $240 minimum and the 2023 guidelines), which supports no SFY2026 or SFY2027 value except the unchanged cap tables. Also missing: the accepted FFY2027 LIHEAP plan, NRS 702.260, LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 2, and the Nevada Fund for Energy Assistance and Conservation (NFEAC) state plans for SFY2026 and SFY2027 (not cited by the branch). These need ingest. Captured: the SFY2026 Appendix A (`us-nv-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml`, identical text), the FFY2026 plan, the 2024, 2025 and 2026 HHS poverty guidelines, LIHEAP IM 2026-01 Attachment 2 and POMS SI 01415.058.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-23; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10432, branch `nv-liheap-wave1d`, head `4c554d9268` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983` and closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10422. The 2026-10-22 review fixes are in the tree: qualified non-citizens within the manual's five-year bar (302 C) leave household size through the new `nv_liheap_immigration_eligible` and four `eligibility/five_year_bar/` parameters; the blind SSI case asserts countable income with Nevada's SSA-paid supplement (`nv_oss`); duplicate cases were removed. Oracle fixtures will pin the merged commit.
- **Scope:** Nevada's EAP, run by the Division of Social Services, pays one Fixed Annual Credit (FAC) a program year toward primary heating and electric costs; the branch models it as the regular benefit: residence, household size (citizens and qualified non-citizens outside the five-year bar), eligibility income against 150% of the guideline, responsibility for an energy cost (a heating bill, heat in rent, subsidized or public housing only with an energy burden), the FAC (energy cost less 1.81% or 1.48% of FAC income), the $360 minimum, the Appendix A caps by size, poverty band and fuel, and the $100 targeted-household cap supplement. Both plans describe one year-round program; no separate cooling award is modeled. Out of scope: Fast Track crisis, the arrearage payment and other specialized components, weatherization, shutdown eligibility (NRS 702.260(4)), payment routing (master meters, landlord accounts, solar vendors), universal energy charge (UEC) funding limits and administrative cap adjustments.
- **Policy periods:** two verified program years, SFY2026 (July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026) and SFY2027 (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027), the “State fiscal year--July-June” (501 A, page 32). Variables are annual and read 1 January values, so period `2026` is SFY2026 and `2027` is SFY2027; `fpg_year_lag` 1 applies the 2025 guidelines in period 2026 and the 2026 guidelines in period 2027, reproducing each Appendix A exactly. Seventeen of the 18 parameter files hold one `2025-07-01` entry; `payment/burden_rate.yaml` holds 0.0181 from `2025-07-01` and 0.0148 from `2026-07-01`. `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2026-2027"`. Earlier periods take SFY2026 values by backfilling on the lagged guideline (period `2025` on the 2024 guidelines): unverified estimates (the FY2024 manual printed 2.63% and $240; SFY2025 was not compared). Later periods carry SFY2027 forward on the lagged guideline (period `2028` on the 2027 guidelines): carried-forward estimates. User decisions: the $360 minimum in SFY2026 (interpretation 2), cap bands from FAC income, top-inclusive, with income over 150% in the last band (3), the energy cost as primary heating plus electricity (4), and the propane and oil table for propane, fuel oil and kerosene (5).
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/nv/dwss/liheap/`: `nv_liheap`, `nv_liheap_energy_cost`, `nv_liheap_household_size`; `eligibility/` `nv_liheap_eligible`, `nv_liheap_immigration_eligible` (person level), `nv_liheap_income_limit`; `income/` `nv_liheap_earned_income` and `nv_liheap_child_earned_income` (person level), `nv_liheap_countable_income`, `nv_liheap_fac_income`. No new input variable.
- **Parameters:** 18 files under `gov.states.nv.dwss.liheap`: `eligibility/` `fpg_rate` (1.5), `fpg_year_lag` (1), and `five_year_bar/` `years` (5), `child_age_limit` (18), `exempt_statuses` (REFUGEE, ASYLEE, DEPORTATION_WITHHELD, CUBAN_HAITIAN_ENTRANT) and `qualifying_quarters` (40); `income/` `child_age_limit` (18), `sources/earned` (5 sources) and `sources/unearned` (23); `payment/` `burden_rate`, `minimum` (360), `targeted/elderly_age` (60), `targeted/young_child_age_limit` (6), and `cap/` `standard` and `propane_and_oil` (8 sizes by 4 bands), `income_band` (band tops 0.75, 1 and 1.25, `right=True`, `-.inf` first threshold), `max_household_size` (8) and `targeted_supplement` (100). Plus the `programs.yaml` entry and the changelog fragment.
- **Tests:** 56 YAML cases in 7 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/nv/dwss/liheap/` (`nv_liheap.yaml` 24, `nv_liheap_energy_cost.yaml` 3, `eligibility/nv_liheap_eligible.yaml` 12, `eligibility/nv_liheap_immigration_eligible.yaml` 3, `eligibility/nv_liheap_income_limit.yaml` 5, `income/nv_liheap_countable_income.yaml` 7, `income/nv_liheap_fac_income.yaml` 2). Every household case sends `heating_type`; the three person-level immigration cases need none. A local run on 2026-10-22 passed all 56 cases before the 2026-10-22 review fixes; the fixed tree was not re-run. CI validates.

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence on axiom-corpus `main` (`dce8e44665`, 2026-10-23) was checked on 2026-10-23 against the full manifest list, by reading the relevant manifests and by GitHub code search for the source URLs; presence in the signed release was not checked. rulespec-us `main` (`115bad3183`, 2026-10-23) has `us-nv/policies/` (`cms`, `dwss/eligibility-payments/a-600`, `income_tax`) but no LIHEAP module, no `us-nv/regulations/` or `us-nv/statutes/`, and no `us/` poverty-guideline module; the paths below follow that layout, with the agency folder `dwss` of the existing module and the branch. Pages are physical PDF pages.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-nv/policies/dwss/energy-assistance-program-manual/sfy2026/section-300/non-citizens` | 302 A eligible categories and the 302 A I note (page 21); 302 A VIII-XIV, 302 B ineligible categories, 302 C five-year bar and exemptions I-III (page 22); exemptions IV-VIII and 304 (page 23) | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. Official copy, for every SFY2026 manual row: [SFY2026 EAP Manual, pages 21-23, 31-37, 43-48, 57, 59-61, 104-105 and 110-111](https://dss.nv.gov/uploadedFiles/dwssnvgov/content/Energy/FY%202026%20EAP%20Manual%2008.2025%20ADA.pdf#page=21) (115 pages). |
| `.../sfy2026/section-500/non-financial-eligibility` | 500 vendor account and 501 I subsidized housing (page 31); 501 A program year, 502 and 502 A.I household size and excluded members (pages 32-33); 503 public housing and 504 A master meters (page 34); 505 targeted households (page 35); 505 D, F and G landlord accounts and solar vendors (pages 36-37); 507 energy sources (page 37) | none | Same file. |
| `.../sfy2026/section-700/income` | 700 non-citizen income, 701 the 150% limit, 702 income consideration and the $240 line, 703 A earned income (pages 43-44); 703 B.I Medicare deduction (page 44); 705 income table (pages 46-48); 706 exempt income (page 48); 707 N children's earned income (page 57) | none | Same file. |
| `.../sfy2026/section-800/budgeting` | 800 IV 30-day income annualized (page 59); 802 income eligibility and 803 I-V.1 (page 60); 803 V.2-VI minimum and cap (page 61) | none | Same file. |
| `.../sfy2026/glossary` | Child and Disabled items 1-3 (page 104); Disabled items 4-8, Elderly, Energy Burden (page 105) | none | Same file. |
| `.../sfy2026/appendix-a/income-energy-burden-benefit-cap` | Income table for sizes 1-8 and each additional person, the 1.81% burden (page 110); both cap tables and the $100 targeted note (page 111) | `us-nv/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026-benefit-matrix` | In manifest `us-nv-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml` (Clearinghouse attachment, 2 pages, expression date 2025-10-01): the same MTL 01/25 footer and identical text as manual pages 110-111; the appendix applies from July 1, 2025. ## Source text (verbatim)

Quotations come from the official files above (pdftotext, line breaks collapsed); FFY2026 plan check-box states come from renders of pages 5, 6, 8 and 9, and the FFY2027 plan text from OCR of the scanned file, checked against renders. “MS” is the manual's own abbreviation for its sections. Except where noted, the SFY2027 manual repeats the SFY2026 text quoted here.

**Statute.** NRS 702.260(3): “to be eligible to receive assistance from the Division pursuant to this section, a household must have a household income that is not more than 150 percent of the federally designated level signifying poverty, as determined by the Division.” (7)(a): “Shall, to the extent practicable, determine the amount of assistance that the household will receive by determining the amount of assistance that is sufficient to reduce the percentage of the household’s income that is spent on natural gas and electricity to the median percentage of household income spent on natural gas and electricity statewide.” (7)(b) allows adjustments for income, size, “The type of energy that the household uses; and” vulnerability. (8) requires regulations; NAC chapter 702 adopts none for the EAP benefit.

**Program and dates.** FFY2026 plan page 1: “Report Period: 10/01/2025 to 09/30/2026” and “Report Status: Submission Accepted by CO”; page 4, item 1.1: “Nevada has a combined year-round heating and cooling program. All the information will be provided in the Heating Assistance section.” Section 3 (page 11) refers to the heating section. FFY2027 plan page 1: “Report Period: 10/01/2026 to 09/30/2027”; page 4 adds cooling dates and 40.00% of funds for cooling; page 11: “Nevada has a year-round program - same as Heating Assistance.” Manual page 32, 501 A: “One program year (State fiscal year--July-June)”.

**Household.** Page 32, 502: “The total number of household members living in the home is used to determine eligibility and the Fixed Annual Credit (FAC).” 502 A.I: “The following individuals are excluded from the household; however, their income is counted when determining the household’s gross countable income:” the list names ineligible non-citizens, persons who do not provide an SSN, intentional program violations and, on page 33, “Students who live outside of the household. Exception: their income is excluded when determining the household’s gross countable income.”

**Citizenship and the five-year bar.** Page 21, 302 A I, after the permanent resident category: “NOTE: Non-citizens, legally admitted for permanent residence, may also need to meet the five year bar – See MS 302C for Eligibility Rules”. 302 A also lists refugees, asylees, deportation withheld, conditional entrants, parolees, battered spouses or children (page 21), Cuban/Haitian entrants, Amerasians, PRUCOL, Native American Indians, Hmong or Highland Laotians, trafficking victims and COFA citizens (page 22); 302 B IV excludes “individuals paroled for less than one year”. 302 C (page 22): the bar “only applies to” qualified non-citizens “who entered the United States on or after August 22, 1996. This means qualified non-citizens are ineligible for a period of 5 years beginning on the date of their entry into the United States if they entered after August 22, 1996, unless they qualify for one of the exemptions below:” I, children under 18; “II. Aliens who were lawfully residing in the U.S. and were age 65 or older on August 22, 1996;” III, members of a federally recognized tribe; page 23: IV, American Indians born in Canada; V, certain Hmong and Highland Laotians; “VI. Refugee and Asylees, aliens whose deportation is being withheld, Amerasians, and Cuban/Haitian entrants, and victims of a severe form of trafficking;” “VII. Veterans, members of the military on active duty, and their spouses and unmarried dependent children; or” “VIII. Legal Permanent residents who have worked 40 qualifying quarters of coverage.” Page 23, 304: “A household member without proof of immigration status will be excluded from the household size; however, their income is considered countable and will be included when calculating the household’s gross income.” Page 43, 700: “NOTE: A non-citizen’s income is counted in determining financial eligibility; however, that individual is not counted as a household member when determining the household size.”

**Two income measures.** Page 43, 702 I note: “Exempt income and FAC countable income is disregarded when determining program eligibility.” 702 II note: “Income exempt from determining eligibility that comes directly to the household, is counted when determining the FAC benefit.” Page 57, 707 N: “Earned income for children who are under the age of 18 and attend elementary or high school or GED classes at least half time or are too young to attend school and who reside with applicant parent/legal guardian, is excluded income when determining eligibility, but is countable income when determining the FAC benefit.” Page 59, 800 IV: “Verified countable gross income (both earned and unearned) received by a household in a 30-day period preceding the application/application review. **Heating responsibility and housing.** Page 31, 500: “An applicant household must have or qualify to have an active open account with a Nevada utility/energy vendor.” 501 I: “Households residing in subsidized housing where all utilities are included in the rent and they are not billed unless they have an energy burden. **Benefit rule.** Page 60, 803 II applies the Appendix A median energy burden to annual gross income: “This computation is the amount of money the household is expected to pay for the energy costs for the year.” 803 III: “For the vendors that do not interface with the EAP system calculate the household’s energy dollar usage for the prior twelve (12) months and enter amount in the screen.
