## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Six-person limit (source conflict).** 415-25-05-10 and 415-30-10-01 print a six-person annual limit of $102,984 beside a monthly $8,574.50; 12 x 8,574.50 = 102,894, the workbook figure, and sizes 1 to 6 otherwise rise by $12,468 to $12,480 a step. The branch uses $102,894 (comment in `income_limits.yaml`; candidate `us-nd:liheap-six-person-limit-workbook-vs-manual`, follows conflicting-source). The reading matters only from $102,895 to $102,984.
2. **Renter payment (source conflict and inferred rounding).** 415-30-30 pays the table amount by SMI group and fuel; 415-30-30-10 says the share-based amount is “subtracted from the monthly estimated cost of heating”, which would pay a 100%-share renter nothing. The branch follows the table, whose amounts keep the 45% to 100% range of 415-30-05 (candidate `us-nd:liheap-renter-table-vs-subtraction-prose`, follows conflicting-source). The branch computes each cell as the yearly cap x share / 12 rounded to the nearest dollar with halves up, which reproduces all 20 published cells (for example 2,200 x 0.45 / 12 = 82.50, published $83); the manual states no rounding. A full year is 12 monthly payments, at most the yearly cap (propane at 100%: 1,752 capped at 1,750); partial years are not modeled.
3. **Federal floor (source conflict).** The workbook's 60% limits for 21 to 28 members fall below 110% of the 2025 guideline (21 members: 137,970 against 138,215; 28 members: 154,338 against 180,565). The branch follows 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B): a household the table excludes gets the 45% minimum share when income is strictly below 1.1 x the guideline, rounded to cents, through `gov.hhs.liheap.fpg_floor` (candidate `us-nd:liheap-income-floor-vs-smi-limit`, follows statute). Above 28 members the floor also exceeds the 60% state median income extrapolation. The 45% share for these households is the branch's choice; the statute sets no amount.
4. **Plan narrative and the manual (plan against manual).** Plan item 2.5 describes a 6%-of-income cap, an estimated cost of heat and a family share, checks dwelling type and energy burden, and item 2.6 lists $1 and $7,500. The web manual pays a fixed share of actual bills (415-20-05-05, 415-30-05, 415-30-10), keeps the estimated cost table for reporting only (415-30-15) and sets neither a 6% cap nor a $7,500 maximum. The branch follows the manual and applies neither (comment in `nd_liheap.py`); `candidates.yaml` has no entry for this. Plan item 1.8 checks “Gross Income” while page 7 and the manual use gross income less deductions; the branch applies the manual's deductions.
5. **Households above 28 members (extension).** The workbook stops at 28. The branch applies 20% to 60% of the size-adjusted state median income (shared `smi`: four-person amount x 96.85(b) factor), unrounded. North Dakota's own table differs slightly from the HHS amounts (one person: 40,530 against 40,531; six: 102,894 against 102,888), so its rounding above 28 is unknown.
6. **Annual income (simplification).** North Dakota annualizes application-month income (x12, x52, x26, x24), or a three-month average x4 when income changes by $400 or more (415-25-05-15), and applies the result for 12 months (415-30-01). The branch uses annual amounts.
7. **Household and size (simplification).** The SPM unit stands in for the household that buys energy in common. `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant` approximates the qualified-noncitizen list, some of whose statuses `immigration_status` lacks. Roomers, foster persons, college students away, institutional and transient units and occupancy dates are not identified. Households on the four reservations with tribal LIHEAP are served by those programs, and mixed households may elect (415-20-10-15); the branch assumes the state program.
8. **Children's earnings (proxy and plan box).** The branch excludes the earnings of a member with `is_tax_unit_dependent`, aged under 20, with `is_in_k12_school` or `is_in_secondary_school`, standing in for a dependent child attending elementary or high school half time or more; GED classes and home schooling are not identified, and the earnings of minors not in school count. Plan item 1.9 leaves “Earned income of a child under the age of 18” unchecked; the branch follows the manual's narrower exclusion.
9. **Self-employment, farm and rental income (simplification).** The branch uses the model's net inputs, each floored at zero, so a loss offsets nothing (415-25-05-15, 415-25-05-27-05); losses inside one input cannot be separated, and the tax-form adjustments of 415-25-05-27-20 are not reconstructed. Partnership income is earned; S corporation and estate income, rental and farm rental income are unearned (415-25-05-27-15 makes rental income earned when actively engaged), each floored. `capital_gains` is not counted, although 415-25-05-27-15 calls business capital gains earned. Military pay and employer-paid disability are not added separately because `employment_income` may contain them; `disability_benefits` is treated as paid by someone other than the employer.
10. **Unearned items without a matching input (simplification).** Gambling winnings are not counted because `gambling_winnings` does not separate recurring from non-recurring winnings (comment in `unearned_sources.yaml`). Royalties, recurring settlements and inheritances, trust income, tribal payments, military allotments and contract-for-deed interest have no separate input. `financial_assistance` counts in full at $360 or more a year, treated as regular and unconditional. `retirement_distributions` is treated as regular withdrawals; `veterans_benefits` may include education benefits, which the manual excludes. Interest and dividends are excluded.
11. **Social Security and Medicare (encoded reading).** `social_security` counts gross. Reported Medicare Part B premiums (`medicare_part_b_premiums_reported`, or a positive `health_insurance_premiums` total) are deducted as medical expenses under 415-25-05-05-05; the computed premium is not imputed, so a member with Medicare and no reported premium has no deduction (companion test 12(f)). Plan item 1.9 checks “Excluding MediCare deduction”. The manual's bar on Part A and B premiums of QMB, SLMB, QI-1 or Buy-In members is not applied.
12. **Deductions (simplification).** Medical costs are deducted as reported, without the paid-or-payment-plan condition; dependent care is `childcare_expenses` without the work, training or education condition; nonqualified members' deductions count. Garnishments, payee fees, the away-from-home deductions and approved special expenses have no input.
13. **TANF and SSI (encoded reading).** TANF counts once per SPM unit through `tanf` (actual receipt under the model's take-up); `ssi` counts as modeled unless supplied. Withheld unearned income counts gross, as reported.
14. **Fuels (coverage limit and inference).** `heating_type` is a required input (settled); UNSPECIFIED has no bill and no renter cap, so it pays $0 (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the default); NONE is not eligible. Direct payments are fuel-independent: the share of the annual bill for the primary fuel, read through `heating_expense` (kerosene through `fuel_oil_expense`, solar through the electricity bill). With the electric adjustment repealed, electric heat is paid on the whole pre-subsidy electricity bill. For heat in rent, kerosene, wood, coal, solar and other take the “Natural Gas and Other” column by 415-30-15-01. Secondary heat (415-30-15-05), separately billed incidental charges (415-20-05-05) and the nonresidential caps (415-20-05-05-15) need facts the inputs lack and are not modeled.
15. **Housing (proxies and scope).** Subsidized means `receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing`; subsidized households paying their own heat follow the ordinary rules. A subsidized household with heat in rent and an electric bill in its name is eligible under 415-20-10 for the electric bill only; that non-heating electric benefit and the Renter Electric Utility Benefit Table are outside regular heating scope, so the branch pays $0. Owners and renters are treated alike.
16. **Years and dates (simplification).** All FY2026 values apply to the whole calendar year 2026, including October to December 2026, which fall in FY2027. The program page's FY2027 monthly limits ($3,446 for one person) and any FY2027 renter or band changes are not encoded. Earlier and later periods are estimates (see Policy periods).
17. **Other gaps.** Funding-based adjustment or suspension of benefits (415-20-10), first-come first-served service, authorization periods (415-30-20), vendor payment routing and stockpiling limits (415-20-05-05-10) are not modeled.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-nd-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-nd-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [us-nd-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-nd-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml) (Manual Letter 3750, October 1, 2023; no FY2026 value)
- [us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml) (2025 guidelines for the FY2026 floor; 2024 for the period 2025 estimate)
- [us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml) (2026 guidelines and the FY2027 state median income table, period 2027 estimate)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-nd/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover all 140 FY2026 upper limits for sizes 1 to 28 with their inclusive boundaries (including the six-person $102,894 reading), the five LIHEAP shares, the state median income bands above 28 members, the strict 110% federal floor at the 45% minimum share, direct bills at the share for every fuel with no electric adjustment, the renter table and yearly caps for fuel oil, propane, electricity and natural gas or other (kerosene, wood, coal, solar and other included), unspecified fuel and no heat, subsidized housing with and without heat in rent, nonqualified members (income counted, size not), the 27% earned deduction, the dependent-student earnings exclusion, the medical, Medicare, support and dependent-care deductions, the $360 contribution rule, every listed countable and excluded source, per-source loss floors, and any 2025 or 2027 period kept in scope. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: Source-conflict register: readings already taken without an entry (sweep, 2026-10-12)
items.body:
The source-conflict register (`known-source-conflicts.yaml`, #1710) starts with the ten Social Security readings from PolicyEngine/microcosm-dynamics#528, #529 and #530. This issue lists other places, found on 2026-10-12, where an encoding or a draft already takes a reading between disagreeing sources and no register entry exists.

**None of these has a ruling in the register.** Each would enter as `status: open` until a ruling with a public record exists. Where a PR or module already records a decision, the table says so; that is not a ruling.

## How the sweep was run

- RuleSpec module text and YAML comments in rulespec-us, plus the locally cloned active rulespec repositories, searched for reading language: "operational reading", "literal reading", "source conflict", "interpretive ruling" and similar.
- axiom-oracles `closure/` and `dispositions/`.
- PR and issue bodies across TheAxiomFoundation and PolicyEngine: 144 hits on phrases such as "Readings that need", "literal reading", "operational reading", "sources disagree" and "agency manual".
- Track B design docs in microcosm-dynamics.
- The `module.interpretations` backfill list for UK council schemes.

## rulespec-us candidates

| # | Program | Sources in tension | Reading taken, where | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SNAP ABAWD time limit | 7 U.S.C. 2015(o)(3)(A) as amended by P.L. 119-21: "under 18, or over 65, years of age", which leaves age exactly 65 subject. Against it, FNS OBBBA ABAWD exceptions implementation memorandum (2025-10-03): ages 18–64 subject, 65 and older excepted. | `us/regulations/7-cfr/273/24.yaml` follows the memorandum (`member_age >= 65` excepts). This is stated in a YAML comment and in #1212. axiom-oracles' ABAWD grid labels it "the USDA operational reading". | **Taken silently**: no register entry, no ruling. Effect: a 65-year-old ABAWD is excepted rather than subject to the three-month limit. |
| 2 | Tariffs, section 232 | HTSUS ch. 99 U.S. note 16 clause (9)'s once-rule, which names only the clause (2), (3) and (5) rates; a literal reading gives a Russian aluminum-covered article 200 + 50 = 250 percent from April 6 to July 20, 2026. Against it, note 16(a)'s exception for 9903.85.67/.68 and note 19's compiler's note, which give 200 percent. | Draft #1408 calls this "an interpretive ruling" and follows note 16(a). | Open draft. The reading is recorded in the PR; no register entry. Affects one entry, 7614.10.10.00 RU. |
| 3 | SSI/SSP, California | The CDSS monthly payment-standard table prints $3,239.14 for every couple NMOHC row. SSA POMS SI 01415.058B and CDSS's own 2026 May Revision tables print $3,252.14. | Issue #1450 asks the encoding to make the conflict visible rather than choose. | Open issue; not encoded yet. $13.00 a month per couple. |
| 4 | LIHEAP, New York HEAP | Manual D.4(a)(5) excludes "Federal living arrangement code C SSI recipients". D.13(a)(11), 14-ADM-07 Attachment 2 and SSA's definition of Code C differ on who that is. | Draft #1480 marks it "source conflict, owner decision pending". | Open draft. |
| 5 | LIHEAP, New York HEAP | For a household of 14, D.9(c) and plan 2.1 give 150% of the poverty guideline, $10,893 a month. The benefit matrix's "14+" row and OTDA's "Add $687" give $10,908. | Draft #1480 follows the rule (D.9(c)). | Open draft. $15 a month on the income limit; sizes 1 to 13 agree. |
| 6 | LIHEAP, New Jersey | N.J.A.C. 5:49 disagrees with the handbook three times. (1) Income ceiling: 175% of the FPI capped at 60% SMI, against 60% SMI alone. (2) Earnings disregard: $268, against $500 a month. (3) Subsidized tenant with a heating bill: the renter benefit, against the fuel rule. | Draft #1481 follows the handbook on (1) and (2) and the regulation on (3). The PR records an owner decision on (3). | Open draft; (1) and (2) are marked "owner decision pending". |
| 7 | LIHEAP, New Jersey | Plan 1.4a makes a TANF, SNAP or PAAD household "categorically eligible". Handbook 3.1.a.2 and 2.2 keep the income test. | Draft #1481 applies the income test to every household. | Open draft, "owner decision pending". A SNAP household over 60% SMI is eligible only under the plan's literal reading. |
| 8 | LIHEAP, New Jersey | The FY2027 plan 1.9 leaves strike pay, GA and TANF unchecked. Handbook 2.2 counts them. | Draft #1481 follows the handbook. | Open draft. |
| 9 | SNAP work registration | 7 U.S.C. 2015(d)(2)(E) refers to the FLSA federal minimum wage. The module's earnings branch reuses the regulation-derived federal-or-state minimum wage input of 7 CFR 273.7. | `us/regulations/7-cfr/273/7.yaml` explains this in a YAML comment: a higher state wage makes the test stricter than the statute. | Weaker candidate: an input-reuse choice more than a disagreement between sources. Listed for completeness. |

## Other registers (each repository keeps its own)

| Repository | Candidate | Sources in tension | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| rulespec-uk | Council tax reduction "daily 20%" (Babergh, Ipswich, Guildford, Mid Suffolk) | A scheme's paragraph on the daily percentage, against its own daily maximum and UC table | Being backfilled as `module.interpretations`. Babergh's ruling record is TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-uk#449. Each needs an entry naming its module pair once the backfill lands. |
| rulespec-uk | Arun, Charnwood, Burnley and Cambridge CTR schemes | Within-scheme tensions: Band A 100% under para 23(3); 85% under para 29(1A) and penny-gap bands; para 58.2 non-dependant bands; a UC table row missing "x 52" | Wave-11 fix rounds. Cambridge is open. |
| rulespec-uk | HB (SPC) Regs 2006 Sch 3 para 12(1)(b)(i), severe disability premium (rulespec-uk#383) | The paragraph's words, under which any carer benefit in payment counts, against the narrower carer-for-a-member-of-the-couple reading that para 6(2)(b) and SPC reg 6(5)(b) use | Open issue; unresolved. The proposed encoding keeps the literal words as a separate leaf. |
| rulespec-uk | Sharers and a looked-after 17-year-old who has left education (rulespec-uk#406) | Para 9(2)(c) and 9(3), read through the reg 2 foster-parent definition (under 18), against WRA 2012 s.40 (child under 16) | Open issue, which says to record this as a ruling. |
| rulespec-nz | Orphan's and Unsupported Child's Benefit age bands | Social Security Act 2018 Sch 4 Parts 4–5 cl 1, "over 5 years and under 10" and "over 10 years and under 14", leave ages exactly 5 and 10 unassigned. Work and Income's deskfile administers 5–9 and 10–13. | `nz/statutes/social_security/orphans_unsupported_child_benefit/core.yaml` follows the deskfile. Taken silently. |

## Considered and left out

- axiom-oracles dispositions describing Axiom-versus-PolicyEngine conventions on one source, for example 7 CFR 273.10(e) whole-dollar against cents rounding, and the CMS eligibility-levels table scope. These are single-source readings; they belong in `module.interpretations`, not the register.
- #1697: committed fixtures that contradict statute arithmetic. That is a test bug, not a disagreement between sources.
- rulespec-uk#398: dating Carer Support Payment amendments. The sources agree.
- PolicyEngine/microcosm-dynamics#532: a delayed-retirement-credit erratum. The Act and POMS agree.

items.title: LIHEAP wave 1d: encode Missouri LIHEAP Energy Assistance regular heating assistance

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Missouri LIHEAP Energy Assistance regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1d, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10438 (branch `mo-liheap-wave1d`), open, not merged. Head `2b62923ca0` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983`; this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10438 opened on 2026-10-23 with no reviews yet, so there is no revision to pin.
- **Sources missing from the corpus.** No axiom-corpus manifest on `main` holds 13 CSR 40-19.020, the LIHEAP rule (definitions, eligibility, the medical deduction, the 8% renter payment, the 2017 table); Appendix K FFY26 (the FFY2026 limits and fuel amounts); application MO 886-4576 (8-2026), the only FFY2027 source with printed values; the draft FFY2027 plan; the FFY2024 and FFY2025 plans; RSMo 660.115; 42 U.S.C. 8624; and the FY2026 SMI table (LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 4). These need ingest. Captured: the October 2025 LIHEAP Policy and Procedure Manual, the edition the branch now cites (`us-mo-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml`), the FFY2026 plan, the 2025 and 2026 poverty guidelines and the FY2027 SMI table.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-23; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10438, branch `mo-liheap-wave1d`, head `2b62923ca0` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983` and closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10428. The branch includes the 2026-10-22 review fixes (among them the source-conflict candidate for rule (14) and a wider disability list for the medical deduction) and the 2026-10-23 switch to the October 2025 manual (user decision): every manual citation now points to that edition; members left out of the household size as non-citizens have their income counted and the child support they pay deducted; earned income and `disability_benefits` of members under 18 are excluded (new list `income/adult_unearned_sources.yaml`; `income/earned_income_min_age.yaml` renamed `income/adult_age.yaml`), while their Social Security and SSI count; the earlier exclusion of members 18 or older in secondary school is gone. A comment the same day records why IRA and 401(k) withdrawals stay excluded. Everything below describes that tree; oracle fixtures will pin the merged commit.
- **Scope:** Missouri LIHEAP Energy Assistance (EA), the once-a-year regular heating payment of the Department of Social Services, Family Support Division, for FFY2026 and FFY2027: Missouri residence; household size counting citizens and qualified noncitizens; countable income of every member, including members left out of the size (earned income of members 18 or older less 20%, unearned income, Social Security net of the Part B premium, Missouri TANF, less child support paid and the $100 monthly medical deduction); the 60% state median income (SMI) limit with the federal 110% poverty floor; the $3,000 resource limit; heating cost through the household's own fuel bill or unsubsidized rent that includes heat; the subsidized-housing bar; the coal denial; the payment by heating fuel; and the renter payment of 8% of annual rent, capped at the fuel amount. Out of scope: the Energy Crisis Intervention Program (ECIP, winter and summer crisis, including equipment repair or purchase), emergency services, supplemental EA payments, cooling and weatherization.
- **Policy periods:** two verified seasons. FFY2026 heating assistance runs October 1, 2025 to May 31, 2026 (plan item 1.1, page 4); FFY2027 runs October 1, 2026 to May 31, 2027 (draft FFY2027 plan, page 4; application, page 1). Missouri variables are annual and read 1 January values: period `2026` is FFY2026 (Missouri SMI $109,229 from `2025-10-01`; the 2025 HHS guidelines through `fpg_year_lag` 1) and period `2027` is FFY2027 (SMI $113,137 from `2026-10-01`; the 2026 guidelines). State parameters carry `2017-05-30` for rule values, `2023-10-01` for values unchanged since the FFY2024 manual (fuel amounts, 60% SMI rate, 20% deduction, adult age, income lists) and `2025-10-01` for the guideline lag and the adult-only list. `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2026-2027"`. FFY2027 rests on the 8-2026 application (limits for sizes 1 to 10, unchanged amounts); the DSS copy of the FFY2027 plan reads “Saved -- with Errors”, and the Clearinghouse has no FFY2027 plan or matrix. Above ten members the model keeps 60% SMI rather than the application's $170-per-member addition (user decision 2026-10-21; interpretation 4). Earlier periods are unverified estimates by backfilling: period `2025` reads SMI $105,825 and reproduces the October 2025 manual's Appendix K ($2,751 for one person). Periods after 2027 use the uprated SMI and lagged guidelines: carried-forward estimates.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/mo/dss/liheap/`: `mo_liheap`, `mo_liheap_household_size`; `eligibility/` `mo_liheap_eligible`, `mo_liheap_income_limit`; `income/` `mo_liheap_countable_income_person` (person level), `mo_liheap_countable_income`, `mo_liheap_medical_deduction`. No new input variable. The limit reuses `liheap_smi_limit` (`gov.hhs.smi`) and the floor reuses `fpg` and `gov.hhs.liheap.fpg_floor` (1.1).
- **Parameters:** 13 files under `gov.states.mo.dss.liheap`: `amount` (by `heating_type`), `rent_share` (0.08); `eligibility/` `smi_rate` (0.6), `fpg_year_lag` (1), `resource_limit` (3,000); `income/` `earned_sources` (5 sources), `unearned_sources` (14), `adult_unearned_sources` (`disability_benefits`), `earned_income_deduction_rate` (0.2), `adult_age` (18), `medical_deduction` ($100 a month), `elderly_age` (65), `disability_benefit_sources` (8). Plus a `programs.yaml` entry, a changelog fragment and two `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml` entries (interpretations 1 and 3).
- **Tests:** 52 YAML cases in 8 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/mo/dss/liheap/` (`mo_liheap.yaml` 6, `mo_liheap_household_size.yaml` 4, `integration.yaml` 3, `eligibility/mo_liheap_eligible.yaml` 13, `eligibility/mo_liheap_income_limit.yaml` 2, `income/mo_liheap_countable_income.yaml` 5, `income/mo_liheap_countable_income_person.yaml` 10, `income/mo_liheap_medical_deduction.yaml` 9). Every case sends `heating_type`. The 2026-10-23 change rewrote person-income Cases 3 and 8, countable-income Case 5 (now $46,320) and integration Case 3 (now $45,760), and added person-income Case 10. All 52 cases passed locally on 2026-10-23 (`policyengine-core test` on the program folder, before merging `main`).

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence on axiom-corpus `main` (`dce8e44665`, 2026-10-23) was checked on 2026-10-23 against the full manifest list and the Missouri, poverty-guideline and LIHEAP manifests; the signed release was not checked. rulespec-us `main` (`115bad3183`, 2026-10-23) has `us-mo/policies/` (`cms` CHIP and Medicaid eligibility levels, `dss/snap` manual 1105, `income_tax`) and `us-mo/manual/dss/snap`, but no LIHEAP module, no `us-mo/regulations/` or `us-mo/statutes/`, and no `us/` poverty-guideline or SMI module; `us/statutes/42/` holds other sections. The paths below follow that layout. Pages are physical PDF pages: in the October 2025 manual the printed “pg.” number plus 5, in 13 CSR 40-19 the printed number minus 1.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-mo/regulations/13-csr/40-19.020/definitions` | (2)(C) disabled, (2)(D) elderly (65 for the deduction), (2)(G) household, (2)(H) monthly income, (2)(M) renter household, (2)(N) resources; (3)(A) EA (page 2) | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. Official copy, for every rule row: [13 CSR 40-19 (4/30/17), pages 2-5](https://www.sos.mo.gov/cmsimages/adrules/csr/current/13csr/13c40-19.pdf#page=2) (5 pages). |
| `us-mo/regulations/13-csr/40-19.020/eligibility` | (4) one EA a year; (6)(A)-(D) and (6)(D)1 criteria and the $100 deduction; (7)(A)-(H) ineligible households; (8) excluded individuals (page 3) | none | Same file. |
| `us-mo/regulations/13-csr/40-19.020/application-and-payments` | (9)(B)5-7 prior-month job income, self-employment, court-ordered child support (pages 3-4); (13) renter payment; (14) income ranges and payment table, not applied (page 4); amendment history, effective May 30, 2017 (page 5) | none | Same file. |
| `us-mo/policies/dss/liheap-policy-procedure-manual/ffy2026/income` | Income of the month before application, members 18 and older (pages 30-31); earned income: wages, self-employment, roomer-boarder and rent income (pages 31-32); unearned income: contributions, alimony, child support, benefits, CRP and strike benefits (pages 32-34); deductions: 20% of earned income, medical, child support paid, SMI premium (pages 36-37); exclusions: earnings and disability income of children, interest and dividends, lump sums and tax refunds, student income, other (pages 37-39) | `us-mo/manual/dss/liheap-policy-procedure-manual` | In manifest `us-mo-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml`, the edition the branch cites (129 pages, expression date 2025-10-01; its `page-N` suffix counts text-bearing pages, so N can be below the PDF page). Official copy, for every manual row: [LIHEAP Policy and Procedure Manual, October 2025 posting, pages 15, 30-44, 48, 51, 59, 62-63, 66, 82-83, 122 and 129](https://dss.mo.gov/sites/mydss/files/media/pdf/2025/10/liheap-policy-procedure-manual.pdf#page=15). |
| `.../ffy2026/eligibility` | Resources and household (pages 40-41); ineligible individuals and households, income of ineligible members counted (pages 42-43); citizenship, documents, COFA citizens (pages 43-44); disability (page 48) | `us-mo/manual/dss/liheap-policy-procedure-manual` | Same manifest. |
| `.../ffy2026/payments` | EA description (page 15); EA fuel types (page 51); Category A deduction display (page 59); payment determination and renter payment (pages 62-63); renter situation (page 66); rent actually paid and subsidized renters (pages 82-83) | `us-mo/manual/dss/liheap-policy-procedure-manual` | Same manifest. |
| `.../ffy2026/appendices` | Appendix E code sheet, denial codes M and O (page 122); Appendix K, labelled FFY 24: 60% SMI maximums (FFY2025 values) and fuel amounts (page 129) | `us-mo/manual/dss/liheap-policy-procedure-manual` | Same manifest. |
| `us-mo/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-1` | Report period and status (page 1); 1.1 dates (page 4); 1.4 no categorical eligibility, 1.8 gross income (page 5); 1.9 countable-income boxes and Other list (pages 5-7) | `us-mo/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | In manifest `us-mo-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml` (the Clearinghouse file the branch cites, expression date 2025-10-01). Official copy: [FFY2026 Detailed Model Plan, pages 1, 4-9](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/state-plans/MO_Plan_2026.pdf#page=1). Check boxes and radio buttons read from renders of pages 5-9. |
| `us-mo/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-2` | 2.1 60% SMI for all sizes; 2.2 additional requirements; 2.3 $3,000 assets test, subsidized renters, 16% for utilities in rent (page 8); 2.5 benefit variables; 2.6 minimum $153, maximum $495 (page 9) | `us-mo/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | Same manifest. |
| `us-mo/policies/dss/liheap-appendix-k/ffy2026` | 60% SMI monthly maximums for sizes 1-20 and the seven fuel amounts | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. [Appendix K, FFY 26 Income Ranges and Benefit Amounts](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/benefits-matricies/MO_BenefitMatrix_2026.docx) (Word file, one page). |
| `us-mo/policies/dss/liheap-application/mo-886-4576-2026-08` | FFY2027 dates, EA amounts, monthly limits for sizes 1-10 and the $170 note (page 1); fuels (page 3); renter questions, job income of members 18 or older (page 4); child support paid, other income (page 5); resources (page 6) | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. [Application MO 886-4576 (8-2026), pages 1 and 3-6](https://dssmanuals.mo.gov/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/liheap-application.pdf#page=1) (6 pages). |
| `us-mo/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2027-draft/section-2` | Report period and status (page 1); 1.1 dates (page 4); 1.9 (pages 5-7); 2.1, 2.3 and 2.6, unchanged from FFY2026 (pages 8-9) | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest if FFY2027 rests on it. [Draft FFY2027 plan, DSS copy, pages 1 and 4-9](https://dss.mo.gov/sites/mydss/files/media/pdf/2026/08/liheap-active-ffy2027.pdf#page=1) (report status “Saved -- with Errors”). |
| `us-mo/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2024` and `.../fy2025` | 2.3 renter payment of 16% (page 8) | none | Not in a manifest; cited only in a comment. [FFY2024 plan, page 8](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2024/state-plans/MO_Plan_2024.pdf#page=8) and [FFY2025 plan, page 8](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2025/state-plans/MO_Plan_2025.pdf#page=8). |
| `us-mo/statutes/660.115` | Utilicare renter payments, the lesser of 8% of annual rent or $100 (state fund only) | none | Not in a manifest (`us-mo-benefits-w6-statute.yaml` holds RSMo 208 and 209); cited in a comment. [RSMo 660.115](https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=660.115). |
| `us/statutes/42/8624` | (b)(2)(B) 150% FPG or 60% SMI ceiling and the 110% floor | none | Not in a manifest. The corpus LIHEAP program bundle lists `us/statute/42/8621` with no manifest named; check for `us/statute/42/8624` before ingest. The branch cites Cornell LII; official copy: [42 U.S.C. 8624, 2024 edition, pages 1-2](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2024-title42/pdf/USCODE-2024-title42-chap94-subchapII-sec8624.pdf#page=1). |
| `us/` poverty guidelines module | 2025 guidelines ($15,650 and $5,500) behind every FFY2026 floor; 2026 guidelines ($15,960 and $5,680) for FFY2027; 2024 guidelines for the period 2025 estimate | `us/guidance/hhs/aspe/poverty-guidelines/2025/federal-register`, `.../2026/federal-register`, `.../2024/federal-register` | 2024 and 2025 in `us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml` (HTML editions); 2026 in `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml`. PDF copies: [90 FR 5917, page 1](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-17/pdf/2025-01377.pdf#page=1) and [91 FR 1798, page 2](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-01-15/pdf/2026-00755.pdf#page=2). The `fpg_year_lag` reference, [LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 2](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_IM2025-02_FPGSte-Table_Att2.pdf#page=1), is in no manifest. |
| `us/` SMI module | Missouri four-person SMI and 60% SMI by size; 45 CFR 96.85(b) size percentages | `us/guidance/acf/ocs/liheap-im/2026-01/attachment-4-smi-table` (FY2027 only) | FY2027 table in `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml`. The FY2026 table is in no manifest (the program bundle lists it without a citation path): [LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 4, pages 2 and 6](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_IM2025-02_SMIStateTable_Att4.pdf#page=2). FY2027: [Attachment 4, pages 2 and 5](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_Att4SMITable_States_FY2027.pdf#page=2). 45 CFR 96.85 is listed in the program bundle as `us/regulation/45/96/85` with no manifest. |

The FFY2024 manual (updated 10/2023), which the branch cited until 2026-10-23, is no longer cited and is in no manifest; the passages that changed are quoted below from [LIHEAP Policy and Procedures Manual, FFY2024, pages 23-24 and 42](https://mydss.mo.gov/sites/mydss/files/media/pdf/2023/10/liheap-manual.pdf#page=23).

## Source text (verbatim)

Quotations come from the official files above (pdftotext, line breaks collapsed; the Appendix K Word file converted to text). Plan check boxes and radio buttons come from renders of plan pages 5 to 9. Below, the manual is the October 2025 manual unless the FFY2024 manual is named.

**Program and dates.** 13 CSR 40-19.020(3)(A), page 2: “Energy Assistance (EA), which provides a direct one (1) time lump sum payment of utility costs incurred for home heating by qualified Missouri residents continuing so long as funds remain available for this purpose.” Rule (4), page 3: “Not more than one (1) LIHEAP qualified EA benefit will be paid for each qualified individual eligible household, with the exception of a possible additional supplemental payment, during any LIHEAP fiscal year.” History, page 5: “Amended: Filed Sept. 21, 2016, effective May 30, 2017.” Plan page 1: “Report Period: 10/01/2025 to 09/30/2026” and status “Submission Accepted by CO”; page 4, item 1.1: heating assistance “10/01/2025” to “05/31/2026”, and “Energy Assistance: 10/1/25 (Elderly/Disabled applications, remaining application 11/1/25 - 5/31/2026)”. Manual page 51: “DSS will only pay EA as a one-time payment towards one (1) fuel type per program year.” Draft FFY2027 plan page 1: “Report Period: 10/01/2026 to 09/30/2027” and “Report Status: Saved -- with Errors”. Application page 1: “Send your application on or after October 1, 2026, if: Any member of your household is age 60 or over, or if any household member is disabled.” and “The last day to apply for EA is May 31, 2027.”

**Household and members.** Rule (2)(G), page 2, defines “Household”: “shall be defined as an individual(s) living in private living quarters (a space with a private entrance) for which residential heat is purchased in common.” Rule (6), page 3: “(A) All household members must be a citizen of the United States or be a legal permanent resident admitted to the United States for permanent residence status and a current resident of Missouri;” Rule (8): “(8) Individuals meeting any of the following conditions shall not be included in a LIHEAP household: (A) Individuals that are not citizens of the United States or a legal permanent resident;” and “(D) Individuals defined as roomers, boarders, or live-in-attendants;”. Manual page 40: “Household is defined as an individual(s) living in private living quarters (a space with a private entrance) for which residential heat-cooling is purchased in common.” Page 42 lists among ineligible individuals “Not a citizen of the United States or a Legal Permanent Resident.”; the same page speaks of households “with ineligible household members”. Pages 42-43: “Any income made available to the household by an ineligible individual, including individuals that are ineligible because they are not citizens of the United States, or … a legal permanent resident must be included in the household income.” (the ellipsis marks the page break). Page 43: “Each household member must either be a citizen of the United States or admitted for legal permanent residence.”, “Exclude individuals not meeting these criteria from the household count. | 11 | Medical deduction (`income/mo_liheap_medical_deduction.yaml` Cases 1-9) | Period 2026: applicant 65; applicant 64; spouse 48, `is_disabled`, SSI $11,928; applicant 50, `is_disabled`, private disability $18,000 only; applicant 52, `is_blind`, `social_security_disability` $18,000; dependent grandparent 74 with adults 45 and 43; couple 70 and 67; citizen 60 with undocumented spouse 67; applicant 45, `is_disabled`, `medicaid` $21,297 only | Elderly is 65 or older; disabled is disabled or blind and receiving a listed benefit (SSI, Social Security disability, Medical Assistance); one $100 a month per household; only the applicant or spouse counts; a non-citizen spouse is outside the household. | 1,200; 0; 1,200; 0; 1,200; 0; 1,200 (not 2,400); 0; 1,200 | Rule (2)(C), (2)(D), (6)(D)1; manual pp. 36, 43, 48 (interpretations 7 and 11) |
| 12 | Earned income and age rules (`income/mo_liheap_countable_income_person.yaml` Cases 1-4, 9 and 10; `mo_liheap.yaml` Case 6) | (a) Wages $31,200. (b) Parent 40 (wages $31,200) and member 17 (wages $6,000, `social_security_survivors` $9,600). (c) Parent 46 with no income and a dependent aged 18 in high school (`is_in_secondary_school`), wages $7,800. (d) `self_employment_income` $24,000, `farm_operations_income` -$3,000. (e) Head 25 in GED classes, wages $58,240, child 6, NATURAL_GAS. (f) Period 2027: parent 41 (wages $41,600, bank $900), member 16 (wages $5,200); KEROSENE, `fuel_oil_expense` $1,500. (g) Parent 44 with `disability_benefits` $18,000; member 17 with `disability_benefits` $1,440 and `social_security_survivors` $9,600 | (a) 31,200 x 0.8 = 24,960. (b) Earned income under 18 is excluded; SSA income counts: 24,960 and 9,600. (c) Only earned income under 18 is excluded, and 18 is not under 18; school attendance no longer matters: 7,800 x 0.8 = 6,240. (d) Losses are not included: 24,000 x 0.8 = 19,200. (e) 58,240 x 0.8 = 46,592 > 3,714 x 12 = 44,568; the floor, 23,265, does not apply. (f) 41,600 x 0.8 = 33,280 <= 3,847 x 12 = 46,164; kerosene $153. (g) The adult's disability payments count: 18,000. The minor's $1,440 is “Unearned income from disability” and is excluded; the $9,600 is SSA income and counts. | (a) $24,960; (b) $24,960 and $9,600; (c) $0 and $6,240; (d) $19,200; (e) $46,592, not eligible, $0; (f) $33,280, $153; (g) $18,000 and $9,600 | Manual pp. 32, 36, 38; plan item 1.9; application p. 4 (interpretation 8) |
| 13 | Unearned income and deductions (`income/mo_liheap_countable_income_person.yaml` Cases 5-7; `income/mo_liheap_countable_income.yaml` Cases 1, 2 and 4) | Period 2026: (a) ages 72 and 66, Social Security $23,400 and $1,800, Part B $2,434.80 each, the second with pension $6,000; (b) age 38: unemployment $6,000, child support received $4,800, `financial_assistance` $1,200, taxable interest $300; age 41: `military_retirement_pay` $24,000, VA $6,000; (c) age 45, `is_disabled`, SSI $11,928; (d) adult 27 with child support received $2,400, children 6 and 3, `mo_tanf` $3,504; (e) age 35, wages $31,200, child support paid $4,800; (f) age 24, wages $6,240, child support paid $6,000 | (a) 23,400 - 2,434.80 = 20,965.20; max(1,800 - 2,434.80, 0) + 6,000 = 6,000. (b) 6,000 + 4,800 + 1,200 = 12,000, interest excluded; 24,000 + 6,000 = 30,000. (c) 994 x 12 = 11,928. (d) 3,504 + 2,400 = 5,904. (e) 24,960 - 4,800 = 20,160. (f) 6,240 x 0.8 = 4,992 - 6,000, floored at 0. | (a) $20,965.20 and $6,000; (b) $12,000 and $30,000; (c) $11,928; (d) $5,904; (e) $20,160; (f) $0 | Plan item 1.9; manual pp. 33, 36, 38; application p. 5 (interpretations 9, 10 and 12) |

No branch test disagrees with these derivations. Test 4 depends on interpretation 3, test 5 on 14, test 6 on 2, test 8(b) on 7, tests 12(b) and 12(g) on 8, test 13(a) on 10 and test 13(b) on 9.

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Rule payment table against current agency values (source conflict; user decision 2026-10-22).** Rule (6)(D) ties eligibility to the ranges of section (14), 0 to 135% of the poverty level, and (14) prints payments that fall by range. The FFY2026 plan, Appendix K, the October 2025 manual, the draft FFY2027 plan and the 8-2026 application set 60% of SMI for every size and one amount per fuel. The branch applies the agency values; (14) says payments use “metrics established by the division”. Under the rule table, companion test 1 (124% of the guideline, range E) pays $221 for natural gas, and test 10 (176%) is ineligible. Candidate `us-mo:liheap-rule-income-ranges-and-payments` (unreviewed) records this; the code carries no `# Source conflict` marker until registration.
2. **Renter payment rate and base (source conflict; user decision 2026-10-21).** Rule (13) sets “no more than eight percent”; the manual (page 63), the FFY2024 to FFY2026 plans and the draft FFY2027 plan describe 16%. The branch applies 8% (rule over manual and plan), capped at the household's fuel amount (page 63). Unlike interpretation 1, the rule governs here. RSMo 660.115.2 caps Utilicare state-fund renter payments at the lesser of 8% of rent or $100; EA uses federal funds, and the branch does not apply the $100. The base is `pre_subsidy_rent`, the regular monthly rental charge times 12 (rule (13); page 63); page 82 uses the rent actually paid, the same for the unsubsidized renters the branch makes eligible. The note on the rule-ranges candidate records the rate choice.
3. **Federal 110% floor.** 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B) bars excluding a household on income below 110% of the poverty guideline. The 60% SMI limits fall below that floor from size 16 in both years, so the branch admits a household whose income is below 1.1 times the lagged guideline (rounded to cents, strict “less than”). Candidate `us-mo:liheap-110-percent-poverty-floor` (unreviewed) records it; no Missouri source mentions the floor.
4. **FFY2027 limits above ten members (user decision 2026-10-21).** The application adds $170 a month for each member above 10. 60% SMI, divided by 12 and rounded, gives the same $8,316 for 11 members but $1 to $2 a month less for 12 to 15 ($8,485, $8,655, $8,825, $8,994 against $8,486, $8,656, $8,826, $8,996); from 16 the federal floor governs. The branch keeps 60% SMI until an FFY2027 Appendix K is published.
5. **Monthly limits and annual income (inferred rounding; simplification).** The published maximums equal the HHS 60% SMI amount for the size divided by 12 and rounded to the nearest dollar, half up (FFY2027 size 1: 35,298 / 12 = 2,941.50, printed $2,942); this reproduces all 30 rows but is not stated. Missouri counts the income of the month before application (rule (9)(B)5; manual pages 30-31); the branch compares annual countable income with 12 times the monthly maximum.
6. **Household and citizenship (proxies).** The SPM unit stands in for the household buying heat in common. `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant` stands in for the rule's “citizen of the United States or be a legal permanent resident”; the manual (page 44) also accepts an I-94 marked refugee, parolee or asylum, and the model's list adds deportation withheld, Cuban/Haitian entrant and conditional entrant. COFA citizens, eligible from March 9, 2024 (page 44), have no matching model status. Rule (6)(A) requires all members to be citizens, while (8)(A) and the manual exclude the member; the branch excludes the member from the size. A non-citizen applicant makes the case ineligible, and a refusal to document makes the household ineligible (page 43); the model has no applicant or refusal input. Roomers, boarders, live-in attendants and absent members are not identified.
7. **Members left out as non-citizens (readings; user decision 2026-10-23).** Following the October 2025 manual (pages 42-43), their income counts; the FFY2024 manual (pages 23-24) excluded it. The branch also deducts the child support they pay: page 36 deducts payments “paid by any household member to someone not included in the LIHEAP household”, and page 42 calls these members “ineligible household members”. A reading that treats them as outside the household would deny the deduction (companion test 8(b): $49,920 instead of $46,320). The medical deduction still requires a citizen or qualified-noncitizen applicant or spouse: page 36 is silent on a spouse left out of the household, and a non-citizen applicant makes the case ineligible (page 43); companion test 11's undocumented spouse aged 67 gives no deduction.
8. **Members under 18 (readings; user decision 2026-10-23).** Page 38 excludes earned income and “Unearned income from disability” of members under 18 but counts their “SSA income”. The branch excludes earned income and `disability_benefits` (private short- and long-term disability) under 18, and counts Social Security and SSI at any age, reading SSI as SSA income. A child's SSI is paid on the basis of disability, so reading it as disability income would exclude it. A minor's veterans benefits, workers' compensation and `mo_ssp` count. The FFY2024 manual's exclusion for members 18 or older in high school, GED classes or home school (page 42) is gone, matching plan item 1.9.
9. **Interest, dividends, contributions and withdrawals (plan against manual; user decisions 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-23).** Plan item 1.9 checks “Interest, dividends, or royalties” and leaves cash gifts unchecked; the manual excludes interest and dividends (page 38) and counts contributions (page 33), and the application asks for money received from friends, family or organizations. The branch follows the manual. Capital gains are excluded as lump sums (page 38), although page 32 lists the Form 1040 capital gains line among self-employment documents. IRA and 401(k) withdrawals are not counted: the sources are silent, and IRA and Keogh balances count as resources (rule (2)(N); page 40).
10. **Social Security and Medicare (settled).** Plan item 1.9 checks “Excluding MediCare deduction”, and the manual deducts the SMI (Part B) premium for B and C case members paying it (page 36). The branch counts `social_security` net of the computed `medicare_part_b_premium`, floored at zero per person; a Part B premium paid by a member without Social Security (for example a railroad beneficiary) is not deducted. The October 2025 deduction list no longer names Medicare Part D, which the FFY2024 manual deducted, though page 59 still calls the Category A SMI and Part D figures “these deductions”; the branch deducts no Part D premium.
11. **Medical deduction proxies.** The tax-unit head and spouse who are citizens or qualified noncitizens stand in for the applicant and spouse. Disabled means `is_disabled` or `is_blind` with a positive listed benefit (rule (2)(C); page 48); the general veterans, railroad and Social Security dependent and survivor inputs stand in for the disability forms of those benefits and also catch benefits paid for other reasons. Civil Service Disability and Black Lung have no input; `medicaid`, a per-capita value, is read as receipt. The $100 is monthly by inference from rule (2)(H).
12. **Earned income, TANF, veterans benefits and child support (simplifications).** The 20% deduction comes from the manual, not the rule or plan. Each earned source is floored at zero, with net self-employment, partnership and farm inputs for the Form 1040 lines (“don’t include if a loss”); roomer-boarder income has no input. Missouri TANF counts as computed (`mo_tanf`; plan 1.9 checked). Page 34 heads the documentation list with “Veterans Administration Disability Benefits”, while the plan checks VA benefits and the application lists veterans benefits; the branch counts all `veterans_benefits`. The application deducts court-ordered child support paid outside the household, and rule (9)(B)7 asks for that amount; the manual deducts all child support paid to someone outside the household except lump sums; the branch deducts all `child_support_expense`. Foster care, adoption subsidies, allotments, royalties, installment and insurance payments have no input.
13. **Rent income (source structure).** The October 2025 manual places “Roomer-Boarder / Rent Income:”, including rent from land or buildings, under “Earned Income and Documentation:” (pages 31-32), and treats CRP payments as rental income (page 34), while its 20% deduction names roomer-boarder and self-employment income but not rent (page 36). The branch keeps `rental_income` and `farm_rent_income` unearned, without the 20% deduction; reading rent as earned would cut it by 20%. No companion test uses rent.
14. **Fuels (settled and inferred; user decision 2026-10-21).** `heating_type` is a required input; UNSPECIFIED pays $0 (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the default). PROPANE is paid as tank propane; cylinder propane ($177) is unreachable. SOLAR is paid at the electric amount, by inference from plan item 2.5. OTHER has no printed row: eligible, $0. COAL is denied (code O). NONE has no heating cost. Self-cut wood (rule (7)(G)) is not identified.
15. **Resources (proxy).** `spm_unit_cash_assets` (bank, stock and bond assets) stands in for resources; IRAs, Keoghs, deferred compensation and annuities (rule (2)(N); the manual's page 40 list omits annuities) have no asset input, and the subtraction of tax refunds from resources (page 38) is not modeled.
16. **Heating responsibility and housing (proxies).** `has_heating_expense` stands in for an account in the household's name or a landlord bill. Subsidized means `receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing`; with heat in rent it bars the household, with its own fuel bill it does not. The rule (7)(B), (C), (E), (F) and (H) exclusions have no inputs.
17. **Appendix labels (source wording).** The manual's Appendix K (page 129) is still labelled “FFY 24” and prints the FFY2025 limits ($2,751 for one person), and its renter text (page 63) points to Appendix E, now the code sheet. The branch takes FFY2026 limits from Appendix K FFY26 and FFY2027 limits from the application; fuel amounts agree in every source.
18. **Years and dates (simplification).** Annual periods read 1 January values, so period 2026 applies FFY2026 to all of 2026, including October to December 2026 in FFY2027. FFY2027 rests on the 8-2026 application and the unaccepted draft plan. Earlier and later periods are estimates (see Policy periods).
19. **Other gaps.** The one EA per year rule, supplemental EA payments, application windows and priority, Category A (SNAP) income from FAMIS, overpayment recovery, supplier participation and funding availability are not modeled.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-mo-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-mo-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [us-mo-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-mo-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml) (the October 2025 manual, the edition the branch cites)
- [us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml) (2025 guidelines, FFY2026 floor; 2024 for the period 2025 estimate)
- [us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml) (2026 guidelines and the FY2027 SMI table)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-mo/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the FFY2026 limits for sizes 1 to 20 and the FFY2027 limits for sizes 1 to 10 with the inclusive ceiling, the rounding of 60% SMI to the published dollar, the 110% floor at size 16 and its strict edge, the $3,000 resource edge, citizens and qualified noncitizens in size, with the income of members left out counted and their child support paid deducted, the 20% earned income deduction with per-source loss floors, the under-18 exclusion of earned income and disability payments with Social Security and SSI counted at any age, every counted and excluded source, Social Security net of the Part B premium, Missouri TANF, child support paid, the $100 monthly medical deduction with the age 65 edge and each disability benefit, all seven fuel amounts and the treatment of solar, other, coal, no heat and unspecified fuel, the 8% renter payment below and at the fuel cap, subsidized housing with heat in rent or its own bill, and any period before 2026 or after 2027 kept in scope. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: LIHEAP wave 1d: encode New Mexico LIHEAP regular heating assistance

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Objective

Ship New Mexico LIHEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1d, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10431 (branch `nm-liheap-wave1d`), open, not merged. Head `cb11d7d132` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983`; this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10431 opened on 2026-10-23 with no reviews yet, so there is no revision to pin.
- **Sources missing from the corpus.** No axiom-corpus manifest on `main` holds the program's rule, 8.150 NMAC, the Health Care Authority (HCA) LIHEAP rule effective July 1, 2024. Its parts 100, 110, 410, 510, 520 and 620 define the household, heating responsibility, housing, citizenship, countable income and every point. Also missing: the FFY2027 Point and Income Guidelines ($40 a point, the $298 allowance and the FFY2027 tables), the FFY2027 ISD 017 card, the accepted FY2027 Detailed Model Plan, LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 2 (cited for the guideline year) and the LHP 602 application (the highest monthly bill). These need ingest. Captured on `main`: the FY2026 plan, the FFY2026 Point and Income Guide and the FY2026 ISD 017 card (in a SNAP manifest), each the file the code cites, and the 2024, 2025 and 2026 HHS poverty guidelines. No manifest holds a different edition of a cited source.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-23; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10431, branch `nm-liheap-wave1d`, head `cb11d7d132` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983` and closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10421. The branch includes the 2026-10-22 review fixes: `retirement_distributions` joined the unearned income list (8.150.520.13 A), with a new case (`nm_liheap.yaml` Case 21); five cases that repeated another case's equivalence class were removed; the changelog fragment now says regular heating; and the source-conflict backlog note names the deciding parameter. Everything below describes the branch with those fixes; oracle fixtures will pin the merged commit.
- **Scope:** New Mexico LIHEAP regular heating assistance, the one benefit a household receives each federal fiscal year, for FFY2026 and FFY2027: New Mexico residence; a household with at least one citizen or qualified noncitizen, sized by those members; proration of an ineligible noncitizen's income; gross countable income (earnings of members over 18, unearned income of all members, TANF); the 150% income limit; heating responsibility (a heating bill, gathered or bought wood, heat in rent, subsidized housing); and the point system: energy burden points with the energy standard allowance, the propane points, income points at the 110% cutoff and vulnerable-member points, times the point value. Out of scope: crisis and life-threatening crisis intervention, including the net-income test for households over the limit (8.150.520.16 to 8.150.520.19); households with only a cooling cost, and the use of the annual benefit for cooling; supplemental benefits at the secretary's direction; weatherization; heating equipment repair or replacement; and tribal LIHEAP.
- **Policy periods:** New Mexico's program year is the federal fiscal year, with applications taken from October 1 to September 30 (8.150.110.9 C; plan item 1.1, page 4: heating assistance 10/01/2025 to 09/30/2026). FFY2026 runs on the 2025 HHS guidelines, mandatory for LIHEAP from October 1, 2025 (LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 2), and FFY2027 on the 2026 guidelines; `fpg_year_lag` is 1. All 15 parameter files hold a `2025-10-01` entry; `payment/point_value.yaml` adds $40 and `payment/energy_standard_allowance.yaml` adds $298 on `2026-10-01`. New Mexico variables are annual and read 1 January values, so period `2026` is FFY2026 ($35 a point, $291 allowance, 2025 guidelines) and period `2027` is FFY2027 ($40, $298, 2026 guidelines). `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2026-2027"`. Earlier periods take the FFY2026 values by backfilling, on the lagged guideline (period `2025` on the 2024 guidelines): unverified estimates. Later periods carry the FFY2027 values forward on the lagged guideline (period `2028` on the model's 2027 guidelines): carried-forward estimates. No estimated value was approved for this state.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/nm/hca/liheap/`: `nm_liheap`, `nm_liheap_household_size`; `eligibility/` `nm_liheap_eligible`, `nm_liheap_income_limit`; `income/` `nm_liheap_countable_income`. No new input variable. The energy, propane, income and vulnerable points are computed inside `nm_liheap`.
- **Parameters:** 15 files under `gov.states.nm.hca.liheap`: `eligibility/` `fpg_rate` (1.5), `fpg_year_lag` (1); `income/` `earned_income_age` (18), `sources/earned` (5 sources), `sources/unearned` (20 sources); `payment/` `energy_burden_points` (single-amount scale: 0 from 0, 1 from 0.06, 2 from 0.11, 3 from 0.16), `energy_standard_allowance` ($291 a month, $298 from 2026-10-01), `propane_points` (2), `income_points/low` (3), `income_points/high` (2), `income_points/low_income_fpg_rate` (1.1), `vulnerable_points` (2), `young_child_max_age` (5), `elderly_age` (60), `point_value` ($35, $40 from 2026-10-01). Plus a `programs.yaml` entry, a changelog fragment and the `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml` backlog entry `us-nm:liheap-three-income-points` (interpretation 1).
- **Tests:** 46 YAML cases in 4 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/nm/hca/liheap/` (`nm_liheap.yaml` 21, `eligibility/nm_liheap_eligible.yaml` 12, `eligibility/nm_liheap_income_limit.yaml` 6, `income/nm_liheap_countable_income.yaml` 7). Every case sends `heating_type`. A local run on 2026-10-22 passed the 50 cases then present, before the 2026-10-22 review fixes; the fixed files were not re-run. CI validates them.

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence on axiom-corpus `main` (`dce8e44665`, 2026-10-23) was checked on 2026-10-23 against the full manifest list, by reading every `us-nm-*` manifest and the federal poverty-guideline and LIHEAP manifests, and by GitHub code search of `manifests/` for each source URL; presence in the signed release was not checked. rulespec-us `main` (`115bad3183`, 2026-10-23) has `us-nm/policies/cms` (Medicaid and CHIP eligibility levels), `us-nm/policies/income_tax` and `us-nm/statutes/7-2-5` and `7-2-18`, but no `us-nm/regulations/` tree, no HCA or LIHEAP module, and no `us/` poverty-guideline module; the paths below follow that layout. NMAC parts are HTML pages without page numbers; PDF pages are physical pages.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-nm/regulations/nmac/8/150/100` | 8.150.100.9 C (no categorical eligibility), D (150% of the guideline), E (110% floor); 8.150.100.10 A(3) (gathered wood), A(5) (homeless applicants) | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. [8.150.100 NMAC](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title08/08.150.0100.html). |
| `us-nm/regulations/nmac/8/150/110` | 8.150.110.8 D (one benefit each federal fiscal year; benefit from another grantee), E (supplemental benefit); 8.150.110.9 C (application period) | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. [8.150.110 NMAC](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title08/08.150.0110.html). |
| `us-nm/regulations/nmac/8/150/410` | 8.150.410.8 (household); .9 A to D (energy cost, gathered wood, direct or indirect cost); .11 A to C (housing type, subsidized rent); .12 (tribal); .13 (citizenship); .14 (residency); .15 (enumeration); .16 (facilities) | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. [8.150.410 NMAC](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title08/08.150.0410.html). |
| `us-nm/regulations/nmac/8/150/510` | 8.150.510.8 (no assets test) | none | Not in a corpus manifest; needs ingest. [8.150.510 NMAC](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title08/08.150.0510.html). |

## Source text (verbatim)

Quotations come from the official files above (NMAC from the SRCA HTML pages; PDFs through pdftotext, line breaks collapsed). Plan check-box and radio states come from page images, not the text layer. NMAC section numbers are the rule's own; the rule has no page numbers.

**Program, year and one benefit.** 8.150.110.8 D: “Each eligible household will be issued one benefit each federal fiscal year.” and “Receipt of a LIHEAP benefit from any other LIHEAP administering entity (tribe, state or territory) funded by HHS during any federal fiscal year would prohibit the receipt of LIHEAP in New Mexico during that FFY.” 8.150.110.8 E: “A supplemental benefit may be established under certain conditions at the direction of the HCA secretary.” 8.150.110.9 C: “The application period is October 1st through September 30th for each federal fiscal year.” 8.150.520.15: “Income guidelines for eligibility will be updated at the beginning of each federal fiscal year as required by federal statute.” and “The guidelines will be effective for the entire federal fiscal year beginning October 1 and ending September 30.” FY2026 plan, page 1: “Report Period: 10/01/2025 to 09/30/2026” and “Report Status: Submission Accepted by CO”; page 4, item 1.1, heating assistance from 10/01/2025 to 09/30/2026. FY2027 plan, page 1: “Report Period: 10/01/2026 to 09/30/2027”. LHP 602, page 2: “Do you need LIHEAP for:” Heating or Cooling (one box each); page 3: “Please choose one heating or cooling energy bill that you want help with and attach proof of the expense.” FFY2027 guidelines: “LIHEAP helps eligible New Mexico households with home heating and cooling costs.”

**Household and members.** 8.150.410.8: “For purposes of LIHEAP, a household is an individual, or group of individuals living together, who incurs a heating or cooling cost.” 8.150.410.13: “To be eligible, a LIHEAP household must contain at least one member who is a (1) U.S. citizen, or (2) a qualified non-citizen considered eligible to participate in the TANF program.” 8.150.410.15: “To be eligible for inclusion in the LIHEAP benefit group, a social security number (SSN) or proof of application for a number must be provided for each citizen and qualified non-citizen for which assistance is being requested.” and “Any member(s) of a LIHEAP applicant household who do not meet the requirements of this section will not be eligible for a LIHEAP benefit.” 8.150.520.10: “The gross income received by any ineligible non-citizen household member must be prorated and counted to establish the benefit amount.” 8.150.520.10 B: “Calculate the gross income of the ineligible non-citizen and divide the total by the number of members, eligible and ineligible, in the household.” and “To determine the portion of the income to be counted, multiply the pro rata portion by the remaining number of eligible household members.” 8.150.410.16: “Persons residing in New Mexico but living in group homes, halfway houses, institutions, homeless shelters, or in places not normally intended for human occupation are not eligible unless they can document heating/cooling expenses.”

**Residence, tribes, categorical eligibility and assets.** 8.150.410.14: “To be eligible, a LIHEAP household must have a residence in New Mexico and be occupying that residence at the time of application.” 8.150.410.12 A: “Indian tribal members living on their tribe's tribal lands, whose tribe administers their own LIHEAP program, are not eligible for HCA-administered LIHEAP benefits.” 8.150.100.9 C: “No household is categorically eligible to receive LIHEAP.” 8.150.510.8: “No assets test is required to be eligible for LIHEAP benefits.” FY2026 plan, page 5: items 1.4 (categorical eligibility), 1.5 (automatic enrollment) and 1.7a (SNAP nominal payments) answered No; page 9: item 2.2 (additional eligibility requirements) No; “Do you require an Assets test?” No.
