**Countable income.** FY2026 plan, page 5, item 1.8: Gross Income checked. 8.150.520.12: “Gross income of the household member is defined as all income received prior to deductions, including taxes, garnishments, whether voluntary or involuntary and net business income.” 8.150.520.12 B: “The gross unearned income of all household members is counted in its entirety, and the gross earned income of all household members over the age of 18 is counted in its entirety, unless:” the income is exempt, self-employment, an ineligible noncitizen's, or weekly or biweekly: “income received on a weekly basis is averaged and multiplied by four;” and “income received on a biweekly basis is averaged and multiplied by two;”. 8.150.520.12 C: “HCA shall establish income by utilizing the gross income of the household for the 30 day period immediately preceding the date on which LIHEAP eligibility is determined by ISD.”

8.150.520.8 A: “Earned gross income is defined as income received in the form of wages paid on a predetermined regular basis, pay received irregularly for work performed irregularly, or income resulting from self-employment activities.” and “Income from rental property, if 20 hours or more per week are spent working as a landlord, is also countable as earned income.” 8.150.520.9 C: “For self-employment income, the net income of the business activity is considered the gross income of the household member.” and “The net income of the business is derived by subtracting the allowable costs of doing business from the business's gross income.” 8.150.520.9 D(2) disallows, among other costs, “net losses from previous periods” and depreciation.

8.150.520.13 A: “Unearned income is income received in the form of entitlement, disability, retirement, unemployment benefits or payments, including but not limited to the following:” child support; alimony; “temporary assistance to needy families (TANF) benefits”; “general assistance (GA) payments”; royalties; dividends and interest; tribal benefits. 8.150.520.13 B: “The gross amount of the benefit or payment must be counted. In the case of OASDI benefits, the gross amount of the benefit includes the amount deducted for the medicare premium, if applicable.” 8.150.520.13 C: “Monthly payments resulting from the sale of property and contributions from family or friends are also countable unearned income.” 8.150.520.13 D excludes in-kind benefits, vendor payments, “lump sum payments: as defined in food stamp regulations at 8.139.520.9 NMAC”, loans, “charitable contributions from nonprofit agencies to meet household expenses”, earned income tax credits, the value of food stamps, the TANF annual clothing allowance, “monies received for the care of a third party beneficiary who is not a household member” and monies excluded by federal statute; 8.150.520.8 B repeats the list, with “lump sum payments: see food stamp regulations on lump sum payments in 8.139.520.9 NMAC”.

FY2026 plan item 1.9 (pages 5-6, page images), checked: wages, self-employment, contract income, payments from mortgage or sales contracts, unemployment insurance, “Social Security Administration (SSA ) benefits” with “Excluding MediCare deduction” checked and the Including MediCare deduction box unchecked, SSI, “Retirement / pension benefits”, general assistance, TANF, “One-time lump-sum payments, such as rebates/credits, winnings from lotteries, refund deposits, etc.”, rental income, Workforce Investment Act employment, work study, alimony, child support, “Interest, dividends, or royalties”, commissions, legal settlements, VA benefits, “Funds received by household for the care of a foster child” and “Ameri-Corp Program payments for living allowances, earnings, and in-kind aid”. Unchecked include strike pay, loans, cash gifts, the savings account balance, jury duty, both insurance payment rows, “Earned income of a child under the age of 18”, “Balance of retirement, pension, or annuity accounts where funds cannot be withdrawn without a penalty.”, income tax refunds and senior companion stipends. The FY2027 plan's item 1.9 (pages 5-6) has the same boxes checked.

**Heating responsibility and housing.** 8.150.410.9 A: “To be eligible for LIHEAP benefits, the household must incur an energy cost.” and “The energy cost may be for a primary heat source, i.e., the energy source or fuel with which the household is predominantly heated, or for a secondary heat source.” 8.150.410.9 C: “Households who use wood as a fuel to heat their home and gather the wood themselves are considered to have a heating responsibility.” 8.150.410.9 D: “The heating/cooling cost may be direct in the form of a utility payment or fuel purchase, or indirect in the form of a non-subsidized rent payment which either designates or does not designate the included utility cost, or costs associated with obtaining wood for heating households.” 8.150.100.10 A(3): “With the exception of households that use wood as their primary heat source and gather their own wood supply, households that do not incur a direct or indirect home energy cost are not eligible.” 8.150.100.10 A(5): “Homeless applicants who meet the eligibility criteria are eligible for benefits under this program.” and “Applicants who do not incur an energy cost will not be allowed an energy burden as defined in Paragraph (1) of Subsection A of 8.150.620.9 NMAC.”

8.150.410.11 A(2): “Households paying non-subsidized rent whose utility costs are included in their rent, even if no such cost is designated, are eligible for LIHEAP.” 8.150.410.11 B: “Subsidized rent assistance is defined as a payment for shelter, or shelter and utilities, the cost of which has been reduced due to a subsidy from a housing or other assistance program.” and “University housing does not meet this definition and is therefore not considered subsidized housing.” B(1): “Households receiving subsidized rent assistance who incur a separate direct cost for heating/cooling are eligible for LIHEAP benefits”. B(2): “Households receiving subsidized rent assistance who receive a subsidy for utilities but who incur an additional out-of-pocket expense for utilities are eligible for LIHEAP”. B(3): “Households receiving subsidized rent assistance whose heating/cooling cost is included in their subsidized rent and do not incur an additional out-of-pocket heating or cooling expense are not eligible for LIHEAP”. B(4): “Households receiving subsidized rent assistance who pay rent but do not pay utilities are not eligible for LIHEAP”. B(5): “Households receiving subsidized rent assistance who pay no rent and no utilities are not eligible for LIHEAP”. 8.150.410.11 C: “Households who pay a mortgage or own their own home and incur a separate heating/cooling cost are eligible for LIHEAP.” FY2026 plan, page 9, item 2.3, answers Yes for renters in subsidized housing: “Households that receive a utility subsidy but still have out-of-pocket utility costs (e.g., electricity, gas) are eligible for LIHEAP.” and “Households whose heating or cooling costs are fully included in the subsidized rent and who do not pay separately for utilities are not eligible for LIHEAP.”; and Yes for renters with utilities in rent.

**Benefit rule.** 8.150.620.8: “A point allocation system is used to ensure that the highest level of assistance is provided to those households with the highest energy needs, lowest income and largest household member size while giving priority to those households with vulnerable members.” 8.150.620.9: “To determine the amount of the benefit for households with an energy cost, HCA assigns points for each following factors.” 8.150.620.10 A: “Households eligible for a LIHEAP benefit will have their point total multiplied times the point value.” 8.150.620.10 B: “Based on the availability of funds, benefits are issued for eligible applications received through September 30.” 8.150.620.10 C: “At the direction of the HCA secretary, the point value for energy cost points, income points, vulnerable population points, additional energy burden points, or any of their parts, may be adjusted as necessary taking into consideration the factors described in Subsection A of 8.150.620.10 NMAC.”

Energy points. 8.150.620.9 A: “Points are assigned based on the energy burden at the household's current residence for households that have a direct cost for heating or cooling expenses.” A(1) defines energy burden as “the expenditures of the household for home energy divided by the income of the household.” and continues: “Points are assigned to the household by determining the households' percentage of energy burden.” and “(a) Zero points for zero to five percent energy burden; (b) One point for six to ten percent energy burden; (c) Two points for eleven to fifteen percent energy burden; or (d) Three points for sixteen percent or more energy burden.” A(2): “If the household's energy burden is for the use of propane, an additional two points will be allocated.” A(3): “Certain households do not receive energy burden points:” “households whose utilities are included in the rent” and “households that use wood to heat their home and do not purchase wood”. A(4): “Each year an ESA will be determined.” “The standard amount will be based on the fuel and electricity standards calculated for the standard utility allowance (SUA) used in the New Mexico supplemental nutrition assistance program (SNAP).” and “The ESA may be used when the monthly utility costs provided by the applicant are: a) less than the standard; or b) the applicant has new service and costs are not available.” FFY2026 guide: “Highest Energy Bill divided by income”; “16% or greater 3 Points”, 11% - 15% 2 Points, 6% - 10% 1 Point, “5% <” 0 Points; “Propane additional 2 Points”; “Energy Standard Allowance $291”. FFY2027 guidelines: “16% or greater:” 3 pts, 11%–15% 2 pts, 6%–10% 1 pt, “Less than 5%:” 0 pts, Propane +2 pts, “Standard Utility Allowance:” $298. FY2026 ISD 017 card, page 1: “LIHEAP Energy Standard Allowance” “(ESA): $291.”; FY2027 card, page 1, deductions table: the last column, LIHEAP Energy Standard Allowance (ESA), $298. LHP 602, page 3: “How much was your highest monthly bill in the last 12 months?”

Income points. 8.150.620.9 B: “HCA assigns income points using the household's monthly total countable gross income and the household size.” “The number of points is determined by identifying what percentage the household's income is of the federal poverty guidelines (FPG) for the LIHEAP FFY.” “For example, if the total monthly income is sixty percent of the FPG, the household will receive three income points.” (1) “Three points - income is zero to one hundred percent of the FPG”; (2) “Two points - income is one hundred to one hundred fifty percent of the FPG”. FFY2027 guidelines: “Income at or below 110%:” +3 pts and “Income at 111%-150%:” +2 pts; FFY2026 guide: 3 Points and 2 Points columns (table above). FY2026 ISD 017 card, page 1, LIHEAP columns headed 110% FPG or Below, Receives 3 Points and 111%-150%FPG, Receives 2 Points, with the same values. The FFY2025 guide also printed a 110% column ($1,381 for one person, 110% of the 2024 guideline of $15,060 over 12 months).

Vulnerable points. 8.150.620.9 C: “HCA assigns additional points for any household members in the following vulnerable groups.” C(1): “Two points are assigned to eligible households based on the inclusion of one or more household members age 60 or over as determined by birthdate data.” C(2): “Two points are assigned to eligible households based on the inclusion of one or more household members age five and under as determined by birthdate data.” C(3): “Two points are assigned to eligible households having one or more members with a disability.” “When one or more members receive disability based income, the household is entitled to the points.” and “A doctor's statement of current disability will be required for assignment of the point for this factor if the disabled member does not receive disability-based income.” FFY2026 guide: “Age 5 or younger 2 Points”, “Age 60 or older 2 Points”, “Disabled 2 Points”. FY2026 plan, page 10, item 2.4: “Households with vulnerable members; such as age 60 and over, age 5 and under, members with a disability, and for any household that is seeking assistance with bulk fuel propane are eligible for an additional benefit.” Item 2.5 checks income, household size, fuel type, individual bill, energy burden, energy need and Other, not climate or dwelling type.

Point value and range. FFY2026 guide: “Point Values - $35 per” point, 2 points $70 to 14 points $490. FY2026 ISD 017 card, page 1: “Maximum points granted is 14 points”, “Minimum LIHEAP amount is $70”, “Maximum LIHEAP amount is $490”. FY2026 plan, page 10, item 2.6: “Minimum Benefit $70 Maximum Benefit $490”. FFY2027 guidelines: “3. TOTAL POINTS = LIHEAP BENEFIT • $40 PER POINT”, 2 pts $80 to 14 pts $560, and “Example: 6 total points × $40 = $240 LIHEAP benefit.” FY2027 plan, page 9, item 2.6: “Minimum Benefit $80 Maximum Benefit $560”.

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Income points at 110% (source conflict).** 8.150.620.9 B gives three points for income “zero to one hundred percent of the FPG” and two for “one hundred to one hundred fifty percent”. HCA's FFY2027 guidelines and the FY2026 ISD 017 card give three points at or below 110% of the guideline, and the FFY2025 and FFY2026 guides print 3-point maximums equal to 110%. The branch follows the guides, which HCA applies (`payment/income_points/low_income_fpg_rate.yaml`, 1.1). 8.150.620.10 C lets the secretary adjust point values and does not mention this cutoff. The branch adds the backlog entry `us-nm:liheap-three-income-points` to `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml` (regulation against guidance, FFY2026 to FFY2027, `state: ruled`, `follows: unknown`, `code: []` until merged, no `# Source conflict` marker until registered). Its example: a one-person FFY2026 household with $1,400 a month (107% of the guideline) scores two points under the rule and three under the guides. Companion test 4 shows the difference.
2. **Energy burden bands, rounding and zero income (encoded reading).** The rule prints whole-percent bands (zero to five, six to ten, eleven to fifteen, sixteen or more); the FFY2026 guide prints “5% <” and the FFY2027 guidelines “Less than 5%” for 0 points. The branch scores the unrounded ratio with lower-inclusive cutoffs at 6%, 11% and 16%, so 5.99% scores 0 and 10.99% scores 1. A reading that first rounds the burden to a whole percent would score 5.5% to 5.99% as 1 point and change the second case of tests 1 to 3. With zero income the ratio has no value; the branch gives the top band, 3 points (test 4). The ratio of the annual amounts is computed in one division, so exact cutoffs land on them.
3. **Bill measure and the allowance (encoded reading).** The application asks for the highest monthly bill in the last 12 months, and the FFY2026 guide divides the “Highest Energy Bill” by income. The model has no highest-bill input; the branch uses the annual bill for the named fuel over 12, an average that is at most the highest month. 8.150.620.9 A(4) says the allowance “may be used” when the applicant's monthly costs are below it or unavailable; the branch always raises a lower bill to the allowance, for every fuel, including bought wood. Only test 2 uses a bill above the allowance.
4. **Monthly income and annual inputs (simplification).** New Mexico counts gross income of the 30 days before the determination (8.150.520.12 C), converting weekly and biweekly pay by four and two (8.150.520.12 B(4)), and 8.150.620.9 B uses monthly income. The branch divides annual amounts by 12 and compares them with the printed monthly figures. The annual limit is therefore 12 x $1,956 = $23,472 for one person, while the FFY2026 guide's annual column prints $23,475 (150% of $15,650); test 10(a)'s $23,473 is not eligible under the monthly reading and eligible under the annual column. The guide's eight-person annual figure, $79,080, repeats the FFY2025 guide's value; 150% of $54,150 is $81,225.
5. **Rounding and sizes over 8 (inferred).** Every printed monthly limit and 3-point maximum for sizes 1 to 8 in both years equals the rate times the guideline over 12, rounded to the nearest dollar (no row falls on a half dollar; the branch rounds halves up), for example 1.5 x 15,650 / 12 = 1,956.25, printed $1,956; 1.5 x 54,150 / 12 = 6,768.75, printed $6,769. The branch extends the rate to every size. The guides' “each additional” increments differ by $1 for some sizes: FFY2026 150% size 9, $7,457 by increment and $7,456 by rate (test 10(c)); FFY2027 110% size 9, $5,629 and $5,628. The FFY2025 guide does not follow one rounding rule (size 1: 1.5 x 15,060 / 12 = 1,882.50, printed $1,882; 1.1 x 15,060 / 12 = 1,380.50, printed $1,381), so the period 2025 estimate gives $1,883 where that guide printed $1,882.
6. **Countable income: rule over plan checklist (settled).** The FY2026 and FY2027 plans' item 1.9 differs from 8.150.520 on four items, and the branch follows the rule: Social Security counts gross, including the Medicare premium (8.150.520.13 B; the plan checks “Excluding MediCare deduction”); lump sums are excluded (8.150.520.13 D(3); the plan checks one-time lump-sum payments), and no input separates them; contributions from family or friends count as `financial_assistance` (8.150.520.13 C; the plan leaves cash gifts unchecked); and an 18-year-old's earnings are excluded, since the rule counts earnings of members “over the age of 18” (the plan's box reads “under the age of 18”). Tests 13(a) to 13(c) rest on this decision.
7. **Retirement-account withdrawals (encoded reading).** `retirement_distributions` (IRA, 401(k) and 403(b)) counts as “retirement ... benefits or payments” (8.150.520.13 A), and plan item 1.9 checks “Retirement / pension benefits”. No New Mexico source names account withdrawals. Nonrecurring lump-sum withdrawals, excluded under 8.150.520.13 D(3), cannot be separated in the annual input, so every withdrawal counts (test 13(g)).
8. **Other income items (simplification and inference).** Capital gains are not counted: the rule's lists and plan item 1.9 do not name them (test 13(e)). Strike pay is not counted (plan box unchecked; the rule is silent). Rental income and farm rent are listed with unearned income; the rule counts a landlord's rent as earned income when 20 or more hours a week are worked, which differs only for members aged 18 or under, and the model has no input for landlord hours. Self-employment, farm and partnership income use the model's net inputs, each floored at zero; the model's net income may deduct depreciation, which 8.150.520.9 D(2) disallows. `military_retirement_income`, `survivor_benefits` (non-Social Security), `veterans_benefits`, `disability_benefits`, `workers_compensation`, `total_unemployment_compensation`, `general_assistance`, `estate_income`, interest and dividends count in full. Royalties, tribal benefits, real-estate contract payments, legal settlements, foster-care funds and AmeriCorps payments have no input. The New Mexico SSI state supplement (`nm_ssi_state_supplement`, for residents of adult residential care homes) is not in the list. TANF is the SPM unit's take-up-gated `tanf`, counted once in full.
9. **Household, size and vulnerable members (simplification and reading).** The SPM unit stands in for the household of 8.150.410.8. `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant` stands in for TANF-qualified noncitizen status (8.150.410.13); the Social Security number requirement (8.150.410.15) has no input. Size counts those members; the same flag marks the ineligible noncitizens whose income is prorated (8.150.520.10 B, implemented as income x size / `spm_unit_size`, algebraically the rule's steps). Vulnerable points count only those members: 8.150.620.9 C says “household members”, while 8.150.410.15 says other members “will not be eligible for a LIHEAP benefit” (test 12(b): $175, or $245 with the age points). Migrant households (8.150.520.11) and facility residents (8.150.410.16) are not identified.
10. **Disability (proxy).** `is_disabled` stands in for disability-based income or a doctor's statement (8.150.620.9 C(3)); test 8(d) sets both.
11. **Heating responsibility and housing (proxies and reading).** Subsidized means `receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing`; university housing, which the rule says is not subsidized, has no input. For subsidized heat in rent, a positive bill for the named fuel stands in for the out-of-pocket cost of 8.150.410.11 B(2). Such a household gets no energy points, since 8.150.620.9 A(3)(a) excludes “households whose utilities are included in the rent”, although A gives energy points to households “that have a direct cost” (test 6(c)). Secondary heat sources (8.150.410.9 A and B), shared meters and homeless applicants (8.150.100.10 A(5)) have no separate input.
12. **Fuels (settled and inference).** `heating_type` is a required input; UNSPECIFIED pays $0 except with heat in rent, where the rule needs no fuel (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the default). NONE is no heat. WOOD with no wood bill is gathered wood, eligible without energy points; with a bill it is bought wood. PROPANE (bottled gas; the application lists propane and butane together) adds 2 points. Electricity, natural gas, fuel oil, kerosene, coal and other fuels have no fuel points. SOLAR reads the electricity bill under the model's convention for grid-tied solar homes; the rule has no solar provision.
13. **One benefit, heating or cooling (scope).** New Mexico issues one benefit a federal fiscal year (8.150.110.8 D), applied to the heating or cooling bill the household chooses (LHP 602, pages 2-3). The branch computes it from the heating bill for households with a heating cost or eligible heat in rent; households with only a cooling cost receive $0, and the cooling-bill computation is out of scope. Funding limits (8.150.620.10 B), supplemental benefits (8.150.110.8 E), a benefit received from a tribe or another state (8.150.110.8 D) and tribal LIHEAP (8.150.410.12) are not modeled.
14. **Years and dates (simplification).** All parameters start `2025-10-01`, with the point value and allowance changing on `2026-10-01`. Annual periods read 1 January values, so period 2026 applies FFY2026 to the whole calendar year, including October to December 2026, which fall in FFY2027; period 2027 applies FFY2027 likewise. Earlier and later periods are estimates (see Policy periods); period 2025 keeps the FFY2026 allowance of $291, while the FFY2025 guide printed $283.

Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: Encode Montana separate-filing deductions through 2023 and elderly homeowner/renter credit income without losses

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Encoding gap

**Parity status: queued.** Each signed-encoder run needs Max’s approval. Historical-source ingestion, restoration of omitted credit tables, and a signed corpus release containing the forms are also prerequisites. This issue supplies the targets, evidence, `review_finding`, and companion expectations; no encoding or workflow was run.

PolicyEngine-US’s proposed PR `fix-mt-separate-filing-allocations`, inspected at local HEAD `304d880bb6`, changes three calculations:

- Federal income tax is attributed before applying each separately filing spouse’s $5,000 deduction limit.
- Child/dependent-care expenses are phased out using combined Montana AGI, then divided equally for spouses filing separately on the same form. Unmarried filers and joint returns receive the whole applicable deduction.
- Elderly-credit gross household income adds back losses included in federal AGI.

The first two deductions apply only through TY2023. The elderly-credit loss rule continues afterward.

**What the search found** (rulespec-us `origin/main` `f468c8daeb3c0e7184b85be7fb97585475d74a1b`, October 4, 2026; obtained with `git -C ~/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us log -1 origin/main`):

| Existing module | Exact rules or boundaries relevant to this issue | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| `us-mt/statutes/15-30-2318.yaml` | `state_earned_income_tax_credit_percentage`, `reduction_percentage`, `montana_earned_income_tax_credit`, `montana_earned_income_tax_credit_refund` | Encodes the **EITC**, not either historical deduction or the elderly credit. Citation: `us-mt/statute/15-30-2318`. |
| `us-mt/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml` | `mt_pit_pilot_taxable_income`, `mt_pit_pilot_filing_status_threshold`, `mt_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability` | TY2026 schedule using caller-supplied completed-return taxable income. Citation: `us-mt/statute/15-30-2103`. Historical deductions and elderly credit are outside its calculation. |
| `us-mt/policies/income_tax/resident_core_liability_pipeline.yaml` | `mt_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies`, `mt_pit_2026_supported_profile_candidate_refundable_credits`, `mt_pit_2026_supported_profile_candidate_net_income_tax_liability` | Cites §§2337, 2338, 2340 and 2341, but excludes the elderly-credit branch through `not mt_pit_2026_has_elderly_property_tax_credit`. Complete `mt_pit_2026_net_income_tax_liability` is deferred. |
| Former §15-30-2131(1)(b), (c) | No corresponding module or computing rule | **Not encoded.** |
| §15-30-2337 income without loss; elderly-credit computation | No dedicated statute module or computing rule | **Not encoded.** The resident pipeline’s citations and typed hold are source awareness, not a computed credit. |

The resident pipeline explicitly says:

> The elderly property-tax-credit tables are absent from the normalized provision, and annual-return instructions and credit ordering are not pinned.

**Validation state.** `known-validation-gaps.yaml` has a `validate_failures` waiver for `us-mt/policies/income_tax/resident_core_liability_pipeline.yaml`, owned by `@MaxGhenis`, tracked under [#782](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us/issues/782), expiring December 21, 2026. `.axiom/pending-validation-fingerprints.json` also records that module with `passed: false`. No waiver names the proposed new modules. Adding these provisions does not resolve the pipeline’s other complete-liability blockers.

## Why this matters

The companion cases expose different errors:

- Federal tax attributed as $24,000/$6,000 yields deductions **$5,000/$5,000**. Applying a $10,000 couple cap before allocation instead understates the second spouse’s deduction.
- One qualifying child, expenses $3,000 and combined Montana AGI $20,000 yield a $1,400 care deduction: **$700 per separate column**, or **$1,400 on a joint return**.
- Pension income $20,000, a deducted capital loss $3,000 and untaxed Social Security $10,000 yield elderly-credit gross household income **$30,000**, contribution **$870**, and owner-only credit **$1,130**.

These are form calculations, subject to the methodology distinctions below. PE’s outputs are not evidence of the law.

## Corpus (confirmed at the pin)

rulespec-us pins:

- `axiom_corpus_ref`: `8f7d60aaced28ee4252b9237f9d6e02360dc34bc`;
- signed release: `us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap`;
- release content SHA256: `0d69a0cdbe024fc2276f3c261c00402bb0a47488ac5f482cc20bd3404980adbc`.

The corpus working checkout is **stale and diverged**: HEAD `2794b5448e81525f0ee351cdac2a49d32327aade`, July 27, 2026. The pinned object is locally available; the findings below use `git show` at that object, not the working tree. No fetch occurred.

All confirmed rows below are in:

`data/corpus/provisions/us-mt/statute/2026-07-16-pit-central-us-mt-title-15.jsonl`

That scope is selected by the pinned release. These rows identify source year 2025 and source/expression date March 24, 2026.

| File line | Exact confirmed citation path | Content and limitation |
|---|---|---|
| 1280 | `us-mt/statute/15-30-2131` | **Repeal marker only:** `15-30-2131. Repealed. Secs. 65, 70(1), Ch. 503, L. 2021.` It cannot ground the historical deductions. |
| 1311 | `us-mt/statute/15-30-2337` | Includes definitions (4), (8), (9) and the remaining definitions. |
| 1312 | `us-mt/statute/15-30-2338` | Eligibility, disallowance and rent adjustment. |
| 1313 | `us-mt/statute/15-30-2339` | Filing provisions; history includes a 2025 amendment. Do not project the entire current section backward. |
| 1314 | `us-mt/statute/15-30-2340` | Computation, $1,150 cap and refundability, but **both subsection (4)/(5) tables are omitted from the normalized body**. |
| 1315 | `us-mt/statute/15-30-2341` | One claimant per household and other limitations. |

No subsection rows were confirmed for these sections.

The raw pinned §2340 HTML preserves the omitted tables at:

`data/corpus/sources/us-mt/statute/2026-07-16-pit-central-us-mt-title-15/montana-code-html/title_0150/chapter_0300/part_0230/section_0400/0150-0300-0230-0400.html`

Subsection (4)’s table is at HTML lines 144–204; subsection (5)’s table is at lines 209–237. Repair normalization and promote the repaired evidence into a signed release.

**No operative historical row can be confirmed** for §2131(1)(b) or (c). **No corpus row can be confirmed** for the 2022 Form 2 instructions, 2022 Form 2441-M, 2023 Form 2EC, or 2025 Schedule 2EC. The pinned release has no Montana form/guidance scopes. Ingest the historical statute with TY2021–2023 applicability and the year-specific forms/instructions, including the 2024 instructions used by the business-loss companion. Record the actual resulting citation paths before dispatch; no form row IDs or citation paths are assumed here.

## Statute and forms (verbatim; independently re-verified)

The supplied files are under `~/reviews/us-hub/state-allocation-fixes/sources/`. Quotes were checked against their text or HTML and the cited PDF pages. PDF whitespace and column wrapping are normalized.

### Historical deductions

**Source integrity.** `mt-15-30-2131-2021.txt` is a failed download containing `404` / `NOT FOUND`. The valid supplied `mt-15-30-2131-2022.html` is headed **Montana Code Annotated 2021**, despite its filename.

[Former MCA §15-30-2131](https://mca.legmt.gov/bills/2022/mca/title_0150/chapter_0300/part_0210/section_0310/0150-0300-0210-0310.html), supplied HTML, subsection (1)(b):

> (b) federal income tax paid within the tax year, not to exceed $5,000 for each taxpayer filing singly, head of household, or married filing separately or $10,000 if married and filing jointly;

Subsection (1)(c)(v):

> (v) if the combined adjusted gross income of the taxpayers exceeds $18,000 for the tax year during which the expenses are incurred, the amount of the employment-related expenses incurred, to be reduced by one-half of the excess of the combined adjusted gross income over $18,000;

Subsection (1)(c)(vi)(A), (D):

> (A) married couples shall file a joint return or file separately on the same form;

> (D) the deduction for employment-related expenses must be divided equally between the spouses when filing separately on the same form;

The statute limits eligible services to expenses necessary for gainful employment and qualifying individuals. Subsection (1)(c)(i) states:

> (i) expenses for household and dependent care services necessary for gainful employment incurred for:  
> (A) a dependent under 15 years of age for whom an exemption can be claimed;  
> (B) a dependent as allowable under 15-30-2114(5), except that the limitations for age and gross income do not apply, who is unable to provide self-care because of physical or mental illness; and  
> (C) a spouse who is unable to provide self-care because of physical or mental illness;

The supplied HTML’s repeal annotation states:

> (Repealed effective January 1, 2024--secs. 65, 70(1), Ch. 503, L. 2021.)

**2022 Form 2 instructions, Itemized Deductions Schedule line 4**, [PDF p.33, printed p.27](https://revenue.mt.gov/files/forms/Montana-Individual-Income-Tax-Return-Form-2-Instructions/2022_Montana_Individual_Income_Tax_Return_Form_2_Instructions.pdf#page=33), `mt-2022-instr.txt:1851–1887`:

> Enter the total amount of federal income tax paid in 2022.

> 4a. Enter the income tax withheld that was reported to you on your federal Forms W-2 and 1099. If you are married filing separately with your spouse, the federal income tax withheld should be reported by the spouse who earned the income.

> 4b. Enter the amount of federal estimated income tax payments.

> 4c. Enter the balance of the total amount of the 2021 federal income tax that you paid in 2022.

> 4d. Enter the total amount of additional back year federal income taxes that you paid in 2022. For example, you may have paid additional 2019 federal income taxes in 2022.

> Add lines 4a through 4d. Your federal tax deduction is limited as follows:  
> ● If your filing status is Single, Married Filing Separately, or Head of Household, your deduction is limited to $5,000.  
> ● If your filing status is Married Filing Separately, you are each limited to the $5,000 federal tax deduction and you cannot arbitrarily allocate this deduction between spouses.  
> ● If you file your Montana tax return jointly with your spouse, your federal income tax deduction is limited to $10,000.

**2022 Form 2 instructions, line 14**, [PDF p.35, printed p.29](https://revenue.mt.gov/files/forms/Montana-Individual-Income-Tax-Return-Form-2-Instructions/2022_Montana_Individual_Income_Tax_Return_Form_2_Instructions.pdf#page=35), `mt-2022-instr.txt:1970–2000`:

> You qualify if you and your spouse’s total Montana Adjusted Gross Income is:

The accompanying table specifies under $22,800 with one child, under $25,200 with two children, and under $27,600 with three or more children.

> To qualify for this deduction if you are married, you must either file Married Filing Jointly (Filing Status 4) or file Married Filing Separately on the Same Form (Filing Status 2a). When you file separately on the same form, your deduction must be divided equally between both spouses. If you are married and filing separately on separate forms, or your spouse is not filing, you cannot qualify for this deduction.

**2022 Form 2441-M**, [PDF p.1, lines 1–7](https://revenuefiles.mt.gov/files/Forms/Child-and-Dependent-Care-Expense-Deduction-Form-2441-M/2022_Child_and_Dependent_Care_Expense_Deduction_Form_2441-M.pdf#page=1), `mt-2022-2441m.txt:12–33`:

> 1. Enter the number of qualifying individuals you cared for in 2022

> 2. Enter the lesser of your actual amount of dependent care expenses paid in 2022, or the amount listed below  
> ● $2,400 for one qualifying individual  
> ● $3,600 for two qualifying individuals  
> ● $4,800 for three or more qualifying individuals

> 3. Add the amounts in columns A and B, line 14 of Form 2  
> ● If line 3 above is $18,000 or less, stop here and enter the amount from line 2 above on Form 2, Itemized Deductions Schedule, line 14.  
> (If you are married filing separately on the same form, enter one-half of the amount from line 2 in columns A and B.)  
> ● If line 3 is $18,001 or greater, complete lines 4 through 7 below.

> 4. Your Montana adjusted gross income base amount is entered here

Line 4 has the preprinted amount **$18,000**.

> 5. Subtract line 4 from line 3

> 6. Multiply line 5 by 50% (0.50)

> 7. Subtract line 6 from line 2.  
> ● If your result is zero or less, stop here, you are not allowed this deduction.  
> ● If your result is greater than zero, enter the amount from line 7 above on Form 2, Itemized Deductions Schedule, line 14.  
> (If you are married filing separately on the same form, enter one-half of the amount from line 7 in columns A and B.)  
> This is your child and dependent care expense deduction.

**Historical reading.** TY2021 uses the historical statute and matching wording checked in `mt-2021-instr.txt`—withholding attribution at line 1976, allocation restriction at 1935, combined Montana AGI at 2063 and equal division at 2075. TY2023’s matching care filing/split wording is at `mt-2023-instr.txt:2258–2265`. The 2022 form is not being represented as a TY2021 form.

### Elderly-credit income

[MCA §15-30-2337](https://mca.legmt.gov/bills/mca/title_0150/chapter_0300/part_0230/section_0370/0150-0300-0230-0370.html), supplied `mt-15-30-2337.txt`, MCA2025:

> (4) "Gross household income" means all income received by all individuals of a household while they are members of the household.

> (7) (a) "Household" means an association of persons who live in the same dwelling, sharing its furnishings, facilities, accommodations, and expenses.  
> (b) The term does not include bona fide lessees, tenants, or roomers and boarders on contract.

> (8) "Household income" means the amount obtained by subtracting $12,600 from gross household income.

> (9) (a) "Income" means, except as provided in subsection (9)(b), federal adjusted gross income, without regard to loss, as that quantity is defined in the Internal Revenue Code of the United States, plus all nontaxable income, including but not limited to:  
> (i) the amount of any pension or annuity, including Railroad Retirement Act benefits and veterans' disability benefits;  
> (ii) the amount of capital gains excluded from adjusted gross income;  
> (iii) alimony;  
> (iv) support money;  
> (v) nontaxable strike benefits;  
> (vi) cash public assistance and relief;  
> (vii) interest on federal, state, county, and municipal bonds; and  
> (viii) all payments received under federal social security except social security income paid directly to a nursing home.  
> (b) For the purposes of this subsection (9), income is reduced by the taxpayer's basis.

> (11) "Rent-equivalent tax paid" means 15% of the gross rent.

**2023 Form 2EC instructions, line 9**, [PDF p.52, printed p.45](https://revenue.mt.gov/files/forms/Montana-Individual-Income-Tax-Return-Form-2-Instructions/2023_Montana_Individual_Income_Tax_Return_Form_2_Instructions.pdf#page=52), `mt-2023-instr.txt:3105–3109`:

> Line 9–Enter all losses included on Form 2, line 11. The gross household income cannot be reduced by any losses. If losses are included on line 1, you must add them back here as a positive number. Include net operating losses taken on federal Schedule 1, line 8a.

**2025 Schedule 2EC instructions, line 7**, [PDF p.45, printed p.39](https://revenuefiles.mt.gov/files/Forms/Montana-Individual-Income-Tax-Return-Form-2-Instructions/2025_Montana_Individual_Income_Tax_Return_Form_2_Instructions.pdf#page=45), `mt-2025-instr.txt:2411–2417`:

> Line 7 – Capital gain, including any exclusion. Report the total amount of capital gains received during the tax year adjusted for the basis of the property. Do not adjust the capital gain for any federal exclusions, such as the gain from the sale of a primary residence and do not include any capital losses.

Line 7 is on **PDF p.45**, rather than p.46. Lines 10–13 are on [PDF p.46, printed p.40](https://revenuefiles.mt.gov/files/Forms/Montana-Individual-Income-Tax-Return-Form-2-Instructions/2025_Montana_Individual_Income_Tax_Return_Form_2_Instructions.pdf#page=46), `mt-2025-instr.txt:2436–2456`:

> Line 10 – Business income. If you operated a business or practiced your profession as a sole proprietor, report your net income. Do not include any losses generated from the business.

> Line 11 – Other gains. Enter the total of income received from the sale or exchange of assets used in a trade or business. Do not include any losses in this amount.

> Line 12 – Rental real estate, royalties, partnerships, S corporations, trusts, etc. Enter the total income received that you would normally report on a federal Schedule E. Do not include any losses in this amount.

> Line 13 – Farm income. Enter the total income received from farming activities and that are normally reported on a federal Schedule F. Do not include any losses in this amount.

### Credit computation and source readings

**2023 Form 2EC**, [Form 2 PDF p.10](https://revenuefiles.mt.gov/files/Forms/Montana-Individual-Income-Tax-Return-Form-2/2023_Montana_Individual_Income_Tax_Return_Form_2.pdf#page=10), `mt-2023-form2.txt:667–699`:

> For lines 1-7 and 9, use the amounts reported on Forms 2, page 1, for ALL members of the household. (See instructions)

> 10 Add lines 1 through 9. This is your gross household income.

Line 11 has the preprinted exclusion **$12,600**.

> 12 Subtract line 11 from line 10 and enter the result here, but not less than zero

> 13 Enter your multiplier rate from the Household Income Reduction Table (See table below)

> 14 Multiply line 12 by line 13. This is your net household income.

> 17 Multiply line 16 by 15% (0.15)

> 18 Add lines 15 and 17

> 19 Subtract line 14 from line 18 and enter the result here, but not less than zero

> 20 Enter the lesser of line 19 or $1,150

> 21 Enter the percentage from the Credit Multiplier Table that corresponds to your gross household income (See table below)

> 22 Multiply line 20 by the percentage on line 21 and enter the total here and on Other Payments and Refundable Credits Schedule, line 7. (See page 11.) This is your elderly homeowner/renter credit.

The p.10 reduction table gives rates 0, .006, .016, .024, .028, .032, .035, .039, .042, .045, .048 and .05 for line-12 income bands $0–1,999, $2,000–2,999, successive $1,000 bands through $11,000–11,999, and $12,000 or greater. Its credit multiplier is 100% below gross income $35,000; 40% at $35,000–37,500; 30% at $37,501–40,000; 20% at $40,001–42,500; 10% at $42,501–44,999; and 0% at $45,000 or greater.

**Supplemental statute evidence.** §§2338–2341 are absent from the supplied review-source folder. Their official pages were checked separately, and their pinned corpus bodies were inspected.

[§2338(1)](https://mca.legmt.gov/bills/mca/title_0150/chapter_0300/part_0230/section_0380/0150-0300-0230-0380.html):

> (a) must have reached age 62 or older during the claim period for which relief is sought;  
> (b) must have resided in Montana for at least 9 months of that period;  
> (c) must have occupied one or more dwellings in Montana as an owner, renter, or lessee for at least 6 months of the claim period; and  
> (d) must have less than $45,000 of gross household income.

[§2341(1)](https://mca.legmt.gov/bills/mca/title_0150/chapter_0300/part_0230/section_0410/0150-0300-0230-0410.html):

> (1) Only one claimant per household in a claim period under the provisions of 15-30-2337 through 15-30-2341 is entitled to relief.

[§2340(6), (7)](https://mca.legmt.gov/bills/mca/title_0150/chapter_0300/part_0230/section_0400/0150-0300-0230-0400.html):

> (6) The credit granted may not exceed $1,150.

> If the amount of the credit exceeds the claimant's liability under this chapter, the amount of the excess must be refunded to the claimant. The credit may be claimed even though the claimant has no income taxable under this chapter.

Historical agreement for §§2338, 2340 and 2341 is a **reading based on amendment histories and agreement with the 2023 form**, not an archived-year verification. §2339 has a 2025 amendment and needs dated evidence for any historical filing output.

Two source differences must remain visible:

- **Gross-income multiplier.** §2340(5)’s introduction says “household income,” but its table heading says “Gross household income.” Form 2EC line 21 and its table explicitly use gross household income, line 10. Companion expectations follow that **form reading**.
- **Mixed owner/renter claims.** §2340(3)(a)–(b) places the subsection (4) deduction in each owned/rented addend. Form 2EC lines 18–19 combine property tax and rent-equivalent tax, then subtract one contribution. That combined formula is a **form reading**, not an unqualified transcription of subsection (3). The owner-only worked companion does not depend on resolving this difference.

## Encoding path

- **Signed encoder only.** Use `targeted-signed-reencode.yml`; never hand-write RuleSpec. Each billed run requires Max’s separate approval under PE `CLAUDE.md:149–152`.
- **Pinned toolchain.** `.axiom/workflow-toolchain.toml` pins encoder `4956c8305ee155f476a3c0c6dbe8efbd443626a4`, version `0.2.2087`, and rules engine `89571cc2a938707fd60a5489b951135345697296`.
- **Corpus prerequisite.** Historical deductions cannot be encoded from the current repeal marker. Table-dependent credit outputs require normalized tables and pinned form evidence.
- **Dispatch preparation.** Use `country=us`, the immutable rulespec main SHA above, and approved corpus/engine refs. Refresh these immutable inputs after corpus promotion; confirm the signing encoder matches the consuming pin.

## Plan

### Step 1. Complete the source bundle

Ingest the operative historical §2131 text and the cited annual forms/instructions; repair §2340’s normalized tables; promote an approved signed successor release. Confirm historical applicability before selecting versions.

### Step 2. Encode the missing modules

These are **proposed destinations**, not existing files:

| Proposed module | Corpus target |
|---|---|
| `us-mt/statutes/15-30-2131/1/b.yaml` | Historical version of `us-mt/statute/15-30-2131`, after ingestion |
| `us-mt/statutes/15-30-2131/1/c.yaml` | Historical version of `us-mt/statute/15-30-2131`, plus confirmed ingested Form 2441-M/instruction citations |
| `us-mt/statutes/15-30-2337.yaml` | `us-mt/statute/15-30-2337` |
| `us-mt/statutes/15-30-2338.yaml` | `us-mt/statute/15-30-2338` |
| `us-mt/statutes/15-30-2341.yaml` | `us-mt/statute/15-30-2341` |
| `us-mt/statutes/15-30-2340.yaml` | Repaired `us-mt/statute/15-30-2340`; annual-form composition must identify its ingested form evidence |

Nested subsection modules using whole-section citations have precedent in `us-co/statutes/39/39-22-104/1.7/a.yaml` and `/1.7/b.yaml`.

Paste this as `review_finding` **after the source prerequisites are satisfied**:

> Encode Montana’s former MCA 15-30-2131(1)(b) and (1)(c) at us-mt/statutes/15-30-2131/1/b.yaml and us-mt/statutes/15-30-2131/1/c.yaml. Use the ingested historical operative version of corpus citation us-mt/statute/15-30-2131, not the current repeal-marker body. Bound the historical deduction versions to TY2021–2023 and provide a source-grounded zero/non-applicability result from TY2024.
>
> Encode elderly-credit definitions at us-mt/statutes/15-30-2337.yaml, eligibility at us-mt/statutes/15-30-2338.yaml, limitations at us-mt/statutes/15-30-2341.yaml, and computation at us-mt/statutes/15-30-2340.yaml. Their confirmed section citations are us-mt/statute/15-30-2337, us-mt/statute/15-30-2338, us-mt/statute/15-30-2341 and us-mt/statute/15-30-2340. Use the repaired tables and actual ingested annual-form citations. Include verbatim proof excerpts and explicit source versions for every output.
>
> Required outputs:
>
> 1. Person/return-scoped federal-income-tax deduction: federal income taxes paid during the year, with withholding assigned to the spouse who earned the income; apply the $5,000 separate-filer limit after attribution. Preserve the statutory $10,000 joint-return limit. Other payment categories must have resolved attribution, not an invented allocation rule.
> 2. Care qualifying-individual/eligible-expense boundary, respecting employment-related services, household-maintenance requirements, qualifying dependents or incapable spouse, and excluded payees. If dependencies are deferred, name them precisely; childcare spending alone is not proof of eligibility.
> 3. Form 2441-M line-2 capped eligible expenses: lesser of eligible expenses and $2,400/$3,600/$4,800 for one/two/three-or-more qualifying individuals.
> 4. Combined Form 2441-M deduction: max(0, line2 − 0.5 × max(0, combined Montana AGI − 18,000)). For separate columns, combine Form 2 columns A and B before phase-out. Divide the resulting deduction equally only for married filing separately on the same form. An unmarried filer or joint return receives the whole applicable amount. Separate-form married filers do not qualify.
> 5. Elderly-credit income without loss: reconstruct federal AGI without losses included in AGI, including NOL deductions, and include the specified nontaxable income without double counting; respect taxpayer basis. An aggregate AGI floor is insufficient. Inputs must disclose losses already netted within categories.
> 6. Gross household income: sum qualifying income over every statutory household member while a member, including dependents where applicable. Household membership follows §2337(7), not an assumed tax-unit relation.
> 7. Distinct outputs for statutory household income G − 12,600, the form’s nonnegative income base max(0, G − 12,600), and the income-based property-tax contribution obtained by multiplying that base by the reduction-table rate. Do not label the contribution as the statutory household-income amount. Version the exclusion; the quoted $12,600 evidence does not establish TY2021’s amount.
> 8. Eligibility judgments covering §2338, with gross household income strictly below $45,000, and §2341’s one-claimant and other limitations.
> 9. Owner-only form-composed credit: apply the contribution, zero floor, $1,150 limit and gross-income multiplier in Form 2EC lines19–22 order; provide refundability under §2340(7). Preserve the disclosed §2340(5) gross/household-income source reading. Any mixed owner/renter output must separately disclose the §2340(3) versus form-lines18–19 difference.
>
> Methodology boundaries: PE’s positive-federal-AGI weighting of modeled liability, its zero-positive-income head fallback, and assigning a return-wide loss or final credit to the head are projection/bookkeeping choices. The forms do not prescribe them as statutory allocations. Keep such projections separately identified from the legal outputs. Do not carry PE’s omission of other household members’ income into the statutory household rule.
>
> Add the companion cases below, retaining their expected values and source derivations. Preserve TY2021–2023 applicability and TY2024 repeal controls. Do not import the existing TY2026 liability pipeline into these source modules or release its complete-liability hold merely because these outputs exist.

### Step 3. Oracle coverage and integration

Map the legal outputs to PE variables with the projection boundaries documented. Run `axiom-encode oracle-coverage-pending sync` for outputs without matching oracle coverage.

In particular, PE’s `mt_elderly_homeowner_or_renter_credit_net_household_income` corresponds to the **contribution after the reduction-table multiplier**—Form 2EC line 14—not the statutory income after the exclusion.

Wire the historical care deduction once into the appropriate itemized aggregate. Integrate the elderly credit into annual liability only after that year’s remaining source, ordering and eligibility dependencies are resolved.

## Companion tests

The PE YAML files were read in full in `~/PolicyEngine/_worktrees/fix-mt-separate`. Paths below are relative to:

`policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/mt/tax/income/`

Money expectations retain PE’s values and $0.01 tolerance where supplied. Arrays follow PE member order. For legal companions, explicitly provide statutory membership, filing status and resolved eligibility; unspecified monetary components are zero.

### Federal tax deduction

Sources: former §2131(1)(b) and Form 2 Itemized Deductions line 4. The legal expectations below are conditional on attributed **payments**. AGI shares and modeled liability are separately identified PE methodology.

| PE file/start line | TY | Inputs | Preserved expectation and derivation |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `deductions/itemized/mt_federal_income_tax_deduction_indiv.yaml:8` | 2021 | Federal AGI `[60,000,40,000]`; modeled federal tax 3,000 | PE shares `[0.6,0.4]` are methodology. Supply attributed payments `[1,800,1,200]` to the legal companion; deductions **`[1,800,1,200]`** follow line 4. |
| Same file `:30` | 2022 | AGI `[80,000,20,000]`; modeled tax 30,000 | PE attribution `[24,000,6,000]`; each line-4 limit gives **`[5,000,5,000]`**. |
| Same file `:54` | 2022 | Federal AGI `[50,000,50,000]`; spouse Montana subtraction 20,000; modeled tax 6,000 | PE supplies attributed payments `[3,000,3,000]`; deductions **`[3,000,3,000]`**. A Montana subtraction does not change those supplied payments. |
| Same file `:78` | 2022 | AGI `[40,000,0,0]`; third person dependent; modeled tax 2,000 | Attributed payments `[2,000,0]`; PE deduction array **`[2,000,0,0]`**. Despite its name, this fixture gives the dependent **zero income**. |
| Same file `:102` | 2024 | AGI `[60,000,40,000]`; modeled tax 3,000 | **`[0,0]`**, repeal control. |
| `deductions/itemized/federal_itemization/mt_federal_income_tax_deduction_for_federal_itemization_indiv.yaml:5` | 2021 | Own withholding `[3,000,1,000]` | **`[3,000,1,000]`**, line 4a attribution and line-4 limits. |
| Same file `:27` | 2021 | Own withholding `[7,000,1,000]` | **`[5,000,1,000]`**, independent caps. |

The legal fixtures do not establish that federal liability equals federal income tax paid during the year. The supplied instructions expressly include estimated payments and prior-year balances paid during the current year.

### Child/dependent-care deduction

File: `deductions/cdcc/mt_child_dependent_care_expense_deduction.yaml`.

Every calculation below uses Form 2441-M line 1 for qualifying count, line 2 for capped expenses, lines 3–6 for the combined-AGI reduction, and line 7 for the deduction and same-form equal split.

The first 15 TY2021 fixtures are retained compactly below. Each unmarried filer receives the amount shown; each dependent’s output remains zero.

| Qualifying children | Expenses | Montana AGI values, in order | Expected filer deductions, in order | PE start lines |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2,401 | 18,000; 20,000; 30,000 | **2,400; 1,400; 0** | 1; 25; 49 |
| 2 | 3,601 | 18,000; 22,000; 35,000 | **3,600; 1,600; 0** | 71; 98; 125 |
| 3 | 4,801 | 18,000; 24,000; 34,000 | **4,800; 1,800; 0** | 150; 180; 210 |
| 1 | 2,000 | 18,000; 30,000 | **2,000; 0** | 238; 261 |
| 2 | 3,000 | 18,000; 24,000 | **3,000; 0** | 283; 309 |
| 3 | 4,000 | 18,000; 26,000 | **4,000; 0** | 334; 363 |

For example, the one-child moderate case is `2,400 − (20,000 − 18,000) × .5 = 1,400`; the amount is not halved for an unmarried filer.

| PE start line / case | TY | Inputs | Preserved expectation |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `:391`, equal distribution | 2021 | Separate same-form spouses’ AGI `[10,000,8,000]`; three children; expenses 4,000 | Combined line 3 = 18,000; deduction 4,000; **`[2,000,2,000,0,0,0]`**. |
| `:422`, case 17 | 2021 | AGI 18,000; one incapable adult dependent; care 4,000 | Line 2 = 2,400; **`[2,400,0]`**. |
| `:447`, case 18 | 2021 | AGI 18,000; child care 1,000; capable disabled adult’s care 2,000 | Adult is not qualifying on these facts; **`[1,000,0,0]`**. |
| `:476`, case 19 | 2021 | AGI 18,000; child plus incapable adult; expenses 3,000 + 1,000 | Two-person cap; **`[3,600,0,0]`**. |
| `:506`, case 20 | 2021 | AGI 18,000; one incapable adult; care 5,000 | One-person cap; **`[2,400,0]`**. |
| `:531`, case 21 | 2021 | Same-form spouses’ AGI `[9,000,9,000]`; incapable spouse; care 4,000 | One qualifying individual; 2,400 split equally; **`[1,200,1,200]`**. |
| `:558`, case 22 | 2024 | Child plus incapable adult; expenses 3,000 + 1,000 | **`[0,0,0]`**, repeal. |
| `:585`, case 23 | 2021 | AGI 18,000; one incapable child under 15; expenses 1,000 + 1,500 | Count the child once; **`[2,400,0]`**. |
| `:612`, case 24 | 2021 | Same-form spouses’ AGI `[9,000,9,000]`; incapable spouse plus two children; expenses 6,000 | Three-person cap 4,800; **`[2,400,2,400,0,0]`**. |
| `:647`, case 25 | 2022 | Same-form spouses’ AGI `[20,000,0]`; one child; expenses 3,000 | Eligible expenses **2,400**; line 6 = 1,000; line 7 = 1,400; **`[700,700,0]`**. |
| `:678`, case 26 | 2022 | Joint Montana AGI 20,000; one child; expenses 3,000 | Joint deduction **1,400**. |
| `:704`, case 27 | 2024 | Joint Montana AGI 10,000; one child; expenses 3,000 | Joint deduction **0**, repeal. |

These fixtures assume the expenses meet the employment-related and other legal restrictions. Disability alone does not establish inability to provide self-care.

Add a **supplemental TY2023 date-boundary companion** repeating the case-25 facts: `[700,700,0]`. Its historical applicability comes from the historical statute/repeal annotation and matching 2023 instructions; it is not an existing PE YAML case.

### Elderly-credit income and owner-only credit

Files:

- `credits/elderly_homeowner_or_renter/mt_elderly_homeowner_or_renter_credit_gross_household_income.yaml`;
- `credits/elderly_homeowner_or_renter/mt_elderly_homeowner_or_renter_credit.yaml`.

| PE fixture/start line | TY | Inputs | Preserved expectation and ground truth |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Gross-income file `:1` | 2025 | Veterans benefits 5,000; support 3,000; strike benefits 2,000; assistance 1,000 | Gross **11,000**, §2337(9)(a)(i), (iv), (v), (vi). |
| Gross-income file `:22` | 2025 | Social Security 30,000 | Gross **30,000**, §2337(9)(a)(viii); count taxable/nontaxable portions once. |
| Gross-income file `:41` | 2023 | Pension 20,000; deducted capital loss 3,000; other refundable credits zero | Form 2EC line 1 = 17,000; line 9 = 3,000; line 10 gross **20,000**. |
| Gross-income file `:63` | 2024 | Head pension 20,000; spouse business loss 5,000; other refundable credits zero | Gross **20,000**; income base **7,400**; rate .035; contribution **259**. PE array **`[259,0]`** is bookkeeping. |
| Credit file `:227`, “2023 Elderly Homeowner/Renter Credit Schedule worked case, a capital loss does not reduce gross household income” | 2023 | Age 70; pension 20,000; deducted capital loss 3,000; untaxed Social Security 10,000; qualifying property tax billed 2,000; rent and other refundable credits zero | Gross **30,000**; contribution **870**; credit **1,130**. |

The 2024 business-loss companion uses that year’s category-based schedule, not 2023’s line numbering. The supplied [2024 instructions, PDF p.48, printed p.40](https://revenue.mt.gov/files/forms/Montana-Individual-Income-Tax-Return-Form-2-Instructions/2024_Montana_Individual_Income_Tax_Return_Form_2_Instructions.pdf#page=48) identify gross income at line 18 and the contribution calculation at lines 19–22. They prescribe subtraction of $12,600 and the .035 rate for a $7,400 base.

For the 2023 worked companion, set the federal amounts explicitly so the Montana test does not depend on an engine’s federal calculation:

| Form 2EC line | Hand computation |
|---|---|
| 1 | Federal AGI 17,000 |
| 5 | Untaxed Social Security 10,000 |
| 9 | Loss addback 3,000 |
| 10 | **30,000** |
| 11–12 | `30,000 − 12,600 = 17,400` |
| 13–14 | `17,400 × .05 = 870` |
| 15–18 | Property tax billed 2,000; rent equivalent zero |
| 19 | `2,000 − 870 = 1,130` |
| 20 | `min(1,130,1,150) = 1,130` |
| 21–22 | Gross below 35,000: `1,130 × 1 = 1,130` |

### Wiring regressions and additional coverage

The changed joint-itemization fixtures retain totals **9,588**, **16,234**, **8,818**, and **`[2,212,0,0]`** in both `deductions/itemized/mt_itemized_deductions_joint.yaml` and `deductions/itemized/federal_itemization/mt_itemized_deductions_for_federal_itemization_joint.yaml`. They inject deduction components and test summation/wiring; they do not independently establish eligibility or filing rules.

The changed `integration.yaml:546` fixture retains rebates **`[1,250,1,250]`** and tax **6,295.56**. That whole-tax expectation also requires TY2021 rate, exemption, standard-deduction and rebate evidence. It is an integration regression, not an expectation established solely by the allocation pages quoted here.

**Properties and supplemental cases to pin:**

- Each separate filer’s federal deduction is at most $5,000 and at most that filer’s attributed qualifying payments.
- For same-form separate care deductions, the spouse amounts are equal and sum to the common Form 2441-M result.
- Income-based care phase-out uses the combined amount before allocation.
- Loss addbacks occur once; all losses included in AGI, including NOL deductions, are covered.
- Elderly-credit household membership includes qualifying dependent income. PE’s PR acknowledges that omission as a separate follow-up; Axiom must not encode it as an exclusion.
- Gross household income exactly $45,000 fails §2338 eligibility.
- Zero-positive-AGI attribution, negative-tax flooring and positive-dependent-AGI exclusion need separate **methodology** fixtures if the PE projection is implemented. They are not established by the present federal-deduction fixtures.
- Keep unresolved mixed owner/renter adjudication separate from the owner-only credit expectation.

## Related

- PolicyEngine-US proposed PR/branch: `fix-mt-separate-filing-allocations`, local HEAD `304d880bb6`.
- rulespec-us [#1403](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us/issues/1403), [#1416](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us/issues/1416), and [#1494](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us/issues/1494): signed-encoding/parity issue precedents.
- rulespec-us [#782](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us/issues/782): existing resident-pipeline validation waiver.

## Update after the PE review (head 6eefe271dc)

- **Separate forms.** A married person filing on a separate form gets no child and dependent care expense deduction. Authority: MCA 15-30-2131(1)(c)(vi)(A), "married couples shall file a joint return or file separately on the same form", and the 2022 instructions, line 14. Companion case 28: TY2022, federal filing status separate, care expenses 2,000; both the per-column and joint deductions are **0**.
- **Schedule name.** The 2023 credit schedule is the **Elderly Homeowner/Renter Credit Schedule**. It was renamed Schedule 2EC in 2024. The references above to a "2023 Form 2EC" mean that schedule.

Drafted by a Codex research lane from the PolicyEngine-US branch and the downloaded primary sources; checked by Claude Code against the rulespec-us and corpus refs quoted above.


<!-- pe-parity-wave1 pr-9981: MCA 15-30-2131(1)(a), (1)(c)(i)(C) -->

## Wave-1 supplement: qualifying first-listed spouse (PE-US #9981)

Reuse this open `pe-parity` issue for the newly changed historical Montana care qualification; do not duplicate its already documented allocation and repeal blockers. No signed encoder is run by the US hub. Max approved wave-1 billed runs under d1142; the Axiom engineering hub owns dispatch.

Searched rulespec-us main `207486d8b5194b46d52e54e2b1302ec36681f62b`. No module and companion exercises an incapacitated first-listed married filer under former MCA 15-30-2131(1)(c)(i)(C). Target `us-mt/statutes/15-30-2131/1/c.yaml` (or the encoder's generated historical section module). The pinned corpus row `us-mt/statute/15-30-2131` in the July title-15 scope contains only the repeal notice. Its exact body was recovered and verified again for this wave. Admit the operative TY2021–2023 expression and matching year-specific forms before signing. This supplements, and does not lift, the existing source blocker.

### Official operative source, fetched again on 2026-10-09

[Former MCA 15-30-2131](https://mca.legmt.gov/bills/2022/mca/title_0150/chapter_0300/part_0210/section_0310/0150-0300-0210-0310.html) is headed **Montana Code Annotated 2021** despite the URL's `2022` segment. Subsection (1)(c)(i)(C), with HTML spacing normalized:

> (C) a spouse who is unable to provide self-care because of physical or mental illness;

Subsection (1)(c)(vi)(A):

> (A) married couples shall file a joint return or file separately on the same form;

The existing issue supplies the official Form 2441-M arithmetic, expense limits, equal split, and employment restrictions. Keep those conditions. The qualifying spouse is a real marital relationship, independent of which married person is first listed. A single claimant cannot be their own spouse. Generic disability does not establish inability to provide self-care.

### Required outputs and companion tests

Output the qualifying-spouse judgment and resulting qualifying-individual count, then compose the existing historical care calculation. These expectations use the same historical statute cited by #9981's `mt_child_dependent_care_expense_deduction_qualifying_individual.yaml`; no value is produced by PolicyEngine. TY2021; no children or other qualifying individuals; all gainful-employment, household, filing and expense conditions satisfied where relevant.

| Case | Facts | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| First-listed incapable spouse | Married A/B, both age 45; A incapable of self-care because of mental illness; B works; joint or separate same-form return | A qualifies as B's spouse; one qualifying individual |
| Listing exchanged | Same people and legal facts; A second-listed | Same qualification and count 1 |
| Single claimant | A single and incapable; no dependent | No qualifying spouse; count 0 |
| Disability without incapacity | Married A disabled but able to provide self-care | No qualifying spouse through this paragraph |
| Historical limit | Same qualifying-spouse facts in TY2024 | Former care deduction unavailable after repeal; retain the issue's existing date-boundary evidence |

The PR's first-listed output assignment and duplicate prevention are representation conventions. Do not turn those into additional statutory exclusions. Preserve the existing issue's blocked historical-source item and its evidence until an admitted source supports the signed encoding.

### Wave-1 supplement: historical joint mortgage and investment interest

#9981 also changes the historical joint-itemized interest aggregate: it includes qualifying interest of both married filers and excludes a dependent's own interest. This is a taxpayer-qualification and amount rule, not merely output storage. Reuse this issue's former MCA 15-30-2131 source blocker and add a target for subsection (1)(a), `us-mt/statutes/15-30-2131/1/a.yaml` or the encoder's generated historical section module. The consuming corpus still has **only the repeal notice**; this supplement does not lift or rewrite that blocked item.

The same fetched **Montana Code Annotated 2021** official page states, joining HTML link spacing:

> (1) In computing net income, there are allowed as deductions:
> (a) the items referred to in sections 161, including the contributions referred to in 33-15-201(5)(b), and 211 of the Internal Revenue Code, 26 U.S.C. 161 and 211, subject to the following exceptions, which are not deductible:

Interest is subject to the imported federal deduction and qualification rules. The unchanged core language of [26 USC 163(a), official GovInfo 2024 edition](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2024-title26/html/USCODE-2024-title26-subtitleA-chap1-subchapB-partVI-sec163.htm), fetched for this wave and saved in `hub-evidence/pr-9977/sources/uscode163-2024.txt`, states:

> There shall be allowed as a deduction all interest paid or accrued within the taxable year on indebtedness.

Section 163(d)(1) states:

> In the case of a taxpayer other than a corporation, the amount allowed as a deduction under this chapter for investment interest for any taxable year shall not exceed the net investment income of the taxpayer for the taxable year.

Section 163(h)(3)(A) ties qualified-residence interest to the taxpayer's residence:

> The term "qualified residence interest" means any interest which is paid or accrued during the taxable year on—
> (i) acquisition indebtedness with respect to any qualified residence of the taxpayer, or
> (ii) home equity indebtedness with respect to any qualified residence of the taxpayer.

These quotations do not override the year-specific acquisition-debt, home-equity, investment-income or other federal limits. The companions below explicitly supply interest amounts already established as legally deductible for the stated year, after every applicable federal and Montana restriction. A dependent's own loan/investment and residence remain that dependent's taxpayer facts; no §163 qualified interest or election transfers to the parents solely because the dependent is on their return. The federal allowed-investment-interest producer is separately queued in [#1558](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us/issues/1558), with the Montana year-specific form producer in [#1560](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us/issues/1560). Do not substitute the PR's raw expense variable for a legally established allowed amount.

Required output: the TY2021–2023 joint-return interest component equals the allowed mortgage plus allowed investment interest of both filer taxpayers, with the dependent's own interest excluded. Filing-order exchange changes neither that amount nor its taxpayer qualifications. Storing a return-wide output on the first-listed record remains a representation convention.

Companion facts use former MCA 15-30-2131(1)(a), the imported §163 qualifications, and the same interest sources cited by the changed `mt_itemized_deductions_joint.yaml` and `mt_itemized_deductions_for_federal_itemization_joint.yaml`. TY2021 joint Montana return; A/B are the married filers, C is their dependent; all other deduction components are zero and every stated filer interest amount is otherwise legally allowed.

| Case | Legally established own interest amounts A/B/C | Expected joint-return interest |
|---|---|---|
| Mortgage interest | 1,000 / 2,000 / 3,000 on each person's own qualifying debt/residence | **3,000** = 1,000 + 2,000; C's own interest is excluded |
| Investment interest | 1,000 / 2,000 / 3,000 on each person's own investment debt, after §163(d) limits | **3,000** = 1,000 + 2,000; C's own interest is excluded |
| Filer labels exchanged | Exchange A/B listing in either preceding case, preserving ownership/payment/qualification facts | Same **3,000** |

These are source-based conditional amounts, not PolicyEngine-calculated oracles. Admit the operative historical MCA provision and matching annual-form expressions into a signed self-contained release before dispatching this historical aggregate. Preserve the existing **“MCA 15-30-2131 (Montana itemized deductions, 2021–2023) queued, blocked: the corpus has only the repeal notice”** item exactly.

items.title: LIHEAP wave 2b: encode Alaska HAP regular heating assistance

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Alaska HAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 2b, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10341 (branch `ak-liheap-wave2b`), open, not merged. Head `6d826ceb31` (2026-10-23), whose parent merges policyengine-us `main` at `ee6c90961d`; this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **Sources missing from the corpus.** The FY2027 Heating Assistance Program (HAP) manual pages the branch cites are captured in `us-ak-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml` (transmittal 2026-02 edition), and the 2026 HHS poverty guidelines in `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml`. Missing: manual section 3000 (the LIHEAP 150% and AAHP split); section-level text of 7 AAC 44, the heating assistance regulation (corpus `main` holds only the whole Title 7 PDF at page granularity, with section rows for chapter 45 alone); and the sources behind the branch's geography and kerosene inferences (the Census 2025 Alaska places gazetteer, the Alaska DEC Cook Inlet community profiles and page 23 of the Alaska Housing Finance Corporation consumer guide). These need ingest. Transmittal 2026-03 (October 9, 2026) changed only Addendum B contacts and is also uncaptured. `us-ak-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml` and `us-ak-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml` hold the FY2026 edition, which the branch does not cite.
- **Source conflicts not registered.** The shared-dwelling conflict (manual against 7 AAC 44.035(c) and 44.080(h)) has a register entry proposed in draft TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us#1846, which has not merged. The utility-allowance order conflict (manual step 8 against 7 AAC 44.080(l) to (n)) has no proposed entry.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-23; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.
- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10341 was a draft from 2026-10-21 and was marked ready for review on 2026-10-23; a review is requested and none has been received, so there is no revision to pin.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10341, branch `ak-liheap-wave2b`, head `6d826ceb31` (2026-10-23), which closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10335. Commit `fa0c83642f` applies the 2026-10-21 review fixes: unearned income reads `military_retirement_income`, so military Survivor Benefit Plan annuities count; the output-only `ak_hap_income_limit` variable, its `fpg_rate.yaml` and its test file were deleted (the income factor enforces the 150% ceiling); `ak_hap` is labelled the federal LIHEAP component; the `programs.yaml` note names the state-funded AAHP as out of scope; two candidates were added to `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml`; tests gained a survivor-annuity case (`ak_hap.yaml` Case 14), lost three duplicate purchased-fuel cases and were tidied, with no other expected value changed. Commit `6fb9eadb46` replaces the built-in `sum()` over unearned sources with an explicit loop (no behavior change). Merge `62236d1fd6` brings in `main` at `ee6c90961d`. Commit `6d826ceb31` floors each business income source at zero, so a business loss no longer offsets wages or other income; `ak_hap_countable_income.yaml` Cases 3, 4 and 7 now expect $12,000, $3,800 and $100 (were $9,000, $3,200 and $0), and `ak_hap_base_benefit.yaml` Case 48 changed only its comment.
- **Scope:** HAP's federal LIHEAP component, the once-a-season regular heating benefit administered by the Division of Public Assistance (DPA), FY2027: Alaska residence; routing of all-resident tribal communities; at least one citizen or qualified alien; household size from those members; gross countable income of all members; six income bands up to 150% of the Alaska guideline; annual heating costs over $200 (rent when heat is included); the subsidized-housing exclusion; Addendum A community points by fuel; the dwelling factor; the vulnerable point; the 2.0-point minimum; whole-point rounding; the 35-point cap; $175 a point; the shared-dwelling split; and the 50% utility-allowance reduction. Out of scope: the state-funded Alaska Affordable Heating Program (AAHP, above 150% and up to 225% at $130 a point), Subsidized Rental Housing Utility Deposits, crisis and expedited assistance, cooling, weatherization, equipment, supplemental benefits, recoupment, funding order and tribal LIHEAP programs.
- **Policy periods:** one verified season, FY2027: Addendum E applies from October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027; applications run September 1 to April 30 (7 AAC 44.020(c), 44.900(10)); payments start the first state business day in November (44.090(a)). All 21 parameter files hold one `2026-10-01` entry. Alaska variables are annual and read 1 January values, so period `2027` is FY2027 on the 2026 Alaska guidelines (`fpg_year_lag` 1; Addendum E is “Based on January 2026 Federal Register Notice”). `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2027"`. Period `2026` takes the same values by backfilling, on the 2025 guidelines: an unverified estimate (transmittal 2026-02 changed the small-mobile-home factor and North Pole gas points for FY2027). Period `2028` and later carry FY2027 forward on the next guideline: carried-forward estimates. October to December 2027 fall in FY2028 but are read as FY2027.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/ak/dpa/hap/`: `ak_hap`, `ak_hap_base_benefit`, `ak_hap_countable_income`, `ak_hap_household_size`, `ak_hap_income_factor` (calls `fpg` in `variables/gov/hhs/tax_unit_fpg.py`) and the new input `ak_hap_dwelling_type` (eight categories; default TWO_BEDROOM_HOUSE, a modeling assumption).
