## Source text (verbatim)

Quotations come from the official files above as served on 2026-10-23 (HTML converted to text, glossary pop-ups removed, line breaks collapsed; the FR notice and consumer guide by pdftotext). The manual pages match the 2026-10-20 captures except Addendum B contacts.

**Program and season.** Manual 3000: “Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) for households with income up to 150% of the federal poverty income guidelines.”; “Alaska Affordable Heating Program (AAHP) for households with income above 150% and up to 225% of the federal poverty income guidelines.”; “This manual contains policies for state-administered HAP only.” Transmittal 2026-02: “DATE: September 1, 2026”; “Removed mobile homes from the factor for boats with heated living space less than 980 square feet to correct the applicable dwelling factor.”; “Added natural gas points for North Pole.” Addendum E: “FFY 2027”, “October 1, 2026 - September 30, 2027”. 7 AAC 44.020(c): “an identifiable application must be postmarked or received by the department on or after September 1 of a year, but not later than April 30 of the following year.” 44.030(b): “The department will award only one heating assistance payment under 7 AAC 44.080 per household for applications received during the period set out in 7 AAC 44.020.”

**Household and members.** Manual 3000-2: “Household: An individual or group of individuals who are living together as one economic unit and for whom residential heating is customarily purchased in common, or who make undesignated payments for heat in the form of rent.” 3002-1 A.1 requires that “at least one member of the household is a U.S. citizen or qualified alien”. A.10: “All U.S. Citizens and Qualified Aliens residing in the household at the time of application are included when computing the household size.” and “If a household member is not a U.S. citizen or qualified alien, they should not be counted as a family member in the case but their income is counted and included.” D lists citizens and nationals, qualified aliens and “A Compact of Free Association (COFA) migrant from the Federated States of Micronesia, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the Republic of Palau.”, then: “All other household members are treated as excluded household members.” D.6 note: “When determining heating assistance benefits, the illegal alien's income is included in the income calculation but the person is not counted as a family member.” E.3: “A client without a SSN in subsequent application submissions will be excluded from the household size but their income will remain countable.” A.3: “A room renter is not counted as a member of the applicant's household.” 7 AAC 44.035(a): “A household must include (1) the applicant; and (2) a United States citizen or a qualified alien”.

**Eligibility and income limit.** 3002-1 A.1: “the household's annual home heating costs exceed $200;” and “the household's gross monthly income does not exceed 225 percent of the federal poverty guidelines for Alaska as listed in Addendum E.” Manual 3000: “LIHEAP is available to households with income at or below 150% of the federal poverty income guidelines for Alaska.” 7 AAC 44.040(a): “(3) the household's annual home heating costs exceed $200; and (4) the household's gross monthly income is no more than 150 percent of the level set in the federal poverty guidelines for Alaska”. A.2, ineligible: “The household is eligible for or has received benefits from a tribal organization providing heating assistance funded by LIHEAP, unless an agreement to the contrary has been executed between the division and the tribal organization.”; “The household resides in a subsidized rental housing and has no direct home heating costs.” Also ineligible: temporary shelters for less than 60 days, institutions, dormitories, correctional facilities, military bases and some house sitters. Addendum A key: “Indicates the tribe serves Alaska Native/American Indians only.” (*) and “Indicates the tribe serves all residents.” (0); communities without a provider are “served by DPA”; “0/USA - Service members living on base do not qualify.”

**Countable income.** 7 AAC 44.040(c): “The department will calculate the household's gross monthly income by counting total cash receipts before taxes, earned and unearned, derived from any source by any member of the household in the calendar month before the date of signature on the completed application.” and it prorates “income from self-employed occupations, seasonal employment, and irregular work schedules during the 12-month period before the date of signature”. Manual 3003-6 A: “The Heating Assistance Program generally uses actual gross countable income received by the household in the month prior to the application being received.” C: “HAP will calculate their income using a 12-month average of all available income for the previous 12 months from the date they applied.” E: “Income from all members in the household, including ineligible aliens, is counted, except earned income from students under the age of 18 who are not the head of household.” and “All unearned income is counted unless it is specifically listed in HAP MS 3003-2, Non-Countable Income.”

Counted (3003-1): A.1 “Earned income includes, but is not limited to: monetary compensation for services as an employee, including gross earned income before any deductions or garnishments”, including “military pay”; A.3 “Heating Assistance uses net self-employment from the previous 12-month period, after allowable deductions.”; B.1 “Public assistance income includes TANF payments (Alaska Temporary Assistance Program and Native Family Assistance) and APA payments (Aid to the Disabled, Aid to the Blind, Old Age Assistance, Interim Assistance).”; B.2 “Social Security benefits (SSA) - retirement, survivor's disability and dependent benefits; Supplemental Security Income (SSI) - aged, blind and disabled person's benefits; and Veteran's benefits are considered unearned income.” and “The monthly entitlement including the cost of Medicare, if deducted, is counted as income in the month of intended use.”; B.3 child support received, but for TANF recipients “Only the first $50 per month received and kept by TANF recipients directly from the non-custodial parent is countable.”; B.6 workers' compensation, unemployment insurance, “Annuities, pensions, retirement, and disability benefits”, alimony, “Rental income (gross income minus costs of doing business).”, “Dividends, interest, royalties, estates, trusts and similar recurring payments”, strike benefits, “Any money benefit not otherwise exempted including lump sum payments unless specified as not countable”, bingo and lottery winnings, “BIA General Assistance Program payments made to the household”, “Cash gifts over $20 per person, per month” and capital gains. B.6.h: “The Heating Assistance Program does not count Alaska PFDs unless it is received by a household for a person who is not a household member.”

Self-employment (3003-4): A.7 “Adjusted gross self-employment income means the gross self-employment earnings less allowable costs of doing business.”; B.1 “The self-employment standard deduction is 50% of the estimated gross self-employment income.”; B.2.b disallows “Net losses from previous periods.” A.3: “When the property owner is not actively engaged in the management of the property for at least 20 hours per week, costs of doing business are deducted from the rental income and the adjusted gross income is considered unearned income.”

Not counted (3003-2 A): 6 “Any gain or benefit that is not in the form of money is exempt income”; 9 a housing authority payment to the household “is called a utility allowance or utility reimbursement and is included as income.”; 10 “For HAP, ANCSA payments are fully exempt, regardless of the amount received.”; 14 “ATAP benefits are only countable to the HAP household when the parent or caretaker relative receiving the benefit on behalf of the child(ren) are included in the HAP household.”; 15 “Earned income of a student is exempt when an individual:” is “under age 18”, “Lives with his or her parents or is under parental control of an adult household member” and “Is currently enrolled at least half-time in elementary or secondary school.”; 19 “State of Alaska GRA program payments paid on behalf of the household to a vendor for household expenses such as rent, food, fuel, clothing, utilities, house repair, transportation, and burial are exempt.”; 24 “Cash gifts under $20 per person per month are non-countable.”; 30 Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend; 31 Alaska's Senior Benefits. 7 AAC 44.042 exempts “(2) payments received under 43 U.S.C. 1601 — 1629 (Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act); (3) payments received under AS 43.23 (Alaska permanent fund dividend program)”, “(5) wages received by a full-time student under 18 years of age who is not the head of household”, “(16) cash gifts that do not exceed a total of $20 per month per individual in the household”, “(18) payments received under 7 AAC 38.030 (General Relief Assistance)” and “(20) payments received under AS 47.45.301 — 47.45.309 (senior benefits payment program)”.

**Heating costs and housing.** 3000-2: “Home Heating Costs: An amount the household pays for its own home heating needs either directly or indirectly through rent.” 3001-4 C: “When heat and/or electricity is included in rent, the rental payment itself is considered the household’s heating and/or electric expense for purposes of meeting the annual heating cost requirement.” 3000-2: “Subsidized Housing: Housing subsidized by a government, housing authority, or non-profit entity, in which tenants pay only a portion of their adjusted monthly income for rent, mortgage, and home heat.” 3007-1: “If the applicant lives in subsidized rental housing (public housing) and heat is included in the rent, the application is denied.”; “If the household is receiving any type of utility allowance for heat, the HAP benefit is processed normally and the final amount is reduced by 50 percent because they are already receiving a subsidy towards heating costs.”; for LIHTC and home purchase programs, “If there is a utility allowance, the household's final point count will be reduced by 50 percent.” 3004-4: “For the purposes of identifying the fuel type, it does not matter if the applicant pays for their own heat or has heat included in the rent payment.”

**Benefit rule.** Manual 3004-5, Step 1: “If the household primarily uses natural gas for heat, use the community heating cost points for natural gas. If no natural gas points are listed for a specific community, use the points from the nearest community with natural gas on the listing.”; self-harvested wood or coal “multiplied by 0.5”; “If the household primarily uses purchased wood or coal for heat, use the community heating cost points for oil multiplied by 0.8.”; wood pellets “multiplied by 0.9”; steam, electric and gasoline for a vehicle lived in for 60 days or more use oil points. Step 2: “Multiply the community heating cost points by the first factor listed below that describes the household's dwelling:” 1.4 (mobile home or boat, 980 heated square feet or more), 0.4 (recreational vehicle, tent, or pickup camper), 0.15 (one-room dwelling such as a studio apartment, hotel, or boarding home), 0.35 (boat under 980 square feet), 0.55 (one-bedroom dwelling, or one-room house or cabin), 1.3 (three-or-more-bedroom single family, duplex, or triplex home), 0.7 (“a two-bedroom unit in an apartment building of four or more attached units or resides in a mobile home with less than 980 square feet of heated living space, regardless of the number of bedrooms”), 1 (“two-bedroom single family home, duplex, or triplex home”), 0 (SRHUD); “A loft counts as one bedroom.” Last sentence: “If the household resides in a single residence with one or more households, the heating cost points are reduced to the household's proportionate share of the home heating expenses.” Step 3: “100 percent of points if the household's gross monthly income is no more than 25 percent of Alaska's federal poverty level;” then 90, 80, 70, 60 and 50 percent “more than 125 percent but no more than 150 percent of Alaska's FPL.” (AAHP bands follow); “If the household's gross monthly income exceeds the maximum allowable FPL, the household is not eligible.” Step 4: “Add one point to the income adjusted heating cost points if the household meets the vulnerable population definition per HAP MS 3000-2.” Step 5: “Households must have heating cost points of 2.0 or more to be eligible for HAP.” Step 6: “Round the final total heating cost points to the nearest whole number. The total heating cost points is limited to 35 points.” Step 8: “Households residing in any type of subsidized housing who are responsible for paying all or a portion of their heating costs directly to a vendor and who also receive a utility allowance as part of their housing cost calculation shall have their total benefit reduced by 50 percent, regardless of their utility allowance amount.” Rate: “For the FY 2027 heating assistance season, this rate is $175 per point for LIHEAP eligible households and $130 per point for AAHP eligible households.”

3000-2: “Vulnerable Population: Households containing an older adult, disabled person, or child under 6.”; “Elderly: A person age 60 years or older.”; “Disabled: A person with a physical or mental impairment, which limits one or more major life activities, as determined by eligibility for:” veterans or Social Security disability benefits, SSI, APA, permanent disability retirement or a qualifying railroad annuity. 3002-1 A.13: “Households that include one or more members who are 60 years of age or older, legally disabled, or under six years of age are recognized by HAP as vulnerable populations”. 3004-4 lists “Coal”, “Electric/Steam”, “Gasoline”, “Kerosene”, “Natural Gas”, “Oil”, “Propane”, “Wood Pellets”, “Wood (cord)”. 3000-2: “Deliverable Fuel: Fuel such as oil, kerosene, wood, or coal that is not metered and requires delivery by truck or counter sale pick-up.” Consumer guide, page 23: “Grade 1 heating oil (also known as kerosene or fuel oil No. 1) is often used in buildings with an above-ground storage tank”.

7 AAC 44.080: (f) “If a household uses electricity, steam, hot water, or propane for heat, the department will use the community heating cost points for oil in Appendix A.”; (g) the same eight factors, “(8) the factor of 1.0 if the household resides in a two-bedroom single-family home.”; (h) “If the household resides in a single dwelling with one or more other households, the heating cost points determined under (a) - (g) of this section are reduced to the household's proportionate share of the home heating expenses.”; (i)(6) “50 percent of points if the household's gross monthly income is more than 125 percent of the Alaska poverty level but no more than the maximum allowable Alaska poverty level under this chapter.”; (k) “The department will add one point to the heating cost points determined under (a) - (i) of this section if the household includes one or more members 60 years of age or older, legally disabled, or under six years of age.”; (l) “The department will reduce the heating cost points determined under (a) - (k) of this section by 50 percent, regardless of the amount of the utility allowance for heat”; (m) “A household with heating cost points determined under (a) - ( l) of this section to be less than 2.0 is not eligible”; (n) “The department will round the total heating cost points computed in (a) - ( l) of this section to the nearest whole number and multiply by the benefit rate”; (o) “The total heating cost points determined under (n) of this section may not exceed 35 points.” Appendix A footnote: “the department will use the natural gas points from the geographically closest community with natural gas listed in Appendix A.” Appendix A lists Loring oil 5, Tetlin oil 16 and North Pole gas N/A; FFY2027 Addendum A lists 4, 12 and 8.

**Shared dwellings.** 3002-1 A.3 note: “Each household in the dwelling should be worked separately and then the share reduction applied.” A.5: “If the household resides in a single residence with one or more other households, the total grant amount is reduced to the household's proportion of the total number of households in the dwelling.”; “In a house sharer situation, a household's share should never exceed 50%. The amount each household contributes to heat or rent is not considered.”; “The benefit is based upon the total number of eligible households in a residence, regardless of how many apply.” 7 AAC 44.035(c): “If more than one household lives in the same dwelling, the department will determine an award for each household as if it were the sole household in the dwelling and pay the household a percentage of that household's award equal to the percentage of the total heating cost for the dwelling that the household actually pays.”

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Shared dwellings (source conflict, candidate `us-ak:hap-shared-household-allocation`).** The branch follows manual 3002-1 A.3 to A.5: each SPM unit's award is computed alone, then divided by the number of SPM units in the household with a positive award, at most 50%. 7 AAC 44.035(c) pays each household its actual share of the dwelling's heating cost; 44.080(h) and the last sentence of manual step 2 reduce points to that share before the income factor, minimum and rounding. The register entry is proposed in draft TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us#1846 (not merged); the branch adds no source-conflict marker yet. SPM units stand in for economic households; room renters and owner-occupants (A.3) are not identified, and a co-resident SPM unit without an award is not counted.
2. **Utility-allowance order (source conflict, candidate `us-ak:hap-utility-allowance-order`).** The branch halves the rounded dollar award under step 8 and 3007-1, whatever the allowance amount. 7 AAC 44.080(l) to (n) halves points before the 2.0 minimum and rounding, and 3007-1's last bullet speaks of the final point count for LIHTC and purchase programs. No register entry is proposed for this order.
3. **One-person 25% cell.** Addendum E prints $407; 25% of the 2026 guideline gives $415 ($1,662 x 0.25 = $415.50, rounded down); $407 matches the 2025 guideline ($19,550 / 12 = $1,629, x 0.25 = $407, 90 FR 5917). The branch follows the step 3 rule ($415). Incomes from $408 to $415 a month get 1.0 instead of 0.9.
4. **Band tops and rounding (inferred).** The branch reproduces Addendum E by rounding the monthly guideline down, then each percentage down, and treats each printed top as inclusive; this matches the other 161 published cells (18 sizes by nine bands, AAHP bands included). A reading against the unrounded percentage would move incomes up to about $1 a month above a printed top into the lower band. Points round half up (“nearest whole number”); the 2.0 minimum applies before rounding.
5. **Annual income (simplification).** Alaska uses gross income of the month before application, a 12-month average for self-employment, seasonal and irregular work, and an application-month exception (3003-6). The branch divides annual amounts by 12. The self-employment annualization standard (3003-4 E) is not modeled.
6. **Business and rental income (simplification).** Supplied net business income stands in for gross less the 50% standard or actual costs; no second deduction is taken. Each business input is floored at zero (the partnership and S corporation aggregate as one), as are wages, each unearned source, rental income and farm rental income, so a loss in one source offsets no other income; neither manual 3003-4 nor 7 AAC 44 provides for a current business loss to reduce other income, and 7 AAC 44.040(c) counts “total cash receipts”. Losses inside one source (several businesses, or partnership against S corporation income), losses from earlier periods and disallowed tax expenses cannot be separated; supplied net rent stands in for gross rent less costs, and active management of 20 hours a week (earned rent) is not identified.
7. **Income items without a matching input.** `ordinary_dividend_income` includes ANCSA dividends, which are fully exempt (3003-2 A.10; 7 AAC 44.042(2)). The PFD and Senior Benefits are not counted, including a PFD received for a non-member. Social Security counts gross, as the code comment says (3003-1 B.2.c). `general_assistance` counts as cash assistance; the manual exempts GRA vendor payments (A.19) and 7 AAC 44.042(18) exempts all General Relief Assistance. All child support received counts; the $50 limit for TANF recipients is not applied. Veterans and disability subtypes, education assistance, foster care, royalties, trusts, lump sums, property sales, excess reimbursements and cash utility reimbursements have no separate input; `hud_utility_allowance` is not treated as income.
8. **Cash gifts at exactly $20 (source wording).** Manual A.24 excludes gifts “under $20”; B.6.r counts gifts “over $20”; 7 AAC 44.042(16) excludes gifts that “do not exceed a total of $20”. The branch excludes amounts under $20 a month per person and counts $20 in full, using `financial_assistance` divided by 12.
9. **Student earnings (proxy).** Manual A.15 (under 18, under parental control, at least half-time in elementary or secondary school), 3003-6 E (not head of household) and 7 AAC 44.042(5) (full-time student) differ in wording; the branch excludes the earnings of a member under 18 who is a tax dependent in K-12 or secondary school.
10. **Household, status and the vulnerable point (proxies).** `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant` stands in for citizens, nationals, qualified aliens and COFA migrants, with no five-year bar; SSN and documentation rules, custody, foster members and room renters are not modeled. Excluded members' income counts. Only counted members add the vulnerable point, a reading the text does not state. `is_disabled` stands in for the manual's benefit-based disability list.
11. **Fuels (inference and coverage limit).** Fuel oil and electricity use oil points (step 1); propane does under 7 AAC 44.080(f) though step 1 omits it; kerosene does by inference (fuel types list, deliverable fuel definition, consumer guide page 23). WOOD and COAL use the purchased factor 0.8; `heating_type` cannot identify self-harvested fuel (0.5) or pellets (0.9). Steam, hot water and gasoline for a vehicle used as a home have no `heating_type`; OTHER and SOLAR pay $0. `heating_type` is a required input; UNSPECIFIED pays $0 (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the default). NONE is no heat.
12. **Geography (derived crosswalk).** Points attach to Census `place_fips`: 262 places carry oil points; 355 carry gas points, 25 by direct match and 330 by the nearest published gas community (great-circle distance, Census and DEC locations), which is not a state crosswalk. The Anchorage municipality has no oil value because its listed communities differ (Anchorage 08, Chugiak 07); unmatched places pay $0 as a modeling gap, not a denial. The FFY2027 Addendum A is used over the regulation's Appendix A (Loring 4 and Tetlin 12 against 5 and 16; North Pole gas 8 against N/A).
13. **Tribal routing.** All residents of the 119 Census places whose Addendum A provider is marked 0 get $0; Native-only providers (*) and 0/USA bases are not routed, and tribal enrollment is never inferred. Tribal agreements and denials for failing tribal rules are not modeled.
14. **Heating cost and housing (proxies).** Annual `pre_subsidy_rent` is the heating cost when heat is in rent; the award is not capped at the cost. Subsidized means `receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing`; LIHTC without a voucher is not identified. `hud_utility_allowance` has no Alaska schedule and is 0 unless supplied; the step-down exception after year one is not modeled.
15. **Dwelling input.** `ak_hap_dwelling_type` defaults to TWO_BEDROOM_HOUSE (factor 1), a modeling assumption; callers choose the first matching category.
16. **Limits and programs.** 3002-1 A.1 states 225% (with AAHP); manual 3000 and 7 AAC 44.040(a)(4) state 150% for LIHEAP. The branch models only the federal component, so households above 150% get $0. Categorical eligibility changes verification, not the amount.
17. **Worked examples (stale labels).** Step 3 Examples 2 and 3 carry earlier bands: Example 2 (size 2, $2,800) is labelled 125.01-150% but is at or below $2,817 (100-125%) and pays $875 either way; Example 3 (Savoonga, size 5, $3,000) is labelled 75.01-100% and $3,500, but $3,000 is at or below $3,021, giving 0.8, 22.6 points and $4,025. Companion test 4(d) uses $2,900.
18. **Years and dates.** See Policy periods: only FY2027 (period 2027) is verified; the parameters start `2026-10-01`; other periods are estimates.
19. **Other gaps.** The one-benefit-per-season rule, application order and funding, supplemental benefits, recoupment, residence in institutions, dormitories, bases or temporary shelters under 60 days, house sitters, SRHUD, credit balances and AAHP are not modeled.

Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-ak/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the FY2027 Addendum E bands for sizes 1 to 18 with inclusive tops and the one-person 25% cell, the 150% limit, Addendum A oil and gas points with the nearest-gas rule and unmapped places, every dwelling factor, every fuel (propane, kerosene, purchased wood and coal, other, solar, no heat and unspecified), the vulnerable point (age 60, under 6, disability, counted members only), the 2.0 minimum before rounding, half-up rounding, the 35-point cap, $175 a point, the $200 cost test with rent for heat in rent, the subsidized exclusion and the utility-allowance halving and its order, shared dwellings and their source conflict, all-resident tribal routing, excluded members (income counted, size not), student earnings, gifts, per-source floors for business, rental and unearned income, every listed countable and excluded source, and any period other than 2027 kept in scope. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: Encode IRC §1(g)(7) parent's election (the rule that decides whether a child's items reach a parent's return)

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Encoding gap

rulespec-us has no rule that decides which return a dependent child's items go on. PolicyEngine-US got this wrong: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9646 deducts a dependent's rental, business and capital losses from the parent's AGI, and the fix is PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9647. Axiom cannot check either side, because the one statutory election that moves a child's items onto a parent's return, 26 U.S.C. §1(g)(7), is not encoded.

**What the search found** (rulespec-us `origin/main` `54d90a725`):

- **No §1(g)(7) module.** `us/statutes/26/1/` holds only `h.yaml` and `j.yaml` and their tests. A grep of `us/` for `1(g)`, `8814` and `kiddie` finds only the AMT kiddie-tax exemption addition in `us/policies/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/alternative-minimum-tax.yaml` and a §1(g)-child flag input in `lifetime_learning_credit_pipeline.yaml`.
- **AGI takes return-level inputs.** `us/statutes/26/62.yaml` rule `adjusted_gross_income` (`entity: TaxUnit`, `effective_from: '1990-01-01'`) is `max(0, gross_income - deductions_described_in_subsection_a)`. Both operands are TaxUnit inputs, and the module defers the (a) composition (`deferred_outputs`: `us:statutes/26/62/a#deductions_described_in_subsection_a`).
- **The capital-loss limit also takes return-level inputs.** `us/statutes/26/1211.yaml` rule `other_taxpayer_capital_losses_allowed` (`entity: TaxUnit`) limits the return's own `losses_from_sales_or_exchanges_of_capital_assets` to gains plus $3,000 ($1,500 for a separate return).
- **So no Axiom rule pools a dependent's items into another return,** though the oracle bridge does (see "Why this matters"). But no rule or companion test says which items cross, and nothing covers the case PolicyEngine got wrong. `us/statutes/26/63/c/5.yaml` already models a dependent's own return as a separate TaxUnit, through the relation `exemption_individual_of_another_tax_unit`.
- **§461(l) is not encoded either** (no `us/statutes/26/461*`). It is not in the pinned corpus; `us/statute/26/461/l` is only in the `2026-09-13-tax-statute-closure-31-title-26` corpus version. It is out of scope here and noted under "Related".

## Why this matters

- **PolicyEngine-US 2.15.1** (engine output, not evidence of the law): TY2025, TX. The head has wages 20,000, taxable interest 9,000 and rental income 4,000. A dependent child has a rental loss of 4,000. PE gives the parent AGI 29,000. The parent's own return has AGI 33,000 (NBER `taxsimtest` v10, build `cd2026081819`, with only the parent's items).
- **Cause.** `irs_gross_income` drops dependents' income, but `loss_ald` and `limited_capital_loss` sum every tax-unit member.
- **Population.** On PE-US 2.15.1's default Populace 2025 dataset, the fix raises AGI in 93,953 weighted tax units by $593M in total, and raises income tax by $127M.
- **Oracle lanes cannot catch it today.** The axiom-oracles Populace lane copies PolicyEngine's own `adjusted_gross_income` into Axiom (`project_tax_unit_inputs`, `axiom_oracles/bridges/tax_populace.py:1930`, axiom-oracles `b22a8525b`).
- **The oracle bridge also pools dependents.** For a child's short-term loss of 4,000, the case-path projection at axiom-oracles `b22a8525b` sends `us:statutes/26/1/h#input.short_term_capital_gains = -4000` on the parent's TaxUnit, and `relation.business_income_of_tax_unit` lists the dependents. Probe: `probe_oracle_projections.py`, run against `git archive b22a8525b`.

## Statute (verbatim, pinned corpus)

The source is axiom-corpus `data/corpus/provisions/us/statute/2026-07-13-recovery-r2026-07-15-self-contained-r2026-07-17-dedup.jsonl`:
- row `us/statute/26/1/g/7` (line 807, heading "Election to claim certain unearned income of child on parent’s return");
- source USLM `usc26-section-1.xml`;
- at the pinned `axiom_corpus_ref` `8f7d60aac` (`.axiom/workflow-toolchain.toml`).

It matches the OLRC text ("laws in effect on September 25, 2026"), apart from dash glyphs.

**Scope.** The paragraph applies to a child to whom §1(g) applies and to the parent determined under §1(g)(5).

> (A) In general If— (i) any child to whom this subsection applies has gross income for the taxable year only from interest and dividends (including Alaska Permanent Fund dividends), (ii) such gross income is more than the amount described in paragraph (4)(A)(ii)(I) and less than 10 times the amount so described, (iii) no estimated tax payments for such year are made in the name and TIN of such child, and no amount has been deducted and withheld under section 3406, and (iv) the parent of such child (as determined under paragraph (5)) elects the application of subparagraph (B), such child shall be treated (other than for purposes of this paragraph) as having no gross income for such year and shall not be required to file a return under section 6012.
>
> (B) Income included on parent’s return In the case of a parent making the election under this paragraph— (i) the gross income of each child to whom such election applies (to the extent the gross income of such child exceeds twice the amount described in paragraph (4)(A)(ii)(I)) shall be included in such parent’s gross income for the taxable year, (ii) the tax imposed by this section for such year with respect to such parent shall be the amount equal to the sum of— (I) the amount determined under this section after the application of clause (i), plus (II) for each such child, 10 percent of the lesser of the amount described in paragraph (4)(A)(ii)(I) or the excess of the gross income of such child over the amount so described, and (iii) any interest which is an item of tax preference under section 57(a)(5) of the child shall be treated as an item of tax preference of such parent (and not of such child).
>
> (C) Regulations The Secretary shall prescribe such regulations as may be necessary or appropriate to carry out the purposes of this paragraph.

(B)(i) moves only the child's **gross income**. Nothing in the paragraph moves a deduction or a loss.

**Amount.** Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §3.02, printed page 13 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf, sha256 `e9ada115…4635b`, `pdftotext -layout`):

> .02 Unearned Income of Minor Children Subject to the "Kiddie Tax". For taxable years beginning in 2026, the amount in § 1(g)(4)(A)(ii)(I), which is used to reduce the net unearned income reported on the child's return that is subject to the "kiddie tax," is $1,350. This $1,350 amount is the same as the amount provided in § 63(c)(5)(A), as adjusted for inflation. The same $1,350 amount is used for purposes of § 1(g)(7) to determine whether a parent may elect to include a child's gross income in the parent's gross income and to calculate the "kiddie tax." For example, one of the requirements for the parental election is that a child's gross income is more than the amount referred to in § 1(g)(4)(A)(ii)(I) but less than 10 times that amount; thus, a child's gross income for 2026 must be more than $1,350 but less than $13,500.

The $1,350 is already encoded as `us:policies/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/standard-deduction#dependent_standard_deduction_floor_amount` (`standard-deduction.yaml:84`; its test expects 1350).

## Encoding path

- **Signed encoder only.** Use axiom-encode's `targeted-signed-reencode.yml` (the `production-signing` environment) or a supervised `axiom-encode encode us/statute/26/1/g/7 --apply`. Hand-written RuleSpec is rejected by the generated-guard. OpenAI-billed signed runs need Max's approval.
- **Pin.** `.axiom/workflow-toolchain.toml` pins `axiom_encode_version` 0.2.2049 (`06b01708`) and `axiom_corpus_ref` `8f7d60aac`. The corpus row above is at that ref.
- **New file.** `us/statutes/26/1/g/7.yaml` has no validation waiver or open PR, and nothing else imports it yet.

## Plan

### Step 1. Encode `us/statutes/26/1/g/7.yaml` (corpus citation `us/statute/26/1/g/7`)

`review_finding`:

> Encode 26 USC 1(g)(7) (corpus us/statute/26/1/g/7) as its own module at us/statutes/26/1/g/7.yaml. Nothing in rulespec-us says which return a dependent child's items belong on, and PolicyEngine-US deducted dependents' losses from the parent's AGI. The paragraph is the only statutory election that moves a child's items onto a parent's return, and it moves gross income only, never a deduction or loss. Import the §1(g)(4)(A)(ii)(I) amount from us:policies/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/standard-deduction#dependent_standard_deduction_floor_amount ($1,350 for 2026, which Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §3.02 says is the same amount); do not re-author it. Entity: the child's TaxUnit, as us/statutes/26/63/c/5.yaml models a dependent's own return.
>
> Required outputs, each with verbatim proof excerpts from the corpus provision:
>
> 1. (A)(i) Bool: the child's gross income for the year is only from interest and dividends (including Alaska Permanent Fund dividends). Leaf inputs: the child's gross income and the child's interest and dividends. The test holds when gross income equals interest plus dividends.
> 2. (A)(ii) Bool: that gross income is more than the imported amount and less than 10 times it. Both comparisons are strict.
> 3. (A)(iii) Bool: no estimated tax payments were made in the child's name and TIN, and nothing was withheld under section 3406. Take two leaf Bool inputs scoped exactly so.
> 4. (A)(iv) Bool: the parent determined under paragraph (5) elects. This is a leaf input; paragraph (5) is a deferred dependency.
> 5. `parent_election_applies` Bool = (A)(i) and (A)(ii) and (A)(iii) and (A)(iv). When it holds, the child is treated as having no gross income (other than for this paragraph) and is not required to file under section 6012.
> 6. (B)(i) Money `child_gross_income_included_in_parent_gross_income` = if the election applies, max(0, the child's gross income − 2 × the imported amount); otherwise 0.
> 7. (B)(ii)(II) Money `parent_tax_addition_for_child` = if the election applies, 10% × min(the imported amount, max(0, the child's gross income − the imported amount)); otherwise 0.
> 8. (B)(iii) Money: the child's §57(a)(5) tax-preference interest, treated as the parent's. This is a pass-through of a leaf input.
>
> Invariant: output 6 is never negative, and nothing in this module lowers a parent's gross income or AGI.

### Step 2. Oracle coverage

Run `axiom-encode oracle-coverage-pending sync` for the new outputs (precedent: #1381).

### Step 3. Later wiring (not in this dispatch)

When the §62(a) deduction composition (`us:statutes/26/62/a#deductions_described_in_subsection_a`) is encoded, key its (a)(1), (a)(3) and (a)(4) components to the return's own taxpayer or taxpayers. Add a fixture in which a dependent's loss is an input of the dependent's TaxUnit and leaves the parent's `adjusted_gross_income` unchanged.

## Companion tests

All tests are TY2026, on the child's TaxUnit, with the imported amount of $1,350. Unlisted inputs are 0 or false, and (A)(iii) holds and (A)(iv) elects unless noted.

- **Cases 1–6** are hand-computed from the statute and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §3.02 above, and cross-checked against Form 8814 line arithmetic.
- **Case 1** is the official worked example in the Instructions for Form 8814 (2025), pp. 3–4, "Capital Gain Distributions — Example" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8814.pdf, sha256 `2a2ec11f…9cc6`). That example's base amounts ($1,350 and $2,700) are the same as TY2026's.
- **Cases 7–9** are regression anchors for Step 3, in the existing `62.test.yaml` and `1211.test.yaml` rather than in `1/g/7.test.yaml`. They check `62.yaml` and `1211.yaml` with the same external ground truth as the PolicyEngine-US tests: the NBER `taxsimtest` binary (build `cd2026081819`, TY2026, state 0), run on the parent's own return only. TAXSIM has no input for a dependent's income.

**Worked example text.** Instructions for Form 8814 (2025), pp. 3–4:

> Example. Fred is 6 years old. In 2025, he received dividend income of $2,800, which included $2,190 of ordinary dividends and a $610 capital gain distribution from a mutual fund. [...] He has no other income and isn’t subject to backup withholding. No estimated tax payments were made under his name and SSN. Fred’s parents elect to include Fred’s income on their tax return instead of filing a return for him. [...] They subtract the base amount on line 5, $2,700, from the amount on line 4, $2,800, and enter the result, $100, on line 6. This is the total amount from Form 8814 to be reported on their return.

**Form 8814 (2025) Part II**, lines 13–15, gives the tax addition: "13 Amount not taxed $1,350", "14 Subtract line 13 from line 4", "15 Tax. Is the amount on line 14 less than $1,350? No. Enter $135 [...] Yes. Multiply line 14 by 10%".

| # | Case | Inputs | (A)(i) | (A)(ii) | election applies | (B)(i) included | (B)(ii)(II) addition | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fred (Form 8814 example) | gross income 2,800; dividends 2,800 | holds | holds | holds | 2,800 − 2,700 = **100** | 10% × min(1,350, 1,450) = **135** | 8814 example: line 6 is $100. Line 14 is 1,450, which is not less than 1,350, so line 15 is $135. |
| 2 | interest only | gross income 5,000; interest 5,000 | holds | holds | holds | **2,300** | **135** | (B)(i), (B)(ii)(II) |
| 3 | small, under the 10% cap | gross income 2,000; interest 2,000 | holds | holds | holds | max(0, 2,000 − 2,700) = **0** | 10% × min(1,350, 650) = **65** | Form 8814 line 15 "Yes" branch |
| 4 | **PE parity: child has a rental loss** | interest 5,000; gross rents 6,000 and rental expenses 10,000 (net rental −4,000). Gross income is 11,000, because gross rents are gross income under §61(a)(5). | **not_holds** (6,000 of gross income is neither interest nor dividends) | — | **not_holds** | **0** | **0** | (A)(i). The child's rental loss stays on the child's own return. |
| 5 | at the floor | gross income 1,350; interest 1,350 | holds | **not_holds** (not "more than" 1,350) | not_holds | 0 | 0 | (A)(ii) |
| 6 | at the ceiling | gross income 13,500; interest 13,500 | holds | **not_holds** (not "less than" 13,500) | not_holds | 0 | 0 | (A)(ii); Form 8814 line 4, "If the total is $13,500 or more, do not file this form" |
| 7 | parent's own return, `62.yaml` | `gross_income` 33,000 (wages 20,000, interest 9,000, rents 4,000); `deductions_described_in_subsection_a` 0 | | | | | | `adjusted_gross_income` **33,000** = TAXSIM v10 33,000.00 (the child in case 4 contributes nothing) |
| 8 | parent's own capital gain, `1211.yaml` | gains 4,000; losses 0 | | | | | | `other_taxpayer_capital_losses_allowed` **0**. The parent's AGI with wages 20,000, interest 9,000 and long-term gain 4,000 is TAXSIM v10 33,000.00; the child's short-term loss of 4,000 is on the child's return. |
| 9 | parent's own capital loss, `1211.yaml` | gains 0; losses 5,000; filing status head of household | | | | | | `other_taxpayer_capital_losses_allowed` **3,000**. AGI with wages 50,000 is TAXSIM v10 47,000.00. |

If the encoder's leaf input is "gross income from sources other than interest and dividends", set it to 6,000 in case 4.

**Properties the tests should pin, for every input:**

- (B)(i) ≥ 0, and (B)(i) ≤ the child's gross income.
- (B)(ii)(II) ≤ 10% × the imported amount, which is 135 for 2026.
- The election never applies when any gross income comes from outside interest and dividends.

## Related

- PolicyEngine:
  - PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9646 and the fix, PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9647;
  - PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9618, a dependent's own return;
  - PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9635, the EITC investment income test.
- rulespec-us:
  - #1416 and #1403 (template, same pattern);
  - §461(l) encoding, not yet in the pinned corpus.
- axiom-oracles: the Populace lane copies PE's AGI (`bridges/tax_populace.py:1930`).

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Wyoming LIEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 2b, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10346 (branch `wy-liheap-wave2b`), open, not merged. Head `5c968f998b` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `ee6c90961d`; this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **Sources missing from the corpus.** No axiom-corpus manifest on `main` holds either of the branch's two main sources: the Wyoming LIEAP rules (Family Services, Chapter 1, reference 049.0024.1.10312012, effective October 31, 2012: household, income, exemptions, vulnerability, benefit calculation, the $10 minimum, overpayments) and the FY2026 benefit matrix workbook `WY_BenefitMatrix_2026.xlsx` (six fuel cost standards, Table 1 fractions, 10% holdback). The corpus LIHEAP queue records the Wyoming matrix as absent (the Clearinghouse answered 404 for the 2026 file on 2026-09-14); on 2026-10-23 the Clearinghouse served it, byte-identical to the copy the branch was built from (SHA-256 `7ed173d7aa618fb3f2f6d2eeb4da55936685c2f9010825087703a5209056ead0`). Also missing: the FFY2026 Wyoming state median income (SMI) amounts behind every FY2026 limit (the Clearinghouse page the code cites and HHS LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 4, which the shared SMI parameter cites), 42 U.S.C. 8624 (the federal 110% floor), the About LIEAP handout of September 24, 2026 (FY2027 limits), the draft FY2027 plan and the 2016 DFS statute clean-up memo behind one candidate. These need ingest. Captured: the FY2026 plan (Clearinghouse copy; the code links the DFS copy, with identical text and matching renders of the check-box pages compared), Wyoming Statutes Title 42 (whole-title PDF, the file the code links), the 2025 HHS poverty guidelines, the FY2027 SMI table and the CMS 2026 Part B premium. No manifest holds a different edition of a cited source, but the LIHEAP program bundle marks the FY2026 plan, the only captured Wyoming LIHEAP document, as excluded (“Back-year table: not current law”), though FY2026 is the branch's only verified year.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-23; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.
- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10346 was a draft from 2026-10-21 and is marked ready for review on 2026-10-23 with no reviews yet, so there is no revision to pin.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10346, branch `wy-liheap-wave2b`, head `5c968f998b` (2026-10-23), which closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10340. Three commits of 2026-10-23: `9b5042a826` applies the 2026-10-21 review fixes (military Survivor Benefit Plan annuities count through `military_retirement_income`, which replaces `military_retirement_pay` in the income list; Social Security counts net of the computed `medicare_part_b_premium`; the $10 minimum now applies to the computed benefit before the actual-cost cap; two `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml` entries; a comment that the plan's “No” to categorical eligibility is followed over rules 7(a)(i); plan references cite pages 5-6; the 17-member federal-floor fixture becomes the compact Case 151; Cases 151 and 152 are named; Cases 153 and 154 are added; Cases 129, 130 and 147 change for the cutoff order). `932f077d48` replaces the built-in `sum()` over person calls in `wy_lieap_countable_income` with explicit loops (no behavior change). `5c968f998b` merges policyengine-us `main` at `ee6c90961d`. Everything below describes that head; oracle fixtures will pin the merged commit.
- **Scope:** Wyoming LIEAP regular heating assistance, the seasonal heating benefit of the Department of Family Services (DFS) for FY2026: Wyoming residence, household size from citizens and qualified noncitizens (other members' income still counts), gross countable income (earnings of members 18 and over less child support paid, unearned income of all members, Social Security net of the Medicare Part B premium, interest and gifts over $30 a month, veterans benefits over 100% of the poverty guideline), the 60% SMI limit with the federal 110% poverty floor, responsibility for a primary heating cost, the fuel cost standard of the primary fuel (coal, heating oil, electricity, natural gas, propane, wood) times the Table 1 entitlement fraction, the 10% holdback, the $10 minimum and the cap at the actual primary fuel cost. Out of scope: crisis assistance, cooling, weatherization, heating-equipment repair or replacement, the hidden 5% and 15% holdback tables, release of the holdback, work registration, application timing and priority intake, vendor payment, overpayment recovery and tribal LIHEAP.
- **Policy periods:** one verified season, FY2026: plan item 1.1 dates heating assistance October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026 (page 4), applications open to priority households on September 2, 2025 (item 2.4, page 9), and the workbook's six worksheets are named “25-26”. Wyoming variables are annual and read 1 January values, so period `2026` is FY2026: the HHS Wyoming four-person SMI of $114,837 (from `2025-10-01`) and the 2025 HHS guidelines (`fpg_year_lag` 1) for the veterans exclusion and the federal floor. All 12 Wyoming parameter files hold one `2025-10-01` entry. `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2026"`. Period `2027` reads the FY2027 SMI of $114,932, which reproduces the September 2026 handout's limits for sizes 1 to 5, and the 2026 guidelines, but carries the FY2026 fuel standards, fractions and holdback forward: a carried-forward estimate (no FY2027 matrix was found; the draft FY2027 plan estimates $50 to $2,252). Earlier periods take the FY2026 values by backfilling with their own SMI and lagged guideline (period `2025`: $111,736 and the 2024 guidelines): unverified estimates.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/wy/dfs/lieap/`: `wy_lieap`, `wy_lieap_eligible`, `wy_lieap_countable_income`, `wy_lieap_income_limit`, `wy_lieap_household_size` and `wy_lieap_fpg`. No new input variable. The limit calls the shared `smi` helper in `variables/gov/hhs/hhs_smi.py`; the guideline calls `fpg` in `variables/gov/hhs/tax_unit_fpg.py`; the benefit reads the shared `heating_expense` (the bill of the primary `heating_type`).
- **Parameters:** 12 files under `gov.states.wy.dfs.lieap`: `smi_rate` (0.6); `income/` `earned_income_min_age` (18), `earned_sources` (5 sources), `unearned_sources` (15 sources), `interest_monthly_threshold` (30), `gift_monthly_threshold` (30), `veterans_fpg_rate` (1), `fpg_year_lag` (1); `payment/` `fuel_cost` (by `heating_type`), `entitlement_fraction` (single-amount scale), `holdback_rate` (0.1), `minimum_payment` (10). Federal parameters read: `gov.hhs.smi` (amount and size adjustments), `gov.hhs.fpg`, `gov.hhs.liheap.fpg_floor` (1.1), and through `medicare_part_b_premium` the Part B premium. Plus a `programs.yaml` entry, a changelog fragment and two `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml` entries (`us-wy:lieap-income-floor-vs-smi-limit`, `us-wy:lieap-income-limit-statute-lesser-of`, both `state: unreviewed`).

Rules 10(a), page 15: “The fuel cost standard tables in the LIEAP State Plan shall be used to determine household benefits. The tables provide the average cost of home energy allowed in the State for each type of fuel consumed by a recipient.” 10(c): “Payment is based on an entitlement as specified in the LIEAP State Plan.” Plan page 53 lists among required attachments a “Heating component benefit matrix, if applicable”.

**Household and immigration.** Rules 3(kk), page 4: “any individual or group of individuals living together in the same building and who commonly benefit from the primary and secondary heating source unless the utility is metered separately and in separate names and accounts or do not have access to the other occupant’s living space and can provide verification they are responsible for the heat costs. The energy purchase may be in the form of rent.” 3(b), page 2: “a person eighteen (18) years of age or over or an emancipated minor who is the head of their household.” 7(a), page 10: “The following person or groups of persons are eligible if they meet all other eligibility factors as set forth in these rules:”, including (v) “Legal aliens/immigrants.” 7(b) excludes a person under 18 living alone unless head of household, a person on strike, Northern Arapaho and Eastern Shoshone members on the Wind River Reservation, commercial accounts, and (iv) “Residents who do not reside in their Wyoming home in the winter months are not eligible for LIEAP benefits.” 3(fff), page 6: “a person who lives or dwells in Wyoming for a continued period of time with the intent to reside permanently in the state.” 8(a)(i)(A)(II), page 11: “Income of an alien/immigrant sponsor and his/her spouse must be deemed available one hundred percent (100%) for determining LIEAP benefits.” Plan page 38, item 17.3: “What are your procedures for ensuring LIHEAP recipients are U.S. citizens or qualified non-citizens who are eligible to receive LIHEAP benefits?”; only “Non-Citizens must provide documentation of immigration status” is checked. ## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Band edges (settled convention).** Table 1 prints ranges with two-decimal gaps (“0 - .20”, “.21- .25”, ..., “.86 - .99”, “1.00 +”) and names no rounding or denominator. The branch divides unrounded countable income by the income limit and treats .21, .26, ..., .86 and 1.00 as inclusive upper bounds. A ratio between printed rows (0.5582 in companion test 10) takes the higher fraction. At exactly .21, .26, ..., .86 the branch pays the higher fraction where the printed rows start the next band (companion test 4(b): $1,901, against $1,782 in the “.21- .25” row), and at exactly 1.00 it pays 0.10 where the printed “1.00 +” row pays zero (4(e): $238). The convention was approved for the branch; it is not a recovered agency instruction.
2. **Fraction for floor-protected households (unverified).** For a household eligible only through the federal floor, the branch computes the ratio against the larger of the SMI limit and 110% of the guideline (companion test 6). In FY2026 the floor exceeds the limit only from 17 counted members ($114,015 against $113,688). The agency's method for these households was not found.
3. **Federal 110% floor (federal law; candidate).** 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B) bars excluding a household on income alone when its income is “less than 110 percent of the poverty level”. The plan's assurances (page 49) repeat the statutory text; neither the rules nor the plan's eligibility sections apply it. The branch applies it with the one-year guideline lag, rounds 1.1 x guideline to cents and compares strictly. It registers `us-wy:lieap-income-floor-vs-smi-limit` (follows statute, `state: unreviewed`).
4. **W.S. 42-2-501(c), “lesser of” (source conflict; candidate).** The statute directs the plan to “provide eligibility for those households with incomes which do not exceed the lesser of” 215% of the poverty level or 60% of state median household income; rules 3(oo) and 7(a)(ii) call that the maximum income; the FY2026 plan sets 60% of SMI for every size. The branch follows the plan and reads the statute as a coverage minimum that the plan meets. Under a ceiling reading, FY2026 sizes 1-3 with incomes of $33,647.50-$35,829, $45,472.50-$46,853 and $57,297.50-$57,877 (215% of the 2025 guideline up to 60% of SMI) would be ineligible; from size 4 the SMI amount is the lesser. The 2016 DFS memo quotes the clause as “greater of” and asked to remove the 215% clause; no amendment history was found. Candidate `us-wy:lieap-income-limit-statute-lesser-of` (follows conflicting-source, `state: unreviewed`). Companion test 4 and every limit depend on the plan reading.
5. **Income limit arithmetic (inferred rounding; settled).** HHS states the order (60% of the four-person SMI, then the size percentage) but no rounding. The branch floors once, floor(114,837 x factor x 0.6), which reproduces Wyoming's published FY2026 sizes 1-6 and the handout's FY2027 sizes 1-5. Attachment 4 prints Wyoming sizes 7-12 as $93,017, $95,084, $97,151, $99,218, $101,285 and $103,353; flooring 60% of the four-person SMI first ($68,902) reproduces those, while the branch's single floor gives $1 more at sizes 8 to 11 ($95,085, $97,152, $99,219, $101,286), and `wy_lieap_income_limit.yaml` Case 9 expects $95,085. For period 2027 the single floor gives $1 more than IM 2026-01 Attachment 4 at sizes 6, 10 and 11 ($91,026, $99,301, $101,370 against $91,025, $99,300, $101,369 on pages 3 and 6); the handout prints sizes 1-5 only. Wyoming publishes no limit above size 6. The four-person SMI comes from the shared `gov.hhs.smi` parameter; the Clearinghouse page the code cites leaves that cell blank.
6. **Earnings of members under 18 (plan followed; settled).** Plan 1.9 leaves “Earned income of a child under the age of 18” unchecked; rules 8(a)(ii)(A) exempt only earnings of children under 14 and of full-time students under 18. The branch excludes all earnings under 18, by user decision. Under the rules, the 17-year-old nonstudent's $6,000 in companion test 1 would count (15,600 / 46,853 = 0.333: 0.65, $1,544). Emancipated minors heading a household (3(b)) are not identified.
7. **Household and size (simplification).** The SPM unit stands in for the 3(kk) household of people sharing heat; separately metered roomers and boarders are not identified. Size counts `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`, an approved assumption: plan 17.3 requires status documentation and rules 7(a)(v) make legal immigrants eligible, but no source sizes a mixed-status household. All members' otherwise countable income is kept and no further proration applies. Sponsor deeming (8(a)(i)(A)(II)) has no input.
8. **Annual income for a monthly test (simplification).** Rules 8(a) average current monthly gross income. The branch uses annual amounts; the $30 monthly interest and gift tests become $360 a year, which assumes even monthly receipts. Prospective income, pay-period conversion (the unpublished manual) and the exemption of irregular receipts under $30 a month (8(a)(ii)(I)) are not modeled.
9. **Fuels (coverage; settled).** `heating_type` is a required input; UNSPECIFIED pays $0 (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the default), as does NONE, since neither has a bill in `heating_expense`. Only the six worksheet fuels have a standard. KEROSENE is not mapped to the heating-oil standard although 3(hh) lists “diesel, oil”; SOLAR (read with the electric bill) and OTHER have no standard. Those three are eligible with a bill but receive $0. The model has no pellet or corn heating type. The electric label shows “$1713.00”; the branch keeps the cell value 1,712.997, as the cached cells do.
10. **Holdback (source arithmetic).** Only the visible 10% table is used; the hidden 5% and 15% tables and any later release of withheld amounts are not modeled. The withheld amount is rounded half up to whole dollars, as Excel's ROUND does for these positive values; the adjusted benefit is not rounded.
11. **$10 minimum and the cost cap (settled order).** The $10 test applies to the computed adjusted benefit (10(d)) before payment is limited to the actual primary fuel cost (13(b)(i), 12), so a bill below $10 is paid in full and exactly $10 is paid. In FY2026 the smallest computed benefit is $47.50, so the minimum never binds; plan 2.6 estimates $48 to $1,901. Annual `heating_expense` stands in for the season's actual primary fuel cost.
12. **Heating responsibility and housing (proxies).** `heating_expense` > 0 stands in for vulnerability. For heat in rent the caller supplies the documented prorated heating share as the expense; the branch derives no share from rent, and `heat_expense_included_in_rent` alone does not qualify a household. Subsidized housing changes nothing (10(e); plan 2.3). The 8(b)(ii) settings and landlord-held accounts have no inputs.
13. **Social Security and Medicare (settled).** Social Security counts net of the computed `medicare_part_b_premium`, per person and floored at zero (8(a)(ii)(U); plan 1.9). The premium is zero for a person not enrolled and excludes any share a Medicare Savings Program pays. SSI counts gross. The optional state Medicaid supplement benefit (8(a)(ii)(U)) has no input.
14. **Veterans exclusion (settled proxies).** Total `veterans_benefits` stands in for service-connected disability benefits, and one exclusion of 100% of the household-size guideline applies per SPM unit; the rule does not say how to divide it among several recipients (companion test 11(a)). The proxy also exempts non-service-connected VA income up to the guideline, which can understate countable income. 8(a)(ii)(S) says the plan publishes a poverty table each year; the FY2026 plan has none, and the branch uses the 2025 HHS guidelines.
15. **Plan and rules on other items (sources followed).** Lump sums: plan 1.9 checks them, rules 8(a)(ii)(L) exempt them; the branch follows the rules, but annual inputs cannot separate embedded lump sums or exempt reimbursements (callers may supply `wy_lieap_countable_income`). TANF (POWER) and child support received: unchecked in the plan, while rules 9(g)(ii)(B) list their documents among income evidence; the branch excludes both. Categorical eligibility: rules 7(a)(i) list recipients of POWER, SNAP and veteran or survivors' pensions, plan 1.4 answers No; the branch follows the plan. Child support paid comes off the payer's own earnings; the input does not show a court order. No source conflict is registered for these plan-rule differences.
16. **Income items without a matching input (simplification).** Contract income, mortgage or sales-contract payments and royalties (checked in plan 1.9) have no input; commissions are inside `employment_income`. `retirement_distributions` can include account withdrawals. All `interest_income` is tested, though 8(a)(i)(A) names specific instruments. Strike benefits are not counted (plan 1.9 unchecked); a person on strike (7(b)(ii)) has no input.
17. **Where the tables live (source location).** Rules 10(a) and 10(c) place the fuel cost standard tables and the entitlement in the State Plan; the FY2026 plan as published has neither (its attachment list names a heating benefit matrix). The Clearinghouse workbook is the only FY2026 copy located.
18. **Years and dates (simplification).** All Wyoming parameters start `2025-10-01`; annual periods read 1 January values, so period 2026 applies FY2026 to the whole calendar year, including October to December 2026, which fall in FY2027. Earlier and later periods are estimates (see Policy periods).
19. **Other gaps.** Work registration for unemployed members aged 18 to 49 (September 2026 FAQs), the other 7(b) exclusions, residence beyond `state_code`, application dates, priority intake, verification, vendor payment and overpayment recovery are not modeled.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-wy-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-wy-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml) (Clearinghouse copy of the FY2026 plan)
- [us-wy-tanf-ccdf-w6-statute.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-wy-tanf-ccdf-w6-statute.yaml) (Wyoming Statutes Title 42, whole-title PDF)
- [us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml) (2024 and 2025 guidelines)
- [us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml) (2026 guidelines and the FY2027 SMI table, period 2027 estimate)
- [us-cms-annual-notices-2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-cms-annual-notices-2026.yaml) (2026 Part B premium, test input)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-wy/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the FY2026 limits for sizes 1 to 7 and the inclusive limit, the size-0 case, the federal 110% floor and the fraction for floor-protected households, the statute's 215% reading, all 16 Table 1 rows for each of the six fuel standards with the inclusive band tops, the rounded 10% holdback, the $10 minimum before the cap at the actual primary fuel cost, kerosene, solar, other, no heat and unspecified fuel, heat in rent and subsidized renters, members excluded from size (income counted), earnings of members under 18, child support paid against the payer's earnings, Social Security net of the Medicare Part B premium, the $30 monthly interest and gift tests, the veterans exclusion at 100% of the guideline, every listed countable and excluded source, per-source loss floors, and any 2025 or 2027 period kept in scope. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: LIHEAP wave 1d: encode Vermont Seasonal Fuel Assistance regular heating assistance

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Vermont Seasonal Fuel Assistance regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1d, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10436 (branch `vt-liheap-wave1d`), open, not merged. Head `d1c6ff4ffe` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983`; this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10436 opened on 2026-10-23 with no reviews yet, so there is no revision to pin.
- **Sources missing from the corpus.** No axiom-corpus manifest on `main` holds: 33 V.S.A. §§ 2604 and 2605; procedures P-2910, P-2913 (the 2025-26 limits) and P-2927B; the AHS 2026-2027 Benefits Matrix; a dated capture of the DCF 2026-27 income guidelines page; LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 4 (FFY2026 state median income); 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B) and 45 CFR 96.85(b) (no per-section manifest; bulk coverage not checked); and, as evidence for the 2026-27 rate, the draft FFY2027 plan and the DCF memo of September 16, 2026. These need ingest. Captured, in the editions the branch cites: rule 2900, P-2914A, P-2914B, P-2914D, P-2915, P-2916, the FFY2026 plan, the 2024-2026 poverty guidelines and the FFY2027 median income table.
- **Unpublished payment rate.** DCF sets the payment rate by procedure each season and does not publish it. The branch uses 51%, an inference from the FFY2026 plan's $2,089 maximum that the user approved as an estimate for 2025-26 and 2026-27. No source can prove it; the encoding must carry it as a declared estimate or limit the release scope (interpretation 1).
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-23; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10436, branch `vt-liheap-wave1d`, head `d1c6ff4ffe` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983` and closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10426. The tree includes the 2026-10-22 review fixes (the federal `fpg_limit` dated `1981-10-01`, corrected comments, a reworded registry note, `vt_liheap_income.yaml` Case 5) and the 2026-10-23 table fixes (the whole-dollar monthly guideline, the printed income limits and band tops, and the statute cap). After merging `main`, a separate commit adds `vt_aabd` (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10171), the state AABD supplement, to the unearned list (rule 2911.2(b)(1)). Oracle fixtures will pin the merged commit.
- **Scope:** Vermont Seasonal Fuel Assistance, the regular seasonal benefit under 33 V.S.A. chapter 26 and rules 2900-2927: residence; size from citizens and qualified immigrants, with every member's income counted; gross income with the student-earnings exclusion; the printed 185% limit capped by the statute's exact 185% and the LIHEAP maximum; the heat cost percentage; the standard heating cost by dwelling, fuel and bedrooms; the payment rate; the housing factors (100%, 55%, 30% with a $50 minimum, $21); rounding down. Out of scope: crisis fuel (rules 3100-3113), Heat and Eat (33 V.S.A. 2605(h)), weatherization, tank and furnace repair or replacement, cooling. Not modeled for lack of inputs: the December to February reductions (rule 2914(b)), the $21 roomer benefit, excludable members, the 150-night test.
- **Policy periods:** two verified seasons (season: first issuance on or after May 1 to April 30, rule 2901(a)(8); guidelines change each March, P-2910). Vermont variables are annual and read 1 January values. Period `2026` is the 2025-26 season: the 2025 guidelines (`fpg_year_lag` 1), the FFY2026 state median income ($131,654 for four), the P-2916 tables and the 51% rate. Period `2027` is the 2026-27 season: the 2026 guidelines, the FFY2027 median ($135,326), the same heating-cost cells, bands built on the 2026 guideline (no 2026-27 P-2914A exists) and 51% carried forward. Parameter dates: rule values from `2024-06-22` (rule adoption), `fpg_year_lag` and `fpg_table_size` from `2025-03-01`, `heating_cost` and `max_bedrooms` from `2025-07-01` (the 7/1/25 procedures), `payment_rate` from `2025-10-01`, the federal `fpg_limit` from `1981-10-01`. `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2026-2027"`. The 51% payment rate is a user-approved estimate in both years; DCF publishes none. Periods 2025 and earlier backfill the state values on the lagged guideline (2025 on the 2024 guidelines): unverified estimates. Periods 2028 and later are carried-forward estimates.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/vt/dcf/liheap/`: `vt_liheap`, `vt_liheap_fpg` (12 x the whole-dollar monthly guideline behind P-2913 and P-2914A), `vt_liheap_household_size`, `vt_liheap_income` and the new input `vt_liheap_dwelling_type` (SINGLE_FAMILY_OR_MOBILE_HOME, the default, and MULTI_FAMILY); `eligibility/` `vt_liheap_eligible`, `vt_liheap_income_limit`; `payment/` `vt_liheap_heat_cost_percentage`, `vt_liheap_heating_cost`.
- **Parameters:** 14 files under `gov.states.vt.dcf.liheap`: `fpg_year_lag` (1); `fpg_table_size` (8, the sizes HHS lists); `eligibility/fpg_rate` (1.85); `income/` `child_earnings_age_limit` (18), `sources/earned` (5 sources), `sources/unearned` (20); `payment/` `heat_cost_percentage` (thresholds 0.74 to 1.74 times the monthly guideline, rounded up, are the band tops), `heating_cost` (2 dwelling types x 6 fuel rows x 4 bedroom columns), `max_bedrooms` (4), `payment_rate` (0.51, estimate), `heat_in_rent_rate` (0.30), `heat_in_rent_minimum` (50), `subsidized_rate` (0.55), `nominal_benefit` (21). New federal `gov.hhs.liheap.fpg_limit` (1.5, 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B)(i); also on the Maine branch); `smi_limit` (0.6) and `gov.hhs.smi` reused. Plus `programs.yaml`, two `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml` entries and a changelog fragment.
- **Tests:** 45 YAML cases in 9 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/vt/dcf/liheap/` (`vt_liheap.yaml` 5, `vt_liheap_fpg.yaml` 2, `vt_liheap_household_size.yaml` 1, `vt_liheap_income.yaml` 5, `integration.yaml` 4, `eligibility/vt_liheap_eligible.yaml` 7, `eligibility/vt_liheap_income_limit.yaml` 4, `payment/vt_liheap_heat_cost_percentage.yaml` 6, `payment/vt_liheap_heating_cost.yaml` 11). The 27 cases that assert eligibility, a heating cost or a benefit send `heating_type`; the 18 guideline, income, size, limit and percentage cases do not read it. All 45 cases passed locally on 2026-10-23 (`policyengine-core test` on the program folder, after merging `main` and adding `vt_aabd`).

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence on axiom-corpus `main` (`dce8e44665`, 2026-10-23) was checked on 2026-10-23 against the full manifest list and by reading each Vermont LIHEAP, poverty-guideline and annual-figures manifest (four later commits that day touch none of them). The signed release was not checked. rulespec-us `main` (`115bad3183`, 2026-10-23) has only `us-vt/policies/` cms and income_tax, and no `us/` poverty-guideline, median-income, 42 U.S.C. 8624 or 45 CFR 96 module; the paths follow its layout. Pages are physical PDF pages (rule 2900 prints one lower); the manifests' `page-N` suffix counts text-bearing pages only.

[33 V.S.A. § 2604](https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/33/026/02604) (Vermont Statutes Online, including the 2026 session; captured 2026-10-21). |

[33 V.S.A. § 2605](https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/33/026/02605). Subsection (h), Heat and Eat, is out of scope. |

## Source text (verbatim)

Quotations come from the official files above (pdftotext, line breaks collapsed; the statutes, the DCF page and 42 U.S.C. 8624 from their HTML). Plan check-box and radio states come from renders of plan pages 5, 6, 7, 9 and 10.

**Program and dates.** Rule 2901(a)(8), page 4, Heating Season: “means the period that begins when the Department first issues fuel benefits each year, on or after May 1, and ends April 30 of the following year.” Plan page 1: “Report Period: 10/01/2025 to 09/30/2026” and “Report Status: Submission Accepted by CO”; page 4, item 1.1, heating assistance from 10/01/2025 to 09/30/2026. P-2910: “Fuel begins with the new income guidelines in March.” P-2913: “Effective March 1, 2025 to February 28, 2026”. P-2916, page 1: “FOR 2025-26 HEATING SEASON”. AHS 2026-2027 Benefits Matrix, page 2: “FOR 2026-27 HEATING SEASON”. DCF income guidelines page: “Below are incomes guidelines for 2026 - 2027.”

**Household and members.** Rule 2901(a)(6), page 4, Fuel Household: “means any person or group of people who live together as one economic unit and either:” (i) “Customarily make purchases in common for home heating fuel; or” (ii) “Make undesignated payments for home heat in the form of rent.” Rule 2903(a), page 10, households may be eligible if all members are Vermont residents and: “A household member must be a citizen or national of the United States or a qualified immigrant under rule 2907;” “The total gross income of all fuel household members must not exceed 185% of the federal poverty guidelines based on household size;” “Total fuel household gross income is based on the combined countable income of all persons residing in the fuel household, regardless of immigration status; and” “The head of household must spend at least 150 non-consecutive nights in their living unit between November 1 and April 30.” Rule 2903(b): “Any person who resides in the living unit is included in the fuel household, unless they may be excluded as one of the following:” roomers or boarders, caretakers or companions, medically necessary caregivers, and foster or residential care placements; rule 2903(c), page 11, bars excluding the head, spouse or partner, minor children and their parents. Rule 2907(a), page 16: “To receive fuel assistance benefits, at least one member of the household must be a:” citizen or national, or qualified immigrant; rule 2907(f), page 17: “No immigrant or non-citizen is eligible for fuel assistance unless that person is a qualified immigrant.” Rule 2914(a)(1), page 39, excludes ineligible persons from household size. P-2910: “However, if the member is ineligible, e.g., undocumented immigrant, then that member’s income is counted, but the person is not counted in the total number of household members.”
