## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Payment rate (estimate, user-approved).** Rule 2914(a)(8) and 33 V.S.A. 2605(c) set the rate by procedure. P-2914B prints no number (staff read it in ACCESS), and P-2914D's 29% is a training figure. No 2025-26 rate is published. The branch's 51% is an inference: floor(4,552 x 0.90 x 0.51) = 2,089, the FFY2026 plan's maximum (item 2.6), and no other whole percent reproduces it; that plan figure was itself an estimate filed before benefits were issued. The user approved 51% as an estimate for 2025-26 and its reuse for 2026-27. The DCF memo of September 16, 2026 says the 2026-27 levels were not yet determined; the draft FFY2027 plan's 1966 maximum implies 48% (a June 2026 planning figure). Mid-season changes (2914(a)(8)(ii)) are not represented.
2. **Monthly tables (inferred construction).** Rules 2914(a)(3)-(4) and 2915(b) take the limit and the percentage of poverty from the procedure tables, which print monthly dollars for sizes 1 to 15 without saying how they are built. The branch builds them from the HHS guideline: a whole-dollar monthly guideline M (the guideline for sizes 1 to 8 divided by 12 and rounded half up, plus the additional-person amount divided by 12 and rounded half up for each person above eight); the printed limit, 185% of M rounded half up; band tops, each cutoff times M rounded up, an income at a top staying in that band. This reproduces all 165 printed 2025-26 P-2914A tops, all 15 P-2913 limits and all 15 DCF 2026-27 limits. It is a numerical inference, not a stated rule; rounding each size's own guideline misses 53 of the 55 tops for sizes 11-15. Annual income divided by 12 stands in for the 30-day income and the 4.3 and 2.15 conversions of rule 2911(c).
3. **Statute cap on the printed limit (source conflict, registered).** 33 V.S.A. 2604(a) allows income “no greater than 185 percent of the federal poverty level”. P-2913's half-up rounding is above that for some sizes (two people in 2026: $3,262 a month against $3,260.625). The branch reads the statute as a ceiling: the limit is the lowest of 12 times the printed amount, exactly 185% of the annual guideline and the LIHEAP maximum. The cap binds in 2026 for sizes 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and 10 and in 2027 for sizes 1, 3, 4, 6 and 7; the printed amount binds for one person in 2026 ($2,412 against $2,412.71). The branch adds candidate `us-vt:liheap-income-maximum-rounding` (follows statute; state ruled).
4. **Bands between whole percentages (source wording).** Rule 2915(d) lists “Under 75%” then 75% - 84%; P-2915 prints “0-74%”. P-2914A labels its first band 0 To <75% but ends it at 74% of the monthly guideline rounded up, so 74.1% to 74.9% falls in 75% To 84%, and likewise for later bands. Rule 2915(b) assigns the percentage of poverty to that table. The branch follows the printed tops (interpretation 2).
5. **Income limit for large households (source conflict, registered).** 33 V.S.A. 2604(a) and rule 2913(b) bar income above 185% of the guideline or above the LIHEAP maximums (42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B)). P-2913 prints 185% amounts for sizes 10-15 above that maximum (size 10: $120,528 a year against $113,748); so does the DCF 2026-27 page ($10,340 a month against $116,920). The branch follows the statute and rule and adds `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml` entry `us-vt:liheap-income-maximum-large-households` (follows statute; state ruled). Plan item 2.1 reports 60% of state median income for all sizes; the branch reads it as the federal ceiling, not Vermont's own test.
6. **Household and members (simplification).** The SPM unit stands in for the fuel household; size counts `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`. Excludable members, roomer households and their $21, and the 150-night test have no inputs.
7. **Income items (settled decisions and proxies).** Each source is floored at zero, so a loss offsets nothing; `rental_income` is assumed nonnegative and listed once (it counts under 2911.3(a)(1) or 2911.2(b)(13)). Self-employment uses net business inputs. Social Security counts gross (plan 1.9 checks Including MediCare deduction). `retirement_distributions` counts as retirement benefits (2911.2(b)(4)), `miscellaneous_income` as other direct money payments (2911.2(b)(16)), `estate_income` as trust income and royalties. K-12 enrollment and tax-unit dependency stand in for the student and parental-control tests of rule 2912(a)(12); the exclusion also zeroes a student's self-employment income, which 3SquaresVT treats as earned. Plan 1.9 leaves strike pay and a child's earned income unchecked; the branch follows rules 2911.2(b)(10) and 2912(a)(12). Cash gifts, jury duty, foster care payments and scholarships have no input. The Vermont AABD supplement (`vt_aabd`) counts under rule 2911.2(b)(1) and joins the list when `main` is merged.
8. **Fuels (settled decisions and coverage limits).** `heating_type` is a required input (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the default). UNSPECIFIED has no row and pays $0, except the $21 for subsidized heat in rent, which needs no fuel. NONE is always ineligible. SOLAR reads the electricity row (user decision; rule 2901(a)(14)); an off-grid solar-only home cannot be told apart. OTHER has no row and is ineligible. WOOD and COAL share the firewood, pellets and coal row; the model has no pellet type.
9. **Heating cost, dwelling and bedrooms (settled decisions and proxies).** `vt_liheap_dwelling_type` defaults to the single-family and mobile home table; modular homes are single family (P-2927B). Zero bedrooms use the 1-bedroom column (user decision); four or more use 4+. The benefit uses the standard cost, never a bill; a listed fuel without heat in rent is treated as paid to a certified supplier (2914(c)(1)), and households not charged for heat are not identified.
10. **Housing proxies (settled reading).** `receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing` stands for Section 8 or other public housing (2914(c)) and a public, subsidized or Section 8 program (2605(e)-(f)). 33 V.S.A. 2604(c)(1) deems residents of subsidized units to have no heating cost, except Reach Up, SSI/AABD, Emergency Assistance or General Assistance recipients without other housing-targeted aid. The branch reads rule 2914(c)(3)-(4), 55% and $21, as carrying this out, and does not model the exception separately.
11. **Order and rounding.** The branch multiplies percentage, cost, rate and housing factor, applies the $50 floor after the rate (2914(c)(2)(i)) and rounds down once (2914(d)). P-2914D multiplies by the ratable last and omits the $50 minimum; the products agree. Rule 2915(c)'s 90% cap holds by construction.
12. **Late applications (not modeled).** Rule 2914(b) cuts December, January and February applications to 80%, 60% and 40%. The model has no application month and applies 100%.
13. **Years and dates (simplification).** Period 2026 applies the 2025-26 season to the whole calendar year, although applications from March 2026 use the 2026 guidelines (P-2910). No 2026-27 P-2913 or P-2914A is published. The construction reproduces the DCF page's 2026-27 limits; the 2026-27 bands apply it to the 2026 guideline and are unverified. Earlier and later periods are estimates.
14. **Worked example (source detail).** P-2914D's example is illustrative: $893.04 for one person falls in 0 To <75% of the 2025-26 P-2914A, not 75%-84%, and 29% is a training figure. Companion test 7 uses only its cost and percentage.
15. **Other gaps.** SNAP categorical eligibility changes certification periods only (plan 1.4-1.6). Funding availability (rule 2917), payment routing, credit balances and recoupment are not modeled. Heat and Eat and crisis assistance are out of scope; plan item 1.7a reports no SNAP nominal payment.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-vt-liheap-benefit-matrix-rule.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-vt-liheap-benefit-matrix-rule.yaml) (rule 2900; also crisis rule 3100, out of scope)
- [us-vt-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-vt-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml) (P-2914A, P-2914B, P-2914C, P-2914D, P-2915, P-2916; 2025-26)
- [us-vt-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-vt-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml) (2024 and 2025 guidelines)
- [us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml) (2026 guidelines and the FFY2027 state median income table)
- [us-vt-3squaresvt-manual.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-vt-3squaresvt-manual.yaml) (3SquaresVT income rules adopted by rules 2910(b) and 2911.3(b); not cited by the branch)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-vt/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the whole-dollar monthly guideline (half-up rounding, the per-person amount above eight), the printed 2025-26 and 2026-27 limits for sizes 1 to 15 with the inclusive ceiling, the statute cap where the printed amount rounds above 185%, the LIHEAP maximum for sizes 10 and up in both years, all twelve bands at the printed P-2914A tops and $1 above, all 48 heating-cost cells with the bedroom bounds, every fuel the code distinguishes (wood and coal on one row, solar on electricity, other, none, unspecified), the four housing treatments with the $50 floor and $21, rounding down, the declared 51% estimate, ineligible members (income counted, size not), the student-earnings exclusion, every listed income source with per-source loss floors, and the 2026-27 season and any 2025 or 2028 period kept in scope. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: LIHEAP wave 2a: encode Pennsylvania LIHEAP regular heating assistance

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Pennsylvania LIHEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 2a, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9971 (branch `pa-liheap`), open as a draft, not merged. Head `a76331a0c4` (2026-10-21). The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

- **Sources need ingest.** Most of the official text this program rests on is in no axiom-corpus manifest on `main`: the Pennsylvania FY2026 and FY2027 final LIHEAP State Plans (the Appendix B rules numbered 601.3 to 601.84), the FY2025 federally filed plan, the Energy Year 2024-2025 county benefit charts, the DHS LIHEAP Benefit Table lookup that carries the FY2027 amounts, Operations Memoranda 26-07-01 and 25-08-01, the July 30, 2026 DHS announcement, earlier editions of handbook sections 638.3, 650.3 and 650.6, 55 Pa. Code chapter 601, and the 2024 and 2025 HHS poverty guidelines. The FY2026 final plan's official URL answers 404; its bytes were recovered from an Internet Archive capture. Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-06. Presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not checked.
- **Billed encoder runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval. None has been requested.
- **Oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9971 is open as a draft and has not been reviewed or merged, so there is no revision to pin.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9971, open as a draft, not merged. Pushed head `a76331a0c4` (2026-10-21) edits comments on `a9b232038c`, which merges upstream/main `a6fafb06c2` into `76e3a39d80`, which replaces the six printed payment tables with a formula reproducing every printed cell of the seven priced fuel rows. Earlier commits: `ec20411713` and `d17ba3bd15` (2026-10-03) add the components and connect the award; `3edfbe149f` (2026-10-06) applies a local policy and code review. Everything below describes `a76331a0c4`.
- **Scope:** the Cash component (regular heating grant) for FY2025 to FY2027: residence, qualified household size, gross income at or below 150% of the poverty guideline, heating responsibility with the heat-in-rent and income-based-rent rules, countable income and exclusions, the benefit-only 20% wage disregard, the five heating regions, the county and region payment amounts by fuel, $1,000 income band and household size (1 to 20), and the $100 vulnerable-household supplements that Operations Memoranda 25-08-01 and 26-07-01 issued in August 2025 and July 2026 to vulnerable Cash households of the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 seasons. Out of scope: the Crisis component (including winter crisis and the DCED Emergency Services Program), weatherization, cooling (Pennsylvania operates none), heating-equipment repair or replacement, the SNAP "Heat and Eat" nominal payment, the all-Cash, all-Crisis and income-level supplements, Blended Fuel (fuel code 708; no model input), payment application and refund rules, and the 50% back-balance rule.
- **Policy periods:** three seasons. Program year FY N opens in November of N-1 and is read at model period `N`: every Pennsylvania variable is annual and reads the value in force on 1 January. The six fuel-base parameters carry change-only values at `2024-11-04` (FY2025 heating start, federally filed FY2025 plan section 1.1), `2025-11-03` (FY2026 Cash opening, FY2026 final plan page 5) and `2026-11-02` (FY2027 Cash opening, FY2027 final plan page 5). The income multipliers, member amount, minimum, maximum and size cap carry one value from `2024-11-04`. The eligibility, income and region parameters start at `2025-11-03` and backfill to 2025. The income limit is 1.5 times the HHS guideline of the year before the model year (`fpg_year_lag` 1): the 2024, 2025 and 2026 guidelines for 2025, 2026 and 2027, which reproduces every published limit. The supplement amount is $100 at `2025-01-01` (OPS 25-08-01, issued August 15, 2025), $100 at `2026-01-01` (OPS 26-07-01, issued July 16, 2026) and $0 at `2027-01-01` (no 2026-2027 directive as of October 6, 2026); its age thresholds start at `2025-01-01`. `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2025-2027"`; years before 2025 are backfilled, unverified estimates.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/pa/dhs/liheap/`: `pa_liheap` (adds the next two), `pa_liheap_household_size`; `payment/pa_liheap_matrix_amount`, `payment/pa_liheap_supplement`; `eligibility/pa_liheap_eligible`, `eligibility/pa_liheap_income_limit`; `income/pa_liheap_income`, `income/pa_liheap_countable_employment_income`, `income/pa_liheap_benefit_income`. No new input variables. The limit reuses the federal `fpg` helper (`gov.hhs.fpg`).
- **Parameters:** `gov.states.pa.dhs.liheap` (`eligibility/`: `fpg_rate` 1.5, `fpg_year_lag` 1; `income/`: `benefit_wage_disregard` 0.2, `child_age_limit` 18, `monthly_interest_dividend_disregard` $25, `sources/business`, `sources/unearned`, `support/monthly_child_disregard` (0, $100, $200 by children), `support/monthly_spousal_disregard` $50; `payment/`: `regions` (`region_1` to `region_5`), `income_multiplier` (21 brackets, $0 to $20,000+; interpretation 18), `base/electricity` and `base/wood_other` keyed by heating region, `base/natural_gas`, `base/fuel_oil`, `base/coal` and `base/kerosene` keyed by the 67 counties (834 season values across the six base files), `additional_member_amount` $5, `minimum` $200, `maximum` $1,000, `maximum_household_size` 20, and `supplement/amount`, `supplement/child_age_limit` 5, `supplement/elderly_age` 60). 24 files.

Page 2: "the household must have a vulnerable member in the household, which is defined as having a member that has a disability, a member age 60 or older, or has a child under the age of five." "NOTE: The LIHEAP State Plan defines a disabled individual as someone receiving financial assistance for a disability." "A household will be ineligible for the supplement if their address changed after the most recent LIHEAP payment was issued." DHS announcement, July 30, 2026: "include at least one family member who has a disability, is age 60 or older, or is a child under the age of six." OPS 25-08-01, page 1: "The Department of Human Services will be issuing a $100 supplemental payment to all vulnerable households that received a LIHEAP Cash grant during the 2024-2025 heating season." and "Payments will be issued on August 15, 2025, with a Treasury pay date of August 27, 2025." Page 2 applies the same test "to all 2024-2025 LIHEAP season Cash recipients": a member with a disability, aged 60 or older, or a child under five.

**Superseded code text.** 55 Pa. Code 601.42: "Eligible roomers receive 50% of the LIHEAP cash benefit for which they would otherwise qualify."

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Seasons and dates.** Model period N reads the value in force on 1 January N, so 2025 uses the bases from the FY2025 chart (values at `2024-11-04`), 2026 those from the FY2026 chart (`2025-11-03`) and 2027 those from the lookup (`2026-11-02`). The FY2025 final State Plan was not read (its pa.gov URL returned 404 to the review); the FY2025 limits come from FY2026 plan page 10 and the FY2025 chart headers, and the FY2025 wage deduction, support exclusions, age 18 and region lists are carried back from the FY2026 plan's `2025-11-03` values.
2. **Mid-season guideline update (simplification).** The FY2026 plan says the limit updates "each January" and the FY2027 plan "each February"; handbook 650 Appendix A lists $23,940 for one person effective February 2026. The branch keeps the opening limit for the whole model year, which is the limit in force on 1 January. An application in February to April 2026 faced $23,940, not $23,475. Companion case 4 relies on this convention.
3. **The lookup is FY2027 (inferred dating).** The lookup prints no season label. It is dated FY2027 because the FY2027 plan (page 39) sends readers to the LIHEAP Benefit Amount Table on the DHS LIHEAP page, whose LIHEAP Benefit Table link opens the lookup, handbook Appendix A (reviewed August 5, 2026) links it, OPS 26-08-01 (August 13, 2026) says parameters are posted in the handbook, and its cells differ from both charts. It was captured before the November 2, 2026 opening; re-capture after opening and compare. Companion case 14 depends on this.
4. **Income above the printed bands (inferred).** The charts and lookup stop at "$ 22000-22999" while limits reach $105,975 and handbook 638.3 says brackets continue in $1,000 steps. Every printed cell from $20,000 to $22,999 is $200, the plan minimum, and lower brackets carry higher multipliers. The branch's multiplier is 0 from $20,000, so it pays $200 at $20,000 and above. `integration.yaml` Case 2 (Bradford couple, benefit income $29,930.40, $200 plus $100) and `payment/pa_liheap_matrix_amount.yaml` Cases 10, 12 and 15 depend on this.
5. **Cents within a band (inferred).** The tables print whole-dollar bands. The branch's multiplier brackets start at each multiple of $1,000, so $999.99 is in "$ 0-999" (matrix Cases 6 and 7 send cents). No source states the rounding.
6. **Sizes 12 to 20 (inferred).** Handbook 638.3 says "Household Size values range from 1-20." but every published table stops at 11. The branch continues the $5 member amount through size 20 and uses size 20 for any larger household. At FY2026 Adams Electric, band 5, where the chart prints 552 for size 1 and 602 for size 11, it pays 607 for size 12 and 647 for sizes 20 and 21 (`payment/pa_liheap_matrix_amount.yaml` Case 10). No published amount confirms sizes above 11, so no companion test uses them.
7. **Fuel mapping.** PROPANE uses the electricity base: the Propane or Bottled Gas row equals the Electric row in every county, band and season (checked over all three sources). KEROSENE uses the kerosene base and OTHER the Wood/Other base. SOLAR uses the electricity base: no fuel code exists for solar and a grid-tied solar home pays an electricity bill (the pairing `heating_expense` uses). Blended Fuel (code 708) has no input. `heating_type` is a required input: UNSPECIFIED pays $0 (policyengine-us issue 9754 tracks the default), and here this holds even with heat in rent because Pennsylvania's amount depends on the fuel; NONE is ineligible. Fixtures must send `heating_type` with the matching bill. 601.41(4) prices a secondary-fuel payment at the primary fuel, which matches `heating_type` being the primary fuel.
8. **Heating responsibility proxies.** `has_heating_expense` (by default a positive primary-fuel bill with heat not in rent) stands for paying a vendor for the primary fuel; a secondary-fuel bill does not establish it (`eligibility/pa_liheap_eligible.yaml` Case 7). The plan's test for heat in rent is whether rent "is based on a fixed percentage of their income or on their source of income"; the branch uses `receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing` for that, which misclassifies a subsidized tenant whose rent is not income-based. Bills paid by someone outside the household, agency-paid bills, campers, home businesses, institutions and the roomer rule in 601.31(2)(i)(C) have no inputs.
9. **Household (simplification).** The SPM unit stands in for the economic unit. Prior-recipient, temporary, institutional and fleeing-felon members (601.41(1)(i)-(iii), (v)) are not identified. Nonqualified noncitizens are dropped from size through `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`, whose list has no value for battered noncitizens, Iraqi or Afghan special immigrants or COFA migrants; handbook 622.2 ("Updated August 15, 2025") and the FY2027 plan count them, so such members are left out of size (coverage gap). Everyone's income counts.
10. **Medicare premium (settled: handbook over plan).** The plan nets only Social Security: 601.84(10) excludes "Medicare premiums deducted from Social Security benefit payments." (55 Pa. Code 601.84(10) is the same; federal plans 1.9 check the box excluding it). Handbook 650.6(10), FY2026 and current editions, excludes "Medicare premiums deducted from Social Security, Railroad Retirement, and other benefit payments." The branch follows the handbook: one `medicare_part_b_premium` comes off the person's `social_security` plus `railroad_benefits`, once, floored at zero, so it never reduces other income (companion case 2). The model's premium already omits the share a Medicare Savings Program pays, matching the handbook's buy-in note. Other annuities that withhold the premium have no input.
11. **Interest and dividends (settled: handbook over plan, with an inferred reading).** The plan counts "Interest and/or dividends from investments or bank accounts." with no threshold (601.82(4)(ix)); handbook 650.3(9), FY2026 and current editions, counts only those "of more than $25 per month". The branch follows the handbook through `monthly_interest_dividend_disregard` ($25): $300 a year comes off the unit's combined `interest_income` and `ordinary_dividend_income`, assuming steady monthly receipt. The handbook does not say whether the $25 is per source or per person. The branch shares one $25 between interest and dividends because 650.3(9) lists them as one item, and applies it once per household because the test is household income (650.1: "LIHEAP uses gross income to figure out whether a household qualifies for LIHEAP."). The other readings change two branch cases: `income/pa_liheap_income.yaml` Case 4 (interest 120 and dividends 240 a year: 9,660, or 9,600 with a separate $25 each) and Case 19 (two members with $300 of interest each: 300, or 0 with $25 per person). Companion case 11 uses only one-person, one-source cases.
12. **Other income simplifications.** Annual income stands in for the applicant's choice of the prior month or 12 months (601.83(1)); handbook 650.7 makes the CAO use the prior month when it is lower. Each income source is floored at zero separately, including rental and farm rent (601.82(2)(ii); settled). Self-employment uses the model's net inputs with no further deduction. Rental income is counted in full; handbook 650.2 counts room rent at 50% and treats self-managed rentals as earned, and no input separates them. TANF is read through the take-up-gated `tanf` (settled). Cash gifts use `financial_assistance` and IRA withdrawals `retirement_distributions`. Not modeled for lack of inputs: utility allowances paid to the household, certificate-of-deposit and stock-sale proceeds, legal settlements and insurance payments (checked in federal 1.9), support paid by a household member, refunded support, the deduction for expenses of getting unearned income (601.84(29)), Medicare Part D premiums and representative-payee shares. The support exclusions are annual ($1,200 or $2,400 and $600) and only the larger applies, a steady-receipt reading of the monthly rule; the child count includes nonqualified children. Tax-dependent status stands in for "dependent child".
13. **Benefit-only wage deduction.** The 20% applies to countable wages only (`employment_income` of members who are not dependent children), not to self-employment profit, and only after the gross test (601.41(2); handbook 650.5). Handbook 650.21 enters self-employment profit "minus the 20 percent disregard" for the benefit amount, which conflicts with 601.41(2) ("deducting 20 percent from the gross wages") and with the handbook's own 650.5 ("Only wage income, not total household income, is eligible for the deduction."). The branch follows 601.41(2) and 650.5, so $6,250 of business profit stays $6,250 of benefit income (`income/pa_liheap_benefit_income.yaml` Case 2) where 650.21 would give $5,000. This handbook-internal conflict stays open; no companion test depends on it.
14. **Supplement.** (a) Timing: each issuance is recorded in its calendar year, which is also the model year of its season: OPS 25-08-01 (2024-2025 season, issued August 15, 2025) in 2025 and OPS 26-07-01 (2025-2026 season, issued July 16, 2026) in 2026. 2027 is $0 because no 2026-2027 directive exists as of October 6, 2026; this is a scope convention, not a finding that later supplements are barred. (b) Child age: the plan says "age five and under", the announcement "under the age of six", and both memos "under the age of five". The branch follows the operating memos, so a household whose only vulnerable member is five gets nothing (`payment/pa_liheap_supplement.yaml` Case 2). (c) Disability: the branch counts Social Security disability, `disability_benefits`, or SSI with a disability or blindness flag, per the memo's "receiving financial assistance for a disability"; the plan's optional MA or TANF disability criteria and veterans' disability compensation (aggregated in `veterans_benefits`) are not used. (d) Annual age stands in for age at application; actual Cash receipt in the season is approximated by eligibility; the address-change exclusion is not modeled. (e) The plan's alternative cumulative amounts ($50, $50, $75) were not used for either issuance.
15. **Roomers (source conflict).** The annual plans' 601.42 gives heat-in-rent roomers "the full LIHEAP Cash benefit"; 55 Pa. Code 601.42 (1988) gives roomers 50%. The branch follows the annual plans. There is no roomer input.
16. **County input.** With no `county` input the model's Pennsylvania county defaults to Adams County (Region 4); an explicit UNKNOWN county gives a $0 table amount. Oracle fixtures must always send a county.
17. **Not modeled by design.** The one-Cash-benefit-per-year rule (601.43), the 50% back-balance rule, payment routing to vendors or landlords, and the all-Cash, all-Crisis and income-level supplements.
18. **Payment formula (inferred representation).** DHS prints no multipliers or fuel bases; handbook 638.3 says each $1,000 bracket is "associated with a different benefit multiplier" and fuel values "depend on the cost of the fuel in the household's county of residence". The branch computes min(max(round half up(m x (base + 5 x (min(size, 20) - 1))), 200), 1,000), reading from the printed cells 21 multipliers m (the same in all three seasons: 2.1 at $0-999 to 0.1486 at $19,000-19,999, then 0) and 834 bases (electricity and Wood/Other by region; the other four fuels by county, natural gas by region in FY2025 and FY2026), with the Cash minimum and maximum (plan page 5; FY2025 federal plan 2.6, page 9; handbook Appendix B). This reproduces all 355,971 printed cells for the seven priced rows (67 counties x 7 x 23 bands x 11 sizes x 3 seasons) with 0 mismatches; with the same parameters, half-to-even rounding changes 600 cells (125 in FY2025, 92 in FY2026, 383 in the lookup). Companion case 14(c) pins two half-up cells. The parameters are a reading of the tables, not printed law; a module may encode the printed cells and use interpretations 4 and 6 above $22,999 and size 11.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [FY2026 state-plan manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-pa-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [FY2026 benefit-chart manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-pa-liheap-benefit-matrix-attachments.yaml)
- [LIHEAP Handbook manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-pa-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml)
- [LIHEAP annual figures 2026 manifest](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission. The FY2026 and FY2027 final State Plans, the FY2025 federal plan and chart, the FY2027 lookup, Operations Memoranda 26-07-01 and 25-08-01, the FY2026 handbook editions, 55 Pa. Code chapter 601 and the 2024 and 2025 poverty guidelines are not in any manifest and need ingest before the modules above can be proved. The handbook manifest holds the current (FY2027) edition only.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-pa/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the FY2025 to FY2027 income limits, the $1,000 band edges, the county and region tables by fuel for FY2025 (chart), FY2026 (chart) and FY2027 (lookup), including the lookup's half-up cells, heat in rent and income-based rent, nonqualified members, the benefit-only 20% wage deduction, the support exclusions, Social Security and railroad retirement net of Medicare, interest and dividends above $25 a month, per-source loss floors, TANF receipt/take-up, and the August 2025 and July 2026 vulnerable-household supplements. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: LIHEAP wave 1d: encode Maine HEAP regular heating assistance

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Maine HEAP regular heating assistance (Fuel Assistance) in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1d, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10437 (branch `me-liheap-wave1d`), open, not merged. Head `bbdb9b5f78` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983`; this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10437 opened on 2026-10-23 with no reviews yet, so there is no revision to pin.
- **Sources missing from the corpus.** On axiom-corpus `main`, `us-me-liheap-benefit-matrix-rule.yaml` holds the June 29, 2026 replacement of MaineHousing Rules Chapter 24 (SOS filing 2026-134), which governs period 2027 only, and `us-me-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml` holds the FFY2026 plan. No manifest holds the 2025 edition of Chapter 24 (SOS filing 2025-135), whose matrix, percentages and rounding sentence govern period 2026, or its Clearinghouse extract. Also in no manifest: the FFY2025 plan (the $1,012 maximum behind the point value), MaineHousing's 2025-26 and 2026-27 income tables, LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachments 2 and 4 (the FY2026 guideline mandate and Maine's FFY2026 state median income), MaineHousing board packets, the FY2023 matrix and notice 2024-HEAP-003. 42 U.S.C. 8624 and 45 CFR 96.85 have no manifest file; corpus ingest notes record their scopes. These need ingest or admission.
- **No published value per point.** MaineHousing has published no dollar value per point for FFY2025, FFY2026 or FFY2027. The branch uses $22, inferred from the FFY2025 and FFY2026 plans' $1,012 maximum and approved as an estimate (interpretation 1). No official source grounds that number, and every points-based benefit in the companion tests scales with it.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-23; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10437, branch `me-liheap-wave1d`, head `bbdb9b5f78` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983` and closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10427. The branch includes the 2026-10-22 review fixes: eligibility requires a Direct or Indirect Determinable Energy Cost (rule 3(A)(4)); `fpg_limit.yaml` starts 1981-10-01; multiplier thresholds are fractions with a rounding-increment parameter; paying test cases carry a fuel bill; `integration.yaml` Case 4 tests a household with no bill. Oracle fixtures will pin the merged commit.
- **Scope:** Maine HEAP Fuel Assistance, the regular heating benefit under 99-346 CMR ch. 24 section 4(A), for FFY2026 and FFY2027: residence, household size counting citizens, nationals and qualified aliens (all members' income counted), gross income of members 18 and over with the listed inclusions and exclusions, the medical-expense adjustment, the income limit (the greater of 150% of the guideline and 60% of state median income), categorical eligibility through SNAP or TANF, the energy-cost condition, each edition's points matrix and percentage of points, proration for ineligible members, rounding up, the dollar value per point, and the $21 nominal benefit for subsidized tenants with heat in rent. Out of scope: ECIP crisis assistance, the TANF Fuel Supplemental Benefit, Supplemental Benefits, HEAP Weatherization, CHIP, the Heat Pump Program, Energy Self Sufficiency services, funding availability, application windows, payment routing and the HEAP Guide's procedures. Maine runs no cooling component (plan item 1.1).
- **Policy periods:** two verified seasons. The Heating Season runs October 1 to April 30 within an October-to-September Program Year (rule 1(Z) and 1(PP), pages 2-3); FFY2026 applications ran August 1, 2025 to May 29, 2026 (plan item 1.1, page 4). Maine variables are annual and read 1 January values. Period `2026` is FFY2026: the 2025-edition matrix (parameters dated `2024-07-03`, the filing date of the 2024 edition, which has the same matrix), the 2025 HHS guidelines (`fpg_year_lag` 1) and the FFY2026 state median income ($118,065, dated `2025-10-01`). Period `2027` is FFY2027: the replacement rule's matrix (dated `2026-06-29`), the 2026 guidelines and $122,022 (dated `2026-10-01`). `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2026-2027"`. In both periods the $22 value per point (from `2024-10-01`) is an estimate: MaineHousing has announced none, and $22 is inferred from the plans' $1,012 maximum and approved as an estimate (interpretation 1). The $21 nominal benefit (FFY2026 plan) carries into period 2027, since no FFY2027 plan is posted. Period 2025 (same matrix, 2024 guidelines) is an unverified estimate; periods 2024 and earlier backfill these values although Maine then used an older energy-cost matrix. Periods 2028 and later are carried-forward estimates.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/me/msha/heap/`: `me_heap`, `me_heap_household_size`, `me_heap_income` and the new input `me_heap_dwelling_type` (STICK_BUILT_OR_MODULAR, MOBILE_OR_MANUFACTURED, CONDO_DUPLEX_OR_APARTMENT; default STICK_BUILT_OR_MODULAR); `eligibility/` `me_heap_categorically_eligible`, `me_heap_eligible`, `me_heap_income_limit`; `payment/` `me_heap_income_multiplier`, `me_heap_points`. The limit and multiplier reuse the existing `fpg()` helper (year lag) and `liheap_smi_limit()` (45 CFR 96.85 size factors on the `gov.hhs.smi` amounts).
- **Parameters:** 19 files under `gov.states.me.msha.heap`: `fpg_year_lag` (1); `income/` `minimum_age` (18), `medical_expense_sources` (2 inputs), `sources/earned` (5 sources), `sources/unearned` (17); `payment/` `value_per_point` (22, estimate), `nominal_benefit` (21); `points/` `base` (0, then 8), `dwelling` (by `me_heap_dwelling_type`), `county` (16 counties), `fuel` (7 fuels), `subsidized_heating` (-9, then -3), `income_multiplier` (single-amount scale on band starts), `poverty_level_rounding_increment` (0.01, then 0.0001); `points/priority/` `amount` (5), `older_child_amount` (3, then 0), `elderly_age` (60), `young_child_age` (6), `child_age_limit` (18). Plus a new federal parameter `gov.hhs.liheap.fpg_limit` (1.5 from `1981-10-01`, 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B)(i)), byte-identical to the copy on the Vermont wave 1d branch, a `programs.yaml` entry and a changelog fragment. No `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml` entry.
- **Tests:** 43 YAML cases in 9 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/me/msha/heap/` (`me_heap.yaml` 4, `me_heap_household_size.yaml` 1, `me_heap_income.yaml` 9, `integration.yaml` 4, `eligibility/me_heap_categorically_eligible.yaml` 2, `eligibility/me_heap_eligible.yaml` 4, `eligibility/me_heap_income_limit.yaml` 3, `payment/me_heap_income_multiplier.yaml` 4, `payment/me_heap_points.yaml` 12). The 42 cases that existed then passed locally on 2026-10-21; the 2026-10-22 review fixes, which added `integration.yaml` Case 4 and bills to the paying cases, were not re-run. CI validates them. Every case that tests eligibility or the benefit sends `heating_type`.

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence on axiom-corpus `main` (`dce8e44665`, 2026-10-23) was checked on 2026-10-23 against the full manifest list, the Maine manifests and corpus locks, and GitHub code search for the source URLs; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not checked. rulespec-us `main` (`115bad3183`, 2026-10-23) has `us-me/policies/` (cms and income_tax), `us-me/regulations/dhhs/ofi/chapter-331` and `us-me/statutes/36`, but no MaineHousing, HEAP or LIHEAP module, no `us/statutes/42/8624`, no 45 CFR 96.85 module and no `us/` poverty-guideline or state-median-income module; the paths below follow that layout. Pages of the 2026 rule are physical PDF pages, equal to its printed pages; the 2025 edition's SOS copy is a Word file, cited by section.

| Proposed module path | Provisions | Corpus citation path | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-me/regulations/msha/chapter-24/2026-134/section-1/definitions` | 1(M) Direct Energy Cost, 1(Q) Energy Cost, 1(T) Fuel Assistance, 1(Z) Heating Season, 1(BB) Heating System (page 2); 1(DD) Household, 1(EE) Household Income, 1(HH) Indirect Determinable Energy Cost, 1(NN) Person with a Disability, 1(PP) Program Year (page 3); 1(VV) Subsidized Housing (page 4) | `us-me/regulation/mainehousing-rules/chapter-24` | In manifest `us-me-liheap-benefit-matrix-rule.yaml` (expression date 2026-06-29, 33 pages); its corpus lock records the same SHA-256 (`8d2e48b5…`) as the copy retrieved on 2026-10-21. Official copy, for every 2026 rule row: [99-346 CMR ch. 24, effective June 29, 2026, pages 2-4, 6-17 and 32-33](https://www.mainehousing.org/docs/default-source/msha-rules/ch24-home-energy-assistance-program-rule.pdf#page=2). |
| `.../2026-134/section-3/eligibility` | 3(A)(1) citizenship and size (page 6); 3(A)(4) residence and energy cost, 3(A)(7)-(9) roomers, absent members, college students (page 10); 3(A)(10) live-in attendants, 3(B) dwelling unit and subsidized housing with heat in rent, 3(C) income eligibility (page 11); 3(C)(1) inclusions and exclusions (pages 11-15), medical adjustment and ineligible members' income, 3(C)(2) categorical income eligibility (page 15) | same | Same manifest. |
| `.../2026-134/section-4/benefit-determination` | 4 and 4(A) points, percentage, proration, value announcement (page 15); matrix (page 16); multipliers, rounding up, 4(B) subsidized heat in rent (page 17); basis statement (page 32); effective date (page 33) | same | Same manifest. Its `benefit_matrix_pdf_pages: none printed in this document` is wrong: the matrix prints on PDF pages 16-17. |
| `us-me/regulations/msha/chapter-24/2025-135/section-1`, `section-3` and `section-4` | The same definitions and eligibility text in the 2025 edition; its 4(A) matrix, percentage of points and rounding sentence, 4(B) TANF Fuel Supplemental Benefits (out of scope) and 4(C) subsidized heat in rent; the filing history | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest. Official copies: [SOS Word copy, 346c024.docx](https://www.maine.gov/sos/sites/maine.gov.sos/files/inline-files/346c024.docx) (retrieved 2026-10-21: the 2025-135 text with its filing history) and the [Clearinghouse FY2026 Benefit Matrix, pages 1-2](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/benefits-matricies/ME_BenefitMatrix_2026.pdf#page=1) (rule pages 14-15 of 30). |
| `us-me/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026/section-1` | Report period and status (page 1); 1.1 dates (page 4); 1.4 categorical eligibility, 1.7 nominal payment, 1.8 gross income (page 5); 1.9 countable income (pages 6-7) | `us-me/policy/acf/liheap-plan/fy2026` | In manifest `us-me-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml` (expression date 2025-10-01; same SHA-256, `b83d155c…`, as the retrieved copy). The LIHEAP program bundle marks it excluded as a back-year table, although it governs period 2026. Check boxes and radio buttons were read from renders of pages 4-7, 9 and 10. Official copy: [FFY2026 Detailed Model Plan, pages 1, 4-7 and 9-10](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2026/state-plans/ME_Plan_2026.pdf#page=1). |
| `.../fy2026/section-2` | 2.1 thresholds by size, 2.2 and 2.3 (page 9); 2.4 priority, 2.5 benefit variables, 2.6 minimum and maximum (page 10) | same | Same manifest. |
| `us-me/policies/acf/liheap-plan/fy2025/section-2` | 2.6 minimum $88, maximum $1,012 (page 8, an image page read from a render) | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest: [FFY2025 Detailed Model Plan, page 8](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2025/state-plans/ME_Plan_2025.pdf#page=8). |
| `us-me/policies/msha/heap-income-limits/2025-2026` | 2025-2026 season maximum gross income, sizes 1-10, one, three and twelve months | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest: [MaineHousing HEAP page as captured 2025-11-01](https://web.archive.org/web/20251101091454id_/https://www.mainehousing.org/programs-services/energy/energydetails/liheap). |
| `us-me/policies/msha/heap-income-limits/2026-2027` | 2026-2027 season maximum gross income, sizes 1-10 | none | Not in a manifest; needs ingest: [MaineHousing HEAP Income Eligibility Guidelines](https://www.mainehousing.org/charts/) (live page, retrieved 2026-10-21). |
| `us-me/policies/msha/heap-point-value` | The dollar value per point (none published for FFY2025-FFY2027) | none | Nothing official to ingest until MaineHousing announces a value. Context, in no manifest: [May 2024 board packet, page 52](https://www.mainehousing.org/docs/default-source/boarddocs/may-2024-board-packet.pdf#page=52), [April 2026 board packet, pages 66 and 110](https://www.mainehousing.org/docs/default-source/boarddocs/april-2026-board-packet.pdf#page=66), [October 2026 board packet, page 18](https://www.mainehousing.org/docs/default-source/boarddocs/october-2026-board-packet.pdf#page=18) and, under the older matrix, [FY2023 Benefit Matrix, page 2](https://liheapch.acf.gov/docs/2023/benefits-matricies/ME_BenefitMatrix_2023.pdf#page=2). |
| `us-me/policies/msha/notices/2024-heap-003` | $21 benefits for subsidized heat-in-rent applicants (supports plan 1.7b) | none | Not in a manifest: [notice 2024-HEAP-003, archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20240715064535id_/https://mainehousing.org/docs/default-source/ehs-partners-library/ehs-partner-notices/2024-heap-003-py2024-heap-application-updates.pdf) (1 page). |
| `us/statutes/42/8624/b/2/B` | The greater of 150% of the poverty level or 60% of state median income; the 110% floor | expected `us/statute/42/8624` | No manifest file; `docs/ingest-runs/2026-09-13-federal-statute-layer.md` records scope `2026-09-13-liheap-statute-chapter-94-title-42` (42 U.S.C. 8621 to 8630). The branch cites [Cornell LII, (b)(2)(B)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/8624#b_2_B); official copy: [42 U.S.C. 8624, GovInfo, 2023 edition](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2023-title42/html/USCODE-2023-title42-chap94-subchapII-sec8624.htm). |
| `us/regulations/45/96/85/b` | Household-size percentages of 60% of the four-person state median income | expected `us/regulation/45/96/85` | No manifest file; `docs/ingest-runs/2026-09-13-federal-cfr-layer.md` records scope `2026-09-13-title-45-part-96` (sections 96.80 to 96.89). Official copy: [45 CFR 96.85, eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-A/part-96/subpart-H/section-96.85); the percentages are quoted below from IM 2025-02 and IM 2026-01. |
| `us/` poverty guidelines module | 2025 guidelines (period 2026), 2026 guidelines (period 2027), 2024 guidelines (period 2025 estimate) | `us/guidance/hhs/aspe/poverty-guidelines/2025/federal-register`, `.../2026/federal-register`, `.../2024/federal-register` | In `us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml` (90 FR 5917 and 89 FR 2961) and `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml` (91 FR 1797; IM 2026-01 at `us/guidance/acf/ocs/liheap-im/2026-01` and its Attachment 2 at `.../attachment-2-fpg-tables`). IM 2025-02 Attachment 2, which `fpg_year_lag` cites for mandatory FY26 use, is in no manifest: [IM 2025-02 Attachment 2, page 1](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_IM2025-02_FPGSte-Table_Att2.pdf#page=1). |
| `us/` state median income module | Maine four-person state median income and 60% rows: $118,065 (FFY2026), $122,022 (FFY2027) | `us/guidance/acf/ocs/liheap-im/2026-01/attachment-4-smi-table` (FFY2027 only) | FFY2027 in `us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml`. FFY2026, [IM 2025-02 Attachment 4, pages 2-3 and 5-6](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_IM2025-02_SMIStateTable_Att4.pdf#page=2), is in no manifest; the LIHEAP program bundle lists it as excluded as a back-year table. Needs ingest for period 2026. FFY2027 official copy: [IM 2026-01 Attachment 4, pages 2-3 and 5-6](https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/ocs/COMM_LIHEAP_Att4SMITable_States_FY2027.pdf#page=2). |

## Source text (verbatim)

Quotations come from the official files above (pdftotext, the SOS Word text and the archived HTML pages, line breaks collapsed). Plan check boxes and radio buttons come from renders of FFY2026 plan pages 4-7, 9 and 10; FFY2025 plan page 8 is an image.

**Editions and dates.** 2026 rule, page 33: “EFFECTIVE DATE: June 29, 2026”. Page 32, basis statement: “This replacement rule repeals and replaces in its entirety the current Home Energy Assistance Program Rule.” and it “updates the matrix used for determination of benefits”. 2025 edition, filing history: “2024-151 – repeal and replace – July 3, 2024 – filing” and “2025-135 – repeal and replace – July 1, 2025”. 2026 rule, page 2, 1(Z): Heating Season “means the period of time beginning October 1 and ending April 30.” Page 3, 1(PP): Program Year “means the period of time beginning October 1 and ending September 30.” FFY2026 plan, page 1: “Report Period: 10/01/2025 to 09/30/2026” and “Report Status: Submission Accepted by CO”; page 4, item 1.1: Heating assistance 10/01/2025 to 09/30/2026, no cooling component, and “Heating Assistance: For FFY2026, Subgrantees will begin taking applications on August 1, 2025 and will continue taking applications through May 29, 2026.” October 2026 board packet, page 18: “MaineHousing submitted the LIHEAP State Plan to the Dept of Health and Human Services (HHS) for Program Year 2027 on August 18, 2026.”, “We anticipate receiving the Notice of Award by the end of October.” and FFY2027 households certified “since the start of the program on August 3rd”.

**Household and size.** 2026 rule, page 3, 1(DD): Household “means any individual or group of individuals who are living together as one economic unit for whom residential energy is customarily purchased in common or who make undesignated payments for energy in the form of rent”. Page 6, 3(A)(1): “The Primary Applicant and each additional Household Member must be one of the following: (1) a U.S. Citizen; (2) a U.S. Non-Citizen National; or (3) a Qualified Alien. If the Primary Applicant or any Household Member does not meet this requirement they must be excluded from the total number of Household Members when calculating a Benefit.” Pages 7-8 list the qualified-alien categories, refugees among them. Page 15: “The income of Household Members who do not meet the citizenship or legal status requirements must be included in the Household’s income.” Page 10, 3(A)(7) and (9), let Roomers apply separately and let the Primary Applicant exclude a dependent full-time college student up to age 23; page 11, 3(A)(10), leaves out a qualifying Live-In-Care Attendant. Page 3, 1(NN), defines a Person with a Disability by 5 M.R.S. § 4553-A. The 2025 edition has the same text with “Applicant” for “Primary Applicant”.

No branch test disagrees with these derivations. Benefits in tests 1-3 and 11-13 depend on the $22 estimate (interpretation 1); test 6's 25.5% and test 7's 176.00% on interpretation 2; test 14(b) on interpretation 6; the SOLAR, WOOD, OTHER and UNSPECIFIED rows of test 9 on interpretation 11; tests 10 and 11(b) on interpretation 13.

## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Dollar value per point (estimate).** Rule 4(A) promises an announcement within fifteen days of the federal award; none was located for FFY2025, FFY2026 or FFY2027 on MaineHousing's pages, its April 2024 to October 2026 board packets, the Clearinghouse or archived copies. The branch uses $22, approved as an estimate: under the 2025 edition the largest total is stick-built 9 + Aroostook 7 + electricity 14 + priority 5 = 35, and 35 x 130% = 45.5, rounded up to 46; $1,012 / 46 = $22, the FFY2025 and FFY2026 plans' estimated maximum (item 2.6). Their $88 minimum equals 4 x $22 but does not confirm the value: the smallest unprorated 2025-edition award is apartment 6 + county 2 + wood 4 - 9 = 3 points, x 70% = 2.1, rounded up to 3 ($66). The pair first appears in the draft FFY2025 plan of May 2024 (May 2024 board packet, page 52, replacing $176 and $2,530), before that year's award; FFY2026 repeats it. The draft FFY2027 plan repeats $88 and $1,012 with “Get this information”; under the June 29, 2026 matrix the largest total is (8 + 3 + 6 + 8 + 5) x 1.8 = 54 points, and $1,012 / 54 is not a whole number, so no FFY2027 value can be derived. Period 2027 reuses $22. The last announced values ($55 and $44 per point, FFY2023) belong to the older energy-cost matrix and are not used. RuleSpec should carry the value as a separately sourced input or a marked estimate.
2. **Poverty-level rounding (inferred).** The 2025 edition rounds to the whole percent by example (75.1% to 75%, 100.6% to 101%) without saying what happens at exactly .5; the branch rounds half up, so 25.5% becomes 26% (companion test 6). The 2026 rule has no rounding sentence and prints bands to hundredths; the branch rounds half up to hundredths of a percent. Its bands “151-175.99%” and “>176%” leave exactly 176.00% outside both; the branch applies 0.7 there (companion test 7). Both editions' poverty levels use the guideline for the counted size, and the percentage applies after the medical adjustment.
3. **Categorical households (settled).** The branch passes the income test when any SPM unit member receives SNAP or TANF and computes the percentage from actual countable income, following 3(C)(2)'s “actual vetted income” option. Plan 1.4a instead says these households' benefit is “calculated based on the highest FPL allowable for each benefit type above”, and 3(C)(2) also allows “a pre-established percentage of the federal poverty level”; MaineHousing publishes no such percentages. The 2026 rule limits categorical status to adult members on the notice and requires income documentation for other members; that split is not modeled.
4. **Income limit (source wording).** The 2025 edition's 70% row names “the maximum of the greater of 150% FPIG or 60% state median income”; the 2026 rule only says MaineHousing uses both guidelines. Plan 2.1 assigns 60% of state median income to sizes 1 to 9 and 150% of the guideline to sizes 10 to 12. The branch applies the federal maximum, max(150% of the lagged guideline, 60% of state median income), which reproduces all twenty published chart rows. For size 10 in FFY2026 the chart's $102,008 (60% of state median income) exceeds plan 2.1's 150% figure ($97,725); the branch follows the chart. Above size 10 the charts refer households to their Community Action Agency; the branch extends the same formula (size 11: $105,975 in period 2026). The 110% floor of 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B) never binds. The limit uses the counted size, inferred from 3(A)(1)'s exclusion “when calculating a Benefit”.
5. **Annual income (simplification).** The charts print one-, three- and twelve-month limits, and the HEAP Guide, which sets the income period, is not public; the branch compares annual income with the twelve-month limit.
6. **Members over 18 (reading).** 3(C)(1) counts members “over the age of 18”; the branch counts members aged 18 and over, consistent with plan 1.9's unchecked box for a child under 18. A literal reading (19 and over) gives $15,236 in companion test 14(b).
7. **High school students and the applicant (proxies).** `is_in_k12_school` stands for a full-time high school student and `is_tax_unit_head` for the Primary Applicant; only earned sources are zeroed for such a student.
8. **Income items (simplification).** Every source is floored at zero separately, so a business loss offsets nothing; `rental_income` is assumed nonnegative (settled). Self-employment is net (the model's only measure) and includes partnership and S corporation income; farm rent is unearned. `financial_assistance` stands for cash gifts from outside the household, `disability_benefits` for long-term disability (item n of the 2026 rule; the 2025 list “includes, but is not limited to”), `military_retirement_income` for a government pension and `estate_income` (which includes royalties) for estates, trusts and royalties. Social Security and SSI count gross, with no `medicare_part_b_premium` subtracted (settled). `retirement_distributions` are not counted (assets drawn down), nor are capital gains, TANF or General Assistance. Contract income, mortgage or sales contracts, combat pay and education aid have no specific input.
9. **Medical adjustment (simplification).** Annual `medical_expense_health_insurance_premiums` and `other_medical_expenses` of all members stand in for documented expenses “paid during the income period” under IRS Publication 502. The adjustment applies only above the limit and stops at the limit, so an adjusted household is scored at the limit (36,836 / 15,650 = 235%, 70%).
10. **Household and size (simplification).** The SPM unit stands in for the Household. Size counts `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`, which approximates 3(A)(1)'s documentary test and 3(A)(3)'s SSN proof. Roomers, live-in-care attendants, the optional college-student exclusion, residency and the dwelling-unit tests have no inputs. Proration divides by all SPM unit members, so only immigration status reduces the share; rounding up follows the multiplication (companion test 13(c) is exactly 22).
11. **Fuels (coverage limits and decisions).** `heating_type` is a required input and UNSPECIFIED pays $0, except heat in subsidized rent, which needs no fuel (settled; PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the default). The 2025 edition's bio-fuel including bio-bricks, wood pellets and corn rows and the 2026 rule's wood pellet and biobrick rows have no `heating_type` value; OTHER has no row and is ineligible even with a bill. WOOD uses the cordwood “Wood” row. SOLAR uses the electricity row, as a grid-tied home with electric heat (decided); an off-grid solar home has no electricity bill and so no energy cost. NONE fails the functioning-heating-system test. Kerosene keeps its own row and reads `fuel_oil_expense` for its bill.
12. **Energy cost and housing proxies.** A positive bill for the named fuel with heat outside the rent stands for a Direct Energy Cost, and `heat_expense_included_in_rent` for an Indirect Determinable Energy Cost. An unsubsidized tenant with heat in rent scores the building's fuel and needs a listed one. Subsidized Housing is `receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing`, narrower than 1(VV). Whether a subsidized tenant with heat in rent “pays a portion of their rent or utility costs” is not checked. The $21 is the FFY2026 plan's nominal payment under 4(B) (2025 edition 4(C)); with no FFY2027 plan posted, period 2027 reuses it.
13. **Priority points (reading).** Both matrices print one priority value. The branch awards it once per household: 5 if any member is 60 or over, has `is_disabled` (for 1(NN)) or is 6 or under; otherwise 3 in the 2025 edition if any member is 7 to 17. The 2026 rule's “Points for the first in the house” confirms once per household for that edition; for the 2025 edition it is inferred from the “or” between the rows. The April 2026 memo proposed points for additional at-risk members, but the adopted table shows only the first-member column. Members outside the counted size can trigger the points.
14. **County and dwelling (inputs and defaults).** County points read `county`; an unlisted county, such as UNKNOWN, scores 0 (companion test 8). Condo/Duplex and Apartment carry the same points in both editions and share one category. `me_heap_dwelling_type` defaults to STICK_BUILT_OR_MODULAR, so a caller that omits it gets 9 points (period 2026) or 3 (period 2027). A hotel or motel residence has no category.
15. **Years and dates (simplification).** Annual periods read 1 January values, so period 2026 applies FFY2026 values to October to December 2026, which fall in FFY2027, and period 2027 applies FFY2027 values to all of 2027. The replacement rule took effect June 29, 2026, after the FFY2026 application window closed (May 29, 2026) and before FFY2027 applications opened in August 2026. The matrix parameters' first date, `2024-07-03`, is the 2024 edition's filing date as printed in the filing history; its effective date is not printed there, and no period 2026 or 2027 value depends on it. Period 2025 and earlier are estimates (see Policy periods).
16. **Other gaps.** The TANF Fuel Supplemental Benefit (2025 edition 3(A) and 4(B); absent from the 2026 rule), Supplemental Benefits, ECIP, weatherization, CHIP and the Heat Pump Program are out of scope. Funding availability (“Benefit availability is based on HEAP funding availability”), one application per Program Year (2(A)), application windows, payment routing and the HEAP Guide's procedures are not modeled. The branch adds no `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml` entry; readings 3 and 4 are recorded here.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-me-liheap-benefit-matrix-rule.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-me-liheap-benefit-matrix-rule.yaml) (June 29, 2026 replacement rule; period 2027 only)
- [us-me-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-me-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml) (FFY2026 plan)
- [us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml) (2025 guidelines for period 2026; 2024 for the period 2025 estimate)
- [us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml) (2026 guidelines, IM 2026-01 and FFY2027 state median income, period 2027)
- [us-hhs-poverty-guidelines.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-hhs-poverty-guidelines.yaml) (undated, never extracted)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-me/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover both editions' matrices (base points, three dwelling categories, all 16 counties, every fuel row the model encodes, priority points once per household with the 2025 edition's 7-17 row, the subsidized adjustment), both percentage tables with their band edges, whole-percent and two-decimal rounding and the 176.00% gap, proration for ineligible members and rounding up, the income limit as the greater of 150% of the lagged guideline and 60% of state median income for sizes 1 to 11 with the inclusive ceiling, categorical SNAP and TANF receipt, the energy-cost condition, heat in subsidized and unsubsidized rent with the $21 nominal benefit, counted members aged 18 and over with the high school student rule, every listed and excluded source, per-source loss floors, the medical adjustment on both sides, the $22 value per point as a marked estimate, other, solar, wood, no heat and unspecified fuel, and any 2025 or 2028 period kept in scope. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: LIHEAP wave 1d: encode Tennessee LIHEAP regular heating assistance

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Tennessee LIHEAP regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1d, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10430 (branch `tn-liheap-wave1d`), open, not merged. Head `5ddb74f1cc` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983`; this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10430 opened on 2026-10-23 with no reviews yet, so there is no revision to pin.
- **Sources missing from the corpus.** Corpus `main` holds the four main Tennessee sources in the editions the branch cites (2026 Policy Manual, LIHEAP 2026 Benefit Matrix, FY2027 Benefit Matrix LI-12, FY2026 plan Revision 1); no manifest holds a different edition. Missing and needed: the LIHEAP 26 workshop deck (size groups, matrix factors, income table labels); the draft 2027 Policy Manual and the draft FY2027 plan (status Saved), which set the FY2027 limits (60% of SMI for sizes 1 to 8, 150% of the guideline rounded down for 9 and over) and drop the propane minimum; LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 4 (FY2026 SMI by size, behind every FY2026 limit) and Attachment 2 (2025 guidelines at 100%, 110% and 150%); and 45 CFR 96.85(b) (size adjustment of SMI). 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B) (the 110% floor) is in no manifest; an ingest-run record on corpus `main` describes an unsigned extraction of 42 U.S.C. 8621 to 8630. The LIHEAP program bundle on corpus `main` (as of 2026-10-06) marks the FY2026 plan and IM 2025-02 Attachment 4 `scope: excluded` as back-year tables, although period 2026 rests on both.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-23; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10430, branch `tn-liheap-wave1d`, head `5ddb74f1cc` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983` and closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10420. It includes the 2026-10-22 review fixes (half-up burden rounding with a tie case at 0.12145; `has_heating_expense` set directly in two eligibility cases so the fuel rule alone decides; manual page 35 cited; one duplicate income-limit case removed) and the 2026-10-23 comment on retirement-account withdrawals (still excluded, settled). No `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml` entry. Oracle fixtures will pin the merged commit.
- **Scope:** Tennessee LIHEAP Regular Energy Assistance (Tennessee Housing Development Agency, THDA) for FY2026 and FY2027. Tennessee pays one regular benefit per program year from one statewide matrix and applies it as heating from October through May; the model returns that single annual award. Covered: residence; household size counting citizens and qualified aliens, every member's income counted; gross countable income; the income limit (60% of state median income, and in FY2027 150% of the guideline for sizes 9 and over); the federal 110% floor; an energy account or heat in rent; the energy burden from all household energy bills; the matrix (four size groups, four income groups, nine burden columns); and the FY2026 $500 propane minimum. Out of scope: Crisis Energy Assistance, a second award as cooling (June to September), LIHEAP weatherization, HVAC repair and replacement, Assurance 16 services, disaster benefits, waitlists, priority order and funding availability, Social Security number refusal and prior-year LIHEAP credit.
- **Policy periods:** two verified program years. FY2026: October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026, heating to April 30, 2026, opened November 1, 2025 (plan pages 1 and 4; manual page 13). FY2027: October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027, heating to April 30, 2027 (draft plan pages 1 and 4), start pending the federal award (draft manual page 51). Parameters hold `2025-10-01` entries; `payment/amount`, `eligibility/fpg_rate` (1.5 for sizes 9 and over), `payment/income_group/uses_fpg_rates` (false) and `payment/propane_minimum` ($0) change at `2026-10-01`, and `payment/income_group/max_table_size` and `top/A`, `top/B`, `top/C` start at `2026-10-01`. Variables are annual and read 1 January values (`fpg_year_lag` 1): period `2026` is FY2026 on the 2025 guidelines and the FY2026 four-person SMI ($102,735); period `2027` is FY2027 on the 2026 guidelines and the FY2027 SMI ($105,327). `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2026-2027"`. FY2027 rests on the posted LI-12 matrix while the FY2027 plan and manual are drafts (settled). Period `2025` and earlier apply the FY2026 matrix and rates to the 2024 guidelines and the FY2025 SMI ($98,377): unverified estimates (FY2025 used points, workshop page 23). Periods `2028` and later are carried-forward estimates of FY2027. No other estimate was approved.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/tn/thda/liheap/`: `tn_liheap`, `tn_liheap_household_size`; `eligibility/` `tn_liheap_eligible`, `tn_liheap_income_limit`; `income/` `tn_liheap_countable_income`. No new input variable. The formulas reuse the federal helpers `liheap_smi_limit` (`gov.hhs.smi`) and `fpg` (`gov.hhs.fpg`) and the federal floor `gov.hhs.liheap.fpg_floor` (1.1).
- **Parameters:** 19 files under `gov.states.tn.thda.liheap`: `eligibility/` `fpg_rate` (0 by size; 1.5 for sizes 9 and over from `2026-10-01`), `fpg_year_lag` (1), `smi_rate` (0.6); `income/` `earned_income_min_age` (18), `interest_threshold` (200), `sources/earned` (5 sources), `sources/unearned` (18); `payment/` `amount` (size group x income group x burden column, both years), `burden_column` (nine column starts), `burden_decimals` (4), `energy_cost_sources` (7 bills), `propane_minimum` (500; 0 from `2026-10-01`), `size_group` (1-2, 3-5, 6-8, 9 and over); `payment/income_group/` `fpg_rate` (A 0.71, B 0.87, C 1.17), `uses_fpg_rates` (true; false from `2026-10-01`), `max_table_size` (16), `top/A`, `top/B`, `top/C` (printed FY2027 tops for sizes 1 to 16). Plus a `programs.yaml` entry and a changelog fragment.
- **Tests:** 49 YAML cases in 4 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/tn/thda/liheap/` (`tn_liheap.yaml` 21, `eligibility/tn_liheap_eligible.yaml` 10, `eligibility/tn_liheap_income_limit.yaml` 7, `income/tn_liheap_countable_income.yaml` 11). Every case sends `heating_type`. A local run on 2026-10-22 passed the 50 cases then in the tree, before the 2026-10-22 review fixes; the fixed tests were not re-run. CI validates them.

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence on axiom-corpus `main` (`dce8e44665`, 2026-10-23) was checked on 2026-10-23 against the full manifest list; the signed release was not checked. rulespec-us `main` (`115bad3183`, 2026-10-23) has `us-tn/policies/` (cms, dhs/snap and income_tax) and `us-tn/regulations/1240-01`, but no THDA or LIHEAP module, and `us/` has no poverty-guideline, state-median-income, 45 CFR 96 or 42 U.S.C. 8624 module; the paths below follow that layout. Pages are physical PDF pages. Every page of the four captured Tennessee PDFs carries text, so a corpus `page-N` suffix equals the PDF page; the FY2026 manual prints page numbers one lower.
