## Interpretations and gaps

1. **FY2026 income groups (inferred rates).** The 2026 matrix prints the income starts and ends without percentages. 71%, 87% and 117% of the 2025 guideline reproduce all 36 printed tops for sizes 1 to 12; no document states these rates, and workshop slide 30 heads the same columns “0% - 50%”, “51% -75%” and “76% - 100%”. The branch computes the tops from the rates, rounded to cents (for size 3, 1.17 x 26,650 is 31,180.4999 in floating point; printed $31,180.50). Group D runs to the income limit.
2. **FY2026 income limits.** The branch floors 60% of the four-person SMI, then floors its product with the 45 CFR 96.85(b) size factor; this reproduces every IM 2025-02 Attachment 4 value for sizes 1 to 12. The matrix prints the size 8 ceiling as $85,064.50 and workshop slide 30 prints size 6 as $81,336; the branch uses $85,064 and $81,366, as Attachment 4 prints. Manual page 10 defines the standard as 60% of SMI or 150% of the guidelines; the FY2026 plan and manual apply 60% of SMI to every size, and the branch follows them.
3. **FY2027 printed values.** The LI-12 tops do not follow one rate of the 2026 guideline (size 12 group A, $55,592.50, is 70.87% of $78,440), so the branch stores the printed tops for sizes 1 to 16; larger households use size 16. LI-12 prints “C 4 $28,710.51 $38,610.50”, repeating the size 4 group B end as the group C start; the branch keeps that income in group B (companion test 14(b): $505, or $496 in group C). “D 5 $44,255.51 $73,307.00” starts below the group C end of $45,255.50 and is read as a misprint; the branch uses only the tops. LI-12 prints the size 13 to 16 ceilings $125,910 to $150,660, which step by $8,250 from size 12, the 150% add-on in the FY2026 Attachment 2; the FY2027 rule gives $126,180 to $151,740 (add $8,520). The branch applies the stated rule (settled; companion test 14(f)). The draft plan lists sizes 9 to 15 and the draft manual 9 to 16; larger households keep 150%.
4. **Households over 12 in FY2026 (inference, settled).** The 2026 matrix stops at size 12. The branch extends the 9 and over size group and the guideline rates (companion test 6: group B, $525; the size 12 tops would put $68,000 in group C, $500), and the limit continues with three points per added member (Attachment 4).
5. **Federal floor.** 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B) bars excluding a household on income below 110% of the guideline. The floor uses the same lagged guideline, rounded to cents, and a strict comparison. In FY2026 it binds from size 15 (limit $98,009, floor $101,915).
6. **Burden rounding (inferred).** The manual's examples print burdens to two percentage decimals (8.79%, 8.39%); the matrix columns have four decimals. The branch rounds the ratio half up to four decimals; the sources state no tie rule. Only exact ties change the result (companion test 3(a): 0.12145 gives column 6, $540, against column 5, $445, under half-to-even rounding).
7. **Burden inputs (simplifications).** The manual divides a monthly energy expense, from up to 12 months of bills, by 30-day current income. The branch divides annual bills by annual income. The cost is the sum of seven bill inputs, which cannot separate deposits, optional charges or late fees. Zero or negative income uses column 9; the manual does not address it. This holds even when the counted cost is $0, so a household with heat in rent and no other bill receives $750 at $0 income and $174 at $1.
8. **Heating responsibility and heat in rent.** The branch reads an active energy account as `has_heating_expense` (a positive bill for the primary heating fuel, heat not in rent) or heat in rent. A household whose only active account is not its heating fuel (for example, gas heat with only an electric bill entered) is not eligible in the model. Heat in rent has no input for the energy cost a landlord attributes to the tenant, so its burden counts only separately billed energy and is a lower bound (settled; companion test 10(a)). `heating_type` is a required input; NONE is never eligible and UNSPECIFIED pays $0 unless heat is in the rent (settled; PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the default). SOLAR reads the electric bill, like ELECTRICITY. Subsidized tenants meet no added condition: own-name bills are processed without adjustment, and housing-agency overage bills are entered as bills.
9. **Fuel and matrix.** The matrix has no fuel dimension and plan item 2.5 leaves fuel type unchecked, so every fuel with a bill reads the same cell. Help with the main heating source only (page 6) and the choice of one utility (page 25) concern payment routing; not modeled.
10. **Propane minimum (reading, settled).** Page 25 says the minimum payment for propane assistance will be $500 when a household with a smaller benefit applies it to propane. The branch raises the award to $500 for a PROPANE household in FY2026, assuming it applies the benefit to propane. The text does not say whether the benefit itself rises or the household covers the difference. Kerosene, fuel oil and wood, also home-delivered fuels (page 9), get no minimum. The draft FY2027 manual omits the minimum, so period 2027 has none.
11. **Members not counted in size.** Page 18 asks grantees to prorate benefits that can reasonably be prorated by the number of eligible members, and in the same paragraph to exclude ineligible members from the household count when determining the benefit. The branch applies the matrix at the reduced size and does not prorate on top (settled; companion test 11(c)). Size counts `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant`; the SPM unit stands in for the household; Social Security number refusal has no input.
12. **Earned income of minors and dependents (settled).** Plan item 1.9 leaves “Earned income of a child under the age of 18” unchecked; the manual excludes the earnings of a dependent aged 18 or older and of a dependent in school living with a parent or guardian (page 28). The branch excludes the earnings of members under 18 and of every tax-unit dependent, which stands in for the manual's dependent and student tests. A minor emancipated by marriage (page 8) is still excluded (companion test 13(a)). The plan box and the manual wording differ; the branch combines them and records no source-conflict entry.
13. **Unearned income readings (settled or simplified).** Social Security counts net of the computed `medicare_part_b_premium` (settled); premiums withheld from pensions or VA benefits, overpayment recovery and garnishment are not subtracted. Interest counts in full above $200 a year per person and is assumed withdrawn; dividends count in full (the draft FY2027 wording “Dividends and/or interest that $200 annually” may extend the threshold to dividends; the branch keeps the FY2026 reading). IRA and 401(k) withdrawals are excluded like bank-account withdrawals: the list names pensions, annuities and regular insurance payments, not retirement-account withdrawals (settled 2026-10-23). Each source is floored at zero separately and `rental_income` is assumed nonnegative (settled). Black Lung benefits ($20 monthly disregard), royalties, severance, adoption assistance, training stipends, military allotments and irregular income have no input. Cash gifts are irregular income on page 27 and excluded on page 28; no gift input exists. TANF counts through the SPM unit's `tanf`.
14. **Income period (simplification).** Tennessee counts income received in the 30 days before application (2.14) and converts weekly pay at 4.33; the branch uses annual amounts.
15. **Years and dates (simplification).** Annual periods read 1 January values, so period 2026 applies FY2026 to all of calendar 2026, including October to December 2026, which fall in FY2027. FY2027 rests on the posted LI-12 matrix; the plan (status Saved) and manual (marked Draft) are not final, and on 2026-10-21 the THDA program page still described the 2025-2026 program. The FY2026 plan dates heating to April 30 and cooling from May 1 (printed 05/01/2025), while the manual applies the award as heating through May; the amount is the same either way.
16. **Other gaps.** Waitlists, the priority order, funding depletion, the prior-year LIHEAP credit and the $50 prepaid-account balance (2.8), crisis assistance and the cooling application of the award are not modeled.
